title: The Immortal Paradise Building in the Mountain
description: Attributed to the tenth-century master Dong Yuan, this hanging scroll in ink and light colour on silk imagines a paradise hall of the Immortals deep in the mountains, its pavilions nested among mist-wrapped peaks. The towering vertical composition, over 1.8 metres tall, is held in the National Palace Museum, Taipei.

title: Traveling on the River in Snow
dateCreated: latter half of the 10th century AD
description: Cargo ships with stern-mounted rudders glide through a snow-stilled river, accompanied by a smaller craft. Painted in fine ink on silk, the work exemplifies early Song dynasty jiehua, the precise ruled-line technique used to render boats and architecture with engineering accuracy.

title: Xiao and Xiang Rivers
description: A detail from a long handscroll associated with the Southern Tang master, depicting the misted reaches of the Xiao and Xiang rivers in Hunan. Dong Yuan's soft hemp-fibre brushstrokes and graded ink washes established the canonical southern landscape mode followed for centuries.

title: Travelers Among Mountains and Streams
dateCreated: between circa 1000 and circa 1020 Song dynasty (960–1279)
description: A monumental hanging scroll in which towering peaks rise abruptly above a thread of waterfall, while travelers and pack mules trace a path across the valley floor. A landmark of Northern Song monumental landscape, the work uses dense raindrop texture strokes and a vertiginous vertical scale to express the Confucian ideal of nature dwarfing humanity.

title: Finches and Bamboo
description: Two finches perch on the arching stems of teal-green bamboo beside a weathered rock, observed with the minute feather detail characteristic of the imperial court bird-and-flower idiom. The handscroll, attributed to the Northern Song Emperor Huizong (r. 1100–1125) and held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, exemplifies the exacting naturalism and calligraphic elegance of the gongbi tradition.

title: Imaginary tour through Xiao-xiang
description: A Southern Song handscroll, nearly four metres long, leading the viewer through the misted river country at the confluence of the Xiao and Xiang. Painted in monochrome ink on paper, it belongs to the contemplative literati tradition and is held by the Tokyo National Museum.
credit: Tokyo National Museum

title: Hungry Ghosts Scroll
description: A late Heian-period handscroll depicting gaki, the emaciated hungry ghosts of Buddhist cosmology, condemned by past greed to wander among the living unseen. Ink and colour on paper carry the doctrine in plain pictorial narrative, the suffering specters set against scenes of human everyday life in twelfth-century Japan.
credit: Tokyo National Museum, Emuseum

title: Dancing and Singing
description: A hanging scroll in ink and light colour depicting misty mountains, gnarled trees, and a small figure resting near a rocky outcrop, with calligraphic inscriptions at the upper left. Ma Yuan, a leading court painter of the Southern Song dynasty working around 1200, was celebrated for compositions that concentrate pictorial weight to one side and leave open space to suggest an infinite, fog-shrouded distance.

title: Nine Dragons 九龍圖 九龙图
description: Nine dragons surge through clouds, mist, and crashing water across a long handscroll of ink and wash on paper. Chen Rong, a Southern Song scholar-official, painted the work in 1244; it is celebrated for its splashed-ink dragons and is held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts (Boston, USA)

title: 15 Qian Xuan Eight Flowers National Palace Museum Beijing
description: A handscroll by the thirteenth-century painter Qian Xuan, spacing eight flowering sprays — narcissus, blossoming branches and garden flowers among them — across a plain paper ground. Qian Xuan, a Song loyalist who declined to serve the Mongol court, renders each specimen in fine outline filled with pale colour washes, in his deliberately refined, archaistic manner. The scroll is held in the Palace Museum, Beijing.

title: Early Autumn
description: A handscroll in ink and color on paper showing dragonflies, frogs, and aquatic plants beside a pond. Qian Xuan was a scholar-painter of the late Song and early Yuan, and the work pairs close natural observation with the lyric reserve of literati painting.
credit: Description on archive.org ( Original )

title: Handrolle »Acht Ansichten der Gegend von Hsiao-Hsiang«
description: A section of the celebrated handscroll cycle Eight Views of the Xiao and Xiang Rivers, in which Muqi distils river, mist and distant peak into broad ink washes. The Chan-Buddhist economy of means deeply influenced later Japanese ink painting.

title: Dwelling in the Qingbian Mountains
description: A towering hanging scroll in ink on paper, its densely textured peaks built from layered hemp-fibre strokes and moss dots. Wang Meng's restless, near-trembling line gives the Qingbian range a vibrating, almost airless density emblematic of late-Yuan literati landscape.

title: Durán Madonna
description: The Virgin Mary, clothed in saturated red, is seated within a Gothic stone arch and holds the Christ Child, who reaches toward the open pages of a book resting on her lap. An angel bearing a crown appears at the apex of the arch against a dark background. Dating from between circa 1435 and 1438, this panel — known as the Durán Madonna — demonstrates van der Weyden's mastery of finely modelled drapery and tender devotional intimacy, and is held in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.

title: Saint Christopher
description: Saint Christopher wades through dark water bearing the Christ Child, his giant frame sharply lit against a wooded shore. Witz, working in Basel, was an early Northern realist whose granular textures and naturalistic landscape settings broke with International Gothic abstraction.

title: The Virgin with Chancellor Rolin by Jan van Eyck
description: A masterwork of Flemish painting depicting the Virgin Mary and Christ Child in a sacra conversazione composition with a kneeling chancellor. This iconic work showcases Jan van Eyck's revolutionary oil painting technique and meticulous attention to luminous detail, set within an elaborate interior and landscape vista that exemplifies Northern Renaissance realism.

title: The Battle of San Romano
description: From the three-panel cycle painted for the Bartolini Salimbeni and later Lorenzo de' Medici, this London panel shows Niccolo da Tolentino leading the Florentines against Siena. Uccello's foreshortened lances, fallen soldier and patterned ground are a famous early experiment in linear perspective.

title: Nuremberg chronicles - Dance of Death
englishTitle: Dance of Death, from the Nuremberg Chronicle
description: A celebrated woodcut from Hartmann Schedel's Nuremberg Chronicle of 1493, showing capering skeletons in the late-medieval danse macabre tradition. Wolgemut's workshop produced one of the most ambitious printed-image programs of the incunabula period.

title: Portrait of a Young woman with a Winged Bonnet
description: A Netherlandish bust portrait of a young woman whose elaborate winged linen headdress frames a composed, downcast face. Rogier's precise contours, translucent skin and patient observation of folded cloth set the model for fifteenth-century Burgundian portraiture.
credit: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

provenance.location: Paintings in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin - Room IV

title: Portrait of an unknown young woman
description: A young woman in a starched linen headdress turns slightly to the left, her hands not yet finished in the drawing, the outline of one sketched at lower left. The silverpoint study, now in the British Museum, belongs to a small group of preparatory portrait drawings attributed to Rogier van der Weyden's Brussels workshop around 1440.

title: Deposition
description: The body of Christ is lowered from the cross within a shallow gilded niche, surrounded by ten mourners arranged in a tight, frieze-like rhythm. Van der Weyden's sharp drapery folds and tear-streaked faces compress the Passion into a sculpted relief of grief, a touchstone of Early Netherlandish painting.

title: Seven Sacraments Altarpiece
description: A triptych setting the seven sacraments inside a vast Gothic church, with the Crucifixion at the center of the nave and the rites unfolding in the aisles. Van der Weyden orchestrates devotional precision, contemporary Netherlandish architecture, and an extraordinary system of inscribed banderoles.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"w/weyden/rogier/05sevens/0sevens"

title: Joseon-Kang Huian-Gosagwansudo
description: A Joseon scholar reclines on a rocky outcrop, overlooking water below — the scene identified by its title Gosagwansudo as a seonbi gazing from a high hill. Kang Hui-an was a fifteenth-century Korean court official and one of the earliest named painters in the Korean literati tradition. The work is small (15.7 by 23.4 cm) and executed in a gestural ink manner characteristic of his surviving output.

title: Saint Jerome in the Wilderness
description: Saint Jerome sits at the entrance of a rocky red-brown outcrop, a book open on his lap and his hand raised, while a lion faces him from the foreground and a horse grazes in the arid landscape beyond. The panel, signed 'IOANNES BELLINVS' and dated around 1455 to 1460, is among the artist's earliest treatments of the hermit-saint subject he would revisit throughout his career.

title: Christus on the Cross with Mary and St John
description: A T-shaped cross holding the crucified Christ rises before a red cloth of honour and a stone wall, flanked by the white-robed Virgin and Saint John. The reduced palette and stark spatial setting strip away narrative detail, concentrating on grief and bodily presence in a manner unusual for mid-fifteenth-century devotional painting.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"w/weyden/rogier/14pieta/5crucifi"

title: Christ on the cross with Mary and Saint John the Evangelist
description: A stark devotional Crucifixion in which the swooning Virgin and grieving Saint John flank the cross against a flat red cloth and grey wall. Rogier strips the scene of landscape and narrative incident, concentrating the drama into sculptural silhouettes and restrained, almost monochrome colour.

title: Madonna and Child with an Angel
description: The Madonna stands holding the Christ Child while a kneeling angel in a blue robe looks up in adoration, a composition typical of Botticelli's early years in the orbit of Filippo Lippi. The soft modelling and delicate linearity announce the Florentine grace of his mature style. The panel, dated 1465, is held at the Musée Fesch in Ajaccio.
credit: Musée Fesch

title: A Foolish Virgin in Half-Figure
description: A young woman with elaborately knotted braids is shown half-length, turning her oil lamp upside down to show that it is empty — the mark of the foolish virgins of the parable in Matthew 25, who let their lamps run dry before the bridegroom came. The engraving relates to Schongauer's series of the Wise and Foolish Virgins and bears his monogram. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: Death of the Virgin
description: The Virgin lies dying on a great canopied bed surrounded by the twelve apostles: one reads the office of the dying, another places a taper in her hands, and a tall candlestick stands at the foot of the bed. Engraved around 1470-75, it is one of Schongauer's largest and most influential prints, copied across Europe and studied closely by the young Dürer. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: Griffin
description: A griffin — eagle's head, beak and wings joined to the body of a lion — stands in profile, its tail curling over its back and its front talons gripping the ground. The small engraving, one of Schongauer's rare secular subjects, bears his monogram below the creature. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, acquired through the Harris Brisbane Dick Fund.

title: Hl. Georg im Kampf mit dem Drachen
description: Uccello's late panel of the chivalric saint lancing the dragon, with a tethered princess and a stylised storm gathering overhead. The artist's lifelong fascination with linear perspective is visible in the geometric grid of the cave and patterned ground.

title: Madonna and Child with the Young St. John the Baptist
description: Botticelli treats the popular Florentine subject of the infant Christ greeted by the young John the Baptist, a tondo-like intimacy enclosed within a vertical panel. The crisp contour drawing and Mary's downcast features are hallmarks of his Quattrocento workshop.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"b/botticel/1early/15virgin"

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Ornament with Owl Mocked by Day Birds
description: An engraving by Martin Schongauer in which an owl with outstretched wings perches at the base of a dense thicket of curling foliage, harried by the small day birds that dart through the scrollwork above. The owl mocked by daytime birds was a familiar medieval emblem of folly attracting scorn, and Schongauer works the motif into an ornament design of the kind used as a model by goldsmiths and other craftsmen. The sheet bears his monogram and belongs to the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: Peasant Family Going to Market
description: A peasant strides ahead on foot, laden with his gear, leading the horse on which his wife rides with a small child clinging on behind her; the road winds past a rocky crag toward a village with a church in the distance. One of Schongauer's secular genre engravings, it treats everyday rural life with the same fineness of line as his devotional prints. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: Print
description: An engraving showing the Virgin and Child on the donkey under a date palm, with angels shaking down its fruit while Joseph gathers the dates. Schongauer's fine, controlled burin work and tender narrative detail set the model for later northern printmaking, including the young Dürer.

title: Retour de Judith 1
englishTitle: The Return of Judith to Bethulia
description: Judith strides forward carrying an olive branch and sword, while her maidservant lifts the shrouded head of Holofernes behind her. The small Uffizi panel, dated 1470, pairs Old Testament tyrannicide with Botticelli's lyrical, wind-swept drapery. It is held in the Uffizi Gallery, Florence.

title: Saint John on Patmos
description: Saint John the Evangelist sits on the rocky shore of Patmos with a book open on his lap, looking up at a radiant vision of the Virgin and Child in the sky; his eagle perches at his side and a small sailing boat crosses the sea behind him. Schongauer's engraving joins the saint's exile on the island to the apocalyptic vision he recorded there, and carries his monogram below. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: St. Martin
description: Saint Martin stands wrapped in a deep fur-lined cloak, drawing his sword to cut away a portion of it for the half-naked beggar kneeling at his feet. Schongauer presents the saint's famous act of charity as a standing figure rather than the more familiar scene on horseback, signing the plate below with his monogram. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: St. Michael
description: The archangel Michael, wings spread and robes swirling, drives a long-shafted lance into the dragon sprawled beneath his feet, its clawed wings and barbed tail thrashing across the lower margin. Schongauer's engraving renders feathers, drapery, and scaled hide with the disciplined burin work that made him the most influential Northern printmaker before Dürer. The plate carries his M†S monogram and dates from his Colmar workshop, around 1470-91.

title: The Madonna and Child in the Courtyard
description: The Virgin sits directly on the ground in the pose of the Madonna of Humility, her ample drapery pooling around her as she holds the Christ Child, whose head radiates spikes of light. Behind her a bare tree and the gate tower of a walled courtyard close off the scene — an enclosed garden alluding to Mary's purity. The engraving bears Schongauer's M†S monogram and was made in his Colmar workshop around 1470-91.

title: The Third Wise Virgin
description: A young woman with loose waist-length hair and a wreath of foliage holds a burning oil lamp upright on her open palm — the mark of the wise virgins in Christ's parable of the ten bridesmaids (Matthew 25), who kept their lamps filled for the bridegroom's arrival. The sheet belongs to Schongauer's engraved series of the Wise and Foolish Virgins, each figure isolated on a small mound of ground. His M†S monogram appears below.

title: Vienna Diptych
description: A small devotional diptych pairing the Fall of Man with a Lamentation, in which Van der Goes channels acute emotional weight through pale, exhausted flesh and the slumped diagonal of Christ's body. The meticulous Eyckian observation is carried by a temperament closer to mournful introspection than ceremonial display.
credit: File:Hugo_van_der_Goes_-_Vienna_Diptych_(Lamentation).jpg File:Hugo_van_der_Goes_-_The_Fall_of_Man_and_The_Lamentation_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg

title: Wild Woman Holding a Shield with a Lion's Head
description: In this circular engraving a wild woman wearing only a leafy wreath nurses her child while steadying a tilted shield emblazoned with a snarling lion's head; ragged heraldic mantling fills the edges of the roundel. The hairy 'wild folk' of medieval legend were popular shield-supporters in fifteenth-century German art, and Schongauer here turns the motif into an oddly tender domestic image. The plate is signed with his M†S monogram.

title: Winter Landscape
description: A winter landscape in ink on paper, with sheer rock formations rising over snow-laden ground, bare trees, and a small dwelling nestled in the valley below. Attributed to the Muromachi-period Zen monk-painter Sesshū Tōyō and dated to around 1470, the work is held in the Tokyo National Museum.

title: Ginevra de' Benci
description: Ginevra de' Benci, daughter of a Florentine banker, is portrayed before a juniper bush whose Italian name, ginepro, puns on her own. Painted in oil on poplar between circa 1474 and 1478, the panel is the only Leonardo in the Americas and hangs at the National Gallery of Art in Washington.

title: Saint Jerome praying in the cave
description: Jerome reads at the mouth of a rocky grotto with the lion crouched beside him, a fortified town and distant horsemen visible beyond. The oil-on-wood panel, 151 by 113 cm, hangs in the Uffizi and shows Bellini integrating northern landscape detail into a Venetian devotional altarpiece.

title: Allegory of Abundance
description: A standing female personification of Abundance is accompanied by children carrying and clutching bunches of fruit and grapes, executed in pen, ink and chalk on tinted paper. Datable to between 1480 and 1485, the sheet is one of Botticelli's most finished surviving drawings and is held in the British Museum.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"b/botticel/92drawin/3abundan"

title: Creation
description: When closed, the triptych shows the world on the third day of Creation in grisaille: a translucent globe enclosing a dark, watery earth, with God depicted small in the upper left. The muted tonality contrasts sharply with the saturated colour of the interior panels, framing the work as an unfolding cosmological drama.

title: Giovanni bellini
englishTitle: Crucifixion in a Jewish Cemetery (Crocifisso Niccolini da Camugliano)
description: Christ is shown crucified against a detailed Italian cityscape of towers, domes, and fortified walls, with a tree and bare branches framing the composition. Known as the Niccolini da Camugliano Crucifixion and dated around 1480 to 1485, the panel is attributed to Giovanni Bellini and takes its name from the private collection in which it was long preserved.

title: Hl.Augustinus
description: Saint Augustine sits in his study, deep in thought before book, inkwell and astronomical instruments. Botticelli's fresco for the Florentine church of Ognissanti casts the Church Father as a Renaissance scholar, painted as a pendant to Ghirlandaio's Saint Jerome.

title: Idealised Portrait of a Lady
description: A profile bust of a young woman with elaborately plaited hair, long identified, however speculatively, with the Florentine beauty Simonetta Vespucci. Botticelli converts a Quattrocento portrait formula into a half-mythological nymph, the linear refinement balanced by jewels and serpentine ornament.

title: Nativity
description: An Adoration of the Shepherds set in a ruined Romanesque shed, the rough stonework and spiky straw rendered in the crisp, hatched line for which Schongauer was renowned. His Late Gothic prints circulated widely and were copied closely by the young Albrecht Dürer.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"s/schongau/nativit"

title: Saint Francis in the Desert
description: Francis stands barefoot outside his rocky cell, arms slightly spread, lit by a raking light that ignites a slender laurel and bends the surrounding plants toward him. Oil on poplar, around 1480, the panel is at the Frick Collection in New York and is among the earliest devotional pictures to place an outdoor landscape on equal footing with the saint.

title: Schongauer Anthony
description: An engraving in which the hermit saint is hoisted into the air and tormented by a swarm of bristling, scaled, and beaked demons. Schongauer's burin work, with its dense parallel hatching and inventive monstrous anatomy, exerted a famous influence on the young Dürer.
credit: http://www.abcgallery.com/S/schongauer/schongauer12.html image

title: St. Sebastian
description: Saint Sebastian stands bound to a fragmented classical column, his body bristling with arrows against a ruined ancient cityscape. Mantegna fuses humanist antiquarianism with Christian martyrdom, a recurring preoccupation in his Mantuan years.

title: Temptations of Christ
description: A fresco from the south wall of the Sistine Chapel staging all three temptations of Christ around a centrally placed temple based on Rome's Hospital of Santo Spirito. Botticelli folds the gospel narrative into a contemporary Roman setting alive with allegorical figures and Medici allusions.

title: The Holy Family
description: The Virgin in a red gown holds the Christ Child while Joseph, holding a bundle of straw, stands behind her alongside an ox and donkey in a stable interior. This painting, attributed to Martin Schongauer or his circle, is in the collection of the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna. A wicker basket sits in the foreground of the intimate, devotional scene.

title: Pallas and the Centaur
description: Botticelli pairs Pallas Athena, dressed in a gown embroidered with interlocking rings and olive branches and holding a long halberd, with a subdued centaur whose hair she grasps. The tempera allegory, painted around 1482, is read as reason mastering brute instinct, and the olive-and-diamond-ring motifs on her garment connect the figure to Medici humanist symbolism. The work belongs to Botticelli's mature Florentine period and remains one of the most discussed mythological allegories of the Renaissance.

title: Venus and Mars
description: Venus, dressed and alert, watches Mars sleep so deeply that the infant satyrs playing with his lance, helmet, and cuirass cannot rouse him — one even blows a conch shell in his ear. Love disarms war: the long horizontal panel was almost certainly a spalliera, a painted backboard for furniture in a Florentine bedchamber, and the wasps buzzing by Mars's head may pun on the Vespucci family, Botticelli's neighbors and likely patrons. Painted around 1483, the panel is now in the National Gallery, London.
credit: National Gallery, UK

title: Madonna Bardi
description: The enthroned Virgin prepares to nurse the Christ Child, flanked by Saint John the Baptist at left and Saint John the Evangelist at right, set against a lush garden bower dense with lilies and palms. Known as the Madonna Bardi, the panel was painted by Botticelli between 1484 and 1485 and is held in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin. The figures' linear refinement and the symbol-laden botanical setting are hallmarks of Botticelli's mature altarpiece manner.

title: The Birth of Venus
description: The newborn goddess arrives at Cyprus on a scallop shell, blown ashore by Zephyr while a Hora prepares to robe her. Painted on canvas for a Medici villa and indebted to the antique Venus Pudica, the image fuses Neoplatonic philosophy with Botticelli's hallmark linear grace.
credit: Adjusted levels from File:Sandro Botticelli - La nascita di Venere - Google Art Project.jpg , originally from Google Art Project. Compression Photoshop level 9.

provenance.location: Uffizi Gallery - Room 11-12, Botticelli's, Florence, Italy

title: Cestello Annunciation
description: Gabriel kneels before a swaying Virgin whose body bends in a pronounced S-curve, the two figures separated by an opening onto a Tuscan landscape. Botticelli painted the panel for the Cestello convent in Florence between 1489 and 1490; the bold red-and-white tiled floor grounds the composition in his late, austere manner.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"b/botticel/22/81cestel"

title: 1280px-Vittore Carpaccio - Hunting on the Lagoon
englishTitle: Hunting on the Lagoon (recto); Letter Rack (verso)
description: Hunters draw bows at waterbirds from flat-bottomed boats on the still Venetian lagoon, rendered with the crystalline detail typical of Carpaccio's narrative cycles. The panel was originally the upper portion of a larger work: its lower half is the Two Venetian Ladies in the Museo Correr, and the lily at the bottom edge once continued into a vase beside the seated women. Oil on panel, about 1490–1495, J. Paul Getty Museum; the verso carries a trompe-l'oeil letter rack.

title: Coronation of the Virgin
description: A predella scene from the San Marco altarpiece, showing John the Evangelist receiving his vision on the rocky island of Patmos. The miniature format allowed Botticelli's workshop to compress dramatic landscape and visionary light into a narrow horizontal panel.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"b/botticel/8smarco/21predel"

title: Lamentation over the Dead Christ with Saints
description: The dead Christ is supported across the Virgin's lap as Mary Magdalene clasps his feet and saints crowd the dark mouth of the tomb. Botticelli's late Lamentations, painted in the wake of Savonarola's preaching, abandon courtly sweetness for compressed, anguished figures.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"b/botticel/91late/01lament"

title: Madonna and Child with Saints John the Baptist and Elizabeth
description: The Virgin holds the Christ Child in a half-length sacra conversazione, flanked by a long-haired John the Baptist on the left and an elderly Elizabeth on the right, set against a luminous blue sky. Signed 'IOANNES BELLINUS', the panel dates from between 1490 and 1500 and is held at the Städel Museum in Frankfurt.
credit: Städel; ArtDaily.org

title: Portrait of a man
description: A clean-shaven man in a dark cap and tunic faces slightly left against a pale ground, depicted in the bust-length format Bellini favoured for Venetian portrait subjects. The painting, dated between 1490 and 1495, bears the inscription 'IOANNES BELLINUS' on the lower frame and is sometimes identified as a self-portrait by Giovanni Bellini.
credit: Régi könyvből digitalizálva

title: The Deposition
artist: Follower of Rogier van der Weyden
description: A close adaptation of Rogier van der Weyden's celebrated Descent from the Cross, with the limp body of Christ lowered amid a tightly grouped frieze of mourners. The sharp Netherlandish drawing, jewel-toned drapery, and shallow gilded space follow the prototype's compressed, sculptural staging.

title: The lamentation over the dead Christ
description: Christ's body is laid on a marble slab and seen in radical foreshortening from the soles of his pierced feet. Mantegna's hard, sculptural line and reduced palette turn the Lamentation into an exercise in perspectival shock.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"m/mantegna/2/dead_chr"

title: The Virgin and Child
description: The Virgin stands before a landscape background, her blue mantle wrapping around the Christ Child, who reaches upward and meets her gaze. The panel, dated 1490, is in the collection of the Fogg Museum at Harvard Art Museums. Botticelli's characteristic linear contours and pale tonality place the work within the Florentine devotional tradition of the late Quattrocento.
credit: Harvard Art Museums

title: Dormition of the Virgin
description: The Virgin lies on her deathbed surrounded by the apostles, one holding a taper, another reading aloud from a book, Christ receiving her soul above. The panel of 1491 to 1492 is part of a Marian altarpiece from the Augsburg workshop of the elder Holbein, father of the better-known portraitist.

title: Eichhörnchen
description: A watercolour and gouache study of two red squirrels rendered with near-zoological precision, each tuft of fur picked out in fine brush. The sheet belongs to Dürer's lifelong investigation of nature, alongside his hare and great piece of turf.
credit: Albertina, Vienna (?)

title: Portrait of a Man
description: A bust-length study of a weathered older man, painted with the linear precision and severe modelling for which the Cortona master was celebrated. Signorelli's interest in anatomical truth, sharpened by his fresco cycles at Orvieto, surfaces in every furrow of the sitter's face.

title: The Virgin and Child Enthroned
description: The Virgin sits on a gilt Gothic throne holding the Christ Child, who clasps a book, while two angel musicians flank them at ground level and two more hover above in adoration. Painted between 1493 and 1497, the panel exemplifies the refined Flemish devotional mode Quinten Metsys established as Antwerp's leading master.

title: Prodigal Son amid the swine
description: Dürer's celebrated early engraving sets the parable in a meticulously observed German farmyard, the kneeling youth surrounded by snouting pigs and timber outbuildings. The print, made soon after his first Italian journey, fuses Northern realism with new Renaissance ideas of psychological inwardness.
credit: Rijksmuseum

title: The Ship of Fools
description: A surviving fragment of a dismembered triptych depicting passengers crammed into a small boat, drinking, singing, and grasping at food while their craft drifts aimlessly. Bosch borrows the late-medieval Narrenschiff allegory to lampoon clerical vice, populating the scene with a lute-strumming nun and a tonsured friar.
credit: http://www.hetnoordbrabantsmuseum.nl/english/press-jheronimus-bosch/persbeelden-eng/ Previously: www.arthistory.cc : Home : Info : Pic

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Académie de femme debout
description: A pen study of a standing female nude seen from behind, holding a staff from which a veil falls. Made during Dürer's first Italian journey, the sheet shows him grappling with classical proportion and the contrapposto idealised by his Venetian contemporaries.

title: Beweinung Christi
description: A late Lamentation showing the dead Christ across the Virgin's knees, ringed by mourners in a steeply compressed group. Botticelli's tightly knotted figures and stark grief reflect the religious severity that gripped Florence in the Savonarola years.

title: View of the Arco Valley
description: A topographical watercolour of the Arco valley in the southern Tyrol, made during Dürer's return journey from his first Italian trip. The fortified hilltop town, terraced vineyards, and outcrops of rock are observed with surveyor's precision, an early instance of independent landscape study in Northern art.
credit: photo Shonagon 2021-02-11

provenance.collection: Department of Prints and Drawings of the Louvre

title: Autumn Landscape
description: An autumn landscape built from firm contours and axe-cut texture strokes, a temple compound rising beyond rocky bluffs while a lone sail crosses the water at left. Sesshū studied Ming Chinese ink painting at first hand during his 1467-69 journey to China; this work, dated 1496, is in the Tokyo National Museum.
credit: Emuseum Original uploader was ToraryuKawabata at en.wikipedia

title: Bath House
description: An early woodcut of six men relaxing around a Nuremberg bathhouse pump, several modelled on Dürer's friends and possibly himself. The crowded composition lets him show male anatomy from multiple angles in a vernacular setting.

title: Calumny of Apelles
description: Botticelli reconstructs a lost painting by the Greek master Apelles as described by Lucian: King Midas with ass's ears is approached by Slander, dragged forward by a sinister train of Envy, Deceit and Conspiracy, while naked Truth points to the heavens. The panel is a humanist defense of innocence against false accusation.

title: dürer seven headed dragon
englishTitle: The Apocalyptic Woman and the Seven-Headed Dragon
description: A dramatic woodcut from Albrecht Dürer's Apocalypse series depicting the vision described in the Book of Revelation - a woman clothed in sunlight and standing on the moon confronted by a seven-headed dragon. This masterwork from 1497-1498 exemplifies Dürer's technical mastery of the woodcut medium and his ability to capture apocalyptic grandeur through intricate line work and bold composition.

title: The Flagellation
description: Christ stands bound to a tall column in a vaulted hall while a crowd of tormentors presses in from every side, scourges raised; a small dog at the foot of the column underlines the casual cruelty of the scene. The woodcut belongs to Dürer's Large Passion, the ambitious series he began around 1496-97 and published as a book in 1511. The dense, swarming composition shows the young Dürer pushing the woodcut toward an expressive power the medium had never carried before.

title: dürer dragon fight
description: Saint Michael Fighting the Dragon is a celebrated woodcut from Albrecht Dürer's Apocalypse series, created in 1498. The composition depicts the archangel Michael vanquishing a demonic dragon below, rendered with Dürer's characteristic precision and dramatic intensity. This iconic image exemplifies Northern Renaissance printmaking and has become one of the most recognizable representations of the saint in Western art.

title: dürer selbstportrait
description: One of Albrecht Dürer's most iconic self-portraits, created in 1498 when the artist was 26 years old. The oil-on-panel painting is held in the Prado Museum in Madrid and exemplifies the Northern Renaissance tradition of artist self-portraiture, with the inscription "Das macht Ich nach meiner gestalt" ("I made this according to my features").

title: dürer vier reiter
englishTitle: The Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse
description: Albrecht Dürer's masterwork engraving from his Apocalypse series, depicting the four horsemen riding forth as described in the Book of Revelation. Created in 1498 using copper plate engraving, this print exemplifies Northern Renaissance technique and remains among the most iconic interpretations of the biblical subject in Western art history.

title: Self-Portrait
description: Painted shortly after his first Italian journey, the twenty-six-year-old Dürer presents himself as a gentleman scholar in tasselled cap and silk-trimmed jacket rather than a craftsman. The Alpine landscape glimpsed through the window signals his new cosmopolitan ambitions for the German artist.
credit: Museo Nacional del Prado, Galería online

title: The Four Horsemen
description: The four horsemen of the Apocalypse ride down humanity in the most celebrated woodcut from Durer's Apocalypse series of 1498, illustrating the vision of Revelation 6. This impression is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Christ Blessing
description: Christ is shown half-length, raising his right hand in blessing and holding a long staff in the other, a landscape with buildings and a cloudy sky opening behind him. The oil-on-panel painting, dated around 1500, is in the Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth and exemplifies Bellini's late preference for isolated devotional figures set against an evocative outdoor background.

title: Death and the Miser
description: The right wing of the dismantled Wayfarer triptych, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. A dying man hesitates between an angel at his pillow and a demon offering a sack of gold, while Death enters at the door — a memento mori rendered with the artist's cool, lapidary palette.
credit: Noordbrabantsmuseum

title: Hans Holbein dÄ und Werkstatt Hl Thekla
artist: Hans Holbein the Elder and workshop
description: A seated woman is shown from behind, her head wrapped in a cloth and her body enveloped in heavy drapery that pools at the base of the chair. The drawing, produced circa 1500 in the workshop of Hans Holbein the Elder, is a preparatory study for the figure of Saint Thecla in the Basilica panel for San Paolo fuori le Mura, now in the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen, Augsburg.

title: The Tree Man
description: A drawing of the hollow tree-bodied figure that recurs in the right wing of the Garden of Earthly Delights, his cracked eggshell torso supported on legs that end in tiny boats. Long attributed to Bosch's own hand, the sheet is among the few surviving drawings linked to him.
credit: www.jeroenbosch-artcenter.nl : Home : Info : Pic

title: The Trees have Ears and the Field has Eyes
description: A pen drawing illustrating the Flemish proverb that walls and woods betray secrets, with eyes scattered through the meadow and ears sprouting on tree trunks. The sheet, in the Berlin Kupferstichkabinett, is among the few autograph drawings linking Bosch's moralising imagination to his painted demonology.

title: Wing of a European Roller
description: A watercolor and gouache study of a severed roller's wing, its ultramarine, turquoise, and rust feathers laid out with near-scientific precision. The sheet exemplifies Dürer's habit of treating natural specimens as objects of sustained, meditative observation.

title: Young Hare
description: A young hare crouches alert against a blank ground, its fur built up in fine watercolour and bodycolour strokes that distinguish guard hairs from softer underfur. Among the most exacting nature studies of the Northern Renaissance, the sheet even records the cross-barred reflection of a studio window in the animal's eye.

title: =Madonna and Child between St. Francis and St. Nicasius
englishTitle: The Castelfranco Madonna (Madonna and Child between St. Francis and St. Nicasius)
description: A sacra conversazione altarpiece commissioned for the chapel of Tuzio Costanzo in Castelfranco Veneto, with the enthroned Virgin lifted high above SS. Francis and Nicasius. Giorgione's softly fused light and twilight landscape behind the parapet anticipate the lyrical mood of Venetian painting to come.

title: Christ on the cross with Mary and John
description: The Virgin and Saint John mourn beneath the crucified Christ in a windswept landscape that owes much to the young Cranach's time in Vienna. The agitated drapery and emotional pitch place the panel at the heart of the early Danube School.

provenance.location: Alte Pinakothek, upper floor, gallery II

title: Mona Lisa
description: A Florentine woman, traditionally identified as Lisa Gherardini, sits before an imaginary mountain landscape with a winding road and a distant bridge. Oil on poplar, begun around 1503 and reworked over more than a decade, the panel was acquired by Francis I and has hung in the Louvre since the French Revolution.
credit: Cropped and relevelled from File:Mona Lisa, by Leonardo da Vinci, from C2RMF.jpg . Originally C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition : image page

title: The Large Piece of Turf
description: A watercolour and gouache study of a clump of meadow plants, dandelions and grasses, viewed at ground level with botanical exactitude. The work is a touchstone of Renaissance nature study and prefigures modern ecological imagery.

title: The Mocking of Christ
description: A crowd of figures mock and beat a bound Christ, pressing around him in a compact, turbulent mass rendered in a shallow pictorial space. The Mocking of Christ was painted between 1503 and 1505 and is one of Grünewald's earliest surviving works, prefiguring the expressive violence of the Isenheim Altarpiece.

title: The Tempest
description: A nursing woman sits on the right bank of a stream while a young man with a staff watches from the left, a thunderstorm breaking over the small walled city behind them. Painted in oil on canvas around 1505 and listed in Marcantonio Michiel's notes of 1530, the picture entered the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice in 1932.

title: Adam and Eve
description: Dürer's celebrated copperplate engraving applies the canon of human proportion he had absorbed from Jacopo de' Barbari in Nuremberg. Adam and Eve flank the Tree of Knowledge amid a forest stocked with elk, ox, rabbit, and cat — emblems of the four humours soon to be unbalanced by the Fall.
credit: themorgan.org

title: Hieronymous Bosch The Last Judgement
description: A monumental triptych depicting the Day of Judgment, with divine judgment of humanity set against a complex landscape of heaven, earth, and damnation. Executed in oil on panel, this iconic work by Hieronymus Bosch synthesizes medieval eschatological imagery with his characteristically imaginative grotesque details, now housed in Vienna's Academy of Fine Arts.

title: Judith with the Head of Holophernes
description: Judith stands in a pink and red dress beside a balustrade, a long sword in her right hand, her bare left foot resting on the severed head of Holofernes below her. Painted around 1504 and now in the State Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg, the work was originally on panel and later transferred to canvas; it is one of the most securely attributed works in Giorgione's small surviving oeuvre.
credit: Livre de Stefano G. Casu, Elena Franchi et Andrea Franci : Les Grands Maîtres de la peinture européenne , Paris : Hazan, 2003. ISBN 2850259063

title: Adoration of the Shepherds
description: Two shepherds kneel before the Christ Child at the mouth of a dark cave, Mary and Joseph adoring beside them, a pastoral landscape opening to the left. The Allendale Nativity, painted around 1505 to 1510 and now in the National Gallery of Art in Washington, is among the most secure attributions to Giorgione.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Madonna and Child
description: The Virgin in a red dress and green mantle holds the Christ Child against a low Umbrian horizon, with distant buildings and a tower visible at the right. Known as the Small Cowper Madonna for its nineteenth-century English owner, this panel of around 1505 is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: pintura.aut.org

title: Three Philosophers
description: Three robed men stand at the entrance of a rocky outcrop, the youngest seated with a compass and tablet, the older two conferring behind, a sunlit valley falling away to the right. The Three Philosophers, painted around 1508 for the Venetian collector Taddeo Contarini, hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.
credit: Kunsthistorisches Museum Wien, Bilddatenbank; gallerix.ru

title: Triptych of Temptation of St Anthony
description: The desert hermit Anthony is besieged by a phantasmagoria of hybrid demons, burning villages and blasphemous rites across three panels now in Lisbon. Bosch's most influential triptych, it codified the visual vocabulary of grotesque temptation that fed Bruegel and the later Surrealists alike.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"b/bosch/90anthon/1triptyc"

title: Col tempo by Giorgione
description: An elderly woman behind a parapet turns toward the viewer with her mouth half open, holding a small slip inscribed 'Col tempo,' so it goes with time. Painted on canvas around 1506, the work is one of the earliest unflinching portrayals of old age in Italian painting; it hangs in its original frame at the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice.

title: Saint George and the Dragon
description: Saint George on a white horse drives his lance into the dragon while the rescued princess kneels in prayer at the right. Painted around 1506 as a diplomatic gift from Guidobaldo da Montefeltro to Henry VII of England, the small panel is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Young Woman
description: A young woman in a fur-trimmed red mantle turns to the viewer with one breast bared against a sprig of laurel, the leaves giving the panel its traditional title. Inscribed on the reverse with the date 1 June 1506, the picture is the earliest dated work by Giorgione and hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.

title: Adam and Eve
description: Two life-size oil panels showing the first humans isolated against black grounds, Dürer's first attempt to model nudes in the Italian manner after his second Venice trip. Each figure is treated as a study in idealized anatomy, paired across the diptych held by the Prado.
credit: Galería online del Museo del Prado de Madrid: Adán y Eva

title: Praying Hands
description: A brush study in white and grey on blue prepared paper, drawn as a detail for an apostle in the Heller Altarpiece. The folded hands have since detached from their context to become one of the most reproduced devotional images in Western art.

title: Self-portrait as David
description: A young man in armour, long dark hair framing a pensive face turned slightly aside, emerges from a deep shadow in this work attributed to Giorgione and titled Self-portrait as David. The panel, dated circa 1508–1510, is held at the Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum in Braunschweig and has long been identified through Vasari's account of the painter's self-portraits.
credit: Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum, Braunschweig

title: Sleeping Venus
description: A nude Venus reclines along a hillside, eyes closed, her body echoing the gentle curves of the landscape. Begun by Giorgione and finished after his death by Titian, who is thought to have added the drapery and setting, the picture launched the long line of reclining Venuses culminating in the Urbino Venus.

title: Adam and Eve in Paradise
description: An early treatment of the Fall by the Wittenberg court painter, set within a paradise teeming with stags, lions, and small game. Cranach's slender, mannerist nudes and crisp linear drawing reflect his proximity to Luther's circle, where the subject carried fresh theological weight.
credit: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco

title: Escola de Atenas - Vaticano 2
description: Painted for Pope Julius II's private library in the Stanza della Segnatura, this fresco assembles the philosophers of antiquity beneath a vast coffered vault, with Plato and Aristotle striding through the central arch. Raphael's lucid one-point perspective and idealised figures became a touchstone of High Renaissance harmony.

title: Giorgione-BildnisGiovanniBorgherini.ud.TrifoneGabriele.1509-10.BSTGS7452
englishTitle: Portrait of Giovanni Borgherini and Trifone Gabriele
description: The young Giovanni Borgherini faces the viewer from the left, holding a book or tablet, while the older Trifone Gabriele, draped in a fur-lined blue and red mantle, turns to address the space behind him. The double portrait on canvas, dated 1509 to 1510, is held by the Bavarian State Painting Collections in Munich and is traditionally attributed to Giorgione, though an attribution to the young Titian has also been advanced.

title: Katharina Schwarz mit den Attributen ihrer Namensheiligen
description: Katharina Schwarz of Augsburg stands holding the attributes of her name-saint Catherine of Alexandria, the broken wheel and the sword at her side. Painted around 1509 to 1510 as a donor portrait, the panel is among the late works of Hans Holbein the Elder before his move to Issenheim and Lucerne.

title: Le Concert champêtre
description: A Venetian poesia of two clothed gentlemen and two nude female figures, attended by music, in a pastoral landscape. Begun by Giorgione and likely completed by the young Titian, the picture established the lyrical pastoral genre that would echo through Manet's Déjeuner sur l'herbe.

title: The School of Athens
description: Ancient philosophers, mathematicians and scientists gather under coffered Roman barrel vaults, with Plato and Aristotle striding forward at the vanishing point. Painted between 1509 and 1511 for the Stanza della Segnatura in the Vatican, the fresco includes Raphael's own face beside Ptolemy in the lower right group.

title: Bellini — Madonna and Child 1510
description: Giovanni Bellini's Madonna and Child of around 1510 presents the Virgin in a blue mantle and rose dress, the infant Christ seated on her lap raising his right hand in a gesture of blessing, set before an open landscape with trees, hills, and scattered buildings. The intimate frontal composition and luminous palette reflect Bellini's late Venetian manner.

title: Madonna under the fir tree
description: The Virgin cradles the Christ Child against a landscape backdrop dominated by a dark fir tree, a German woodland motif that replaces Italian landscape conventions with Saxon scenery. Cranach's panel, dated 1510, balances tender intimacy against the spiky verticals of conifer needles, a hallmark of his court style at Wittenberg. A castle and mountain range recede into the distance behind the figures, giving the devotional image a characteristically Northern Renaissance sense of place.
credit: www.culture.pl

title: Pastoral Concert
description: Two clothed musicians and two nude women sit in a wooded clearing near Venice, a shepherd driving his flock past in the middle distance. Long attributed to Giorgione, the Pastoral Concert is now generally given to the young Titian and entered the French royal collection by 1671 before passing to the Louvre.

title: Portrait of a Venetian Gentleman
description: A young Venetian man is shown in three-quarter view, with short dark hair and a slight beard, holding an object such as a ring or coin and resting his arm on a ledge beside a book; a cityscape is visible through a window behind him. Dated between circa 1510 and 1515, the portrait belongs to Titian's early period and is held in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: The Alba Madonna
description: In this tondo of around 1510, the Virgin sits in an open Italian landscape, supporting the Christ Child who holds a slender cross while the young Baptist looks on from the left. The Alba Madonna is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: The Expulsion from Paradise
description: A small woodcut from Dürer's Small Passion series, dated 1510 in the block, showing a sword-wielding angel driving the naked Adam and Eve out of Eden beneath the trees of Paradise. Densely cut parallel hatching gives the bodies sculptural weight at this modest scale. This impression is held by the National Gallery of Art.
credit: National Gallery of Art .

title: The Martyrdom of Saint Barbara
description: Saint Barbara kneels as her own father raises the sword, the executioner's act that, according to legend, struck him down with lightning. The early panel shows Cranach still close to the dramatic, expressive line of the Danube School.

title: Altaarstuk van het schrijnwerkerambacht
description: The altarpiece of the Antwerp joiners' guild, with the Lamentation at centre flanked by wing scenes of the martyrdoms of John the Baptist and John the Evangelist. Completed by Quinten Metsys in 1511 for the cathedral of Our Lady, the triptych is now held by the Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp under inventory numbers 245-248.
credit: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

title: Ambrosius Holbein and Hans Holbein
description: Two boys share a single sheet drawn from life by their father: Ambrosius (left) and the young Hans Holbein the Elder's son, later Hans Holbein the Younger (right), with their names inscribed above each head. Executed in silverpoint on white-coated paper, 10.3 × 15.5 cm (1511), the study is preserved in the Kupferstichkabinett of the Berlin State Museums.
credit: Stephanie Buck, Hans Holbein , Cologne: Könemann, 1999, ISBN 3829025831 .

title: Creación de Adán
description: One of the most iconic frescoes in the history of Western art, painted by Michelangelo on the Sistine Chapel ceiling in Vatican City. This scene depicts God breathing life into Adam, the first human, and is celebrated for its masterful depiction of human anatomy and the moment of divine creation. The work remains among the most recognized and studied paintings in existence.

title: Michelangelo libyan
description: A red-chalk preparatory study for the Libyan Sibyl on the Sistine Chapel ceiling, drawn from a male studio model whose torsion and shoulder muscles Michelangelo refined toward the finished figure. Detail studies of the toes and a turning head fill the sheet, now held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
credit: www.wga.hu

title: Portrait of Pope Julius II
description: The aged della Rovere pope is seated in three-quarter view, beard untrimmed in mourning for the loss of Bologna, hands resting on the arms of his chair. Raphael's psychologically piercing portrait introduced a new informal type that would dominate papal imagery for over a century.

title: Separation of the Earth from the Waters
description: God the Father, robed in pink and surrounded by attendant figures, extends both arms sideways in a commanding gesture of separation, his bearded face turned toward the viewer. The fresco is one of the smaller central Genesis panels on the Sistine Chapel ceiling, painted by Michelangelo in 1511 as part of the sequence completed when the scaffold reached the altar end of the chapel.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"m/michelan/3sistina/1genesis/7earth/07_2ce7f"

title: The Creation of Adam
description: A fresco at the centre of the Sistine Chapel ceiling, in which God reaches across the void to a languid Adam. Michelangelo compresses the moment of ensoulment into the famously unmet gap between the two extended fingers.

title: The Small Crucifixion
description: Christ hangs on a T-shaped cross against a deep teal sky, his contorted figure framed by the grieving Virgin and a kneeling Magdalene on his left, and the upright John the Evangelist on his right. Painted on panel between about 1511 and 1520, the Small Crucifixion is among Grünewald's most concentrated expressions of sacred suffering and is now held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: The Massacre of the Innocents
description: Herod's soldiers, rendered as muscular nudes, seize infants from their screaming mothers in a paved square before a bridge, the violence choreographed across the sheet like a frieze. The engraving was cut by Marcantonio Raimondi around 1512-13 after a design Raphael made expressly for the print — the tablet at left reads 'RAPH URBI INVEN' — and their partnership became the chief channel through which Raphael's compositions spread across Europe. It ranks among the most celebrated engravings of the Italian Renaissance.

title: A Grotesque old woman
description: An elderly woman in a horned headdress and low-cut Burgundian bodice gazes from the frame, her features caricatured in a spirit of satirical grotesque. Painted around 1513 by Quinten Metsys and now in the National Gallery, London, the panel is traditionally identified as a pendant to a portrait of an old man and became the source for John Tenniel's Ugly Duchess in his illustrations to Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
credit: National Gallery, London

title: Liefdespaar
description: A pair of lovers sits in a wooded grove, the nude man turning toward the woman beside him. The plate is one of the engravings published after Parmigianino's drawings, the Mannerist designs that carried his eccentric grace north into the print culture of sixteenth-century Europe.

title: Barbara Dürer
description: A charcoal portrait of the artist's mother drawn weeks before her death, capturing her gaunt cheekbones and sunken eye in unsparing detail. Dürer's inscription records her age and condition, turning the sheet into a private memorial as much as a likeness.

title: Fire in the Borgo
description: A fresco in the Vatican's Stanza dell'Incendio del Borgo, depicting the miraculous extinguishing of a fire in Rome's Borgo district by Pope Leo IV. Heroic nudes and a fleeing Aeneas-like figure carrying his father give the scene a deliberately classical cast.

title: Melencolia I
description: An engraving from Dürer's so-called Master Prints in which a winged figure broods amid scattered tools of geometry, a polyhedron, and a magic square. The image has been read as an emblem of artistic genius stalled by melancholic temperament.

title: Portrait of Baldassare Castiglione
description: Raphael portrays his friend, the courtier and author of The Book of the Courtier, in a restrained palette of grey, black, and pearly white. The composed three-quarter pose and steady gaze became a touchstone for European court portraiture, admired and copied by Rembrandt and Rubens.
credit: Photographed by Elsa Lambert of C2RMF on 2010-06-23, retouched from File:Balthazar Castiglione, by Raffaello Sanzio, from C2RMF.jpg , originally C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition : image page

title: The Feast of the Gods
description: Olympian gods picnic in a wooded clearing while Priapus reaches under the sleeping nymph Lotis at right, a satyr filling cups from a wine bowl. Signed by Giovanni Bellini in 1514 for Alfonso d'Este's camerino in Ferrara, the landscape background was overpainted by Titian around 1529 and the picture is now at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: The Moneylender and his Wife
description: A money changer weighs gold coins on a precision balance while his wife, distracted from a book of hours, turns to watch. Signed and dated 1514, the Louvre panel adapts Jan van Eyck's convex mirror motif on the table edge, reflecting a window and a small figure reading outside.

title: Young Man Carrying an Old Man on His Back
description: A red-chalk drawing of Aeneas carrying Anchises from burning Troy, made as a study for the figure group in the Fire in the Borgo fresco. The athletic torsion and confident hatching show Raphael's response to antique sculpture and to Michelangelo.

title: Albrecht Dürer Druckplatte Christus am Ölberg
englishTitle: Christ on the Mount of Olives (Printing Plate)
description: The only surviving printing plate from Dürer's hand, preserved in the Bamberg State Library. It bears his 1515 composition of Christ praying on the Mount of Olives, an angel appearing above while the disciples sleep in the foreground.
credit: staatsbibliothek-bamberg.de

title: Bindo Altoviti
description: A portrait of the young Florentine banker Bindo Altoviti, who turns over his shoulder to meet the viewer's gaze. The cool palette, soft modeling, and elegant turn of the head exemplify Raphael's late Roman portrait style.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Landscape with Saint Jerome
description: Patinir places the penitent Saint Jerome amid a sweeping panoramic landscape of crags, rivers, and distant towns. The Flemish painter is credited with elevating landscape to a primary subject in Western art, the figure dwarfed by the world he renounces.
credit: Museo del Prado, online collection

title: Raimondi Lucretia's suicide
description: An engraving after a design by Raphael showing the Roman matron Lucretia about to plunge a dagger into her breast. Raimondi's burin work helped establish reproductive printmaking as a vehicle for disseminating Italian Renaissance invention across Europe.

title: St Jerome in the Desert
description: The hermit saint bends in his makeshift wilderness shelter amid the craggy stratified landscape that is Patinir's hallmark, with a vast river valley and distant town dissolving into atmospheric blue behind him. Patinir uses the eremitic subject to display his trademark world-landscape, in which the human figure of penitence is dwarfed by enormous geological formations. Held in the Department of Paintings of the Louvre (RF 2429), the panel dates from between circa 1515 and 1520.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"p/patenier/s_jerome"; GalleriX

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: The Hay Wagon
dateCreated: circa 1515 Prado from 1510 until 1516 Jheronimus Bosch - Visions of genius
description: The central panel of a triptych in the Prado, drawn from the Flemish proverb that the world is a haystack from which each takes what he can. Crowds claw at a giant cart of hay drawn by demons toward hell, Bosch's signature grotesques staging human greed with miniaturist precision.
credit: Museo Nacional del Prado

title: The Judgment of Paris
description: The shepherd Paris hands the golden apple to Venus while river gods recline at the foreground edge. Known chiefly through Marcantonio Raimondi's engraving after Raphael's lost design, the composition shaped European depictions of the nude for centuries.
credit: Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (A 85.1), 24 January 2006

title: The Miraculous Draft of Fishes
description: A cartoon for the Sistine Chapel tapestry series commissioned by Pope Leo X, showing Christ blessing Peter and Andrew as their nets break under the weight of fish. The kneeling apostle and the cranes on the shore are among the most studied figures in Renaissance art.

title: Self-portrait
description: Hans Holbein the Elder draws his own face in middle age, a long flowing beard framing his features, his gaze directed upward and to the side. Inscribed and dated 1516, this silverpoint sheet is among the last self-portraits by the Augsburg master before his final years in Isenheim and Lucerne.

title: Transfiguration
description: Christ rises in light between Moses and Elijah above the apostles on Mount Tabor, while in the lower zone the disciples fail to heal a possessed boy. Commissioned in 1516 by Cardinal Giulio de' Medici for Narbonne Cathedral, Raphael was still completing the panel when he died in 1520 and it now belongs to the Vatican Pinacoteca.
credit: Downloaded from Artist Hideout

title: A Prince of Saxony
description: A young Saxon prince is shown half-length against a flat black ground, his golden hair crowned with a delicate jewelled garland and his pale features set above a richly jewelled collar and brown fur-trimmed cloak over red brocade sleeves. The portrait, held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, exemplifies the dynastic likenesses Cranach produced for the Saxon court around 1517.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Correggio
description: A three-quarter-length portrait of a seated woman in a dark overmantle and white chemise, holding a small dish, set before an open landscape. The work is signed with the Latinised "Anton(ius) Laet(us)" and has traditionally been identified as either Veronica Gambara or Ginevra Rangoni. Painted between 1517 and 1518, it is held at the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg and represents Correggio's early mature manner.

title: Death and the Maiden Baldung
description: A tempera painting on limewood by German Renaissance artist Hans Baldung Grien, depicting the allegorical encounter between personified Death and a young maiden. The work exemplifies the Northern Renaissance fascination with the danse macabre theme, exploring mortality and youthful vitality through an intimate compositional arrangement.

title: La Fornarina by Raffaello
description: Long identified as the baker's daughter Margherita Luti, Raphael's lover, the sitter wears an oriental turban and a slim arm-band inscribed with the painter's name. The picture, completed near the end of Raphael's life, has the tactile sfumato modelling and direct erotic charge of his late Roman period.

title: Portrait of a Man
description: A clean-shaven man in a black cap and dark cloak fills a narrow panel, the modelling concentrated in the smooth planes of cheek and brow. Painted between 1518 and 1520, the portrait is held by the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid and shows the Augsburg branch of the Holbein workshop in its last years.
credit: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid

title: Rest during the Flight to Egypt
description: Mary is seated in a sunlit meadow nursing the Christ child while Joseph stands in the middle ground with the donkey, the Holy Family embedded in a sweeping Patinir world-landscape of green hills, rivers, and pale blue rock formations. The devotional subject serves as a vehicle for expansive landscape invention, layering warm foreground greens against cool rocky distances. Oil on panel, c. 1518–1520; Museo del Prado, Madrid (inv. P001611).
credit: Museo del Prado

title: Self-portrait with a friend
description: Raphael places himself behind a foregrounded companion who turns to point outward, the two men linked by a cascade of hands and gazes. The double portrait is among the late, most psychologically intricate works produced in his Roman studio.
credit: Retouched from File:Portrait de l'artiste avec un ami, by Raffaello Sanzio, from C2RMF retouched.jpg , originally C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition : image page

title: Bad-war
description: Swiss pikemen and German Landsknechts press into the murderous close-quarters combat known as der schlimme Krieg, where the long pike shafts become unmanageable and halberds and short swords decide the outcome. This engraving by Hans Holbein the Younger, preserved in the Albertina in Vienna, is among the most visceral early sixteenth-century images of infantry battle.
credit: Albertina online

title: Crossing the River Styx
description: Charon ferries a soul across the underworld river, with paradise and a fiery hell flanking the panel in classic Netherlandish duality. Patinir, credited as the first dedicated landscape painter, expands the mythological subject into a panoramic geography of cliffs, water and atmospheric distance.
credit: Museo Nacional del Prado

title: Kenkō Shōkei - Shōshō Hakkei - Enji Banshō
englishTitle: Enji Banshō (from Eight Views of Xiaoxiang)
description: Ink-painting from the Zen monk-painter's interpretation of the Eight Views of Xiao and Xiang, the canonical Chinese landscape suite of distant temples, mist and migrating geese. Shōkei trained in Kamakura under Geiami and brought a flecked, slightly nervous brush to the Muromachi suiboku tradition.

title: Landscape with the Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
description: Patinir fills nearly the entire sky and middle distance with the lurid orange glow of burning Sodom and Gomorrah, while pale rock formations rise at right and tiny figures — Lot and his companions guided by angels — appear at lower right. The work treats the Old Testament catastrophe as a panoramic landscape spectacle, with smouldering cities silhouetted against the inflamed horizon. Oil on panel, c. 1520; formerly Hermann Göring Collection.
credit: collectie.boijmans.nl : Home : Info : Pic

title: Portrait of a Woman
description: A woman in a dark gown and broad white linen headdress gazes past the viewer from behind a painted arch with marbled columns, one ringed hand holding open a small prayer book at the lower edge. Painted around 1520, the portrait is characteristic of the sober likenesses Quinten Metsys produced for burgher patrons in Antwerp.
credit: https://www.flickr.com/photos/unforth/2346337090/ , https://www.flickr.com/photos/unforth/ Taken on 12 March 2008

title: The temptations of St. Antony Abbot
description: Three demonic women in courtly dress press around the hermit Anthony at the lower edge while a vast world-landscape of rocks, rivers and burning towns recedes behind them. A documented collaboration: Quinten Metsys painted the figures and Joachim Patinir the panorama. The Prado panel carries inventory number P 1615.

title: Head of an Old Man
description: A brush drawing heightened with white on prepared paper, recording a bearded man of ninety-three whom Dürer met in Antwerp during his Netherlandish journey. The head served as a study for his 1521 painting of Saint Jerome, and the sheet is held by the Albertina in Vienna.

title: Saint Christopher Facing Left
description: A small copper engraving by Albrecht Dürer showing Saint Christopher wading through the river with the Christ Child on his shoulders, bracing himself on his staff as he strides to the left. Dürer engraved two versions of the subject in 1521, distinguished by the direction the saint faces. This impression, measuring only about twelve by seven centimeters, is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, which received it in the bequest of Julie Parsons Redmond.

title: 1522 Holbein d.Ä. Angehöriger der Augsburger Familie Weiss anagoria
description: Half-length portrait of a clean-shaven young man in a broad black hat and patterned damask robe, identified as a member of the Weiss family of Augsburg. He holds a sprig of red carnations and an inscribed metal object before a dark foliate ground. Hans Holbein the Elder painted the portrait in 1522, two years before his death.

title: Head of a Woman
description: A young woman's head and bust, her hair worn loose in braided plaits and falling to her shoulders, is depicted with fine chalk on paper. Dated 1522, the drawing is an early study from Holbein the Younger's Basel years, before his departure for England and the Tudor court portraits that would define his later practice.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"h/holbein/hans_y/2drawing/1530/06headwo"

title: Landscape with St. Christopher
description: Saint Christopher wades across a wide river bearing the Christ Child on his shoulder, dwarfed by a panoramic landscape of jagged rocks, distant towns and luminous water. The sweeping high viewpoint is characteristic of Patinir, often credited as the first specialist in Western landscape painting.
credit: Escorial, Real Monasterio de San Lorenzo; pinturaycomunicacion.blogspot.de

title: Coat of Arms of Albrecht Dürer
Head of Saint John the Baptist
description: A young man's face is rendered in chalk on paper, his gaze directed forward and his curly hair loosely framing his features. The drawing, attributed to Andrea del Sarto and dated to around 1523, is now in the collection of the National Gallery of Art, Washington, and exemplifies his sensitive handling of line and tone in preparatory work.

title: Pietà with Saints
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"a/andrea/sarto/2/pieta"

title: Tauberbischofsheim altarpiece
description: Christ hangs on a T-shaped cross against a near-black ground, flanked by the Virgin on the left and John the Evangelist on the right in attitudes of grief and supplication. Painted between 1523 and 1524 for the parish church of Tauberbischofsheim, the panel is one of Grünewald's last known works and is now in the Staatliche Kunsthalle, Karlsruhe.

title: Head of an Old Man
description: An elderly bearded man in a plain, coarse garment turns in three-quarter view, his deeply furrowed brow and creased skin recorded with close physiognomic attention. Painted around 1525, the panel belongs to Metsys's late interest in expressive character heads, paralleling his more overtly grotesque caricature studies.

title: Portrait of Federico II Gonzaga
description: Federico II Gonzaga, Marquis of Mantua, is shown half-length against a dark ground wearing a richly embroidered dark blue velvet doublet with gold decoration, one hand resting on a small white dog that looks up at him. Painted circa 1525, the work is held in the Museo del Prado, Madrid, and is among Titian's most celebrated court portraits.
credit: Museo del Prado

title: Adam and Eve
description: The first parents stand on either side of the apple tree, slim and pale against a forest dense with deer, lions and stags. Cranach made the Fall a workshop staple, prized by Lutheran patrons as a meditation on sin made flesh.
credit: Courtauld Institute of Art

title: Cupid Complaining to Venus
description: A naked Venus wears only a wide-brimmed hat and gold chain while a small Cupid, stung by bees, complains of the honey he has stolen. Cranach often paired the subject with a Latin epigram warning that pleasure is mixed with pain.
credit: Web Gallery of Art; nevsepic.com.ua

title: Danse Macabre. I. The Creation
description: The opening plate of Holbein's Dance of Death, designed in Basel in the 1520s, shows the Creation that frames the cycle's moral argument. Cut by Hans Lützelburger from Holbein's miniature designs, the series compresses scriptural and social satire into woodblocks scarcely larger than a thumbprint.

title: Darmstadt Madonna
description: The Virgin stands on a shell-headed niche above the kneeling family of Burgomaster Jakob Meyer zum Hasen, the Christ Child raising a small hand in blessing. Commissioned in 1526 from Holbein the Younger during his first Basel residency, the panel is now in the Johanniterkirche in Schwäbisch Hall after a long sojourn at Schloss Darmstadt.

title: Portrait of Hieronymus Holzschuher
description: Hieronymus Holzschuher, Nuremberg patrician and city councillor, is rendered in near-forensic detail: flowing white curling hair, a full beard, and a fur-trimmed cloak. Painted in 1526 and now in the Gemäldegalerie Berlin (inv. 557E), the portrait stands as one of Dürer's most penetrating late character studies, fixing the sitter's frank gaze with an intensity the artist had refined over three decades of observing individual faces.
credit: Online catalogue of Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

title: Portrait of Sir Thomas More
description: Sir Thomas More sits in a black gown with brown fur trim and crimson velvet undersleeves, the Collar of Esses hanging at his chest and a paper held in one hand. Painted in 1527 during Holbein's first London stay, the portrait is now in the Frick Collection, New York.

title: Portrait of a Man
description: Half-length portrait of an ecclesiastic in dark robes, his hand resting on a closed volume. Vasari identifies the sitter as a Canon of Pisa Cathedral and close friend of the painter, credited with helping Andrea secure his final commissions before his death in 1530.

title: Portrait of the painters' wife and their two oldest children
dateCreated: between 1528 and 1529 / between circa 1528 and circa 1529
description: Elsbeth Binzenstock, Holbein's wife, sits with their children Philipp and Katharina, her face worn and watchful. Painted shortly after Holbein's 1528 return to Basel from his first English sojourn, the picture is identified through the Amerbach inventory of 1587 and now hangs in the Kunstmuseum Basel.
credit: kunstmuseumbasel

title: Self-portrait
description: The Florentine painter regards the viewer with a sober, narrow-eyed gaze, his beard close-trimmed and his black cap drawn low. Painted in 1528 and now in the Uffizi, the panel belongs to the final years of Sarto's career, two years before his death from plague during the siege of Florence.

title: 1529 Cranach Allegorie auf Gesetz und Gnade anagoria
description: A programmatic Lutheran image divided down the middle: on the left, Death and the Devil drive a sinner toward Hell beneath the Tablets of the Law; on the right, John the Baptist directs the same figure to the crucified Christ. Cranach worked closely with Luther in Wittenberg, and this composition became a template for Reformation visual theology.

title: Schlacht bei Issus
englishTitle: The Battle of Alexander at Issus
description: Commissioned by Duke William IV of Bavaria, Altdorfer compresses Alexander's 333 BC victory over Darius III into thousands of tiny figures swarming under a cosmic sky. The Danube School master treats landscape and weather as protagonists, the curving horizon and apocalyptic sun lifting the battle into world-historical drama.

title: Assumption of the Virgin
description: The Virgin ascends on a bank of clouds, hands clasped in prayer, as putti attend her on either side. Below stand four saints — including a warrior saint and a Franciscan friar — set against a rocky Italian landscape. Andrea del Sarto painted this altarpiece in 1530 for the church at Poppi in Tuscany; it is now in the Galleria Palatina at the Palazzo Pitti, Florence.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"a/andrea/sarto/3/virgin"

title: Ca' Rezzonico - Matrimonio mistico di Santa Caterina
description: The Christ Child, seated on the Virgin's lap, reaches toward Saint Catherine in the traditional gesture of the Mystic Marriage, while an elderly bearded male figure — likely Saint Joseph — attends on the right. The panel is attributed to the Bolognese painter Biagio Pupini, called Dalle Lame, and dated circa 1530–1540; it is held at the Ca' Rezzonico in Venice under inventory number 236. The Raphaelesque grace of the figures reflects the influence of the Roman manner on Bolognese painting of the period.

title: Judith with the head of Holofernes
description: The Hebrew widow displays the severed head of the Assyrian general she has just decapitated to save her city, set against Cranach's signature inky black ground. Pearled jewels and a slashed velvet bodice betray the panel's origin as a courtly Saxon trophy rather than a devotional image.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"c/cranach/lucas_e/06/2judith2"

title: Lucas Cranach d.Ä. - Herkules und Atlas
englishTitle: Hercules Relieving Atlas of the Globe
description: In this pen-and-wash drawing of 1530, Hercules bears the great celestial globe aloft while the freed Atlas stands to one side in a broadly sketched landscape — the eleventh labour rendered in Cranach's assured draughtsmanship. The sheet, held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, illustrates the Renaissance enthusiasm for Antique mythology and offers a rare glimpse of Cranach's working method outside the painted panel.

title: Moses and the Pillar of Cloud
description: Moses leads the Israelites through the wilderness beneath the divine pillar of cloud described in Exodus 13. A workshop production from the busy Cranach studio, the panel keeps the master's compact figure types and bright, decorative landscape.
credit: M.S. Rau, New Orleans; Stockholms Auktionsverk, Stockholm, 7 December 2021, Lot 345 via auctionet

title: The Golden Age
description: Naked figures dance in a ring beneath fruit trees in the mythical age of innocence described by Hesiod and Ovid. Cranach turns the classical theme into a playful, decorative idyll suited to the humanist tastes of the Saxon court.
credit: Nasjonalgalleriet, Presse, aktuelle Utstillinger i Oslo

title: Portrait of the Elector John Frederic the Magnanimous of Saxony
