description: Johann Friedrich, the Lutheran champion who would lose his electorate after the battle of Mühlberg, shown here in jewelled chain and flat black cap. Cranach was court painter at Wittenberg for half a century and produced numerous variants of this loyal Reformation portrait.
credit: This file was derived from: Lucas Cranach d. Ä. 044.jpg :

title: Leda and the Swan
description: An erotic mythology painted for Federico II Gonzaga of Mantua as part of a series of Loves of Jupiter intended as a gift to Charles V. Correggio orchestrates Leda's encounter in soft chiaroscuro and a continuous lateral rhythm of figures, the smoky modelling that would inspire Parmigianino and the Carracci.

title: Portrait of Margaret à Barow
description: Margaret à Barow, wife of the humanist Sir Thomas Elyot, faces right in a gabled hood, drawn in coloured chalks strongly reinforced with Indian ink around the head and headgear. Holbein made the study around 1532 alongside one of her husband, as preparation for matching painted portraits now lost, both sheets preserved in the Royal Collection at Windsor. The drawings are unusually well preserved, retaining white chalk heightening on the nose and forehead.
credit: Royal Collection

title: The Merchant Georg Gisze
description: The Hanseatic merchant Georg Gisze stands in his London counting-house among a glass vase of carnations, scales, a table clock, a quill, signet rings, and letters precisely arranged on the carpet-covered table. Painted in 1532 for the German Steelyard community on the Thames, the panel is now in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

title: Adam and Eve in paradise
englishTitle: Adam and Eve in Paradise (Gemäldegalerie Berlin, 1531)
description: Adam reaches for the apple Eve has plucked while the serpent watches from the branches above, the trees of paradise teeming with creatures. The panel is among Cranach's most fully developed treatments of the subject, painted for the Lutheran market that prized its theological clarity.

provenance.location: German painting from the 13th to 16th centuries, room III

title: The Ambassadors
description: Jean de Dinteville, French ambassador to Henry VIII, stands beside Georges de Selve, Bishop of Lavaur, with a globe, lute, Lutheran hymnal, and astronomical instruments on a shelf strewn between them. Across the foreground lies a famous anamorphic skull, decipherable only from an oblique angle, painted in 1533 and now in the National Gallery, London.

title: Charles de Solier
description: Charles de Solier, Sieur de Morette, French ambassador to the English court, stands three-quarter length in a dark fur-trimmed coat, his hand resting on a sword hilt. Holbein painted the panel around 1534 during the sitter's Tudor mission; it entered the Saxon collections in the seventeenth century and now hangs in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.

title: Madonna and Child with Angels
englishTitle: The Madonna with the Long Neck
description: Known as the Madonna of the Long Neck, this unfinished altarpiece is a touchstone of Italian Mannerism. Parmigianino elongates the Virgin's anatomy and tilts the spatial logic of the column and miniature prophet for an unsettling, refined elegance.

title: Madonna mit dem langen Hals
description: A refined female bust by Parmigianino, likely a detail fragment, shows a young woman with downcast eyes, pearled headband, and elongated neck, rendered in the cool, polished manner that defines his Mannerist style. The figure's delicately idealised features and translucent drapery are characteristic of Parmigianino's work of the 1530s. The painting is associated with the title Madonna mit dem langen Hals in the record.

title: The Last Judgment
description: Christ presides at the centre of a roiling vortex of saints, the resurrected, and the damned dragged toward Charon's boat, the entire altar wall of the Sistine Chapel given to a single muscular composition. Commissioned by Pope Paul III and painted in fresco between 1536 and 1541, the work was later partly draped by Daniele da Volterra under the censorship of the Council of Trent.
credit: derivated work from

title: Caritas
description: The personification of Christian charity sits nude, nursing one infant at her breast while holding a second child against her shoulder and a third rests at her feet — the traditional three-child emblem of the virtue. Cranach reduced the iconography to slender contours and a verdant garden setting, producing the composition in several small-scale variants between circa 1537 and 1540; this panel is held at the Royal Museum of Fine Arts, Antwerp.
credit: Lukas - Art in Flanders

provenance.collection: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp
provenance.location: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

title: Justice
description: Justice personified as a nude woman holding sword and scales, a humanist subject Cranach's Wittenberg workshop produced in many versions for Saxon patrons. The sinuous body type and dark ground are signatures of his late mythological and allegorical nudes.

title: Portrait of Henry VIII
description: Henry VIII is shown in three-quarter view, wearing an embroidered doublet with jewelled gold chains and a black cap trimmed with white feathers, his broad shoulders and steady gaze projecting regal authority. Painted around 1537 in a type derived from Holbein the Younger's lost Whitehall mural, workshop versions such as this one disseminated the canonical royal image across Europe.

title: Edward VI as a Child
description: Holbein portrays Edward Tudor, the future Edward VI, as an infant in a red velvet cap and gold-embroidered dress, his right hand raised in a gesture borrowed from adult royal portraiture. A Latin inscription below urges the boy to equal and surpass his father Henry VIII. The panel was likely presented to the king as a New Year's gift in 1539 and now hangs in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Reclining Venus
description: Ingres's exact-size copy of Titian's Venus of Urbino (1538), made during his Florentine years of 1820–1824 when he had access to the original at the Pitti Palace. The canvas was intended to serve as a model for his close friend, the sculptor Lorenzo Bartolini, who was working on a sculpture of the same subject. It is now in the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore (inv. 37.2392).
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Hasegawa Tohaku - Pine Trees
englishTitle: Pine Trees (Shōrin-zu byōbu) - right hand screen
description: The right wing of the celebrated Pine Trees screens, designated a National Treasure of Japan. Tōhaku, founder of the Hasegawa school, paints the pines with rapid sumi ink in pale wash and dry brush, leaving vast areas of unpainted paper to suggest swirling mist — a high point of Momoyama monochrome ink.

title: Portrait of Anne of Cleves
description: Anne of Cleves is shown frontally in a richly embroidered red and gold gown with layered jewelled chains and a rounded bonnet-style cap, her hands clasped low before her. Holbein painted the small panel in 1539 during his mission to the Continent to assess the Duke of Cleves's sister as a potential bride for Henry VIII; the portrait is now in the Louvre.
credit: photo Shonagon 2024-03-15

title: Hunting near Hartenfels Castle
description: The Saxon court drives stags into the Elbe before the towers of Schloss Hartenfels, with the Elector and his guests stationed at crossbows along the bank. Cranach made several versions of this hunt, half topographical record and half dynastic propaganda.
credit: The AMICA Library; The Cleveland Museum of Art

title: Portrait of Henry VIII of England
description: Henry VIII appears half-length in a richly embroidered gold doublet with dark puffed sleeves set with jewels, a heavy jewelled collar across his broad shoulders. Dated 1540 and now in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica at Palazzo Barberini in Rome, the panel is among Holbein's autograph small-format Tudor portraits produced for diplomatic and courtly circulation.
credit: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica

title: Self-portrait
description: The painter shows himself in three-quarter view against a gold ground, bearded and cap-clad, his eyes shadowed. Drawn in coloured chalks around 1542, the sheet in the Uffizi was later enlarged and reworked, but enough of the original survives to confirm Holbein's hand in the last year of his life before his death from plague in London.
credit: Stephanie Buck, Hans Holbein , Cologne: Könemann, 1999, ISBN 3829025831 .

title: The Battle of Cascina
description: Florentine soldiers scramble naked from the Arno after a false Pisan alarm, twisting their bodies as they grab for arms on the bank. The composition survives only through Bastiano da Sangallo's 1542 grisaille copy at Holkham Hall, the lost cartoon Michelangelo prepared in 1504 for the Palazzo Vecchio having served as a school of anatomy for a generation of Florentine artists.
credit: scan of 1542 art

title: Anatomy
englishTitle: Muscle Man, from De humani corporis fabrica
description: An écorché muscle man from Vesalius's De humani corporis fabrica, standing upright with the superficial musculature of the trunk and limbs laid bare. Published in Basel in 1543 by Johannes Oporinus, the woodcut plates of the Fabrica set a new standard for anatomical illustration by uniting empirical dissection with the figure conventions of Renaissance art. This plate is held in the Bijzondere Collectie of the Universiteit van Amsterdam.
credit: Bijzondere collectie Universiteit van Amsterdam

title: De humani corporis fabrica
englishTitle: On the Fabric of the Human Body, Plate 24
description: A muscleman écorché stands in a Paduan landscape, layers of musculature peeled back to reveal underlying anatomy. The plate, cut for Vesalius' 1543 treatise, was carved in the Titian workshop circle and revolutionised medical illustration by binding observation to a humanist visual language.
credit: Bijzondere collectie Universiteit van Amsterdam

title: De humani corporis fabrica
englishTitle: On the Fabric of the Human Body, Plate 25
description: Another of the Fabrica's flayed figures, posed against a continuous Veneto skyline that links the seven plates into a single panorama when arranged in sequence. Vesalius insisted on direct dissection, and the woodcut renders the layered musculature with unprecedented anatomical accuracy.
credit: Bijzondere collectie Universiteit van Amsterdam

title: De humani corporis fabrica
englishTitle: On the Fabric of the Human Body, Plate 26
description: A deeper écorché stage from the Fabrica, with skin and superficial muscle stripped away to expose the trunk and limbs. Printed in Basel by Oporinus, the plates set a new standard for the integration of artistic skill and dissection-based medical knowledge.
credit: Bijzondere collectie Universiteit van Amsterdam

title: The venous and arterial system of the human body. Engraving
description: The venous and arterial system of the human body. Engraving by J. Wandelaar, 1726, after a woodcut, 1543.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/74/2e/0ac8113e668180f3691fd8145046.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/V0007816EL.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-04-05): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/tkbvmyhw CC-BY-4.0

title: Man in a Black Cap
description: An unknown sitter in a flat black cap and fur-collared dark coat, turned three-quarters to the viewer, inscribed with his age and the date 1545. The panel — signed on the reverse 'faict par Johan Bettes Anglois' — is the only securely attributed work by Bettes, whose technique shows the influence of Hans Holbein the Younger; the background, originally painted in blue smalt, has since degraded to brown. The portrait is now in Tate Britain.
credit: Karen Hearn, Dynasties: Painting in Tudor and Jacobean England, 1530–1630 , London: Tate, 1995, ISBN 1854371576 .

title: Lucas Cranach - Der Jungbrunnen
description: Aged women are carried into a stone basin on the left and emerge as nubile young brides on the right, an allegory of rejuvenation popular at the Saxon court. Cranach unfolds the fantasy across a panoramic landscape with the crisp outlines and porcelain flesh tones of his Wittenberg workshop.

provenance.location: German painting from the 13th to 16th centuries, room III

title: Equestrian Portrait of Charles V
description: Titian's monumental equestrian portrait shows Charles V in gilded armour, lance couched, astride a black charger caparisoned in crimson and gold — painted in Augsburg in 1548 to commemorate the Habsburg victory at the Battle of Mühlberg. The image defined the template of sovereign equestrian portraiture that Velázquez and Van Dyck would later inherit. The work has been in the Museo del Prado, Madrid, since the seventeenth century.
credit: The Prado in Google Earth: Home - 7 th level of zoom, JPEG compression quality: Photoshop 10.

title: The Conversion of Mary Magdalene
description: An early devotional canvas in which Christ raises the kneeling Magdalene from her former life. Veronese's Venetian instinct for sumptuous fabric, architectural staging, and silvery light is already evident in this youthful composition.
credit: National Gallery

title: Google Art Project
description: Groups of elegantly dressed figures gather beneath flame-red maples and beside a stream bridged by a stone arch, in a composition that spans the full width of a six-panel folding screen. Snow-capped ground in the upper left panel and flying cranes signal the transition of seasons across the composition. Attributed to Kanō Hideyori and dated to the sixteenth century, it is one of the earliest surviving Japanese genre paintings and is held at the Tokyo National Museum.

title: St Christopher Bearing the Christ Child
description: The giant ferryman wades a river bearing the Christ Child on his shoulder, the saint's labor dwarfed by Patinir's signature world-landscape stretching to a hazy blue horizon. The Antwerp master pioneered this compositional formula in which figures recede before vast geological panoramas.
credit: Rockox House, Antwerp

title: Susanna and the Elders
description: The chaste Susanna recoils as two elders intrude on her bath, the biblical pretext for a study of startled flesh against shaded foliage. Carracci stages the assault with the firm contour and idealised anatomy he was simultaneously developing for the Farnese ceiling.

title: The Fall of Man
description: Adam and Eve beneath the Tree of Knowledge, the serpent rendered as a child clutching the fatal fruit. Titian gives the Genesis subject a sculptural, classicizing weight, drawing on Northern prototypes filtered through Venetian colorism.
credit: Museo del Prado, Madrid

title: Venus and organist and little dog
description: Venus reclines nude on a draped bed, her small dog beside her, while an organist turns from his keyboard to gaze at her body. Part of a series Titian produced for European courts, the composition stages a debate between sight and sound as competing routes to the experience of beauty.

title: Juno Showering Gifts on Venetia
description: A ceiling allegory painted for the Doge's Palace, in which Juno rains crowns, jewels, and ducal regalia onto a personified Venice. Veronese exploits the di sotto in sù viewpoint to send the goddess plunging through illusory clouds.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/v/veronese/08/dieci/3dieci"

title: Venus and Adonis
description: Venus, seen from behind, twists to embrace the youthful hunter Adonis as he pulls away with his hounds towards the hunt that will kill him. One of the mythological poesie made for Philip II of Spain, the canvas exemplifies Titian's late, freely brushed handling of flesh and landscape.

title: Venus with a Mirror
description: Venus is depicted partially nude, turning toward a mirror held by two cupids — one also raising a wreath or crown above her head — while red drapery frames the composition behind her. Painted around 1555, the canvas is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, and represents the prime version of a composition Titian repeated across several decades for European patrons.

title: Diana and Callisto
description: One of Titian's mythological poesie made for Philip II of Spain, depicting Diana's discovery of the pregnant nymph Callisto among her bathing companions. Diagonal drapery, a marbled fountain and richly varied flesh tones articulate the moment of accusation.
credit: National Gallery, London - online catalogue .

title: Pieter Bruegel d. Ä. 066
englishTitle: The Fight Between Carnival and Lent
description: A teeming village square stages an allegorical joust between a barrel-riding Carnival, armed with a spit of meat, and a gaunt Lent on a church cart. Bruegel packs the panel with proverbs, Shrovetide revels, and Lenten almsgiving in a panoramic moral inventory of Netherlandish life.

title: Danaë
description: Danaë reclines nude on her bed as Jupiter descends as a shower of gold, while an old nursemaid stretches up an apron to catch the falling coins. Among Titian's poesie for the Spanish court, the scene contrasts youthful flesh and wizened greed in loose, atmospheric paint.
credit: Official gallery link Enlace a la galería oficial

title: Landscape with the Fall of Icarus
description: A ploughman, shepherd, and angler go about their work along a sunlit harbor while Icarus's legs vanish almost unnoticed into the sea at lower right. The composition reads as a quiet meditation on Ovid's myth and human indifference, later memorialized in Auden's poem.

provenance.collection: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

title: The Rape of Europa
description: A late poesia for Philip II showing the Phoenician princess carried across the sea on the back of Jupiter disguised as a bull. Loose, atmospheric handling and a glowing pink-gold sky transform the abduction into a turbulent seascape.

title: Marriage at Cana
description: A crowded banquet hall, coffered ceiling hung with chandeliers, frames the wedding feast at Cana, with Christ visible among the assembled guests and servants filling water jars in the foreground. Tintoretto animates the scene with strong diagonals, dramatic lighting, and a press of richly dressed figures. Dated 1561 and catalogued by the Web Gallery of Art, this canvas belongs to Tintoretto's intense Mannerist engagement with large-scale narrative subjects.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"t/tintoret/3_1560s/2cana"

title: De triomf van de Doods The Triumph of Death
description: Death triumphs over the world: a vast army of skeletons drives the living of every estate into a great coffin, the landscape behind reduced to ruin. Pieter Bruegel the Elder's panel of c. 1562 fuses the medieval danse macabre with the panoramic worldview that would carry into seventeenth-century Flemish painting.
credit: Museo del Prado

title: Libararian
description: Arcimboldo's composite portrait assembles a human bust entirely from stacked and open books: an open volume with fanned pages forms the top of the head, volumes of varying sizes build the face and torso, and loose bookmarks suggest beard and fingers. Painted in 1562 and now at Skokloster Castle, Sweden, the panel is traditionally identified as a satirical likeness of the Habsburg court scholar Wolfgang Lazius, made for the court of Maximilian II.

title: Self-Portrait
description: A late self-portrait of the Venetian master, shown in three-quarter profile with brush in hand and the gold chain of imperial favor across his black robe. The looser handling and reserved gaze typify Titian's introspective final decade.
credit: Museo Nacional del Prado online

title: Allegory of Winter
description: From Arcimboldo's Four Seasons cycle painted for the Habsburg court, Winter is a gnarled tree-stump head with bark for skin, ivy for hair and a lemon and orange hanging from broken branches. The conceit flattered the emperor as the season that endures and rules over all others.

title: Maximilian II
description: Emperor Maximilian II stands with his consort Maria of Austria and their children Anna, Rudolf, and the infant Ernst in a cradle, dressed in mid-century Spanish court fashion. Painted around 1563 after a model from 1553-54, the dynastic group is preserved in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
credit: Kunsthistorisches Museum Wien, Bilddatenbank .

title: Pieter Bruegel der Ältere - Landschaft mit der Flucht nach Ägypten
englishTitle: Landscape with the Flight into Egypt
description: The Holy Family threads a precipitous mountain path while a vast world landscape opens beneath them, with rivers, cliffs, and a shadowed pagan idol toppling on a column. Bruegel's panoramic Weltlandschaft tradition dwarfs the sacred travelers within Alpine and Flemish topographies.

title: The Summer
description: A profile head built from peaches, cherries, plums, ears of wheat, a cucumber nose, and an artichoke breastplate, the collar inscribed with the artist's name and the date. Painted in 1563 as part of the first Four Seasons cycle for Maximilian II, the panel is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

title: The Tower of Babel
description: King Nimrod inspects stonemasons in the foreground as the colossal tower rises above a Flemish port, its arcades modeled on the Colosseum. The painting marries Genesis with a sober warning about overreaching ambition, rendered with engineering exactitude.
credit: Levels adjusted from File:Pieter_Bruegel_the_Elder_-_The_Tower_of_Babel_(Vienna)_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg , originally from Google Art Project.

title: Portrait of Quinten Massijs *
description: A bust-length profile engraving of the Antwerp painter Quentin Massys (Quintin Mesijs), identified by the Latin inscription below: QUINTINUS MESIUS ANVER PIANU[S] PICTOR. Johannes Wierix cut the plate, probably in the 1560s-1570s, as part of a series of artists' likenesses circulating in the late sixteenth century.
credit: Geheugen van Nederland : Info : Pic

title: Winter Landscape with a Bird Trap
description: Villagers skate and slide on a frozen river beside snow-covered houses, while at right a propped board baited with grain forms a trap for unwary birds. One of around a hundred surviving versions after Pieter Bruegel the Elder's composition, it pairs winter genre with a quiet emblem of human precariousness.
credit: Kunsthistorisches Museum Wien, Bilddatenbank .

title: 2560px-Pieter Bruegel the Elder - Hunters in the Snow
description: Returning hunters and their lean dogs trudge across a snowy ridge above frozen ponds where villagers skate, the panel that anchors Bruegel's celebrated cycle of the months commissioned by the Antwerp merchant Niclaes Jonghelinck. Now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna, it set the template for European winter landscape painting.

title: Allegory of Wisdom and Strength
description: Divine Wisdom, crowned and turned upward, stands beside a brawny Hercules whose attention is fixed on the worldly riches at his feet. The pairing, painted for the Habsburg court, sets celestial contemplation against earthly power in characteristic Venetian color.
credit: Frick Collection : online database: entry 277; Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"v/veronese/10/1allego3"

title: Massacre of the Innocents
description: Soldiers ransack a snowbound Flemish village in a transposition of Herod's biblical slaughter into the contemporary Low Countries under Spanish occupation. In the Royal Collection version many of the slain children were overpainted as bundles, geese, and game by later hands.

title: The Family of Darius before Alexander
description: The defeated Persian queen and her household kneel before Alexander the Great after Issus, in a vast frieze-like composition acquired by London's National Gallery in 1857. Veronese fills the picture with contemporary Venetian costume, courtly architecture, and a noble gesture of clemency.

title: Fire
description: Part of the Four Elements cycle painted for Maximilian II in Vienna, Fire builds a head from candles, oil lamps, flintlocks and burning kindling. Arcimboldo's witty composite portraits flatter the Habsburgs as masters of the elements while showcasing his Mannerist appetite for paradox.

title: The Air
description: Birds of every order roost on and form a human profile, one of four allegories of the elements painted for the Habsburg court. Arcimboldo's composite portraits flatter the encyclopaedic ambitions of Maximilian II while showing off the painter's natural-history library.
credit: Arcimboldo. 1526-1593. Ausstellungskatalog des Kunsthistorischen Museums Wien 2008, p. 147. ISBN 978-3-85497-118-4 , Scanned by uploader

title: The allegory of Water
description: A profile fashioned from fish, crustaceans, coral and pearls, completing the Vienna set of the four elements. Arcimboldo treats the composite as both witty courtly device and a serious display of zoological knowledge.
credit: Arcimboldo. 1526-1593. Ausstellungskatalog des Kunsthistorischen Museums Wien 2008, p. 1152. ISBN 978-3-85497-118-4

title: The Earth
description: A bust assembled from terrestrial mammals — stag, leopard, hare, sheep and many others — interlocks to form a human profile in Arcimboldo's allegorical conceit for Earth. Painted possibly in 1566, the composite portrait was part of a series on the four elements produced for the Habsburg court, in which the emperor's dominion is cast as a literal embodiment of the natural world.
credit: Arcimboldo. 1526-1593. Ausstellungskatalog des Kunsthistorischen Museums Wien 2008, p. 1152. ISBN 978-3-85497-118-4 , Scanned by uploader

title: The Ill-matched Pair
description: A satirical scene in which a young woman in an orange dress flatters an enamoured old man at a table set with gold coins, fruit, and bread, while a younger man smirks behind them and an old woman watches from a doorway. Jan Matsys treats an ill-matched-couple theme inherited from Flemish tradition with vigorous caricature and a warm, richly coloured palette. Dated 1566 and now held at the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.
credit: Nationalmuseum

title: The Lawyer
description: A pile of legal books and document rolls draped in a fur-trimmed gown, the face assembled from plucked poultry and small fish, possibly satirising the humanist jurist Ulrich Zasius. Painted in 1566 and now in the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm, the panel reads as a sly Habsburg court joke at the expense of paper-bound learning.
credit: Hans Thorwid / Nationalmuseum

title: Anbetung der Könige im Schnee
englishTitle: The Adoration of the Kings in the Snow
description: Bruegel sets the Adoration of the Magi inside a snowbound Flemish village, the Holy Family barely visible amid the crowd, woodcutters, and falling flakes. Painted in oil on wood in 1567, it is among the earliest winter scenes in Western painting and now belongs to the Oskar Reinhart Foundation in Winterthur.

title: Adoration of the Magi
description: The Magi present their gifts to the Virgin and Child before classical columns, a camel and horses crowding in at the left and a crown laid on the steps. An early work by El Greco of 1568-69, made shortly after the young painter left Crete for Italy, it is now in the Museo Soumaya, Mexico City.
credit: Museo Soumaya Plaza Carso

title: The building of the tower of Babel
description: The smaller of Bruegel's two surviving Babel panels shows the spiraling brick ziggurat looming over a coastal plain, swallowed by storm clouds at its summit. Painstaking architectural detail draws on Roman ruins Bruegel had studied in Italy.
credit: Levels adjusted from File:Pieter_Bruegel_the_Elder_-_The_Tower_of_Babel_(Vienna)_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg , originally from Google Art Project.

title: The Parable of the Blind Leading the Blind
description: A line of six blind men stumbles diagonally across the panel toward a ditch, each face individually studied for the disfigurements of disease. Bruegel illustrates Christ's parable from Matthew 15 with clinical precision and an unforgiving rhythm of falling bodies.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"b/bruegel/pieter_e/11/01parabl"

title: Christ at the Sea of Galilee
description: A Venetian rendering of the Gospel episode in which Christ appears to the disciples on a storm-tossed sea. The dramatic torsion of the figures, raking light and turbulent green-grey waves are characteristic of the Tintoretto workshop, though the attribution has been debated in favour of Lambert Sustris.

title: Christ Cleansing the Temple
description: Christ swings his cord of whips through the money-changers in a vaulted Renaissance temple, figures recoiling around him in pinks, blues, and acid greens. Painted probably before 1570 during El Greco's Venetian apprenticeship and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the panel is the earliest of his several versions of the subject.

title: Self Portrait
description: The painter looks out frontally in a black cap and dark doublet, presenting himself in straightforward likeness rather than as a composite. Drawn in the 1570s while in service to the Habsburg court in Prague, the sheet stands apart from his fruit-and-fish portraits as a record of how Arcimboldo wished to be remembered by his employers.

title: The Flaying of Marsyas
description: Apollo punishes the satyr Marsyas for his musical hubris, suspending him upside down to be skinned alive. Painted in the artist's final years, the canvas is built from open, almost dissolving brushwork that anticipates later European painting.
credit: Scanned from the book The Complete World of Greek Mythology , ISBN 0500251215 (orginal uploaded by en:User:BorgQueen as en:Image:The Flaying of Marsyas.jpg ); Bridgeman Art Library : Object 388734

title: Musée de Capodimonte - Le Gréco
description: The Croatian miniaturist Giulio Clovio holds open his illuminated Farnese Hours, gesturing toward a stormy landscape beyond a window. Painted around 1571-72 during El Greco's Roman years, the portrait now hangs in the Museo di Capodimonte, Naples, and records the friendship that helped the young Cretan secure Farnese patronage.

title: Feast in the House of Levi
description: A vast Venetian banquet is staged beneath a Palladian loggia of three grand arches, populated by guests of diverse social rank, servants, dwarves, dogs, and a falconer with a hawk at the right. Originally intended as a Last Supper for the refectory of Santi Giovanni e Paolo, the work was retitled after the Inquisition objected to its profane figures; it is now in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.
credit: This image has been extracted from another file

title: La Primavera
description: A profile bust composed entirely of spring blossoms, with a face of pink and white rose petals, a collar of small white flowers, and a torso of green leaves and flowering branches. Painted in 1573 as part of the Four Seasons series presented to Emperor Maximilian II, the panel exemplifies Arcimboldo's Mannerist conceit of building a human likeness entirely from natural produce.

title: Les saisons - L'automne
description: A male head built from the harvest, with a pear nose, apple cheeks, a pomegranate chin and a crown of grapes and vine leaves bound by a barrel-stave neck. Part of the Seasons series Arcimboldo painted for the Habsburg court in 1573, the version at the Louvre carries the imperial monogram tying the cycle to Emperor Maximilian II.
credit: Photographies prises au Louvre-Lens en 2025

title: The Waiter
description: A figure assembled entirely from cellar vessels: stacked wooden barrels form the torso, while earthenware jugs, cups, and smaller drinking vessels compose the head and face beneath a red beret-like hat. Painted in 1574, the image extends Arcimboldo's composite-portrait method from natural produce to the tools of the wine cellar.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"a/arcimbol/4composi/4waiter"

title: Perseus Freeing Andromeda
description: Andromeda, chained to the rock, twists toward the descending hero as Perseus swoops down on the sea monster with drawn sword. The picture's silvery palette and elongated figures, long debated between Veronese and his workshop circle, exemplify late-sixteenth-century Venetian narrative painting.

title: El Expolio
description: Christ in a vivid red robe stands hemmed in by jeering soldiers as a workman bores holes for the nails in the cross at his feet. Painted between 1577 and 1579 for the sacristy of Toledo Cathedral, El Greco's first major Spanish commission compresses the crowd into a vertical wall of heads behind the still, gazing figure.
credit: Pictorpedia

title: Madonna and Child
englishTitle: Madonna and Child with Saint Anne (after Rubens, Lady Margaret Hall)
description: The Virgin in red cradles the sleeping infant Christ on white drapery, while an elderly woman — Saint Anne — looks on from the upper left. The full English title recorded for this copy-after-Rubens work at Lady Margaret Hall is 'Madonna and Child with Saint Anne', and the three-figure grouping is central to the composition.

title: Man in a Ruff
description: A bust-length portrait of a man with moustache and pointed beard, wearing a large white ruff and a dark coat with a gold chain and pendant. The Colchester picture is an after-Rubens version, dated possibly c. 1650–1750, held in the Colchester and Ipswich Museums Service.

title: The Holy Tninity
description: God the Father supports the dead body of Christ while the dove of the Holy Spirit hovers above, attended by mourning angels. Painted between 1577 and 1579 for the high altar of Santo Domingo el Antiguo in Toledo, the composition draws directly on a Dürer engraving but elongates the figures in El Greco's emerging Mannerist idiom.

title: Tarquin and Lucretia
description: A late Mannerist treatment of the Roman legend in which Tarquin's assault on Lucretia precipitates the founding of the Republic. Tintoretto stages the violence with twisting bodies, broken pearls and torn drapery, the diagonal composition lit by sharp Venetian chiaroscuro.

title: The Nobleman with his Hand on his Chest
description: A bearded Castilian gentleman in black lays his right hand flat against his chest in a deliberate gesture, the gold hilt of his sword visible below. Painted around 1580 and now in the Prado, the portrait is often read as an oath of loyalty and is among the most reproduced images of the Spanish Golden Age.
credit: The Prado in Google Earth: Home -

title: Allegorische voorstelling van het werk en de vlijt
description: Print depicting an allegorical representation of work and diligence. Created by Hendrick Goltzius.
credit: Ghent University Library

title: Der Bohnenesser.jpeg
description: A celebrated painting by Annibale Carracci created between 1584 and 1585, exemplifying the artist's naturalistic approach to genre scenes. The work depicts a humble figure eating beans, rendered with the careful attention to everyday life that characterized Carracci's innovative departure from Mannerist convention. This painting is now in the public domain and represents an important moment in the development of modern European art.

title: Christ wearing the Crown of Thorns
description: An early devotional work from the Bolognese reformer of late-Mannerist painting, the composition tightens onto the suffering Christ as winged attendants steady his body. Carracci leans on the warm chiaroscuro and sculptural drapery he absorbed from Correggio and Venetian sources.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"c/carracci/annibale/1/thorns"

title: Lamentation over the Dead Christ
description: The body of Christ, still bearing his wound, is lowered by several figures in an animated, brightly coloured composition set against a pale sky, with the Virgin fainting at the lower right. Tintoretto organises the scene through compressed, overlapping figures and the turbulent energy typical of his late Venetian manner, painted around 1585–90. The large canvas is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.

title: Leda and the Swan
description: Veronese's late rendering of Jupiter's seduction of Leda shows the reclining nude against a richly draped background of deep crimson velvet, the white swan pressing close as she reclines on a cushioned couch. The work demonstrates the master's assured handling of the female figure and luxuriant textiles, characteristic of his mature Venetian style around 1585.

title: Horatius Cocles De Romeinse helden
englishTitle: Horatius Cocles, from The Roman Heroes
description: Horatius Cocles stands full-length at the centre, sword raised in his right hand and shield in his left, while the battle at the Tiber bridge plays out in the background. Goltzius engraved the plate in Haarlem in 1586 as the second of eight numbered hero subjects within a ten-print series titled The Roman Heroes. The work is in the collection of the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

title: The Burial of the Count of Orgaz
description: Saints Stephen and Augustine lower the armoured body of Don Gonzalo Ruiz de Toledo into his tomb while a celestial throng receives his soul above. Painted between 1586 and 1588 for the parish church of Santo Tomé in Toledo, where it still hangs over the count's actual grave, the canvas splits earthly funeral and heavenly vision across a single vertical axis.
credit: Unknown photographer Unknown photographer

title: Goltzius's right Hand
description: A virtuoso pen-and-ink study of the artist's own drawing hand, deformed since childhood by a burn. Goltzius turns the disability into a manifesto of skill, building the form from his signature swelling-and-tapering parallel hatchings copied across Europe.

title: The Fall of Ixion
description: Cornelis van Haarlem shows Ixion in extreme foreshortening, his muscular nude body tumbling headlong through flames into Tartarus, limbs splayed against a nearly black ground. The single-figure close-up, painted around 1588 and now at the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen in Rotterdam, demonstrates the Haarlem Mannerists' virtuoso command of contorted anatomy and dramatic chiaroscuro.

title: The Fall of the Titans
description: The defeated Titans tumble headlong from heaven, their nude bodies twisting around each other in a virtuoso lattice of foreshortening. Cornelis treats the mythological subject as an excuse for anatomical display, central to the late-sixteenth-century Haarlem Mannerism he developed with Goltzius and Van Mander.

title: Four Seasons in One Head
description: A grizzled head turned in profile, with a wrinkled tree-bark cheek, a cluster of cherries and grapes for the brow, withered leaves for the hair and a stump for the throat. Painted in his final Milanese years around 1590, Arcimboldo collapses the earlier Four Seasons cycle into a single allegorical face about aging and the passage of time.

title: River Landscape
description: A wooded river scene in which large trees fill the foreground and a narrow stream winds toward a distant valley and pale hills. A lone figure pauses by the water's edge, dwarfed by the dense canopy. Carracci painted this ideal landscape around 1590, helping establish the classical tradition later developed by Poussin and Claude; the canvas is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: A monk and a nun [ 3 ]
description: A monk and a beguine paired in earthy proximity, a stock anticlerical jab popular in late-sixteenth-century Dutch genre. Cornelis softens his Mannerist drawing for the satirical mode, fixing the figures in close focus against a plain dark ground.
credit: www.franshalsmuseum.nl : Home

title: Vertumnus årstidernas gud målad av Giuseppe Arcimboldo 1591 - Skoklosters slott - 91503
description: The Roman god of seasons assembled entirely from fruit, vegetables, grains and flowers, each species chosen to flatter Emperor Rudolf II as the bringer of perpetual abundance. The composite portrait is the most refined example of the painter's signature conceit, made for the Prague court.

title: Farnese Hercules
description: The colossal Farnese Hercules, leaning on his club with the apples of the Hesperides behind his back, observed from below by two awed connoisseurs. Goltzius' celebrated engraving exaggerates the antique's swelling musculature with his trademark swelling-and-tapering burin lines.

title: The Apostle Peter
description: A close head study of an aged, bearded man in strict profile, his white hair rendered with loose, fluent brushwork against a warm dark ground. The work belongs to Rubens's series of apostle heads and is held at the Statens Museum for Kunst, Copenhagen, where it is catalogued under the broad date range of 1592 to 1640.

title: The Emperor Commodus as Hercules
description: An engraving from Goltzius's Roman Heroes series, depicting the megalomaniac emperor in the lion-skin and club of Hercules. The muscular low-angle figure and virtuoso swelling burin lines exemplify the technical bravura of Northern Mannerist printmaking.
credit: Engravings collection

title: The Last Supper
description: Painted for the chancel of San Giorgio Maggiore in the last year of Tintoretto's life, the scene tilts the table on a sharp diagonal and dissolves the upper room in smoky angelic apparitions. It marks the radical conclusion of his Mannerist experiments with light and off-axis composition.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"t/tintoret/5_1580s/3lastsup"

title: Boy with a Basket of Fruit
description: An early Roman work made soon after Caravaggio entered the household of Cardinal del Monte, the youth offers a basket spilling with grapes, peaches, and figs. The naturalistic still life, with its bruised leaves and worm-eaten apples, helped found a new Italian tradition of painting fruit from life.

title: Francis of Assisi in Ecstasy
description: The saint swoons in the arms of an angel after receiving the stigmata, his companions sleeping in the moonlit landscape behind. One of Caravaggio's earliest religious nocturnes, the picture introduces the raking light and tender naturalism that would shape his mature style.

title: Portrait of an Old Man
description: A bald, white-bearded man in a white ruff collar and dark robe trimmed with fur turns toward the viewer, the lined face rendered with El Greco's characteristic psychological directness. Painted between 1595 and 1600, the portrait has traditionally been described as a presumed self-portrait, though the identification of the sitter remains uncertain.

title: The Great Floode
description: The Genesis flood overtakes humanity in Wtewael's 1595 canvas: contorted nude figures scramble up trees and rocky outcrops as the waters rise, the doomed crowding every ledge of the darkening landscape behind. The Utrecht Mannerist favoured such teeming figure compositions for biblical and Ovidian subjects; the painting is in the Germanisches Nationalmuseum, Nuremberg.

title: The Musicians
description: Four young musicians, one tuning a lute, prepare to perform in a tightly packed half-length composition. Commissioned by Cardinal Francesco Maria del Monte for his Roman household, the picture launched Caravaggio's career and introduced his trademark modelling of flesh against deep shadow.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art

title: The Lute Player
description: An early half-length picture from Caravaggio's years in the household of Cardinal del Monte, showing an androgynous youth absorbed in playing a lute. The still life of violin, recorder and open sheet music is rendered with the same forensic light that became the artist's signature, the figure pulled forward against a dark wall. Caravaggio treated the subject more than once: this version, with its red oriental carpet and spinet keyboard, was painted for Cardinal del Monte and is the canvas long exhibited at the Metropolitan Museum from the Wildenstein Collection. The closely related version in the Hermitage, made for the Marchese Vincenzo Giustiniani, sets flowers, fruit and a violin on a marble table in their place.
credit: Wildenstein Collection de:Image:1596 Caravaggio, The Lute Player Wildenstein Collection.jpg

title: View of Toledo
description: A spectral storm rolls over the Spanish hill city, with the Alcázar and cathedral picked out against acid-green hills and ink-black clouds. One of the earliest pure landscapes in Western art, El Greco rearranged Toledo's topography for symbolic, almost visionary effect.

title: Adam and Eve
description: Adam and Eve stand in a verdant Paradise in a dialogue that alludes to the Fall — Adam gestures toward Eve beside the Tree of Knowledge, an apple visible among the branches above. Painted between 1597 and 1600 and now in the Rubenshuis, Antwerp, this is among Rubens's earliest surviving figure compositions, reflecting the influence of his Flemish training before his Italian sojourn.
credit: www.aiwaz.net : Home : Info : Pic

title: Basket of Fruit
description: A wicker basket of grapes, figs, peaches and a withered apple sits at eye level on a bare ledge, projecting slightly into the viewer's space. Often cited as the first autonomous still life in Italian painting, the work is unsparing about wormholes and decay; its plain ground is a later overpaint.

title: Medusa
description: The Gorgon's severed head shrieks the instant of decapitation, her snakes still writhing. Painted on a convex tournament shield as a gift from Cardinal del Monte to the Grand Duke of Tuscany, the work conflates mirror, weapon, and self-portrait.

title: Narcissuss
description: The youth Narcissus leans over a dark pool, his lit shoulder mirrored by his reflected face. Caravaggio reduces the Ovidian myth to a single closed circle of body and image, with the harsh tenebrist contrast that defined early Baroque painting in Rome.

title: Nicolas Rubens
description: This painted portrait depicts Nicolas Rubens as a young man, shown in three-quarter view wearing a broad-brimmed black hat and dark coat with a white collar, his long wavy hair falling to his shoulders. The confident bearing and direct yet composed expression distinguish it from the intimate childhood studies Rubens made of his children. The work is held at the Art Institute of Chicago (inv. 1954.299).

title: Judith Beheading Holofernes
description: The Hebrew widow grips the Assyrian general's hair and saws through his neck while her aged maid waits with a sack. Caravaggio renders the ugly mechanics of beheading with forensic clarity, the spurting blood lit as starkly as the white sheets.

title: The Adoration of the Shepherds
description: Shepherds, animals, and attendant figures press in around the newborn Christ and the Madonna in a crowded scene set among crumbling brick ruins, with a fire illuminating the foreground and a goat prominent at right. Signed and dated 1598, the picture is a characteristic Utrecht Mannerist work by Wtewael, who specialised in large-scale scenes painted with intense colour and dynamic figure groupings.

title: Bust of Pseudo-Seneca
description: Rubens drew this gaunt, furrowed head from the famous Hellenistic bust then believed to portray the Stoic philosopher Seneca — an identification since abandoned, hence 'Pseudo-Seneca.' The sheet is worked in pen and brown ink over black chalk, heightened with white and gray wash, with the searching intensity Rubens reserved for his studies after antique sculpture. He owned a version of the bust himself and reused the head in paintings such as The Death of Seneca; the drawing is now in the Robert Lehman Collection at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: English: The Feast of Herod
description: Salome presents the head of John the Baptist on a salver as Herod recoils at the banquet table. Rubens stages the gruesome moment with theatrical lighting and a dense crush of guests, balancing horror against the gleam of silver and silk.

title: Portrait of a Cardinal
description: Cardinal Fernando Niño de Guevara sits in an ornate chair, his scarlet robes spread across the canvas against a gold-patterned tapestry backdrop, a pair of round spectacles resting on his nose. Painted around 1600 by El Greco, the portrait records the Grand Inquisitor of Spain and stands among the artist's most commanding ecclesiastical likenesses.

title: Portrait of the Artist's Son Jorge Manuel Theotokopoulos
description: A young man in a starched white ruff and dark doublet holds the brushes and palette of a painter, his gaze level and composed. Painted between 1600 and 1605, the portrait shows Jorge Manuel Theotocópuli, El Greco's son and workshop heir, who would later complete several of the master's late altarpieces in Toledo.

title: Sine Cerere et Libero friget Venus
description: The Terentian motto — without Ceres and Bacchus, Venus grows cold — is set as a chiaroscuro nocturne, the goddess illuminated by a torch held by a satyr. Goltzius, the virtuoso Haarlem engraver, here works with brush on prepared ground in his late painterly mode.

title: The Martyrdom of Saint Sebastian
description: Sebastian is bound to a tree in an outdoor wooded landscape, his arms raised above and his body twisting, as figures around him prepare or discharge arrows. A winged putto descends from the upper right. Signed and dated 1600, the panel exemplifies Wtewael's Utrecht Mannerism, with elongated nude forms, restless poses, and vivid contrasts of flesh and foliage.

title: Amor Vincet Omnia
description: A naturalistic Cupid in the Berlin Gemäldegalerie, who clambers grinning over scattered emblems of music, war, science, and rule. Caravaggio's tenebrist lighting and the boy's frank nudity made the picture notorious among Roman collectors.
credit: Cropped from [1]

title: Leda and the Swan
description: An early treatment of the myth from Rubens's Italian years, when his study of Michelangelo and Venetian colour was reshaping his approach to the sensual nude. The composition shows Leda reclining against a dark landscape as the swan presses close, its large dark wings contrasting with warm flesh tones in the kind of erotically charged mythology Rubens would refine for decades. The work, dated 1601, is now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"es-e.html?/html/r/rubens/index"

title: Mars and Venus Surprised by Vulcan
description: Vulcan drops his golden net over the naked lovers Mars and Venus in their bed while the Olympian gods crane down from the clouds to watch. Painted on copper in 1601, this Mauritshuis cabinet picture is one of several treatments Wtewael made of the Ovidian scene, prized in late Mannerist circles for its erotic-comic intricacy.

title: Portrait of Christina Wtewael van Halen
description: Christina van Halen, wife of the painter Joachim Wtewael, sits in a black gown with a wide millstone ruff, her right hand raised in a composed gesture beside a small table bearing jewellery. Signed and dated 1601, the panel is understood to be a pendant to Wtewael's own self-portrait of the same year, both associated with the Centraal Museum in Utrecht.

title: Self-portrait
description: The painter looks out in a white millstone ruff and black costume, holding his palette, brushes, and a maulstick as emblems of his craft. A coat of arms carved in relief is visible in the background. Signed and dated 1601, the panel is understood to be a pendant to the portrait of his wife Christina van Halen, both associated with the Centraal Museum in Utrecht.

title: The Incredulity of Saint Thomas
description: Christ guides the apostle's finger into the wound in his side as two other disciples crane forward to watch. Caravaggio collapses the moment into a tight, half-length composition lit from the upper left, the brows knit in shared concentration.

title: Jupiter and Juno Annibale Carracci fragment
englishTitle: Jupiter and Juno (fragment from the Farnese Ceiling)
description: A section of Annibale Carracci's fresco decoration of the Farnese Gallery in Rome, painted for Cardinal Odoardo Farnese and completed around 1602. The panel shows Juno, half-draped, coming to Jupiter on his couch, his eagle gripping a thunderbolt at the bedside and her peacock looking on; the scene is framed like an easel picture within an illusionistic surround of nude youths and feigned stone atlantes. The cycle of the Loves of the Gods made the gallery one of the founding monuments of Baroque ceiling painting.

title: Sacred and Profane Love
description: Baglione's allegory of Sacred and Profane Love, painted in 1602, sets a winged divine figure in armour above a reclining Eros who gazes upward in submission, while a crouching devil recoils at left. The composition directly rivals Caravaggio's treatment of the same subject and reflects the bitter professional rivalry between the two Roman painters in the early seventeenth century.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/b/baglione/sacred2"

title: The Deposition
description: The dead Christ is supported in the arms of a dark-robed figure — likely the Virgin — while two angels and Mary Magdalene attend in grief, the pale body dramatically lit against a storm-darkened sky. Painted in 1602 and held in the Galleria Borghese, this early Lamentation of Christ reflects Rubens's absorption of Italian models, particularly the lessons of Caravaggio and the Carracci encountered during his Roman years.

title: The Entombment of Christ
description: Christ's lifeless body is lowered onto the anointing stone, his arm and shroud dropping toward the viewer. Painted for the Chiesa Nuova in Rome, the altarpiece compresses the mourners into a powerful diagonal lit by Caravaggio's signature raking shaft.

title: The Taking of Christ
description: Judas presses forward to deliver his kiss as an armoured soldier seizes Christ's neck and a fleeing apostle howls behind. A self-portrait of the painter raising a lantern at the right edge introduces the artist into the violent nocturne.

title: Copy after the Battle of Anghiari by Leonardo da Vinci
description: Four mounted soldiers strain over the standard of Anghiari, mouths open and horses crashing teeth-to-teeth in the central fight. Drawn around 1603 after Leonardo's lost mural for the Palazzo della Signoria, the sheet is the most authoritative surviving record of the composition Vasari painted over around 1560.

title: Portrait of Jan Govertsz. van der Aer
description: Jan Govertsz. van der Aer, a Haarlem shell collector, is depicted seated and holding a large conch aloft, with further exotic shells arranged on the table beside him. Goltzius records both the penetrating directness of the sitter's gaze and the varied surfaces of his collection with equal precision in this 1603 painting, now in the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen.

title: The Fall of Phaeton
dateCreated: between circa 1604 and circa 1605 , probably reworked between circa 1606 and circa 1608
description: Phaeton plummets from the chariot of the Sun as Jupiter's thunderbolt scatters the bolting horses and the Hours recoil through the zodiac. An early mythological tour de force, the picture shows Rubens already pushing Mannerist motion toward Baroque theater.
credit: nga.gov National Gallery of Art, Washington D.C.

title: Vincenzo II. Gonzaga
description: A head-and-shoulders portrait of the young Vincenzo II Gonzaga, rendered with a large lace ruff collar and a richly embroidered golden doublet against a dark ground. Rubens painted the Mantuan duke around 1604 to 1605 during his years at the Gonzaga court, absorbing the courtly polish of his Italian models. The panel is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
credit: Kunsthistorisches Museum Wien, Bilddatenbank .

title: David with the Head of Goliath
description: The young David holds out the severed head of Goliath, in which Caravaggio is widely thought to have painted his own features. Made in his fugitive late period and probably sent to Cardinal Scipione Borghese as a plea for pardon, the canvas distils tenebrist drama into a single beam of light.

title: Saint Jerome
description: The aged Church Father bends over an open volume, his bald skull echoing the memento mori at his elbow. Painted in Rome for Cardinal Scipione Borghese, Caravaggio strips the scholar's cell to a few essentials so that flesh, parchment and shadow can do all the speaking.

title: The Golden Age
description: A crowded paradisal scene drawn from Ovid's Metamorphoses, with figures feasting, dancing, and celebrating in a wooded landscape alongside cattle and other animals. Painted in oil on copper in 1605 and held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the small plate showcases Joachim Wtewael's Utrecht Mannerism at its most refined, the polished metal support intensifying the jewel-like colour of the intricate composition.

title: Transfiguration-Rubens
description: Christ rises in radiant white between Moses and Elijah while the apostles below shield their eyes, a subject drawn from Matthew 17. Rubens organizes the composition around a vertical axis of light, marrying Italian disegno with Flemish painterly warmth.

provenance.collection: Museum of Fine Arts of Nancy
provenance.location: Museum of Fine Arts of Nancy

title: Mars and Venus Surprised by the Gods
description: Mars and Venus tangle naked in a curtained bed while Apollo, Diana and the rest of the Olympian gods sail in on clouds to mock them. Painted on copper between 1606 and 1610 and now in the Getty, the panel packs more than a dozen figures into a polished cabinet-sized surface intended for close, private viewing.

title: Portrait of Kaspar Scioppius
description: Kaspar Scioppius, the German Catholic controversialist, is shown in a three-quarter-length standing pose, wearing a dark cloak over a richly embroidered doublet with a white lace collar and holding a small object at his side. The direct, self-possessed gaze and the warm palette reflect the Venetian influence Rubens absorbed during his Italian years. Painted circa 1606, the portrait is now in the Galleria Palatina, Florence.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/41portra/05sciopp"

title: Saint Sebastian tended by two angels
description: After the Roman martyr's ordeal at the column, two angels withdraw the arrows and bind his wounds. Rubens treats Sebastian's nude body in the heroic manner of antique sculpture and Italian masters, softening the violence into a Baroque tableau of muscular grace.

title: The Judgment of Paris
englishTitle: The Judgement of Paris (early version, c. 1606)
description: The Trojan prince Paris weighs the golden apple between Juno, Minerva and Venus while Mercury looks on. An early version of a subject Rubens revisited often, the composition arranges three nude goddesses to display Italianate disegno absorbed during his stay in Rome.
credit: Museo del Prado, Madrid

title: The Seven Works of Mercy
description: All seven corporal acts of mercy, from burying the dead to Roman Charity, unfold in a single torch-lit Neapolitan alley. Painted for the Pio Monte della Misericordia, the altarpiece set the template for Neapolitan tenebrism that Ribera and the Caravaggisti would extend.

title: Anatomical study
description: An ecorche drawing exposing the muscles of the male torso and limbs, made for the artist's own study of human structure. Such sheets fed the powerfully built figures of his history paintings and were later engraved as a teaching aid.

title: Cain slaying his brother Abel
description: The first murder rendered as violent close-quarters struggle, Cain's club raised above his fallen brother. Rubens compresses the action into a tight pyramidal group, exploiting contorted limbs and chiaroscuro for moral force.
credit: The Courtauld Institute of Art, London

title: Der lachende Philosoph
description: A workshop image of Democritus, the Greek thinker known in antiquity as the laughing philosopher, mocking the follies of humankind. His broad smile and weathered features draw on the Northern tradition of philosopher portraits revived by Rubens and his circle.

title: Ecce homo
description: A bound and crowned Christ is presented to the crowd, his torso lit against a brooding ground in the manner Rubens used to dramatize Passion scenes. The taut musculature and fall of light over the shoulders intensify the Counter-Reformation appeal to compassion.

title: Saint Jerome in his study
description: A monumental Saint Jerome sits absorbed at his open book, lion at his feet and deep red drapery enveloping his powerful aged form, while two putti attend him. Rubens emphasises the hermit-scholar's muscular anatomy and the cardinal's scarlet, a saint central to Counter-Reformation imagery as an emblem of biblical orthodoxy. The painting, dating from 1608–09, is held at the Bildergalerie Sanssouci, Potsdam.
credit: Bildergalerie Sanssouci in Potsdam; brandenburg.museum-digital.de

title: The Beheading of Saint John the Baptist
description: Painted for the Oratory of San Giovanni in Valletta, where it remains the only canvas Caravaggio signed — in the spilled blood of the saint. The huge, half-lit composition stages the executioner mid-action with Caravaggio's signature tenebrist sobriety.

title: The Virgin of the Immaculate Conception
description: The Virgin rises on a billowing cloud attended by four full-sized angels against a dramatic sky, her hands clasped at her breast, with lilies and symbolic objects below her. Begun by El Greco between 1608 and 1614 and completed by his son Jorge Manuel Theotokópoulos, the painting presents the Immaculate Conception in the elongated, intensely spiritual manner of El Greco's late Toledan period, and now hangs in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid.

title: The Vision of Saint John
description: Saint John, robed in blue, raises his arms toward a turbulent sky as nude figures surge upward grasping a billowing green cloth at the opening of the fifth seal. Painted between 1608 and 1614 and now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, the unfinished canvas is cited as an acknowledged source for Picasso's Demoiselles d'Avignon.

title: Fray Hortensio Félix Paravicino
description: The Trinitarian preacher Hortensio Félix Paravicino sits upright in a carved chair in his black and white habit, a book open on his lap. Painted in 1609 and now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, the portrait depicts the court preacher to Philip III, who celebrated El Greco in verse.

title: Susana y los viejos
description: Susanna twists away from two leering elders who press in from the shadows of her garden bath, her startled body and rumpled drapery filling the canvas. Painted shortly after Rubens's return from Italy, the picture fuses Venetian colour with the muscular Roman figures he had studied there.

title: The Adoration of the Shepherds
description: Shepherds press in around the manger, faces lit from below by the Christ child as Mary draws back the cloth. The diagonal massing of figures and theatrical lighting reflect Rubens's recent absorption of Caravaggio during his Italian years.

title: The Holy Family with St. Elizabeth
description: An intimate devotional panel showing the Madonna and Child with St Elizabeth, the infant Baptist and a hovering dove of the Holy Spirit. The warm flesh tones and tender exchange of glances reflect Rubens's recent return from Italy.
credit: Image: http://collections.lacma.org/sites/default/files/remote_images/piction/ma-31767707-O3.jpg Gallery: http://collections.lacma.org/node/230317 archive copy at the Wayback Machine

provenance.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
provenance.location: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

title: The Recognition of Philopoemen
description: The Achaean general Philopoemen is recognised by his hosts — an exemplum of stoic humility drawn from Plutarch — while a lavish kitchen table heaped with game, fowl, and produce fills the foreground. The still life is by Frans Snyders, a frequent collaborator who supplied naturalistic animal subjects, while Rubens painted the figures. The Recognition of Philopoemen, circa 1609, is held in the Museo del Prado.
credit: Philopoemen Recognized . Museo del Prado. Retrieved on 23 October 2013 .

title: Virgin with the Child
description: The Virgin, dressed in a rose-red gown, looks tenderly down at the active Christ Child seated in her lap, who turns toward her holding a small red fruit. Painted around 1609–1610 near the start of Artemisia Gentileschi's Roman career, the work is now in the Galleria Palatina, Florence, and shows her absorbing her father Orazio's cool, silvery palette within a spare Caravaggesque interior.

title: Anyone who is bitten by a snake is cured by looking at the brazen serpent raised by Moses
description: Moses raises the bronze serpent on a pole as stricken Israelites writhe in the foreground, their wounds healed at a glance. The crowded, twisting figures provide a typological prefiguration of the Crucifixion familiar in Counter-Reformation imagery.

title: Christ between the two malefactors
description: A close study of a bearded man's head thrown violently upward in an expression of anguish or extremity, the loose, energetic brushwork typical of Rubens's preparatory studies. The work, titled 'Christ between the two malefactors,' is held at the Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburgh, and dates to the early seventeenth century.

title: Christ on the Cross - Peter Paul Rubens
description: Christ hangs alone on the cross against a darkened sky, his pale body lit sharply against the gloom and his head sunk toward his shoulder. Rubens painted this single-figure devotional crucifixion in oil on oak panel, stripping away mourners and thieves to concentrate everything on the modelling of the body. The painting belongs to the Bavarian State Painting Collections in Munich.

title: El Salvador
description: Christ raises his right hand in benediction and rests his left on a dark orb, his face framed by a luminous halo against a near-black ground. The panel is part of the Apostolado series painted by El Greco, preserved in the Museo del Greco in Toledo, where the Saviour heads a cycle of the twelve apostles.

title: Juno and Argus
description: Juno, in crimson robes, receives the eyes of the slain Argus — whose body lies at the lower right — and places them into the fanned tail of her peacock, which dominates the left of the composition. Female attendants and putti animate the open-air tableau, and a rainbow is visible in the upper sky. The Ovidian subject is drawn from the Metamorphoses and the painting of the 1610s is in the Wallraf–Richartz Museum, Cologne.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/21mythol/08mythol"

title: Laocoön
description: El Greco's dynamic interpretation of the Laocoön myth, depicting the Trojan priest and his sons in a dramatic struggle with serpents. Painted between 1610 and 1614, this oil canvas exemplifies the artist's characteristic elongated forms, intense emotionality, and spiritual intensity. The work is held in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.

title: Lot and his daughters in a rock grotto
description: Set in a rocky grotto with a distant fiery glow, Rubens depicts Lot flanked by his two daughters who offer him wine from an ornate golden vessel. Contrary to convention, Lot is rendered not as a passive victim but as a bearded yet physically vigorous man reaching actively toward the younger daughter. The canvas dates to circa 1610, shortly after Rubens's return from Italy, and is held at the Staatliches Museum Schwerin.
credit: akbrzeski.de; Staatliches Museum Schwerin; Google Art Project works from the Staatliches Museum Schwerin

title: Portrait of Dr. Francisco de Pisa
description: An elderly man in a dark robe trimmed with fur sits before an open book spread on a table, his hands resting on its pages. Painted between circa 1610 and 1614 in El Greco's late manner, the portrait is identified as the Toledan canon and historian Dr. Francisco de Pisa.

title: Saint Jerome
description: Jerome appears as a bare-chested penitent in half-length, holding a crucifix in his right hand and a stone in his left, a skull and hourglass placed before him and a red cardinal hat visible to his side. Dated to around 1610 and held at the Hispanic Society of America in New York, the painting belongs to El Greco's late series of the penitent saint in contemplation.
credit: Hispanic Society of America

title: Sotatsu Dragons and Clouds
description: Two dragons coil out of swirling ink clouds across a pair of folding screens by Tawaraya Sōtatsu, the early seventeenth-century founder of the Rinpa school. Working in ink alone, Sōtatsu pooled and blotted washes to make the beasts surface and dissolve in the mist. The screens are held by the National Museum of Asian Art in Washington, D.C.

title: Study for the figure of Christ on the Cross
description: A chalk drawing of a crucified figure seen from below, arms extended upward and head thrown back with gaze directed to the heavens, the musculature of the torso rendered in crisp black-and-white contour and shading. Dated 1610, the study relates to Rubens's preparation for one of his major Antwerp altarpiece commissions, demonstrating his rigorous figure studies in drawn media before translating compositions to large-scale paint.

title: Study of an Old Woman
description: An oil sketch on oak panel of an elderly woman, made as preparatory study for figures populating Rubens's larger religious and mythological compositions. The loose, economical handling typifies the head-studies the Antwerp workshop produced from life models.
credit: The Phoebus Foundation

title: Susanna and the Elders
description: Painted when the artist was seventeen, the canvas turns the usual erotic pretext on its head: Susanna twists from the leering elders in unmistakable distress. The closed marble parapet and tightly wound figures give the scene a claustrophobia rare in the subject's long history.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"g/gentiles/artemisi/susanna"

title: The Apostle Saint Peter
description: Saint Peter is shown in papal vestments holding the keys of heaven, his weathered features turned upward in devotion. Painted soon after Rubens's return from Italy, the half-length follows a Caravaggesque tradition of monumental, close-cropped apostle portraits.

title: The Elevation of the Cross
description: Muscular soldiers heave the cross upright on a steep diagonal, Christ's luminous body twisting against a stormy sky. Conceived for Antwerp's St. Walburga, the great triptych translates Italian heroic anatomy into a Flemish altarpiece of unprecedented physical force.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: The Lamentation
description: The dead Christ is supported between two mourners — a young man in red (Saint John) on the left and a woman in blue (the Virgin Mary) on the right — in a tightly focused composition of restrained grief. This school-of-Rubens Lamentation, dated c. 1610–1640, is in the collection of Durham University.

title: The Return from War: Mars Disarmed by Venus
description: Venus, partly nude, lifts the helmet from Mars as the fully armoured war-god yields to her embrace, while putti tug at his lance and scattered weapons and armour fill the foreground — an allegory of love's pacifying power over violence. The composition is set within a vaulted interior opening onto a background landscape with military activity. Painted around 1610, the work is held at the J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles (inv. 2000.68).

title: Bacchic scene with the dream of Silenus
description: Silenus slumbers in heavy intoxication while nymphs and attendants surround him amid an abundance of gold vessels, dishes, and luxurious still-life objects, a leopard resting at his side. Rubens painted this Bacchic scene in 1611, shortly after his Italian years, combining the antique subject of Silenus's drunken sleep with the lavish material culture of a princely feast. The work is held in the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna.

title: Perseus Releases Andromeda
description: Andromeda stands chained on a rocky shore, largely unclothed, while Perseus arrives on horseback from the upper right and a sea creature lurks in the middle ground, with a coastal town visible in the distance. The foreground is strewn with shells and sea-life rendered in Wtewael's characteristically minute detail. Joachim Wtewael, a leading Utrecht Mannerist, painted this version of the subject in 1611.
credit: towerweb.net : Home : Info : Pic

title: Prometheus Bound
description: Prometheus, chained to a rocky outcrop, twists violently as the eagle of Zeus tears at his torso in a dramatically diagonal composition Rubens developed with Frans Snyders, who painted the bird. The torsion of the figure draws on Michelangelo and the Laocoön, fused with North-Italian colorism. This autograph version, begun around 1611–12, is held at the Philadelphia Museum of Art (inv. W1950-3-1).

title: St. Andrew
description: From the Twelve Apostles series painted for the Duke of Lerma, Andrew is identified by the X-shaped saltire cross of his martyrdom. Rubens characterizes the fisherman-evangelist as a weather-beaten elder, modelled with the bold chiaroscuro he absorbed in Italy.

title: St. Paul
description: Paul appears as a forceful, full-haired elder gripping the sword of his beheading and cradling a book, in keeping with Counter-Reformation Pauline iconography. The half-length panel belongs to the Apostolado painted for the Duke of Lerma's collection, circa 1611, and is now in the Museo del Prado.

title: St. Simon
description: Simon the Zealot appears in profile, absorbed in a worn book, the long saw of his legendary martyrdom resting half-visible at the lower left against a dark ground. The panel belongs to the Twelve Apostles series Rubens painted around 1610-12 for the Duke of Lerma, preserved intact at the Museo del Prado.

title: The Massacre of the Innocents
englishTitle: The Massacre of the Innocents (Art Gallery of Ontario, c. 1611)
description: A violent biblical tableau of soldiers wrenching infants from their mothers in a tangle of straining muscle and contorted limbs. Rubens compresses the figures into a writhing pyramid, drawing on his Italian study of Michelangelo, Caravaggio and antique sculpture.

title: Danae
description: Danaë reclines across white and red drapery as a shower of gold falls from the dark upper field, while a servant in blue and white stands behind her holding a cloth. Attributed to Artemisia Gentileschi and dated to around 1612, the work applies Caravaggesque tenebrism to this Ovidian subject. The canvas, measuring approximately 53 by 41 cm, is a relatively intimate treatment of the theme.

title: Descent from the Cross
englishTitle: Saint Christopher (outside right wing of the Descent from the Cross triptych)
description: A solitary bearded figure, robed and sandalled, raises a lantern against a nocturnal sky marked by a crescent moon, his face turned upward in watchful attention. This tall outer wing of Rubens's Descent from the Cross triptych at the Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekathedraal, Antwerp (1612–14), is identified as Saint Christopher, serving as the shuttered face the congregation would see when the triptych was closed.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/11religi/07desce5"

title: Jupiter and Antiope
description: The Haarlem master, better known as a virtuoso engraver, treats the mythological seduction with a sculptural nude and the warm flesh tones he absorbed from his late Italian journey. Jupiter approaches in satyr disguise, the composition borrowed from Northern Mannerist prints Goltzius himself had popularised across Europe.

title: Roman Charity
description: An interpretation of the antique tale of Pero, who secretly nurses her imprisoned father Cimon to keep him alive. Rubens treats the moralising subject with characteristic warmth of flesh, dramatic chiaroscuro and a tender, tightly compressed embrace.

title: Study of the head of a young man turned to the left
description: A close study of a young man's head in strict profile, turned to the left, with wavy blond hair rendered in vigorous chiaroscuro. Dating to 1612 and held at the Norton Simon Museum, the panel demonstrates Rubens's habit of accumulating head studies as reference material for larger narrative compositions.

title: The Denial of St. Peter
description: Around a candlelit table, a servant girl holds a flame and points an accusing finger at Peter while other figures look on and play cards at the right. Honthorst, who trained in Rome and absorbed Caravaggio's tenebrism, uses the hidden candle to bathe the apostle's denial in warm planes of orange light, a technique that earned him the Italian nickname Gherardo delle Notti. The work dates between 1612 and 1620.
credit: Self-photographed , Photograph taken at: Corps et Ombres : Le Caravagisme européen , Category:Musée des Augustins de Toulouse , 23 July 2012 – 14 October 2012 , Caroline Léna Becker

title: The Dying Seneca
description: The Stoic philosopher stands in a basin while a physician opens his veins, his upturned head and outstretched arms recalling the antique sculpture Rubens had drawn in Rome. The picture distills the Baroque taste for Stoic exemplars of virtuous death.

provenance.location: Alte Pinakothek, upper floor, gallery VII

title: The Entombment
description: Christ's body is lowered onto the slab of anointing as the Marys and disciples crowd in grief. Rubens tightens Caravaggio's Vatican prototype into an oval of mourning figures, the dead flesh phosphorescent against the surrounding shadow.
credit: J. Paul Getty Museum

title: The lamentation of Christ
description: A large, multi-figure Lamentation in which the dead Christ is laid out horizontally and surrounded by a dense group of mourners, including the Virgin, Saint John, and several other holy women and men. The warm, broadly lit composition conveys collective grief through varied expressions and gestures rather than chiaroscuro drama. Painted in 1612, the work is in the Liechtenstein Collections (inv. GE 62).
credit: Liechtenstein Museum

title: 0 Le Sultan Mulay Ahmad de Tunis - Rubens - Museum of Fine Arts
englishTitle: Portrait of Sultan Mulay Ahmad of Tunisia
description: Rubens reworks an earlier portrait by Jan Cornelisz Vermeyen of the Hafsid sultan, lending the Tunisian ruler the broad shoulders, ruddy flesh and lustrous turban he reserved for noble sitters. Such copies after Vermeyen fed Rubens's lifelong fascination with cosmopolitan dress and the wider Mediterranean world.
credit: User:Jean-Pol GRANDMONT (2013)

title: Death of Cleopatra
description: Cleopatra lies fully reclined across rumpled white and crimson drapery, her eyes closed and one arm raised above her head, a small asp coiled at her wrist. The foreshortened nude composition is attributed to Artemisia Gentileschi, dated 1613 or 1621–1622, and belongs to her series of monumental heroines drawn from antiquity.

title: Lot and his Daughters
description: The episode from Genesis 19, in which Lot's daughters ply their father with wine to secure descendants after the destruction of Sodom. Rubens treats the subject with characteristically warm flesh tones and muscular, twisting figures, the canvas later extended at top and bottom in the early eighteenth century.
credit: Christie´s

title: Virgin with the Child
