description: The Virgin, in a pink robe and blue mantle with a halo suggested by warm light, holds the Christ Child on her lap as he reaches up toward her, a tall candle visible in the upper left. Painted between 1613 and 1614 and now in the Galleria Spada, Rome, the work demonstrates Artemisia Gentileschi's adaptation of Caravaggesque modelling — strong directional light giving the figures a sculptural solidity — to an intimate devotional subject.

title: A child with bird
description: A young blonde child turns in profile, intently watching a small green bird perched on its hands. The intimate bust-length format and warm flesh tones place this panel within Rubens's circle of domestic portraits, a private counterpart to the grand commissions for which he is better known. The painting is held at the Gemäldegalerie Berlin (inv. 763), dated between 1614 and 1625.
credit: Objekt in der Onlinesammlung der Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin: 870518 Fotograf: Christoph Schmidt

title: Annunciation
description: The Virgin, dressed in rose and blue, kneels at a lectern as the Angel Gabriel approaches from the right in a luminous yellow robe, his hand extended in address. Above, a heavenly gathering of figures and cherubim surrounds a radiant burst of light, with the Holy Spirit implied by the golden glow descending between the two figures. El Greco painted this Annunciation in 1614, in the elongated, flickering style characteristic of his final years.

title: Christ Giving the Keys to St. Peter
description: Christ, robed in red and nimbed, extends the keys to a white-bearded Saint Peter, who bows to receive them, while a group of apostles bears witness behind. Painted in 1614 and now in the Gemäldegalerie Berlin, the composition translates the biblical grant of papal authority into Rubens's characteristic idiom of crowded, animated figures lit against a cool architectural ground.
credit: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
description: Daniel sits among nine lions in a rocky den, hands clasped and gaze lifted upward in prayer as the beasts prowl, yawn, and doze around him. Painted circa 1614–1616 and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the canvas demonstrates Rubens's close study of live lions and his ability to combine vigorous animal observation with Counter-Reformation religious conviction.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/15biblic/07daniel"; National Gallery of Art, Washington D.C

title: Judith Beheading Holofernes
description: The biblical heroine and her maidservant pin the Assyrian general to his bed, blade drawn across his throat as blood spurts onto the linen. Gentileschi heightens the Caravaggesque tenebrism with a tightly compressed composition and the unflinching, muscular cooperation of the two women.

title: Kitchen Still Life
description: A loaded kitchen table heaves with game, fruit and copper vessels in the lavish Antwerp manner that Snyders developed alongside Rubens. Strong diagonals and life-size scale push the still life toward decorative grandeur, intended for the dining halls of patrician collectors.
credit: collectie.boijmans.nl : Home : Info

title: Lamentation of Christ by Mary and John
description: In this intimate Lamentation, the dead Christ is supported by Saint John, who is dressed in vivid red, and the Virgin, whose green-draped figure bows over the body from the right. Rubens reduces the cast to its essential mourners, concentrating devotional intensity in the contrast of pale, lifeless flesh and richly coloured drapery. Painted circa 1614–1615, the work is in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna (inv. GG 529).
credit: Kunsthistorisches Museum

title: Neptune and Amphitrite
description: Neptune, depicted as a venerable old man, is seated beside the standing nude Amphitrite at the centre of a monumental allegory populated by exotic animals — a lion, tiger, rhinoceros, and crocodile — flanking the divine pair. Painted in 1614 and held in the Gemäldegalerie Berlin (inv. 776A), the composition is Rubens's ambitious synthesis of mythological and allegorical traditions, here grouping the sea-deities with creatures symbolising the earth's continents and waters.
credit: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

title: Saint Teresa of Avila's Vision
description: Saint Teresa of Ávila kneels in her Carmelite habit before a table bearing a skull, crucifix, and open book, her gaze lifted towards a luminous vision above. The work, dated c. 1614 and in the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, Rotterdam, typifies Rubens's treatment of Counter-Reformation visionary subjects with controlled interior light and devotional symbolism.
credit: collectie.boijmans.nl : Home : Info : Pic

title: The Death of Adonis
description: The dead Adonis lies outstretched on the ground while three mourning nymphs or Graces attend him, one cradling his head, as a grieving putto and a hound stand to the right. Rubens composed this Ovidian lamentation around 1614 with characteristic attention to the beauty of pale flesh against rich drapery; the work is held at the Israel Museum, Jerusalem.
credit: The Israel Museum, Jerusalem

title: Venus and Adonis
description: Venus clings to the departing Adonis as he shoulders his spear and his hounds strain toward the fatal hunt. Rubens reworks Titian's Prado composition, heightening the embrace into a Baroque farewell of foreboding and tender resistance.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/21mythol/16mythol" http://hermitagemuseum.org/wps/portal/hermitage/digital-collection/01.+paintings/48132?lng=en

title: Venus in front of the mirror
description: Venus gazes at her own face in a large octagonal mirror held by a winged Cupid, while a dark-skinned attendant looks on from behind. Painted between 1614 and 1615 and now in the Liechtenstein Collection, the composition presents Venus seen from the back, her warm flesh contrasted against the cool reflective surface of the mirror, within the Venetian tradition of the toilette subject.

title: Warrior
description: An oil study of an armoured soldier, executed with the loose brushwork and ruddy palette Rubens reserved for working sketches. The figure's head and gleaming breastplate are modelled with rapid, confident strokes, capturing the swagger of a Baroque military type.

title: Yhe holy Family with the parrot
description: Mary and the infant Christ, supported by the elderly Joseph, gather in a semi-outdoor setting before a stone column and open landscape, while a large blue-and-gold macaw perches at left — a bird traditionally read as a symbol of the Virgin's purity. Rubens reworks the Renaissance devotional formula for the Holy Family with the characteristic warmth and fleshy vitality of his Flemish Baroque manner. The painting of 1614 is held at the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp and displayed in the Rubenshuis.
credit: DAMS Antwerpen

provenance.collection: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

title: Descent from the Cross
description: Christ's body is lowered from the cross in a diagonal cascade of pale flesh and white shroud, supported by mourning saints. Rubens returned to this Counter-Reformation subject repeatedly after his Antwerp Cathedral altarpiece, modelling the dead Christ on classical sculpture studied during his years in Rome.
credit: Władysław Kwiatkowski (1929). Obraz Rubensa w Kaliszu . Towarzystwo Przyjaciół Książki

title: Ibrahim 'Adil Shah II holding instruments
description: A Deccani miniature of around 1615 depicting Ibrahim Adil Shah II of Bijapur standing in a garden, wearing golden robes over a white garment and a white turban, and holding a small object — likely a flower — at chest height. The refined Bijapur idiom is evident in the jewel-like colour, precise draughtsmanship, and lush landscape setting with a palace visible in the background. The work is attributed to Ali Riza.

title: Landscape with the Ruins of Mount Palatine in Rome
englishTitle: Landscape with the Ruins of Mount Palatine in Rome
description: Roman ruins on the Palatine hill rise above figures and herds in a panoramic landscape conceived from sketches made during the artist's years in Italy. Antiquity is set in dialogue with a fertile, lived-in countryside.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Saint Francis
description: Saint Francis of Assisi kneels in ecstatic communion, his gaunt features and brown habit picked out against a darkened ground. The economy of means and devotional intensity reflect Counter-Reformation taste for affective images of penitent saints.

title: The Four Continents
description: An allegory of the four continents personified as river gods reclining beside their female consorts, traditionally identified with the Danube, Nile, Ganges and Rio de la Plata. Tigers, a crocodile and lush vegetation underscore the cosmographic ambition of the Vienna canvas.
credit: Kunsthistorisches Museum

title: The Garden of Eden with the Fall of Man
description: Jan Brueghel the Elder painted the abundant menagerie of Eden — peacocks, leopards, parrots, deer, and many other creatures amid lush vegetation — while Rubens contributed the figures of Adam and Eve at the Tree of Knowledge. The collaboration dates to 1615 and is now in the Mauritshuis, The Hague.
credit: Geheugen van Nederland : Home : Info : Pic

title: The hunting of the hippopotamus
description: One of four exotic hunts Rubens painted around 1615 for Maximilian I of Bavaria, blending Flemish pictorial drama with antique pathos. Spear-wielding riders, snarling hounds, and writhing reptiles crash together in a swirling diagonal composition that became a touchstone for Baroque action painting.

title: The Judgement of Paris
description: Paris, seated in a red cap among a flock of animals, extends the golden apple towards Venus while the two other goddesses and Mercury look on, with Cupid hovering above and a peacock perched in the trees. Wtewael sets the Olympian contest in an elaborate wooded landscape peopled with gods, shepherds, and cattle. The work is dated 1615 and is held at the National Gallery.
credit: National Gallery

title: Isabella Brant as Glycera
description: A young woman, identified as Rubens's first wife Isabella Brant in the guise of Glycera, the ancient Greek flower seller, is shown in bust-length holding a garland of mixed blooms. She wears a pearl necklace and drop earring, and her braided hair is pinned up. The conceit fuses tender domestic portraiture with classical learning, and the work of circa 1616 is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Judith with the Head of Holofernes
description: Judith, young and partially bare-shouldered, grasps the severed head of the Assyrian general Holofernes at mid-level while an aged maidservant assists beside her, both figures lit against deep shadow. Judith's sword is visible at left, reinforcing the immediate aftermath of the biblical act. Rubens treats the Old Testament heroine with the heightened drama of his early Italianate manner; the work of circa 1616–1618 is in the Herzog Anton Ulrich Museum, Brunswick.

title: Lot and his Daughters
description: Beneath a tree the daughters press wine on their father while Sodom burns in the distance, a small dog and a still life of bread and cheese anchoring the foreground. Goltzius, the great Haarlem engraver turned painter, sets the nudes in cool, sculptural light typical of his late Mannerist style.
credit: www.rijksmuseum.nl : Home : Info : Pic

title: Mariae Himmelfahrt
description: The Virgin is borne aloft by a swirl of angels while the apostles cluster around her empty tomb below. The upward spiralling composition is a hallmark of Rubens's altarpieces for the Antwerp churches of the early seventeenth century.

provenance.location: State Gallery in the New Schleißheim Palace

title: Old woman and boy with candles
description: An aged woman shields a candle flame as a boy leans in to light his own taper from hers, the two faces modelled by the small light source. The picture belongs to the Northern tradition of nocturnal genre studies descending from Caravaggio and the Bassano workshop.
credit: Mauritshuis

title: Portrait of Clara Serena Rubens
description: This close-up portrait of Clara Serena Rubens, the artist's eldest daughter, shows her as a young child with reddish-auburn hair neatly pinned, rosy cheeks, and an alert, slightly parted lips. The brisk yet affectionate handling — close in spirit to a rapid life study — is among the most intimate of Rubens's family works. Painted in 1616, it is now in the Liechtenstein Museum (inv. GE 105); Clara Serena died in 1623 at the age of twelve.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/r/rubens/41portra/10portra"

title: Study of a Man's Head
description: A bearded male head in strict left profile, the face deeply furrowed and lit from the left against a dark ground, with wavy grey-brown hair falling to the shoulder. Painted in 1616, the study belongs to the tradition of tronies — head studies used as reference for apostles, elders, and biblical figures in large-scale compositions. The work is held in the Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest.

title: The Fall of Man
description: Adam and Eve recline together beneath the Tree of Knowledge, Eve offering the forbidden fruit while the serpent winds through the branches above. A cat rests at their feet and goats graze in the background landscape. Painted in 1616 by the Haarlem master Hendrick Goltzius and now at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the picture exemplifies the smooth, naturalistic idealism of his mature style.

title: The Ferry Boat to Antwerp
description: Despite the catalogue title, the panel records a bustling Flemish ferry crossing to Antwerp, packed with passengers, cargo and livestock. Jordaens animates the scene with the boisterous, low-life realism that anchored his early Antwerp output.
credit: www.smk.dk and soeg.smk.dk

title: Allegory of sight
description: Sight, the most celebrated of the Five Senses series produced jointly with Jan Brueghel the Elder, sets Venus and Cupid in a kunstkammer crowded with paintings, scientific instruments and rarities. The picture doubles as an inventory of the Archdukes' collection in Brussels.
credit: Museo del Prado, Madrid

title: Christ before the High Priest
description: Caiaphas leans across the table to question Christ, the two faces lit only by a single candle set between them. Honthorst painted the canvas in Rome around 1617 for the Marchese Vincenzo Giustiniani, and the radical nocturne earned him the Italian nickname Gherardo delle Notti.

title: Descent from the Cross
description: A workshop variant of Rubens' Antwerp Cathedral altarpiece, with the pale body of Christ lowered diagonally onto a white shroud held by mourners. The composition's coiling diagonals and contrasted flesh tones became a Counter-Reformation template repeated across Catholic Europe.

title: Diana returning from the Hunt
description: Diana strides forward holding a long hunting spear, attended by two nymphs and accompanied by hounds, her quiver of arrows visible at her side. The composition presents the goddess of the hunt in motion, affording Rubens scope for studies of the female figure in varied poses. Painted between 1617 and 1620, the work is held at the Museo del Prado, Madrid (inv. P001727).

title: George Villiers
description: This bust-length portrait shows George Villiers, 1st Duke of Buckingham, in a dark doublet with a lace collar and the blue sash of the Order of the Garter. Long regarded as a later copy of a lost Rubens, dendrochronological and technical analysis of the panel subsequently confirmed an attribution to Rubens's studio, dating the support to the 1620s. The painting hung for generations at Pollok House before the attribution was revised.

title: Head Study of a Bearded Man
description: An oil head study, painted directly from a Antwerp model, of the kind Rubens kept on file for reuse as apostles, philosophers and patriarchs in larger compositions. The rapid wet-into-wet handling and ruddy flesh tones show his working method at its most direct.

title: Hearing
description: From the Five Senses cycle painted with Jan Brueghel the Elder for the Archdukes Albert and Isabella in Brussels. Brueghel laid in the encyclopaedic gallery interior crammed with instruments, music books and singing birds; Rubens contributed the figure of Venus listening to a concert of Cupids.
credit: Museo del Prado, Madrid

title: Lamentation
description: The dead Christ lies on a sheaf of straw, his pallid body supported by a group of mourners that includes the Virgin in a dark hood, an older bearded man at left, and a young woman with loose hair at right. The sharply upturned face and foreshortened limbs intensify the grief of the surrounding figures, recalling Rubens's debt to Italian models of the Pietà. Painted 1617–1618, the work is in the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (inv. 300).

provenance.collection: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp
provenance.location: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

title: Mars and Rhea Silvia
description: The war god looms over the Vestal Rhea Silvia, the union that will produce Romulus and Remus and so found Rome. Rubens stages the encounter with cascading drapery, fluttering putti and the warm flesh-tones that mark his mythological inventions.

title: Milkmaids with Cattle in a Landscape
description: Milkmaids tend cattle amid baskets of fruit and vegetables in a fertile Brabant landscape, a cornucopia of rural abundance. Rubens fuses pastoral genre and landscape with sweeping diagonal composition and an almost mythological sense of fertility.

title: Pan and Syrinx
description: Rubens stages the Ovidian myth of Pan pursuing the nymph Syrinx, who is moments from transformation into the riverside reeds that crowd the right of the composition. The figures rush through a lush, flower-strewn wetland, birds and frogs scattered at their feet. Painted between 1617 and 1619 and held by the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister in Kassel (inv. GK 1229), the small panel is a characteristic Baroque fusion of mythological narrative and sensuous naturalism.

title: Smell
description: An outdoor garden setting overflowing with flowers, fruits, and foliage frames two figures — a woman and a winged putto — from the Five Senses series painted with Jan Brueghel the Elder for the regents of the Spanish Netherlands. Brueghel contributed the encyclopaedic floral abundance while Rubens supplied the figures. The panel is held at the Museo del Prado.

title: The miracles of St. Francis Xavier
description: The Jesuit missionary Francis Xavier raises the dead and heals the afflicted before a toppling pagan idol, the converted crowding toward him in awe. Painted for Antwerp's Jesuit church, the altarpiece celebrates the global reach of Counter-Reformation evangelism.

title: The mocking of Christ
description: Soldiers crowd around the seated, crowned Christ by the light of a torch held openly at the centre of the composition, their mocking gestures emerging from dense shadow. Gerard van Honthorst painted this nocturnal devotional scene around 1617, applying the Caravaggesque tenebrism he developed in Rome; the work is now in the collection of the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.
credit: http://collections.lacma.org/node/197948 archive copy at the Wayback Machine

provenance.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
provenance.location: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

title: The Vision of St Hubert
description: A collaborative panel: Rubens painted the kneeling huntsman Saint Hubert encountering the cross-bearing stag, while Jan Brueghel the Elder provided the meticulous forest setting. Such division of labour between figure-painter and landscape specialist was a hallmark of Antwerp's Baroque studio system.
credit: Museo Nacional del Prado, Galería online

title: Theodosius and Saint Ambrose
description: Bishop Ambrose bars Emperor Theodosius from Milan Cathedral after the massacre at Thessalonica, a Counter-Reformation parable of clerical authority over secular power. Rubens stages the confrontation on the church steps with massed retinues, reworking a composition first treated by his Venetian model Veronese.
credit: Kunsthistorisches Museum

title: Christ at Simon the Pharisee
description: Christ sits at the Pharisee's table while a kneeling woman — traditionally identified as Mary Magdalene — bows over his feet, scandalising the assembled guests. Rubens orchestrates the Gospel scene as Baroque theatre, with richly contrasted light, elaborate tableware, and vivid emotional reaction rippling through the crowd. The painting, dated between 1618 and 1620, is in the Hermitage Museum.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/12religi/39religi"

title: Der Tod des Decius Mus in der Schlacht
description: From the Decius Mus cycle, a tapestry-cartoon-scale battle scene in which the Roman consul plunges to his ritual death amid rearing horses and clashing standards. The composition is a swirling diagonal of armoured bodies, an early showcase of Rubensian dynamism.

title: Head of Medusa
description: The severed head of the Gorgon lies on a stony ledge, eyes still rolling and snakes writhing into a teeming brood of vipers, scorpions and lizards. Rubens collaborated with the animal specialist Frans Snyders on the reptilian still life, fusing Baroque horror with naturalist precision.
credit: Kunsthistorisches Museum Wien, Bilddatenbank; GalleriX

title: Kitchen Scene with Christ in the House of Martha and Mary
description: A bodegón that folds a domestic kitchen scene around a small framed vignette of Christ admonishing Martha. The young Velázquez sets garlic, eggs and a glistening fish in tight tenebrist focus, signalling the Sevillian taste for moral allegory dressed as still life.
credit: picasaweb; gallerix.ru; National Gallery, London - online collection

title: Peter Finds the Coin in the Mouth of the Fish
description: Five full-length figures stand on a coastal shore beneath a cloudy sky as one of them — Peter — holds up a large fish from whose mouth a coin is to be retrieved, fulfilling the miracle of Matthew 17:27. The tall, narrow format of the panel reflects its function as an altarpiece panel in the Church of Our Lady across the river Dijle, Mechelen, for which Rubens painted it circa 1618–1619.

provenance.collection: Church of Our Lady across the river Dijle
provenance.location: Church of Our Lady across the river Dijle

title: The Rape of the Daughters of Leucippus
description: A vehement Baroque mythology in which Castor and Pollux carry off the daughters of Leucippus, the rearing horses and twisting nudes locked into Rubens's signature swirling diagonal. Painted in Antwerp at the height of his powers, the picture exemplifies the warm, pearly flesh and muscular drama that defined his manner.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/22mythol/28mythol" Originally from en.wikipedia ; description page is/was here . 2005-07-01 (original upload date). Original uploader was Cow at en.wikipedia . Originalmente carregado às 22:31hs do dia 01 maio 2007 por DIEGO RICARDO PEREIRA .

title: Two Satyrs
description: Two satyrs appear in close half-length view against a dark ground: the foreground figure, horned and wreathed, holds a bunch of white grapes and stares directly at the viewer, while the older satyr behind him drinks from a vessel with averted eyes. Painted between 1618 and 1619 and now in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich, the double tronie distils Rubens's vision of bacchic appetite into an arresting pair of bestial yet humanly knowing faces.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/22mythol/32mythol"

title: Union of Earth and Water
description: An allegorical pairing of Earth and Water in which a muscular Neptune-like figure crowns a reclining female personification, while putti frolic below and a cornucopia of fruit overflows at left. Painted in 1618 and now in the Hermitage Museum, the picture has been read as a plea for Antwerp's access to the sea. The warm flesh tones and surging figures are characteristic of Rubens's mature Baroque manner.
credit: Рубенс, Питер Пауль - Союз Земли и Воды (Антверпен и Шельда) (1618). Часть 14, высокое разрешение • описание картины, скачать репродукцию • Gallerix.ru

title: Winter: The Interior of a Barn
description: Peasants, cattle, horses, and farm tools fill an open barn structure whose rear doorway reveals a snowy yard beyond. Rubens painted this interior scene circa 1618–19 — one of several works from this period treating the working Flemish countryside with the same vigorous handling he applied to mythological subjects. The painting is held in the Royal Collection at Buckingham Palace (RCIN 401417).
credit: Royal Collection

title: Adoration of the Child
description: The infant Christ lies on manger straw and radiates his own light, illuminating the faces of the Virgin and gathered figures who lean in from surrounding darkness. Honthorst's hidden-light technique — the source of his Italian nickname Gherardo delle Notti — reaches its clearest expression here. The painting is oil on canvas, dated circa 1619–1620, and is held in the Uffizi, Florence (Inv. 1890 no. 739).

title: Drunken Silenus
description: The corpulent Silenus staggers forward at the centre, supported by satyrs and a Black figure playing a tambourine, while maenads, putti, and grapes fill the scene in a riotous frieze of Bacchic excess. Dated 1619 and held in the Bode Museum, Berlin, the composition draws on antique precedents and Venetian colour to celebrate — rather than moralize — the pleasures of wine.
credit: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

title: Lille Pdba rubens marie madeleine
description: The Magdalene lies swooning on rocky ground, supported by two angels, as a shaft of heavenly light breaks through the dark canopy above. Painted between 1619 and 1620 and held at the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille, the large canvas deploys the dramatic chiaroscuro and dynamic figural grouping characteristic of Rubens's mature Baroque manner.

title: A Kitchenmaid
description: A young kitchenmaid in a white cap and ruff raises a spitted fowl in one hand and holds a plucked bird in the other, surrounded by shelves of earthenware and metal vessels, a laid table with bread and fish, and a foreground basket of cabbages, cucumbers, and a joint of meat. Through the opening behind her, Christ appears in the house of Mary and Martha. The oil on canvas, signed by Joachim Wtewael and dated 1620–1625, measures roughly 103 by 72 centimetres and belongs to the Centraal Museum, Utrecht.
credit: Centraal Museum Utrecht

title: Allegory of Painting
description: A largely nude female figure is seen from behind, sprawling or bending low amid scattered painting implements on a studio floor, a canvas on an easel visible at the right edge. Attributed to Artemisia Gentileschi and dated 1620–1630, the work is held at the Musée de Tessé, Le Mans. The pose and setting connect the figure to allegorical representations of Painting, though the composition differs markedly from the artist's better-known upright self-portrait in the Royal Collection.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic

title: Augustins - Le Christ entre les deux larrons - Rubens
description: Rubens stages the Crucifixion with the two thieves flanking Christ, the muscular bodies twisting against a darkened sky in the dynamic Counter-Reformation idiom. Originally painted for a Flemish religious setting, the altarpiece deploys the diagonal energy and ruddy flesh tones characteristic of his Antwerp workshop, and now hangs in the Musée des Augustins in Toulouse.

provenance.location: Église du Musée des Augustins de Toulouse

title: Drunken Silenus supported by Satyrs
description: The wine-soaked Silenus, fleshy and unsteady, is supported by a rowdy Bacchic company of satyrs, a maenad, and cherubs bearing grapes. Painted around 1620, when the young van Dyck was absorbing Rubens's workshop practice, the canvas shares the older master's ruddy, full-bodied paint handling and preference for closely pressed, animated flesh. The work is held by the National Gallery, London.

title: Jael and Sisera
description: Jael drives a tent peg through the temple of the sleeping Canaanite general Sisera, a biblical assassination Artemisia returned to repeatedly. Caravaggesque chiaroscuro isolates the act against deep shadow, with the heroine's calm, deliberate grip typical of Gentileschi's strong-willed women.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"m/g/gentiles/artemisi/jaelsise"

title: Junger Mann mit schwarzem Barett
description: A bust-length portrait of an unidentified young man wearing a distinctive black beret, rendered against a neutral dark ground and gazing toward the viewer. He is dressed in black with a white ruffled collar and wears a jewelled ring, the restrained palette and even lighting giving the work a sober, Northern character. Painted in oil on oak panel in the 1620s, the picture is in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich, within the Bavarian State Painting Collections.

title: La Sainte Trinité
dateCreated: 19 th century , copy of a painting of circa 1620
description: A Counter-Reformation altar composition showing the Trinity enthroned amid swirling clouds and angels. Rubens deploys his characteristic ruddy flesh tones, golden draperies and dynamic Baroque diagonals to lift the eye toward the heavenly group.

title: Landscape with a Gnarled Tree and a Farm
description: A twisted, half-bare tree dominates this quick pen-and-brown-ink study of a farmstead, its trunk drawn with the same nervous, broken line as the low buildings behind. Landscape drawings like this are rare survivals from Van Dyck, who made them for his own use rather than as preparation for paintings — private observations from a career otherwise devoted to portraiture. The sheet is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, acquired in 1997.

title: Landscape with Philemon and Baucis
description: A storm-drenched Ovidian landscape in which Jupiter and Mercury, sheltered by the pious Philemon and Baucis, unleash a deluge upon the surrounding valley. The boiling sky, falling trees and rain-swollen torrent show Rubens absorbing Venetian and Adam Elsheimer landscape models for cosmic moral drama.
credit: Kunsthistorisches Museum

title: Penitent Mary Magdalene
description: The penitent Magdalene twists in her chair, gold gown slipping, hand pressed to her breast in conversion. Artemisia gives the Counter-Reformation subject the muscular, psychologically charged female protagonist that is her hallmark.

title: Pieter Bruegel the Younger
description: An ageing Pieter Brueghel the Younger turns toward the viewer in a quiet half-length portrait. The plate belongs to Van Dyck's Iconography, his series of etched and engraved likenesses of the leading artists, scholars and statesmen of his day.
credit: Frick Collection

title: Portrait of a woman with braided blond hair
description: A bust-length portrait of a young fair-haired woman, her blond curls gathered into braids above a plain dark dress with a simple white décolletage. The luminous skin and lively gaze are typical of Rubens's smaller-scale portraits, now in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.

title: Portrait of Anne of Austria
description: An early seventeenth-century studio copy of a lost Rubens portrait of Anne of Austria, queen consort of Louis XIII. The Spanish-born queen wears stiff court dress and an elaborate ruff, recorded with the smooth porcelain finish typical of Rubens's diplomatic likenesses of European royalty.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: The Three Crosses . [ 1 ] Alternative title
description: Christ hangs between the two thieves, the crosses set against a darkening sky in a tightly massed composition. Rubens compresses the Calvary scene into a vertical screen of straining bodies, a Counter-Reformation meditation on suffering and redemption.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/12religi/45religi"

title: 0 Entrevue du roi et de Marie de Médicis à Lyon - P.P. Rubens - Louvre 2
englishTitle: The Meeting of Marie de Médicis and Henry IV at Lyon
description: Part of Rubens's twenty-four-canvas Marie de' Medici cycle commissioned for the Luxembourg Palace and now in the Louvre. The royal meeting at Lyons is staged as an allegorical pageant, with personifications of the city, putti and a chariot drawn by lions glorifying a politically uneasy marriage.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: The Soldier and the Girl
description: A smiling man and young woman bend close together over a smoldering torch in the darkness, their faces illuminated by its glow in a characteristic Honthorst candlelit half-length. The work, dated circa 1621 and held in the Herzog Anton Ulrich Museum, Brunswick, exemplifies Honthorst's Utrecht Caravaggism in its intimate nocturnal lighting and genre subject.
credit: Kulturerbe Niedersachsen

title: The Triumphant Entry of Constantine into Rome
description: Part of the Constantine cycle designed for tapestries woven for Louis XIII, showing the emperor's victorious procession through Rome after the Battle of the Milvian Bridge. Rubens stages the parade as a ceremonial relief, packed with banners, classical architecture and rearing horses.
credit: Photographed by Zambonia 2011-10-28 http://collection.imamuseum.org/artwork/79267/index.html

title: The Virgin and Child in a Garland of Flowers
description: The Madonna and Child appear within an exuberant wreath of blossoms, painted in collaboration with the flower specialist Jan Brueghel the Elder. The conceit fuses Marian devotion with Antwerp's expertise in still life, the garland a votive offering of created beauty.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/13religi/51religi"

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: King David Playing the Harp
description: The crowned and bearded David tilts his head back with eyes raised in song as he plays a wooden harp, his brocaded robe trimmed with spotted fur. Painted in 1622, the close-cropped composition shows Honthorst adapting his Caravaggist approach — strong modelling against a dark ground — to a single biblical musician after his return from Rome.

title: Legend of Tomyris
description: Herodotus' Massagetae queen receives the severed head of the Persian king Cyrus, whom she will plunge into a vessel of blood. Rubens stages the Antwerp workshop's signature pile-up of muscular soldiery and silken courtiers, the carmine drapery and pearled flesh tones unmistakably his.

title: Mary Magdalene as the Melancholy
description: The Magdalene rests her cheek on her hand in the conventional pose of melancholia, jar of ointment beside her. Painted during Gentileschi's Roman years, the work fuses Caravaggesque chiaroscuro with the artist's signature interest in solitary, introspective female protagonists.
credit: Museo Soumaya Donation link to the image painting

title: Musical Group on a Balcony
description: A group of musicians and singers lean over a painted balustrade, looking down at the viewer in a bold di-sotto-in-su perspective — a composition Honthorst would have absorbed during his years in Italy. Instruments include a lute and a long wind instrument, with a red macaw visible among the figures. Signed and dated 1622, the painting demonstrates Honthorst's mastery of illusionistic ceiling decoration.

title: Perseus Releases Andromeda
description: Perseus, fresh from slaying the sea-monster, unbinds the nude Andromeda as putti and Pegasus crowd the rocky shore. The composition pairs heroic male armor with luminous female flesh in a swirling Baroque celebration of rescue and erotic deliverance.
credit: Hermitage Museum

title: Portrait of Susanna Lunden
description: A portrait long mistitled 'The Straw Hat' — the hat is in fact black felt — depicting Susanna Lunden, sister of Rubens's second wife Helena Fourment. The sitter wears a black bodice with vivid red sleeves, and the picture is celebrated for its luminous flesh painting and the deft rendering of cool daylight on her tilted hat brim. Now in the National Gallery, London, it dates from between 1622 and 1625.
credit: http://www.nationalgallery.org.uk/paintings/peter-paul-rubens-portrait-of-susanna-lunden-le-chapeau-de-paille (has Description )

title: The Adoration of the Shepherds
description: Shepherds and attendant figures crowd around the manger, their weathered faces lit from below by the radiant Christ child, with Mary leaning tenderly over the swaddled infant and Joseph to the right beside an ox. Honthorst's 1622 canvas deploys the Caravaggist nocturne he had mastered in Rome, making the Christ child himself the sole source of light in a horizontal Nativity composition.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"h/honthors/1/08adorsh"

title: The Coronation of Marie de' Medici in Saint-Denis
description: Part of the twenty-four-canvas Marie de' Medici cycle commissioned for the Luxembourg Palace, this scene stages the queen's 1610 coronation at Saint-Denis. Rubens orchestrates a vast crowd of dignitaries in a sweeping diagonal, mythologizing the event the day before Henri IV's assassination.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: The Disembarkation at Marseilles
description: From the Marie de' Medici cycle commissioned for the Luxembourg Palace, the canvas shows the queen's arrival at Marseilles in 1600, greeted by an allegorical France while Tritons and Nereids churn the water below. Painted between 1622 and 1625, Rubens fuses official Bourbon state imagery with Baroque mythological invention in this monumental work now in the Louvre.
credit: photo Shonagon 2022-09-20

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Judith and Her Maidservant
description: Judith and her servant pause in Holofernes's tent, alerted by a sound outside; a single candle throws Judith's shielding hand into silhouette and glances off the discarded gauntlet. The Detroit canvas is among Artemisia's most theatrical exercises in Caravaggesque candle-light.

title: Marchesa Elena Grimaldi Cattaneo
description: The Genoese noblewoman descends a terrace beneath a parasol held by an African page, the pairing a familiar device in van Dyck's Italian portraits of patrician women. Crimson drapery, towering verticals and a reserved, columnar pose set the template for European court portraiture.
credit: National Gallery of Art .

title: Portrait of an Old Man
description: A three-quarter-length portrait of an elderly man in black robes with a large white ruff, shown in profile to the right, his grey beard framing a composed and authoritative face. A heraldic coat of arms appears in the upper left, confirming this as a formal commission; the work is dated 1623 and is in the Gemäldegalerie Berlin.
credit: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

title: The Concert
description: A large company of musicians and revellers crowds around a draped table to sing, play lutes and violin, and drink by bright indoor light, with open music books spread before them. Gerard van Honthorst renders each face with animated expression, situating the scene within the Utrecht Caravaggist tradition of merry company paintings he developed after returning to his home city. Signed and dated 1623, the canvas is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: The Merry Fiddler
description: A bearded fiddler in a plumed hat raises a wine glass with one hand and holds his violin aloft with the other, leaning out through a window hung with an ornate carpet. Gerard van Honthorst painted this merry half-length figure in 1623; it belongs to the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, and is among his best-known tavern genre works.
credit: www.rijksmuseum.nl : Home : Info : Pic

title: The steadfast philosopher
description: A bearded scholar seated at a book-strewn table raises his hand in refusal as a laughing nude young woman in a feathered hat reaches toward him, staging the Stoic ideal of constantia. Signed and dated 1623, the candlelit half-length is held in the Hohenbuchau private collection at Schlangenbad and follows Honthorst's Utrecht practice of dramatising moral themes through strong chiaroscuro.
credit: Private collection institution QS:P195,somevalue,P3831,Q768717 Hohenbuchau, Schlangenbad

title: Christ Blessing the Children
description: Christ stands and places a hand on the head of a small child while a second child leans close, rendered in a spare, close-cropped composition against a landscape background. Artemisia Gentileschi painted this interpretation of the gospel injunction 'Suffer the little children to come unto me' between 1624 and 1625, applying the direct naturalism and strong colour contrasts associated with the Caravaggesque Baroque. The reduced cast of figures concentrates attention on the gesture of blessing rather than on narrative spectacle.

title: Laughing violinist making a fist
description: A laughing musician in a feathered cap raises a clenched fist while his violin is tucked under his left arm, his gaze directed off to the side as if sharing a joke with an unseen companion. Honthorst painted the half-length figure in 1624, employing the warm artificial light and direct engagement characteristic of his Utrecht Caravaggist manner.
credit: http://www.pubhist.com/w9532 pubhist.com

title: Lute Player
description: A young woman in a yellow-gold drape and a feathered cap holds a small stringed instrument, glancing to the side with a broad smile. The half-length single-figure format belongs to the series of Utrecht musician pictures Honthorst produced for the open market in the early 1620s, deriving from his study of Caravaggio's followers in Rome. The work is dated 1624.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"h/honthors/2/04lutepl"

title: Merry Violinist
description: A grinning young man in a feathered hat raises a wine glass while cradling a violin against his body, his expression caught in a moment of convivial pleasure. Painted circa 1624, this half-length belongs to the series of merry musicians that Honthorst's Utrecht workshop produced for the bourgeois market, each varied by costume and instrument.

title: Moses Striking the Rock
description: Moses lifts his rod over the desert rock as water gushes out for the kneeling Israelites who crowd forward with jars and children. Signed and dated 1624, the National Gallery of Art panel in Washington is one of Wtewael's late biblical pictures, executed on a small scale in the polished Mannerist manner he kept up long after the style had passed in Utrecht.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Solon and Croesus
description: The Lydian king Croesus, enthroned and crowned, gestures toward his treasure — gold coins and silver vessels arrayed on the floor before him — as the aged, barefooted Solon stands at right, staff in hand. A chained captive kneels at the king's feet, amplifying the contrast between material power and moral wisdom. Signed and dated 1624 and now in the Hamburger Kunsthalle, Honthorst stages the Herodotean encounter as a full-length figure composition, each character individuated in his characteristic manner.
credit: Kunsthalle, Hamburg

title: The guitar player
description: A young blonde woman in a white chemise with blue and yellow drapery plays a guitar, looking sideways with parted lips. Painted around 1624, the canvas is one of Honthorst's Utrecht single-figure musicians in which the open neckline and direct presentation pitch the work between portrait and genre piece for the cabinet market.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"h/honthors/2/051guita"

title: Büßende Maria Magdalena
description: Mary Magdalene sits in candlelit profile, one hand resting on a skull in her lap, before a candle whose flame is reflected in a gilt-framed mirror; pearls are scattered on the table beside her. Georges de La Tour's Penitent Magdalene at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (inv. 1978.517), dated 1625–1650, is one of several versions the artist made of this subject, each exploring how a single flame renders flesh, fabric, and vanitas objects in near-total darkness.

title: Granida and Daifilo
description: The shepherd Daifilo reclines at the feet of the princess Granida, gazing up at her in a leafy pastoral setting with goats visible in the background. Signed and dated 1625, Honthorst's canvas takes its subject from Pieter Cornelisz Hooft's popular Dutch pastoral play Granida, which served as a vehicle for veiled court portraiture in the period.

title: Head of a monk
description: A monk's head is shown in three-quarter view with downcast, closed eyes, the cowl framing a heavy, meditative face. The drawing, 277 by 196 mm, is held by the British Museum and dated between 1625 and 1664; it belongs to the body of figure studies Zurbarán made in connection with his austere Seville altarpieces depicting Carthusian and Mercedarian friars.
credit: British Museum

title: Job mocked by his Wife
description: A standing woman in a red robe holds a candle close to a seated, half-naked bearded man who bows his head — La Tour's depiction of Job mocked by his wife. The wife's gesture and downward gaze over the hunched figure convey both contempt and proximity, the single candle she carries casting warm light across both figures in a deep nocturnal field. The work is dated 1625–1650 and is attributed to Georges de La Tour.

title: Massacre of the Innocents
dateCreated: Entre 1625-1626 (selon Jacques Thuillier) et 1628-1629 (selon Anthony Blunt)
description: A soldier raises his sword to strike a mother who clutches her infant on the ground, while a woman in blue recoils in anguish at right. Poussin condenses the Massacre of the Innocents into a single searing triangle of figures, achieving maximum dramatic force through the stark confrontation of perpetrator, victim, and witness. The painting, dated between 1625 and 1629, is held at the Musée Condé, Chantilly.

title: Portrait of Marchese Ambrogio Spinola
description: Ambrogio Spinola, 1st Marquis of the Balbases and commander of the Habsburg forces in the Low Countries, is portrayed in ornate gold-inlaid parade armor with a large white ruff and a red shoulder piece, his grey hair and composed expression conveying seasoned authority. Rubens, who knew the marquess personally during the Twelve Years' Truce negotiations, painted this portrait in 1625; it is now in the National Gallery Prague (inv. O 9688).
credit: Národní galerie v Praze - online collection

title: Smiling Girl
description: A young woman grins broadly at the viewer while holding up a small framed picture of a couple in flagrante. Signed oil on canvas of 82 by 64 cm in the Saint Louis Art Museum, the painting belongs to the genre of Utrecht Caravaggesque half-figures in which Honthorst turned tavern wit into salon entertainment.
credit: Saint Louis Art Museum

title: The lapidation of Saint Stephen
description: Saul looks on from horseback as a knot of attackers raise stones above the kneeling deacon, who turns his face toward a beam of heavenly light. Signed and dated 1625, the canvas is Rembrandt's earliest documented painting, completed at nineteen in Leiden and now held by the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon.
credit: Œuvre appartenant au musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon Consulter cette image photographiée par Gilles Alonso spécialiste de la photo en gigapixel en très haute définition (+1 milliard de pixels)

title: The Matchmaker or The Procuress
description: A candle-lit brothel scene in which an old procuress brokers a young woman to a leering client. Honthorst, nicknamed Gherardo delle Notti in Rome, transplanted Caravaggio's tenebrism north; here a hidden flame carves the faces from the dark in glowing reds and ochres.

title: The Merry Student
description: A candlelit group scene shows a young man in a plumed hat raising a drink toward a laughing woman who plays a lute, with further figures and a table strewn with books, cards, food, and a globe visible in the background. The Caravaggist chiaroscuro and moralising props — open manuscript, overturned glass — announce the squandered-learning theme typical of Honthorst's Utrecht tavern pieces. Catalogued as number 391 in the Bavarian State Painting Collections, the work dates to around 1622–1625.

title: The Musicians' Brawl
description: Itinerant street musicians come to blows over a hurdy-gurdy, one wielding a knife as a companion squeezes a lemon to feign a wound. La Tour stages the brawl in cool daylight, his earlier Caravaggesque manner before he fully turned to candlelit nocturnes.

title: River landscape with Pan and Syrinx
description: A collaborative mythological landscape in which Rubens painted the figures of Pan pursuing the nymph Syrinx while Jan Brueghel the Younger supplied the dense reed bed and wooded river setting. Such partnerships between Antwerp masters were a hallmark of Flemish Baroque cabinet painting.
credit: Sotheby's, New York, 22 April 2015, lot 30

title: The Artist in his Studio
description: A small early panel showing a painter, dwarfed by an enormous panel on his easel, contemplating his work from across a bare studio. The image foregrounds thought rather than craft, framing painting as a fundamentally mental activity.

title: The Hermit and the Sleeping Angelica
description: An aged hermit, drawn from Ariosto's Orlando Furioso, gazes upon the nude, sleeping Angelica against a dark, shadowy background. Rubens contrasts the ascetic gauntness of the clothed old man with the luminous flesh of the recumbent figure, transforming the chivalric romance into a Baroque meditation on temptation. The small panel, painted between 1626 and 1628, is held in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/61other/05hermit"

title: 1627 Rubens Maria mit dem Kind anagoria
englishTitle: The Virgin and Child Enthroned with Saints
description: A Nursing Madonna: the Virgin, in a red gown, suckles the standing Christ Child while steadying an open illuminated book beside her. Climbing roses fill the upper left and a still life of fruit spills over the ledge at the right, opening onto a wooded landscape. Painted in 1627, the picture joins warm Rubensian figures to finely observed Flemish flower and fruit painting in the devotional manner cultivated in Counter-Reformation Antwerp; it hangs in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

title: Anton Giulio Brignole-Sale on horseback
description: The Genoese patron Anton Giulio Brignole-Sale rides forward on a grey horse, raising his hat, beside a tall column draped in crimson — an assertive equestrian formula van Dyck adapted from Rubens and Titian. Painted in 1627 during the artist's Italian sojourn, the canvas remains in Genoa at the Palazzo Rosso.

title: Christ on the Cross
description: A life-size crucified Christ emerges from impenetrable darkness, the body modelled with sculptural tenebrism that fooled at least one early viewer into thinking the work a polychrome carving. Painted for Seville's Dominican monastery of San Pablo, it announced Zurbarán's austere devotional manner.
credit: Art Institute of Chicago; Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"z/zurbaran/1/christ_x"

title: Adam and Eve
description: Rubens's homage to Titian, copied during his stay in Madrid where he studied the royal collection. The serpent-child reaches down to Eve as Adam grasps her arm; Rubens warms the Venetian palette and softens the contours toward his own fleshier ideal.

title: Pythagoras advocating vegetarianism
description: Rubens depicts the Greek philosopher gesturing toward a heap of fruit and grain as he urges his listeners to abstain from meat. The composition draws on Ovid's Metamorphoses, with abundant still-life passages painted in collaboration with Frans Snyders.

title: Rembrandt van Rijn - Zelfportret
description: An early self-portrait drawing of Rembrandt van Rijn, circa 1628–1629, in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Executed in pen, ink, and wash, the small work shows the young artist's curly-haired head in three-quarter view with energetic, searching line work. The informal medium and spontaneous handling distinguish it from the more finished self-portrait etchings and paintings of the same years.
credit: www.rijksmuseum.nl : Home : Info & Pic

title: Samson and Delilah
description: Delilah leans forward in shock as Philistine soldiers seize the shorn Samson from her lap, the moment of betrayal pitched between sensuality and violence. Van Dyck reworks Rubens's earlier composition with cooler colour and a more refined, elongated drawing.

title: Sansón matando al león
description: Samson grapples a roaring lion to the ground and tears its jaws apart, the biblical strongman rendered with anatomical force and twisting torso. Rubens reworked the subject several times, transposing the heroic male nude of antique sculpture into a violent Old Testament exemplum.
credit: El Imparcial

title: Self-portrait
description: The young Rembrandt presents himself in a close-cropped bust, face half-lost in raking shadow beneath a tangle of frizzy hair, set against a plain grey ground. Painted between 1628 and 1629 during his Leiden years, the picture is among the earliest in his long series of self-portraits and already shows the experimental chiaroscuro that would define his mature work.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rembrand/27self/03sp1628"

title: The Triumph of Bacchus
description: A pale, half-nude Bacchus crowns a kneeling soldier with vine leaves while a circle of weather-beaten Spanish drinkers grins out at the viewer. Painted in Madrid before Velázquez's first trip to Italy, the canvas pulls classical mythology down to tavern level with a sober, almost documentary realism.

title: Concert of Birds
description: An owl serves as conductor while a riot of songbirds reads from a sheet of music, a witty allegorical conceit Snyders treated repeatedly. The tightly observed plumage of finches, parrots and birds of prey reflects his standing as Antwerp's premier animal specialist.

title: Esther before Ahasuerus
description: The biblical queen swoons before the Persian king as she pleads for her people, a subject Gentileschi treats with operatic gesture and sumptuous fabrics. Painted during her Neapolitan years, it shows her assimilation of Caravaggesque drama into a more courtly, decorative key.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 436453)

title: Isabella von Bourbon
description: A state portrait of Isabella of Bourbon, queen consort of Spain, in stiff black court dress and pearls. Rubens softens the rigid Habsburg formula with subtle modelling of the face and a discreet warmth in the flesh tones.
credit: Kunsthistorisches Museum Wien, Bilddatenbank .

title: Minerva protects Pax from Mars
description: Painted in London for Charles I as a diplomatic gift, the allegory shows Minerva pushing back the war-god Mars while Pax nurses Plutus and children gather around the fruits of peace. The picture distilled Rubens's hopes for an Anglo-Spanish accord into a sumptuous tableau of bodies and abundance.
credit: The National Gallery, London

title: Portrait of Maria Louis de Tassis
description: Maria de Tassis is shown in a three-quarter-length portrait, wearing a starched lace ruff collar and a dark gown with gold-striped bodice, holding an ostrich-feather fan. Van Dyck painted the work circa 1629–30, bringing the silvery elegance of his Genoese manner to this Flemish aristocratic commission. The canvas is in the Liechtenstein princely collection at Vaduz.
credit: Fürstliche Sammlung Liechtenstein

title: Portrait of Thomas Howard
description: A bust-length portrait of Thomas Howard, 14th Earl of Arundel, shown in a dark fur-trimmed coat with white collar and a blue sash, a medal suspended from a ribbon at his chest. Rubens painted the Earl during his diplomatic visit to London around 1629–30, capturing the great English collector in the rich, restrained manner of his mature Flemish Baroque portraiture. The canvas is held by the National Gallery, London (NG2968).
credit: National Gallery, London - online catalogue .

title: Self-Portrait with Gorget
description: Bust-length self-portrait of the painter facing right, wearing a gleaming steel gorget over a white collar and gazing back at the viewer. Long catalogued as a Rembrandt, the panel in the Germanisches Nationalmuseum, Nuremberg, was reassigned by the Rembrandt Research Project to a Leiden studio assistant copying a lost prototype of about 1629.
credit: objektkatalog.gnm.de : Home : Info : Pic

title: Amor Asleep
description: A winged Cupid lies on his back in deep slumber, his nude body draped against rich red fabric, a candle or lamp glowing above him. The motif of the disarmed and sleeping god of love was a favourite of the Flemish Baroque tradition; this painting is linked to the Museo del Prado and dateable to around 1630.

title: Andromeda
description: Andromeda stands chained to a rock face, her arms raised above her head and bound at the wrists, her lower body draped in white cloth, while water and reeds are visible in the distance behind her. Perseus and the sea monster are absent from the composition, which Rembrandt treats as an intimate nude study rather than a heroic confrontation. Painted around 1630 and held at the Mauritshuis in The Hague, the small panel is one of his earliest mythological works.
credit: Geheugen van Nederland : Home : Info : Pic

title: Avondlandschap met boerenkar
englishTitle: Evening Landscape with a Timber Wagon
description: A peasant cart laden with felled timber rumbles down a rutted track as the day's last light catches clouds and treetops. The naturalistic Flemish countryside and warm low sun place this among the personal landscapes Rubens painted for his own pleasure.

title: Bust of an old man with a fur cap
description: A tronie, or character study, of an elderly bearded man in a fur cap and wide fur-collared coat, painted by Rembrandt van Rijn in 1630. The face is shown in three-quarter view, the light falling across deeply creased skin while the shaggy fur textures are rendered with close attention to surface variety. Works of this type — expressive head studies of anonymous figures in exotic costume — were a specialism of Rembrandt's early career.
credit: RKDimages, Art-work number 284532

title: Cats Fighting in a Larder
description: A pantry overturned by brawling cats among hanging game, fish and copper vessels, a kitchen-piece genre popularized by Frans Snyders and continued by his brother-in-law de Vos. The hissing animals serve as a moralized emblem of greed and chaos disrupting domestic order.

title: Drawing of mules by Claude Lorrain
description: Three mules stand in various poses across the sheet — one shown full length in profile with pack saddle on the left, the others more lightly indicated to the right. A brush drawing in brown wash over graphite, 143 by 257 mm, held at the British Museum, London, it is among the livestock studies Claude Lorrain made from observation, later informing the staffage of his pastoral and harbour compositions.
credit: British Museum [1]

title: Jeremiah Lamenting the Destruction of Jerusalem
description: The aged prophet leans on a sumptuous gold vessel, head in hand, while the city of Jerusalem smokes in the dim distance behind him. Signed and dated 1630, the panel in the Rijksmuseum is among Rembrandt's earliest narrative pictures to wed Caravaggesque chiaroscuro to a deeply introspective biblical subject.

title: Martyrdom of Saint Apollonia
description: The martyrdom of Saint Apollonia, whose teeth are being torn out while her pyre is prepared in the foreground. The print follows a composition by Jacob Jordaens and was engraved by the Antwerp printmaker Marinus Robyn van der Goes for the seventeenth-century devotional market.

title: Martyrdom of Saints John and Paul
description: A pen and brown ink with wash drawing shows an executioner raising a sword over a kneeling martyr while a second figure lies fallen to the right. The study, made by Guercino between 1630 and 1632, depicts the martyrdom of Saints John and Paul and is held at the Courtauld Institute of Art. The loose, energetic draughtsmanship and dramatic lighting typical of Guercino's preparatory works are evident in the quick contour lines and brown wash modelling.
credit: Courtauld Institute of Art

title: Portrait of a man
description: A three-quarter-length portrait of an unidentified man in black dress with a white lace ruff, standing before a large red curtain, his gaze direct and his bearing assured. Painted in 1630 and now in the Mauritshuis, The Hague, the portrait is typical of Rubens's formal likeness style in his mature Antwerp years.
credit: www.verenigingrembrandt.nl : Home : Info

title: Saint Luke as a painter
description: Saint Luke, traditionally credited with painting the Virgin's likeness, leans on a palette and gazes up at the crucified Christ, conflating the evangelist with the artist's own self-portrait. The sober brown ground and clipped lighting are characteristic of Zurbarán's monastic Sevillian commissions.
credit: Official gallery link

title: Self portrait in a cap
englishTitle: Self-Portrait in a Cap, Wide-Eyed and Open-Mouthed
description: Rembrandt depicts himself wide-eyed and open-mouthed in this tiny etching from 1630, one of a series of experimental self-portraits in which he pushed his own features into exaggerated expressions to study the physiognomy of emotion. The work, held at the Städel Museum, dates from his Leiden period and demonstrates the graphic virtuosity he was deploying as an advertisement of his skill.

title: Selfportrait
description: A tiny self-image of the painter in dark cloak and beret, head turned three-quarters into a pool of light. Measuring just 15.5 by 12.2 cm on copper and held by the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm, the panel is among Rembrandt's smallest self-portraits, made for the same collectors' cabinets that prized his etched heads of the same year.
credit: Erik Cornelius / Nationalmuseum

title: The Assumption of the Virgin
description: Mary ascends heavenward in a deep blue mantle, borne aloft by a cluster of putti amid billowing clouds framed by classical columns. Below, an empty stone sarcophagus draped in white linen marks her departed tomb, while additional putti scatter flowers. Painted around 1630, the work belongs to Poussin's early Roman period and reflects his engagement with Baroque altarpiece tradition.

title: The Fortune Teller
description: A naive young man has his palm read by an old gypsy while her accomplices pick his purse and cut his medal chain. La Tour stages the swindle in cool daylight rather than candlelight, exploiting fixed sidelong glances to spell out the deception.
credit: MET museum

title: The Garden of Love
description: Elegant couples flirt and recline in a balustraded garden while putti scatter roses overhead. Painted soon after Rubens's marriage to Helena Fourment, the scene celebrates conjugal pleasure in his late, pearly Flemish manner and now hangs in the Prado.

title: The Holy Family under the Apple Tree
description: The reverse panel of the Ildefonso Altar shows the Holy Family at rest beneath a fruiting apple tree, accompanied by the infant St John and St Anne, with putti above. Rubens links Eve's tree of knowledge to Christ's redemption through warm Flemish flesh, billowing draperies, and a luminous sky. Executed between 1630 and 1632, the altarpiece is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

title: The Three Graces
description: The three mythological Graces stand intertwined in an open garden setting, a garland of flowers suspended above and a fountain at right, their forms set against a luminous landscape sky. Rubens is said to have modelled the figures on his second wife Helena Fourment, celebrating a sensuous, unidealised standard of beauty. The painting, from around 1630–35, is held at the Museo del Prado.
credit: Museao del Prado [1]

title: Kanō Sansetsu - Frolicking Birds in Plum and Willow Trees
englishTitle: Frolicking Birds in Plum and Willow Trees
description: Against an expansive gold ground, the gnarled, almost calligraphic branches of a flowering plum extend across the panels while birds perch among the blossoms; a large pine at the right shelters a bird of prey on a rocky outcrop. Kanō Sansetsu (1589–1651), the prominent Kyoto Kanō master, stylises nature into bold rhythmic forms that push the school's bird-and-flower repertoire toward a distinctive early-Edo elegance. Dated 1631, the work is held at Myōshin-ji Temple, Kyoto.

title: Man with viola da gamba
description: A mustachioed musician in a feathered hat holds a viola da gamba and bow, glancing sideways with a hint of a smile against a dark background. The half-length musician type, here clothed in blue satin, continues the format Honthorst popularised after returning from Rome in 1620. The work is dated 1631 and hangs in the Lviv National Art Gallery.
credit: Self-photographed (from book)

title: The institution of the Eucharist during the Last Supper
description: Christ raises the bread at the centre of the long table while the apostles react in agitation; Judas turns toward the viewer with averted eyes. The picture concentrates on the moment of institution rather than the announcement of betrayal, in line with Counter-Reformation Eucharistic devotion.

title: Diana on the stag hunt
description: Diana and a group of hunters drive deer with hounds across an open landscape, the central goddess lunging forward with a spear as the quarry leaps ahead of the pack. Dated 1632 and held in the Bode Museum, Berlin, the panoramic composition distributes the action across a wide frieze, with landscape, animals, and figures typical of Rubens's collaborative hunting scenes.
credit: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

title: Hercules as Heroic Virtue Overcoming Discord
description: A powerful, bearded Hercules raises his club with one hand while seizing a writhing female personification of Discord by the head with the other, as a winged putto looks on from above. Discord, depicted with serpents, is forced down beneath him in a cloud-filled setting that conveys the allegory of heroic virtue overcoming civil strife. Painted between 1632 and 1633, the work is in the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Landscape with a Rainbow
description: A panoramic Flemish countryside after a storm, peasants and cattle moving among glistening fields beneath a translucent rainbow. Painted on his country estate at Het Steen, it shows Rubens turning to landscape in his late years with broad atmospheric breadth.
credit: Ermitage, Sankt Petersburg

title: Portrait of Aeltje Petersdr Uylenburgh
description: An elderly woman in a flat white collar and plain white linen cap meets the viewer's gaze with quiet composure, her face modelled in Rembrandt's characteristic warm chiaroscuro. Signed and dated 1632, this portrait of Aeltje Pietersdr. Uylenburgh belongs to the early Amsterdam years when Rembrandt was working in the studio of Hendrick Uylenburgh. The work is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: The abduction of Europa
description: Europa is borne away across the water on the back of Jupiter disguised as a white bull, while her companions react in alarm on the wooded shore beside an ornate carriage and white horses. Painted in 1632 and now in the J. Paul Getty Museum, the canvas brings an Ovidian subject into the idiom of a Dutch landscape, with a misty harbour and city walls receding into the left distance.

title: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr Nicolaes Tulp
description: A group portrait of the Amsterdam Surgeons' Guild gathered around the dissected forearm of an executed criminal. Tulp's demonstration of the flexor tendons and the differentiated reactions of his colleagues turn a guild commission into a study of attention.
credit: Mauritshuis online catalogue .

title: Christ in the Storm on the Sea of Galilee
description: The disciples struggle with sail and rigging on a heaving boat as Christ is roused to calm the sea. Rembrandt's only known seascape, it was stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in 1990 and remains missing.
credit: www.gardnermuseum.org : Home : Info : Pic

title: Portrait of Saskia van Uylenburgh
description: A portrait of the artist's wife shortly after their marriage, dressed in fanciful pastoral costume with a feathered hat. Rembrandt's warm light glances across pearls, embroidery, and her unguarded expression.
credit: www.rembrandtpainting.net : Home : Info

title: Venetia
description: Venetia, Lady Digby is shown the morning after her sudden death, propped against a pillow with a single rose shedding its petals. Commissioned by her grieving husband Sir Kenelm, the picture is a rare seventeenth-century memorial portrait painted from the corpse.

title: Cook at a Kitchen Table with Dead Game
description: A cook stands at a table laden with dead game birds — a peacock, pheasants, partridges and smaller fowl — raising a knife while a cat tugs at a peacock tail feather on the floor below. Additional birds hang from a hook at upper left. Painted between 1634 and 1637, the work is in the Hermitage Museum, St Petersburg.

title: Descent from the Cross
description: Christ's slack body is lowered from the cross onto a white shroud while torchlight picks out Joseph of Arimathea, the weeping Virgin and a clamouring crowd below. Signed and dated 1634, the canvas in the State Hermitage, Saint Petersburg, is the second of Rembrandt's full-scale Passion pictures commissioned by Stadholder Frederick Henry of Orange.
credit: www.artchive.com : Home : Info : Pic; arthermitage.org; The Hermitage, St. Petersburg

title: Flora
description: Saskia van Uylenburgh in the guise of the goddess Flora, a garland of roses and mixed blooms crowning her head and a flowering staff in her hand. Signed and dated 1634, the canvas at the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg was painted in the year of Rembrandt's marriage, recasting his young wife in Venetian pastoral dress.

title: Hércules lucha con la hidra de Lerna
description: Hercules grapples with the many-headed Hydra of Lerna, his muscular body twisting against the dark serpentine coils. The canvas belongs to a series of ten Labours of Hercules painted for the Hall of Realms in the Buen Retiro Palace, where Zurbarán's stark tenebrism set the hero against an almost theatrical void.
credit: Galería online , Museo del Prado.

title: Nicolas Poussin - L'Enlèvement des Sabines
description: Roman soldiers seize Sabine women in a violent twist of bodies, framed by classicizing architecture. Poussin choreographs the abduction as a sculptural relief of opposing diagonals, applying his rigorous study of antique gesture to the legendary founding episode of Rome.

title: Portrait of Haesje Jacobsdr. van Cleyburg
description: A bust-length portrait of a middle-aged woman in a black gown and wide pleated white ruff collar, set within a painted oval and turned slightly toward the viewer. Signed and dated 1634, the panel in the Rijksmuseum depicts Haesje Jacobsdr. van Cleyburg and is the pendant to a portrait of Dirck Pesser, together among the Amsterdam burgher commissions that established Rembrandt as the city's leading portraitist.
credit: www.rijksmuseum.nl : Home : Info : Pic

title: The Battle of Nördlingen
description: Two armoured commanders on horseback dominate the foreground, surveying the sprawling engagement below as troops and banners mass toward the right and smoke rises over the distant plain. Jan van der Hoecke's large canvas, painted in 1634 and now in the Royal Collection at Windsor Castle (RCIN 400100), commemorates the Habsburg victory at Nördlingen — one of the decisive engagements of the Thirty Years' War — in the grand battle-piece manner Rubens established for court patronage.
credit: Royal Collection

title: A Landscape with Cows and Duck Hunters
description: A wooded pastoral landscape in which a large herd of cattle fills the foreground, with dairymaids milking and carrying filled copper jugs, while a figure at right appears to be a hunter near the water. Painted by Rubens between 1635 and 1638, the work belongs to a group of expansive Flemish landscapes notable for their loose, atmospheric handling, and is held by the Gemäldegalerie Berlin.
credit: Objekt in der Onlinesammlung der Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin: 865663 Fotograf: Christoph Schmidt

title: Atalanta and Hippomenes
description: Hippomenes sprints ahead as Atalanta stoops to retrieve one of the golden apples, the mythological wager from Ovid's Metamorphoses that costs her the race. The painting, attributed to Jacob Peter Gowy after a design by Rubens and dated between 1635 and 1637, is held at the Museo del Prado. Spectators crowd the background while the two protagonists surge diagonally across the foreground, their fluttering drapery and animated bodies typical of Flemish Baroque treatment of Ovidian subjects.

title: Bathsheba at Her Toilet
description: Bathsheba sits at her bath while a black page delivers David's letter, the Old Testament narrative reframed as an excuse for sumptuous flesh, drapery, and still life. The painting now hangs in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.

title: Belshazzar's Feast
description: The Babylonian king recoils as a glowing Hebrew inscription, MENE MENE TEKEL UPHARSIN, appears on the wall during his blasphemous feast. Rembrandt stages the moment with theatrical lighting, overturned vessels, and a sumptuous gold-embroidered cloak.
credit: www.nationalgallery.org.uk : Home : Info

title: Charles I
description: Van Dyck painted Charles I simultaneously from three angles — left profile, full face, and three-quarter right — providing the sculptor Gian Lorenzo Bernini with the reference views needed to carve a marble bust without the king travelling to Rome. Executed between 1635 and 1636 and now in the Royal Collection (RCIN 404420), the work is one of the most innovative portraits of the Stuart court, combining technical virtuosity with a dynastic purpose beyond the conventions of single-sitter portraiture.

title: Francisco de Zurbarán 006
description: A bound lamb lies on a grey ledge against a dark ground, an Agnus Dei meditation on Christ's sacrifice rendered with extraordinary fleecy detail. The picture, in the Prado, distils Zurbarán's ascetic Sevillian piety into one of the most economical still lifes of the Spanish Baroque.

title: Market Scene on a Quay - Frans Snyders and Workshop
description: A teeming Antwerp quayside laden with game, fish, fruit and live animals, painted on a near three-metre canvas typical of Snyders's grand market series. The Flemish Baroque specialist often collaborated with Rubens on such still-life pageants, and his workshop reproduced the format for aristocratic dining halls.

title: Nativity of St. John the Baptist
description: An interior crowded with attendants tends to the newborn John the Baptist while Elizabeth rests nearby. Gentileschi treats the sacred subject as a domestic event, modelling figures in the warm tenebrist light typical of her Neapolitan period.
credit: Museo del Prado info pic

title: Rape of Ganymede
description: Rembrandt reimagines the classical myth as a startled, urinating infant snatched skyward by Jupiter's eagle. The unsettling realism breaks sharply with the idealized Italian tradition of the subject.
credit: Cropped from File:Rembrandt - The Abduction of Ganymede - Google Art Project.jpg , originally from Google Art Project.

title: Saint Teresa of Avila's vision of the dove
description: Saint Teresa of Ávila kneels in her Carmelite habit, hands raised and gaze lifted towards a dove descending from above in a burst of light. The finished painting of 1635, in the Fitzwilliam Museum, presents the saint's mystical vision with controlled drapery and luminous effect characteristic of Rubens's devotional works.

title: Still Life with Fruit
description: The Antwerp specialist piles a Baroque larder with grapes, peaches, dead hare and game birds, animated by a thieving monkey, a wary cat and a darting squirrel. Snyders, Rubens's regular still-life collaborator, treats abundance as theatre, a moralising display of plenty under threat.
credit: Hohenbuchau Collection, on permanent loan to Liechtenstein, The Princely Collections, Vienna

title: The Birth of Venus
description: Venus rises from the sea attended by tritons, nereids and putti in a Baroque treatment of the Anadyomene theme. Poussin organizes the marine cortege into a frieze-like rhythm, marrying Ovidian mythology with the cool classical structure he distilled from antique relief sculpture.

title: The Brazen Serpent
description: Moses raises the bronze serpent on a pole as Israelites writhe with snakebites below, looking up to be healed (Numbers 21). Rubens packs the foreground with anatomical contortions, a Counter-Reformation allegory of salvation through faith in the Crucified.

title: The lamentation over the dead Christ
description: The dead Christ lies stretched out on a white shroud over blue drapery, his head fallen back toward the Virgin, who throws her arms wide in grief while Saint John and weeping angels gather around the body beneath a darkened sky. Anthony van Dyck painted this horizontal Lamentation in oil on canvas around 1635, after his return to Antwerp from England. It hangs in the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), inventory number 404.
credit: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

provenance.collection: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp
provenance.location: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

title: The rape of Europa
description: Europa, in a red drape, clings to the horn of a white bull as it carries her through turbulent waves, her hair streaming in the wind. Erasmus Quellinus II painted this interpretation of Ovid's myth in 1635; the canvas is in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.

title: The Repentant Magdalen
description: The Magdalen sits in near-total darkness, her face faintly lit as she rests her cheek on her hand and contemplates a skull placed before her on a ledge. A candle provides the sole source of light, and a mirror to her left reflects its glow. La Tour pares the vanitas iconography to its essentials, letting the single flame model her features with calm geometry, in a composition dateable to circa 1635–1640.

title: The Sacrifice of Isaac
description: An angel seizes Abraham's arm at the moment the knife slips from his grasp, while Isaac lies bound and bare-chested on the altar below. Signed and dated 1635, the canvas in the Hermitage in St Petersburg depicts the binding of Isaac at its most violent instant, with the blade caught in mid-fall — one of Rembrandt's most kinetic early narrative compositions.

title: The Surrender of Breda
description: Justin of Nassau hands the keys of the Dutch city to the Genoese general Ambrogio Spinola, who lays a conciliatory hand on the defeated commander's shoulder.
