The forest of upright Spanish pikes that gives the painting its nickname, Las Lanzas, organises the right half of the composition, painted for the Hall of Realms in the Buen Retiro.

title: A View of Het Steen in the Early Morning
description: Rubens's own country estate near Mechelen lies under a low, golden dawn, with a hunter, hay wagon and far-flung fields stretching to the horizon. The expansive panorama, painted for personal pleasure, helped redirect Northern landscape toward atmospheric naturalism.
credit: httpsː//www.nationalgallery.org.uk/paintings/peter-paul-rubens-a-view-of-het-steen-in-the-early-morning

title: Adoration of the Magi
description: A Neapolitan-period altarpiece in which the Magi crowd around the Virgin and Child by torchlight. Gentileschi pushes the figures close to the picture plane and stages the gift-giving in heavy raking light, drawing on the Caravaggism she had carried south from Rome.
credit: http://www.museumsyndicate.com/item.php?item=26954 https://picasaweb.google.com/lh/photo/vLoMRu1PcbSaDYUKQ0cZGdMTjNZETYmyPJy0liipFm0?full-exif=true

title: Diana and two nymphs surprised by satyrs while bathing
description: Diana and her companions recoil from leering satyrs at a forest pool in a late mythological invention treating chastity disturbed. Rubens entrusted much of the landscape and animal staffage to specialist collaborators, while reserving the warm, dimpled female nudes for himself.
credit: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

title: Landscape with a Rainbow
englishTitle: Landscape with Cattle and a Rainbow (Wallace Collection)
description: A broad Flemish countryside opens out under a sky cleared by a passing storm, a rainbow arching over fields, milkmaids and grazing cattle. Often paired with the View of Het Steen, it expresses Rubens's late identification with the land around his country house.
credit: https://wallacelive.wallacecollection.org:443/eMP/eMuseumPlus?service=ExternalInterface&module=collection&objectId=64938&viewType=detailView Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/5landsca/16landsc"

title: Landscape with a Tower
description: A small panel showing a fortified tower set on a wooded rise, approached by a slender bridge under the warm light of a lowering sun. The intimate scale and rapid, fluid brushwork are characteristic of the late landscape sketches Rubens made around his estate at Elewijt.
credit: Objekt in der Onlinesammlung der Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin: 867302 Fotograf: Jörg P. Anders

title: Landscape with Cows
description: Cattle are tended and milked by farmers in a broad Flemish meadow beneath a dramatic, cloud-filled sky. Rubens painted such pastoral subjects in the mid-1630s, around the time he acquired his country estate at Het Steen; the work is held in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich (Bavarian State Painting Collections, inv. 322).

title: Mercury and Argus
description: In a wooded landscape, Mercury raises his sword to slay the sleeping Argus, who slumps at his feet exhausted. A white heifer — the transformed Io — stands to the left, the immediate object of this divine mission. Painted between 1636 and 1638, the composition draws on Ovid's Metamorphoses and exemplifies Rubens's late handling of mythological narrative in monumental outdoor settings.

title: Orpheus and the animals
description: Orpheus charms a menagerie of beasts and birds with his lyre, the Ovidian subject becoming a pretext for Snyders's encyclopaedic display of fur, feather and scale. The composition crowds exotic species into a forested clearing in the Flemish Baroque manner.

title: Saturn
description: The aged god Saturn devours one of his infant sons, biting into the flesh as the child writhes in his grip beneath the cold light of his eponymous planet. Painted for Philip IV's Torre de la Parada, Rubens fuses Ovidian myth with unflinching late-Baroque violence.

title: Silenus
description: A lean, elderly faun stands before a stone pedestal, one arm raised holding a pelt or cloth, the other hand carrying what appears to be a mask or severed head. The muscular yet weathered figure, painted by Rubens between 1636 and 1638, exemplifies the studio's engagement with antique subjects of Bacchic mythology.

title: Susanna
description: Rembrandt's small panel catches Susanna at the moment she steps from her robe, glancing back with sudden alarm as the elders emerge from the dark garden. The pearly nude and deep umber surroundings show the painter testing a Lastman-derived biblical mode in the year of Danaë.

title: The Blinding of Samson
description: A violent rendering of Judges 16, with Philistine soldiers pinning Samson while a blade is driven into his eye and Delilah flees with the shorn hair. Rembrandt extracts maximal drama from a sudden shaft of daylight cutting into the cave-like darkness.

title: The creation of the milky way
description: The infant Hercules, set to Juno's breast by Jupiter, draws milk so forcefully that the spilled stream becomes the Milky Way. Painted for Philip IV's Torre de la Parada, the canvas turns an Ovidian etiology into a swirl of cosmic drapery and divine flesh.

title: The Feast of Venus
description: Worshippers garland a statue of Venus while putti, nymphs and satyrs dance in pagan revelry. Inspired by Titian's Worship of Venus and a passage in Philostratus, the late composition assembles Rubens's lifelong vocabulary of mythic celebration.

title: The Massacre of the Innocents - Peter Paul Rubens
englishTitle: The Massacre of the Innocents (Alte Pinakothek, c. 1638)
description: Herod's soldiers wrench infants from their mothers in a writhing knot of bodies before a palace portico, the women clawing and biting back at their attackers. This is Rubens's second, late treatment of the subject, painted around 1636-38 with the loose handling and theatrical energy of his final decade. The monumental canvas, over three metres wide, hangs in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich.

title: The Rape of Europe
description: Europa clings to the white bull as he moves swiftly forward, her wind-blown drapery in red and pink behind her. This small oil sketch, dated 1636 and now in the Museo del Prado, is a modello related to Rubens's engagement with Titian's celebrated composition of the same subject, paying homage to Venetian colour in a rapid, fluid touch.

title: The Sacrament of Ordination
description: Christ gestures upward as he delivers the keys to a kneeling Peter, with the remaining apostles gathered around them in an open landscape setting. From Poussin's second series of the Seven Sacraments, painted between circa 1636 and 1640, the composition translates the scriptural moment of institutional founding into the artist's mature, archaeologically informed figure style. The work is held at the Kimbell Art Museum.

title: A Polish Nobleman
description: A bearded man in furred coat and a tall fur cap, a heavy gold chain across his chest, turning to meet the viewer's eye. Signed and dated 1637, the panel in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, belongs to Rembrandt's series of tronies of sitters in exotic and Eastern European costume rather than to commissioned portraiture.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: An Elephant
description: A chalk drawing of a tame Asian elephant, the wrinkled hide rendered with close hatching and smudged strokes, the trunk extended as the animal walks. Signed and dated 1637, the sheet is one of several studies Rembrandt made of Hansken, a celebrated travelling elephant who visited Amsterdam and other Dutch cities during the 1630s.

title: The abduction of the Sabines
description: Roman soldiers seize the Sabine women at Romulus's signal in a frieze of taut, sculptural figures arrayed before classical architecture. Poussin choreographs the violence with archaeological detail and disciplined gesture, exemplifying the rational French classicism he forged in Rome.
credit: photo Shonagon 2016-10-25

title: The Consequences of War
description: An allegory painted for the Medici and addressed to the disasters of the Thirty Years' War. Mars, dragged forward by a Fury, tramples the arts and a despairing Europe, while Venus tries vainly to restrain him — Rubens's late, politically engaged history painting at its most charged.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/30allego/06allego"

title: As the Old Sing
description: A multi-generational Flemish family bellows around a table while a child blows a pipe, illustrating the proverb inscribed at the top: as the old sing, so the young pipe. Jordaens returned to the boisterous moralised feast many times, this version inscribed Ut genus est genius.
credit: The National Gallery of Canada

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Bacchus
description: The wine god is shown half-length, his head garlanded with vine leaves and full grape clusters, holding a large glass goblet in both hands while bunches of grapes trail across his bare torso. Wtewael, the Utrecht Mannerist who excelled in small cabinet pictures and mythological subjects, gives Bacchus a fleshy, ruddy vitality against a dark ground. The work is dated before 1638.

title: Bull subdued by dogs
description: A bull-baiting scene of the kind de Vos perfected in Rubens's Antwerp circle, with mastiffs lunging at a tethered bull's flanks. The diagonal tangle of muscle, horn and fang demonstrates the Flemish taste for animal combats as showcases of anatomical drama and tonal bravura.

title: Het Pelsken
description: An intimate, near-life-size portrait of Rubens's second wife Helena Fourment, draped only in a fur cloak. The picture's frank sensuality and tender naturalism mark it as a private image, kept in the artist's own household.

title: Landscape with the Good Samaritan
description: An imaginary landscape staging Christ's parable beneath a turbulent, storm-bruised sky. Rembrandt dwarfs the small figures of the Samaritan and the wounded traveller at lower right within a vast expanse of rocky terrain, tossed trees, and brooding tonal contrasts that recall the influence of Hercules Seghers. Dated 1638, the work exemplifies Rembrandt's brief engagement with the heroic landscape tradition.

title: Landscape with the Tower of Castle "Steen"
englishTitle: Landscape with the Tower of Het Steen
description: A panoramic view of the country estate Rubens purchased in 1635, with its turreted manor set among golden Brabant fields. The artist treats native landscape with vigorous brushwork and a low, glowing horizon, anticipating later Romantic vistas.

title: Self-Portrait as the Allegory of Painting
description: Gentileschi merges self-portrait and emblem, depicting herself as the personification of Painting from Ripa's Iconologia: brush raised, gold chain bearing a mask, sleeves pushed back over a working arm. The conceit could only be staged by a woman, since the allegory was female.

title: Selfportrait
description: The painter, near sixty, presents himself in broad-brimmed hat, sword, and gloves — courtier and diplomat as much as artist. The dignified late self-portrait, withholding palette and brushes, asserts his ennoblement and standing among Europe's rulers.
credit: Kunsthistorisches Museum

title: The Crucifixion of Saint Peter
description: The apostle is shown crucified upside down at his own request, his contorted, foreshortened body filling a tall altarpiece format. Commissioned for St Peter's Church in Cologne, the work was among the artist's last major altarpieces, completed shortly before his death and dispatched to the parish where his father had once lived.

title: The Judgment of Paris
englishTitle: The Judgement of Paris (late version, c. 1638)
description: Paris awards the golden apple to Venus while Juno and Minerva recoil in defeat, their nudes arranged in a graceful triad against an Arcadian landscape. Rubens revisited this mythological subject several times; the late Prado version is among his most assured.

title: The Raising of the Cross
englishTitle: The Raising of the Cross (modello after the Antwerp triptych, 1638)
description: Straining executioners heave the cross bearing Christ skyward in a violent diagonal of muscular labor. A late reprise of his Antwerp altarpiece, this version concentrates the drama into a tighter, more urgent gathering of bodies and tackle.

title: Virgin with Child and saints
description: Painted as the altarpiece for Rubens's own funerary chapel in St Jacob's Church, Antwerp, the panel surrounds the Virgin and Child with saints in whose features the artist included self-portrait and family likenesses. It is among his last works, executed in the warm, fluid manner of his final Antwerp years.
credit: Musea en Erfgoed Antwerpen

title: Diana and nymphs attacked by satyrs
description: Diana and her companions, returning from the hunt with hounds and game, are accosted by lecherous satyrs at the edge of a wood. The collision of nude bodies, fur and dead quarry typifies Rubens's late mythological mode.

title: Hercules and the Nemean Lion
description: Hercules grapples the invulnerable Nemean lion in a knot of straining limbs, the hero's first labor reduced to its essential close-quarters violence. The Apsley House version follows a Rubens prototype that translates antique sculptural sources, especially the Belvedere Torso, into Baroque flesh and sinew.

title: Hercules Strangling the Nemean Lion
description: Hercules wraps the invulnerable lion in a strangling embrace, the hero's bunched muscles answered by the beast's twisting flank. The motif derives from antique sarcophagi Rubens had studied in Italy.
credit: Harvard Art Museums

title: Naked old man
description: An academic figure study of an aged male model, drawn from life with the meaty corporeality typical of the Antwerp Baroque. Jordaens repeatedly used such studies as a stockpile for the satyrs, river gods, and apostles populating his crowded canvases.

provenance.collection: Department of Prints and Drawings of the Louvre

title: Self-Portrait Leaning on a Stone Sill
description: Rembrandt leans his folded arm on a stone ledge, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer and wearing a beret and furred cloak — a composition that self-consciously echoes the poses of Titian and Raphael portraits then in Dutch collections. Signed and dated 1639, this is among the most ambitious of Rembrandt's self-portrait etchings, the work now held in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: www.nga.gov : Home : Info

title: A Female Saint and Martyr
description: A young woman in a mauve robe leans on a stone ledge, her arms resting on a book with a martyr's palm beside her, her gaze turned toward a distant landscape. Painted by Artemisia Gentileschi around 1640 and tentatively identified as Saint Catherine of Alexandria, the painting is in the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.

title: Four Studies of a Head of a Moor
description: Four oil sketches of the same Black sitter, observed from different angles and in varied light, made as working material for finished compositions including the Adoration of the Magi. The studies are notable for their direct, dignified attention to an individual model.

provenance.collection: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

title: Pierre Paul RUBENS
description: A religious oil painting by Flemish master Peter Paul Rubens depicting the miraculous appearance of Saint Justus, who stands at center holding his severed head in his hands with onlookers present. Created by 1640 and held in the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Bordeaux, this work exemplifies Rubens' dramatic Baroque composition and rich color palette.

title: Portrait of Mary Ruthven
description: Van Dyck's wife Mary Ruthven is shown in a rich blue satin gown with pearl necklace and gold hair ornament, posed with calm composure against a dark ground. The portrait, dated 1640, is unusually domestic in register for the painter, setting aside the aristocratic trappings of his formal commissions in favour of a quiet, personal likeness.

title: Prometheus Bound
description: Chained to the Caucasus, Prometheus writhes as the eagle of Zeus rends his liver — a punishment renewed each day. Jordaens treats the Titan with brawny, ruddy realism, working in the Rubensian Antwerp idiom of muscular flesh and dramatic chiaroscuro.
credit: Wallraf-Richartz-Museum

title: Rachel de Ruvigny
description: Rachel de Ruvigny, Countess of Southampton, is shown in blue and white satin drapery beside a large terrestrial globe, a skull resting at her feet in a Vanitas allusion to worldly transience. The full-length allegorical portrait, painted around 1640, is in the collection of the National Gallery of Victoria, Melbourne, and is among van Dyck's most ambitious English-period compositions.
credit: National Gallery of Victoria

title: The Dream of Saint Joseph
description: An angel appears to the sleeping Joseph in a candlelit interior, the standard Lorraine nocturne formula put to a religious end. The shielded flame, smooth modelling and quiet psychology are characteristic of La Tour's mature devotional pictures.

title: The Feast of the Bean King
description: A boisterous Twelfth Night feast in which whoever finds the bean in the cake reigns as king while companions roar 'The king drinks!' Jordaens returned to the proverbial subject several times, packing the table with three generations and the wet-eyed comedy of overindulgence.

title: Woman with a Mirror
description: A half-length figure of a clothed woman in a dark dress with white collar and ruffled sleeves looks down at a small dark mirror held in one hand, her other hand raised to her hair. The composition, calm and interior in character, is held in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Kassel, and dated to around 1640.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/30allego/08allego"

title: Scholar at his Writing Table
description: A bearded scholar in a fur-trimmed gown and black cap sits at a writing table, quill in hand over an open book, caught in a moment of concentration. Painted in 1641 and now in the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin, the canvas is the pendant to The Girl in a Picture Frame and is among the few Rembrandt pairs to have survived together.
credit: pl.pinterest.com

title: The Girl in a Picture Frame
description: A young woman leans out of a painted frame, her hands resting on the illusory ledge in a sly play on the picture's own boundary. The trompe l'oeil device reflects Rembrandt's interest in animating the threshold between image and viewer.
credit: kolekcja.zamek-krolewski.pl

title: The Windmill
description: An etching of a stout post mill rising above a bastion, probably the bulwark known as 'Het Blauwhoofd' on the Amstel, etched by Rembrandt van Rijn in 1641. The composition places the mill and its adjoining low buildings close to the picture plane, with open countryside stretching behind. Rembrandt's drypoint reinforcements give the brickwork and timber a characteristic grainy luminosity prized by collectors of his prints.

title: Famille de paysans dans un intérieur
artist: Attributed to Louis Le Nain / Antoine Le Nain
description: A peasant family pauses around a sparse table in a dim cottage interior, each face turned outwards with quiet directness. The Le Nain brothers' rare empathetic treatment of rural poverty, painted in a sober earthen palette, anticipates the realism of Courbet two centuries later.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Searching for Immortals
description: An album leaf from Shitao's (1642–1707) Landscapes series, part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art collection. This work exemplifies the Qing dynasty master's innovative approach to landscape painting, blending Southern school traditions with his distinctive expressionistic style.
commonsUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:清 石濤(朱若極) 山水圖 冊-Searching for Immortals MET DP162813.jpg

title: Self-Portrait in a Flat Cap
description: Rembrandt van Rijn gazes outward in this 1642 self-portrait wearing a black flat cap and dark fur-trimmed coat, a gold chain visible at the chest. The face is lit from the upper left against a neutral grey-green ground. RCIN 404120 in the Royal Collection, the panel is among the most composed of Rembrandt's mid-career self-portraits.
credit: Royal Collection

title: The Night Watch
description: Captain Frans Banning Cocq in black with red sash steps forward giving the order to march, Lieutenant Willem van Ruytenburch in pale yellow strides beside him, and the company tumbles into motion behind. Signed and dated 1642, the canvas of 363 by 437 cm in the Rijksmuseum is the largest of the Amsterdam civic-guard group portraits.

title: The three trees Alternative title
description: Three trees crown a low rise above a flat Dutch polder, with a thunderstorm rolling in from the left and tiny figures fishing and sketching at the margins. Rembrandt's largest landscape etching combines drypoint and engraving to model an unusually dramatic sky.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art

title: Daedalus and Icarus
description: Daedalus attaches wings to the seated young Icarus, who raises his arm as if readying himself for flight. Attributed to Charles Le Brun and dated between 1645 and 1646, the canvas was painted during the artist's Roman period when he was working in proximity to Poussin, whose classicising influence is evident in the monumental figure grouping.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/l/le_brun/daedalus"

title: Judith and her maid Abra with the Head of Holofernes
description: By candlelight Judith stands and turns, her hand raised near the flame, while Abra crouches at her feet tending to the severed head of Holofernes. A late work from Gentileschi's Naples period, dated circa 1645–1650, the painting is held at the Museo di Capodimonte and revisits the artist's signature subject in a quieter, nocturnal register, the single candle gilding the women's drapery against deep shadow.

title: The Mill
description: A windmill stands silhouetted against a turbulent, luminous sky on a high earthen rampart above a quiet river. Long read as a brooding emblem of Dutch identity, the painting fuses topographical record with charged atmosphere.

title: The Rape of Lucretia
description: A woman lies on a bed, restrained by a male assailant who threatens her with a knife while a second figure looks on from the left — a depiction of the rape of Lucretia rather than her subsequent suicide. Attributed to Artemisia Gentileschi and dated circa 1645–1650, the large canvas is held at the New Palace (Neues Palais), Potsdam. The dramatic chiaroscuro and forceful physical confrontation are characteristic of Gentileschi's Baroque manner.

title: Le Souffleur à la pipe
description: A young man in a dark cap leans forward and blows on the glowing tip of a burning stick or coal, the ember's light illuminating his cheek and jaw against a near-black ground; a long pipe is held in his other hand. Georges de La Tour's Le Souffleur à la pipe (1646) depicts the act of kindling a pipe rather than smoking one, reducing the subject to an intimate nocturne built around a single point of combustion. The work is held at the Tokyo Fuji Art Museum.
credit: Tokyo Fuji Art Museum

title: Winter Landscape
description: A small winter landscape of 1646, now in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden, showing figures in a frost-bound village setting with bare trees and low farm buildings beneath a pale, luminous sky. The thinly brushed surface and cool, silvery palette are unusual among Rembrandt's works, placing this panel in a distinctly Dutch tradition of winter landscape painting.
credit: www.tweevioleneneenbas.nl : Home : Info : Pic

title: Portret van Willem II
description: William II, Prince of Orange, stands in full armour with a commander's baton beside his English wife Mary Stuart on a balcony, both shown full-length. Painted in 1647 for the Stadholder's court, the double portrait belongs to the Rijksmuseum (SK-A-871) and helped fix Honthorst's reputation as the dynasty's preferred image-maker.
credit: Rijksmuseum

title: Susanna and the Elders
description: The chaste Susanna shrinks as the two elders intrude upon her bath, drawn from the Book of Daniel. Rembrandt focuses on her vulnerability and the elders' menace, modeling flesh and drapery with a soft, glowing chiaroscuro.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rembran/painting/biblic1/suzanna"

title: The Sacrifice of Polyxena
description: Polyxena is led to the altar to appease the ghost of Achilles while her mother Hecuba reaches to restrain her and the soldier Neoptolemus lifts his sword. Le Brun painted the subject from Ovid's Metamorphoses in 1647, before his career as premier peintre to Louis XIV.

title: Allegory of Painting
description: In this Allegory of Painting attributed to Gerard van Honthorst (1648), a seated woman holds palette and brushes while painting a male portrait, a winged putto leaning over the canvas behind them. The controlled chiaroscuro and intimate grouping are characteristic of Honthorst's mature Dutch Baroque style.
credit: Self-photographed , Amadscientist , 2012-07-01

title: Christ Preaching
description: Christ stands at the centre with the sick crowded to his right and parents pressing children toward him on the left, the dark archway opening onto Lazarus the leper. Known as the Hundred Guilder Print for the unprecedented price it fetched in Rembrandt's lifetime, the etching combines drypoint and engraving to compress several episodes from Matthew 19 into one nocturnal scene.

title: Portrait of Innocent X
description: A famously unflinching state portrait of the pope, whose shrewd, suspicious gaze emerges from a cascade of crimson and white. Velázquez orchestrates a near-monochrome of vermilions and rose tones, using fluid brushwork to render lace, silk and satin with startling immediacy.

title: Susanna and the Elders
englishTitle: Susanna and the Elders (later autograph version)
description: A late treatment of the Book of Daniel episode, with the bathing Susanna recoiling from the two judges who threaten to denounce her. Gentileschi returned to the subject across her career, here in a more restrained, tenebrist key than her early Pommersfelden version.
credit: Moravian Gallery in Brno

title: Equestrian portrait of Louis XIV of France
artist: Charles Le Brun / Adam Frans van der Meulen
description: Louis XIV reins in a rearing mount in a gold-brocade costume with red ribbons and a red-plumed hat, a blue sash at his waist, while troops mass on the plain beyond. The canvas is attributed jointly to Charles Le Brun and the Flemish battle painter Adam Frans van der Meulen and hangs in the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Tournai.
credit: BridgemanortonDemand.com; Bridgeman Art Library : Object 208670

title: Frederik Hendrik
description: Frederick Henry, Prince of Orange (1584–1647), is shown in three-quarter length wearing full burnished armour and a blue sash of office against a red draped curtain. This posthumous workshop portrait, produced in 1650 by the atelier of Gerard van Honthorst, is held in the Rijksmuseum collection.
credit: www.rijksmuseum.nl : Home : Info : Pic

title: Greyhound Catching a Young Wild Boar
description: A white greyhound pins a young wild boar to the ground in an open landscape of rolling hills and scattered vegetation, a cloudy sky above. The work displays the precise animal anatomy Snyders brought to hunting subjects, and dates to the first half of the seventeenth century.

title: Juan de Pareja
description: Velázquez painted this portrait of Juan de Pareja — his enslaved assistant and a painter of Moorish descent — in Rome in 1650 as a demonstration of his skill. The sitter's dignified bearing is rendered in a restrained palette of dark olive, grey, and brown, the face emerging with remarkable presence from the plain neutral background. Now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (inv. 1971.86), the portrait was exhibited at the Pantheon in Rome before Velázquez freed Pareja.

title: Landscape with a Calm
description: An Italianate landscape with a shepherd and goats in the foreground, a horseman near a rustic shelter at left, and a fortified villa reflected in the still waters of a pool. Poussin organises the composition with characteristic measure, placing each figure and architectural element for balance rather than picturesque incident. The work, dated 1650–51, is held at the J. Paul Getty Museum.

title: Les reines de Perse aux pieds d'Alexandre dit aussi la tente de Darius
englishTitle: The Queens of Persia at the Feet of Alexander (The Tent of Darius)
description: The mother, wife and daughters of the defeated Darius prostrate themselves before Alexander and Hephaestion in the Persian camp after Issus. Painted between 1660 and 1661 and shown to Louis XIV at Fontainebleau, the canvas won Le Brun his role as premier peintre and ushered in his cycle of Alexander histories for the Crown.

title: Lying Lioness
description: A lioness lies collapsed against a wooded rocky ground, her head turned toward the viewer with mouth slightly open, in a large-format oil attributed to Frans Snyders now held at the Liechtenstein Museum. Snyders, the leading Flemish Baroque animal painter, brought close observation and confident brushwork to his animal subjects throughout his career in Antwerp.
credit: Liechtenstein Museum

title: Narcissus
description: The Antwerp Baroque painter Jan Cossiers depicts Narcissus nearly full-length, kneeling beside a pool and gazing at his reflection, a red drapery billowing behind him. A strong raking light models the flesh against a shadowy landscape. The work, dated to the seventeenth century, is held at the Museo del Prado.
credit: Details of painting at the Prado Museum site Narciso at the Prado

title: Portrait of Amalia van Solms
description: This portrait from the workshop of Gerard van Honthorst (1650) depicts Amalia van Solms, widow of Frederick Henry of Orange-Nassau, at knee-length beside a draped curtain and column, an olive branch held in her lowered right hand. Painted as the pendant to her husband's posthumous portrait, the work is held in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
credit: www.rijksmuseum.nl : Home : Info

title: San Jerónimo leyendo
description: The Church Father is depicted half-length in a rocky grotto, bare-chested and absorbed in his book, a crucifix steadying his left hand. Murillo treats the penitent scholar with restrained naturalism, the warm Sevillian light modelling weathered skin and beard against a deep brown ground.

title: Self portrait
description: Jordaens presents himself in middle age wearing a green cloak with gold buttons over a dark garment, holding a rolled sheet of paper and turning to face the viewer with characteristic directness. Dated 1650, the portrait — inventory no. 12876 — is held by the Bavarian State Painting Collections in Munich.

title: The Adoration of the Shepherds
description: Shepherds gather around the Virgin and the naked Christ Child in a manger, bringing offerings including a lamb and a basket of eggs. A bull stands to the left and a rooster pecks at the foreground, grounding the holy scene in the rural world of the visitors. Painted around 1650 and now in the Museo del Prado, the work reflects Murillo's early naturalist manner, indebted to the Spanish Tenebrist tradition in its warm, earth-toned palette and unpretentious figure types.
credit: Museo Nacional del Prado

title: The boar hunt
description: Hounds tear at a cornered boar in a churning Baroque mêlée, the kind of large hunting piece Snyders supplied with workshop assistance for aristocratic galleries. Sweeping diagonals, splayed limbs and a bruised sky echo the dynamic compositions he had honed beside Rubens.

provenance.collection: Art Gallery of New South Wales
provenance.location: Art Gallery of New South Wales

title: The Holy Family with a Bird
description: The Holy Family is arranged in an intimate domestic interior: the Christ Child reaches upward toward a small bird held or guided by the seated Joseph, while Mary looks on at the left, her spinning frame visible behind her. A small white dog sits at the foreground. The warm chiaroscuro and genre-inflected tenderness are characteristic of Murillo's Sevillian devotional paintings of around 1650, now in the Museo del Prado.

title: The Man with the Golden Helmet
description: A bearded soldier in shadow tilts his head down, the entire light of the picture pooled on the embossed gold helmet that gives the work its name. Long catalogued as a Rembrandt at the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin, the painting was reattributed in 1986 to a member of his close circle, though the impasto handling of the gilt remains exceptional.

title: The Shell
description: A rare still life from Rembrandt's etched oeuvre, depicting a single cone shell (Conus marmoreus) rendered with delicate cross-hatching and drypoint burr. The print attests to the Dutch fascination with exotic naturalia gathered through global trade.
credit: www.rijksmuseum.nl : Home : Info

title: The Triumph of Bacchus
description: A Flemish baroque procession of Bacchus and Ariadne, with putti, satyrs, and tipsy revellers wreathed in vine. De Vos, best known for his crisp portraits of Antwerp burghers, here works closer to Rubens's mythological idiom, ordering the throng with broad, ruddy modelling.

title: Triumphant Cupid among Emplems of Art and War
artist: Thomas Willeboirts Bosschaert / Paul de Vos
description: Cupid sits in triumph atop instruments of art, science and war, a Baroque allegory of love's universal sway. Willeboirts Bosschaert painted the figures and de Vos the still-life trophies, reflecting the seventeenth-century Antwerp practice of collaborative specialization.
credit: Hans Thorwid / Nationalmuseum

title: Two young seals on the shore
description: Two young harbor seals lie on a stretch of Flemish shoreline, painted with the close observation of fur, hide, and salt-damp sand for which the de Vos workshop was prized. The Antwerp painter built his career on Baroque animal subjects, often supplying livestock and game for collaborators including Rubens.
credit: Joconde database : entry M0332001003

provenance.collection: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon
provenance.location: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon

title: Stormy Landscape with Pyramus and Thisbe
description: Storm clouds boil over a vast Italianate landscape as the Ovidian lovers meet their tragedy beside a reflective lake. Poussin uses meteorological drama to magnify human catastrophe, with sheet lightning, fleeing horses and bowed trees orchestrated into a single classical machine.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"p/poussin/4/38landsc"

title: The Kitchen Maid
description: A young girl in a red jacket rests her chin on her hand at a stone windowsill, her gaze directed slightly off to the side. Rembrandt renders her with warmth and individuality in the dark ochres and reds characteristic of his mid-career genre portraits; the Nationalmuseum's source notes she is probably someone from his household, though not Hendrickje. The painting is signed and dated 1651 and is held at the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.
credit: Nationalmuseum

title: Large Self Portrait
description: Rembrandt presents himself at forty-six in a dark cloak and broad flat beret, gazing out with composed gravity against a neutral background. Painted in 1652 and now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna, the large canvas belongs to the series of self-portraits that spans his entire career and marks a period of mounting financial pressure before the bankruptcy proceedings of 1656.

title: Margaretha Maria de Roodere
description: Margaretha Maria de Roodere sits before an easel, palette in hand, pointing to the portrait she has painted while a figure in black stands behind her to the right. Honthorst signed and dated the picture in 1652, presenting his sitter as a practising painter — one of the few documented women artists working in Utrecht in the mid-seventeenth century.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"h/honthors/2/13rooder"

title: Mercury and Argus
description: An engraving after Jordaens showing Mercury raising his sword above the slumbering hundred-eyed giant Argus, with Io transformed into a cow at the left. The print belongs to the wide diffusion of Jordaens' mythologies through reproductive engraving, here cataloged in Hollstein as Dutch 7.

title: Psyche receives the cup of immortality on the Olympus
description: Jordaens arranges the gods of Olympus in a sweeping circular composition around a luminous central opening, with Psyche at the centre receiving the cup of immortality that will seal her union with Cupid. Painted around 1652 and now in the collection of The Phoebus Foundation, the large-scale work — 266.5 by 226 cm — deploys the warm flesh tones and dynamic figural groupings characteristic of the Antwerp Baroque.

title: Rembrandt Harmenszoon van Rijn - An Old Man in Red
description: An oil on canvas portrait painted by Rembrandt between 1652 and 1654, depicting a distinguished elderly gentleman in a deep red robe. The work, measuring 108 x 86 cm, exemplifies Rembrandt's mastery of color and chiaroscuro in portraiture and resides in the Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg.

title: Triumph of Frederick Henry
description: An allegorical celebration of the Dutch stadtholder Frederick Henry, painted for the Oranjezaal at Huis ten Bosch. Jordaens orchestrates a swirling Baroque cavalcade of personifications, captives, and trophies in the Rubensian Antwerp manner, glorifying the prince's military and political triumphs.
credit: Paleis Huis ten Bosch (Oranjezaal)

title: Aristotle with a Bust of Homer
description: The philosopher Aristotle, in black robes and a gold chain bearing a portrait of Alexander, lays his hand on a marble bust of Homer. Commissioned in 1653 by the Sicilian collector Don Antonio Ruffo for 500 florins, the canvas was the first painting of a series the patron assembled around the philosopher and now hangs at the Metropolitan Museum.

title: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn - Christ Crucified Between the Two Thieves
englishTitle: Christ Crucified Between the Two Thieves (The Three Crosses)
description: A monumental etching depicting the crucifixion of Christ flanked by the two thieves, demonstrating Rembrandt's mastery of dramatic light and shadow. One of the most celebrated prints in Western art history, this work showcases the Dutch master's technique and theological interpretation of the Crucifixion narrative.

title: A View of Delft after the Explosion of 1654
description: A wide panoramic record of the destruction wrought by the Delft gunpowder magazine explosion of 12 October 1654, showing collapsed buildings, scattered rubble and groups of survivors picking through the debris in the foreground against a broad, cloud-filled sky. Egbert van der Poel painted the aftermath of the disaster, and returned repeatedly to the subject across several canvases. This example, dated 1654, is held at the National Gallery, London (NG1061).

title: Bathsheba with David's letter
description: Bathsheba sits naked after her bath, holding the letter from King David that summons her to him, her old servant drying her feet at the side. Signed and dated 1654, the canvas in the Louvre uses the body of Rembrandt's companion Hendrickje Stoffels for the biblical heroine caught between duty and complicity.

title: Christ in the House of Martha and Mary
description: Vermeer's largest known painting and a rare history piece, made early in his career before he turned to domestic interiors. Christ gestures toward the seated, attentive Mary while Martha presents a basket of bread; the broad handling and warm reds anticipate the artist's mature poise.

title: A Woman bathing in a Stream
description: A woman in a white shift gathers the hem above her knees as she wades into dark water, rich gold and red garments piled on the bank behind her. Painted on a small oak panel in the mid-1650s and signed at the lower left, the picture in the National Gallery, London, is rendered in strikingly free, loaded brushwork and is often thought to depict Hendrickje Stoffels.
credit: National Gallery, London

title: Christ presented to the people: the oblong plate
description: An etching, in its later state, of Pilate presenting the bound Christ to a crowd that demands his crucifixion. Rembrandt scraped away the foreground onlookers and replaced them with shadowed arches, intensifying the confrontation between judge and viewer.
credit: www.rijksmuseum.nl : Home : Info

title: Pallas Athena
description: A figure in gleaming helmet and gorget, traditionally identified as the goddess of wisdom and war. Rembrandt models the armour with thick, gilded impasto against deep shadow, a hallmark of his late chiaroscuro.
credit: museu.gulbenkian.pt : Home : Info : Pic

title: The Polish Rider
description: A young horseman in Eastern European costume rides a pale grey mount through a darkening landscape, bow and quiver at his back and a sabre at his side, with a fortified structure rising on the hill behind him. Attributed to Rembrandt and dated to around 1655, the canvas in the Frick Collection is among his most debated late works, its subject oscillating in scholarship between portrait, allegory, and historical type.
credit: The Frick Collection

title: Jacob Blessing Ephraim and Manasseh
description: Aged Jacob, propped on his deathbed, crosses his arms to lay his right hand on the younger Ephraim while Joseph tries to redirect it, his wife Asenath watching at the side. Signed and dated 1656, the canvas in Schloss Wilhelmshöhe at Kassel reframes the Genesis scene as a tender domestic gathering rather than a formal blessing.

title: Portrait of Hendrickje Stoffels
description: A half-length figure of a young woman in a rich crimson robe, her right hand raised and her left arm resting, her gaze directed slightly downward in warm, raking light. Traditionally identified as Hendrickje Stoffels, Rembrandt's companion in his later years, and painted around 1656, the picture now in the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin belongs to a series of intimate figure studies from his mature period.

title: The anatomy lesson of Dr. Joan Deijman
description: A foreshortened cadaver lies on the dissection table while Dr Joan Deijman, his hands shown above, performs an autopsy on the brain. Painted in 1656 for the Amsterdam Surgeons' Guild as a sequel to the Tulp anatomy of 1632, most of the canvas was destroyed by fire in 1723; only the central fragment survives in the Amsterdam Museum.
credit: ahm.adlibsoft.com : Home : Info : Pic

title: The Maids of Honour
description: The Spanish court group portrait centred on the Infanta Margarita, her maids and dwarves, with Velázquez himself at the easel and the king and queen reflected in a distant mirror. The picture is a sustained meditation on vision, painted for Philip IV and now the cornerstone of the Prado.
credit: The Prado in Google Earth: Home - 7 th level of zoom, JPEG compression quality: Photoshop 8.

title: Girl Reading a Letter at an Open Window
description: An early interior in which a young woman reads at a leaded casement, her face echoed in the panes. Recent restoration at the Gemäldegalerie in Dresden uncovered a painted Cupid on the back wall that had been overpainted after Vermeer's death, sharpening the picture's amorous subtext.
credit: Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden, online collection

title: Self-portrait
description: A self-portrait from the artist's later years, in which he sits frontally with a mahlstick and palette implied by his pose. Broad, loaded brushwork records a lined face that meets the viewer with sober self-knowledge.

title: The Wine Glass
description: A courtship scene in which a man in dark cloak attentively stands beside a young woman in red who raises a glass of wine to her lips. At the upper left window a heraldic stained-glass roundel introduces a note of aristocratic propriety into the domestic interior. Painted between 1658 and 1660, the work is held at the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin (inv. 912C).

title: View of Houses in Delft
description: A modest stretch of Delft brickwork, with figures absorbed in domestic chores in a doorway and an alley. One of only two surviving cityscapes by Vermeer, the picture distills the painter's quiet attention to weathered surface, mortar, and clouded northern light.

title: Figure Studies
description: A bearded, heavily draped man stands gesturing on a rise of ground, surrounded by figures who kneel, crouch, and sprawl around him — a sheet of studies for a crowded religious composition. Ricci worked it up in pen and brown ink with gray wash over traces of red and black chalk, letting rapid hatching stand in for landscape. Such fluent study sheets were the working currency of Venetian painters of his generation; this one is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: Self-portrait
description: A late self-portrait of 1659, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, in which Rembrandt faces the viewer in a dark beret and dark coat. The face, painted with broad and searching brushwork, records the accumulated marks of age with unsentimental directness. The painting is one of several large self-portraits from the artist's final decade in which he positioned himself with the gravitas of an Old Master.

title: Rembrandt’s Son Titus in a Monk’s Habit
description: Rembrandt's son Titus is shown in the brown habit and cowl of a Franciscan friar, his face turned downward in quiet introspection. Painted in 1660 and now in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, the picture employs the genre of the tronie to cast the young man in a devotional role rather than as a conventional portrait.
credit: Rijksmuseum Amsterdam online catalogue .

title: Self-portrait
description: Rembrandt at fifty-four faces the viewer in a dark cap and brown jerkin, the face built up in thick, scraped layers of paint. Signed and dated 1660 and now in the Louvre, the canvas was painted the year he left his bankrupt house on the Jodenbreestraat for a smaller dwelling on the Rozengracht.
credit: eev.liu.edu : Home : Info

title: The Chancelor Séguier
description: Chancellor Pierre Séguier rides on horseback beneath a large parasol, clad in magnificent golden ceremonial robes, accompanied by six young pages on foot. Painted between 1660 and 1661 and now in the Louvre, the picture was Le Brun's tribute to the patron who had supported his Italian studies and secured his career at the French court.
credit: photo Shonagon 2024-04-05

title: The Milkmaid
description: A sturdy kitchen maid pours a thin stream of milk into an earthenware bowl, the room hushed by daylight from a leaded window. Vermeer's pointillé highlights flicker on bread crusts and copper, and the lapis-derived blue of her apron exemplifies his costly pigment habits.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — AHrw. Z3. Av6. Zhjg 9. AHrw. Z3. Av6. Zhjg

title: View of Delft
dateCreated: between circa 1660 and circa 1661 Baroque (late 16 th century –1750s )
description: A panorama of the artist's home city seen across the Schie, rendered with the peculiar optical fidelity for which he is celebrated. Pinpoint dabs of impasto on the boats and roofs, possibly studied via a camera obscura, mimic the glint of refracted morning light.
credit: www.mauritshuis.nl : Home : Info : : Image

title: St. Bartholomew
description: An elderly man, identified as St Bartholomew by the knife of his martyrdom resting on the surface before him, raises one hand to his chin in pensive contemplation. Signed and dated 1661, the canvas in the J. Paul Getty Museum is painted with the loose, expressive brushwork of Rembrandt's late period, giving the figure a worn, deeply human presence.

title: The Conspiracy of the Batavians under Claudius Civilis
description: The surviving central fragment of Rembrandt's largest history painting, commissioned for Amsterdam's new Town Hall. Civilis raises a sword in a one-eyed oath-taking with his Batavian rebels — a coarsely lit, almost barbaric image that the city soon rejected.
credit: Nationalmuseum

title: The evangelist Matthew and the angel
description: The evangelist pauses over his manuscript as an angel leans in to whisper at his ear. Rembrandt models both faces with a quiet warmth, treating divine inspiration as an intimate exchange.

title: The Lute Player
description: A young man plays the lute beside an open window in a Dutch interior, while a woman seated at the laden table listens with her chin resting on her hand. A dog lies on the tiled floor and a canal view opens beyond the red curtain. Sorgh's The Lute Player (1661) exemplifies the warm-toned, anecdotal domestic genre he practised in Rotterdam.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"s/sorgh/luteplay"

title: Gerard Honthorst - gulden cabinet
description: Engraved portrait of Gerard van Honthorst published in 1662 in Cornelis de Bie's Het Gulden Cabinet der edel vry schilder const, the Antwerp directory of painters. Pieter de Jode II cut the plate after a Honthorst self-portrait, with the print issued by Joannes Meyssens for an entry that placed the Utrecht master among the leading Northern painters of his century.
credit: Het gulden cabinet vande edel vry schilder const , online facsimile version in Google books, p.165

title: Alexander Entering Babylon
description: Alexander, clad in gold and laurel, rides in a triumphal chariot as he enters Babylon, surrounded by a throng of soldiers, supplicants, and captives bearing spoils. Le Brun painted the canvas between 1664 and 1665 as part of his celebrated Alexander cycle for Louis XIV; it hangs in the Louvre and served as the basis for the Gobelins tapestry series.
credit: photo Shonagon 2024-04-05

title: A Lady Writing
description: A young woman in a yellow ermine-trimmed jacket pauses at her writing table, lifting her gaze toward the viewer, an ink pot and pearl jewellery at her hand. Painted around 1665 and now in the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the small panel is one of Vermeer's most intimate evocations of the moment of address from writer to absent reader.

title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
description: A tronie rather than a portrait: an anonymous young woman turns over her shoulder, lips parted, against a deep glazed-black ground. Vermeer reserves his most expensive pigments, ultramarine and lead-tin yellow, for the turban, and renders the famous teardrop earring with two soft dabs of lead white. In the Mauritshuis, The Hague.

title: Portrait of a couple as figures from the Old Testament
description: Long known as The Jewish Bride, the painting shows a couple in tender embrace, often identified with Old Testament pairs such as Isaac and Rebecca. Built up with thickly trowelled pigment, the gold sleeve and ruby skirt are among Rembrandt's most celebrated passages of paint.

title: Rest on the Flight into Egypt
description: The Holy Family pauses on its journey into Egypt, Mary cradling the sleeping Christ Child while Joseph watches over them and the donkey grazes nearby. Now in the Hermitage, the picture exemplifies Murillo's mature estilo vaporoso, in which figures emerge from a hazy, golden atmosphere with notably softened contours.

title: Lucretia
description: Lucretia stands in a white shift stained with blood, a dagger in one hand and a bell pull in the other, her eyes lowered in the moment after the self-inflicted wound. Signed and dated 1666, the canvas at the Minneapolis Institute of Art was the second and more restrained of Rembrandt's two paintings of the Roman heroine.
credit: Minneapolis Institute of Arts, online collection

title: The Art of Painting
dateCreated: circa from 1666 until 1668 Baroque (late 16 th century –1750s )
description: An allegory of painting in which an artist seen from behind sets brush to a portrait of Clio, the muse of history, identified by her trumpet and laurel. Vermeer kept the canvas in his Delft studio until his death, and the heavy map of the Seventeen Provinces above the model carries political weight.

title: Charles Le Brun La Colère
englishTitle: Anger, from the Méthode pour apprendre à dessiner les passions
description: Sheet from the Méthode pour apprendre à dessiner les passions, showing the face of Anger with brows drawn together, nostrils flared and teeth bared. Le Brun's 1668 lecture at the Académie Royale built a Cartesian taxonomy of emotion for painters, and the engraved sheets circulated in artist pattern books well into the nineteenth century.

title: The Astronomer
description: A scholar in a long robe leans over a celestial globe, his hand brushing its surface as if to set the cosmos turning. Painted as a pendant to The Geographer, the picture reflects Delft's culture of empirical inquiry, its still light and book-strewn study tuned to quiet concentration.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: The Geographer
description: A scholar in a blue Japonse rok leans over a chart spread on a table, holding dividers, as morning light falls from a leaded window at left. A celestial globe rests atop the cabinet behind him and a sea-chart hangs on the wall at right. Dated 1668 and held at the Städel Museum, Frankfurt, the painting is the companion piece to The Astronomer and forms Vermeer's meditation on seventeenth-century Dutch scientific inquiry.

title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
description: The ragged son kneels before his aged father, who lays trembling hands on the bowed shoulders while elder figures watch from the shadowed background. Painted in Rembrandt's final years around 1668, the canvas now hangs in the Hermitage, its thick impasto and warm umber light marking the late style of his last decade in Amsterdam.

title: The lacemaker
description: The smallest of Vermeer's surviving paintings, focusing tightly on a young woman bent over her bobbins and pins. Threads of red and white spill from a cushion in molten blurs that anticipate optical photography, while her concentrated face is rendered with the artist's signature stillness.
credit: Musée du Louvre

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Santa Rosa de Lima
description: Murillo depicts Santa Rosa de Lima kneeling in the white habit and dark veil of a Dominican tertiary, extending her hands towards the Christ Child who sits beside a woven basket at her feet; scattered roses and a book complete the scene. Painted around 1670, the work displays the warm tonality and tender sentiment characteristic of Murillo's late religious compositions.

title: Woman Writing a Letter
englishTitle: Woman Writing a Letter, with her Maid
description: A seated lady drafts a letter at a draped table while her standing maid waits, glancing toward a sunlit window. Vermeer constructs the interior with his characteristic geometry of floor tiles, parallel walls, and a hanging picture, weaving the small domestic event into a quietly orchestrated study of light and waiting.
credit: Derived from National Gallery of Ireland

title: Alexander and Porus
description: The wounded Indian king Porus is brought before Alexander the Great after the Battle of the Hydaspes, his tall figure refusing prostration. Le Brun painted the scene in 1673 as part of his cycle on the conquests of Alexander, commissioned by Louis XIV to flatter the Sun King by historical parallel.

title: Still Life with Servant
artist: Paul de Vos / Possibly Cornelis de Vos
description: A monumental Flemish still life heaped with hanging game, poultry, fruit, and vegetables, attended by a servant figure at the left — likely contributed by a collaborating figure painter, possibly Cornelis de Vos. The composition exemplifies the Antwerp specialty of combining a Snyders-school animal painter with a figure specialist for sumptuous decorative ensembles. The work dates to before 1678 and is held by the Fundación Banco Santander.

title: Mt. Heng, after Juran, from the Mustard Seed Garden Manual of Painting
englishTitle: Mt. Heng, after Juran, from the Mustard Seed Garden Manual of Painting
description: Woodblock print from the influential Mustard Seed Garden Manual of Painting, designed by Wang Gai and published by Li Yu. This landscape depicts Mount Heng, rendered in the style of Northern Song painter Juran (active ca. 960–965).
objectKey: collection-of-beauty/清_王槩_設計，李漁出版_芥子園畫傳_版本-Mt._Heng,_after_Juran_(active_ca._960–965),_from_the_Mustard_Seed_Garden_Manual_of_Painting_MET_DP-14004-001.jpg
fileUrl: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7a/清_王槩_設計，李漁出版_芥子園畫傳_版本-Mt._Heng,_after_Juran_(active_ca._960–965),_from_the_Mustard_Seed_Garden_Manual_of_Painting_MET_DP-14004-001.jpg
commonsUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:清_王槩_設計，李漁出版_芥子園畫傳_版本-Mt._Heng,_after_Juran_(active_ca._960–965),_from_the_Mustard_Seed_Garden_Manual_of_Painting_MET_DP-14004-001.jpg

title: Capture of the city and citadel of Gand in six days
description: A vast allegorical ceiling composition painted by Charles Le Brun between 1681 and 1684 to commemorate Louis XIV's capture of Ghent in 1678. Winged personifications of Fame and Victory surge through clouds above prostrate enemy figures and symbols of conquest, while allegorical figures of France and the defeated city occupy the lower register — part of Le Brun's pictorial programme glorifying the Crown.

title: Portrait of Charles Le Brun
description: Charles Le Brun is shown seated in an armchair in his studio, richly dressed in red velvet robes, his hand raised toward a large canvas behind him depicting a battle or mythological scene with horses and figures. Sculpted casts and drawings fill the foreground, attesting to his role as director of the Académie royale and the Gobelins manufactory. Largillière painted this homage between 1683 and 1686, near the end of Le Brun's tenure as First Painter to Louis XIV.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"l/largilli/le_brun"

title: Democritus
description: The laughing philosopher Democritus is shown in close-up, a broad grin revealing his teeth, clad in a reddish-purple robe and holding a small object in his raised hand. Coypel renders the Abderan sage as a lively bust-length figure against a dark ground, using warm chiaroscuro to convey the philosopher's characteristic amusement at human folly. Painted in 1692, the work exemplifies the late-seventeenth-century French taste for half-length figures of antique sages treated in a Flemish-influenced painterly manner.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/c/coypel/antoine/democrit"

title: La famille Laffite
description: A group portrait of the Laffite family by the leading court painter of Louis XIV. Rigaud's studio specialised in elaborate full-length likenesses of French nobility, with rich drapery, polished flesh tones and carefully posed sitters that established the visual vocabulary of Bourbon state portraiture.
credit: Paris, musée du Louvre

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Susannah accused of adultery
description: Susannah stands draped before the council of Israel while the two elders point in false accusation, the young Daniel rising to interrogate them. Coypel painted the Book of Daniel episode between 1695 and 1696, the smooth modelling and theatrical gesture already pointing toward the early Rococo.

title: Albinus skeleton w less muscles
englishTitle: Skeletal Figure with Superficial Muscles (Tabula II, after Albinus)
description: A plate from Bernhard Siegfried Albinus's Tables of the Skeleton and Muscles of the Human Body (1749), engraved by Jan Wandelaar. The skeleton is set in a poetic landscape with a rhinoceros, marrying anatomical exactitude to Enlightenment-era pictorial staging. The series was produced at the University of Leiden and was prized for the proportional rigour of its figures.
credit: Historical Medical Books at the Claude Moore Health Sciences Library, University of Virginia

title: Albinus skeleton w muscles
englishTitle: Skeletal Figure with Muscles (Tabula IV, after Albinus)
description: Another plate from Albinus's Tabulae sceleti et musculorum, in which Wandelaar layers the superficial muscles over the skeleton in a posed standing figure. The series was prized for its proportional accuracy, achieved with grids and double-perspective drafting unusual for medical illustration of the period.
credit: Historical Medical Books at the Claude Moore Health Sciences Library, University of Virginia

title: Anatomy
englishTitle: Skeleton, back view, with left arm extended (Scotin after Albinus, 1747)
description: A skeleton seen from behind with the left arm extended, engraved by Gérard Jean-Baptiste Scotin after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Bernhard Siegfried Albinus's anatomical atlas. Albinus's plates, first published in Leiden in 1747, set a new standard of precision by posing the skeleton like a living figure within a measured grid. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/35/5a/62669fc56d5e4b1a275837f10486.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0021853.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-23): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/h4378wsu CC-BY-4.0

title: Anatomy
englishTitle: Standing skeleton, side view, with left arm extended (Ravenet after Albinus, 1747)
description: A standing skeleton in side view with the left arm extended, engraved by Simon François Ravenet after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Albinus's anatomical atlas of 1747. The plates combined exacting anatomical measurement with the poise of classical statuary, and were widely copied across Europe. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/67/a2/b15c9a4ea7a1e9da5f0ea4c4a38d.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0021854.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-23): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/dpbj4te2 CC-BY-4.0

title: Anatomy
englishTitle: Écorché figure, front view, with rhinoceros in the background (Grignion after Albinus, 1747)
description: An écorché figure seen from the front, engraved by Charles Grignion after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Albinus's anatomical atlas. The grazing rhinoceros in the background is Clara, the celebrated Indian rhinoceros who toured Europe in the 1740s — Wandelaar sketched her in Leiden and used her to lend scale and life to the plates. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/a2/54/7cc9fb13563dd7251c28384a1860.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0021855.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-23): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/trnhrsna CC-BY-4.0

title: Self Portrait in a Turban
description: Rigaud, the great portraitist of Louis XIV's court, presents himself in an exotic turban, a studio prop conveying artistic vanity and learned cosmopolitanism. The lustrous fabrics and confident chiaroscuro foreshadow the polished grandeur he would soon bring to royal portraiture.
credit: Musée Rigaud (Web site?)

title: Diana and Her Dog
description: The huntress goddess sits at rest, largely unclothed with white drapery beside her, a large white hound pressed at her side and hunting equipment at her feet. Painted by Sebastiano Ricci between circa 1700 and 1705, the work demonstrates the rich chiaroscuro of late Venetian Baroque while treating the mythological subject with sensuous ease.

title: KorinsScreen
description: A six-panel folding screen depicting the rocky, pine-clad islets of Matsushima Bay, with stylised waves rendered in gold leaf and green pigment. Ogata Kōrin, leading master of the Rinpa school, treats the celebrated scenic site as flat decorative pattern rather than topographic record, in a work of c. 1700 held at the Smithsonian's Freer Gallery of Art.
credit: Ogata Kōrin's Waves at Matsushima, public domain from the Smithsonian Museum of Asian Art

title: Susannah and the Elders
description: The chaste Susanna twists away from two leering elders who corner her at her bath, the apocryphal subject a favorite vehicle for the female nude. Chiari, a pupil of Carlo Maratta, paints in a late-Roman Baroque idiom of cool flesh tones and theatrical gesture.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Portrait of Louis XIV
description: The Sun King at sixty-three, draped in ermine and blue velvet fleurs-de-lis, his bewigged head turned over a leg cocked in a courtly dance pose. Rigaud's state portrait set the template for European royal imagery, multiplied across embassies and palaces in countless studio replicas.
credit: wartburg.edu [ dead link ]

title: Kaigetsudo Ando - Standing Portrait of a Courtesan
description: A Yoshiwara courtesan stands alone in a richly patterned kimono, hip cocked in the languid S-curve that became the workshop's hallmark. As founder of the Kaigetsudō school, Ando concentrated entirely on monumental beauties, painted in fluid ink with broad swathes of color and gold on paper.
credit: Honolulu Museum of Art

title: Matteo Ripa001 - Morning Glow on the Western Ridge
englishTitle: Morning Glow on the Western Ridge, from Thirty-six Views of the Imperial Summer Resort at Chengde
description: A copperplate view of the Kangxi Emperor's summer retreat at Chengde, with mist breaking over the western ridge in fine engraved hatching. Ripa, a Neapolitan missionary at the Qing court, produced the imperial album that introduced Western intaglio printing techniques to China.
credit: Scan from "New Visions at the Ch'ing Court"

title: Portrait of Herman Petersen
description: Herman Petersen is shown in a reddish-brown coat with elaborate braid closures and a lace cravat, the pastel medium giving his face a characteristic softness. Gustaf Lundberg, who spent two decades in Paris absorbing the French pastel tradition before returning to Stockholm as court portraitist, brought the same refined technique to commissions for Swedish merchants and aristocrats throughout the eighteenth century.
credit: bukowskis.se

title: KIYONOBU-Yamanaka-Ichikawa-1714
englishTitle: The Actors Yamanaka Heikurō and Ichikawa Danjūrō II
description: Two kabuki actors square off in a confrontational pose typical of aragoto bravura roles. Kiyonobu, founder of the Torii line of theatre artists, defined the early ukiyo-e print with bold contour lines and the hand-applied tan-e orange-red pigment characteristic of pre-polychrome woodblock work.
credit: p. 38, Japanese Prints, Taschen

title: Self portrait of Antoine Coypel
description: Coypel turns toward the viewer in a large powdered wig and a voluminous dark velvet robe, holding an ornate bound volume — attributes befitting his role as First Painter to the King and director of the Académie royale. The self-portrait is dated 1715, seven years before his death in 1722.

title: WATTEAU Antoine - Huit études de têtes de femme
description: A study sheet by the French Rococo master Watteau, comprising eight head studies executed in sanguine, black chalk, and white chalk on gray paper. Created circa 1715–1716, the work features multiple female heads and at least one male head, likely preparatory studies for figures appearing in paintings such as La Conversation and L'amour dans un théâtre italien. Held in the Louvre Museum (accession INV 33383).

title: Man Resting in the Lap of a Woman
description: Two nude figures — a reclining man and a woman leaning tenderly over him — are depicted in an amorous embrace in this chalk study, the transfer grid still visible across the sheet. Attributed to Antoine Coypel and dated around 1716, the drawing demonstrates the loose, animated draughtsmanship of his later career.

title: Venus and Satyr
description: A reclining nude Venus, a single sleeping infant putto at her legs, is approached by a leering elderly satyr in a warm palette of reds and pale flesh tones. Painted by Sebastiano Ricci between 1716 and 1720, the work is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest, and reflects his debt to the Venetian mythological tradition of Veronese translated into a more intimate register.

title: Pilgrimage to Cythera
description: Lovers prepare to leave the island of Venus in golden afternoon light, a melancholic departure rather than the arrival the title might suggest. Watteau's reception piece for the Académie royale invented the genre of the fête galante, with feathery brushwork drawn from his study of Rubens.
credit: Retouched from File:L'Embarquement pour Cythere, by Antoine Watteau, from C2RMF.jpg , originally C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition : image page

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Nymphe de fontaine
description: A young woman crowned with a laurel wreath sits beside a large ornamental urn from which water pours, her gaze turned upward against an open sky with reeds and foliage behind her. The loose, warm handling of the figure and the pastoral setting align with the decorative mythological subjects Watteau explored in this period. Titled Nymphe de fontaine and dated 1718 in the catalogue, the painting was offered at Sotheby's New York in 2012.
credit: reproarte.com; Sotheby's New York, 26 January 2012, lot 63

title: Portrait of Charles de Geer
description: Pastel portrait of the Swedish industrialist and entomologist Friherre Charles de Geer, shown in coat and powdered wig against a neutral ground. Lundberg, court painter in Stockholm after a long apprenticeship in Paris under Boucher and La Tour, built his reputation on exactly these intimate pastel likenesses of Sweden's eighteenth-century aristocracy.

title: Portrait of Marie Anne de Bourbon
description: A young woman, identified as Marie Anne de Bourbon-Condé, is shown in a pink silk dress adorned with floral garlands, seated in a landscape setting and holding a flower wreath. This pastel copy, executed in 1720 by Gustaf Lundberg after a painted prototype by Jean-Baptiste Santerre, is an early example of the Swedish pastellist's work adapting the Parisian court portrait formula.
credit: Nordén Auktioner

title: Portrait of Cardinal Guillaume Dubois
description: Dubois, tutor to the future Louis XV and chief minister under the Regent, sits enveloped in a voluminous wrap of scarlet silk topped by a short fur cape. Rigaud channels the swagger of Louis XIV-era state portraiture into a study of ecclesiastical and political power, the textiles handled with the sumptuous fluency that made him the Bourbon court's favoured face-maker.

title: Portrait of the Artist's Daughters
description: Thomas Gainsborough's portrait depicts the artist's daughters in a family study from the early 1760s. The painting shows two young women in fashionable dress seated together in an intimate composition. This work exemplifies Gainsborough's skill in 18th-century portrait painting and is held in the Worcester Art Museum collection.

title: Le Peintre dans son atelier
description: A painter in a red coat sits at an easel working on a landscape in a dark, cluttered studio. Boucher painted this small genre scene between circa 1730 and 1735, in the years immediately following his return from Rome, where he had studied at the French Academy.

title: Colonel John Bullock
description: Thomas Gainsborough portrays Colonel John Bullock (1731–1809) full-length in scarlet uniform with green facings, holding his tricorn hat and leaning against a stone plinth, with a black-and-white spaniel seated at his feet. A wooded landscape and a decorative urn occupy the background in the relaxed outdoor manner Gainsborough favoured for his military sitters during the early 1770s.

title: La Continence de Scipion
description: The Roman general Scipio refuses the captive Iberian princess offered as spoils of war, gesturing for her return to her betrothed Allucius. Pittoni painted the moral exemplum in 1733, one of many Venetian treatments of the Livy episode in the pale, sweetened palette he favoured.

title: Farinelli
description: The celebrated castrato Carlo Broschi, known as Farinelli, stands in court dress with the score of an operatic aria in hand. Bartolomeo Nazari painted the oil on canvas in 1734, the year the singer arrived in London to join the Opera of the Nobility, the company set up in rivalry to Handel's. The portrait belongs to the Royal College of Music, London.
credit: Self-photographed . Taken on 4 May 2019.

title: Venus asks Vulcan for Weapons for his Son Aeneas
description: Venus, attended by putti and her swan, descends on clouds toward Vulcan who holds up completed armour, while workers labour in the forge at the right. Submitted as the painter's morceau de réception to the Académie Royale de Peinture et de Sculpture on 31 December 1734, the canvas is a polished demonstration of Rococo mythological painting. It is now in the Musée Fabre, Montpellier.

title: The Triumph of Bacchus; oil on canvas
description: Bacchus, draped in a leopard skin and holding a thyrsus, raises a cup toward a putto who pours wine from above, while a female companion and a reclining satyr complete the intimate mythological group in a vine-hung landscape. Charles-Joseph Natoire painted this oil on canvas in 1736, demonstrating the light palette and fluid handling characteristic of French Rococo court decoration.

title: Robert Fulton
description: Robert Fulton is shown seated three-quarter length in a black coat and white cravat, a red curtain behind him and a marine scene — likely a reference to his torpedo and submarine experiments — visible through a window at left. Painted in London in 1806 by Benjamin West, the oil on canvas (36¼ × 28¼ in.) was gifted by Stephen C. Clark to the Fenimore Art Museum, Cooperstown, New York. The following year Fulton's steamboat Clermont made its celebrated first run on the Hudson River.
credit: Benjamin West, American, 1738-1820. Robert Fulton, 1806, London, England. Oil on canvas, 36 1/4 × 28 1/4 in. (92.08 × 71.76 cm). Fenimore Art Museum, Cooperstown, N.Y., gift of Stephen C. Clark, N0218.1961. Photograph by Richard Walker.

title: Nishikawa Sukenobu
englishTitle: Ehon Asakayama (Picture Book of Mount Asaka), Page 16
description: A page from the Ehon Asakayama (Picture Book of Mount Asaka) of 1739, a woodblock-printed book by Nishikawa Sukenobu, the leading Kyoto designer of pictures of beautiful women. Printed in ink monochrome, this sheet shows a woman at her toilette, her kimono slipped to the waist as she binds up her hair before a lacquer cabinet and a folding mirror stand. The book's two dozen studies of women rank among Sukenobu's most important contributions to the bijin-ga genre.
credit: Hillier, J : The Art of the Japanese Book London : Sotheby's Publications, 1987, pp. 158–173.

title: Louis XV
description: Louis XV is shown in armour beneath the blue sash of the Order of the Holy Spirit, his wig tightly curled in the high court fashion of the late 1730s. Lundberg drew the king in pastel around 1740, the portrait once attributed to Louis-Michel van Loo before research reassigned it to the Swedish pastellist working in Paris.

title: The Rebuke of Adam and Eve
description: God appears in the clouds above, gesturing in rebuke toward Adam and Eve who stand before the forbidden fruit tree in the garden of Eden. A cherub accompanies the divine figure while the pair, clothed only in leaves, react with shame and supplication. Natoire's 1740 canvas, held in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, treats the biblical subject in a Rococo idiom of warm colour and graceful figures.

title: The Triumph of Venus
description: Venus is borne across the swell on a surge of nereids, tritons, and dolphins, while putti tumble through the air trailing a great loop of rose-patterned silk above her head. Painted in 1740, the canvas is Boucher's definitive statement of the mythological marine fantasy — flesh, spray, and drapery dissolving into a single silvery-blue arabesque. It was acquired by Count Carl Gustaf Tessin, the Swedish ambassador in Paris, and hangs today in the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.

title: Portrait of François Boucher
dateCreated: Reception piece for the Académie royale de peinture presented on January 28, 1741.
description: Gustaf Lundberg portrays François Boucher in a three-quarter turn, wearing a grey coat with lace jabot and a powdered wig, against a neutral ground. Presented as Lundberg's reception piece to the Académie royale de peinture on 28 January 1741, the pastel secured his admission as an academician.
credit: http://www.femme-classic-art.com/Fran%C3%A7ois-Boucher/Fran%C3%A7ois-Boucher-self-Portrait.html#sthash.Rv4PWo7e.dpbs ; https://www.1000museums.com/art_works/gustaf-lundberg-portrait-of-francois-boucher-1703-70

title: François boucher
description: A Rococo oil painting depicting the moment Diana emerges from her bath, exemplifying Boucher's characteristic fluid brushwork and sensual treatment of mythological subjects. The work showcases the artist's mastery of light and color in rendering the goddess's attendants and the luxurious bathing scene. Housed in the Louvre, Paris (INV 2712), this painting measures 57 × 73 cm and represents a quintessential example of 18th-century French court painting.

title: La Foire chinoise
description: Figures in fanciful Eastern dress mingle at a lively outdoor market beneath parasols and canopied stalls, with an elevated pavilion at centre right. Boucher designed the canvas around 1742 as part of his chinoiserie cycle for the Beauvais tapestry manufactory, supplying cartoons for a suite of woven panels.

title: La Pêche chinoise
description: Groups of figures in oriental costume populate a fanciful waterside setting, with a pagoda pavilion at centre-left and boatmen fishing from a vessel at right. Painted around 1742, the work belongs to François Boucher's chinoiserie series and evokes an imagined China assembled from imported porcelains and travel prints rather than direct observation.

title: Leda and the Swan
description: Two nude women are seated together in a wooded landscape, one gesturing outward while the other inclines toward the swan at her side, in Boucher's characteristically pale, warm palette of peach and ivory. The 1742 canvas, now at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, treats the myth with the playful sensuality typical of his Rococo mythologies.

title: Clayton Jones
description: Clayton Jones is shown full-length, seated beneath a tree in a parkland landscape, wearing a dark blue coat over a yellow waistcoat and holding a walking cane. Gainsborough painted the portrait between 1744 and 1745, during his early career, and it is now at the Yale Center for British Art.

title: en
description: A wooded lane winds past a pool toward a sandy rise dotted with figures, a thatched cottage, and further structures under a dramatic cloudscape. Gainsborough painted the canvas between circa 1746 and 1750, during his early years working in East Anglia, and it is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

title: A skeleton
description: A full skeleton stands facing the viewer in a lush river landscape, left arm extended, while a winged putto hovers at its shoulder holding up a billowing drape.
