The 1747 etching follows the anatomical tables of Bernhard Siegfried Albinus, whose atlas famously set its specimens in living, pastoral scenery to give the bones scale and vitality; this plate was engraved for the English edition by Charles Grignion. The impression comes from the Wellcome Collection, London.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/6f/25/a5fb05cefd4d73a3fbd8a2130999.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0021852.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-23): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/sx35vhhe CC-BY-4.0

title: Cornard Wood
description: An early woodland scene from Gainsborough's Suffolk years, made before he turned full-time to portrait commissions in Bath and London. Drawing on Dutch landscape models, particularly Ruisdael, he threads a sandy track through scrubby oaks under a broken English sky.
credit: London Gallery

title: Mr. and Mrs. Andrews
dateCreated: between 1748 and 1750 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A double portrait of a young Suffolk landowner and his bride seated at the edge of their estate, the rolling cornfields and oak deliberately presented as part of their identity. The crisp early style fuses French rococo elegance with topographical precision unusual in English portraiture.
credit: The National Gallery

title: Orchids
description: A literati-style study of orchids in ink on paper, drawn with the calligraphic spontaneity that defined Ike no Taiga's Nanga painting. The plant's sparse leaves and blossoms are set down in a few rapid strokes, a Confucian emblem of refined virtue rendered with Edo-period painterly freedom.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art

title: Portrait of Alexandrine Le Normant d'Étiolles
description: A young girl in a teal silk dress holds a pink flower while resting her hand on a wooden birdcage containing a small dark bird. Attributed to François Boucher and dated 1749, the portrait depicts Alexandrine Le Normant d'Étiolles, daughter of Madame de Pompadour, painted during the period when Boucher was the family's favoured artist.
credit: www.sothebys.com

title: Blind-Man’s Buff
description: A blindfolded young woman in a pink gown reaches outward on a garden terrace, flanked by flowers, trees and a young man seated to one side, in this early Fragonard painted around 1750–52. The scene pairs with a companion piece known as The See-Saw (Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum) as a pendant courtship subject, and reflects Fragonard's training in the Rococo pastoral manner under François Boucher.

title: Death of Sophonisba
description: The Carthaginian noblewoman receives the cup of poison sent by Masinissa, surrounded by attendants as she chooses suicide over Scipio's Roman triumph. Pittoni, a founding member of the Venetian Academy in 1750, treats the Livy episode with the pale flesh and silver-grey palette typical of his late Rococo manner.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/p/pittoni/sophonis"

title: Harunobu 2 Pers
description: A pair of figures in the slender, doll-like proportions Harunobu favoured, set within a softly muted interior. He was the pioneer of full-colour nishiki-e printing in 1760s Edo, shifting ukiyo-e away from hand-tinted limited palettes toward layered woodblock impressions.
credit: scan from a postcard

title: Landscape with Stream and Weir
description: A broad river landscape shows cattle and sheep near a weir, with a wooden gate at the water's edge, a cliff and ruined structure at right, and a sweeping cloud-filled sky above. Gainsborough painted the work between 1750 and 1753, and it is now at the Yale Center for British Art.

title: Old man in an eastern attire
description: A bust-length study of a white-haired, white-bearded old man wearing a striped olive-brown garment with a reddish outer layer and a gold-trimmed fastening at the chest. The face is rendered with close attention to aged flesh and wrinkles against a dark ground, in the Rembrandtesque tronie tradition practised by Bartolomeo Nazari in Venice during the first half of the eighteenth century.
credit: www.lazienki-krolewskie.pl

title: Portrait of Juliana Dorotea Henck
description: Juliana Dorotea Henck is shown in a broad-brimmed straw hat trimmed with flowers, her light curled hair framing her face, wearing a pink-toned dress with lace at the collar. The pastel, dated circa 1750, exemplifies Gustaf Lundberg's skill in combining the fashionable informality of French Rococo portraiture with the intimate likeness that made him the foremost pastellist at the Swedish court.
credit: www.uppsalaauktion.se

title: Sketch for a Portrait of Madame de Pompadour
description: Madame de Pompadour stands in a gilded interior wearing an elaborate green silk gown trimmed with flowers, holding a fan, with a tall looking-glass partially visible behind her. Boucher made the study around 1750 as a preparatory work for the formal portraits he produced for his principal patron; the painting is now at Waddesdon Manor, Buckinghamshire, in the National Trust collection.
credit: National Trust, Waddesdon Manor

title: The See-Saw
description: A young woman in a red and green skirt swoops upward on a garden seesaw while a young man and two children look on below, surrounded by a leafy parkland setting. Jean-Honoré Fragonard painted this playful outdoor scene between 1750 and 1752, early in his career.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"f/fragonar/father/1/021swing"

title: Woman Admiring Plum Blossoms at Night
description: A young woman in a kimono holds a paper lantern aloft on a veranda at night, gazing up at a flowering plum branch above her. Suzuki Harunobu was among the first ukiyo-e artists to master the full polychrome nishiki-e technique, and this quiet nocturne, preserved in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, shows the delicate colour harmonies of dark ground, pale blossoms, and warm candlelight that define his work.
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art

title: The Bridge
description: Pastoral figures — a woman leaning on a fence, a drover above with cattle — are disposed around a ruined stone arch bridge over a mill pond, with tall trees massed behind. Boucher signed and dated the canvas 1751, placing small staffage figures within a lush, theatrically composed landscape that draws on the decorative pastoral tradition he had absorbed in Rome.

title: The Toilet of Venus
description: Venus sits partially draped among silks, roses, and pearls while three putti attend to her hair and adornments in this 1751 canvas by François Boucher. The painting, a refined example of French Rococo mythological decoration, is held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (accession 20.155.9).
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (accession number 20.155.9)

title: Venus Consoling Love
description: Venus reclines in a lush woodland setting, attended by multiple putti — one bearing his bow and quiver leans into her, while another peers from above; white doves flutter at the pool's edge below. Signed and dated 1751, the canvas is now in the National Gallery of Art in Washington and exemplifies Boucher's characteristic synthesis of Rococo charm, soft flesh tones, and pastoral fantasy.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Jeroboam Offering Sacrifice for the Idol
description: Before a towering golden calf idol, a prophet raises his arm in denunciation while the king and his attendants react in agitation, the figures arranged in tense Baroque diagonals across a columned temple interior. Fragonard won the Prix de Rome with this composition in 1752 and it now belongs to the Académie des Beaux-Arts.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"f/fragonar/father/1/01jerobo"

title: John Plampin
description: John Plampin sits informally on a mossy bank, one hand grasping a tree branch, his spaniel at his feet, the countryside spreading behind him under a cloudy sky. Painted around 1752 during Gainsborough's Ipswich period, the small canvas fuses portraiture and landscape in the intimate manner of his early career. It is now in the National Gallery, London (NG5984).
credit: National Gallery, London - online catalogue .

title: Resting Girl by François Boucher
description: A sensual Rococo oil-on-canvas depicting a reclining young woman, housed in Munich's Alte Pinakothek since 1909. Boucher dispensed with mythological pretense to present pure erotic nudity, a daring choice even during the Enlightenment. One of two known versions; the other (1751) is in the Wallraf-Richartz Museum, Cologne.

title: John and Ann Gravenor
description: John Gravenor stands at the left while his wife Ann and their two daughters are seated in a wooded landscape at the edge of a field, the younger girl in white with flowers in her lap. Painted around 1754, during Gainsborough's Ipswich period, the canvas is a characteristic conversation piece combining portraiture with natural surroundings. It is now in the Yale Center for British Art, New Haven.

title: Mars
description: Vulcan looms at the forge while Venus reclines with Mars and two cupids gather around a heap of armour, after Ovid's tale of the lovers exposed in the smith god's net. Signed and dated 1754, the canvas is among the earliest surviving paintings by Copley, then about sixteen and working out a European mythological vocabulary from prints in colonial Boston.

title: The Grape Gatherer
description: A young woman cradles a bunch of grapes in her gathered skirt while squeezing juice over a baby at her feet. Painted around 1754-55, the canvas belongs to a set of four pastoral seasons at the Detroit Institute of Arts that Fragonard produced as overdoor or wall-panel decoration for an interior scheme.

title: Aurora Triumphing over Night
description: Aurora rides above the clouds scattering rose petals onto the sleeping figure of Night, lit by an upward-raking perspective. Painted around 1755-56 as an overdoor for a Parisian townhouse, the horizontal canvas was acquired by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston at Sotheby's New York in January 2013.

title: Landscape with a Watermill
description: A thatched watermill with a turning wheel stands at the centre of a wooded river scene; washerwomen crouch at the bank while a standing figure pauses nearby, and a stone bridge appears at right middle distance. Boucher signed and dated the canvas 1755; the work is now in the National Gallery, London (NG6374).

title: The Skating Minister
description: A Church of Scotland minister glides across a frozen Edinburgh loch in elegant profile, arms folded against the chill. The silhouetted black figure on pale ice and misty hills became an emblem of the Scottish Enlightenment and a touchstone of Scottish national painting.
credit: National Gallery of Scotland, Edinburgh, online collection

title: Portrait of Madame de Pompadour
description: Madame de Pompadour reclines in an elaborate teal silk gown embroidered with floral motifs, holding an open book, surrounded by further volumes and writing implements that signal her role as intellectual patron. Signed and dated 1756 and now in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich, the full-length portrait presents Louis XV's official mistress as an educated champion of the Enlightenment.

title: A Man Called Mr. Wood
description: A heavyset man identified as Mr Wood, said to have been a dancing master, is shown half-length in a pale blue coat trimmed with gold braid, against a dark neutral background. The portrait dates from around 1757, near the close of Gainsborough's Ipswich years, and is now in the Paul Mellon Collection at the Yale Center for British Art.

title: Vulcan Presenting Venus with Arms for Aeneas
description: In this large 1757 mythological canvas, Vulcan presents Venus with armour he has forged for her son Aeneas, after the eighth book of the Aeneid; the muscular smith god reclines at lower right amid weapons and tools while Venus and attendant figures fill the luminous centre. Boucher deploys his characteristic theatrical clouds, cupids and warm flesh tones across the ambitious composition.

title: Mary and Elizabeth Royall
description: Two young daughters of the Medford merchant Isaac Royall Jr. are shown full-length in elaborate satin gowns — one blue, one yellow-green — one of them holding a small dark dog. Painted around 1758, when Copley was in his early twenties, the canvas is among his earliest known double portraits; the Loyalist Royall family fled to England in 1776 and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, acquired it in 1925.

title: Portrait of Ann Fairchild Bowler
description: Ann Fairchild Bowler, wife of Newport merchant and politician Metcalf Bowler, stands in a blue silk gown, her left hand resting on a birdcage and a fold of pink drapery over her other arm. Copley painted the portrait in 1758 during his early Boston practice; it is now in the Colby College Museum of Art, Waterville, Maine.
credit: The Colby College Museum of Art <br(>2. The Colby College Museum of Art

title: Self-portrait
description: A self-portrait painted around 1758-59, just as Gainsborough left Ipswich for the spa town of Bath. The small canvas, now NPG 4446 in the National Portrait Gallery, almost certainly hung in his studio as an advertisement of his skill; behind the loose, fluent brushwork the trees of a Suffolk landscape can still be made out.

title: Jupiter in the Guise of Diana
description: Jupiter, disguised as the chaste Diana, leans toward the nymph Callisto with the seducer's eagle hidden above a pink satin curtain. Signed and dated 1759 and acquired by the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art in Kansas City through the William Rockhill Nelson Trust, the small canvas concentrates the late Rococo into a tight palette of pinks, greens and blues.
credit: The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City, Missouri

title: Epes Sargent
description: A man in a grey coat and white wig leans beside a stone pedestal, his hands folded at his chest, with a landscape glimpsed to the right. Painted by John Singleton Copley around 1760 and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the portrait exemplifies the young Copley's command of European compositional formulas adapted for his American clientele.

title: Portrait of Ann Ford
description: Ann Ford sits in a fashionable Bath drawing room with her English guitar across her lap and a viola da gamba propped beside her chair. Painted in 1760 shortly after Gainsborough settled in Bath, the portrait celebrates Ford as a professional musician, a calling unusual for a woman of her class and one her father had tried to suppress.
credit: dezoomify https://piction.cincinnatiartmuseum.org/zoomify/24DB48C39EA3C0FFA3517802F71E7A84875375F79D29561BE0A2774DA0FF8F19_files/14/0_0.jpeg

title: The Painter's Daughters with a Cat
description: Margaret and Mary Gainsborough, the painter's daughters, lean into one another while a cat curls into Margaret's arm, the picture left unfinished with the animal sketched only in outline. One of around a dozen portraits Gainsborough painted of the girls across their childhood, it now hangs in the National Gallery, London.

title: Two faces expressing veneration and rapture. Etching
description: Two labelled heads demonstrate contrasting emotional states after Le Brun: Veneration is shown with the face inclined downward and the eyes cast humbly low, while Rapture turns the head upward with parted lips and an open gaze. The etching, made around 1760 after Charles Le Brun, belongs to the tradition of academic physiognomic instruction and is held by the Wellcome Collection.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/e3/02/687a50a6617f2dcc633f23259342.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/V0009320.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-04-06): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/kvy4wq58 CC-BY-4.0

title: 諸國名橋奇覧 摂洲天満橋-Tenman Bridge at Settsu Province
englishTitle: Tenman Bridge at Settsu Province, from Remarkable Views of Bridges in Various Provinces
description: A Japanese woodblock print by Katsushika Hokusai from the series Shokoku Meikyo Kiran (Remarkable Views of Bridges in Various Provinces). This print depicts Tenman Bridge at Settsu Province. The work is part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art collection and is available under CC0 public domain dedication.

title: A woman with a rose
description: A woman in a wide-brimmed hat and ribbon choker stands in profile, a rose held in her lowered hand against the folds of her full skirts. The drawing dates from around 1763–1765, during Gainsborough's Bath years, and is catalogued in the British Museum's online database as entry 749307.
credit: British Museum: online database: entry 749307

title: Dreaming Shepherdess
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"b/boucher/2/shepdrea"

title: Hilly Landscape with Figures Approaching a Bridge
description: A wooded river landscape in the Dutch-influenced manner of Gainsborough's middle years, with travellers descending toward a rustic bridge. Feathered foliage and a silvery palette establish the gentle, picturesque mood that defined his Bath-period landscapes.

title: Mary Little
description: Mary Little, later Lady Carr, is shown in a rose-pink silk gown with lace cuffs, holding a small bouquet of flowers, against a warm dark background. The portrait dates from around 1763 and is now at the Yale Center for British Art.

title: Mrs. Benjamin Pickman
description: Mary Toppan, wife of the Salem merchant Benjamin Pickman, stands in a blue satin gown trimmed with silver lace, holding a closed parasol at her side, with a stone balustrade behind her. Copley painted the portrait in 1763, and it is held at the Yale University Art Gallery, New Haven (accession 1966.79.3).

title: Mrs. Daniel Sargent
description: Mary Turner Sargent leans on a pedestal beside a fountain, water cupped in her hand, in a Boston society portrait of 1763. The conceit of the basin and the pose derive from English mezzotints after Reynolds, sources Copley studied avidly in colonial Massachusetts before his move to London.

title: Mary Hopkinson
description: Mary Hopkinson sits in a pink silk dress against a dark curtained ground, holding a lute in her right hand and glancing toward the viewer. West painted this three-quarter-length portrait in 1764, shortly after settling in London, and it entered the Smithsonian American Art Museum (accession 1926.6.1).

title: Portrait of Mary
description: Mary, Countess Howe, walks through a wooded landscape in a pink silk gown lifted to show a quilted petticoat, a black ribbon at her throat. Painted in 1764 at Bath and now at Kenwood House, the portrait is among Gainsborough's most admired full-lengths, the gown rendered in feathery strokes that animate the silk.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"g/gainsbor/04m_howe"

title: 1280px-Suzuki Harunobu - Evening Snow on the Heater
description: A polychrome woodblock print from Harunobu's Zashiki hakkei (Eight Parlour Views), a series that recasts the classical "Eight Views" landscape themes as domestic interior scenes. A woman with a pipe sits beside a lacquered dome draped with white silk floss — its unprinted, embossed relief standing in for evening snow — while a girl dozes against her side. Made around 1765, when Harunobu was pioneering full-colour nishiki-e printing; this impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: A Boy with a Flying Squirrel
description: Henry Pelham, Copley's half-brother, sits at a polished mahogany table with a flying squirrel tethered by a gold chain, a glass of water beside him. Shipped to London for the 1766 Society of Artists exhibition, the picture earned Copley election to the Society and Joshua Reynolds's qualified praise.

title: Allegory of Painting
credit: This file was derived from: Allegory of Painting sc493.jpg :

title: Gathering Bamboo Shoots
description: A color woodblock print by Suzuki Harunobu of a young woman in a wide straw hat digging in deep snow with a hoe, where a single bamboo shoot has broken the surface beneath snow-laden bamboo. The unseasonable subject evokes the Chinese filial-piety tale of Meng Zong, who dug for bamboo shoots in midwinter to feed his ailing mother, recast in Harunobu's fashion as a scene with an elegant contemporary beauty. The print, from about 1765, is in the Art Institute of Chicago.

title: Harunobu Kanzan et Jittoku
description: A mitate of the Chinese Chan eccentrics Hanshan and Shide, here reimagined as two Edo youths sharing a scroll, rendered in Harunobu's characteristic nishiki-e palette against a swirling ground. The woodblock print, dated between 1765 and 1770, exemplifies the classical-vernacular layering that defines Harunobu's refined output.

title: Hatred or Jealousy
description: A grimacing head with knotted brow and bared teeth illustrates Hatred or Jealousy, plate from Heads Representing the Various Passions of the Soul published by Robert Sayer in 1765. The series engraves Le Brun's 1668 Paris lecture diagrams, turning the French academy's physiognomic codes into a drawing manual for English students.

title: John Hancock
description: John Hancock sits at a writing table in a blue coat with his ledger open before him, the merchant and future signer of the Declaration of Independence painted at twenty-eight. Copley made the portrait in 1765 for the Hancock family in Boston, and it now hangs in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Karl Friedrich Abel
description: Carl Friedrich Abel is shown three-quarter length, holding his viola da gamba in one hand and its bow in the other, his expression easy and confident. Gainsborough, a close friend of the German-born composer and an amateur viol player himself, painted this portrait in 1765, the year the celebrated Bach-Abel concert series began in London. The instrument dominates the composition, underscoring Abel's renown as the foremost viola da gamba virtuoso of the era.

title: Mrs. George Watson
description: Elizabeth Oliver Watson, wife of the Boston merchant George Watson, is shown in a red satin gown with lace cuffs, her hand resting on a blue-and-white vase of flowers beside her. Copley painted the portrait in 1765; it entered the Smithsonian American Art Museum as a family gift.

title: Mrs. Theodore Atkinson Jr.
description: Frances Deering Wentworth, painted at twenty in oil on canvas, holds a flying squirrel by a chain in a gesture borrowed from Copley's Pelham portrait of the same year. Married first to Theodore Atkinson Jr. and later to Governor John Wentworth, she sat to Copley in 1765 in Boston.

title: Portrait of Nathaniel Hurd
description: The Boston silversmith and engraver Nathaniel Hurd leans on two folios, one labelled with the heraldic engraver's reference works that supplied his trade. Painted around 1765 and now in the Cleveland Museum of Art, the portrait shows Hurd in working dress, a rare colonial likeness of a craftsman rather than a merchant.

title: Terrour or Fright
description: A head with eyes flung wide and mouth open in a scream, codifying Terrour or Fright in the system of facial passions. Engraved for Robert Sayer's 1765 English edition after Charles Le Brun's Paris academy lectures, the plate is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: The High Priest Coresus Sacrificing Himself to Save Callirhoe
description: The high priest Coresus plunges a dagger into his own breast before the altar to save the maiden Callirhoe from the sacrifice Bacchus had demanded, the temple filled with collapsing onlookers. Fragonard's morceau d'agrément for admission to the Académie Royale in 1765, the canvas was bought immediately by Louis XV and hangs in the Louvre.
credit: allart.biz

title: Virgin and Child with the Young Saint John the Baptist and Angels
description: Seated in a garden with a basket of grapes beside her, the Virgin in a blue mantle bends her cheek to the Christ Child, while the young John the Baptist kneels in prayer at the right with his lamb, and cherubs drowse on the clouds above. The oval canvas, signed and dated 1765, shows Boucher translating his pastoral idiom into devotional imagery — sacred subject matter delivered with the powdery color and soft flesh of his mythologies. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: Pylades and Orestes Brought as Victims before Iphigenia
Commodore the Hon. Augustus Hervey
description: Augustus Hervey, third Earl of Bristol, stands in commodore's undress uniform with a coil of rope at his hand and his ship riding at anchor offshore. Painted by Gainsborough in 1767 for Hervey's seat at Ickworth, the portrait is now in the National Trust collection.

title: Judge Martin Howard
description: Judge Martin Howard sits in a green upholstered chair wearing the scarlet and gold robes of a colonial jurist, a powdered wig framing his steady gaze. A bound volume rests at his side. Copley's 1767 portrait, measuring 125.7 by 101 cm, is held by the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid.
credit: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza

title: Road from Market
description: A rural landscape in which figures with laden horses return along a sunken track at the close of day. Gainsborough constructs the scene from imagined, idealised motifs, building a poetic vision of English country life in the Bath-period pastoral mode.

title: The Happy Accidents of the Swing
description: A young woman in a pink silk gown swings forward through a garden bower, kicking off one slipper as a hidden suitor peers up from the bushes below. Commissioned by the Baron de Saint-Julien for his château, Fragonard's canvas became the defining image of Rococo libertinage.

title: The Secret Message
description: A young woman in a pink satin gown sits alone in a garden, leaning forward to read a letter while a white dove perches nearby and a basket of flowers rests at her feet. Signed and dated by François Boucher in 1767, the oil on canvas (60 × 50.5 cm) is in the Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum, Braunschweig.
credit: Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum Braunschweig

title: Young lady with a Bird and dog
description: A girl in a pink silk dress holds a blue ribbon tied to a parrot perched on a chairback, while a black-and-white spaniel stands at her side. Painted in Boston in 1767, before Copley's departure for Europe, the portrait entered the Toledo Museum of Art and shows his characteristic close observation of fabric, feather, and fur.
credit: Toledo Museum of Art

title: Agrippina Landing at Brundisium with the Ashes of Germanicu
description: The widow Agrippina disembarks at the Italian port of Brundisium carrying the urn that holds her husband Germanicus's ashes, flanked by mourners and her children. Commissioned by Archbishop Robert Hay Drummond after a passage in Tacitus, the picture launched West's Neoclassical history practice in London and now hangs at Yale.

title: An Experiment on a Bird in an Air Pump by Joseph Wright 'of Derby'
englishTitle: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump
description: A candle-lit demonstration of a vacuum pump, with a cockatoo gasping in its glass globe as a mixed audience reacts in awe, fascination, and dread. Wright transposes religious chiaroscuro onto the new theatre of Enlightenment science.
credit: National Gallery, London

title: Cleombrotus Ordered into Banishment by Leonidas II
description: Leonidas II points his son-in-law Cleombrotus toward exile while the younger man's wife pleads at his feet with their children. West drew the episode from Plutarch's Life of Agis, treating Spartan civic duty in the friezelike arrangement that marked his Neoclassical history pictures of the late 1760s.

title: Portrait of Paul Revere
description: The Boston silversmith sits in his shirtsleeves at a polished workbench, holding a teapot he is about to finish, engraving tools laid out before him. Copley shows Revere as an artisan rather than a gentleman, an unusually direct conception for a colonial portrait, now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Figure de fantaisie autrefois désignée à tort comme Denis Diderot
englishTitle: Fantasy Figure (Formerly Identified as Denis Diderot)
description: A bare-headed, middle-aged man in rich fantaisie drapery turns toward the viewer with an animated expression, rendered in Fragonard's characteristically rapid and fluid brushwork. Long catalogued at the Louvre as Diderot, the picture is now classed among Fragonard's figures de fantaisie, painted circa 1769 as virtuoso essays in informal costume portraiture.
credit: Louvre: Denis Diderot , vue sans cadre

title: Fragonard Woman w Dog 1769 MMA
description: A woman in an elaborate silk and lace gown holds a small white lapdog on a blue ribbon, raising the animal before her in a formal three-quarter pose. Jean-Honoré Fragonard painted this oil on canvas around 1769; it is in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: François-Henri d'Harcourt
description: A half-length portrait of François-Henri d'Harcourt (1726–1802), dressed in a loosely painted dark costume with a white lace collar and swirling red and blue drapery. Jean-Honoré Fragonard painted the oil on canvas around 1769 in the manner of his figures de fantaisie, in which sitters appear in theatrical or Renaissance-inflected dress.

title: Inspiration
description: A young man in seventeenth-century costume looks upward from his writing desk, quill in hand, as if catching a passing thought. One of Fragonard's figures de fantaisie, the canvas was likely painted at speed in about an hour, an exercise in bravura brushwork over careful underdrawing.

title: Isaac Royall
description: Isaac Royall, the Massachusetts merchant and slaveholder, sits in a dark crimson coat with gold buttons, one hand gesturing toward an open document on the table beside him, a blue-green curtain providing the sole backdrop. Copley painted the portrait in 1769, and it is now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (accession 39.247), one of several Cambridge sittings from the years before Copley's departure for Europe.

title: Self-portrait
description: Copley presents himself in a powdered wig and richly embroidered teal coat, his gaze directed steadily at the viewer. Painted in 1769, the portrait exemplifies the meticulous attention to surface and texture that distinguished his pre-European Boston work and is now held at The Athenaeum.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic

title: The Departure of Regulus
description: The Roman consul Marcus Atilius Regulus tears himself from his wife and children to return to certain torture in Carthage, having kept his oath to the enemy. The first picture George III commissioned from West, RCIN 405416, established the painter's role as history painter to the King and now hangs in the Royal Collection.
credit: Royal Collection

title: the two sisters
description: Two young girls in yellow and pink silk dresses sit close together, their powdered hair and rosy cheeks lit against a dark background, with theatrical masks visible at the lower left. Jean-Honoré Fragonard painted this double portrait, known as The Two Sisters, in 1769.

title: A woman whose face expresses sadness. Etching in the crayon
description: A young woman bows her head into her shawl, mouth set and eyes downcast in unconcealed grief. Etching in the crayon manner by W. Hebert, around 1770, the print belongs to the Wellcome Collection's holdings of physiognomic studies that imitated red-chalk drawing through stippled etched dots.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/8d/5f/0ea6ee3b0f2a388df08dbe99ba45.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/V0009337.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-23): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/y4ujdp9k CC-BY-4.0

title: A Young Girl Reading
description: A young woman in a yellow silk dress sits absorbed in a small book, her head inclined and a cushion visible beside her. Fragonard's oil on canvas, dated 1770, is held at the National Gallery of Art in Washington and is among the most refined of his intimate figure studies.
credit: National Gallery of Art .

title: Benjamin West
description: A bust-length portrait of a young man in a dark green coat with gold buttons, set within a painted oval, against a dark ground. The sitter is identified as the American history painter Benjamin West, depicted here as a young man. The work is attributed to James Smith and dated 1770.

title: Girl with Dog
description: A girl lies on her back amid tumbled bedclothes beneath a golden canopy, balancing a small white dog on her raised legs, her chemise fallen back. Painted around 1770, the canvas belongs to Fragonard's intimate group of boudoir scenes, set down with rapid, broken brushwork.

title: Portrait of Dr. William Hunter's Spaniels
description: Two white-and-brown spotted spaniels stretch beneath a Newport Chippendale mahogany tea table, the larger asleep facing left and the smaller looking out at the viewer. Painted by the young Gilbert Stuart in Newport around 1770, the canvas is among the earliest surviving works by the future portraitist of George Washington.

title: The Blue Boy
description: A young man in a slashed blue satin suit of the Van Dyck period stands in a parkland landscape, plumed hat in hand. Painted around 1770 and shown at the Royal Academy in 1770, Gainsborough's portrait of the ironmonger's son Jonathan Buttall now hangs at the Huntington Library in San Marino.
credit: britsattheirbest.com; The Huntington Library, Art Collections

title: The Death of General Wolfe
description: British General James Wolfe lies dying among his officers on the Plains of Abraham after the 1759 capture of Quebec, a Mohawk scout watching at his side. West broke history-painting decorum by showing his subjects in contemporary uniform rather than classical dress, and the canvas at the National Gallery of Canada was widely copied in engraving.

title: The Love Letter
description: A young woman at a writing table looks up from a sealed letter, a sprig of flowers tucked among the ribbons of her dress, a small dog beside her. Oil on canvas of about 1770, now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the picture is among Fragonard's most polished essays in the gallant tabletop scene.

title: The Oath of Hannibal
description: The young Hannibal kneels at an altar before his father Hamilcar Barca, swearing the lifelong oath of enmity against Rome. Painted as a pendant to The Departure of Regulus for George III, RCIN 405417 in the Royal Collection, the picture pairs Carthaginian and Roman exemplars of stoic resolve.
credit: Royal Collection

title: Daniel Crommelin Verplanck
description: Nine-year-old Daniel Crommelin Verplanck sits against a classical column in a red coat, a squirrel on a chain in his lap, with a landscape background traditionally identified as the Verplanck country house at Fishkill-on-Hudson. John Singleton Copley painted the portrait in 1771, and the work is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: Ezekiel Goldthwait
description: The Boston merchant and town clerk Ezekiel Goldthwait is shown three-quarter length in a dark red coat, holding a quill pen in one hand and a folded document in the other, with papers and an inkstand on the table beside him. Painted in oil on canvas in 1771, it is paired at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (accession 41.85) with Copley's companion portrait of his wife Elizabeth.

title: JohnMontresorByCopley
description: Captain John Montresor, the British military engineer who surveyed Quebec and Detroit, sits in three-quarter view in his red officer's coat. Copley painted the portrait in oil on canvas around 1771, during his Boston practice before he left for London on the eve of the Revolution. The Detroit Institute of Arts holds the canvas.
credit: From the Detroit Institute of Arts ( http://www.dia.org/ ). URL at time of upload: http://www.dia.org/the_collection/overview/viewobject.asp?objectid=41296

title: Jupiter and Antiope
description: A satyr in a spotted pelt leans over the reclining nude figure of Antiope, drawing aside a white cloth as she sleeps in a woodland setting. The work, dated 1771 and associated with the collection at Sens, was painted by David before his departure for Rome and belongs to his early Rococo phase — a sensual mythological subject he would later set aside in favour of Neoclassical severity. The composition echoes a long tradition of the Jupiter-and-Antiope theme in French painting.
credit: Histoire de Sens ville d'Yonne

title: Mrs Humphrey Devereux
description: Mrs Humphrey Devereux, an older woman in a dark dress and white lace cap, leans forward with her elbow on a polished red table, her chin resting on her raised hand. Copley painted the half-length portrait in oil on canvas in 1771; it now hangs at the Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tamaki.

title: Portrait of a Lady
description: A woman in a golden silk gown sits in three-quarter view, holding an open letter or document in both hands. Copley painted this half-length portrait in oil on canvas in 1771, during his Boston practice documenting the merchant class of pre-Revolutionary New England. The blue silk wrap edged in gold, the sitter's composed gaze, and the crimson chair back demonstrate Copley's command of textile and surface.

title: Portrait of Mrs. Thomas Gage
description: Margaret Kemble Gage, wife of British General Thomas Gage, is shown seated in a rose-coloured gown with a decorative blue and gold sash and a turban-style headdress trimmed with gold, her elbow resting on the arm of a dark upholstered sofa. Copley painted the portrait in 1771, adopting the fashionable Turkish-costume convention for informal female portraiture. The work hangs at the Timken Museum of Art in San Diego.
credit: from http://www.mcah.columbia.edu/dbcourses/vrc/large/copley_gage_mrs_thomas.jpg Uploaded to english Wikipedia by en:User:Flying Jazz on 9 May 2005.

title: Sir Joseph Banks
description: Joseph Banks stands full-length in a Maori flax cloak, with a taiaha and other Polynesian objects arranged beside him, presenting the naturalist as the celebrated voyager he had become after Cook's first Pacific expedition. West painted the portrait between 1771 and 1772 in London; it is now in the collection of the Usher Gallery in Lincoln.

title: The Alchemist Discovering Phosphorus or The Alchemist in Search of the Philosophers Stone
description: An aged alchemist kneels before a glowing flask as phosphorus ignites in his laboratory, alluding to Hennig Brand's 1669 discovery. Wright stages the scene with the theatrical single-source illumination that defined his Enlightenment subjects, balancing scientific wonder against gothic shadow.
credit: http://www.tms.org/pubs/journals/JOM/0706/fig3.jpg http://www.culturevoyage.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2013/03/Alchymist.jpg

title: The Progress of Love: The Meeting
description: In a lush garden garden, a young man peers over a low wall while a young woman reclines below, gazing up at him beneath a stone statue of Venus and her attendant putto. Painted between 1771 and 1773 as the first of four panels in Fragonard's Progress of Love cycle, originally commissioned by Madame du Barry for her pavilion at Louveciennes, the suite is now held at the Frick Collection in New York.

title: Apollo and Diana Attacking the Children of Niobe
description: Apollo and Diana descend from clouds to strike down the children of Niobe, who raises her arm in anguished supplication at the centre of the composition, surrounded by falling and dying figures. David painted this canvas in 1772 as one of his repeated unsuccessful entries for the Prix de Rome, a competition he finally won in 1774; the work now hangs at the Dallas Museum of Art. The dynamic groupings and mythological subject reflect the Neoclassical ambitions David pursued throughout his early career.

title: Elizabeth and Mary Linley
description: Elizabeth Linley stands at the left in a blue gown while her younger sister Mary sits beside her in an amber dress, holding a sheet of music. The two are posed in a wooded glade in Gainsborough's characteristic landscape setting. Painted around 1772 and retouched in 1785, the double portrait is in the collection of Dulwich Picture Gallery, London.

title: Erasistratus the Physician Discovers the Love of Antiochus for Stratonice
description: The court physician Erasistratus takes the pulse of the lovesick prince Antiochus as his stepmother Stratonice enters the chamber, revealing the cause of his illness. West painted the Hellenistic anecdote, drawn from Plutarch, in 1772. The canvas is in the Birmingham Museum of Art.

title: Portrait of Samuel Adams
description: Samuel Adams stands in a red coat, one hand resting on rolled documents and the other pointing toward them, in a pose that conveys civic resolve. Copley painted the portrait around 1772, capturing the leading Patriot politician at a moment of political tension; the work is now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
credit: Humanitiesweb.org

title: The Death of Chevalier Bayard
description: The French knight Bayard, mortally wounded by an arquebus shot during the retreat from the Sesia in 1524, leans against a tree to receive the rites as his enemy the Constable de Bourbon kneels beside him. West painted the canvas in 1772 for George III; it remains in the Royal Collection.
credit: Royal Collection

title: Mademoiselle Guimard as Terpsichore
description: The Paris Opera dancer Marie-Madeleine Guimard appears as Terpsichore, the muse of dance, in classical drapery with a lyre at her side. Jacques-Louis David painted the canvas around 1773-1775 in connection with the decoration of Guimard's hotel particulier on the Chaussee d'Antin, a scheme the young painter is traditionally said to have taken over after the dancer's quarrel with Fragonard. The picture was left unfinished and offers an early glimpse of the classicizing manner David would soon bring to maturity.
credit: Christie's

title: Portrait of Mr. and Mrs. Thomas Mifflin
description: Thomas Mifflin, the Pennsylvania merchant and future first governor of the state, sits beside his wife Sarah Morris, who works at a small loom of fringed silk. Copley painted the double portrait in 1773, just before sailing for Europe, as a tribute to the non-importation movement that the Mifflins championed. The Philadelphia Museum of Art holds it.

title: The Artist's Brother
description: An early portrait by the teenage Vigée Le Brun shows her younger brother Étienne in elegant attire, his open expression rendered with the precocious assurance that would soon win her royal commissions. The handling already displays the porcelain finish and Rococo grace of her mature manner.
credit: “Magasine GeoArt Élisabeth Vigée Lebrun” - 2015

title: The muscles of the human body
description: The muscles of the human body, fourth layer, seen from the front. Colour mezzotint by A. E.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/11/91/b968a96254a23b2eb18be9b6d426.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/V0007799.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-04-05): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/jesm64dw CC-BY-4.0

title: The Wife of Arminius brought captive to Germanicus
description: Thusnelda, wife of the Cheruscan chief Arminius, stands captive with her son before the Roman general Germanicus after the campaigns of 15 AD. West painted the Tacitean episode in 1773 for George III as part of the Windsor history series, in oil on canvas. It remains in the Royal Collection.
credit: Royal Collection

title: Adolf Ludvig Gustav Albert Couschi
description: Adolf Ludvig Gustav Albert Couschi, known at the Swedish court as Badin, is shown holding a chess piece over a chessboard, wearing an elaborate feathered turban and ornate blue court costume with a white sash. Gustaf Lundberg drew the pastel portrait in 1775; it is held by the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm under inventory NMGrh 1455. Couschi had been brought to Sweden as a child and became a well-known figure at the court of Queen Lovisa Ulrika.
credit: Nationalmuseum

title: Benjamin Waterhouse
description: Benjamin Waterhouse sits three-quarter length before an open book, his right hand raised to his cheek in a pose of relaxed thoughtfulness. Stuart painted the portrait in 1775 and it is now held at the Redwood Library and Athenaeum in Newport, Rhode Island.
credit: Redwood Library and Athenaeum, Newport, Rhode Island, Bequest of Louisa Lee Waterhouse (Mrs. Benjamin Waterhouse) of Cambridge, Massachusetts. Digitized at National Gallery of Art

title: Blindman's Buff
description: Elegantly dressed women and children gather in a sunlit park, some reclining and others holding parasols, in a hazy golden landscape beneath flowering trees. Fragonard painted this pastoral garden scene between 1775 and 1780, during the period in which he produced numerous fêtes galantes in the Rococo tradition.

title: Daniel Interpreting to Belshazzar the Writing on the Wall - 485-2018 - Saint Louis Art Museum
englishTitle: Daniel Interpreting to Belshazzar the Writing on the Wall
description: Daniel gestures emphatically as he interprets the divine writing to Belshazzar, the Babylonian king, who recoils on his throne amid alarmed courtiers; a scroll bearing the inscription is displayed at the left. West painted the canvas in oil on canvas in 1775, drawing on the Book of Daniel for an early biblical history. The Saint Louis Art Museum acquired the work in 2018.

title: De Kloveniersdoelen aan de Amstel-De Kloveniersburgwal op de hoek van de Amstel met de toren "Swijgh Utrecht"
englishTitle: The Kloveniersdoelen on the Amstel, with the Tower 'Swijgh Utrecht'
description: View of the Kloveniersdoelen on the Amstel, with the militia guildhall and the Swijgh Utrecht tower rising at the corner of the Kloveniersburgwal. Painted in 1775, the cityscape records a stretch of Amsterdam that the Dutch capital would substantially rebuild in the nineteenth century.

title: Isaac's servant tying the bracelet on Rebecca's arm
description: Abraham's servant Eliezer fastens the gold bracelet on Rebecca's wrist at the well, marking her as the chosen bride for Isaac. West painted the Genesis episode in 1775 in oil on canvas. The composition belongs to a series of Old Testament subjects he produced for English patrons in the 1770s.

title: Mr. and Mrs. Ralph Izard
description: The South Carolina planter Ralph Izard and his wife Alice DeLancey sit at a marble table in a Roman interior, a Greek vase between them and the Colosseum visible through the window. Copley painted the double portrait in 1775 during the couple's grand tour in Rome, his first European commission. The Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, holds it.
credit: The Athenaeum [1]

title: Portrait of Colonel Guy Johnson and Karonghyontye
description: Colonel Guy Johnson, British superintendent of Indian affairs for the northern colonies, stands in a red military coat beside the Mohawk diplomat Karonghyontye, with a waterfall visible in the distance. West painted the double portrait between 1775 and 1776, and the canvas is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: Photographed by me at the NGA, 18 August 2005

title: The Honourable Mrs Graham
description: The Honourable Mrs Graham stands full-length in an elaborate silver-white gown with a rose-patterned skirt, a feathered hat, and one hand resting on a stone column. Gainsborough exhibited the portrait at the Royal Academy in 1777; her widower later withheld it from public view, and it entered the Scottish National Gallery in 1859. The picture, painted in 1775, is regarded as one of the grandest statements of his Bath-period portraiture.

title: The Visit to the Nursery
description: A young mother and a visitor lean over a wicker cradle as a nurse holds an older child by the hand, the scene set in a sun-streaked country room. Fragonard painted the canvas around 1775, in the genre vein of domestic sentiment that Greuze had popularized. The National Gallery of Art in Washington holds it under accession 32685.

title: William Curtis 1775
description: Oil portrait of the English botanist William Curtis, demonstrator of plants at the Chelsea Physic Garden from 1771 and later author of Flora Londinensis. The picture, held in the RHS Lindley Collections, captures Curtis during the years before he launched The Botanical Magazine in 1787.
credit: Royal Horticultural Society (London)

title: 'The Fountaine Family' by John Singleton Copley
description: A conversation piece showing a man, woman, and two children with a spaniel in an elegant interior, painted by John Singleton Copley in 1776 at the outset of his English career. The warmly lit domestic setting and characterful poses reflect the English conversation-piece tradition, and the work is now at Tate Britain.
credit: Tate Britain

title: Benjamin West
description: A young man in a broad-brimmed black hat and blue coat rests his chin on one hand while holding drawing implements, in a pose that signals his identity as an artist. This circa 1776 work is a copy after a self-portrait by Benjamin West, the Pennsylvania-born painter who served as historical painter to George III and later as President of the Royal Academy. The original is attributed to West himself; this version is recorded at the National Gallery of Art.

title: Gunseondo
description: Gunseondo depicts a procession of Daoist immortals rendered in Kim Hong-do's fluid ink line across multiple screen panels, with figures shown in animated groupings alongside animals and attendants. Painted in 1776 for the court of King Jeongjo, it stands as one of the Korean master's most ambitious figure compositions and a landmark work of the Joseon dynasty's classical painting tradition.

title: Helen Brought to Paris
description: A seated Paris gazes toward Helen, who is presented to him by a winged Cupid and a second female figure — likely Venus — against a luminous sky with a red curtain at the left. West painted the Homeric subject in 1776, during his tenure as historical painter to George III. No institutional credit is confirmed in the available record.

title: Kim Hong-do
englishTitle: Kyujanggakdo (View of the Royal Library Kyujanggak)
description: Kim Hong-do's view of Kyujanggak records the royal library founded on the grounds of Changdeokgung by King Jeongjo in 1776. The painting shows the complex of buildings nestled among trees against a mountainous backdrop, rendered in the bird's-eye topographical mode characteristic of Joseon court records. Kim Hong-do served as a designated court painter to King Jeongjo.

title: Portrait of Johann Christian Bach
description: Portrait of the composer Johann Christian Bach (1735–1782), youngest son of J. S. Bach and known in England as the 'English Bach'. Gainsborough painted this likeness in 1776, showing the sitter in a buff coat and blue satin waistcoat, resting his hands on a sheet of music. The portrait was commissioned for the gallery of musicians in Bologna assembled by Padre Giovanni Battista Martini.

title: Richard St George Mansergh-St George
description: Richard St George Mansergh-St George stands full-length in the red uniform of the 4th Regiment of Foot, hat in hand, with ships and a coastal cliff visible in the stormy background. A dog sits at his feet. Gainsborough painted the portrait between 1776 and 1780, and it is now held at the National Gallery of Victoria.

title: The Copley Family
description: Group portrait of the artist with his wife Susanna, their four children, and his Loyalist father-in-law Richard Clarke, painted in London after Copley departed Boston in 1774. Exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1777, the large canvas announced Copley's arrival on the London scene; it is now at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: George IV
description: Double portrait of the future George IV in state robes alongside his younger brother Prince Frederick, later Duke of York, painted in 1777 for George III. West executed the canvas (RCIN 403399, Royal Collection) while serving as historical painter to the king, a post he had held since 1772.
credit: Royal Collection

title: John singleton copley
description: A bust-length study of a young Black man, painted by Copley around 1777–78 as a preparatory work connected to Watson and the Shark. The sitter wears a plain brownish garment and turns his head slightly, mouth open, his expression alert and individualised. The Detroit Institute of Arts holds the canvas, which presents its subject with a directness and dignity rare in British painting of the period.

title: Portrait of Anne
description: Anne, Countess of Chesterfield, is shown seated in a pale blue satin gown, leaning thoughtfully against a stone balustrade with trees and a landscape behind her. Gainsborough painted the canvas in 1777–78 with the sweeping, atmospheric brushwork of his late style. The portrait is now at the J. Paul Getty Museum.

title: Two Officers and a Groom in a Landscape
description: Two officers pause with their horses in a rocky landscape: one, in scarlet regimentals, gestures with his hat toward the distant valley, while his companion in a pale uniform rests a boot on a boulder; their groom waits with the mounts at the left. West, born in Pennsylvania and by then historical painter to George III in London, painted the canvas in 1777, in the midst of the American Revolution. Oil on canvas, 101.6 by 127 cm; Princeton University Art Museum.
credit: Princeton University Art Museum

title: Académie d´homme
description: Académie of a recumbent male nude, posed as the dead Hector with one arm hanging limp. David painted the study in 1778 during his Prix de Rome years at the French Academy in Rome, and it never left his studio, eventually entering the Musée Fabre in Montpellier where it remains.
credit: Musée Fabre

title: Joseph Vernet
description: A half-length portrait of the marine painter Joseph Vernet, palette and brushes in hand, in a powdered wig and dark coat against a neutral ground. Vigée Le Brun renders the older painter with the soft modeling and warm flesh tones that defined her late-Ancien Régime studio practice, treating him as a colleague rather than a patron.
credit: Sammyday (2010-10-23)

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Portrait of Margaret Gainsborough
description: A half-length portrait of Margaret Gainsborough, née Burr, the artist's wife, shows her in a dark blue velvet shawl over a gold-brown dress with white lace at the throat. Gainsborough painted the canvas in 1778 with characteristically free brushwork, the features carefully observed against the loosely rendered drapery. The work is held by the Samuel Courtauld Trust at the Courtauld Gallery, London.

title: Portrait of Mrs. Grace Dalrymple Elliott
description: Full-length portrait of the courtesan Grace Dalrymple Elliott, known as 'Dally the Tall', in a yellow Van Dyck-style gown with a towering 1770s coiffure. Commissioned by her lover the Earl of Cholmondeley and shown at the Royal Academy in 1778, the canvas measures 234.3 by 153.7 cm and is now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: The Artist Moved by the Grandeur of Antique Fragments
description: A small artist figure slumps on a plinth dwarfed by colossal antique fragments — a great foot and an outstretched hand — in this pen, ink and wash drawing by Henry Fuseli made during his Roman years (1778–1779). The sheet, now at the Kunsthaus Zürich, encapsulates the Romantic sense of awe and inadequacy before the ruins of classical civilisation.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"f/fuseli/02antiqu"

title: The Battle of La Hogue
description: Admiral George Rooke stands sword aloft in a boat amid the wreckage of the French fleet during the 1692 engagement off La Hogue, with the Soleil Royal running aground in the distance. West began this version in 1778, then his pupil John Trumbull completed it in 1785 and West retouched it in 1806, now at the National Gallery of Art.

title: The Death of Chatham
description: The scene shows William Pitt the Elder, Earl of Chatham, collapsing among peers in the House of Lords on 7 April 1778 after speaking against the surrender of the American colonies. West, history painter to George III, painted this version of the subject in 1778; the more celebrated rendering of the scene was ultimately executed by his contemporary John Singleton Copley.

title: The Collapse of the Earl of Chatham in the House of Lords
description: William Pitt collapses among fifty-five identifiable peers beneath tapestries of the Spanish Armada's defeat, the moment of his fall in the House of Lords on 7 April 1778. Copley worked on the ten-foot canvas for two years and in 1781 installed it in a pavilion as a paying one-work show; it is now at Tate.

title: Zentralbibliothek Zürich - Portät von Anna Magdalena Schweizer geb Hess im Alter von 27 Jahren - 000003019
englishTitle: Portrait of Anna Magdalene Schweizer, née Hess
description: Anna Magdalena Schweizer, née Hess (1751–1814), is shown in a precise profile view, her hair swept up and secured with a ribbon bow. Henry Fuseli executed this pencil portrait drawing on 15 March 1779, when the sitter was 27 years old; it is preserved in the Zentralbibliothek Zürich.

title: Danwon-Bbalrae.teo
description: Women beating laundry at a stream while a passing scholar peers over a rock, from Kim Hong-do's Danwon pungsokdo cheop. The sheet, ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, is held by the National Museum of Korea and belongs to the album of genre scenes that established his reputation as the great chronicler of everyday Joseon life.

title: Danwon-Mudong
description: Dancing boy with musicians playing flute, drum, and zither, a scene from the Danwon pungsokdo cheop. Kim Hong-do worked in ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, with the album of genre studies now held by the National Museum of Korea and considered a benchmark of late 18th-century Joseon painting.

title: Danwon-Nongali
description: Farmers driving an ox-drawn plough through a paddy field, from the Danwon pungsokdo cheop. Kim Hong-do painted the leaf in ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, part of the album of agricultural and artisanal scenes held by the National Museum of Korea as a record of common life under King Jeongjo.

title: Danwon-Ssireum
description: Two wrestlers locked in a ssireum hold while spectators ring the contest, divided into upper and lower groups around the action. From the Danwon pungsokdo cheop in the National Museum of Korea, the sheet is ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm and counts as the most reproduced image of Joseon genre painting.

title: Hugh Montgomerie
description: Hugh Montgomerie, later 12th Earl of Eglinton, stands in the full Highland dress of a British officer — red coat, tartan kilt, and feathered bonnet — his sword at his side and a battle in smoke behind him. Copley painted the full-length portrait in London in 1780 to mark Montgomerie's military service, including his years with the 77th (Highland) Regiment during the Seven Years' War.

title: Johann Heinrich Füssli 064
description: The sea-nymph Thetis bends in mourning over the corpse of her son Achilles, her grief amplified by the painter's sinuous neoclassical line. Fuseli reinterprets the Homeric scene through the proto-Romantic lens of sublime emotion, giving the figures attenuated, almost weightless poise.

title: Kim Hong-do
englishTitle: Feast for the Pyongyang Governor (Scene One: Dinner)
description: Officials and attendants are gathered in an open courtyard before the Pyongyang governor's pavilion, with performers arranged in the forecourt below the dais. The panoramic composition records the banquet in the descriptive mode of late Joseon court documentary painting. This is the first of a three-part series by Kim Hong-do depicting the feast.

title: Kiyonaga bathhouse women-2
description: Half of a celebrated diptych depicting women in a public bathhouse, an unusually informal subject from the Tenmei era. Kiyonaga, head of the Torii school, sets his tall, calm figures in the careful spatial recession that reformed bijinga for the next generation.
credit: Kiyonaga_bathhouse_women.jpg

title: Madame Lebrun
description: A young Frenchwoman in a powdered chignon and pale gauze gown sits half-length against an indistinct landscape. Gainsborough painted the sitter, identified as Madame Lebrun, in London in 1780 with the feathery brushwork and limited palette he favoured in his late portraiture.

title: Patroclus
description: A muscular male nude is shown from behind, seated on red drapery against a dark rocky ground, his body turned away from the viewer in a classic académie pose. Painted in Rome in 1780 during David's pensionnat at the French Academy, the study is an exercise in heroic anatomy and the rendering of the back and shoulders from life. It is catalogued by the Web Gallery of Art as Patroclus, the Homeric hero whose death sets the Iliad's climax in motion.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"d/david_j/1/107david"

title: Peace bringing back Prosperity
description: An allegorical pair: Peace, in classical drapery, gently leads forward Abundance, who carries a sheaf of wheat and a cornucopia. The painting was Vigée Le Brun's reception piece for the Académie Royale, accepted in 1783, and shows her combining Neoclassical subject matter with the warm flesh tones and silken finish of her portrait practice.

provenance.collection: Académie royale de peinture et de sculpture

title: Songhamaenghodo
description: A tiger strides forward beneath a gnarled pine, rendered in colour on silk in the Korean Joseon tradition of auspicious beast painting. The work, attributed to Kim Hong-do (1745–1806?), pairs the apotropaic tiger with the longevity symbol of the pine and is held at the Ho-Am Art Museum.

title: The Garroted Man
description: An etching of a condemned prisoner slumped in the iron collar of the garrote, crucifix in hand. Goya pares the scene to a single lit body against deep aquatint shadow, prefiguring the political grimness of the Disasters of War.
credit: National Gallery of Art .

title: The muscles of the hand
englishTitle: The Muscles of the Hand and Foot
description: An anatomical engraving combining a flayed hand after Bernhard Siegfried Albinus with a foot after De Courcelles, the muscles, tendons and bones laid bare for study. Engraved by Robert Bénard for the late eighteenth-century editions of the Encyclopédie, the plate typifies the Enlightenment project of consolidating earlier anatomical illustration into a single compendium.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/c4/a6/3cc95581d5ae18c92610bd0262f4.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/V0007837.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-04-05): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/g8rb2exe CC-BY-4.0

title: Woman in Blue
description: A three-quarter-length portrait of a woman in a blue silk gown, her tall powdered wig adorned with feathers and a blue ribbon, set against a dark ground. The cool palette and freely handled brushwork are characteristic of Gainsborough's manner from the late 1770s to early 1780s. The canvas is in the Hermitage Museum, St Petersburg.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"g/gainsbor/07lady_b"

title: Portrait of a Woman
description: A bust-length likeness of a woman against a neutral ground, her face modelled with the smooth finish Boilly cultivated for small cabinet portraits. Oil on canvas, 22.2 by 17.5 cm, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. Boilly produced hundreds of these compact heads for a Parisian middle-class clientele.

title: Portret konny Stanisława Kostki Potockiego
description: Stanisław Kostka Potocki reins in a grey horse and extends his arm in a saluting gesture, dressed in a white open-necked shirt with a blue sash and breeches, a hound crouching below the horse's hooves. The stone architecture in the background recalls the antique settings David absorbed during his Roman years. Painted in 1781, the portrait follows the tradition of the Baroque equestrian portrait while projecting an Enlightenment ideal of aristocratic ease.

title: Giovanna Baccelli
description: Full-length portrait of the Italian dancer Giovanna Baccelli (c. 1753–1801), painted by Thomas Gainsborough around 1782. The work depicts her in elegant 18th-century attire against a natural background, capturing the grace and poise of one of the era's most celebrated performers.

title: Madame du Barry
description: Madame du Barry is portrayed in a formal silver-white silk gown with lace-trimmed ruffled sleeves and a pink sash, her powdered hair crowned with a wreath of white feathers and flowers. She stands before a garden backdrop, holding a garland of colourful blooms. Vigée Le Brun painted this three-quarter-length portrait in 1782; it is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: The Corcoran Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C. [1]

title: Portrait of Henry Laurens
description: Henry Laurens sits in a rich burgundy velvet suit, resting one arm on a table strewn with documents and a quill, in this formal portrait by John Singleton Copley dated 1782. Copley painted Laurens in London shortly after his release from the Tower of London, where he had been held as a captured American envoy, and the composition conveys the statesman's recovered dignity.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic

title: Self Portrait in a Straw Hat
description: The artist holds palette and brushes beneath a wide plumed straw hat, smiling outward in a pose adapted from Rubens's Chapeau de Paille. Vigée Le Brun cast herself as both fashionable subject and confident professional, a self-promotional image she repeated.

title: The Skater
description: William Grant of Congalton glides on the frozen Serpentine in a black coat and hat, arms folded, with skating figures and Westminster trees behind. Stuart's 1782 portrait, exhibited at the Royal Academy, established his London reputation and is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: The Tribute Money
description: John Singleton Copley's oil on canvas depicts the Gospel episode of the tribute money, in which Christ, asked whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, points heavenward as a grey-bearded questioner indicates the coin lying in his open palm. The half-length figures press close around Christ, their faces picked out against a dark ground in a deliberately old-masterly manner. Copley gave the painting to the Royal Academy of Arts in London in 1782 as his Diploma Work following his election as a Royal Academician.

title: Yolande-Martine-Gabrielle de Polastron
description: Yolande de Polastron, Duchess of Polignac and intimate of Marie Antoinette, is shown half-length in a straw hat adorned with flowers and black feathers, a white gauze dress, and a dark shawl. Her hands rest lightly on a ledge. Vigée Le Brun signed and dated the canvas 1782; the portrait epitomises her characteristically luminous flesh tones and the informal elegance fashionable at the late ancien régime court.

title: Admiral Rodney at the Battle of the Saintes
description: A swagger portrait of Admiral Lord Rodney, victor over the French at the 1782 Battle of the Saintes, the captured ensign of the Ville de Paris draped behind him. Gainsborough's feathery brushwork and silvery palette soften the formal demands of state portraiture.
credit: philipmould.com

title: American Commissioners of the Preliminary Peace Agreement with Great Britain
description: John Jay, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Henry Laurens and William Temple Franklin sit together around a table in West's unfinished oil sketch for the planned Treaty of Paris group portrait. The British commissioners refused to sit, and West abandoned the canvas; the fragment is held at the Winterthur Museum in Delaware.

title: Coastal Landscape with a Shepherd and His Flock
description: A late landscape in which a shepherd and flock cross a windswept shore beneath gathering clouds. Gainsborough loosens the topography into soft, tonal silhouettes, prefiguring the atmospheric coastal scenes that would influence British Romantic painters.

title: Frances Browne
description: Frances Browne, later Mrs John Douglas, is shown in a silvery-white silk gown, seated against a stone balustrade in a parkland setting. Gainsborough painted the portrait in 1783–84, and it is now held at Waddesdon Manor under the care of the National Trust.
credit: National Trust, Waddesdon Manor

title: John Adams
description: John Adams stands in a brown coat beside a globe and a draped table, one hand resting on a sword hilt, the other holding diplomatic papers. Copley painted Adams in London in 1783 as the Massachusetts minister was negotiating the peace that recognised American independence; the canvas is in the Harvard Art Museums.

title: Marie-Antoinette with the Rose
description: Marie-Antoinette is shown in a pale blue silk court gown trimmed with lace, holding a single rose, with her powdered hair dressed high with feathers. Vigée Le Brun painted this formal version in 1783 as a replacement after the earlier informal muslin-dress portrait caused controversy at the Salon. The work is held at the Palace of Versailles.
credit: Versailles

title: Romantic Landscape with Sheep at a Spring
description: A flock of sheep gathers near a stone trough at the foot of a dramatic rocky gorge, with a herdsman resting among them in the foreground. The scene opens onto a distant mountain valley bathed in pale light. Gainsborough presented this canvas to the Royal Academy in 1783 as his diploma work on election, and it has remained in the Academy's collection ever since.

title: The Angora Cat
description: A young woman in a cream satin gown and wide-brimmed hat stands beside a low chair draped in richly patterned fabric, on which a white Angora cat rears up on its hind legs. Painted between 1783 and 1785 and attributed jointly to Jean-Honoré Fragonard and Marguerite Gérard, the panel hangs in the Wallraf-Richartz Museum in Cologne (inv. WRM 3652). An older male figure is partially visible in the shadowed background, lending the intimate interior a note of quiet observation.

title: The Death of Major Peirson
description: British soldiers surge around the fallen body of Major Francis Peirson after the French assault on Jersey in January 1781, the Union flag pressing forward through cannon smoke above the market square at St Helier. Copley undertook the large history painting on his own initiative and completed it in 1783; it now hangs in Tate Britain, London.

title: The Defeat of the Floating Batteries at Gibraltar
description: Spanish and French floating batteries burn at anchor under the guns of Gibraltar on the night of 13 September 1782, the rock looming behind the rescued sailors in the foreground. Copley spent eight years on the vast canvas, commissioned by the Corporation of the City of London, which still hangs in the Guildhall.

title: The Mall in St. James's Park
description: Fashionable Londoners promenade in pairs and small groups under the avenue of trees in St James's Park, their pale dresses catching the filtered light. Gainsborough modelled the figures from a doll dressed in different gowns; the canvas of 1783 is held by the Frick Collection in New York.

title: Dr Richard Price
description: The dissenting minister and moral philosopher Richard Price sits in his study in clerical black, a letter dated 1784 from Benjamin Franklin open before him. Benjamin West painted the portrait in 1784, the year Price recorded the sittings in his shorthand journal, now held at the National Library of Wales (NLW MS 20721A). This original oil painting remains in the National Library of Wales collection; a later copy is at the National Museum of Wales.

title: Oath of the Horatii
description: Three brothers extend their arms to swear an oath on the swords their father holds aloft, while their womenfolk collapse in grief at the right. David painted the canvas in Rome in 1784 to 1785 for Louis XVI, and its severe Doric setting and frieze-like composition became the manifesto of Neoclassical history painting; it hangs in the Louvre.
credit: photo Shonagon 2025-03-15

title: Portrait of Charles-Alexandre de Calonne
description: The Controller-General of Finances under Louis XVI shown at his desk, gesturing to a state document. The portrait, lavishly painted in silks and gilt, became notorious as evidence at court of the painter's alleged closeness to her Versailles sitters.

title: Portrait of Marie Gabrielle de Gramont
description: The young sitter stands in three-quarter view wearing a wide-brimmed straw hat and a dark bodice over a red skirt, a lace shawl draped across her shoulders. She holds a wicker basket of grapes and other fruit, lending the portrait a pastoral informality favoured by Vigée Le Brun in the 1780s. The painting, dated 1784, is held by the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City.

title: Sir Joshua Reynolds
description: Sir Joshua Reynolds, first president of the Royal Academy, sits in a dark coat with his wig powdered, his gaze turned away in three-quarter profile. Stuart painted the portrait in 1784 during the years he spent in Reynolds's London circle; the canvas is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art

title: "Scorn" from Le Brun
englishTitle: Scorn, from Le Brun's Conférence sur l'expression
description: Head turned aside with brow raised and lip curled to illustrate the passion of scorn, drawn from Charles Le Brun's lecture on expression. Issued by Bowles around 1785 in red-brown ink as part of his English Passions of the Soul, the print belongs to the long afterlife of Le Brun's 1668 lecture to the French Academy.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/52/44/ec51437539e95c5dd6a739a92e8d.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0012155.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-21): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/xzqa6mqj CC-BY-4.0

title: Dovedale by Moonlight
description: A silvered view of the Derbyshire valley of Dovedale under a full moon, its limestone crags and quiet river rendered in a cool, near-monochrome palette. Wright pursued nocturnes throughout his career, applying the dramatic chiaroscuro he developed for candlelit interiors to the open landscape.

title: Horror
description: The plate depicts a bearded male head, brows heavily contracted and gaze cast downward in an expression of dark, brooding horror. It is a stipple engraving in red-brown ink, issued by Bowles around 1785 as part of his English edition of Charles Le Brun's lecture on the passions of the soul, a treatise that codified facial expression for academic painters for over a century.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/17/11/9880e0b1b69697862b1a6a517b40.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0012156.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-21): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/m62pqnjs CC-BY-4.0

title: John Philip Kemble
description: John Philip Kemble appears in a deep blue coat with a frilled white cravat, painted by Gilbert Stuart in 1785, two years after Kemble's celebrated London debut as Hamlet at Drury Lane. The canvas, NPG 49 in the National Portrait Gallery, London, captures the actor in three-quarter bust-length pose against a warm brown ground.

title: Mrs Siddons
description: The actress Sarah Siddons sits in profile against a red curtain, wearing a striped silk dress and a wide black plumed hat. Gainsborough painted his rival to Reynolds's celebrated Tragic Muse in 1785, complaining of the difficulty of her nose; the canvas hangs in the National Gallery, London.

title: Plate from Le Brun
description: An engraved head labelled 'L'Attention' demonstrates one of the expressions catalogued by Charles Le Brun in his influential 1668 lecture on the passions of the soul. The plate comes from Carington Bowles's English edition published in London around 1785, and the impression belongs to the Wellcome Collection.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/35/5e/781f058d43966c2726d1dd7552db.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0012148.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-04-01): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/qtnm6psg CC-BY-4.0

title: Portrait of Benjamin West
description: Benjamin West sits in three-quarter view, a quill and open books before him and a sketch or canvas visible behind, conveying his identity as a practitioner of the intellectual arts. Gilbert Stuart painted his teacher and patron around 1785, during the years Stuart spent under West's roof in London after arriving from America. The portrait is recorded in the collection of the Athenaeum.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic

title: Portrait of Georgiana
description: Georgiana Cavendish, Duchess of Devonshire, is shown three-quarter length in a pale lace dress and a wide black hat trimmed with a white feather, holding a rose. Gainsborough painted the Whig hostess between 1785 and 1787; the canvas was famously stolen from Agnew's gallery in 1876, recovered in Chicago in 1901, and is now at Chatsworth House.

title: Portrait of Joseph Brant
description: The Mohawk leader Thayendanegea, known to the British as Joseph Brant, appears bust-length in a red cloak, silver gorget, and feathered headdress. Stuart painted Brant in London in 1785 during the Mohawk leader's diplomatic mission to negotiate land grants for Loyalist Iroquois resettled in Upper Canada after the American war.

title: Portrait of Mrs. Richard Brinsley Sheridan
dateCreated: between 1785 and 1787 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A portrait of Elizabeth Linley, singer and wife of the playwright Richard Brinsley Sheridan, shown seated against a windswept landscape. Gainsborough merges sitter and setting through loosely brushed foliage and the soft fall of her pink gown, characteristic of his late manner. The canvas, painted between 1785 and 1787, is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art pen Access Images Project. Link: https://www.nga.gov/content/ngaweb/Collection/art-object-page.99.html

title: Simple bodily pain
description: Head contracted around tightened brow and grimacing mouth to illustrate simple bodily pain, after Charles Le Brun. The red-brown stipple engraving was issued by Bowles around 1785 in his English Passions of the Soul, one of many reprints that carried Le Brun's expression studies into eighteenth-century drawing manuals.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/4a/d2/f9c736554fd6144aee6a52d6bd64.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0012151.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-21): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/af2tztpn CC-BY-4.0

title: Various objects
description: Letters, an engraving and a sprig of pansies arranged against a wood surface in a trompe l'oeil of pinned papers. Oil on canvas, 72.4 by 60.3 cm, at the Clark Art Institute, among Boilly's earliest illusionistic still lifes. Several of the letters are addressed to a Monsieur and Madame Dandré, and the pensées (French for both pansies and thoughts) suggest a dedication.
credit: clarkart.edu

title: Alexander III of Scotland Rescued from the Fury of a Stag by the Intrepidity of Colin Fitzgerald
