description: Colin Fitzgerald seizes the stag by the antlers to protect King Alexander III, whose white horse rears at the left, while the hunt party scatters across a dramatic Highland landscape. Benjamin West painted the medieval Scottish episode in 1786 for Francis Humberston Mackenzie, who wished to honour his clan's legendary descent from Fitzgerald. The picture, known also as The Death of the Stag, applies the heroic compositional energy West had established in his earlier history paintings.

title: Portrait of Madame Molé-Reymond
description: Madame Molé-Reymond, actress of the Comédie-Italienne, turns toward the viewer in a purple dress and broad blue hat trimmed with feathers, a fur muff clasped at her side. Vigée Le Brun captures the sitter's animated half-turn with a quick, energetic brushwork characteristic of her informal portraits of the late Ancien Régime. The work entered the collection of the Louvre's Department of Paintings and is dated 1786.
credit: Sammyday (2010-10-23)

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: George Augustus Eliott
description: A bust-length portrait study of George Augustus Eliott, 1st Baron Heathfield, in scarlet uniform with a plumed bicorn hat, set against a loose, smoky background. Copley painted this study in 1787 in connection with his large Siege of Gibraltar composition; the work is held at the National Portrait Gallery, London. Eliott's role as defender of Gibraltar during the Great Siege (1779–1783) is the subject's defining distinction.

title: Sarah Siddons
description: Sarah Siddons, the leading tragedienne of the London stage, is shown here in a white dress and a large white turban, her gaze turned towards the viewer, holding a fan. Gilbert Stuart painted the portrait in 1787 during his London years; it is NPG 50 in the National Portrait Gallery, London.

title: The Death of Socrates
description: Socrates sits upright on his prison bed, one hand reaching for the cup of hemlock, the other raised in mid-discourse as his grieving disciples surround him. David painted the canvas in 1787 for Charles-Michel Trudaine de la Sabliere, exhibiting it at the Salon as a Neoclassical exemplum of stoic civic virtue; it now hangs at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: The Institution of the Order of the Garter
description: Edward III invests the founding knights of the Order of the Garter in 1348, the Black Prince kneeling at the centre of a crowded hall hung with banners. West painted the picture for George III's Audience Chamber at Windsor as part of a chivalric history cycle; it remains in the Royal Collection as RCIN 407521.
credit: Royal Collection

title: The Marquise de Pezay
description: A double portrait set out of doors, the Marquise de Pezay seated beside the Marquise de Rougé, whose two young sons press in beside her. Painted on the eve of the Revolution, the canvas blends the natural settings and tender maternal grouping that Vigée Le Brun had refined in her portraits of Marie Antoinette and her circle.
credit: www.ne.jp; National Gallery of Art, Washington, DC

title: The Marsham Children
description: The four Marsham children of Stratton Strawless play in a wooded landscape, the eldest girl gathering nuts while her brother reaches up to a sapling. Gainsborough painted the group portrait in 1787, the year before his death, combining the conversation-piece tradition with the feathery foliage and silvery palette of his late manner.

title: Edward III Crossing The Somme
description: Edward III leads his army across the tidal ford at Blanchetaque in August 1346, mounted knights pressing forward as French defenders contest the far bank. Part of the Windsor history cycle commissioned by George III, West's canvas was painted in 1788 and is catalogued in the Royal Collection as RCIN 404566.
credit: Royal Collection

title: Edward III with the Black Prince after the Battle of Crécy
description: Edward III embraces his sixteen-year-old son the Black Prince on the field of Crecy in August 1346, French dead heaped at their feet. The 1788 canvas belongs to West's eight-picture chivalric cycle for the Audience Chamber at Windsor Castle, where it remains as RCIN 407523.
credit: Royal Collection

title: Élisabeth-Louise Vigée-Le Brun - Hubert Robert
description: Hubert Robert, the celebrated painter of ruins, is shown half-length in a dark coat with a red-lapelled collar and a loose white cravat, holding a palette and brushes. His grey curly hair and alert, upward gaze animate this intimate portrait of a fellow artist. Vigée Le Brun painted this in 1788, shortly before the Revolution disrupted the social world both painters shared.

title: Johann Heinrich Füssli 011
description: The Norse god Thor wrestles the Midgard Serpent in a churning sea, muscles knotted in the elongated, theatrical anatomy Fuseli favored. The Swiss-born painter mined Eddic and Miltonic mythology for charged subjects, exaggerating chiaroscuro and pose for sublime effect.

title: King Lear
description: Lear rages bareheaded on the heath as the Fool and disguised Edgar shelter against a wind-torn hovel, the storm tearing across a black sky. Painted in 1788 for John Boydell's Shakespeare Gallery, West's canvas illustrates Act III, scene 4; it now belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts Boston

title: Marie-Joseph-Yves-Gilbert du Motier
artist: Louis-Léopold Boilly / Formerly attributed to Henri-Pierre Danloux
description: A bust portrait of Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette, the officer who served in the American and French revolutions. Oil on canvas, dated 1788, formerly attributed to Henri-Pierre Danloux before being given to Boilly. The sitter is shown in civilian dress against a plain ground.

title: Paris and Helen
description: Paris, partially draped and holding a golden lyre, sits turned toward Helen, who stands close beside him in a richly coloured interior with heavy blue and red fabric. Commissioned by the comte d'Artois in 1788, David's canvas is now in the Louvre and reflects the archaeological exactness he developed from his Roman studies.

title: Portrait of Monsieur de Lavoisier and his Wife
description: The chemist Antoine Lavoisier looks up from a manuscript while his wife Marie-Anne stands at his side, her arm resting on the back of his chair; their pneumatic apparatus and glassware are arrayed on a red-draped table. David completed this double portrait in 1788, the year before Lavoisier published the Traité élémentaire de chimie. It entered the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1977 as accession 1977.10.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art : entry 436106 (accession number: 1977.10)

title: Portrait of Muhammad Dervish Khan
description: Muhammad Dervish Khan stands full-length against an open sky, wearing white robes and an elaborately embroidered outer garment, a curved sabre held at his side. Vigée Le Brun painted this monumental portrait in Paris in 1788, presenting her subject with the formal gravity of state portraiture.

title: Thomas Gage John Singleton Copley
description: General Thomas Gage stands in the scarlet uniform of a British commander, his left hand resting on a cane while his right gestures toward the massed troops visible in the landscape behind him. Copley's three-quarter-length oil on canvas (127 × 101 cm) is inscribed at the lower right with Gage's name and death date of 1788; it belongs to the Paul Mellon Collection at the Yale Center for British Art.
credit: Yale Center for British Art, Paul Mellon Collection

title: 김홍도 금강사군첩 - 총석정
description: The basalt sea-stacks of Chongseokjeong rising from the East Sea coast, the fourth leaf of Kim Hong-do's album of the four districts of Geumgang. Ink and light colour on silk, roughly 30 by 44 cm, painted about 1788 after a tour the court painter made of Mount Geumgang and Gangwon Province under King Jeongjo. The clustered hexagonal columns are drawn in fine vertical strokes.

title: A Moonlight with a Lighthouse
description: A tall lighthouse with its lantern ablaze stands beside the Italian coast, its glow competing with a full moon rising through clouds in a teal nocturnal sky. Wright of Derby, painted in 1789, here applies his characteristic study of competing artificial and natural light sources to an outdoor coastal scene. The work is held at Tate, London.

title: Deux jeunes amies qui s'embrassent
description: "Deux jeunes amies qui s'embrassent" ("Two Young Female Friends Kissing") Painting created by French artist Louis-Léopold Boilly circa 1789-1793. Wiltshire, The Ramsbury Manor Foundation
credit: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra / musée Cognacq-Jay, Paris (Wiltshire, The Ramsbury Manor Foundation)

title: Elisabeth Louise Vigée-Lebrun
description: Vigée Le Brun embraces her young daughter Julie, the painter in a white dress with red sash and headband, the child in blue. The intimate staging — figures locked in mutual embrace against a plain ground — was devised to project natural maternal feeling for a Salon audience in 1789. The painting is held in the Louvre, Paris.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Elisabeth Vigée-Lebrun - Self-Portrait with Her Daughter
description: Vigée Le Brun holds her young daughter Julie in a close embrace, the artist dressed in a blue silk gown with long sleeves against a dark ground. Painted in 1789, the canvas adopts the Madonna-and-Child compositional type to express ideals of maternal sentiment fashionable in the late eighteenth century.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"v/vigee/self_da"

title: Portrait of John FitzGibbon
description: Gilbert Stuart's full-length portrait shows John FitzGibbon, 1st Earl of Clare, standing in the black robes of the Lord Chancellor of Ireland, heavy with gold embroidery, wearing a full-bottomed wig and lace cravat; the ceremonial mace and embroidered purse of state rest beside him. Stuart painted the portrait in 1789, the year FitzGibbon was appointed Lord Chancellor.

title: The Burghers of Calais
description: The six leading citizens of Calais approach Edward III bearing the city keys, as Queen Philippa intercedes on their behalf, the figures standing in a scene of formal submission. West's 1789 canvas illustrates the chronicle of Froissart and forms part of the Windsor history cycle for George III, catalogued in the Royal Collection as RCIN 404927.
credit: Royal Collection

title: The Lictors Bring to Brutus the Bodies of His Sons
description: The Roman consul Brutus sits in shadow as lictors return the bodies of his sons, executed for treason on his order. David exhibited the picture at the Salon weeks after the storming of the Bastille, and Revolutionary audiences read its civic stoicism as immediate political instruction.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: The Washington Family
description: George Washington, dressed in military uniform and seated at a table, examines a large map alongside Martha Washington and her two grandchildren in an interior setting hung with red drapery, with an enslaved attendant visible in the background. A globe stands to the left, reinforcing the statesmanlike theme. Savage worked on the canvas from 1789 to 1796 and subsequently engraved a widely circulated print after it; the painting is now at the National Gallery of Art.

title: A View of the Archbishop's Palace
description: Submitted to the Royal Academy in April 1790, the month Turner turned fifteen, this was his exhibition debut. The watercolour shows a topographical precision learned from Thomas Malton, the architecture set at sharp angles to flaunt the teenager's grasp of perspective.
credit: Indianapolis Museum of Art

title: Anne-Marie-Louise Thélusson
description: Anne-Marie-Louise Thélusson, Comtesse de Sorcy, sits in a white gown with a cream embroidered shawl, her powdered hair piled high, against a plain grey wall. David painted the portrait in 1790, the austere setting and clear contour typifying his late pre-Revolutionary female portraits. The picture is now in the Neue Pinakothek, Munich.
credit: http://www.wga.hu/frames-e.html?/html/d/david_j/2/210david.html Original uploader was Gogafax at en.wikipedia ; transfer was stated to be made by User:kirtap .

title: Countess Ekaterina Vassilievna Skavronskaia
description: The countess is shown seated, wearing a blue silk gown with olive-green sleeves and a gold sash, a white veil draped over her curling auburn hair. A pearl necklace and a small hand mirror complete the composition, which has the smooth, polished finish characteristic of Vigée Le Brun's court portraits. The work is dated 1790, painted during the artist's émigré years.

title: Fisherman's Cottage
description: Fishing boats with furled sails crowd a working harbour foreshore beside stone cottages, rendered in monochrome wash with pen-like linear strokes. The sheet dates to circa 1790, placing it among Turner's earliest topographical studies produced in the picturesque watercolour tradition. It is held at the Yale Center for British Art.

title: Maria Luisa di Borbone
description: Maria Luisa di Borbone, princess of the Two Sicilies, shown in a green silk gown and white cap, holding a pen over a large sheet of blue paper at a draped table. The portrait was painted in 1790 by Élisabeth Louise Vigée Le Brun during her Italian years following her departure from France, and is now held at the Museo di Capodimonte, Naples.
credit: www.metmuseum.org

title: Portrait of Emma
description: Emma Hamilton is depicted standing and turning, her right arm raised to hold a tambourine above her head, long dark hair streaming behind her. She wears a loose classical robe with a gold belt, and Vesuvius rises in the background — an allusion to her famous 'attitudes' performed in Naples. The portrait, dated circa 1790, is held by the Lady Lever Art Gallery.

title: Portrait of Princess Maria Christina
description: Princess Maria Christina of the Two Sicilies (1779–1849) is shown as a young girl in a white dress with a red sash, picking roses from a garden bush with a wicker basket of blooms at her side. Vigée Le Brun painted the portrait in 1790, during her period of exile from Revolutionary France. The work is held at the Museo di Capodimonte, Naples.

title: Self-portrait
description: Painted in Florence for the Uffizi's gallery of artists' self-portraits during her revolutionary exile, Vigée Le Brun shows herself at the easel sketching Marie Antoinette. The picture asserts both her professional standing as portraitist to the queen and her loyalty in the face of political upheaval.
credit: Art Renewal Center old image: from [1]

title: The Sorrows of Love
description: A woman supported by a companion grieves while a servant returns her portrait and an unopened letter, signalling the end of an affair. Oil on canvas, 45 by 55 cm, in the Wallace Collection, London. The picture belongs to a set of eleven works on the stages of love that Boilly painted for the Avignon collector Calvet de Lapalun.

title: Titania and Bottom
description: The fairy queen, drugged by Oberon's love-juice, fawns over the ass-headed weaver from A Midsummer Night's Dream. Fuseli, a key contributor to Boydell's Shakespeare Gallery, exaggerates limbs and eyes into a mannerist dream-language drawn from Michelangelo and his own night terrors.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — 3QFfp3FTlt8xYg Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N01228&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: Le Serment du Jeu de paume
description: Deputies of the Third Estate raise their right hands and swear not to disperse until France has a constitution, packed into the Versailles tennis court on 20 June 1789. David began this monumental project in 1791, working from sketches and portrait studies; the large unfinished drawing is now preserved at the Château de Versailles.

title: Portrait of Hyacinthe-Gabrielle Roland
description: The Parisian actress Hyacinthe-Gabrielle Roland — mistress and, from 1794, wife of Richard Wellesley, Earl of Mornington, which later made her Marchioness Wellesley — sits informally with loosened, ribboned hair against a stormy sky. Vigée Le Brun painted her in Rome in 1791, during the Italian years of her emigration from revolutionary France; the portrait now hangs in the Legion of Honor, Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco.
credit: ne.jp; The AMICA Library

provenance.collection: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco

title: Portrait of Maximilien de Robespierre
description: A presumed portrait of Maximilien de Robespierre in a high cravat, set against a dark ground. Oil on canvas, about 41 by 32 cm, in the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille and usually dated around 1791. The attribution and date remain contested, with some scholars placing the canvas before 1789.

title: Life Study of Lady Hamilton as the Cumaean Sybil
description: Emma Hamilton turns in the studio with a turbaned head and parted lips, posed as the prophetic Sibyl of Cumae. Vigée Le Brun carried the resulting composition through her exile from Naples to Vienna and Russia as a calling card of her Italian period.
credit: metmuseum.org

title: Portrait of Jan Anthony d'Averhoult
description: A portrait of Jan Anthony d'Averhoult, the Dutch Patriot of Huguenot descent who chaired parliament in 1792, the year of this likeness and of his death. Oil on canvas by Boilly, the sitter shown bust-length against a plain ground. The portrait dates from the height of the Revolutionary period.

title: The Rising Squall
description: An early oil view from the cliffs above the Avon Gorge as a sudden storm sweeps in over the Hot Wells spa. The seventeen-year-old Turner already orchestrates wind, rain and shifting light into a unified atmospheric event.
credit: Sotheby's, London, 2 July 2025, L25033, lot 28 ( 2000 × 1609 pixel / 1,40 MB ) — with frame

title: Catherine Brass Yates
description: Catherine Brass Yates is shown at her needlework, holding thread between her fingers, in a silvery-grey dress and a pale blue and white cap with ribbon trim. Stuart painted the New York merchant's wife in 1793 just after his return from Dublin; the canvas is now in the Andrew W. Mellon Collection at the National Gallery of Art.

title: Clare Hall and King’s College Chapel
description: An early topographical watercolour from Turner's Cambridge tour, viewing Clare Hall and the soaring Perpendicular pinnacles of King's College Chapel across the Cam. A stone bridge arches over the river in the foreground, and the architecture is rendered with careful precision. Dated 1793, the sheet is now in the collection of the Yale Center for British Art.

title: Horatio Gates
description: General Horatio Gates is shown in three-quarter length, wearing his dark blue Continental Army uniform with gold epaulettes and a large gold medal suspended from a blue ribbon sash — the Congressional Gold Medal awarded for his victory at Saratoga. Stuart painted the portrait between 1793 and 1794 and it is now in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
credit: Downloaded from The Athenaeum original is at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: King Lear and Cordelia
description: The mad Lear, crowned in wildflowers, is reunited with the kneeling Cordelia at the French camp in Act IV, scene 7 of Shakespeare's tragedy. West painted the canvas in 1793 for John Boydell's Shakespeare Gallery; it now belongs to the Folger Shakespeare Library.
credit: Folger Shakespeare Library Digital Image Collection http://luna.folger.edu/luna/servlet/s/0847d6

title: Portrait of La comtesse Siemontkowsky Bystry
description: A society portrait from Vigée Le Brun's years of exile from revolutionary France, painted in Vienna in 1793 when she received numerous commissions from Polish and Austrian aristocrats. The Countess is shown in a crimson antique-style drapery, wearing a floral wreath over a transparent veil and holding an ornate golden cup. The warm palette and classicising costume carry forward the idiom that had made Vigée Le Brun the pre-eminent portraitist of the Ancien Régime.

title: Princess Karoline von Liechtenstein
description: The young princess is depicted as Iris, barefoot and airborne amid stormy clouds, a length of golden gauze billowing from her shoulder while she extends one arm as if pointing the way of the rainbow. Vigée Le Brun completed the large canvas in 1793 in Vienna, during her years of exile from revolutionary France. The work exemplifies the artist's synthesis of Neoclassical mythological allegory with the elegant portraiture of her royal and aristocratic clientele.

title: The Death of Marat
description: The murdered Jacobin Jean-Paul Marat slumps in his medicinal bathtub, the bloodied knife on the floor and Charlotte Corday's letter still in his hand. David finished the canvas in October 1793, three months after the assassination, presenting it to the National Convention as a martyr's icon; it is now in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels.

title: Courtyard with Lunatics or Yard with Madmen
description: A small tin-plate painting from Goya's recovery after the illness that left him deaf, drawing on a violent scene he claimed to have witnessed in Zaragoza. Naked inmates wrestle under a barred opening while a warden flogs them, the cell's harsh chiaroscuro foreshadowing the Black Paintings.
credit: The Meadows Museum's Permanent Collection , accessed 2010-03-20.

title: Ebisu
description: The lucky deity Ebisu is shown clutching a large red sea bream and laughing, a basket of fish at his feet — a subject associated with good fortune and abundance. Issued in 1794 by Tōshūsai Sharaku, the print is part of the artist's brief but prolific output during a single ten-month period of activity.
credit: Yamaguchi, Keizaburō (1994). Sharaku no Zenbō 写楽の全貌 (in Japanese). Tōkyō Shoseki. ISBN 978-4-487-79075-3 .

title: Gentlemen Fishing
description: A group of gentlemen fish from a flat-bottomed boat moored against a dense reed bank, with ships and a distant tower visible on the horizon under a partly cloudy sky. West painted the small cabinet picture in 1794, a rare excursion into the genre of sporting and leisure scenes away from his grand-manner history practice. The signature and date appear at lower left.

title: PeterGansevoortByStuart
description: Peter Gansevoort, the defender of Fort Stanwix in 1777, wears the dark blue coat and gold epaulettes of a Continental general. Stuart painted the portrait in 1794, around the time Gansevoort was commissioned brigadier general of the New York militia; the canvas is now at the Munson-Williams-Proctor Arts Institute in Utica.
credit: Downloaded from the The Athenaeum Original is in the Munson-Williams-Proctor Institute of Art

title: Portrait of John Jay
description: John Jay is seated in the distinctive black and orange judicial robes of the first Chief Justice of the United States, one hand resting against an upright book or document beside him. Gilbert Stuart painted Jay in 1794, the year he travelled to Britain to negotiate the commercial treaty that bears his name; the portrait is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. The handling is Stuart's characteristic blend of assured brushwork and dignified Neoclassical restraint.
credit: The National Gallery of Art

title: Self-portrait
description: David portrays himself in three-quarter bust, holding a palette and brushes, wearing a white cravat beneath a reddish-brown coat. The self-portrait, executed in 1794 while he was imprisoned in the Luxembourg Palace after the fall of Robespierre, shows an intent, slightly dishevelled sitter against a plain warm ground. The canvas is now in the Louvre.

title: The Angler
description: Two figures rest on rocks beside a cascading woodland stream in this early watercolour by Turner, dated 1794. The lush, overhanging trees and tumbling water reflect his training in the British picturesque tradition. The work is held at the Yale Center for British Art.

title: The Triumph of Marat
description: A crowd carries the deputy Jean-Paul Marat aloft after his acquittal before the Revolutionary Tribunal in April 1793, banners and pikes raised above the throng. Oil on canvas, dated 1794, in the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille. Boilly turned to the multi-figure street scene that would occupy much of his later career.

title: William Bayard
description: The New York merchant William Bayard sits in three-quarter view at a writing table, papers in one hand and an inkstand at his elbow, his sage-green coat and white stock set against a backdrop of crimson drapery. Stuart painted the portrait in 1794, during his New York period and shortly before he moved to Philadelphia to begin the presidential portraits that would define his career.
credit: Gilbert Stuart

title: Boilly
description: A sleeping woman waking in disarranged bedclothes, the subject of Boilly's 'Le Doux Réveil' (The Gentle Awakening). Oil on canvas, catalogued J 7 in the Musée Cognacq-Jay, Paris. The boudoir scene is one of the lightly erotic interiors Boilly produced in the 1790s.
credit: This file was derived from: Boilly, Louis Léopold - Le Doux Réveil - J 7 - Musée Cognacq-Jay.jpg :

title: Harvesting at Windsor by Benjamin West
description: Workers cut and gather sheaves in the fields below Windsor Castle, whose outline rises on the distant ridge. Benjamin West painted this harvest scene in 1795; it is now in the Berger Collection, Denver, Colorado.
credit: Berger Collection: id #81 (Denver, Colorado)

title: Musidora and Her Two Companions
description: Three nude bathers from Thomson's poem The Seasons stand at a woodland pool while Damon watches unseen from the foliage. West first painted the subject in 1795 and retouched the canvas in 1806, working in the polished neoclassical idiom expected of the President of the Royal Academy.

title: Portrait of George Washington
description: Washington faces the viewer in a black coat with white stock, his powdered hair brushed back from a high forehead. The 1795 canvas at the Metropolitan Museum (accession 07.160) belongs to the so-called Vaughan type, the first of three Washington portrait formats Stuart developed from life sittings.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (accession number 07.160)

title: Portrait of Pierre Sériziat
description: Pierre Sériziat, the painter's brother-in-law, sits casually in riding dress — black tailcoat, buff breeches, and a tall black hat — a riding crop in one hand. David painted the portrait in 1795 after his release from prison following the fall of Robespierre, combining relaxed informality with Neoclassical clarity of contour.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"d/david_j/3/308david"

title: Takashima Ohisa Using Two Mirrors to Observe Her Coiffure: Night of the Asakusa Marketing Festival
englishTitle: Takashima Ohisa Using Two Mirrors to Observe Her Coiffure
description: Ohisa, a celebrated Edo teahouse beauty, inspects the back of her coiffure with paired mirrors during the Asakusa autumn festival. Utamaro's precise hairlines and luminous mica-dusted ground typify his bust-portrait okubi-e of fashionable contemporary women.

title: The Artist's wife
description: The painter's wife seated in his studio, surrounded by the props of his trade. Oil on canvas, 40.6 by 32.9 cm, at the Clark Art Institute and dated about 1795 to 1799. Boilly returned often to domestic interiors built around a single figure.
credit: clarkart.edu

title: The Nude Maja
dateCreated: 1800 / between 1795 and 1800 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A reclining nude meets the viewer's gaze without mythological alibi, the first life-size unidealized female nude in Spanish painting. Commissioned by prime minister Manuel Godoy for a private cabinet, the picture later drew the Inquisition's attention to Goya himself.
credit: The Nude Maja . On-line gallery . Museo del Prado (2012). Archived from the original on 2010-01-03 . Retrieved on 2013-04-07 .

title: Woodcutters in Windsor Park
description: Labourers fell and trim oaks in a clearing of Windsor Great Park, the felled trunks arranged in diagonals across the foreground. West painted the scene in 1795 as part of the royal commission documenting estate work, pairing rural labour with the picturesque conventions of late eighteenth-century landscape.

title: Alexandra and Elena Pavlovna of Russia
description: A double portrait of Grand Duchesses Alexandra and Elena Pavlovna, daughters of Paul I, painted soon after Vigée Le Brun's arrival at the Russian court in exile from revolutionary France. Soft pastel-like flesh and silvery silks display the courtly grace that made her Marie Antoinette's preferred portraitist.

title: Countess Anna Ivanovna Tolstaya
description: Painted during Vigée Le Brun's émigré years in Saint Petersburg, the Russian countess wears a soft white gown and a velvet wrap. The artist's Russian sitters helped sustain her career through the Revolution and account for many of her finest late portraits.
credit: National Gallery of Canada

title: Fishermen at Sea
description: Turner's first oil exhibited at the Royal Academy, depicting a fishing boat tossed beneath a cold moon off the Needles, Isle of Wight. The contrast of silver lunar light and orange lantern glow announces a lifelong preoccupation with luminous opposition.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — UwG73jK8wqshlw Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=T01585&wwwflag=3&imagepos=2 )

title: George Washington
description: Edward Savage depicts Washington in a close three-quarter bust portrait, the sitter wearing a dark coat with lace cravat against a warm neutral ground. Painted around 1796, this intimate format draws on Savage's earlier life studies of the president and presents Washington in civilian dress rather than military uniform. The portrait is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: George Washington
description: Washington stands full-length in a black velvet suit, his right hand extended over a table covered with bound volumes and a quill, an upholstered chair and crimson drapery behind. Stuart painted the Lansdowne portrait in April 1796 for William Petty, Marquess of Lansdowne, the British statesman who had supported American independence.

title: George Washington
description: The unfinished bust of Washington against a brown ground shows the sixty-four-year-old president from the chest up, his hair powdered and his mouth set over the new wooden dentures. Stuart began the Athenaeum portrait on 12 April 1796 and kept the original at his easel as the master from which he produced more than seventy replicas.

title: Kim Hong-do
description: A scene from the Eight Views of Hwaseong attributed to Kim Hong-do, the fortress wall snaking along a ridge toward a hilltop command pavilion above the new royal city of Suwon. As court painter to King Jeongjo, Kim documented the fortress completed in 1796 in the ink-and-light-colour idiom of late Joseon topographic painting.

title: Martha Washington
description: Martha Washington, in old age, is shown in a dark bonnet and white collar, the bust barely emerging from the unpainted canvas in the unfinished manner Stuart retained for his template portraits. Painted by Gilbert Stuart in 1796 as a pendant to his Athenaeum portrait of the president, this canvas is jointly owned by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (accession 1980.2), and the National Portrait Gallery, Washington.

title: Newport Castle
description: The ruined towers of Newport Castle rise from the water's edge on the river Usk, with several sailing craft and a rowboat moored alongside the ancient stonework. Turner made this watercolour around 1796 from sketches taken during his 1795 South Wales tour, combining topographical accuracy with the atmospheric washes that mark his early career.

title: Boilly incroyable parade
description: An 'incroyable', one of the foppish young men of the post-Revolutionary Directory, shown in exaggerated dress with cravat and high collar. Oil on canvas in a private collection, painted in 1797. Boilly satirised the muscadin fashions then on display along the Parisian boulevards.

title: George Washington
description: Gilbert Stuart's 1797 portrait of George Washington shows the president seated nearly full-length, dressed in black, with a red curtain to the left, a stone column and naval battle scene to the right, and the American eagle on the chair back — characteristics of the presidential portrait type rather than Stuart's unfinished Athenaeum bust. The work was painted for William Constable of New York and is dated 1797.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic

title: Hairdresser
description: A hairdresser (kamiyui) carefully arranges a seated woman's coiffure in this print from Utamaro's series Twelve Types of Women's Handicraft (Fujin tewaza juniko), dating to around 1797–98. Both figures wear patterned grey kimono, and Utamaro's precise linework isolates the subtle gestures of the task against a plain ground. The work is held in the Art Gallery of South Australia (inv. 838G66).

title: Portrait of Princess Anna Alexandrovna Galitzin
description: Princess Anna Alexandrovna Galitzin, great-granddaughter of the Georgian monarch Vakhtang, is shown reclining on a green chaise longue in an orange-amber gown with a red feathered headdress and gold chains. Vigée Le Brun painted the portrait in 1797 during her Russian years, capturing the opulent informality fashionable in St Petersburg society at the close of the eighteenth century.

title: Buttermere Lake
description: A rainbow arcs over Buttermere following a Lake District shower, the slate fells doubled in the still water below. Turner exhibited the picture at the Royal Academy aged twenty-three, after a Cumberland sketching tour. It is one of his earliest essays in the sublime mountain weather effects that would define him.

title: Meeting of Artists in Isabey's Studio
description: Tableau de Louis-Léopold Boilly représentant des artistes influents sous le Directoire. Les identifications des personnes représentées en annotations d'image sont renseignées sur l'élément wikidata : https://wd-image-positions. toolforge.
credit: photo Shonagon 2025-02-12

title: Shipping by a Breakwater
description: A turbulent marine scene from Turner's early career: a crowded rowing boat with figures in colourful dress occupies the foreground, making toward a large vessel grounded or moored in rough seas beside a dark breakwater, with smaller sailing craft to the left. The agitated handling and composition owe a clear debt to the seventeenth-century Dutch marine tradition. Dated 1798 and part of the Turner Bequest at Tate.

title: 960px-Museo del Prado - Goya - Caprichos - No. 43 - El sueño de la razon produce monstruos
englishTitle: The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters (Caprichos No. 43)
description: An artist slumps over his desk as bats and owls swarm from the dark behind him, plate forty-three of Goya's Caprichos. The etching with aquatint, issued in Madrid in 1799, became the central emblem of the series' attack on Spanish superstition and unreason.

title: Harlech Castle
description: An early oil painting by J. M. W. Turner of Harlech Castle on its crag above the Welsh coast, seen across the estuary from Tygwyn Ferry in the fading light of a summer evening. Turner exhibited the picture at the Royal Academy in 1799, the year he was elected an Associate of the Academy, translating his watercolour studies of Welsh castles into the atmospheric oil manner of his early maturity. The painting is in the Yale Center for British Art.

title: Julie as Flora
description: The painter's daughter Julie posed as the Roman flower goddess, garlanded and seen against a soft pastoral ground. The mythological costume portrait belongs to the artist's exile years following the Revolution, when she worked across the European courts.
credit: www.metmuseum.org

provenance.collection: Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg, Florida, USA
provenance.location: Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg, Florida, USA

title: Maria Hamilton Beckford
description: Maria Hamilton Beckford sits in a blue gown, a guitar and an open book of music in her lap, with a classical column, a floral arrangement, and a country house in a landscaped park visible behind her. Benjamin West painted the portrait in 1799 and it is now in the collection of the National Gallery of Art, Washington. The guitar and open score identify the sitter as an accomplished musician.

title: Portrait de madame de Verninac by David Louvre RF1942-16 n2
description: Henriette de Verninac, sister of Eugène Delacroix, is shown full-length, seated on a neoclassical chair in an Empire dress of white muslin with a gold-olive shawl, against a neutral grey ground. Jacques-Louis David painted this portrait in 1799; the Louvre acquired it in 1942 (RF 1942-16).

title: The Intervention of the Sabine Women
description: Hersilia throws herself between the Roman king Romulus and her Sabine father Tatius, infants crawling at her feet as the two armies pause on the field. David painted the canvas in 1799 during and after his post-Thermidor imprisonment, intending the subject of reconciliation as a plea for an end to French factional bloodshed.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: The Surrender of the Dutch Admiral de Winter to Admiral Duncan at the Battle of Camperdown
description: Admiral Duncan receives the sword of the defeated Vice-Admiral de Winter on the quarterdeck of HMS Venerable after the British victory off Camperdown on 11 October 1797. Copley finished the canvas in 1799 for the City of London, now in the National Galleries of Scotland (NG 2661).

title: John Adams
description: John Adams, in a black coat and powdered hair, faces the viewer in a half-length pose against a plain ground. Stuart began the portrait around 1800, when Adams was the sitting second president, and finished it about 1815 for the former president's son John Quincy.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Kim Hong-do
englishTitle: Drunken Monk under a Pine Tree (Songhachwisaengdo)
description: A solitary figure sits slumped beneath a towering gnarled pine, rendered in fluid ink brushwork on a pale ground. Kim Hong-do's composition, titled 'Drunken Monk under a Pine Tree' and dating to around 1800, merges genre humour with the literati ideal of the carefree sage. Calligraphic inscriptions and red seals occupy the upper right of the composition.
credit: http://img219.imageshack.us/img219/1251/drunkenxx5.jpg (forums.soompi.com)

title: Napoleon Crossing the Alps
description: Bonaparte, wrapped in a billowing orange cloak, reins in a rearing piebald horse on the slopes of the Great St Bernard Pass, the names of Hannibal and Karolus Magnus carved into the rock at his feet. David painted this Neoclassical equestrian portrait in 1800, one of five autograph versions produced over the following decade. The Malmaison version is among the best-known, and records the idealized image of command Napoleon wished to project after his Marengo campaign.

title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
description: Oedipus pauses on a rocky ledge to answer the riddle of the Sphinx, his polished nude profile set against deep shadow. Painted in Rome as part of Ingres's Prix de Rome obligations, it distils his Neoclassical doctrine of pure contour and idealised anatomy.

title: Portrait of Colonel Fitch and his Sisters
description: John Singleton Copley depicts Colonel William Fitch in scarlet army uniform beside his rearing chestnut charger, flanked by his two sisters — one in neoclassical white with a veil, the other in dark mourning dress. Painted between 1800 and 1801 in London, the group portrait is now at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art; National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Portrait of George Spencer
description: George Spencer, 2nd Earl Spencer, faces the viewer in a brown coat and white stock, his powdered hair above the blue sash and breast star of the Order of the Garter. Copley painted the portrait around 1800, while Spencer served as First Lord of the Admiralty under William Pitt, overseeing the Royal Navy through Camperdown and the Nile.

title: Portrait of Madame Récamier
description: Juliette Récamier reclines barefoot on a Directoire-style chaise longue in a white chemise dress, her dark curls lightly bound, a tall floor candelabrum standing at the head of the couch. David left the canvas unfinished in 1800 following a dispute with the sitter, and the unpainted ground together with the severe antique furniture have come to embody the austerity of the emerging Empire taste.
credit: [1] , specifically [2]

title: Reiter von Riesenschlange überfallen
englishTitle: Horseman Attacked by a Giant Snake
description: A figure is overwhelmed and dragged down by an enormous serpent in a stormy outdoor setting, the attacker's coils filling the composition in a characteristic Fuselian display of overwhelming animal force. The work on paper, dating to circa 1800, draws on Mannerist precedents to push human anatomy into expressive distortion, and is titled 'Horseman Attacked by a Giant Snake' in the record.

title: Snow Scene
description: Three figures in richly patterned kimonos dance or move through a snow-covered landscape beneath flowering plum branches, their overlapping forms conveying animated motion. The woodblock print is a product of the Utagawa school and carries the seal of Kunisada (Utagawa Toyokuni III), held today in the Brooklyn Museum. The densely printed textile patterns and speckled snow ground demonstrate the expanded colour range available to nineteenth-century Edo publishers.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum ; Photo: Brooklyn Museum, X632.2_IMLS_PS3.jpg

title: Academic study of a male torso
description: A youthful académie made in Jacques-Louis David's studio, drawn from a posed model with painstaking anatomical observation. Such exercises were the bedrock of Ingres's Neoclassical training and prefigure the sculptural torsos in his later history paintings.
credit: pl.pinterest.com

title: Kim Hong-do
englishTitle: Samgongbulhwando (Not to Be Exchanged for the Three Highest Offices)
description: A long horizontal handscroll in ink and colour on silk, Samgongbulhwando contrasts the freedom of nature with the burdens of office through scenes of recluses and scholars in mountain retreats. Kim Hong-do painted the scroll in 1801, measuring 133.7 by 418.4 cm and now held by the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art in Seoul.

title: Milkmaids in St. James's Park
description: Milkmaids sell pails of fresh milk to passers-by in the open ground of St James's Park, the towers of Westminster Abbey rising in the haze beyond. West painted the London genre scene in 1801, now at the Yale Center for British Art, joining royal pastoral subjects with a documentary view of city trade.

title: Study of a Male Nude
description: An academic male nude executed during Ingres's training under David, when he was competing for the Prix de Rome. The figure's smooth modelling and elongated proportions already announce the linear classicism that would define his career.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"i/ingres/00ingres"

title: 'Arethusa' by Benjamin West
description: A nude nymph turns and looks back over her shoulder in a darkened woodland setting, red and white drapery falling around her as she appears to flee. The work, painted in 1802 and now at the High Museum of Art in Atlanta, depicts Arethusa from Ovid's Metamorphoses in the moment before her transformation. Benjamin West was then serving as President of the Royal Academy.

title: Agapanthus Umbellatus
description: Agapanthus umbellatus, its tuberous root throwing up a leafless stalk topped by an umbel of fifteen to twenty hyacinth-blue funnel-shaped blooms. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802); the plate dissections enlarge the stamens, ovary and style.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Albuca Minor
description: Albuca minor, an Albuca recognised by its yellowish pendent flowers set in a loose spike on a stalk of four to five decimetres. Three of its six stamens are sterile, a trait of the genus; the dissection figures enlarge the flower's parts below.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Striatum
description: Allium striatum, its channelled green leaves and a scape bearing an umbel of seven to ten white flowers grooved along each lobe. The dissection figures at the foot show the orange anthers and the awl-shaped filaments; the plate opens the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Alstrœmeria Ligtu
description: Alstroemeria ligtu, set apart by its fine foliage and an irregular flower mottled in pink and white. From a fascicle of tuberous roots rise simple angular stems ending in two or three flowers on naked stalks. The enlarged ovary and petal figures below follow the botanical convention of the period.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Atamasco
description: Amaryllis atamasco, the Virginia amaryllis, a single regular bloom on a slender scape rising from a rounded brown bulb, with narrow leaves spread along the ground. The text contrasts the one-flowered species with the irregular multi-flowered amaryllis. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Equestris
description: Amaryllis equestris, its bright red funnel flowers carried two to a scape, the curve of stalk, ovary and tube together suggesting an English saddle that gives the plant its name. The throat is bearded, the segments wavy with three broader outer lobes. Plate 32 belongs to the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Formosissima
description: Amaryllis formosissima, the Jacobean lily, its large nodding scarlet flower split so deeply that the three upreared and three drooping segments suggest two lips. The hollow reddish scape rises beside oblong two-ranked leaves. Plate 5 opened the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Reginæ
description: Amaryllis reginae, the Mexican lily, its very large bright red flowers borne two to four on a scape shorter than the two-ranked leaves. The bell-shaped corolla has a bearded throat, the outer segments tipped with a green callus. Plate 9 belongs to the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Sarniensis
description: Amaryllis sarniensis, the Guernsey lily, its umbel of seven to ten vivid red flowers on a naked cylindrical scape, the segments spreading and curled back. Reddish membranous bracts wrap the base of the umbel. Despite the island name, the text notes the plant's structure and colour point to an origin outside Europe.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Vittata
description: Amaryllis vittata, its tall hollow scape bearing four funnel-shaped flowers, each white segment marked with two longitudinal purple-red bands and crisped at the edges. The plate appeared in the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802), stipple-engraved and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Anthericum Milleflorum
description: Anthericum milleflorum, named for its immense number of flowers borne in small clusters along slender spreading panicle branches, the white blooms tinged with lilac. Issued in the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802), the plate was stipple-engraved and coloured by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Antholyza Cunonia
description: Antholyza cunonia, its slender stem from a small bulb bearing a two-ranked spike of poppy-red flowers whose two-lipped corolla resembles a pea blossom. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802), with the flower's parts enlarged in dissection below.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Astrœmeria Pelegrina
description: Alstroemeria pelegrina, the Pelegrina of Peru, its stems carrying three spreading flowers of pale purple marked with darker spots on the inner surface. The leaves are narrow, lance-shaped, and resupinate, twisted so the lower surface faces upward. Plate 46 belongs to the first volume of Les Liliacées (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Crinum Erubescens
description: Crinum erubescens, named for the purple-red wash across the outer surface of its fragrant white flowers, four to seven borne on a flattened stalk above lance-shaped leaves. The plate opened the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802), set in the amaryllis family of the Jussieu line.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Cypripedium Calceolus
description: Cypripedium calceolus, the lady's slipper orchid, shown here bearing two flowers on a leafy stem, each with four spreading maroon outer divisions surrounding an inflated yellow pouch. Redouté drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacées (1802), and the accompanying text notes it as a European orchid that resists cultivation.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Cypripedium Flavescens
description: Cypripedium flavescens, close to the alpine slipper orchid but with an entirely pale-yellow flower, the upper division spotted with small red points and finely veined. The supplied text gives it as native to North America; the plate appears in the first volume (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Daisia Iridifolia
description: Diasia iridifolia, a tuberous bulb the size of a hazelnut raising a slender branched stem with flattened iris-like leaves and scattered sessile flowers. The yellowish corolla, each segment marked with a purple line, divides into six deep lobes; the plate opened the first volume (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Dianella Ensifolia
description: Dianella ensifolia, its iris-like striate leaves rising from fibrous roots to a leafless scape bearing a loose panicle of small flowers with six spreading petals and yellow-tipped stamens. The plate opened the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802); the dissection figures follow period convention.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ferraria Undulata
description: Ferraria undulata growing from a rounded tuber like a cyclamen's, with sword-shaped leaves and bizarre brown-purple flowers whose six spreading segments have markedly crisped, undulate margins. An iris-family plant, it opened the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Fishermen Upon a Lee-Shore in Squally Weather
description: Fishermen struggle to bring a sailing vessel ashore as breaking surf and squall lines press against a steep coast. An early Royal Academy exhibit, the canvas sets Turner's lifelong concern with mariners' jeopardy in a darker, more Dutch-inflected idiom.

title: Fritillaria Latifolia
description: Fritillaria latifolia, a close relative of the snake's-head fritillary with broader, flatter leaves clustered toward the upper stem and a solitary nodding flower whose outer surface is yellowish, the inner face purple with greenish chequering. The plate, in the first volume (1802), sets out the leaf and marking differences that separate this species from F. meleagris, with which it had long been confused.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Galaxia Ixiæflora
description: Galaxia ixiaeflora, an iris-family plant resembling an Ixia but set apart by stamens fused into a cylindrical column. Its short spike carries two to five flowers tinted cinnamon at the base and lilac to purple above. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Cuspidatus
description: Gladiolus cuspidatus, notable for its large flesh-coloured corolla, undulate limb, and blood-red ring-shaped marks on the three lower segments. The botanist A.P. de Candolle and others supplied the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plates. This sheet opens the first volume of the series (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Inclinatus
description: Gladiolus inclinatus, recognised by its hairy leaves and a scape that bends to one side, here toward the light, bearing a spike of long-tubed flowers. The dissection figures at the foot of the sheet enlarge the flower's sexual parts, a botanical convention of the period.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Lineatus
description: Gladiolus lineatus, its pale almost transparent flowers veined with dark anastomosing lines, seven or eight to a simple spike above the stem. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine; many of the work's specimens came from the gardens at Malmaison. This sheet is from the first volume (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Merianus
description: Gladiolus merianus, standing between the antholyzas and the true gladioli, with cherry-red tubular flowers slightly recurved and alternate sword-shaped leaves. The plate opens the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802); the corolla's base holds a sweet liquid noted in the text.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Tristis
description: Gladiolus tristis is recognised by its rush-like leaves channelled with three to five longitudinal furrows, the stem bearing usually two pale-yellow flowers tinged brown on the exterior. A detail of the bottle-shaped tuber is shown alongside the main plant. From the first volume of Les Liliacées (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Globba Nutans
description: Globba nutans, a tall reed-like stem with long oblong leaves and a nodding raceme that lifts as the buds, rose-and-white and varnished in sheen, open. It appeared in the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802), the stipple engraving coloured from a single plate and hand-finished.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Grenoble Seen from the River Drac with Mont Blanc in the Distance
description: Grenoble lies between the Drac and the distant snowfields of Mont Blanc, drawn during Turner's first Continental tour after the Peace of Amiens reopened France. The 1802 Alpine campaign permanently reshaped his sense of geological scale. The picture's stretched horizontal format prefigures his later panoramic mountain views.

title: Hæmanthus Coccineus
description: Haemanthus coccineus, two broad tongue-shaped leaves spread on the ground beside a spotted scape opening into a scarlet involucre that holds a tight umbel of red flowers. The name means blood-flower; the plate appeared in the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Helonias Bullata
description: Helonias bullata, a hollow stem rising above orchid-like basal leaves to a dense oblong spike of small, fragrant pink flowers on short pedicels. The plate places it among the rushes (Joncs) in Jussieu's order; it appeared in the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Hemerocallis Flava
description: Hemerocallis flava, the common yellow daylily, with keeled linear leaves and a branched scape bearing fragrant funnel-shaped flowers in a loose corymb. Its straight, non-anastomosing veins distinguish it from the tawny species; the plate appeared in the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Hemerocallis Fulva
description: Hemerocallis fulva, the tawny daylily, larger in every part than the yellow species, its broad keeled leaves and funnel-shaped flowers in a loose corymb running fawn to reddish. The plate appeared in the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802), the stipple engraving printed in colour and hand-finished.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Hemerocallis Japonica
description: Hemerocallis japonica, set apart by its broad heart-shaped leaves narrowed to channelled petioles and a loose spike of large white bell-shaped flowers on thick pale pedicels. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802), printed in colour and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Hyacinthus Amethystinus
description: Hyacinthus amethystinus, a small bulb sending up linear channelled leaves and a slender scape with five or six tubular blue flowers on short pedicels. It appeared in the first volume of Les Liliacées (1802), drawn by Pierre-Joseph Redouté.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Florentina
description: Iris florentina, the white-flowered Florentine iris, its glaucous sword-shaped leaves shorter than the scape and its root strongly scented when dried. The accompanying text distinguishes it from the violet German iris, which it closely resembles in form and size.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Sisyrinchium
description: Plate 29 shows Iris sisyrinchium, named for its unusual root of two solid bulbs set one above the other, with a cylindrical stem and two or three flowers opening in succession. The French text notes it grows wild across southern Europe; Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees in 1802.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Suziana
description: Plate 18 shows Iris suziana, distinguished by its single very large flower mottled white and blackish-purple, the falls reflexed and bearded with violet hairs at the base. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine, and many specimens for the work came from the gardens at Malmaison. From the first volume of Les Liliacees, 1802.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Tuberosa
description: Plate 48 shows Iris tuberosa, named for a root of two or three thick cylindrical tubers, with four-angled grooved leaves and a single dull-green flower whose outer segments are tipped deep purple. Tournefort once made it the type of a separate genus; Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees in 1802.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Filiformis
description: Ixia filiformis shows a dense crimson spike at the top of a fine, slender scape twice the length of its sword-shaped leaves. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802). The flowers turn mostly to one side in a nodding, tightly packed head.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Longiflora
description: Ixia longiflora bears oblong segments spread above a slender cylindrical tube the length of a finger, set in a loose spike along the stem. The French text notes several varieties, one white flushed with rose and banded yellow on the lower divisions. The work belongs to the iris family in Triandria monogynia.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Kœmpferia Longa
description: Kaempferia longa, whose flower pushes from the ground in a distinct spathe before or with the rolled, oblong leaves marked by a reddish central blotch. De Candolle's text noted specimens observed at Malmaison and in the garden of Cels. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Lachenalia Lanceæfolia
description: Lachenalia lanceaefolia, set apart by an outsized whitish bulb and a rosette of thick ovate-lanceolate leaves, the young foliage spotted green. Its small flowers crowd two flexed flowering stalks, half-pendent and reddening as they open. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Lachenalia Pallida
description: Lachenalia pallida, named for its pale flowers, with two long narrow channelled leaves and a short raceme on a stalk sometimes dotted red. The bell-shaped flowers carry six petals in two ranks, the upper sterile ones forming a tuft of purple bracts. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Lachenalia Pendula
description: Lachenalia pendula, its cylindrical poppy-red flowers tipped brown and over four centimetres long, hanging in a loose raceme that stands erect before flowering and droops at pollination. The species belongs to the Asphodel family in the Jussieu classification printed on the sheet.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Lachenalia Tricolor
description: Lachenalia tricolor is easily identified by the brown spots flecking its leaves and stalk, and by a loose raceme of pendent flowers borne on orange pedicels. The three outer segments are orange, while the three longer inner ones are yellowish at the base and purple-red toward the tip. Redouté drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacées (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Lilium Pomponium
description: Lilium pomponium, its scarlet flowers in a terminal cluster, nodding earthward with petals coiled fully back, above a leafy stalk whose lower leaves are whorled. Redoute drew it as plate 7 of the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802), a stipple engraving printed in colour and hand-finished.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Limodorum Tankerwillæ
description: Limodorum tankerwillae, an orchid whose large parts let de Candolle's text examine the family's structure in detail, with five or six veratrum-like leaves and a tall raceme of two to thirteen flowers. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Maranta Arundinacea
description: Maranta arundinacea, the arrowroot, with reed-like jointed stems, ovate-pointed leaves sheathing at the base, and single white flowers borne on short forked pedicels. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from one plate and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Merendera Bulbocodium
description: Merendera bulbocodium, long confused with the spring meadow saffron it resembles, distinguished by its three basally united ovaries each topped by a separate style. Per the supplied text it carries the corolla of Bulbocodium, the pistil of Colchicum, and the anther of saffron.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Methonica Superba
description: Methonica superba, the glory lily, its leaves tipped with curling tendrils and flame-coloured flowers whose wavy petals rise back with the base yellow marked red. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802); the slender stem reaches some two metres.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Montbretia Securigera
description: Montbretia securigera, an iris-family plant from two small white bulbs, its sword-shaped basal leaves and a simple spike of three to five orange-yellow funnel flowers, the lower lobes bearing a pale auricle within a reddish blotch. The plate appeared in the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Morœa Iridioides
description: Moraea iridioides, near to the irises for its large petal-like stigmas, its fan of flat sword-shaped leaves and stalked flowers mingling white, yellow, and blue. It sits among the Moraeas because the six corolla segments spread nearly equal, the outer trio yellow-spotted at the base.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Morœa Vaginata
description: Moraea vaginata, an iris-family plant whose flower stalk stays sheathed for its whole length inside an upper leaf, so the blooms seem to spring from the side of a flattened stem. Its fan of compressed dark-green basal leaves reaches six or seven decimetres.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Narcissus Bulbocodium
description: Narcissus bulbocodium, the hoop-petticoat daffodil, a single yellow flower whose funnel-shaped nectary runs longer than the six narrow corolla segments, set above slender linear leaves. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand, the method Redoute used across the eight folio volumes of Les Liliacees.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Narcissus Tazetta
description: Narcissus tazetta, the bunch-flowered daffodil, two or three scapes from one bulb each carrying three to eight flowers above broad green leaves, with a cylindrical tube and six spreading segments around a yellow cup. The text records white and yellow-cupped variants beside the form shown; this plate opened the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Pancratium Maritimum
description: Pancratium maritimum, the sea daffodil, its glaucous strap-like leaves in two ranks below a scape of fragrant white flowers, the limb cut into six pointed segments above a funnel-shaped nectary. The pistil and three-angled ovary appear in figures at the foot. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ships bearing up for Anchorage
description: A fleet of sailing vessels bears up for anchorage in squally open water, their hulls and rigging silhouetted against a turbulent, cloud-laden sky. Turner's treatment recalls the seventeenth-century Dutch marine tradition of Willem van de Velde while asserting a broader atmospheric ambition. Exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1802, the work is known as 'The Egremont Seapiece' and is held by the National Trust at Petworth House.

title: Sisyrinchium Convolutum
description: Plate 47 shows Sisyrinchium convolutum, with sword-like glaucous leaves and a wheel-shaped yellow flower deeply cut into six segments that roll up on themselves after blooming. It appeared in the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802), classed by Jussieu among the Iridaceae.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: The Tenth Plague of Egypt
description: Storm and divine wrath sweep over a darkened Egyptian city as the firstborn die. An early bid for the prestige of Old Master history painting, the picture leans openly on Poussin's biblical compositions.

title: Tigridia Pavonia
description: Tigridia pavonia, its single bell-shaped flower opening to six petals spotted crimson and flame at the centre, set above sword-shaped pleated leaves. The plate belongs to the iris family and led off the very first volume of Les Liliacees (1802), printed in colour and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Tulipa Celsiana
description: Tulipa celsiana, a small wild-type tulip with narrow channelled leaves and a solitary upright yellow flower, faintly scented and smaller than the common species. The plate belongs to the true lilies of Jussieu; Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Tulipa Clusiana
description: Tulipa clusiana, its solitary white bell-flower marked with bright red-violet on the outer face of the three larger segments, appearing wholly violet when closed. The plate belongs to the true lilies and appeared in Volume 1 of Les Liliacees (1802), printed in colour and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Tummel Bridge
description: Turner depicted the stone arch of Tummel Bridge spanning a turbulent Highland river, with dramatic storm clouds gathering over the mountains behind, painted between 1802 and 1803 following his Scottish tour. Cottages and cattle animate the middle ground beneath a brooding, weather-laden sky. The work is held at the Yale Center for British Art.

title: Vieusseuxia Glaucopis
description: Vieusseuxia glaucopis, its flower of six divisions, the three outer white with a fine blue blotch at the base, the inner three narrow and tipped with three points. The stamen filaments unite in a column around the style, shown enlarged below. Redoute drew this iris-family plant for the first volume of Les Liliacees (1802).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Bonneville
description: An Alpine view from Turner's first Continental tour following the Peace of Amiens, recording the town of Bonneville against the Mont Blanc range. The classical compositional structure recalls Claude Lorrain, whom Turner studied closely as a young Royal Academician.

title: Calais Pier
description: Embarking passengers and fishwives crowd the French pier as a squall builds beyond the harbour mouth. Turner had himself crossed to Calais in rough weather in 1802, and he exhibited this large canvas to challenge the marine paintings of his French contemporaries.

title: Paris art deco boilly houdon
description: The sculptor Jean-Antoine Houdon at work in his studio, modelling a clay bust of the astronomer Pierre-Simon Laplace. Oil on canvas, about 1803, in the Musée des Arts décoratifs, Paris. Finished casts and tools fill the cluttered workshop behind the seated sculptor.
credit: http://www.the-athenaeum.org/art/detail.php?ID=79614 musée des Arts décoratifs de Paris.

title: The Pass of Saint Gotthard
description: A vertiginous Alpine gorge on the St Gotthard road, with a narrow stone path clinging to the cliff face and cloud billowing through the chasm below. Turner painted the scene following his first Continental tour after the Peace of Amiens reopened Europe in 1802, completing the oil between 1803 and 1804. The composition, in which sheer scale becomes the subject, is now held by Birmingham Museums Trust.

title: Albuca Cornuta
description: Albuca cornuta, its bulb sending up broad glaucous leaves and a bare stalk carrying a raceme of green-and-white flowers. The style here ends in three projecting horns, the feature that names the species. Drawn for the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Albuca Major
description: Albuca major, its bulb producing eight to ten upright leaves striped green and white, with a long raceme of nodding yellowish six-parted flowers on a stalk reaching nearly a metre. A botanist supplied the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plate.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Aletris Fragrans
description: Aletris fragrans, a shrub two to four metres tall with a ringed stem and dark-green lance-shaped leaves, bearing an upright panicle of fragrant whitish flowers tinged violet. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine, many of whose specimens were grown at Malmaison.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Carolinianum
description: Allium carolinianum, an oblong brown-tunicked bulb throwing up flat dark-green leaves and a globular umbel of twenty-five to thirty fragrant white flowers flushed rose. The plate enlarges the apricot-yellow anthers and the ovary below, from the second volume (1804).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Flavum
description: Allium flavum, the yellow garlic, recognised at once by its loose pendent yellow flowers and the two long leaf-like valves of its spathe. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand, the method Redoute used throughout the eight folio volumes.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Fragrans
description: Allium fragrans, its sweetly scented flowers pink in bud then white with rose lines, set in an upright umbel above channelled basal leaves. The dissection figures below show the six stamens gathered into a cylinder around the pistil, a botanical convention of the day.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Moly
description: Allium moly, the golden garlic, with its broad flat leaves and a loose umbel of bright yellow star-shaped flowers. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand, the technique Redoute used across the eight folio volumes of Les Liliacees.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Moschatum
description: Allium moschatum, the musk garlic, its flat umbel of about twenty white flowers veined brown-purple and carrying a fine scent. Redoute drew it for the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804); the enlarged pistil figure shows the ovary marked with purple and green spots.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Nigrum
description: Allium nigrum, largest of the garlics shown, its tall solid scape ending in a broad flat umbel of some fifty yellowish-white flowers. The dark green ovary turns almost black late in flowering, the trait that gives the species its name; drawn for the second volume (1804).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Obtusiflorum
description: Allium obtusiflorum, its two unequal scapes each carrying a tight globular umbel of fifteen to twenty-five white flowers tinged rose and green-veined. Redoute drew it for the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804); the dissection figures show the blunt, almost truncate perianth segments.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Scorzoner­æfolium
description: Allium scorzoneraefolium, with leaves like those of scorzonera and a loose umbel of four to six spreading yellow flowers, small reddish bulbils set among them. The plate belongs to the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804); the blooms resemble those of Allium moly.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Tataricum
description: Allium tataricum, its cylindrical leafy stalk rising about a metre to a flat umbel of white flowers veined in violet-purple. The dissection figures at the foot of the sheet enlarge the six purple-tipped stamens and the rounded ovary. Plate 98 appeared in the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Aurea
description: Amaryllis aurea, its golden-yellow flowers crisped at the margins and gathered into an umbel of five to eight blooms on a stout compressed scape. The strap leaves are glaucous beneath, the corolla split into six narrow wavy segments. Plate 61 belongs to the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Broussonetii
description: Amaryllis broussonetii, distinguished by a compressed scape and a long-tubed flower borne only two to a spathe, the white segments crossed lengthwise by a purple band. The pleated leaves are bright green, the floral tube greenish below and purplish toward the top. Plate 62 appeared in the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Undulata
description: Amaryllis undulata, an ovoid bulb sending up narrow basal leaves and a smooth scape carrying an umbel of nine or ten small rose-pink flowers, their six narrow lobes wavy at the margins. Redouté drew it for Les Liliacées (1804); the dissection details at lower left show the pistil and the bulbils that develop in place of seeds, following standard botanical illustration convention.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Antholyza Æthiopica
description: Antholyza aethiopica, its leafy stem rising from a tuberous root to a spike of bright red flowers set spirally along the axis, each with a long curved tube twisted at the base. The classification line places it among the Iridaceae; Redoute drew it for the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Boats Carrying Out Anchors to the Dutch Men of War
Canna Flaccida
description: Canna flaccida, its pale lance-shaped leaves sheathing an upright herbaceous stem topped by one to three large soft yellow flowers in a short spike. The text distinguishes it from the glaucous canna by its blooms, twice as large and fewer in number. Redoute drew it for the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Commelina Tuberosa
description: Commelina tuberosa, the tuber dayflower, its tubercled root sending up herbaceous stems banded with hairs and bearing wavy-margined lance-shaped leaves. Four to six flowers sit in a terminal umbel hidden in a boat-shaped spathe, each bloom opening for only a few hours. Redoute drew it for the second volume of Les Liliacees (1804).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Convalaria Japonica
description: Ophiopogon japonicus, shown here as Convallaria japonica, a low tufted plant of grassy linear leaves with a short raceme of small white flowers half-hidden among them. The text places it near the asparagus family; the six stamens and tiny ovary are enlarged in the figures below.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Crocus Minimus
