description: Tulipa oculus-solis, its large solitary flower of six deep-red petals each bearing a prominent blackish basal blotch edged by a pale zone — the eye-of-the-sun marking that gives the species its name. The outer three petals taper to a distinct point, a feature the accompanying text uses to distinguish it from Tulipa gesneriana. Redouté drew it for the fourth volume of Les Liliacées (1807).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Uvularia Perfoliata
description: Uvularia perfoliata, the perfoliate bellwort, its pale drooping flowers hung from a slender stem that pierces the clasping leaves. Despite the title Les Liliacees, the work ranges across many monocot families, as the Jussieu classification line on each plate shows. Redoute drew it for the fourth volume (1807).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Veltheimia Abyssinica
description: Veltheimia abyssinica, drawn for the fourth volume of Les Liliacees (1807), a bulbous plant of the asphodel family with a scape of tubular nodding flowers above strap-shaped leaves. The plates were printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Veltheimia Capensis
description: Veltheimia capensis, the Cape veltheimia, its tubular pink-spotted flowers nodding in a dense ovoid spike above a fan of wavy-edged glaucous leaves. The botanical text places it in the asphodel family. Redoute drew it for the fourth volume of Les Liliacees (1807).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Vue du lac de Challes et du Mont Blanc
description: A Savoyard panorama of Lake Challes with Mont Blanc rising in the distance, unusual within the painter's output for being a pure landscape rather than a portrait. The view records her travels through the Alps during her long emigration from revolutionary France.
credit: Minneapolis Institute of Art, online collection

title: Cupid and Psyche
description: Cupid enfolds the conscious Psyche in his winged embrace, both figures gazing at one another against an open, cloud-filled sky, while putti attend in the middle distance. West painted the canvas in 1808, during his presidency of the Royal Academy, drawing on the Apuleius myth for one of his late mythological commissions. The work is now in the collection of Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art.
credit: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art

title: Gerhard von Kügelgen portrait of Friedrich
description: A bust-length portrait of the Romantic landscapist Caspar David Friedrich, showing him with reddish-blonde curly hair, a short beard, and an open coat with a green cravat against a loosely sketched landscape ground. Painted in 1808 by his contemporary Gerhard von Kügelgen, the work is housed in the Hamburger Kunsthalle and represents the canonical early image of Friedrich at the outset of his mature career.

title: Goethe Kügelgen
englishTitle: Portrait of Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
description: A three-quarter portrait of Goethe, painted by Gerhard von Kügelgen in 1808–1809, showing the poet in a dark coat with a crimson sash and an order on his chest against a grey-blue atmospheric ground. The smooth, restrained handling is characteristic of Kügelgen's Neoclassical manner, and this is among the best-known likenesses of the poet from his later years.

title: La Grande baigneuse
description: A seated nude seen from behind, her head wrapped in a patterned red-and-white turban, sits at the edge of a draped bath. Ingres painted this canvas in Rome in 1808 as part of his required submissions to the Académie, and its flawlessly modelled back — elevated to the surface as pure contour — became a touchstone for his later Turkish bath subjects. The work is now in the Louvre (RF 259).
credit: r Gallerix.ru

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Léopold Boilly Les conscrits de 1807 défilant devant la porte Saint-Denis
description: Young conscripts of the 1807 class marching past the Porte Saint-Denis as families crowd to bid them farewell. Oil on canvas, 84.5 by 138 cm, in the Musée Carnavalet, Paris, since 1888 and first shown at the Salon of 1808. The triumphal arch anchors the deep boulevard view behind the column of recruits.

title: Mrs. James Swan
description: Hepzibah Clarke Swan, wife of the speculator James Swan, sits in a high-waisted dress with a sheer wrap around her shoulders. Stuart painted her in Boston in 1808; the portrait, accession 27.539 at the Museum of Fine Arts, joined the museum from the sitter's descendants over a century later.

title: Purfleet and the Essex Shore as seen from Long Reach
description: Several vessels navigate a choppy reach of the Thames at Purfleet: a three-masted ship at left, sailing barges at centre, a hoy to the right, and a small rowboat with figures in the foreground. Painted in 1808, Turner's oil on canvas captures the heavy drama of an approaching storm set against patches of pale breaking sky, the flat Essex shore just visible in the distance.

title: Sheerness as seen from the Nore
description: A large warship stands silhouetted against a glowing, haze-wrapped sun on the left, while a smaller vessel with an ochre sail and a crowded rowboat labour through the rough swell in the foreground, with the Kent shore and Sheerness faintly visible to the right. Painted in 1808, the canvas was exhibited at Turner's own gallery and is now held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.

title: The Colossus
dateCreated: after 1808 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A naked giant rises behind a mountain ridge as a panicked crowd and herds flee across the plain below. Long attributed to Goya and tied to the Peninsular War, the picture stages collective terror with the bituminous darkness of his late, troubled imagination.

title: The Confluence of the Thames and Medway
description: Estuary shipping gathers where Thames and Medway meet, painted in the tradition of seventeenth-century Dutch sea pieces. Heavy cloud and a low horizon underline Turner's command of English coastal weather.

title: The Monk by the Sea
description: A solitary figure stands on a pale dune before an immense, near-empty expanse of sea and sky. Friedrich strips the composition to horizontal bands, dwarfing the human silhouette to evoke spiritual confrontation with the infinite — a foundational image of German Romantic landscape.

title: The painter and writer Friedrich August von Klinkowström
description: A portrait of the painter and writer Friedrich August von Klinkowström, Runge's close friend and a fellow figure in early German Romantic circles. The sitter is shown with a Nazarene-like clarity of contour and a steady, contemplative gaze.

title: The Siege of Cozel
description: A group of mounted officers and attendant cavalry survey a distant city from a high ridge in this 1808 painting by Wilhelm von Kobell. The work depicts the 1807 siege of Cosel in Silesia, recording the Bavarian repulse of a Prussian sortie during the Third Coalition War; the city lies in the misty valley below, framed by bare winter trees at right.

title: Alisma Damasonium
description: Alisma damasonium, the star fruit, its long-stalked ovate leaves below whorls of pale lilac flowers whose six ovaries ripen into a star of capsules. The text places it in the water-plantain family (Alismacées); enlarged floral figures appear at the foot of the sheet.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Alisma Natans
description: Alisma natans, a floating water-plantain with slender creeping stems and elliptical leaves resting at the surface, the small solitary flowers opening on long stalks and appearing white or very pale flesh-coloured. Drawn for the fifth volume of Les Liliacées, issued in 1809.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Alisma Ranunculoïdes
description: Alisma ranunculoides, its lance-shaped basal leaves below one or two umbels of lilac flowers with yellow claws, the many ovaries gathered into a bristly spherical head. The text places it in the water-plantain family (Alismacées), from the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Album
description: Allium album, a small violet bulb producing a few flat green leaves and a stalk topped by a flattened umbel of large milk-white flowers. The plate shows the three-angled ovary and capsule below, each cell holding two black seeds. From the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Angulosum
description: Allium angulosum, an onion springing from a creeping woody rootstock, its glaucous channelled leaves often spiralled at the tip and its lilac flowers gathered in a half-spherical umbel. Drawn for the fifth volume of Les Liliacees, issued in 1809.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Bisulcum
description: Allium bisulcum, an onion named for its half-cylindrical leaves grooved on both faces, bearing a full spherical umbel of pale-violet bell-shaped flowers. A botanist supplied the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plate in Les Liliacees.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Lusitanicum
description: Allium lusitanicum, the Portuguese garlic, with its fan of slender two-ranked leaves and a hemispherical umbel of some forty deep-lilac bell-shaped flowers. The plate appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809); the dissection figures show the violet anthers holding pale blue pollen.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Pallens
description: Allium pallens, its spherical umbel of numerous whitish flowers forming small bell-like cups, the brown-veined segments pressed together. The plate belongs to the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809), the long-pointed spathe valves drawn well beyond the umbel's width.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Paniculatum
description: Allium paniculatum, its slender stem ending in a loose terminal umbel of violet-red flowers, the outer pedicels recurved and pendent. The leaves are rolled into a channel with three rough toothed ribs; Redoute drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Victorialis
description: Allium victorialis, its rootstock wrapped in a netted sheath of dark fibres, sending up a slender scape to a tight spherical umbel of greenish-white flowers. The two or three broad elliptic leaves sheathe the stem at the base. Plate 265 belongs to the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Curvifolia
description: Amaryllis curvifolia, its scarlet umbel of about fifteen flowers on a scape rising five or six decimetres above a fascicle of sickle-curved glaucous leaves. The leaves open at the same time as the bloom and stay shorter than the scape. Redoute drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Montana
description: Amaryllis montana, set apart by its slender leafy stem, linear leaves and regular blue flowers split to the ovary, the segments about three centimetres long. The blooms form an irregular panicle or umbel framed by lance-shaped bracts. Plate 241 appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Anthericum Aloides
description: Anthericum aloides, its thick fleshy aloe-like leaves giving rise to slender, somewhat pendulous scapes that carry elongated racemes of six-parted flowers, each segment with a green midrib. Redouté prepared the plate for Les Liliacées (1809); the source description confirms the characteristic charnu root and glaucous green leaves of this aloe-like species.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Anthericum Frutescens
description: Anthericum frutescens, a half-woody species with a twisted creeping stem, a terminal cluster of fleshy half-cylindrical leaves, and a bare scape ending in a raceme of yellow flowers. The descriptive text accompanying Redoute's plates was supplied by botanists including A.P. de Candolle.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Asparagus Horridus
description: Asparagus horridus, a woody bristling species whose spine-like leaves and angular branches almost hide its membership of the lily family, betrayed only by the small greenish flowers clustered in the leaf axils. Redoute drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Crocus Biflorus
description: Crocus biflorus, two or three blooms to a tuft, the whitish segments marked outside with broad violet lines and the corm wrapped in smooth brown scales. Redoute drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809); it sits in the iris family on the classification line.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Crocus Susianus
description: Plate 293 shows Crocus susianus, its orange-yellow segments recurving and rolling outward at opening, the three outer ones backed with violet lines, above narrow grooved leaves. The plate appears in the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809), in the iris family.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Crocus Vernus
description: Crocus vernus, a solitary flower of six lance-shaped segments ranging from white to violet or blue, the corm sheathed in netted brown fibres and the leaves marked with a white midrib. Redoute, flower painter to Empress Josephine, drew it for the fifth volume (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Fishing upon the Blythe-Sand
description: Sailing vessels move through a choppy estuary beneath a luminous amber sky, the horizon loaded with incoming weather. The setting is the Blythe-Sand off the Suffolk coast, not the Thames, as the title records. Painted in 1809 and now at Tate Britain (National Gallery collection), the work reflects Turner's sustained engagement with Dutch seventeenth-century marine painting.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — MQG2rOTbb5MaqQ Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00496&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: Flagellaria Indica
description: Flagellaria indica, a climbing plant whose leaf tips coil into circinately coiled tendrils, depicted with its small flowers arranged in terminal branched panicles. The plate appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacées (1809) and includes botanical dissection figures at the foot of the sheet.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Galaxia Ovata
description: Galaxia ovata, a small iris-family plant with ovate leaves and short-tubed flowers, its three stamens joined at the filaments. The plate appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809), a stipple engraving printed in colour and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Communis
description: Gladiolus communis bears six to twelve stalkless, slightly nodding red flowers in a loose one-sided spike, its sword-shaped leaves sheathing the slender scape. The lower segments carry a white longitudinal line. This plate comes from the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Hirsutus
description: Gladiolus hirsutus on a smooth slender stem, its sword-shaped leaves edged red and clothed in soft hairs along the sheath, carrying two large pinkish flowers. Despite the title, Les Liliacees covers many Iridaceae like this one, as the Jussieu classification line on the plate shows.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Tubatus
description: Gladiolus tubatus, close to the leaning gladiolus, with hairy pleated leaves and a scape that bends horizontal to carry twelve or fourteen long-tubed flowers in a loose spike. Redoute drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809); enlarged floral figures sit at the foot of the sheet.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Heritiera Tinctorum
description: Heritiera tinctorum, a leafy stem with sword-shaped basal leaves and a tight corymb of woolly-coated flowers, orange within and split into six segments. Redoute drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacées (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Hypoxis Luzulæfolia
description: Hypoxis luzulaefolia, pleated linear leaves edged with hooked cilia and a hairy scape ending in a single greenish-yellow flower split to the base into six segments. Redoute drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809), the stipple engraving printed in colour and hand-finished.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Arenaria
description: Iris arenaria, one of the smallest species of its genus, with sword-shaped leaves and pale yellow flowers borne in pairs on short stems. The outer segments are bearded past the middle, the inner ones upright and wavy below; A.P. de Candolle supplied the accompanying botanical text.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Graminea
description: Iris graminea is readily recognised by its strongly compressed stems, which are two or three times shorter than the bright green, grass-like leaves. The stems each bear two, or occasionally three, flowers whose outer segments have a whitish rounded blade veined with blue, above a violet lower portion with a yellow stripe. Redouté drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacées (1809–1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Lutescens
description: Iris lutescens, a low species bearing a single yellow terminal flower above sword-shaped leaves, the outer spatulate segments deeper in colour and bearded with yellow filaments. The plate is a stipple engraving printed in colour from one plate and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Pumila
description: Iris pumila, the dwarf iris, shown in flower above its short sword-shaped leaves in a plate from Redoute's Les Liliacees. The image is a stipple engraving printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Veriegata
description: Plate 292 shows Iris variegata, its sword-shaped leaves below a branched stem with two or three flowers; the outer segments are yellow streaked with red-violet and bearded along the midline, the inner ones wholly yellow. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and watercoloured by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Virescens
description: Plate 295 shows Iris virescens, its sword-shaped leaves below a short stem bearing one yellowish flower in a two-valved spathe; the outer segments are lilac above and yellow with violet veins below, bearded with yellow filaments. From the fifth volume of Les Liliacees, 1809.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Filifolia
description: Ixia filifolia bears solitary terminal flowers, sometimes bright yellow and sometimes reddish, above very fine thread-like leaves. The French text notes its close kinship with Ixia rosea, from which it differs by its shorter foliage. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Recurva
description: Ixia recurva bears solitary greenish-yellow flowers above sharply arched basal leaves, on a triangular stem winged with a fine brown membrane. The French text assigns it to the section Gawler set apart as Trichonema, marked by hairy filaments. The plate belongs to the iris family in Triandria monogynia.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Lachenalia Luteola
description: Lachenalia luteola is distinguished from its kin by two linear-lanceolate leaves that are smooth and free of the dark spots typical of the genus, and by a glabrous stalk carrying about fifteen pendent yellow flowers. The upper portion of the raceme bears six to eight small sterile pink blooms above a cluster of reddish bracts. The plate appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacées (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Lilium Chalcedonicum
description: Lilium chalcedonicum, the scarlet Turk's-cap lily, with whorled leaves and pendent flowers whose segments roll fully back. The plate appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809); the descriptive text accompanying Redoute's plates was supplied by A.P. de Candolle and others.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: London from Greenwich Park
description: A panoramic survey of the capital seen from the hill at Greenwich, with the Queen's House and Wren's Royal Hospital below and St Paul's hazed in coal-smoke distance. The painting belongs to a series celebrating the Thames as the artery of empire.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — IAHskvl8KuvdYw Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00483&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: Melanthium Gramineum
description: Melanthium gramineum, the grass-leaved species, growing from a scaly bulb that buds offsets, with narrow basal leaves and two or three sessile whitish flowers tinged yellow. The corolla divides to the base into six lance-linear segments marked with even longitudinal veins.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Mrs. Harrison Gray Otis
description: Sally Foster Otis, wife of the Federalist senator and mayor of Boston, sits in a white empire-line gown with a red shawl draped at her elbow. Stuart painted her in Boston in 1809, the canvas now held by the Reynolda House Museum of American Art in Winston-Salem.
credit: The Reynolda House Museum of American Art

title: Omnia Vincit Amor Alternative title
description: A winged Eros stands triumphant amid clouds, holding a flaming torch and a leash that subdues a lion reclining at his feet, while Venus with a flaming sceptre, putti, and a dark horse attended by further putti fill the allegorical scene. West signed the canvas in 1809, now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (accession 95.22.1), as one of his late London allegories illustrating Virgil's phrase that love conquers all.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (accession number 95.22.1)

title: Ornithogalum Nutans
description: Ornithogalum nutans, its channelled basal leaves matching the scape, which ends in a one-sided raceme of six to twelve greenish flowers that spread then droop. The broad membranous filaments and the three-valved seed capsule appear in figures at the foot. Redoute drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ornithogalum Spathaceum
description: Ornithogalum spathaceum, distinguished from its yellow umbel-flowered kin by a slender scape, thread-like basal leaves, and a single spathe-like leaf rising on the stem to the level of the smaller flowers. Long confused with related species, it grows from a pea-sized bulb. Redoute drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Phalangium Liliago
description: Phalangium liliago, narrow keeled leaves below a tall simple scape ending in an elongated raceme of pure white flowers, each cut to the base into six three-nerved segments with yellow anthers. The plate dates to the fifth volume of Les Liliacées (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Phalangium Liliastrum
description: Phalangium liliastrum, the St Bruno's lily, its few large bell-shaped white flowers turned mostly to one side on a leafless scape, the stamens curving toward the lower side of the flower. Redouté drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacées (1809), where it is noted as intermediate between the spider-plants and the day-lilies.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Phalangium Ramosum
description: Phalangium ramosum, fleshy white roots spread like spider's legs below a branched scape carrying a loose pyramidal panicle of white wheel-shaped flowers, each perianth divided to the base into six spreading lanceolate segments. The plate appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacées (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Phalangium Serotinum
description: Phalangium serotinum, a slender bulb sending up two narrow leaves and a scape topped by one large flower whose six spreading segments are yellow at the base, white within and reddish outside. The plate, from the fifth volume (1809), notes the top-shaped three-celled capsule. Redoute placed the genus among the asphodels.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Philipp Otto Runge
description: This chalk and pencil study of 1809, now at the Hamburger Kunsthalle, shows a single nude infant kneeling among flowers and low plants, reaching towards a blossom. It is a preparatory sheet for Runge's ambitious but unfinished Great Morning, part of his cosmological Times of Day cycle, in which such child figures carry symbolic weight as embodiments of natural and spiritual renewal.

title: Pleea Tenuifolia
description: Pleea tenuifolia, slender sword-shaped basal leaves below upright stems bearing a few fairly large flowers, each perianth tawny-yellow and cut to the base into six lanceolate segments that persist around the ripening fruit. The work places it in the rush family on the Jussieu line. The plate appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Polygonatum Latifolium
description: Polygonatum latifolium, a flexuous stem with broad alternate leaves hairy beneath along the veins, the white green-lined flowers hanging from branched axillary stalks. The plate, from the fifth volume (1809), records the spherical blue-black three-celled berry. Redoute placed the genus in the asparagus family on the Jussieu line.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Polygonatum Verticillatum
description: Polygonatum verticillatum, a slender stem set with crowded whorls of five or six lanceolate-linear leaves, the small whitish pendulous flowers borne from the middle and lower whorls. The plate, from the fifth volume (1809), records the round violet three-celled berry. The genus sits in the asparagus family on the Jussieu line.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Polygonatum Vulgare
description: Polygonatum vulgare, Solomon's seal, a strongly angled stem with eight to ten ovate leaves and solitary or paired white pendulous flowers on arched axillary stalks. The plate appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809). The dissection figures at the foot of the sheet show the flower's parts enlarged.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Sagittaria Sagittifolia
description: Sagittaria sagittifolia, the common arrowhead, with its triangular arrow-shaped leaves on stout air-filled petioles and a simple terminal raceme of whorled flowers. The plate appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809); the lower stalks usually stand submerged in water.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Sanseviera Zeylanica
description: Sanseviera zeylanica, the Ceylon bow-string hemp, with fleshy channelled leaves marked by transverse bands and a thick scape carrying a crowded raceme of greenish-white flowers in clusters of four or five. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Scilla Amœna
description: Plate 298 shows Scilla amoena again, an ovoid bulb sending up channelled leaves and slender scapes bearing four to six pale-blue flowers in a loose raceme, each segment marked with two whitish elongated spots at the base. Dissection figures at the foot of the sheet enlarge the stamen and fruit. Redouté drew this plate for the fifth volume of Les Liliacées (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Scilla Bifolia
description: Scilla bifolia, the two-leaved squill, with a pair of opposite sheathing leaves and a short terminal raceme of blue flowers whose perianth splits to the base into six spreading segments. The bulb, leaves, and multiple scapes bearing flowers at various stages are shown together. The plate appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacées (1809), drawn by Pierre-Joseph Redouté.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Sisyrinchium Collinum
description: Sisyrinchium collinum, a small iris-relative drawn with its flattened stem, narrow fan of leaves and wheel-shaped flowers within their spathes. The plate appeared in the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809), the stipple engraving printed in colour and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Sisyrinchium Gramineum
description: Sisyrinchium gramineum, its grass-like sword-shaped leaves flanking flattened winged stems that end in small clustered flowers held in a two-valved spathe. The plate belongs to the iris family in Jussieu's system; Redoute drew it for Volume 5 of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Sisyrinchium Tenuifolium
description: Sisyrinchium tenuifolium, forming a turf of slender flattened stems among very narrow sword-shaped leaves, with yellow six-parted flowers opening one at a time from each terminal umbel. The plate belongs to the iris family and appeared in Volume 5 of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Streptopus Amplexifolius
description: Streptopus amplexifolius, a slender plant with clasping heart-based leaves and solitary white bell-flowers hanging on sharply bent stalks. The work assigns it to the asparagus family of Jussieu; Redoute drew it for Volume 5 of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: The Abbey in the Oakwood
description: A procession of monks bears a coffin into the snow-rimed ruin of a Gothic abbey, the gnarled oaks around them silhouetted against a pale winter dusk. Friedrich exhibited the canvas in Berlin alongside Mönch am Meer as a Romantic meditation on death and resurrection.

title: The Garreteer’s Petition
description: A poet implores his muse in a cramped attic, an unusually literary genre subject for Turner. Exhibited at the Royal Academy with verses of his own composition, it shows him courting the hierarchy of history painting.

title: The Great Morning
description: A detail from the unfinished Great Morning, showing the radiant central figure Runge devised as the embodiment of dawn within his Times of Day cycle. The hard-edged drawing and saturated colour reveal the artist's mystical, almost emblematic Romanticism.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/runge/2morning"

title: The Trout Stream
description: Several figures fish and work along the shallows of a broad river beneath an open, cloud-filled sky, with a prominent hill dominating the left background and a bridge visible in the middle distance. The expansive, unwooded landscape departs from the enclosed pastoral of Turner's Thames studies, lending the scene a grander scale. Painted in 1809, the canvas is held by the Taft Museum of Art, Cincinnati (inv. 1931.459).

title: Thomson's Aeolian Harp
description: A pastoral elegy for the poet James Thomson, with classical figures grouped on a hillside above the Thames at Richmond. Turner pairs the picture with verses of his own, blending Claudean idyll and literary tribute.

title: Tofieldia Palustris
description: Tofieldia palustris, its sword-shaped basal leaves below a narrow terminal raceme of small white six-parted flowers, with the three-horned ovary shown enlarged at the foot. The plate places it among the Colchicaceae of Jussieu and appeared in Volume 5 of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Tritoma Uvaria
description: Tritoma uvaria, its stiff keeled leaves with finely toothed margins around a stout bare scape carrying a dense raceme of pendent tubular flowers, saffron-yellow below and scarlet toward the tip. The work places it among the asphodels of Jussieu and appeared in Volume 5 of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Witsenia Maura
description: Witsenia maura, an iris-family shrublet from the Cape, its woody jointed stem carrying fans of stiff narrow leaves and flowers with a pink-purple tube and yellow lobes, each pair emerging from overlapping brown scaly spathes. Redouté drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacées (1809); dissection figures at lower left show the short-filament stamens and elongated style.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Yucca Filamentosa
description: Yucca filamentosa, distinguished by its lack of a stem, with numerous radical leaves whose margins fray into white curling threads. The tall scape carries a pyramidal panicle of whitish nodding flowers shaped somewhat like tulips. Redoute drew it for the fifth volume of Les Liliacees (1809).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Abigail Smith Adams
description: The former First Lady sits with hands folded, wearing a rose-red dress under a sheer embroidered lace overlay and a white lace cap tied with ribbon. Gilbert Stuart painted Abigail Smith Adams between 1810 and 1815 as a companion to his portrait of John Adams; the portrait is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Grande Odalisque
dateCreated: 1810 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A reclining concubine turns her head over a famously elongated back -- Ingres lengthened her spine by several vertebrae in pursuit of an ideal sinuous line. Commissioned by Caroline Murat for the Naples court, the picture was scandalised at the 1819 Salon for its anatomical liberties.
credit: wartburg.edu

title: Petworth House from the Lake: Dewy Morning
description: A view across the Earl of Egremont's lake, painted under the patronage that gave Turner the run of Petworth. Cool morning haze dissolves park, water and sky into the unified atmosphere typical of his Sussex landscapes.

title: Philipp Otto Runge
description: A black and white chalk drawing of the young Sophia Sieveking laid out in death, her features composed against a pale pillow. Runge made the sheet shortly before his own early death, lending its mortuary stillness an autobiographical weight.

title: Prado - Los Desastres de la Guerra - No. 04 - Las mugeres dan valor
englishTitle: The Disasters of War, Plate 4: Las mugeres dan valor
description: Plate 4 of the Disasters of War, captioned 'The women give courage'. Goya shows female combatants resisting French troops during the Peninsular War, the etching and aquatint biting through the page in his characteristically stark contrasts of black and gnawed white.
credit: Museo del Prado

title: Prado - Los Desastres de la Guerra - No. 46 - Esto es malo
englishTitle: The Disasters of War, Plate 46: Esto es malo
description: Plate 46 of the Disasters of War, 'This is bad'. A friar is set upon amid scattered bodies, the scene drawn with the cramped, shallow space and bitten line that give the series its grim moral force. The plates were withheld until decades after Goya's death.
credit: Museo del Prado

title: Prado - Los Desastres de la Guerra - No. 47 - Así sucedió
englishTitle: Los Desastres de la Guerra, Plate 47: Así sucedió (This Is How It Happened)
description: Plate 47 of the Disasters of War, captioned 'This is how it happened'. A robed figure kneels prostrate before a barred enclosure while armed men press in from above, the compressed space and harsh contrasts typical of Goya's documentary etching style. Part of the 80-print series created between 1810 and 1820 and held at the Museo del Prado, Madrid, it was not published until 1863.

title: Shipwreck of the Minotaur
description: A naval transport founders amid towering green-grey waves, lifeboats overloaded with survivors swept up the swells. Turner makes the wreck of HMS Minotaur an early demonstration of his lifelong subject of nature's indifferent force at sea.
credit: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum

title: The Fish Market at Hastings Beach
description: Fisherfolk sell and sort their catch on the broad sandy beach at Hastings, with sailing vessels riding the surf behind them. Turner painted this scene in 1810, a period when Hastings served as both a working fishing port and a fashionable resort. The canvas is held at the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City.

title: The Public Viewing David ’s " Coronation " at the Louvre
description: A dense crowd of visitors examining Jacques-Louis David's vast 'Coronation of Napoleon' on the wall of the Louvre, a guidebook in the hands of a soldier at left. Oil on canvas, 61.6 by 82.6 cm, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. David's painting was shown at the Louvre between 1808 and 1810, the occasion Boilly records here.

title: Agave Yuccæfolia
description: Agave yuccaefolia, its narrow glaucous leaves — finely and irregularly toothed at the cartilaginous margins — gathered in a spreading rosette from which two tall slender stalks rise; the flowering individual documented in the source text reached three metres eight decimetres. The plates of Les Liliacées were stipple-engraved and hand-finished in watercolour, a technique Redouté used across the series issued between 1802 and 1816.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Cernuum
description: Allium cernuum, the nodding onion, recognised by its pendent rounded umbel of pale-rose flowers on a stem curved at the top, with stamens projecting beyond the segments. The text assigns it to the asphodel family; enlarged floral figures appear at the foot of the sheet.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Chamæ-Moly
description: Allium chamae-moly, the smallest of the known garlics, with its rosette of narrow ground-hugging leaves and a short stem bearing an umbel of bell-shaped whitish flowers tinged red. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811), the stem all but hidden in the leaf cluster.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Ciliare
description: Allium ciliare rises from a hazelnut-sized bulb to a smooth scape topped by a flat umbel of pure white, scentless flowers. The enlarged stamen and seed figures at the foot follow the botanical convention of the period, showing the violet-red anthers and the three-grooved ovary.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Denudatum
description: Allium denudatum, its angled scapes nodding before the flowers open, then straightening into a near-hemispherical umbel of small whitish blooms. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811); the species name refers to the early-falling spathe valves.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Longispathum
description: Allium longispathum, its slender compressed scape carrying a loose rounded umbel of greenish flowers with red-veined segments. The species is named for its two long spathe valves, one reaching about a decimetre, the other half again as long, drawn for the sixth volume (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Subhirsutum
description: Allium subhirsutum, its soft ciliate leaves and a flattened umbel of fragrant white flowers with narrow lance-shaped segments. The plate appeared in the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811); two varieties are shown, one with hairy glaucous leaves, the other green and merely fringed.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Triquetrum
description: Allium triquetrum, the three-cornered leek, its sharply triangular scape carrying a loose umbel of large white bells, each segment marked with a green midrib. The bulb sits in reddish coats, the leaves keeled like a sedge. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Ursinum
description: Allium ursinum, wild garlic, recognised at a glance by its triangular stem and broad stalked leaves. The white star-shaped flowers form an open umbel above two or three lance-shaped blades on cylindrical petioles. This stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand, the method used across all eight volumes.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Longifolia
description: Amaryllis longifolia, its very long glaucous leaves curving over and pendent, with about twelve flowers in an umbel on a nearly cylindrical scape. The white segments carry a reddish-brown stripe, the three outer ones recurved at the tip. Plate 347 appeared in the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Asphodelus Ramosus
description: Asphodelus ramosus, growing from a bundle of spindle-shaped tubers, its glaucous channelled leaves below a tall stem carrying a long conical raceme of white flowers, each segment marked with a brown midrib. The plate belongs to the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Canna Gigantea
description: Canna gigantea, a tall canna reaching some two metres, its large ovate-lanceolate leaves carried on arching petioles whose winged margins sheathe the stem. The accompanying text separates it from the Indian canna by its height, its long flower stalks, and the rounded ovary shown enlarged below.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Canna Glauca
description: Canna glauca, its glaucous ovate leaves sheathing a stem about a metre high and its flowers set in pairs along an elongated terminal spike, yellow segments flecked with small red marks. A. P. de Candolle and others supplied the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plates for Les Liliacees.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Commelina Dubia
description: Commelina dubia, close to the tuberous dayflower but lower in stature, its ovate-lanceolate leaves five- to seven-veined and reddish at the cartilaginous margins. The flowers form small terminal clusters, each wrapped in a heart-shaped bract folded along its midrib. The plates were printed in colour and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Crinum Americanum
description: Crinum americanum shown with broad strap-shaped leaves and an umbel of ten to twenty white flowers, the long perianth tube opening into six narrow spreading lobes. The plate belongs to Les Liliacées, Redouté dating it between 1811 and 1813; the source text confirms the distinctive flattened, triangular flower stalk.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Crinum Asiaticum
description: Crinum asiaticum, drawn for Les Liliacees with its bulb sending up long strap leaves and an umbel of long-tubed white flowers. Redoute printed the work in eight folio volumes, this one in 1811; the colour was laid down from a single stipple plate and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: crinum commelini
description: Plate 322 shows Crinum commelini, its six to eight channelled basal leaves rising from a buried bulb beside a cylindrical green scape bearing three or four white flowers with long perianth tubes. Like all the plates, it was printed in colour and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Echeandia Terniflora
description: Echeandia terniflora, its grassy ribbed leaves and slender scapes ending in a long raceme of bright yellow flowers borne three to each bract. The fused anthers form a hollow cone like that of the composite family, an unusual detail Redoute recorded for the sixth volume (1811) of Les Liliacees.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Epidendrum Cochleatum
description: Epidendrum cochleatum, an orchid rising from almond-shaped green pseudobulbs to a nodding scape of three to six flowers. A twist in the pedicel turns the heart-shaped lip upright like a standard, a feature Redoute noted for the sixth volume (1811). Pale green segments hang below the resupinate bloom.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Angustus
description: Gladiolus angustus growing from two stacked corms, with very narrow sword-shaped leaves and a loose one-sided spike of five or six flesh-pink flowers on a slender tube. An iris-family plant, it appeared in the sixth volume (1811); the enlarged dissection figures below show the flower's parts.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Laccatus
description: Gladiolus laccatus grows from two rounded, slightly flattened tubers set side by side, its linear spirally twisted leaves arranged on two opposite ranks below a short spike of seven or eight vivid rose flowers. The angled perianth tube, with its markedly distinct throat and narrow lower section, is described in the accompanying text. This plate belongs to the sixth volume of Les Liliacées (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Hæmanthus Puniceus
description: Haemanthus puniceus, a tuft of wavy ovate leaves spotted with purple beside a thick scape ending in a dense umbel of pale-red flowers within a green spathe. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand, the method used across the eight folio volumes.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Hyacinthus Romanus
description: Hyacinthus romanus, slender scapes rising above keeled linear leaves to a loose cylindrical raceme of about twenty small flowers that pass from greenish to white. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine; this plate ran in the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Hypoxis Erecta
description: Hypoxis erecta, hairy linear leaves in a tuft above a brown-tunicked base, with two-edged scapes bearing four or five small yellow flowers green on their undersides. The plate places it among the Narcisses in Jussieu's order; Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Amœna
description: Iris amoena, its upright leaves reddish at the base and nearly as long as the stem, with bearded outer segments that curve back only at the tip. Redoute treated it as a new species, possibly the same as the Hungarian iris, in the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: iris curtopetala
description: Iris curtopetala, its sword-shaped pale green leaves overtopping the flattened stem, with three yellow flowers veined in violet and ridged near the base of the outer segments. The stipple plate was printed in colour from a single engraving and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Fœtidissima
description: Iris foetidissima, whose leaves give off a roasted-meat odour when crushed, bearing small dull blue-violet flowers two to a stem. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811); the foliage is often striped lengthwise in alternating green and yellow.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Germanica
description: Iris germanica rises from a fleshy knotted rootstock and sends up glaucous, slightly falcate leaves and a branched stem bearing flowers that range from deep violet to pale blue. The outer segments are bearded along the midline with dense yellow filaments, and the spathe valves are foliate and greenish at centre. Redouté drew it for Les Liliacées (1811–1813).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Lurida
description: Iris lurida, its cylindrical creeping rootstock giving rise to upright leaves and flowers whose limb is a glossy blackish-purple, the outer segments bearded in yellow and lined with yellow and violet at the base. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Ochroleuca
description: Iris ochroleuca, reaching nearly a metre, its outer segments tipped with a large whitish elliptical blade above a yellow claw, the inner segments and stigmas white. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811), distinguishing it from a closely allied species.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Plicata
description: Iris plicata rises to about a metre with glaucous sword-shaped leaves and strongly scented flowers. The plate illustrates variant B of the species, whose petals are a uniform blue-violet rather than the whitish-centred, violet-edged form of the type; the outer segments are bearded and veined purple at the base. Redouté drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacées (1811–1813).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Sambucina
description: Iris sambucina, named for its pleasant elder-like scent, carries two large flowers at the tip of each branch above falcate sword-shaped leaves marked with raised veins. The outer segments are purple toward the tip and yellowish at the base; the inner segments are greyish-lilac. Redouté drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacées (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Spuria
description: Plate 349 shows Iris spuria, its sword-shaped glaucous leaves below a tall stem bearing three or four flowers with spatulate, widely spread outer segments; the claw is yellow with red veins and the blade deep violet. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and watercoloured by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Stenogyna
description: Plate 310 shows Iris stenogyna, named for its narrow stigmas, with sword-shaped glaucous leaves and two scentless yellowish flowers emerging from a three-valved spathe. The ribbed oblong ovary and greenish-yellow segments are drawn from life; Redoute made the plate for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees in 1811.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Swertii
description: Iris swertii on a glaucous stem about three decimetres high, usually carrying three flowers whose outer segments are white-bearded along the midline and the inner ones spatulate and waved. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand, the method used throughout the eight folio volumes.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Versicolor
description: Iris versicolor on a slender scape, its small flowers with lance-shaped falls ending in a rounded purple-violet blade that turns strongly outward, the rest dull yellow veined with violet. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811), part of a work spanning 1802 to 1816.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Xiphium
description: Plate 337 shows Iris xiphium, the most variable of its genus in flower size and colour, growing from a white ovoid tuber rather than a true bulb, with awl-shaped channelled leaves and usually two terminal flowers. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Crocata
description: Ixia crocata rises on a slender stem to a loose spike of orange-yellow funnel-shaped flowers, its sword-shaped leaves curved like a sickle below. The classification line places it in the iris family, Triandria monogynia of the Linnaean system. Enlarged stamen and ovary figures sit at the foot of the sheet.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: lilium canadense
description: Lilium canadense, the Canada lily, with whorled lance-shaped leaves and nodding bell-formed flowers on long pedicels. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811); he served as flower painter to Empress Josephine, in whose Malmaison gardens many specimens were grown.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Musa Coccinea
description: Musa coccinea, the scarlet banana, smaller than the long-known banana species but like them in form, with sheathing leaf-stalks and a dense erect spike wrapped in large coloured spathes. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ornithogalum Luteum
description: Ornithogalum luteum, growing from a hazelnut-sized bulb to a single channelled leaf and a terminal umbel of three to seven yellow flowers, green on the outside. A collar of opposite bracts sits below the blooms, with stamen and ovary figures enlarged at the foot. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ornithogalum Minimum
description: Ornithogalum minimum, a dwarf species with a flexuous stem often lying on the ground, two narrow leaves, and a small corymb of six to ten star-shaped flowers, bright yellow within. The Asphodel-family plant shows enlarged dissection figures below, a botanical convention of the period.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ornithogalum Tenuifolium
description: Ornithogalum tenuifolium, its narrow awl-shaped dark-green leaves rising with the bare scape to a short dense raceme of eight to twelve flowers, white with a broad green midrib stripe. Redoute drew this Asphodel-family species for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811); the enlarged stamen figures below follow period convention.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ornithogalum Thyrsoides
description: Ornithogalum thyrsoides, its channelled pale-green leaves below a bare scape ending in a dense raceme that lengthens during flowering, the white segments marked with a small green basal spot. The botanist A.P. de Candolle and others supplied the descriptive text that ran with Redoute's plates in Les Liliacees.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Pancratium Calathiforme
description: Pancratium calathiforme, set apart by its large nectary cup and the arrangement of the stamens, with linear leaves in two ranks and a flattened two-edged scape bearing two stalkless white flowers. The Amaryllis-family plant shows its long green perianth tube and dissection figures, drawn for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Pancratium Declinatum
description: Pancratium declinatum, with dark-green strap-shaped leaves arranged in two ranks below a strongly flattened two-edged scape carrying an umbel of about ten large stalkless white flowers from a two-valved spathe. An inverted-cone nectary joins the stamen filaments. Redouté drew this plate for the sixth volume of Les Liliacées (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Peronia Stricta
description: Peronia stricta, a tall slender stem nearly two metres high carrying large ovate leaves on long sheathing petioles, the scentless flowers gathered in a compound spike with leafy bracts. The work places it in the canna family on the Jussieu line. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Phalangium Pendulum
description: Phalangium pendulum, slender branching stems carrying loose racemes of tiny nodding flowers grouped in threes, the outer segments violet and the inner ones edged in white. The plate, from the sixth volume (1811), records the bearded filaments and citron-yellow anthers. Redoute placed the genus among the asphodels.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Polygonatum Sibiricum
description: Polygonatum sibiricum, an angular stem with narrow whorled leaves hooked at the tips, the small greenish-white flowers on forked stalks ringed by two opposite bracts at the division. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811). The enlarged floral figures below follow the botanical convention of the period.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Sanseviera Carnea
description: Sanseviera carnea, its two-ranked linear-lanceolate leaves rising from a horizontal rhizome to a loose spike of pink flowers, each tubular bloom opening into six recurved segments. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811), placed by Jussieu among the asparagus family.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Sanseviera Guineensis
description: Plate 330 shows Sanseviera guineensis, the bow-string hemp of Guinea, with stiff dark-banded leaves and a green scape bearing a dense raceme of white tubular flowers paired along its length. The dissection figures at the foot enlarge the stamens and floral parts, a botanical convention of the period.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Scilla Autumnalis
description: Scilla autumnalis, the autumn squill, with narrow almost thread-like leaves and slender scapes carrying a loose raceme of pale-blue or rosy flowers, the dissection figures showing ovary, capsule and black seeds. The plate appeared in the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Scilla Italica
description: Scilla italica, the Italian squill, with soft linear leaves and a short crowded terminal raceme of small pale greyish-blue flowers, each carried on a stout pedicel with a membranous bract longer than the pedicel. The plate appeared in Les Liliacées (published 1811–1813) by Pierre-Joseph Redouté, depicting the plant with its ovoid bulb and spreading basal leaves.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Scilla Lingulata
description: Scilla lingulata, set apart by its bracts divided through their entire length into two or three linear shreds, with lanceolate leaves reflexed in their upper portion and a fairly tight raceme of pale-blue flowers. Redouté drew it for Les Liliacées (published 1811–1813), depicting the plant with its hazelnut-sized rounded bulb and short scape rising to eight or sixteen centimetres.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Sisyrinchium Palmifolium
description: Sisyrinchium palmifolium, growing from an oval red-scaled bulb and bearing pleated lance-shaped leaves below white star-flowers enclosed in a green spathe. Redoute drew it for the sixth folio volume of Les Liliacees (1811), the stamen figures at the foot of the sheet enlarged in the manner of the period.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Sowerbæa Juncea
description: Sowerbaea juncea, its tufts of slender rush-like leaves giving rise to bare scapes topped by rounded umbels of lilac-pink flowers within a reddish collar of bracts. The plate places it among the asphodels of Jussieu and appeared in Volume 6 of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Tofieldia Pubescens
description: Tofieldia pubescens, its iris-like flattened leaves beneath a slender bristly stem carrying a narrow raceme of small whitish flowers grouped in threes. Redoute drew it for the sixth folio volume of Les Liliacees (1811), each plate a stipple engraving printed in colour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Yucca Gloriosa
description: Yucca gloriosa, the entire-leaved yucca, a near-shrub whose short woody trunk bears terminal clusters of stiff brown-edged leaves and a metre-high pyramidal panicle. The text counts it among the few lily-family plants that grow on a true woody trunk. Redoute drew it for the sixth volume of Les Liliacees (1811).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Agapanthus Umbellatus
description: A second study of Agapanthus umbellatus, its blue umbel raised on a bare stalk above strap-shaped leaves. Redoute returned to the species for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees, issued in 1812 among the eight folio volumes printed between 1802 and 1816.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Ampeloprasum
description: Allium ampeloprasum, the wild leek, its fist-sized bulb of clustered cloves throwing up a stem to about a metre and a half crowned by a dense near-spherical umbel of small lilac flowers. The dissection figures below enlarge the flower's sexual parts.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Arenarium
description: Allium arenarium, the sand garlic, its bulb sending up a slender glaucous stalk whose umbel is largely replaced by a head of small black bulblets among purple-violet flowers. The text assigns it to the asphodel family (Asphodèles), Linnaean Hexandria monogynia.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Brachystemon
description: Allium brachystemon, a small-bulbed onion with few narrow leaves and a loose umbel of six to eight whitish flowers, the lance-shaped segments marked by a brown midline and notably short stamens. From the seventh volume of Les Liliacees, issued in 1812.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Carinatum
description: Allium carinatum, the keeled garlic, its channelled leaves on a slender stem and a loose umbel mixed with small green bulblets, the long thread-like stamens projecting well beyond the violet-red flowers. The plate dissections enlarge the floral parts below.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Obliquum
description: Allium obliquum, marked by its long stamens, obliquely set linear leaves and an axillary branch from the stem, ending in a nearly spherical umbel of small greenish flowers. The plate appeared in the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812), the stamens nearly three times the perianth length.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Sphærocephalon
description: Allium sphaerocephalon, the round-headed garlic, its tall slender scape ending in a dense spherical umbel of small purple-red flowers. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812); the figures show three inner stamens split into three points, a feature of the genus.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Josephinæ
description: Amaryllis josephinae, named for Empress Josephine, with the largest bulb of any known liliaceous plant supporting an umbel of some sixty flowers up to a metre across. The two-edged scape rises after the long sickle-curved leaves have dried. Redoute was flower painter to Josephine, and many specimens were grown at Malmaison.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Anthericum Annuum
description: Anthericum annuum growing in dense tufts, its awl-shaped grey-green leaves all basal and its flexuous scapes carrying a loose raceme of star-spread yellow flowers, each segment striped with a green longitudinal line. The plate was issued in the seventh volume of Les Liliacées (1812), stipple-engraved and finished by hand in watercolour in the standard technique of the series.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Antholyza Præalta
description: Antholyza praealta, taller and broader-leaved than its Ethiopian relative, rising from a large flattened bulb wrapped in a net of crossed fibres, with sword-shaped leaves and numerous stalkless flowers in two ranks. The plate belongs to the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Asparagus Pectinatus
description: Asparagus pectinatus, a climbing slender vine whose narrow falcate leaves grow in threes along two opposite ranks, with few pendulous flowers on jointed stalks. The plate was issued in the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812), printed in colour and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Asphodelus Capillaris
description: Asphodelus capillaris, close to the yellow asphodel but distinct, with extremely numerous near-threadlike triangular leaves and a tall stem carrying an elongated raceme of yellow flowers, each segment green along the midline. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Bromelia Pinguin
description: Bromelia pinguin, the wild pineapple, its numerous linear leaves edged the whole length with strong recurved spines and a tall scape bearing a tight cylindrical raceme of flowers in clusters of four or five. The plates of Les Liliacees were stipple engravings printed in colour from a single plate, then finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Colonel Alastair Ranaldson Macdonell of Glengarry
description: The Highland chieftain stands in full tartan dress against a plain interior wall hung with a circular targe and crossed weapons, every element of clan regalia on calculated display. Raeburn's 1812 full-length portrait, now at the National Galleries Scotland (NG 420), uses broad, direct brushwork to render Macdonell's self-presentation as a living embodiment of traditional Highland identity — a persona he cultivated with considerable deliberateness.

title: Commelina Dianthifolia
description: Commelina dianthifolia, with fusiform tubers and a slender jointed stem to six or eight decimetres, its narrow five-veined leaves finely ciliate at the margin. The flowers rise from a lance-shaped heart-based involucre folded along its length; Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Commelina Rubens
description: Commelina rubens, with reddish hairy stems trailing below and rising above, its lance-shaped leaves slightly waved near the tip. The flowers form terminal umbels of three or four, each wrapped in a heart-shaped folded spathe. The text notes the genus is large and poorly characterised, making the species hard to fix.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Crinum Taïtense
description: Plate 408 shows Crinum taitense, distinguished by its sharply two-edged compressed scape carrying an open hemispherical umbel of roughly thirty flowers above metre-long leaves. The plate appears in the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Cyanella Capensis
description: Cyanella capensis, its depressed whitish bulbs sending up a slender branched stem with dark ciliate leaves and loose racemes of six-parted flowers, here a pale lilac. The plate sits in the asphodel family of the Jussieu line and appears in the seventh volume (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Cyrtanthus Angustifolius
description: Plate 388 shows Cyrtanthus angustifolius, two narrow upright leaves from an egg-shaped bulb and a scape bearing two to five scarlet tubular flowers, slightly nodding, with six short lobes. The plate belongs to the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812), in the amaryllis family.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Cyrtanthus Obliquus
description: Cyrtanthus obliquus, its fist-sized bulb raising obliquely twisted glaucous leaves in two ranks and a scape of about twelve pendent trumpet flowers, yellow at the base and red beyond. The plate appears in the seventh volume (1812); enlarged floral parts sit at the foot.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Eriospermum Lanceæfolium
description: Eriospermum lanceaefolium, a tuberous-rooted plant with a single ovate-lanceolate leaf dusted with fine points and a slender scape bearing a loose raceme of small green-and-white flowers. The text assigns it to the asphodel family; the enlarged stamen figures below follow the botanical convention of the day.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Carneus
description: Gladiolus carneus on a stem that bends at mid-height, carrying about five white flowers flushed faintly rose in the upper portions, arranged in two near-opposite ranks above narrow ribbed leaves. The source text notes this as a variety distinct from an earlier plate of the same name; Redouté drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacées (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Lineatus
description: A flowering stalk of Gladiolus lineatus from the Iridaceae, its veined funnel-shaped blooms set in a spike above sword-shaped leaves. The plate appears in the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812), stipple-engraved in colour and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Refractus
description: Gladiolus refractus grows from an oval tuber, its linear leaves in two opposite ranks below a doubly bent branching scape that carries a small number of stalkless flowers per branch. The flowers, yellowish-green at the throat with violet markings, are twisted so that the convex side faces downward. This plate appears in the seventh volume of Les Liliacées (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Strictiflorus
description: Gladiolus strictiflorus, with spirally twisted lance-shaped leaves in two opposite ranks and a fairly loose spike of dark flowers around the scape. The botanist A.P. de Candolle and others supplied the descriptive text printed beside Redoute's plates. From the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Tubiflorus
description: Gladiolus tubiflorus grows from an ovoid brown bulb, its sword-shaped pleated leaves clasping the hairy scape, which divides into four or five branches of crowded two-ranked flowers. The hairy three-valved spathe is shown enlarged below. From the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Watsonius
description: Gladiolus watsonius rises on a slender, arched stem with stiff, glaucous leaves grooved on each face, carrying two scarlet flowers veined in yellow and spotted within. The plate belongs to the iris family in Jussieu's arrangement; Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Hæmanthus Albiflos
description: Haemanthus albiflos, a thick hairy scape inclining under the weight of a dense white umbel whose orange anthers project on long filaments from a spathe of green-veined bracts, set beside a pair of broad tongue-shaped leaves emerging from a rounded bulb. Floral dissection details are shown separately. Redouté drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacées (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Heliconia Humilis
description: Heliconia humilis, its banana-like sheathing petioles forming the stem and supporting broad lanceolate leaves, with a spike of boat-shaped spathes set in two opposite ranks. The plate belongs to the Bananiers family in Jussieu's order, drawn for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Cristata
description: Iris cristata, a small species with creeping leafy runners and a triple crest along the outer perigon segments, each bearing a yellow blotch ringed in violet. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812); the dissection figures enlarge the flower's parts in the convention of the day.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Flavescens
description: Iris flavescens, with sword-shaped pleated leaves and three or four yellowish-white flowers grouped at each branch tip, the outer segments bearded and veined in violet-purple at the base. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Pallida
description: Iris pallida, a tall species rising to a metre or more from a knotted rootstock, with glaucous falcate leaves and large pale blue scented flowers. The outer segments are bearded with white-and-yellow filaments and shade to lilac-violet; Redoute drew it for the seventh volume (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Sibirica
description: A slender small-flowered form of Iris sibirica, its thin scape carrying two flowers from a terminal spathe above narrow bright-green leaves; the falls are pale lilac, yellow at the base with violet veins. Candolle treated it as a variety of the Siberian iris though possibly a distinct species. Plate 420, Les Liliacees, 1812.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Squalens
description: Iris squalens on a branching stem, its outer falls purple toward the tip and yellowish at the base with purple veins, the midline bearded with yellow filaments tipped purple. Candolle records that some botanists treated it as a mere variety of the elder-scented iris. Plate 365, Les Liliacees, 1812.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Grandiflora
description: Ixia grandiflora, the large-flowered corn lily of the iris family, set on its slender flowering stem. This plate appeared in the seventh volume of Les Liliacees, issued in 1812. The plates were stipple engravings printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Secunda
description: Ixia secunda gathers about eight flowers into a one-sided spike, the three outer violet-blue segments entire and the inner three paler and notched. The slender flexuous scape is covered in very short hairs that make it appear downy. The plate comes from the seventh volume of Les Liliacees, issued in 1812.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: John Eardley Wilmot
description: Lawyer John Eardley Wilmot sits at a writing desk, a quill in hand and an allegorical group of dispossessed American Loyalists behind him on the wall. West painted the 1812 canvas as a homage to Wilmot, who had chaired the British commission that compensated refugees from the Revolution, the picture-within-a-picture summarising the sitter's public service.

title: Kaempferia Angustifolia
description: Kaempferia angustifolia rises from a cluster of fleshy spindle-shaped tubers to two or three ovate-lanceolate leaves, the flowers borne between their bases. The French text credits its introduction to Willdenow, from the Berlin garden catalogue. The plate places it in the ginger family, Monandria monogynia of the Linnaean system.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Lilium Pumilum
description: Lilium pumilum, a miniature of the pompon and Chalcedonian lilies but with glabrous leaves, growing barely two decimetres from a white scaly bulb. Its single pendent scarlet flower has six lanceolate segments rolled back. The plate belongs to the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Lilium Tigrinum
