description: Lilium tigrinum, the tiger lily, its tall woolly stem bearing scattered linear-lanceolate leaves with small black bulbils in their axils. The red-orange flowers are spotted purple inside and reflexed. The plate belongs to the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812); this young plant carried a single flower.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Major-General Henry Dearborn
description: Henry Dearborn, the Jefferson-era Secretary of War newly returned to active command at the outbreak of the War of 1812, sits in dark blue uniform with gold epaulets. Stuart painted him in 1812; the canvas entered the Art Institute of Chicago as accession 1913.793.

title: Massonia Angustifolia
description: Massonia angustifolia, a Cape bulb bearing two fleshy leaves and a stemless cluster of flowers half-hidden between their bases, each with a whitish tube and six narrow recurved lobes. The botanist de Candolle and others supplied the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plates.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Massonia Violacea
description: Massonia violacea, a small bulb with two opposed basal leaves and a short central scape carrying slender pedicels of lilac-violet flowers, each a funnel of six recurved lobes. The plate dissection figures at the foot of the sheet enlarge the stamens and seed, a botanical convention of the period.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Medeola Angustifolia
description: Medeola angustifolia, a slender climbing vine to about two metres, its scattered narrow leaves and small terminal clusters of six-parted flowers, the outer segments greenish and the inner whitish. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Muscari Botryoides
description: Muscari botryoides, with firm linear channelled leaves and one or two scapes bearing a near-cylindrical raceme of almost spherical bright-blue flowers, each rimmed by six small white recurved teeth. The plate dissection figures below enlarge the black heart-shaped anthers and ovary.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Narcissus Biflorus
description: Narcissus biflorus, the two-flowered daffodil, its scape carrying a pair of whitish blooms above narrow grey-green leaves, with the enlarged stamen and seed figures at the foot of the sheet. Long confused with the poet's narcissus until Curtis fixed its distinguishing characters; Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Narcissus Calathinus
description: A variety of Narcissus calathinus, two nodding flowers on unequal stalks above narrow dark-green leaves, the white perianth segments faintly tinged yellow and turned up around a bell-shaped crown. De Candolle and others supplied the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plates; this one appeared in the seventh volume (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Narcissus Pumilus
description: Narcissus pumilus, the dwarf daffodil, here described as a small undescribed garden species, a solitary small white flower on a short flattened scape above few glaucous linear leaves. De Candolle and others supplied the text accompanying Redoute's plates; this one appeared in the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Neottia Speciosa
description: Neottia speciosa, an orchid with fusiform tubers and oval-lanceolate leaves giving a tall reddish stem topped by a raceme of rose-pink flowers, set among pale-rose bracts of the same colour. From the orchid family in Jussieu's classification; Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ornithogalum Lacteum
description: Ornithogalum lacteum, its strap-shaped fleshy leaves below a dense raceme of milk-white flowers that open from a cone into a near-cylinder. Each segment carries a small green basal spot, and the stamens run half the length of the perianth. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ornithogalum Trigynum
description: Ornithogalum trigynum, growing from an apricot-sized bulb to soft trailing leaves and a long cylindrical raceme of many flowers, whitish above and pale green beneath. Unusually for the group it has three styles, reflected in its Linnaean class on the plate. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Pancratium Amboinense
description: Pancratium amboinense, unusual in the genus for its broad heart-based stalked leaves rather than strap-like ones, with a scape carrying an umbel of about a dozen small white flowers in a two-valved spathe. This Amaryllis-family species was drawn for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Pancratium Declinatum
description: Pancratium declinatum, here flowering nearly year-round with twelve to twenty faintly fragrant white flowers in a terminal umbel above broad pointed leaves. A funnel-shaped nectary with twelve teeth unites the awl-shaped filaments. This second plate of the species appeared in the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Pancratium Fragrans
description: Pancratium fragrans, with about a dozen bright-green tapering stalked leaves and a flattened two-edged scape bearing four to six stalkless white flowers, the limb cut into narrow channelled segments. A funnel-shaped six-toothed nectary unites the stamens. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Pancratium Speciosum
description: Pancratium speciosum, its numerous white flowers cut nearly to the green tube into six narrow recurved lobes, set above dark green ovate-lanceolate leaves on a sharply flattened scape. This plate appeared in the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812). The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Peliosanthes Teta
description: Peliosanthes teta, its lance-shaped strongly veined leaves rising from thick fibrous roots, with a long raceme of small bluish flowers clustered in groups of four or five along the scape. The funnel-shaped perianth has a transverse hexagonal partition across the tube's mouth. The plate appeared in the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Sagittaria Ovata
description: Plate 411 shows Sagittaria ovata, its long-stalked oval leaves rising from the water beneath a loose pyramidal panicle of three-whorled monoecious flowers, male blooms above and female below. The classification line places it in the Alismataceae, the water-plantain family.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Teignmouth Harbour
description: Teignmouth Harbour at sunset: two cattle and a wading figure occupy the shallow foreground, while a large ship's timber frame under construction dominates the right bank. In the middle distance the estuary opens toward the town, its masts and buildings dissolved in golden haze. Painted in 1812, the work is now at Petworth House in the care of the National Trust.

title: The Charging Chasseur
dateCreated: 1812 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A mounted officer of Napoleon's Imperial Guard wheels his rearing grey horse against a smoke-streaked battlefield sky, sabre drawn and leopard-skin saddle cloth billowing. Géricault's Salon debut of 1812, made when the artist was twenty-one, announced a new Romantic energy in French painting through Rubensian colour and a kinetic diagonal that broke decisively from Davidian decorum.

title: The Geography Lesson
description: The paymaster Monsieur Gaudry instructing his daughter at a globe and map, the cartouche of which carries a sphinx and pyramid recalling Napoleon's Egyptian campaign. Oil on canvas, 73.6 by 59 cm, in the Kimbell Art Museum, Fort Worth, shown at the Salons of 1812 and 1814. The fine interior detail draws on the seventeenth-century Dutch genre pictures Boilly collected.

title: Veratrum Nigrum
description: Veratrum nigrum, the black hellebore, its metre-high stem bearing pleated leaves and a very long raceme of small flowers, each segment a blackish purple with a bright basal spot. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812); the dissection figures show the stamens at the petal base.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Yucca Aliofolia
description: Yucca aloifolia, the aloe-leaved yucca, its woody trunk topped by a dense rosette of stiff spine-tipped leaves and a tall branched panicle of pendent flowers. Redoute drew it for the seventh volume of Les Liliacees (1812); the text records stems reaching three or four metres.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gothic Cathedral by the Water
description: A vast Gothic cathedral towers over a riverside town at sunset, its silhouette dwarfing the mortal traffic on the quay. The motif of the imagined medieval Dom appealed to Romantic painters as both architectural dream and patriotic emblem after the Napoleonic Wars.
credit: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

title: Morning
description: A grove of mature deciduous trees crowns a rounded hill, their canopies opening toward a luminous sky that suggests the pale light of morning. A few small figures linger at the hill's foot to the right, giving scale to the landscape without competing with the tranquil mood. Schinkel painted this canvas in 1813; titled Morning, it is held at the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin.

title: (Barcelona) Apullia in Search of Appullus 1814 - William Turner - Tate Britain
description: An early classical landscape by J. M. W. Turner, exhibited at the British Institution and pointedly modelled on Claude Lorrain to challenge the older master's reputation. Sunlit foliage, distant temples and a literary Ovidian subject mark Turner's ambition to inherit the grand European pastoral tradition.

title: Agave Spicata
description: Agave spicata, its stiff dark-green channelled leaves topped by a short crowded spike of fifteen to twenty greenish flowers with long protruding stamens. The supplied text places it in the bromeliad family (Broméliées); enlarged floral parts appear at the foot of the sheet.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Albuca Fastigiata
description: Albuca fastigiata, a knotty green bulb throwing up ribbon-like channelled leaves and a central stalk crowned with a pyramidal raceme of twelve to fifteen flowers. The plate is from the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacees, issued in 1814.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Alisma Plantago
description: Alisma plantago, the common water-plantain, its ovate-pointed basal leaves on long petioles below a tall pyramidal panicle of whorled branches. The plates were printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate, then finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Allium Sulcatum
description: Allium sulcatum, the grooved garlic, with broad flat leaves and stiff triangular scapes ribbed and furrowed along their angles, ending in a tight umbel of snow-white scentless flowers. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814); the bulb is reddish-brown and hazelnut-sized.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Atamasco
description: A fruiting Amaryllis atamasco, drawn to record the seed capsule the earlier plate had lacked, with a smaller flower tinged rose outside and a short scape bent under the three-celled pod. The capsule splits into three valves holding black seeds. Plate 454 appeared in the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Brasiliensis
description: Amaryllis brasiliensis, its ribbon-like distichous leaves curving back in a half-circle and a violet-streaked hollow scape carrying four crimson flowers from a two-valved spathe. The ovate-lanceolate segments are thick and greenish at the claw. Plate 469 closes the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Humilis
description: Amaryllis humilis, a low plant with a fascicle of four or five narrow ribbon leaves and a slender scape bearing six or seven flowers in an umbel. The perigon opens irregularly into linear-lanceolate segments, wavy and recurved above the claw. Plate 450 belongs to the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Pallida
description: Amaryllis pallida, its umbel of five bell-shaped flowers nodding on unequal three-sided stalks, the white segments washed rose along the margins and back. The leaves appear only after the flowers, once the scape has withered. The botanical descriptions accompanying Redoute's plates were supplied by de Candolle and others.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Amaryllis Reticulata
description: Amaryllis reticulata, its tongue-shaped leaves marked with conspicuous longitudinal veins and a compressed glaucous scape carrying four pendent funnel flowers. The wide-spreading limb is yellowish within, the segments separating well above the ovary. Plate 424 belongs to the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Anthericum Longiscapum
description: Anthericum longiscapum, several tufts of fleshy half-cylindrical leaves on a short reddish trunk, with tall slender scapes carrying racemes of brown-and-yellow flowers. Redoute drew it for the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacees (1814); the enlarged floral parts follow botanical convention.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Aphyllanthes Monspeliensis
description: Aphyllanthes monspeliensis, forming small tufts of nearly leafless rush-like stems, each striped stem topped by one or two deep blue flowers wrapped in russet papery bracts. The classification places it among the rushes; Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Aristea Cyanea
description: Aristea cyanea, with compressed sword-shaped leaves in fans and an angular stem ending in heads of blue six-parted flowers, each bloom set in an involucre of fringed bracts. The plate, from the eighth volume of Les Liliacées (1814), shows the plant with its characteristic three stamens, fibre-like filaments, and bilocular anthers as described in the accompanying botanical text.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Asparagus Amarus
description: Asparagus amarus, a slender asparagus with pyramidal panicled branches bearing white triangular stipules and small drooping yellow-green bell-flowers in pairs or threes at each node. The plate belongs to the eighth volume of Les Liliacées (1814); the source description notes that new shoots of this species never exceed the thickness of an ordinary writing quill.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Asparagus Sarmentosus
description: Asparagus sarmentosus, a climbing twining species reaching several metres, with slender short branches above a sharp spur and narrow leaves bearing tiny marginal teeth. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814); the small flowers come in short racemes.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Asparagus Tenuifolius
description: Asparagus tenuifolius, long treated as a variety of common asparagus, with a pale green stem zig-zagging at the branch joints and threadlike leaves bunched fifteen to thirty together. The pendulous bell-flowers grow singly or in pairs; the plate belongs to the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Asparagus Tricarinatus
description: Asparagus tricarinatus, a hard woody climber rising to about five feet, with branches springing from apparent rosettes of six or seven leaves, the leaves and branch tips awl-shaped and bearing three grooves and three keels. Redouté drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacées (1814), placing it among the twining asparagus species that close out the series.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Asphodelus Tauricus
description: Asphodelus tauricus, with cylindrical spindle-shaped roots and tufts of glaucous awl-shaped leaves, the single flowering stem rising beside sterile leaf-clusters to an elongated raceme of bracted flowers. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Bromelia Ananas
description: Bromelia ananas, the cultivated pineapple, its broad spiny-edged leaves spreading at ground level and its flowers packed into a dense terminal cone topped by the familiar crown of foliage. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand, with enlarged figures of the six stamens and pistil at the foot of the sheet.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Bromelia Karatas
description: Bromelia karatas, its stiff leaves nearly two metres long and armed along the margins with hooked brown spines, the flowers crowded into a globular head among coloured bracts. Redoute drew it for the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacees (1814), part of the bromeliad group the work includes despite its title.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: colchicum alpinum
description: Colchicum alpinum, the alpine meadow saffron, one or two rose-coloured flowers on slender tubes rising from a bulb, the six segments veined and spotted with violet. The text notes the linear-lanceolate leaves appear at a different season than the flowers; Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Colchicum Autumnale
description: Colchicum autumnale, the autumn crocus shown here in a broad-leaved form, its bell-opening flowers borne from a tubular spathe that lengthens to reach the soil surface. Redoute placed it in the Colchicaceae; the work was issued in eight folio volumes between 1802 and 1816.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Commelina Periscariæfolia
description: Commelina persicariaefolia, named for a leaf resembling that of the persicaria, its ovate-lanceolate blades rising from ciliate tubular sheaths on upright stems. The flowers emerge in clusters at the stem tips, each group held in a folded heart-shaped spathe with pale blue inner segments.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Curcuma Longa
description: Plate 473 shows Curcuma longa, the turmeric, its sheathing petioles forming an upright stem with broad lance-shaped leaves and a loose pale-green cone of imbricate bracts holding the flowers. The plate closes the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814), in the Cannaceae of Jussieu.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Drimia Elata
description: Drimia elata rising from a scaly greenish bulb half out of the soil, its bare scape carrying a loose raceme of pendent flowers above narrow glaucous leaves. The text places it in the asphodel family; the enlarged stamen figures below follow the period's botanical convention. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: El Tres de Mayo
description: A Spanish patriot in a luminous white shirt flings out his arms before the firing squad of Napoleonic troops on Príncipe Pío hill. Commissioned after the French withdrawal, Goya treats martyrdom with the brutal lighting and crude paint of modern history painting.
credit: This file was derived from: El Tres de Mayo, by Francisco de Goya, from Prado in Google Earth.jpg :

title: Ferraria Ferrariola
description: Ferraria ferrariola, with a fibrous root and a simple leafy stem ending in clustered flowers held within a green two-valved spathe. The text contrasts it with the tuberous, fetid-flowered Ferraria undulata of plate 28; this scentless iris-family species appeared in the eighth volume (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Furcræa Gigantea
description: Furcraea gigantea, a giant agave-like plant with stiff, lance-shaped, toothed leaves and a towering flowering stalk bearing an immense panicle of more than a thousand greenish-white flowers. The plate appeared in the eighth volume (1814) of Les Liliacées, drawn by Pierre-Joseph Redouté.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Gladiolus Gracilis
description: Gladiolus gracilis, a slender glabrous plant with linear sheathing leaves and usually two pale-violet flowers whose throats are marked inside with white spots or dots. Drawn by Pierre-Joseph Redouté, the plate appeared in the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacées (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Hedychium Coronarium
description: Hedychium coronarium, a tall leafy stem with distichous oblong leaves and a terminal spike whose flowers carry a broad heart-notched lip. The plate places it among the Balisiers in Jussieu's order; Redoute drew it for the eighth and last volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Hokusai Manga 01
description: A page from the first volume of the Hokusai Manga, the artist's sprawling printed sketchbooks that catalogue figures, animals, landscapes, and curiosities. Issued from 1814, the volumes circulated widely as drawing manuals and later became a key conduit of Japanese form into European art.
credit: Michener, James A. (1958) Hokusai Sketchbooks: Selections from the Manga , Rutland, Vermont & Tokyo: Charles E. Tuttle Company

title: Hyacinthus Orientalis
description: Hyacinthus orientalis, the garden hyacinth, its bulb sending up strap-shaped leaves and a hampe with a loose raceme of funnel-form flowers, the segments reflexed and ribbed. Redoute drew it for the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacees (1814), printed in colour and hand-finished.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Sibirica
description: Iris sibirica on a tall hollow stem, its narrow sword-shaped leaves nearly as long as the stalk and two or three pedicelled flowers with white-margined outer segments and erect inner ones. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814), the descriptive text supplied by Candolle and his colleagues.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Sisyrinchium
description: A pale-violet form of Iris sisyrinchium on a wiry rush-like stem barely a decimetre high, the lilac falls marked near the claw with a white and yellowish patch and the inner segments lanceolate. The plate belongs to the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814); enlarged figures of the flower parts sit at the foot of the sheet.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Iris Triflora
description: Plate 481 shows Iris triflora, forming dense low tufts of bright green, its leaf-sheaths each enclosing about three blue white-veined flowers that open one after another. The descriptive text for Les Liliacees was supplied by Candolle and others; this plate appeared in the eighth volume, 1814.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Candida
description: Ixia candida grows from a flattened orbicular bulb, its few sword-shaped leaves sheathing the lower stem below a sparse pyramidal raceme of ten or twelve flowers between whitish scarious bracts. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand; from the eighth volume of Les Liliacees, 1814.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Crispa
description: Ixia crispa on a hand-high flexuous stem with three or four alternate flowers, its narrow awl-shaped leaves crisped and symmetrically frilled either side of a transparent midrib, the tips twisting into a tendril. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814), the botanical text supplied by Candolle and others.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Phlogiflora
description: Ixia phlogiflora bears phlox-like flowers in two ranks along a slightly zigzag axis, all turning to one side as they open. The sword-shaped leaves curve like a sickle, with cartilaginous translucent veins. The descriptive text accompanying Redoute's plates was supplied by botanists of the day.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Radiata
description: Ixia radiata shows a one-sided terminal spike, the outer segments veined with purple and reflexed when the flower is fully open, the inner three concave and white. The plate comes from the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacees, issued in 1814. A dissection of the ovary and three stigmas sits below.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Rapunculoïdes
description: Ixia rapunculoides carries ten or eleven lilac bell-shaped flowers in a pyramidal raceme atop a slender, half-transparent scape. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814). The branches curve upward at their base, then run almost horizontal.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ixia Viridiflora
description: Ixia viridiflora bears its distinctive green flowers in a long terminal spike, sessile in the axils of translucent spathes streaked with rust-coloured markings. The linear, sword-shaped leaves carry five pale veins, and the segments of the flower are each marked at the base with a deep dark blotch. The plate belongs to the eighth volume of Les Liliacées, published in 1814.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Lilium Tigrinum
description: Lilium tigrinum drawn again in maturity, taller and many-flowered, its stem producing pea-sized purple-brown bulbils in the leaf axils that root readily. De Candolle's text traces it to the gardens of China and Japan. This second plate appeared in the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Medeola Asparagoïdes
description: Medeola asparagoides, a twining climber of one to one and a half metres with short two-ranked branches, glossy bright-green ovate leaves, and pendent bell-shaped flowers of six greenish-white segments. Many specimens drawn for the work were grown in Empress Josephine's gardens at Malmaison.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Musa Paradisiaca
description: Musa paradisiaca, the cultivated banana, its herbaceous trunk of sheathed leaf-stalks rising four to five metres to a crown of six or seven huge leaves up to two metres long. Redoute drew it for the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Narcissus Dubius
description: Narcissus dubius, the doubtful daffodil, named by Gouan for the difficulty of separating it from the white-flowered forms of Narcissus tazetta, here showing three to six snow-white blooms above glaucous linear leaves. Redoute drew it for the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Narcissus Intermedius
description: Narcissus intermedius, named for standing between the jonquil and the scented daffodils, carrying one to four fragrant yellow flowers above channelled dark-green leaves. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814); the crown sits about four times shorter than the spreading perianth segments.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Narcissus Lætus
description: Narcissus laetus, the glad daffodil, long confused with the scented narcissus it closely resembles, separated by Salisbury for its smaller flower and a crown cut rather than left whole. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814), a stipple engraving printed in colour and hand-finished.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Narcissus Minor
description: Narcissus minor, the lesser daffodil, a single flower on a short scape above glaucous snowdrop-like leaves, its inner crown cylindrical and frilled with six wavy lobes. From the Narcisse family in Jussieu's classification; the enlarged stamen and seed figures below follow the period's botanical convention.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Narcissus Radiatus
description: Narcissus radiatus, a rounded bulb giving linear grooved leaves and a smooth scape ending in two flowers, the six oval-pointed segments spread wheel-like around a very short crenate cup. From the Narcisse family in Jussieu's system; Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Narcissus Tenuifolius
description: Narcissus tenuifolius, the slender-leaved daffodil, close to the hoop-petticoat but smaller throughout, a single golden scentless flower above thread-like dark-green leaves with a protruding style. From the Narcisse family in Jussieu's classification; Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ophiostachys Virginica
description: Ophiostachys virginica, a dioecious plant with a rosette of elliptic basal leaves, shown here as both male and female specimens. The male plant bears a sparse greenish raceme resembling those of weld; the female plant a denser white spike of smaller, more closely set flowers. The plate places it in the Colchicaceae; Redouté drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacées (between 1814 and 1816).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ophrys Lilifolia
description: Ophrys lilifolia, the lily-leaved orchid, two oval keeled basal leaves and a bare scape carrying a loose raceme of about twenty-five flowers, the outer segments greenish-violet and the broad lip pale violet. From the orchid family in Jussieu's system; the dissection figures below enlarge the column and anther after the day's botanical convention.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ornithogalum Aureum
description: Ornithogalum aureum, the golden star-of-Bethlehem, a cylindrical scape bearing a crowded raceme of orange-yellow flowers, the six segments striped lengthwise and green at the base beneath. From the asphodel family in Jussieu's classification; Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Ornithogalum Pyramidale
description: Ornithogalum pyramidale, its drooping pale-green leaves below a tall scape bearing a conical raceme of flowers, white within and green outside with white margins. The plates of Les Liliacées were printed by stipple engraving and finished by hand, the technique Redouté employed throughout all eight folio volumes. This plate appeared in the eighth and final volume (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Pancratium Parviflorum
description: Pancratium parviflorum, with pale-green channelled leaves and a flattened two-edged scape bearing six small star-opening flowers, the white segments marked by a broad green stripe outside. This small-flowered Amaryllis-family species closed out the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Phormium Tenax
description: Phormium tenax, the New Zealand flax, its tough sword-shaped leaves spread fan-wise like an iris below a tall branched flowering stem reaching two metres. The leaves split lengthwise into strong fibres, their margins cartilaginous and orange-red. Redoute drew it for the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Scilla Campanulata
description: Plate 435 shows Scilla campanulata, the bell-flowered squill, its lanceolate arching leaves below a slightly conical raceme of twelve to twenty pale-blue bell-shaped flowers, each pedicel set with two coloured bracts. It appeared in the eighth and final volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Scilla Pomeridiana
description: Scilla pomeridiana, with a large fibrous-coated bulb and lanceolate leaves bearing a prodigious quantity of very fine white points on their surface, the branching stem rising to about one metre and carrying widely spaced pale white-pink flowers along divergent branches nearly at right angles. Redouté drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacées (1814–1816).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: The Second of May 1808 or The Charge of the Mamelukes
description: Madrileños with knives drag Mamluk cavalrymen of the imperial guard from their rearing horses in the Puerta del Sol. Companion to The Third of May, Goya's painting reconstructs the chaos of the popular uprising against Napoleon's occupation in tumbling diagonals.
credit: Museo del Prado, Madrid

title: Tulipa Cornuta
description: Tulipa cornuta, a tall slender tulip whose six narrow segments draw out into long horn-like points, the bud forming a sharp inverted cone before opening. The plate places it among the Liliaceae of Jussieu; Redoute drew it for the eighth and last volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Tulipa Gesneriana
description: Tulipa gesneriana var. dracontia, the dragon tulip, its large solitary terminal flower carried on a stout smooth stem above three broad half-clasping leaves; the six petals are deeply lacerated along their margins, giving the bloom its distinctive feathered appearance in yellow banded with red. A small schematic of the bulb appears to the lower left. Redouté drew this variety for the eighth volume of Les Liliacées (1814), and the accompanying text describes the annual renewal of the bulb through offsets on a common basal plate.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Tulipa Gesneriana
description: Tulipa gesneriana, the garden tulip, its single large terminal flower of six vivid yellow petals streaked with broad converging red bands, rising above three oblong half-clasping leaves on a smooth stem. The source text notes that the varieties of this species are too numerous to catalogue in full. Redouté drew this yellow-and-red variety for the eighth volume of Les Liliacées (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Veltheimia Glauca
description: Veltheimia glauca, its short ovoid spike of pendent flesh-coloured flowers carried on a scape above glaucous channelled leaves. The plate notes the three-winged seed capsule, each cell holding two seeds. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Veratrum Album
description: Veratrum album, the white hellebore, its tall stem set with broad pleated alternate leaves and topped by a long branching raceme of small pale greenish-yellow flowers whose segments are marked with darker green veins on a pale ground. Redouté drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacées (1814); the botanical text describes the plant's fistular stem, its many-nerved leaves, and the dimorphic stamens whose filaments are inserted opposite the perianth divisions.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Witsenia Corymbosa
description: Witsenia corymbosa, a shrubby iris-family plant whose angular stem bears fans of stiff sword-shaped leaves and flowers gathered in a corymb, each pair enclosed in a multi-valved spathe. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814), the stem ringed with scars where old leaves have fallen.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Witsenia Maura
description: Witsenia maura, its shrubby jointed stem bearing distichous fan-arranged leaves and short spikes of paired flowers set among overlapping ovoid scales. The text notes its close kinship to Witsenia corymbosa within the iris family. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Zigadenus Glaberrimus
description: Zigadenus glaberrimus, its triangular two-to-three-foot stem rising from a creeping rootstock and ending in a pyramidal panicle of wheel-shaped flowers with six spreading lance-shaped segments. The classification line places it among the rushes. Redoute drew it for the eighth volume of Les Liliacees (1814).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: 1815 Schinkel Mittelalterliche Stadt an einem Fluss anagoria
description: An imagined medieval city rises in tiers of Gothic spires above a river, lit by a low theatrical sun. Schinkel uses architecture as nationalist allegory in the wake of the Napoleonic wars, the cathedral silhouette standing in for a recovered German past.

title: Gothic Church on a Rock by the Sea
description: A spired Gothic cathedral rises atop a cliff above the sea, more vision than topography. The motif - architecture as sacred outcropping - belongs to the shared Romantic imagination of Schinkel and Friedrich, where the medieval church stands in for a yearned-for unity of faith, nation and landscape.

title: Henry Rice
description: A young man in a dark coat and full white cravat is depicted in three-quarter bust against a plain dark ground, his ruddy complexion and brown hair rendered with the fluid brushwork characteristic of Gilbert Stuart. Painted around 1815 and attributed to Stuart, the portrait reflects his command of the New England mercantile sitter type in his later career.

title: Hokusai Manga 02
description: Another page from the Hokusai Manga, the encyclopedic woodblock sketch compendium that eventually ran to fifteen volumes. The loose, observational lines were intended as study material for students, though they read today as a portrait of Edo's everyday visual world.
credit: Michener, James A. (1958) Hokusai Sketchbooks: Selections from the Manga , Rutland, Vermont & Tokyo: Charles E. Tuttle Company

title: Painting for a stage design for Mozart's opera Magic Flute
englishTitle: Stage Set for The Magic Flute: The Hall of Stars (Queen of the Night)
description: The Queen of the Night appears on a crescent moon beneath a vast hemispherical vault of stars, in Karl Friedrich Schinkel's set design for Mozart's Die Zauberflote. The gouache on paper, about 46 by 61 centimetres, was made around 1815 for the production staged at the Berlin Royal Opera in 1816 and is held in the Kupferstichkabinett of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin. The starry hall became the most reproduced of Schinkel's stage designs and one of the most famous opera sets of the nineteenth century.
credit: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

title: The Eruption of the Soufrière Mountains in the Island of St Vincent
description: A volcanic eruption blazes against a night sky, the summit of the Soufrière bursting with incandescent orange and gold light that reflects across the dark water below. Small dark forms — rocks or boats — punctuate the foreground, but the composition is dominated by the eruptive column and its radiant halo. Painted in 1815 to record the eruption of 30 April 1812, the work is held by the University of Liverpool.

title: Benjamin Franklin Drawing Electricity from the Sky
description: Benjamin Franklin sits on a cloud, surrounded by putti operating the kite-and-key apparatus of his 1752 lightning experiment, while a thunderhead breaks overhead. West painted the apotheosis around 1816 in London, knowingly framing his late countryman as a deified Promethean figure in the manner of Rubens or Reni.

title: Constable osmington bay
description: Osmington Bay on the Dorset coast spreads under a sky of broken cumulus, the cliffs running off toward Weymouth. Constable painted the small oil on his 1816 honeymoon at the village of Osmington, where the rector John Fisher had married him to Maria Bicknell that October.
credit: Unknown Unknown

title: Flatford Mill
description: A view from a footbridge on the Stour, with a barge being unhitched in the foreground beneath open Suffolk sky. Painted largely en plein air on Constable's family land, the picture exemplifies the truth-to-nature creed that underpinned his six large 'Stour' canvases.
credit: Tate Britain

title: Maria Bicknell
description: An intimate portrait of the painter's fiancée, completed shortly before their long-resisted marriage. Constable, primarily a landscapist, treats her face with a reserved tenderness, the muted palette and soft modelling reflecting the private nature of the commission.

title: Portrait of French politician and soldier Étienne Maurice Gérard
description: General Étienne Maurice Gérard stands in full military dress uniform, medals and decorations prominent on his chest, holding papers in one hand. David painted the portrait in Brussels in 1816, sharing exile with his sitter in the aftermath of the Hundred Days. The canvas, now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, shows Gérard against a red drapery with a landscape beyond.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art

title: Portrait of the Comte de Turenne
description: The Comte de Turenne sits in a black fur-trimmed coat, a small medal ribbon at his lapel, his gaze directed at the viewer, one hand resting on his knee and the other holding gloves. A letter addressed to Brussels lies on the table beside him, suggesting David's exile context. Painted in 1816, the portrait is a characteristic product of David's Brussels years, calm and direct in its characterisation.

title: Portrait of the Comtesse Vilain XIIII and her Daughter Louise
description: The Comtesse Vilain XIIII, identified by the source as Sophie-Louise-Zoé de Feltz (1780–1853), sits in a deep navy velvet dress with white lace frills and a bold orange shawl, her young daughter Marie-Louise standing before her. David painted the double portrait in 1816 during his Belgian exile, one of the most intimate of his late commissions. The neutral interior background is characteristic of his Brussels portrait style.
credit: Not necessary, PD by age.

title: The Temple of Jupiter Panellenius Restored
description: A reconstructed view of the Doric temple on Aegina, imagined intact above the Aegean, painted from sketches supplied by an architect-traveller as Turner himself never visited Greece. The canvas answered the British vogue for Hellenic antiquity stoked by the Elgin Marbles.
credit: Sotheby's Lot.92

title: The Wheat Field
description: Reapers and gleaners work a Suffolk wheat field under a high summer sky, painted on Constable's home ground near East Bergholt in 1816. The canvas, now at the National Gallery of Art in Washington with accession 2007.8.27, dates from the months around his marriage and prefigures the six-foot landscapes he began the following year.

title: Wivenhoe Park
description: A panoramic estate view commissioned by Major-General Francis Slater-Rebow, balancing fishermen, swans, a grazing herd, and the distant house. Constable expanded the canvas at the patron's request to include a lawn and outbuildings, evidence of his pragmatic handling of the country-house genre.

title: Cupid and Psyche
description: Cupid, depicted as an ungainly youth with wings and curly hair, sits beside the sleeping Psyche and turns to smirk at the viewer, his bow resting against the gilded couch below. David inverts the convention of the idealised adolescent god, rendering him as a self-satisfied teenager. Painted in Brussels during the artist's exile and dated 1817, the canvas is now at the Cleveland Museum of Art.

title: Portrait of Emmanuel Joseph Sieyès
description: The abbé Sieyès, theorist of the Third Estate and architect of the Brumaire coup that brought Napoleon to power, sits in dark coat against a plain ground. David painted the portrait in Brussels, where both artist and sitter were exiled after the Bourbon Restoration of 1815.
credit: via commons image Image:Emmanuels.jpg Crop of a portrait by Jacques-Louis David (English) / Jacques-Louis David (spanish)

title: Portrait of Louis David
description: François-Joseph Navez painted this half-length portrait of his teacher Jacques-Louis David in Brussels in 1817, the year Navez joined David in Belgian exile. The sitter is shown in a dark coat with a white cravat and a red boutonnière, his direct gaze conveying the authority of the leading French Neoclassical painter.
credit: Photograph by Rama

title: Raby Castle
description: A house portrait commissioned by the third Earl of Darlington, set in his County Durham deer park with a hunt in the foreground. Turner devotes the upper canvas to a churning, dramatic sky, signalling his shift from topography to Romantic landscape.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Rosa Alba
description: The double white rose, Rosa alba flore pleno, its many-petalled bloom packed above pale foliage. The botanist Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plates for Les Roses.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Alba
description: Rosa alba in its royal form, a very large bloom of many petal ranks in white shading toward flesh-pink, borne several together at the branch tips. The French text likens it to the Cuisse de Nymphe and names it the English maiden's blush.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Alpina
description: Rosa alpina in its smooth form, a four- or five-foot shrub with reddish thornless stems and single flowers of five vivid red petals paling toward the claw, set above doubly toothed leaves. The stems are wholly without prickles, a mark of the Alpine roses noted by Thory.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Alpina
description: Rosa alpina pendulina, its long thornless stems carrying nodding single flowers of five rose-violet petals above oval doubly toothed leaflets, the elongated ovaries curving down after pollination. Redoute drew it for Les Roses; this plate appeared in the 1817 volume.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Arvensis
description: Rosa arvensis, the field rose, a trailing shrub with reddish arching branches and fragrant white flowers gathered at the tips of short side-shoots. The plate notes the fused styles forming a slender central column, distinctive to the species.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Berberifolia
description: Rosa berberifolia, the barberry-leaved rose, a small two-foot shrub with simple alternate leaves and solitary canary-yellow flowers, each petal marked with a purple blotch at the claw. The bristly ovary and lobed calyx appear below the bloom in this 1817 plate.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Bifera
description: A white form of Rosa bifera, the four-seasons rose, its full pale bloom set among toothed foliage. The botanist Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the text that accompanied Redoute's plates for Les Roses.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Bifera
description: Rosa bifera in its perfumers' form, a four- or five-foot bush bearing very fragrant rose-pink flowers of four or five petal ranks above oval toothed leaflets. Known as the Puteaux rose, it was the variety most used in the perfume trade.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Bracteata
description: Rosa bracteata, the Macartney rose, a trailing shrub with slender hairy branches and glossy leaflets, its fragrant white flowers wrapped at the base by overlapping fringed bracts. The petals are broad and heart-notched, tipped with a small point.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Brevistyla
description: Rosa brevistyla, the short-styled rose, a dense six- to eight-foot bush with reddish hooked prickles, its faintly scented yellowish-white flowers borne three or four together in a short corymb. The fused styles rise as one short glabrous column from the centre of the bloom.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Carolina
description: Rosa carolina in its corymb-flowered form, light-pink petals notched at the tip above ovate leaflets and reddish stems with scattered prickles. Claude-Antoine Thory, who wrote the text, treats it as a variety of Michaux's R. caroliniana rather than the species Willdenow named.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Centifolia
description: Rosa centifolia bullata, the cabbage rose with puffed, blistered leaflets that swell and curl back on themselves, above a rounded pink double bloom. Thory records it as the lettuce-leaved rose propagated by the nurseryman Dupont.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Centifolia
description: The Vilmorin rose, a cabbage rose with nearly full flowers of a transparent flesh-pink, borne singly or in twos and threes above light-green woolly-backed leaflets. Thory notes the variety, kept by grafting, was named for the nurseryman who first distributed it.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Centifolia
description: The carnation rose, a cabbage rose variety with a small pink corolla above ovate pointed leaflets, woolly beneath, and stems set with unequal reddish prickles. The variety can be multiplied only by grafting or layering, according to Thory's text.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Centifolia
description: A single-flowered cabbage rose, Rosa centifolia flore simplici, showing five pink petals around a boss of stamens rather than the usual full double bloom. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Centifolia
description: Rosa centifolia in the form called the Unique rose, its full bloom shading from white toward pink across the petals. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Roses, issued in 1817.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Centifolia
description: The hundred-petalled cabbage rose, Rosa centifolia, its rounded bloom packed with rose-pink petals that deepen toward the centre, above doubly toothed dark-green leaflets and bristly ovaries. Thory noted the rose had already been figured by Clusius and earlier botanists.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Cinnamomea
description: Rosa cinnamomea in its May-flowering form, single flowers of five heart-notched petals washed red above ovate leaflets and stems crowded with short prickles below. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine, and Les Roses grew out of her Malmaison collection.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Cinnamomea
description: The cinnamon rose, Rosa cinnamomea, with scented red-tinged single flowers gathered in a corymb above seven-leaflet leaves and smooth flowering shoots. Thory records that it flowers in May and grows wild across southern Europe.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Clynophylla
description: Rosa clynophylla, a smooth climbing shrub whose alternate leaves droop in a marked way, bearing solitary white flowers with petals yellowish toward the claw. The stems and the entire calyx are covered in a short silky whitish down, per Thory's text.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Damascena
description: A damask rose grown as the Portland rose, its faintly scented flowers borne three or four to a branch tip in a loose umbel. The corolla holds two or three rows of deep purple petals notched at the apex, above five or seven oval leaflets. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Damascena
description: The York and Lancaster rose, a damask whose four or five rows of petals are most often white streaked and spotted with pink, the same shrub also throwing all-pink and all-white flowers. The sticky red-glanded stems and calyces are fragrant. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text for the plate.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Damascena
description: The damask rose, Rosa damascena, its five notched petals white faintly washed with pink opening from a deep-red bud, the flowers two or three together in a loose panicle. Hairy glandular pedicels and an elongate pinnatifid calyx complete the sheet, drawn for Les Roses.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Eglanteria
description: Rosa eglanteria in its red form, the Austrian copper known in gardens as the Rose Capucine or Rose d'Autriche, the same plant sometimes bearing yellow and red flowers on one stock. The globular hip stays constant across the species. Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text for the plate.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Eglanteria
description: Rosa eglanteria, a tall rose to twelve feet whose large single flowers carry five jonquil-yellow petals nearly two and a half inches across, the styles tipped with purple stigmas. The crushed leaves smell of ripe apple while the flowers are fetid. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, issued between 1817 and 1824.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Fœtida
description: Rosa foetida, a shrub to six feet whose small near-scentless flowers carry five soft pink petals that the sun quickly fades, usually borne singly. The ovoid orange-red hips give off a fetid smell when crushed. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, issued in folio volumes between 1817 and 1824.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Gallica
description: Rosa gallica versicolor, the striped rose of France, always semi-double and never full, its soft-pink petals streaked with brighter red. The leaves bear seven oblong leaflets downy beneath, and the fruit is round and reddish at maturity. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, which grew out of Empress Josephine's rose collection at Malmaison.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Gallica
description: Rosa gallica as the common Provins rose, its large semi-double flowers of fine purple-red borne singly or in pairs at the branch tips. Oval pointed leaflets sit on bristly petioles set with glands and small hooked prickles. The descriptive text accompanying the plate was written by Claude-Antoine Thory.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Hudsoniana
description: Rosa hudsoniana salicifolia, the willow-leaved Hudson rose, with smooth thornless green stems and narrow leaflets resembling those of the osier willow. Its flowers, gathered in a loose cyme, show five petals of a pretty deep pink, often pointed at the tip. The plate was printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: rosa indica
description: Rosa indica, the China rose described by Linnaeus, forming bushes of about two feet with nearly thornless branches and five simply toothed leaflets. Its solitary flowers show five heart-notched petals ranging from the softest pink to deepest purple. The plate was printed in colour from a single stipple-engraved plate and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Indica
description: Rosa indica cruenta, a Bengal rose, a China cultivar carrying deep crimson flowers above glossy toothed leaflets. Redoute was flower painter to Empress Josephine, whose garden at Malmaison held the most celebrated rose collection of the age, and Les Roses grew out of it. The dissection figures at the foot enlarge the flower's parts.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Indica
description: Rosa indica fragrans, the fragrant China rose, its very large nodding flowers often more than two and a half inches across, a flesh-tinged white that looks almost transparent. The globular ovary and calyx lobes are smooth. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand, the method used across all three volumes.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Indica
description: Rosa indica in its dwarf Bengal form, a low shrub under a foot tall with sparse straight prickles and solitary pink flowers of four or five ranks of notched petals. Thory's text notes it was raised from seed and flowers without pause from mid-May to the first frosts.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Indica Acuminata
description: Rosa indica acuminata, a small China rose of about two feet with leaflets washed a wine tint beneath, its lightly scented solitary flowers carrying five always-pointed petals of white flushed with pink. The long stamens curl back over the styles as in all the India roses. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text for the plate.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Indica Vulgaris
description: Rosa indica vulgaris, the common Indian rose, with smooth green canes four to six feet tall, glossy leaflets and semi-double soft-pink flowers borne several together in a loose panicle. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the botanical text that accompanied the plate.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Kamtchatica
description: Rosa kamtchatica, a two to three foot bush bristling with numerous straight whitish prickles, bearing large fragrant flowers of orange-red tinged violet and rounded red-brown hips. Redoute drew it for Les Roses, which grew out of Empress Josephine's rose collection at Malmaison.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Leucantha
description: Rosa leucantha, a tall leafy bush with strong red hooked prickles and large flowers of five white petals faintly pink at the top, notched at the heart, gathered in a corymb. The plate appeared in the first volume of Les Roses, issued in 1817.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Lucida
description: Rosa lucida, the glossy rose, a thick bush five or six feet high with smooth canes and glossy leaflets, bearing light-pink flowers three or four together in terminal corymbs and flattened globular red hips. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Roses, published in 1817.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Montezumae
description: Rosa montezumae, a wild rose with pink bloom and toothed leaflets on a thorned stem. The plate comes from the first volume of Les Roses, published in 1817; the stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Moschata
description: A semi-double musk rose, its white corolla of three or four ranks of petals above leaflets woolly beneath, differing from the single form only in its fuller flower and sparser prickles. Thory's text recounts the rose's musk scent and its use in distilling attar of roses in the East.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Moschata
description: Rosa moschata, the musk rose, with strong broad hooked prickles, oblong dark-green leaflets and faintly scented white flowers borne in a panicle on slender glandular stalks. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text that accompanied Redoute's plate.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Muscosa
description: A white form of the moss rose, its petals a white washed with very tender pink, otherwise matching the ordinary moss rose in habit and the glandular growth that names it. Thory's text notes the flower is never truly white, despite the name it was given.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Muscosa
description: A very double moss rose, its many ranks of petals crumpled and rolled at the centre, barely showing the spreading styles, the bloom sometimes more than three inches across. The moss-like glandular growth on the calyx names the rose; Claude-Antoine Thory supplied the botanical text.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Muscosa
description: Rosa muscosa, the moss rose, a two to three foot bush with straight prickles, its stalks, hips and pinnatifid calyx lobes bristling with long glandular hairs that look like a mass of moss, the five-petalled light-pink flowers sweetly scented. The plate appeared in the first volume of Les Roses, issued in 1817.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Pimpinellifolia
description: A red double form of Rosa pimpinellifolia, a dense bush about a foot and a half high with rounded leaflets and soft-rose, lightly scented flowers, its small cherry-sized hips ripening from red to black. The corolla varies from five to seven rows of petals. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Roses (1817).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Pimpinellifolia
description: Rosa pimpinellifolia, the burnet rose, reaching three to four feet in cultivation with prickly reddish stems and large fragrant white flowers tinged yellow at the claw. Its black hips hang nodding at maturity. Redoute drew it for the first volume of Les Roses (1817).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Pimpinellifolia
description: A small burnet rose barely a foot high, the plate showing a single shoot cut near the root, its brown stems crowded with straight prickles and bearing white, heart-notched five-petalled flowers that hold a cupped form. The hips ripen from red to black. Claude-Antoine Thory wrote the descriptive text for the plate.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Pomponia
description: Rosa pomponia, the pompon rose, a low branchy bush with five wrinkled grey-green leaflets and sweetly scented double flowers in a pretty rose that deepens toward the centre. The pedicels and calyx carry sticky black stalked glands. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Redutea
description: Rosa redutea in its rubescens form, shown in flower with its foliage on a single sheet. Named for Redoute, the plate appeared in the first volume of Les Roses (1817); it was stipple-engraved, printed in colour, and finished by hand in watercolour.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: rosa redutea glauca
description: Rosa redutea glauca, a shrub to about three feet with glaucous five-part leaves rose-tinged beneath and white petals washed with pink, marked inside with dark red dots and striped outside with reddish bands. The name honours Redoute himself, flower painter to Empress Josephine. The plate was drawn for the first volume of Les Roses (1817).
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Rubiginosa
description: Rosa rubiginosa, the sweetbriar of Crete, shown with its prickled stems and glandular foliage. The stipple engraving was printed in colour from a single plate and finished by hand, the method used across all three volumes of Les Roses.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Rubiginosa
description: Rosa rubiginosa, the sweetbriar, a hedgerow rose to five or six feet with hooked prickles and rough leaflets whose glandular undersides give off a winey scent when crushed. Its flowers gather two to five at the branch tips on bristly stalks. The stipple engraving was printed in colour and finished by hand.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Rubrifolia
description: Rosa rubrifolia, a tall briar reddish and glaucous throughout, its flowers red in bud and opening to greenish-white in clustered heads above oval wine-tinted leaflets. Redoute drew it for Volume 1 of Les Roses, published in 1817.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Sulfurea
description: Rosa sulfurea, the sulphur-yellow rose, its stem set with fine yellowish subulate spines and seven-leaflet wings, the solitary scentless flowers a pale yellow on short smooth stalks. Among its earlier illustrators were Clusius, Besler and Andrews, listed in Thory's text.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Turbinata
description: Rosa turbinata, the Frankfort rose, a shrub whose calyx tube narrows and swells into the shape of a spinning top, below tomentose leaflets and sweet-scented double flowers in small corymbs. The young flower stalks bristle with stiff glandular hairs.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: Rosa Villosa
description: Rosa villosa, the soft-haired apple rose, known by the grey down on its leaflets and the large bristly hips that earned it the name Rosier a Pommes. Its lightly scented flowers carry five heart-notched petals, light red in cultivated plants and dirty white in wild ones.
credit: Restoration by Nicholas Rougeux (c82.net), after Pierre-Joseph Redouté

title: The hiker above the sea of fog
englishTitle: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
description: Seen from behind on a rocky outcrop, the wanderer surveys a swirling fog that swallows the peaks below. Friedrich's signature Rückenfigur device invites the viewer into the figure's vantage, making the landscape an interior as much as a topography of the Elbe Sandstone Mountains.
credit: The photographic reproduction was done by Cybershot800i . ( Diff )

title: 1280px-Théodore Géricault - Evening
description: A monumental Roman aqueduct spans an Italianate river valley at dusk, hill-top towers catching the last light while small figures bathe in the stream below. One of the large decorative landscapes depicting times of day that Géricault painted in 1818, it shows him adopting the heroic, Poussin-derived classical landscape mode at the threshold of Romanticism. The painting is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
commonsUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Théodore Géricault - Evening, Landscape with an Aqueduct.jpg

title: Chelsea Pensioners Reading the Waterloo Dispatch
description: Veterans cluster outside a Chelsea pub as a despatch announcing the victory at Waterloo is read aloud. Commissioned by the Duke of Wellington, Wilkie filled the genre tableau with regimental specificity, prompting crowd-control rails when it was shown at the Royal Academy in 1822.
credit: Apsley House

title: Dort or Dordrecht: The Dort Packet-Boat from Rotterdam Becalmed
description: A glassy Dutch harbour bathed in golden morning light, paying open homage to Aelbert Cuyp, whose paintings Turner studied on his 1817 Low Countries tour. The becalmed packet boat anchors a luminous sky that occupies more than half the canvas.

title: Gate in the Rocks
description: A natural rock arch frames a distant view, conceived as the Nordic pendant to a sunlit Italian landscape. The pairing stages a Romantic dialogue between the sublime German wilderness and the classical south, a polarity that runs through the era's painting and through Schinkel's own architectural imagination.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/s/schinkel/gaterock"

title: John Trumbull
description: The history painter John Trumbull, in a warm brown coat with fur collar and white stock, appears in three-quarter profile. Stuart painted his fellow American in 1818; the canvas is at the Yale University Art Gallery. Trumbull was then engaged on the four Revolutionary War scenes commissioned for the United States Capitol Rotunda.
credit: Yale University Art Gallery http://www.the-athenaeum.org/art/full.php?ID=24891

title: Shah 'Alam
description: The Mughal emperor Shah Alam II hands a scroll to Robert Clive on a raised platform, transferring the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the East India Company. West reconstructed the 1765 Treaty of Allahabad fifty years after the event, recasting a profit-making contract as a regal ceremonial scene for the Company's London directors.
credit: British Library https://www.theguardian.com/world/2015/mar/04/east-india-company-original-corporate-raiders http://searcharchives-beta.bl.uk/permalink/f/ja42l1/IAMS032-003264600

title: The Farewell of Telemachus and Eucharis
description: Telemachus, son of Odysseus, takes leave of the nymph Eucharis on Calypso's island, drawn from Fénelon's didactic novel. David painted the canvas in Brussels for Count Nikolai Demidov; it is now at the Getty Museum and shows the late, softened style of his exile years.

title: The Field of Waterloo
description: Night falls on the battlefield as women search the heaped dead by torchlight, three years after the engagement. Turner had walked the ground himself; the picture quotes Byron's Childe Harold and refuses any patriotic triumph.

title: The Penny Wedding
description: A crowded Scottish wedding feast unfolds in a low-beamed interior, fiddler at the front and dancers, drinkers, and gossips crammed across the canvas. Wilkie's careful Dutch-inspired genre painting helped popularize sentimental rural Scottishness for a Regency audience.
credit: Royal Collection

title: Ingres
description: A painted study from the Ingres atelier, held at La Piscine museum in Roubaix, depicting Angélique nude and chained to a sea-cliff, her long hair flowing and wrists bound to the rock above — the subject taken from Ariosto's Orlando Furioso. Dated 1819, the large-scale canvas (102 by 73.7 cm) reflects Ingres's sustained return to this mythological theme across several decades of his career.
credit: La Piscine [1]

title: Self-Portrait
description: Benjamin West portrays himself in old age wearing a red cloak and black top hat, leaning over a table with a pen in hand. Painted in 1819, the year before his death, it records the American-born artist who succeeded Joshua Reynolds as President of the Royal Academy in 1792 and held the post until the end of his life.

title: The Anger of Achilles
description: Achilles draws his sword on Agamemnon as Iphigenia stands veiled for sacrifice, the four figures pressed into a shallow neoclassical frieze. David completed the picture in Brussels in 1819 and exhibited it the following year; it now hangs at the Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth.

title: The Violinist Niccolò Paganini
description: A pencil portrait of the virtuoso violinist captured during Ingres's years in Rome. The drawing distils Paganini to crisp contour and minimal shading, exemplifying the precise linear style for which Ingres's portrait sketches of musicians and patrons remain prized.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"i/ingres/08ingres"

title: The White Horse
description: The first of Constable's six-foot Stour valley canvases, showing a workhorse ferried across the river on a flat-bottomed barge. Constable elevates everyday East Anglian labor to grand-manner scale, with broken impasto highlights and a damp, atmospheric sky.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — the-white-horse-john-constable/gwFCFr13uZfZSg

title: Брюллов Нарцисс
description: Karl Bryullov's 1819 oil painting depicting the mythological figure of Narcissus, the beautiful youth consumed by his own reflection. Housed in the Russian Museum's Academical Hall, this work exemplifies the Romantic era's fascination with classical mythology and human beauty.

title: Castle by the River
description: A fortified castle commands the bend of a broad river under a luminous, theatrical sky. The composition treats architecture scenographically, the way Schinkel did in his stage designs for Berlin, while the contemplative figures and burnished light belong to the wider Romantic landscape current.

title: Cattle Market before a Large City on a Lake
description: Drovers, riders and townspeople negotiate over cattle on a rise overlooking a Bavarian lake, with a distant city silhouetted under bright clear air. Kobell's crisp draftsmanship and high-keyed Alpine light typify his Biedermeier landscapes.

title: Elizabeth Greenleaf Parsons
description: Elizabeth Greenleaf Parsons in lace cap and dark dress, painted in watercolor on ivory. Goodridge was the leading miniaturist of Federal-era Boston, trained partly by Gilbert Stuart; the portrait belongs to the Harvard Art Museums.
credit: Harvard Art Museums

title: Francis Osborne
description: Francis Osborne, 5th Duke of Leeds, is shown as a young man in white ceremonial robes trimmed with gold lace over a red undergarment, the dress of a Knight of the Garter or similar order. Benjamin West painted the portrait before his death in 1820; it was given to the National Portrait Gallery, London in 1888.

title: Hampstead Heath by John Constable watercolour
description: View looking across the undulating ground of Hampstead Heath, where Constable lived for stretches of his later life. The British Museum sheet, watercolour at 124 by 206 mm, belongs to the artist's sustained engagement with the Heath as a working subject for cloud and weather studies.
credit: British Museum [1]

title: Harwich: The Low Lighthouse and Beacon Hill
description: A breezy view of the Essex coast, with the squat Low Lighthouse anchoring a beach where small figures gather under a luminous, cloud-stacked sky. Constable's skies are scientifically observed, drawing on his sustained study of meteorology in oil sketches.

title: Saturn Devouring His Son
dateCreated: between 1820 and 1823 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: From the Black Paintings Goya applied directly to the walls of his Quinta del Sordo, the titan Cronus tears into one of his children, eyes blazing in a void. The savage handling, sooty palette, and private setting belong to the bleak, late vocabulary now reassembled in the Prado.

title: Susanna and the elders
description: A Neoclassical treatment of the biblical episode in which the chaste Susanna, bathing in her garden, is spied upon by two elders concealed in foliage. The smooth handling of the nude and theatrical contrast of light and shadow reflect the Flemish painter's training in the academic tradition of David.

title: The Spring
description: A standing nude pours water from an urn at her shoulder, an allegory of a freshwater spring. Ingres began the picture in Florence around 1820 and worked at it intermittently for decades; its porcelain-smooth contours epitomise his late Neoclassical ideal of feminine form.

title: Waterloo Bridge
description: Waterloo Bridge seen from the north bank of the Thames, its arches stretching across the river under a broad cloudy sky, with figures and rowing boats in the foreground. Constable worked on the Waterloo subject for nearly two decades, building from studies such as this toward the large 1832 exhibition picture commemorating the bridge's opening on the second anniversary of the battle.

title: 2560px-Jean Louis Théodore Géricault 001
description: Four thoroughbreds stretched into the rocking-horse 'flying gallop' pose then conventional in sporting art, set against a low storm-bruised English sky. Géricault painted it in London, where his fascination with horseflesh and equestrian sport reshaped his late Romantic style.

title: James Madison
description: James Madison in old age, in dark coat against neutral ground, painted years after his presidency ended. Stuart had first taken Madison's likeness in 1804; this late repetition, now at the National Gallery of Art, descends from that earlier sitting.

title: Ritratto della famiglia Begas
