description: A single white-eyed vireo perches on a tall flowering plant in Plate 63 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, the pale iris that gives the bird its name clearly visible beside a small spider rendered nearby. The botanical setting — a slender stem with delicate clustered blooms — gives the composition an airy openness quite different from the denser foliage of many plates. The title reflects the unsettled early-nineteenth-century taxonomy that grouped vireos among the flycatchers.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: White-fronted Goose (Plate 286)
description: A male and female White-fronted Goose are shown together in a marsh setting, both displaying the species' characteristic white facial blaze, barred belly, and pink bill against dark brown-grey plumage. The standing male faces left while the female stretches her wings with a boldly patterned dark flight feather spread. Plate 286 of Birds of America by John James Audubon, engraved and coloured by Robert Havell Jr., held by the University of Pittsburgh.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: White-headed Eagle (Plate 126)
description: An immature Bald Eagle — labelled 'Young' on the plate — depicted in full three-quarter view, its dark brown plumage and mottled tail filling the composition. The plate is among the most imposing in Audubon's double-elephant folio, Birds of America (1827–1838), University of Pittsburgh.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: White-headed Eagle (Plate 31)
description: A Bald Eagle stands over a freshly killed catfish, gripping the pale belly of the prey with one taloned foot. The grim, unsentimental treatment of carrion and predation is characteristic of Audubon's approach to North American raptors.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: White-winged Crossbill (Plate 364)
description: Plate 364 of Audubon's Birds of America shows White-winged Crossbills working the seed-bearing stems of a broadleaf shrub, with crimson males and olive-yellow females arranged to display the species' sexual dimorphism. The crossed mandibles, adapted for extracting seeds, are clearly delineated in profile on several birds. The plate was engraved and hand-coloured for the double elephant folio, published between 1827 and 1838.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: White-winged silvery Gull (Plate 282)
description: Two pale grey-and-white gulls are shown on rocky ground — one leaning forward as if foraging, the other at rest — against a dark cloudy sky. The White-winged Silvery Gull, now known as the Iceland Gull, was among the northern species Audubon documented in the later numbers of Birds of America. Plate 282, engraved and coloured by Robert Havell Jr., is held by the University of Pittsburgh.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Wild Turkey (Plate 1)
description: The opening plate of Birds of America presents a male Meleagris gallopavo striding through cane, painted at Beechwoods Plantation in West Feliciana Parish. The towering double-elephant folio format permitted Audubon to render the bird at life size, with iridescent body plumage built up in layered aquatint.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Wild Turkey (Plate 6)
description: A large female wild turkey strides across grassy ground accompanied by a brood of young poults in Plate 6 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, the plate caption reading 'Female and Young.' The hen's iridescent dark plumage and blue-grey head fill the composition, while the alert, scurrying chicks animate the foreground. The double-elephant folio's full sheet is exploited to show the female near life size, establishing the monumental scale that distinguishes Birds of America from all earlier ornithological publications.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Willow Grous or Large Ptarmigan (Plate 191)
description: A willow ptarmigan male in full summer rufous-and-white plumage stands beside a mottled brown female sheltering a brood of downy chicks on mossy, flower-strewn ground. Plate 191 of John James Audubon's Birds of America captures the species in breeding season, showing male, female, and young together and documenting the feathered legs and feet that are a key adaptation to Arctic conditions.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Wilson's Phalarope (Plate 254)
description: Two Wilson's phalaropes depicted in contrasting poses: one bird in flight displaying the chestnut and rufous tones of breeding plumage, the other crouching near reedy water. Audubon's Plate 254 captures both male and female, their needle-fine bills clearly detailed. Wilson's phalarope is notable among shorebirds for its reversed sex-role display during the breeding season.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Wilson's Plover (Plate 209)
description: Two Wilson's Plovers—identified by the plate label as male and female—are shown on a sandy coastal margin, one standing upright and the other crouching to probe the ground. The species' heavy black bill and single dark breast band are rendered with precision against the pale sandy setting. Plate 209 of Birds of America by John James Audubon, University of Pittsburgh.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Winter Hawk (Plate 71)
description: A Winter Hawk — now understood as an immature red-shouldered hawk — is shown in active flight, stooping to seize a large frog amid a marshy, grass-filled setting. Plate 71 of John James Audubon's Birds of America (1827–1838) records a name once believed to designate a separate species, before juvenile and adult plumages of the red-shouldered hawk were correctly correlated.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Woman with a Parrot
description: A nude woman reclines on richly coloured draperies, with a small parrot nearby at the lower edge of the composition. Painted in 1827, the canvas is a small-scale cabinet work by Delacroix combining the Orientalist interest in luxurious interiors with the Romantic preoccupation with the erotic figure, produced in the same period as his large Salon submission The Death of Sardanapalus.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"d/delacroi/2/202delac"

title: Wood Ibiss (Plate 216)
description: Mycteria americana (wood stork) shown stooping over a log at water's edge, the long decurved bill directed toward the ground and the bare, darkly scaled head characteristic of the species clearly delineated. White body plumage contrasts with black flight feathers, set against a wetland background of cypress and water. Plate 216 of Audubon's Birds of America, published between 1827 and 1838.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Wood Pewee (Plate 115)
description: Plate 115 shows the Eastern Wood-Pewee perched among the blossoms of swamp azalea (then Azalea viscosa, now Rhododendron viscosum). The pairing of small flycatcher and flowering branch is typical of Audubon's union of ornithology and botanical record.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Wood Thrush (Plate 73)
description: Two wood thrushes — male above, female below — perch on a branch of fruiting dogwood (Cornus florida), the bold round breast spots of the lower bird contrasting with the deep rufous upperparts of the upper. Plate 73 of John James Audubon's Birds of America (1827–1838) pairs the species with one of the most characteristic trees of eastern deciduous forest, depicted here in berry-laden autumn condition.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Wood Wren (Plate 179)
description: A single Wood Wren picks its way across a mossy ground-level bank set with red berries and broad botanical leaves in Plate 179 of Birds of America. The bird's tail is raised in the alert posture typical of the family, and its barred brown plumage blends with the earthy setting. The plate was engraved and coloured by Robert Havell Jr. and depicts one male (Troglodytes americanus).
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Worm eating Warbler (Plate 34)
description: Plate 34 of Birds of America depicts two worm-eating warblers — buff-toned birds with bold black head stripes — among fruiting and leafy branches. The lower bird clings horizontally to a twig in the posture characteristic of this ground-foraging species. Engraved, printed, and coloured by Robert Havell, the plate was produced between 1827 and 1838 and is held at the University of Pittsburgh.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow bellied Woodpecker (Plate 190)
description: Two yellow-bellied sapsuckers are shown on a branch laden with dark berries, one perched upright and one in a descending posture, both displaying the red crown and strongly patterned black-and-white head that identify the species. Plate 190 of John James Audubon's Birds of America places the birds in a fruiting tree setting rather than on a trunk.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow Red-poll Warbler (Plate 145)
description: A pair of Yellow Red-poll Warblers perch on a flowering plant bearing yellow daisy-like blooms in Plate 145 of Audubon's Birds of America. The warm brownish-rufous streaking on the crowns and the yellow-tinged underparts are rendered with precision by the colourists working under Robert Havell Jr. in London. The birds are shown in complementary attitudes — one upright and alert, the other at a lower angle — capturing their natural deportment.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow Shank (Plate 288)
description: A single Yellow Shank with bright yellow legs stands among tall grasses at the edge of a wide river, surrounded by moss-draped trees in a richly coloured southern landscape. The species, now called the Greater Yellowlegs, is shown in the wooded wetland setting where Audubon observed it along the coasts and rivers of North America. Plate 288 of Birds of America, engraved and coloured by Robert Havell Jr., held by the University of Pittsburgh.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow Throated Warbler (Plate 85)
description: A single Yellow-throated Warbler perches on a chinquapin branch bearing spiny burrs, the bold yellow throat patch and facial striping rendered from Audubon's life-size study. Plate 85 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, hand-coloured aquatint from the double-elephant folio, held at the University of Pittsburgh.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow-billed Cuckoo (Plate 2)
description: Two Yellow-billed Cuckoos are depicted among the large leaves and ripening fruit of a pawpaw, with a tiger swallowtail butterfly resting on the foliage. The elongated S-curve formed by the birds' bodies became a hallmark of the early Birds of America plates. Plate 2 of Audubon's Birds of America, engraved and coloured by Robert Havell Jr., held by the University of Pittsburgh.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow-breasted Chat (Plate 137)
description: Yellow-breasted chats around a nest set among wild-rose branches bearing soft pink blossoms, with birds shown in flight and perched. Audubon plays the chat's lemon-yellow breast against the pale-pink roses in a composition that integrates bird and habitat. The plate is Plate 137 of Birds of America, held at the University of Pittsburgh.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow-breasted Rail (Plate 329)
description: A Yellow Rail crouches in dense sedges, the buff-and-black striping providing camouflage that made the bird notoriously hard to flush. Audubon's plate is among the earliest detailed depictions of this secretive marsh species.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow-breasted Warbler (Plate 23)
description: A small yellow-breasted warbler perches among slim foliage, its citron underparts and olive back rendered with fine stipple. The plate reflects Audubon's effort to document the still-unsettled nomenclature of North American wood-warblers, several of which were known by names that have since been revised.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow-crown Warbler (Plate 153)
description: Three Yellow-crown Warblers are arranged on an iris plant entwined with a berry-bearing vine in Plate 153 of Birds of America. The birds display their yellow crown patches and streaked plumage in varied attitudes — one with wings fanned, one perched alertly on the iris stalk, and one lower on the vine. Audubon frequently grouped several individuals on a single plate to illustrate plumage variation across sex or age.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow-Crowned Heron (Plate 336)
description: Plate 336 of Birds of America shows an adult and an immature yellow-crowned night heron perched together on a gnarled tree branch above a coastal waterway. The adult displays the species' distinctive black-and-white head pattern and long white facial plumes, while the heavily streaked juvenile perches above. The composition, engraved and hand-coloured by Robert Havell Jr., was produced between 1827 and 1838 and is held at the University of Pittsburgh.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow-poll Warbler (Plate 95)
description: A single male Yellow-poll Warbler clings to a leafy branch from which hangs a drooping raceme of pale blue-white flowers, its lemon-yellow plumage set against the green foliage. The plate label identifies the subject as the male. Plate 95 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, from the double-elephant folio held at the University of Pittsburgh.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow-throated Vireo (Plate 119)
description: The yellow-throated vireo is shown among leafy branches, its lemon breast and white spectacles picked out in fine line and watercolour wash. Engraved by Robert Havell Jr. from Audubon's life-size original.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Yellow-winged Sparrow (Plate 130)
description: Grasshopper sparrows, under an older name, posed low among grass stems. Audubon's spare composition reflects the cryptic, ground-dwelling nature of the bird, whose flat-headed silhouette he renders with characteristic precision.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Zenaida Dove (Plate 162)
description: A pair of Zenaida Doves perch on a fruiting branch, their warm cinnamon plumage and iridescent neck patches finely modelled. Audubon studied this West Indian species on his 1832 expedition to the Florida Keys, the principal source for several plates in this section.
credit: University of Pittsburgh

title: Beauty Revealed
description: A self-portrait restricted to the artist's bared breasts amid loose white linen, painted at miniature scale on a 6.6 by 8 centimetre ivory. Goodridge sent the case to the newly widowed senator Daniel Webster in 1828; he kept it among his papers until his death, and the Met acquired it in 2006.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art

title: Chichester Canal
description: The still water of the Sussex canal mirrors a tall-masted ship and a sky drenched in late sun. Turner painted the scene for his patron the Earl of Egremont, one of a set of canvases made for the panelled dining room at Petworth House and now in the Tate.
credit: Tate Gallery, 2012-03-26

title: East Cowes Castle
englishTitle: East Cowes Castle, the Regatta Beating to Windward
description: Racing yachts heel into the wind as they beat to windward through a choppy Solent, with the wooded shoreline of East Cowes Castle beyond. Turner painted this oil on canvas and a companion view for the architect John Nash after staying at the castle, Nash's residence on the Isle of Wight, during the Cowes regatta of 1827, and exhibited both at the Royal Academy in 1828. This canvas is in the Indianapolis Museum of Art; its pendant, showing the regatta boats starting for their moorings, is in the Victoria and Albert Museum.

title: Expulsion from the Garden of Eden
description: Adam and Eve flee through a rocky defile as a blazing shaft of light marks the sealed gate of Eden behind them; to the right, the lush, sunlit interior of paradise recedes while storm, volcanic eruption, and a darkened wilderness surround them on the left. Thomas Cole painted this work in 1828 as a pendant to his Garden of Eden, deploying dramatic contrasts of dark and light to underscore the theological gravity of the fall. The canvas is in the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hill Town on the Edge of the Campagna
description: A broad panoramic view across the flat Roman Campagna, a winding river threading through an ochre plain toward a hazy mountain horizon. The near-abstract handling — thinly applied paint dissolving land, water, and sky — shows Turner working from sketches made during his time in Rome in 1828. The work is part of the Turner Bequest, now held at Tate.

title: Hokusai
description: A cuckoo in swift flight soars above a dense mass of flowering azaleas in this woodblock print by Katsushika Hokusai, dated 1828. The composition pairs a vocal summer bird with the seasonally appropriate blossom, following conventions well established in Japanese kachō-e prints. Haiku text inscribed above the image reinforces the interplay of seasonal imagery and literary allusion central to the genre.
credit: Ukiyo-e.org

title: Petworth Park: Tillington Church in the Distance
description: A long horizontal sweep of Egremont's deer park with Tillington's spire pinning the horizon. One of the studies made in the Petworth studio Egremont set aside for him, the picture is structured almost entirely by golden, grazing light.

title: Portrait of Cornelia Vetterlein
description: Joseph Karl Stieler portrays Cornelia Vetterlein as a three-quarter bust, the young woman in a deep-red velvet dress holding a small bunch of blue flowers, with a pearl headband, drop earrings, and a multi-strand necklace. An open landscape with a river valley and a ruined castle forms the background, characteristic of Stieler's romantic portrait manner; the picture is dated 1828.

title: The Barrel Game
description: Figures gathered around a tonneau game of skill, tossing discs toward the scoring holes of the cabinet. Oil on canvas, 37.8 by 46.8 cm, dated about 1828, in the Ramsbury Manor Foundation. Boilly drew the players in the tight finish he used for his late genre scenes of Parisian amusement.
credit: Alain Truong [1]

title: The Defence of Saragossa
description: Wilkie commemorates the heroine Agustina de Aragón seizing a linstock to fire a cannon during the 1808 siege of Zaragoza, painted after his Spanish travels of 1827–28. The composition — with its windswept figure, fallen defenders, and ruined church towers — reaches beyond Wilkie's usual domestic genre toward the broader Romantic history mode. The work is held in the Royal Collection at Windsor Castle (RCIN 405091).
credit: Royal Collection

title: The Vale of Dedham
description: A sweeping view east from Gun Hill over the River Stour to the tower of Dedham Church and the estuary beyond, painted with thickly worked impasto and white sparkle on the water. Dated 1828 and now in the Scottish National Gallery, the picture echoes Claude's Hagar and the Angel and helped secure Constable's election to the Royal Academy the following year.

title: View of Orvieto
description: The cliff-set Umbrian town floats above its golden plain in a picture begun and finished during Turner's second Roman stay. Exhibited at his studio on the Quattro Fontane, it greeted Italian visitors as a deliberate answer to Claude.

title: Wilhelmine Begas
description: A half-length portrait of Wilhelmine Begas, wife of the painter Carl Joseph Begas, dated 1828. The sitter gazes upward, her auburn hair braided and adorned with a blue ribbon, wearing a dark velvet gown with lace sleeves and a cross pendant; an open landscape with a river and red flowers provides the background. Reinhold Begas, the celebrated German sculptor, was among the couple's sons.
credit: georgeeliot.wordpress.com; GalleriX

title: 2560px-The Big wave from 100 views of the Fuji
description: A page from Hokusai's later, more contemplative woodblock series One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji, in which a curling wave frames the distant sacred peak. Printed in monochrome ink with discreet grey gradations, it reprises in book form the motif of his earlier Great Wave.

title: Banks of the Loire
description: A luminous river view shows wooded cliffs rising above a broad reach of calm water, with sailing vessels in the middle distance and a seated figure in red beside a small bridge in the foreground. The warm amber and golden tones suffuse the landscape with milky riverine light. Painted around 1829, it is held by the Worcester Art Museum (inv. 1940.59).

title: Hadleigh Castle
description: The ruined fourteenth-century keep of Hadleigh Castle stands on the Essex shore above the wide grey mouth of the Thames, gulls wheeling in a clearing morning sky. Constable submitted the picture to the Royal Academy in 1829, the year of his election as an Academician and shortly after the death of his wife Maria; it now belongs to the Yale Center for British Art.

title: Het Suwa meer in de provincie Shinano Shinshu Suwako
englishTitle: Lake Suwa in Shinano Province (Shinshū Suwako), from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Hokusai's view across Lake Suwa, with Mount Fuji on the far horizon and a shrine and two windswept pines on a rocky outcrop in the foreground. The sheet belongs to the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, printed by Nishimura Yohachi in shades of blue using imported Prussian pigment.

title: 冨嶽三十六景 隅田川関屋の里-Sekiya Village on the Sumida River
englishTitle: Sekiya Village on the Sumida River, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's celebrated series "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji," depicting the village of Sekiya along the Sumida River. The composition exemplifies Hokusai's mastery of perspective and color gradation, showing the influence of European compositional techniques on Japanese ukiyo-e printmaking during the Edo period.
objectKey: collection-of-beauty/冨嶽三十六景_隅田川関屋の里-Sekiya_Village_on_the_Sumida_River_(Sumidagawa_Sekiya_no_sato),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141023.jpg
commonsUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:冨嶽三十六景_隅田川関屋の里-Sekiya_Village_on_the_Sumida_River_(Sumidagawa_Sekiya_no_sato),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141023.jpg

title: 2560px-冨嶽三十六景 上総の海路-At Sea off Kazusa
englishTitle: At Sea off Kazusa (Kazusa no kairo)
description: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei), created circa 1830–32. This seascape depicts the Kazusa Province coastline in Japan, exemplifying the ukiyo-e tradition with characteristic compositional balance and atmospheric perspective.

title: A group of mountaineers
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: A group of pilgrims ascends the steep, reddish volcanic slopes of Mount Fuji in single file, their straw hats and blue garments contrasting with the warm brown and orange of the mountain face. This print is plate 34 of Hokusai's celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, first published around 1830, and shows the climbers on the upper reaches of the sacred peak rather than its distant silhouette.

title: A sketch of the Mitsui shop in Suruga in Edo
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: Hokusai frames the snow-capped cone of Mount Fuji between the tiled roofs of the Mitsui dry-goods house on Suruga Street in Edo, kites climbing the sky on long strings while tilers work on a roof at right. The design is number 2 in the woodblock series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, first published around 1830; an impression is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: A Young Tiger Playing with its Mother
description: A tigress reclines on a rocky ground beneath a stormy sky while a young cub presses close and wrestles at her face and neck. Painted in 1830 by Eugène Delacroix, the canvas belongs to the Département des Peintures of the Louvre (RF 1943) and exemplifies the Romantic fascination with wild animal energy.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Asakusa Hongan-ji temple in the Eastern capital
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: The ornate roof of Asakusa Hongan-ji temple fills the right foreground while a kite and its airborne handler drift across the pale sky, with Mount Fuji visible in the distance. Plate four of Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (c. 1830) makes the sacred peak a small, constant presence glimpsed across the rooftops of Edo, held at the Chester Beatty Library.

title: Basket-fishing in the Kinu River
description: From the Oceans of Wisdom series on traditional fishing methods, Hokusai shows villagers wading the Kinu with woven basket traps. The flattened riverbank and tight figural grouping demonstrate his mature handling of genre subjects in the 1830s.
credit: Original publication : Japan, 1830s Immediate source : https://ukiyo-e.org/image/mfa/sc145753

title: Battle poitiers
description: Delacroix renders the Battle of Poitiers of 19 September 1356 as a Romantic mêlée of foot soldiers and cavalry, banners and lances clashing across a wide plain under a stormy sky. A prominent figure in white at the centre, identifiable as King John II of France, stands surrounded by English knights pressing in from all sides. The canvas, dated 1830, is in the Louvre.
credit: Encyclopaedia Britannica

title: Calais Sands at Low Water: Poissards Collecting Bait
description: Local fisherwomen, the poissards, dig for lugworm bait on the broad expanse of Calais beach as the sun sinks behind them. Turner returned to the Channel coast repeatedly, treating Calais as the symbolic threshold between England and the Continent. The sky and wet sand dissolve into a single shimmering field of low light.

title: Carlyle Maclise Original
description: Daniel Maclise's full-length pencil study shows Thomas Carlyle leaning against a pillar, right elbow crooked against it, hat held loosely in his left hand. The portrait belongs to the celebrated series of literary figures Maclise drew for Fraser's Magazine during the 1830s, capturing Carlyle's angular, informal presence with characteristic economy of line.

title: Enoshima in Sagami Province
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: The tidal causeway to the sacred island of Enoshima opens before pilgrims as Mount Fuji rises in the distance. From Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the print exploits imported Prussian blue and the bold diagonal of the sandbar to organise its broad sea view.
credit: Source: http://visipix.com/index.htm

title: Hakone Lake in Sagami Province
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: From Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, this print sets the still mirror of Lake Hakone in the foreground, with Fuji rising over wooded ridges beyond. Hokusai contrasts smooth bands of water with crisply outlined cedars and the modulated bokashi gradations of the sky.

title: Kajikazawa in Kai Province
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: Two fishermen work a line from a jagged green outcrop while Mount Fuji rises pale and triangular beyond the blue surf. The spare composition reduces landscape to interlocking geometric forms printed in the imported Prussian blue (bero-ai) that defines the series. First published around 1830, this is the forty-fifth design in Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, one of the nine additional views added to the original thirty-six.

title: Klosterstraße
description: Gaertner's 1830 view of the Klosterstraße shows the wide Berlin street under a dramatic cloudy sky, with classical and older buildings lining both sides and a church tower rising in the distance. Small figures — pedestrians and a mounted rider — animate the foreground. The composition exemplifies the precise vedute style Gaertner had developed since the 1820s for documenting Berlin's urban fabric.

title: Koishikawa in the Morning after a Snowfall
description: Hokusai's woodblock print shows a snow-covered tea-house pavilion in the Koishikawa district of Edo, with visitors sheltering inside as Mount Fuji rises beneath a clear blue sky on a winter morning. Scene 11 of his celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (c. 1830–35), the print is held at the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam (AK-MAK-1588).
credit: www.rijksmuseum.nl : Home : Info

title: L-L Boilly Une loge
description: Spectators crowd a theatre box on a free-admission performance day, a working-class audience pressed shoulder to shoulder. Boilly titled the panel 'Une loge, un jour de spectacle gratuit'; the small oil measures 32.5 by 41.7 cm and hangs in the Musée Lambinet at Versailles.

title: La Liberté guidant le peuple - Eugène Delacroix - Musée du Louvre Peintures RF 129 - après restauration 2024
description: An allegorical Liberty, bare-breasted and clutching the tricolore, leads insurgents over a barricade strewn with the dead during the July Revolution of 1830. Delacroix, the standard-bearer of French Romanticism, fuses contemporary reportage with classical personification in vivid, brushy oil.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Mount Fuji seen from the tea plantation at Katakura in Suruga Province
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: A woodblock print from the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series, framing the sacred peak through workers tending neat rows of tea bushes in Suruga Province. Hokusai integrates rural labor with landscape, the foreground figures pressing leaves into bundles while Fuji rises in cool, flat planes behind.

title: Paddy fields in Ono
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: From Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (no. 31), this woodblock print depicts farmers and heavily laden pack horses crossing the flat reclaimed lands of Ōno in Suruga Province, bundles of straw strapped to the animals' backs. Fuji's snow-capped peak rises serenely above the wide bay and marshes in the distance. First published around 1830, the composition uses bold horizontal bands of colour to balance the busy foreground activity against the mountain's still silhouette.

title: Pleasure District at Senju
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: From Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the print situates the sacred peak behind travelers and scenery in the provinces. Hokusai's signature flat planes of color and bold contour line organize the landscape into the layered recession the series made famous.

title: Schlüterhof in the Berlin Palace
description: The Schlüterhof, the baroque inner courtyard of the Berlin Palace redesigned by Andreas Schlüter, seen around 1830 with carriages, elegantly dressed figures, and onlookers gathered beneath a cloud-filled sky. Eduard Gaertner's topographically precise canvas records the courtyard's monumental Baroque façades before the palace's later demolition.

title: Self-portrait
description: The artist depicts herself in a red shawl draped over a dark striped bodice with a lace insert at the neckline, her dark hair pinned in curls above a neutral ground. Executed in watercolour on ivory in 1830, this self-portrait is a characteristic example of the intimate miniature format Goodridge practised throughout her Boston career.

title: South Wind
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: Better known as Red Fuji, this woodblock print captures the volcano flushed warm by dawn light during the late summer southerlies. Banded clouds and a near-abstract triangular silhouette make it a touchstone of the Thirty-six Views series.

title: Sunset across the Ryōgoku bridge from the bank of the Sumida River at Onmayagashi
englishTitle: Sunset across the Ryōgoku Bridge from the Bank of the Sumida River
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: Plate twelve of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji shows boatmen and stevedores along the Sumida embankment, the long span of Ryōgoku Bridge cutting the composition while Fuji rises faintly in the dusk. Hokusai keeps the celebrated peak modest in scale, ceding the foreground to working Edo.

title: The back of the Fuji from the Minobu river
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: A woodblock view from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, taken from the rear face of the mountain along the Minobu River. Hokusai contrasts the sinuous river bend and rocky banks with the broad, simplified silhouette of the peak, animated by tiny travelling figures.

title: The Circular Pine Trees of Aoyama
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: A print from Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, in which a clearing of pruned, circular pines frames the distant volcano. The flattened decorative pattern of the foliage demonstrates the artist's command of Edo-period graphic abstraction.

title: The Evening Star
description: A solitary boy with a dog wades along an empty Margate beach as Venus pricks the violet dusk. Pared back to bands of damp sand, sea and sky, the canvas distils Turner's late preoccupation with thresholds of light.

title: The Fuji seen from Kanaya on the Tokaido
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: An additional view from the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, looking across the boulder-strewn Ōi River from the Kanaya post-station toward a snow-capped Fuji. Travellers and porters ford the shallows in the foreground, anchoring the landscape in everyday Tōkaidō life.

title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
dateCreated: First publication: between circa 1830 and circa 1832 .
description: The opening sheet of Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji shows a towering offshore wave (okinami) breaking over fishing boats while Fuji stands small on the horizon. Hokusai's use of imported Prussian blue and his geometric treatment of foam made the print a touchstone of Edo design.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art : entry 45434

title: The Last Day of Pompeii
description: Citizens of Pompeii stumble through the streets as columns crack, lightning splits the sky and ash falls across the doomed city under Vesuvius. Painted in 1830-33 in Rome on commission from Count Anatoly Demidov, the vast canvas, 4.6 by 6.5 metres, won the gold medal at the Paris Salon of 1834 and now belongs to the State Russian Museum.
credit: tAFrCGFUhXM8Jg at Google Cultural Institute zoom level scaled down from second highest

title: The timberyard at Honjo
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: From Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (no. 5), the print frames the distant peak behind a busy riverside timber yard at Honjo, where workers balance atop high stacks of lumber and planks. The composition contrasts the vertical mass of stored timber against the open sky and calm water, a characteristic Edo juxtaposition of urban labour and sublime landscape rendered in Hokusai's bold woodblock style.

title: Umezawa Manor in Sagami Province
dateCreated: First publication: circa 1830 . This edition: circa 1930 .
description: From the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the volcano floats beyond a quiet manor pond ringed by cranes and pines. Hokusai marshals his celebrated bero-ai Prussian-blue gradients to balance domestic foreground against distant peak.

title: Wasserdrachen
description: A coiling water dragon, or mizuchi, from a late ukiyo-e series devoted to birds, beasts, insects and fish. Eisen, better known for bijin-ga prints of Edo women, here adapts the colour woodblock to a more decorative, naturalist mode in keeping with kacho-e tradition.
credit: Museum of Art and Crafts Hamburg

title: Голова Мадонны
description: A close head study of the Virgin, her face inclined and eyes lowered, isolated against a plain ground. Bruni, who served as curator of the Imperial Hermitage picture gallery from 1849, worked the academic Madonna type throughout these decades; the study is dated to the second half of the 1830s into the 1840s and is held in the Hermitage, St Petersburg.
credit: www.hermitagemuseum.org

title: 冨嶽三十六景 下目黒-Lower Meguro
englishTitle: Lower Meguro (Shimo Meguro), from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print from Hokusai's celebrated 36 Views of Mount Fuji series, depicting the view of Mount Fuji from Lower Meguro in Edo-period Japan. Created circa 1830–32, this iconic work exemplifies the ukiyo-e tradition of landscape prints. The image is part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's collection and is available in the public domain via Creative Commons CC0.

title: 冨嶽三十六景 五百らかん寺さざゐどう-Sazai Hall at the Temple of the Five Hundred Arhats
englishTitle: Sazai Hall at the Temple of the Five Hundred Arhats, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Woodblock print depicting the Sazaidō hall of Gohyaku Rakanji temple, part of Hokusai's celebrated series "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. " The composition showcases the artist's mastery of perspective and landscape design, with Mount Fuji visible in the distance. From The Metropolitan Museum of Art collection.

title: 冨嶽三十六景 尾州不二見原-Fujimigahara in Owari Province
englishTitle: Fujimigahara in Owari Province, from the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print from Hokusai's iconic series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting the view of Mount Fuji across the rice fields of Owari Province. Created circa 1830-32, this Japanese print showcases the distinctive composition and color palette characteristic of the ukiyo-e tradition. Sourced from the Metropolitan Museum of Art's open access collection.
objectKey: collection-of-beauty/冨嶽三十六景_尾州不二見原-Fujimigahara_in_Owari_Province_(Bishū_Fujimigahara),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141033.jpg

title: 冨嶽三十六景 常州牛掘-Ushibori in Hitachi Province
englishTitle: Ushibori in Hitachi Province, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's iconic "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji" series, depicting the landscape of Ushibori in Hitachi Province (in present-day Ibaraki, Japan). Created circa 1830-32, this work exemplifies the ukiyo-e tradition with its characteristic use of Prussian blue and compositional depth. The print is part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's collection and is in the public domain.

title: 冨嶽三十六景 東海道保土ケ谷-Hodogaya on the Tōkaidō
englishTitle: Hodogaya on the Tōkaidō, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's iconic series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting the town of Hodogaya along the Tōkaidō road. The composition features one of Hokusai's characteristic elevated perspectives with strong compositional depth. This Metropolitan Museum of Art example (DP141025) represents the series at its artistic zenith during the Edo period.
objectKey: collection-of-beauty/冨嶽三十六景_東海道保土ケ谷-Hodogaya_on_the_Tōkaidō_(Tōkaidō_Hodogaya),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141025.jpg
commonsUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:冨嶽三十六景_東海道保土ケ谷-Hodogaya_on_the_Tōkaidō_(Tōkaidō_Hodogaya),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141025.jpg

title: 冨嶽三十六景 東海道吉田-Yoshida on the Tōkaidō
englishTitle: Yoshida on the Tōkaidō, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei). This print depicts Yoshida station on the Tōkaidō road, a major trade route in Edo-period Japan. The work exemplifies Hokusai's mastery of perspective and landscape composition, featuring bold lines and the characteristic blue pigments he favored during this period.

title: 冨嶽三十六景 東海道江尻田子の浦略図-Tago Bay near Ejiri on the Tōkaidō
englishTitle: Tago Bay near Ejiri on the Tōkaidō, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's renowned series "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji" (Fugaku sanjūrokkei). This print depicts Tago Bay near the town of Ejiri along the Tōkaidō highway, capturing the dramatic coastal landscape with Mount Fuji visible in the distance. Created during the mid-Edo period (1830), it exemplifies the ukiyo-e artistic tradition and Hokusai's mastery of perspective and color composition.
objectKey: collection-of-beauty/冨嶽三十六景_東海道江尻田子の浦略図-Tago_Bay_near_Ejiri_on_the_Tōkaidō_(Tōkaidō_Ejiri_Tago_no_ura_ryaku_zu),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei)_MET_DP141037.jpg

title: 冨嶽三十六景 武州玉川-Fuji—The Tama River
englishTitle: The Tama River, Musashi Province, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's acclaimed series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting the Tama River flowing through Musashi Province with Mount Fuji visible in the distance. Created circa 1830-32, this work exemplifies the ukiyo-e style's masterful composition of landscape and water. Part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's open access collection.

title: 冨嶽三十六景 甲州三坂水面-Reflection in Lake at Misaka in Kai Province
englishTitle: Reflection in Lake at Misaka in Kai Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print from Hokusai's celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting the reflection of the iconic mountain in Lake Misaka in Kai Province. This print exemplifies the series' innovative compositional approach to landscape representation in ukiyo-e tradition.
objectKey: collection-of-beauty/冨嶽三十六景_甲州三坂水面-Reflection_in_Lake_at_Misaka_in_Kai_Province_(Kōshū_Misaka_suimen),_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_(Fugaku_sanjūrokkei_MET_DP141064.jpg

title: 冨嶽三十六景 甲州三島越-Mishima Pass in Kai Province
englishTitle: Mishima Pass in Kai Province, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's celebrated "Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji" series, depicting the dramatic perspective view through Mishima Pass in Kai Province. The composition exemplifies Hokusai's distinctive treatment of landscape and use of Prussian blue, with Mount Fuji visible in the distance framed by the mountain pass. This impression was part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's acquisition and is now in the public domain.

title: 冨嶽三十六景 甲州犬目峠-The Inume Pass in Kai Province
englishTitle: The Inume Pass in Kai Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei), depicting the mountain pass in Kai Province. This iconic work exemplifies the compositional brilliance and atmospheric perspective characteristic of Hokusai's landscape prints during the Edo period's final decades.

title: 冨嶽三十六景 相州七里浜-Shichirigahama in Sagami Province
englishTitle: Shichirigahama in Sagami Province, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A woodblock print by Japanese master Katsushika Hokusai depicting the famous Shichirigahama beach in Sagami Province. This iconic image is part of his celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei), created during the 1830s. The composition showcases the dramatic interaction between human activity and landscape, with Mount Fuji visible in the distant background.
fileUrl: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/冨嶽三十六景_相州七里浜-Shichirigahama_in_Sagami_Province_%28Sōshū_Shichirigahama%29%2C_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_%28Fugaku_sanjūrokkei%29_MET_DP140979.jpg/800px-冨嶽三十六景_相州七里浜-Shichirigahama_in_Sagami_Province_%28Sōshū_Shichirigahama%29%2C_from_the_series_Thirty-six_Views_of_Mount_Fuji_%28Fugaku_sanjūrokkei%29_MET_DP140979.jpg

title: 冨嶽三十六景 遠江山中-In the Mountains of Tōtomi Province
englishTitle: In the Mountains of Tōtomi Province
description: A woodblock print from Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, c. 1830-32. Sawyers rip boards from an enormous beam propped on trestles — one man saws from atop while another works beneath, a woman and child resting nearby — with Fuji framed in the triangle formed by the beam and its supports. This impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: 冨嶽三十六景 隠田の水車-The Waterwheel at Onden
description: A woodblock print from Katsushika Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting a waterwheel in the small settlement of Onden in Sagami Province. The composition showcases Hokusai's masterful use of perspective and detail, with the waterwheel as the focal point framed by surrounding landscape and architecture. This is one of the most celebrated examples of Edo period Japanese woodblock printing.

title: Caligula's Palace and Bridge
credit: Google Arts & Culture — xQFxUjK0z9Pb_Q Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00512&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: Katsushika Hokusai
englishTitle: Rainstorm Beneath the Summit, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A polychrome woodblock print from Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, published around 1830-32, known as Rainstorm Beneath the Summit (Sanka haku-u). While the peak of Fuji stands clear against drifting clouds, a storm breaks over the lower slopes and a jagged bolt of red lightning flashes across the darkened base of the mountain. The design is the stormy counterpart to the serene Fine Wind, Clear Morning, and ranks with the Great Wave among the most celebrated images of the series.

title: Lady Jane Elizabeth Digby
description: Painted for Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie, the portrait shows the English aristocrat at twenty-four, before the marriages and travels that would carry her from Munich to a Bedouin tent near Damascus. Stieler's smooth, neoclassical finish lends the sitter the air of court decorum she would soon scandalously discard.

title: Life-Boat and Manby Apparatus Going Off to a Stranded Vessel Making Signal
englishTitle: Lifeboat and Manby Apparatus Going off to a Stranded Vessel Making the Signal of Distress
description: Oil painting by Joseph Mallord William Turner depicting a dramatic maritime rescue scene, with a lifeboat and the innovative Manby apparatus being deployed to save a vessel in distress. The work showcases Turner's characteristic dynamic composition and atmospheric effects, capturing the tension and urgency of the emergency response at sea.

title: Marianna Marchesa Florenzi
description: The Italian noblewoman, translator and longtime confidante of Ludwig I of Bavaria, shown with the soft idealisation reserved for the king's Gallery of Beauties in Munich. Stieler emphasises her dark eyes and intellectual composure, signalling her standing as a scholar rather than mere society sitter.

title: Parochialstrasse in Berlin
description: Gaertner's 1831 painting records a narrow Berlin street lined with colourful tenements and workshops, its cobbles busy with tradespeople, pedestrians and dogs. A church spire rises at the far end, framing the receding perspective. The work demonstrates Gaertner's characteristic method of combining precise architectural observation with vivid street-level genre incident.

title: Salisbury Cathedral from the Meadows
description: A late, emotionally charged view of Salisbury Cathedral seen across the water meadows under a rainbow, painted in the wake of Constable's wife's death. Flickering white highlights, the celebrated Constable snow, animate trees and sky in a picture that fused topographic affection with personal grief.

title: Sir Richard Steele's Cottage
description: A view from Haverstock Hill in rural Hampstead, looking south toward the dome of St Paul's, with Sir Richard Steele's cottage on the right and the Load of Hay inn on the left. Constable, who had lived in Hampstead since 1819, sketched the rise repeatedly; the cottage was demolished in 1867.

title: The Refugees of Parga
description: A crowd of Greek refugees streams toward the shore as smoke rises from the hilltop town of Parga above them, dramatising the 1819 exodus before Ottoman rule. Men, women, children, and clergy fill the foreground, carrying possessions and looking back at the burning city. Hayez orchestrates the crowded shoreline as a Romantic tableau of exile and loss, in keeping with his patriotic history paintings.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"h/hayez/2hayez"

title: Whaling off the Coast of the Goto Islands
description: Small whaling boats converge on a large whale at the surface of the sea off the Goto Islands of Kyushu, their crews manoeuvring amid choppy water and cresting waves. From Hokusai's Oceans of Wisdom (Chie no umi) series, the woodblock print of around 1831–33 pairs a vernacular subject with the artist's characteristic command of rhythmic line and dynamic composition.

title: 1280px-Wilhelm von Kobell - Reiter am Tegernsee
description: Two riders pause with a pair of riderless horses on a pale track at the shore of the Tegernsee, dogs at their feet and country women passing to the right, while rain streaks from heavy clouds over the mountains beyond. Painted in 1832, the small picture shows the crisp, sharply lit Biedermeier finish for which Kobell is known. It is held in the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin.

title: Bathsheba
description: Bathsheba, nude, reclines in a rocky garden setting as a dark-skinned child attends her, the two figures surrounded by lush foliage. Bryullov treats the biblical subject with the polished academic technique and warm flesh tones characteristic of his mature style. The canvas, dated 1832, remained unfinished; it is titled Bathsheba and was painted during the artist's years in Italy.

title: Childe Harold's Pilgrimage
description: Inspired by Byron's Mediterranean poem, Turner builds a luminous Italian campagna of crumbling arches, distant hills, and a glowing sky. The picture is part of the artist's long late dialogue with Claude Lorrain, dissolving classical landscape architecture into atmosphere.
credit: abcgallery.com; Sotheby’s (not for sale, only as a reference image)

title: Highland Hospitality
description: A Scottish Highland interior from Lewis's early career, showing a group of men and women gathered around a central hearth in a rustic dwelling, with a spinning wheel to one side and dogs at their feet. Travellers or visitors are welcomed with food and drink by their hosts in Highland dress. Painted in 1832 and now held at the Yale Center for British Art, the picture belongs to the early nineteenth-century taste for Walter Scott-inflected genre subjects.

title: Horsewoman
description: Giovannina Pacini reins in a black horse while her younger sister Amazilia watches wide-eyed from the steps of a villa, both wards of Countess Yulia Samoilova. Commissioned by Samoilova in Milan and exhibited at the Brera Academy in 1832, the picture earned Bryullov comparisons to Rubens and Van Dyck before it passed to Pavel Tretyakov in 1893.
credit: here / здесь

title: Katsushika Hokusai
englishTitle: Goten-yama Hill, Shinagawa on the Tōkaidō
description: Cherry-blossom viewers gather on the bluff at Goten-yama overlooking Edo Bay, with Mount Fuji a faint cone on the horizon. Part of the Thirty-six Views, the print binds a popular hanami spot to the sacred mountain through Hokusai's careful balancing of human ritual and distant geology.
credit: https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/jpd.02452/

title: Portrait of Monsieur Bertin
description: The newspaper editor of the Journal des Débats sits forward, hands planted on his thighs, in a pose that became a touchstone for nineteenth-century bourgeois portraiture. Ingres's polished surface and tightly drawn contours register every wrinkle of Bertin's waistcoat without disturbing the granite stillness of the sitter.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Utagawa Kunisada I
description: Dawn breaks over the linked Wedded Rocks at Futami-ga-ura on the Ise coast, their sacred shimenawa rope strung between them. Kunisada renders the famous pilgrimage site in soft graded blues typical of early-1830s ukiyo-e landscape.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: 諸國瀧廻リ 美濃ノ国養老の滝-Yōrō Waterfall in Mino Province
englishTitle: Yōrō Waterfall in Mino Province, from A Tour of Waterfalls in Various Provinces
description: A woodblock print by Hokusai from his series "A Tour of Waterfalls in Various Provinces" (Shokoku taki meguri), depicting the famous Yōrō Waterfall in Mino Province, Japan. Created circa 1832, this print exemplifies Hokusai's mastery of landscape composition and his fascination with natural waterfalls as subjects.
objectKey: collection-of-beauty/諸國瀧廻リ_美濃ノ国養老の滝-Yōrō_Waterfall_in_Mino_Province_(Mino_no_Yōrō_no_taki),_from_the_series_A_Tour_of_Waterfalls_in_Various_Provinces_(Shokoku_taki_meguri)_MET_DP141263.jpg

title: 1849), Kirifuri waterval bij de Kurokami berg
description: The Kirifuri ("falling mist") cascade on Mount Kurokami breaks into numerous white tendrils against dark cliffs, with tiny travellers gazing up from below. From Hokusai's Waterfalls series (c. 1833), the composition treats the sacred fall as a near-abstract decorative pattern, water rendered as flat stylised line rather than naturalistic spray.

title: Antwerp Van Goyen Looking Out for a Subject
description: An imagined homage in which the Dutch master Jan van Goyen sketches from a small boat in Antwerp harbor, surrounded by shipping under broken cloud. Turner pays tribute to the seventeenth-century landscape tradition while asserting his own atmospheric handling of sky and water.

title: Bridge of Sighs
description: Turner's 1833 view of Venice stretches from the Customs House at the left across the basin to the Campanile, Doge's Palace and the Bridge of Sighs, the foreground animated by gondolas, trading vessels and waterside figures. The vivid blue sky and warm stone of the buildings are rendered with relative topographical clarity, marking the work as distinct from Turner's hazier late Venetian oils. Now at Tate (inventory N00370), it was exhibited at the Royal Academy the year it was painted.
credit: Beyeler Foundation

title: Chôshi in Shimôsa Province
description: Chōshi in Shimōsa Province, from Hokusai's Oceans of Wisdom series (c. 1833), places two fishing boats amid churning open seas, their crews bracing against the swell as a rocky headland rises in the background. The forceful wave patterns and restricted blue-and-white palette recall the graphic intensity Hokusai had brought to the Great Wave in the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. The work is held in the Art Institute of Chicago.

title: Hayez
description: Lot's daughters offer their father wine in a cave above the destroyed city of Sodom, Francesco Hayez's treatment of the episode from Genesis 19. Painted in 1833, the canvas stages the scene in a sharply lit grotto, combining Romantic theatricality with the polished figure modelling Hayez retained from his early years in Canova's circle in Rome. The work is recorded in both major catalogues raisonnes of the artist.

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-01-Nihonbashi-BM-03
description: A daimyō procession sets out across Edo's Nihonbashi bridge at dawn, opening Hiroshige's Tokaido Road series for the publisher Hōeidō. The print establishes the journey's ceremonial scale before the road's weather and incident take over.
credit: Hiroshige.org.uk [1]

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-14-Hara-MFA-01
englishTitle: Hara Station: Mount Fuji in the Morning
description: Two travellers make their way across the open plain at Hara station as Mount Fuji dominates the background beneath a pink-tinged morning sky, with birds in flight along the mountain's flank. From Hiroshige's Hōeidō Tōkaidō series (c. 1833–35), this impression is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-16-Kanbara-MFA-02
description: Three muffled figures trudge through deep night snow at Kanbara, the white sky bokashi-graded into a heavy grey. Long counted among Hiroshige's finest landscape prints, the design treats silence and stillness as subject in their own right.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-34-Futagawa-MFA-02
description: Travellers approach a thatched teahouse on the windswept Sarugababa heath outside Futagawa station. Hiroshige builds the scene from broad fields of muted ochre and pine green typical of the Hōeidō Tōkaidō's middle stretch.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-35-Yoshida-MFA-02
description: Workmen scaffold the Toyokawa River bridge at Yoshida station while Yoshida castle rises beyond. Hiroshige uses the diagonal of the bridgework as a vehicle for his characteristic recession into atmospheric distance.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-36-Goyu-MFA-01
description: Serving women aggressively haul reluctant travellers into an inn at Goyu, a stock comic episode of the Tōkaidō. The print is one of several in the series in which Hiroshige slips genre observation into what is nominally a landscape.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-37-Akasaka-MFA-01
englishTitle: Akasaka Station: Inn with Serving Maids
description: The Akasaka inn is shown in a tilted cross-section view: on one side, a traveller is attended to while a companion waits; on the other, maids prepare for guests, the two halves separated by a palm in the courtyard. Hiroshige's elevated vantage and interior detail make this one of the most architecturally observed scenes in the Hōeidō Tōkaidō (c. 1833–35).
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-40-Chiryu-MET-New-York-01
description: Station Chiryū from the Tōkaidō series, depicting the early-summer horse fair on a grassy plain where merchants and tethered animals scatter under wide skies. Hiroshige uses subtle bokashi gradations along the horizon to evoke seasonal atmosphere; the Hoeidō publisher seal marks this as part of his career-making 1833 edition.
credit: Database of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-44-Yokkaichi-MFA-01
description: At Yokkaichi, a traveller rides in a low cart pulled by a bearer along the Mie River's bank, reeds and a lone tree bent hard by the wind against a pale sky with boats beyond. The print, from Hiroshige's Hōeidō Tōkaidō (c. 1833–35), is one of several in the series that makes wind and weather its principal subject.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-53-Kusatsu-MFA-01
englishTitle: Kusatsu Station: Famous Teahouse at the Post Stop
description: The penultimate station of the Tōkaidō, Kusatsu was famed for its meibutsu tateba teahouse where porters rested with fast palanquins. Hiroshige captures the bustle of arriving travelers under banners, his linework crisp and his palette anchored by the deep indigo blues of the early Hoeidō printing.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige11 hakone
englishTitle: Hakone Station: View of the Lake
description: Hakone Station: View of the Lake (1833/34), from Hiroshige's Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō, depicts the steep, faceted peaks above Lake Ashi in vivid planes of yellow ochre, green, and blue. The dramatic verticality of the mountains — the most challenging terrain on the entire road — dominates the composition, conveying the scale of the obstacle that travellers faced at this pass.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige19 ejiri
englishTitle: Ejiri Station: Distant View of Miho
description: Ejiri, set on Suruga Bay near the Miho pine grove, looks across a calm inlet dotted with sailing boats. Hiroshige flattens the distance into bands of graded color, a hallmark of his ukiyo-e landscape mode that influenced later Western printmakers.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige20 fuchu
description: Travelers ford the Abe River at Fuchu, carried piggyback or on platforms by the station's licensed porters. The rhythmic figures across the shallow water exemplify Hiroshige's interest in the practical theater of travel along the Tōkaidō road.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige22 okabe
description: The Okabe station turns inland through the gorge of Utsu Pass, where a stony stream cuts between steep wooded slopes. Hiroshige's compressed verticals and overlapping rocks give the print a closed, intimate atmosphere unusual for the series.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige25 kanaya
englishTitle: Kanaya Station: The Distant Bank of the Ōi River
description: Kanaya sits on the western bank of the Ōi River, reached only by porters who carried travelers across its broad flats. Hiroshige looks down on the receding scene from a high vantage, ordering the mountains and water into clean horizontal registers.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige28 fukuroi
description: At Fukuroi, travelers rest at a tea stand pitched beneath a leafy tree, a kettle steaming on the open fire. The genre vignette is set against a low, level landscape, demonstrating Hiroshige's gift for everyday observation within the Tōkaidō format.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige30 hamamatsu
description: Hamamatsu features a great solitary pine on a windswept field, with figures gathered around a small fire at its base. The motif distills Hiroshige's recurring concern with weather and season, the bare branches and grey sky reading as winter on the road.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige38 fujikawa
englishTitle: Fujikawa Station: Scene at Post Outskirts
description: Fujikawa Station: Scene at Post Outskirts (1833/34), from the Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō, shows travelers and station hands gathered at the edge of the post town, with a tall lantern post marking the road and trees framing the scene. Hiroshige presents a quiet moment of arrival and rest rather than a grand ceremonial event, capturing the everyday texture of life along the road.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige39 okazaki
description: The Yahagi Bridge at Okazaki, said to be the longest on the Tōkaidō, stretches across the river in a single shallow arc. Hiroshige aligns the procession crossing it with the distant castle, framing infrastructure and authority in one elegant span.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige45 ishiyakushi
description: Ishiyakushi takes its name from the Buddhist temple visible among trees behind the village fields. Hiroshige's quiet rural composition, with farmers at work and a stand of pines, exemplifies the lyrical pastoral mode he interleaved with the busier station scenes.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige47 kameyama
englishTitle: Kameyama Station: Clear Weather after Snow
description: Kameyama Castle rises above a snow-blanketed slope as a daimyō procession climbs toward the gate. The print is among the most admired snowscapes of the Hoeidō Tōkaidō, its diagonal trail and white expanse drawn with Hiroshige's restrained graphic economy.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige49 sakanoshita
description: Sakanoshita lies at the foot of the steep Suzuka pass, here dominated by the cliff known as Fudesute-yama, the 'brush-throwing mountain'. Travelers pause at a teahouse to contemplate the rock face, a scene that joins landscape and legend in Hiroshige's understated manner.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige50 tsuchiyama
description: Tsuchiyama is shown in heavy spring rain, a daimyō procession crossing a swollen stream beneath dripping trees. The slanting rain lines and saturated greens make this one of the most atmospheric prints in the Tōkaidō series.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Nichiren bezweert de golven bij Kakuda tijdens zijn verbanning naar Sado
englishTitle: Nichiren Calming the Waves at Kakuda on His Way to Exile on Sado Island
description: The Buddhist reformer Nichiren stands in a pitching boat off Kakuda, calming the waves with the Lotus Sutra during his exile to Sado. Kuniyoshi's woodblock print sets red robes against churning blue surf in the dramatic warrior-print idiom of late Edo Utagawa school design.
credit: http://www.rijksmuseum.nl/collectie/RP-P-1956-717 ( handle )

title: Rōben Waterfall at Ōyama in Sagami Province
description: Pilgrims bathe in the falls at Ōyama, where Rōben is said to have purified himself before founding the mountain's temple. From A Tour of the Waterfalls of the Provinces, Hokusai abstracts cascading water into ribbons of stylised line, treating each fall as a graphic emblem of place.

title: The Amida Falls in the Far Reaches of the Kisokaidō Road
description: The Amida Falls in the Far Reaches of the Kisokaidō Road depicts a great cascade falling from a circular pool — said to resemble the head of the Buddha Amida — above a group of seated figures in a lush mountain setting. The print belongs to Hokusai's Waterfalls series (c. 1833), now in the British Museum, in which each fall is treated as a near-abstract graphic emblem combining sweeping calligraphic line with flat planes of colour.

title: The Titan's Goblet
description: A colossal goblet, its rim overgrown with vegetation and tiny structures, rises from a mountainous landscape as waterfalls cascade from its moss-covered rim into the valley below; tiny boats sail on the water filling its bowl. Thomas Cole painted this fantastical image in 1833, and it has been interpreted variously as an allegory of civilisation and the natural world. The canvas is in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
credit: Own scan, source: Norbert Wolf, Ingo F. Walther (publ.), Romantik, Taschen, Hong Kong, Köln, London, Los Angeles, Madrid, Paris, Tokyo, 2007, ISBN 978-3-8228-5307-8 , p. 75

title: 2560px-Hiroshige Fishing boats on a lake
description: Descending Geese at Katata, from the Eight Views of Ōmi, depicting boats and a flock settling onto Lake Biwa at dusk. Hiroshige distils the classical Chinese-derived theme into broad bands of graded indigo bokashi, a printing technique that became his signature.

title: Caroline von Holnstein from Fronberg
description: Countess Caroline von Holnstein is shown half-length against a dark background, her braided hair dressed high, wearing a white silk dress with pink sleeves beneath a dark fur-trimmed wrap. The smooth flesh modelling and level gaze are characteristic of Stieler's portraits for Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie, painted in 1834.

title: Femmes d'Alger dans leur appartement
description: Three women lounge with a servant in a tiled Algerian harem chamber, surrounded by hookah, slippers and richly patterned textiles. Painted after Delacroix gained rare access to a domestic interior in 1832, the Louvre canvas became a foundational source of the nineteenth-century Orientalist imagination.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Hiroshige Full moon over a mountain landscape
englishTitle: Autumn Moon at Ishiyama Temple, from Eight Views of Ōmi
description: The Autumn Moon at Ishiyama Temple, from Eight Views of Ōmi, shows the bright disc rising over Lake Biwa behind the temple's wooded bluff. Hiroshige draws on the classical meisho tradition, pairing a literary scenic theme with his characteristic graded blue skies.

title: Hiroshige Heavy rain on a pine tree 2
englishTitle: Night Rain at Karasaki, from Eight Views of Ōmi
description: Night Rain at Karasaki, the second view in Hiroshige's Eight Views of Ōmi (c. 1834), isolates the celebrated pine of Karasaki shrine as a dark, cloud-like mass beneath a steady downpour rendered in dense vertical lines. Blue water glimmers below the canopy, and small structures are just visible through the rain. The near-monochrome palette and relentless verticals give the print the hushed atmosphere of a classical meisho theme translated into the late ukiyo-e idiom.

title: Hiroshige View of a long bridge across a lake
englishTitle: Evening Glow at Seta, from the series Eight Views of Ōmi
description: Evening Glow at Seta, from Eight Views of Ōmi, depicts the Karahashi bridge stretching across the southern reaches of Lake Biwa under a flushed sky. Hiroshige uses bokashi gradations to model dusk, a printing technique that gives the series its meditative tonal character.

title: Life stages
description: Five figures on a Baltic shore correspond to five sailing vessels at varying distances — an allegory of the ages of human life rendered in Friedrich's late, hushed palette. The painting was made near the artist's birthplace of Greifswald and is now in Leipzig's Museum der bildenden Künste.
credit: Museum der bildenden Künste, Leipzig

title: Panorama of Berlin
description: One panel from Gaertner's six-part angular panorama of Berlin, taken from the roof of Schinkel's Friedrichswerdersche Kirche in the summer of 1834. The architectural painter worked daily in a wooden booth atop the church, recording the new buildings of the Schinkel circle for King Friedrich Wilhelm III.

title: Panorama of Berlin. View to the South
description: The southern segment of the 1834 Berlin panorama, recording rooftops, courtyards and chimneys spread out below the lantern of the Friedrichswerder church. Gaertner's six-part view was purchased by Friedrich Wilhelm III and a replica was later carried to Russia for Tsarina Alexandra Feodorovna.

title: Panorama von Berlin
description: One panel of Gaertner's six-part 1834 Panorama von Berlin, painted from the roof of the Friedrichswerdersche Kirche, surveys the city's rooftops looking westward toward the Lustgarten and the dome of the Berliner Dom, with the colonnade of the Altes Museum visible to the left. The Gothic parapet of the Friedrichswerdersche Kirche occupies the immediate foreground, grounding the viewer's elevated vantage point. The panorama is one of the most complete topographical records of Berlin in the Biedermeier era.

title: Peaceable Kingdom
description: A lion lies beside a lamb, a leopard with a kid, and a child rests his hand on the leopard's neck, while in the left background William Penn signs his 1681 treaty with the Lenape on the Delaware. Hicks, a Quaker minister and sign painter, made roughly a hundred versions of the Isaiah 11 prophecy as an emblem of Pennsylvania's promise.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Self Portrait
description: The artist at seventeen, with loose hair and a fixed gaze, the face firmly modelled while the clothing is left as bare canvas. Watts painted this oil, his first self-portrait, in 1834; it measures 53.3 by 38.1 cm and remains at the Watts Gallery in Compton, Surrey.

title: The Burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons
description: Westminster's old Palace blazes against the night sky on 16 October 1834, watched by a crowd massed on the Thames. Turner sketched the fire from a hired boat and produced two oil versions, of which this is the Philadelphia canvas. The conflagration let him paint exactly the kind of incandescent yellow-and-red sky he had been pursuing for decades.

title: The Burning of the Houses of Parliament
description: An eyewitness response to the conflagration that destroyed the medieval Palace of Westminster, watched by crowds along the Thames. Turner sketched the blaze from a hired boat and translated it into pyrotechnic yellows and reds against the cool Westminster Bridge.
credit: Cleveland Museum of Art

title: Venice - The Dogana and San Giorgio Maggiore by Joseph Mallord William Turner
englishTitle: Venice: The Dogana and San Giorgio Maggiore
description: A masterwork by the English Romantic painter J. M. W.

title: A colored version of the Big wave from 100 views of the Fuji
description: A reworked echo of the famous Kanagawa wave, drawn from the later One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji. Hokusai mirrors the composition, removes the fishing boats, and turns the spume into a flock of birds — a meditation on transformation rendered in his late, more graphic woodblock manner.

title: Head of a Person Asleep
description: A small, intimate study of a figure asleep, head sunk against bedding, kept in Turner's studio and bequeathed to the nation. The looseness of touch is closer to the colour-beginnings of his late watercolours than to anything he exhibited. It belongs to a private corpus of figurative sketches now in the Tate's Turner Bequest.

title: Keelmen Heaving in Coals by Moonlight
description: Tyneside coal-heavers loading colliers under a full moon at Shields, painted as a pendant to a Venetian scene to contrast industrial north and southern lagoon. The torchlit smoke and silvered water typify Turner's late nocturnes.

title: Line Fishing
description: Fishing boats work the swell off Hastings under a turbulent sky, the figures and rigging set against pale sea-light. Turner treats the everyday coastal labor with the atmospheric breadth of his mature marine paintings.

title: Ono Waterfall on the Kisokaidō
description: Travellers and packhorses pause on the Kisokaidō highway beside the Ono falls, dwarfed by a smooth blue sheet of water. From the Tour of the Waterfalls, the print pairs Hokusai's stylised, almost geometric treatment of cascades with the everyday traffic of one of Edo Japan's great post roads.

title: Stonehenge
description: A late watercolour showing the prehistoric stones beneath a roiling sky split by a double rainbow. Constable, working in his final years, treats the monument as a meditation on time and weather, the broken trilithons set against the moving drama of the English heavens.

title: The Bright Stone of Honour
description: The Rhine fortress of Ehrenbreitstein rises in golden haze above the confluence with the Moselle, paired with the riverside tomb of the French general Marceau. Turner illustrates a passage from Byron's Childe Harold, fusing topography with literary elegy.

title: The Grand Canal - Venice
description: A view down the Grand Canal toward the domes of Santa Maria della Salute, gondolas dispersed across luminous water. Turner dissolves the architecture of Venice into pale light and reflected color, characteristic of his late Romantic vedute.

title: The Yoshitsune Horse-Washing Falls at Yoshino
description: Yoshitsune's retainers wash their horses beneath the Yoshino falls, the cascade splitting into braided ribbons of pale paper. The plate from the Waterfalls series fuses warrior legend with landscape, characteristic of how Hokusai layered narrative into his late topographical print sets.

title: 1836 Heimkehr des Palikaren anagoria
description: A Berlin contribution to European Philhellenism: a palikar, one of the irregular fighters of the Greek War of Independence, returns to his family on the shore at sunset, bending over the infant in his arms while his wife shoulders his rifle and two children press around him. Magnus, a Berlin portraitist, treats the costume and embroidery with ethnographic precision while keeping the emotional register restrained. Painted in 1836; Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin.

title: Fortune-teller Svetlana
description: A young woman sits with her back to the viewer, gazing into a candlelit mirror in a darkened interior, performing a traditional Epiphany fortune-telling rite. Bryullov based the 1836 canvas on Vasily Zhukovsky's popular 1812 ballad 'Svetlana,' and the Russian Museum source identifies it as the only work by the artist on a national everyday theme; it is held by the Nizhny Novgorod State Art Museum.

title: Rome
description: A panoramic view of the Eternal City bathed in golden Mediterranean haze, with the Tiber winding past domes and ruins toward distant hills. Turner exhibited this canvas after his Italian travels, dissolving topographical detail into atmospheric light worthy of Claude Lorrain.
credit: dailymail.co.uk the second upload thehistoryblog.com the third upload thehistoryblog.com

title: The Consummation of Empire from The Course of the Empire
description: The third canvas in The Course of Empire shows a fictive classical city at its zenith, with porticoes, rotundas, statuary and a triumphal procession crossing a marble bridge above the harbour. Cole painted the five-part allegory for his patron Luman Reed's Greenwich Street picture gallery between 1833 and 1836; Reed died in June 1836 without seeing the series completed.
credit: Exlore Thomas Cole

title: View from Mount Holyoke
description: Storm clouds and a gnarled dead tree dominate the left half of the canvas while the right opens onto the sunlit Connecticut River looping in a wide oxbow around the cultivated meadows below Mount Holyoke, with Cole's own figure visible sketching among the rocks in the foreground. Painted in 1836 and exhibited that year at the National Academy of Design, the picture is one of the defining statements of the Hudson River School's dual vision of wild nature and settled landscape. It is now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art

title: (Barcelona) Story of Apollo and Daphne 1837 - William Turner - Tate Britain
description: A late mythological landscape by Turner, the Ovidian chase staged across a golden Italianate valley bathed in the swirling light he had brought back from his Roman travels. Figures dwindle beside vast trees and rivers, drama dissolved into atmosphere in the manner of his ageing Claude homages.

title: Ancient Rome; Agrippina Landing with the Ashes of Germanicus
credit: Google Arts & Culture — 6QEKBj-jyZHtOQ Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00523&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: Arundel Mill and Castle
description: A water mill on the River Arun in the foreground, with Arundel Castle's keep rising through trees on the slope beyond. Constable spent the entire day of 31 March 1837 putting the last touches on the canvas and died unexpectedly that night; his friend C. R. Leslie sent it to the Royal Academy summer exhibition the following year as his final work.

title: Eugene delacroix
description: Delacroix portrays himself in three-quarter view, curly dark hair framing a face of intense, searching expression. He wears a dark coat with a visible green collar, against a warm ochre-brown background that merges with his silhouette. Painted in 1837, when the artist was in his late thirties, this self-portrait is now in the Louvre.
credit: cgfa.sunsite.dk via web.archive.org

title: Fishing Boats with Hucksters Bargaining for Fish
Karl Friedrich Schinkel Allegorie auf Beuth
