description: An allegorical tribute to the Prussian industrial reformer Peter Beuth, shown astride Pegasus as he soars over a panorama of human civilisation and progress. The composition fuses Romantic landscape with Enlightenment allegory, celebrating Beuth's role in the modernisation of the Prussian state.
credit: Kupferstichkabinett, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

title: London National Gallery Turner Hero and Leander
englishTitle: The Parting of Hero and Leander
description: Turner depicts the moonlit parting of Hero and Leander on a turbulent sea, figures clustered on a terrace as the waters churn under a cloud-veiled moon. The canvas, exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1837, is now in the National Gallery, London, and exemplifies Turner's late mythological seascapes in which architecture, water, and atmosphere dissolve into one another.

title: Look to the Large Cascade and Large Petergof Palace
description: The Grand Cascade tumbles down its gilded terraces toward the Marine Canal at Peterhof, the Samson fountain throwing its jet high at the left while the long facade of the Great Palace stretches along the upper terrace; two strollers pause at the water's edge below. Aivazovsky painted the view in 1837, his final year as a student of the Imperial Academy of Arts in Saint Petersburg.

title: Sea coast at night. Near the beacon
description: Moonlight breaks through heavy cloud over a quiet shore where a lighthouse rises above the rocks; a sailing vessel lies beached and heeled over at the right, a rowboat rests on the sand, and ships ride offshore in the silvery light. Aivazovsky painted the nocturne in 1837, the year he completed his studies at the Imperial Academy of Arts with a gold medal.

title: The Wounded Heron
description: A heron struck down in a hawking scene sprawls in the foreground, its wing spread on the ground. Watts, then about twenty, bought a dead heron from a poulterer to study the bird; the oil on canvas, 91.4 by 71.1 cm, was his Royal Academy debut in 1837 and now belongs to the Watts Gallery, Surrey.
credit: BBC Your Paintings; Art UK : entry the-wounded-heron-13235

title: Christophe Colomb et son fils à La Rábida
description: Eugène Delacroix depicts Columbus arriving at the Franciscan monastery of La Rábida with his young son Diego, the exhausted boy slumped asleep in a chair while friars in white-and-black habits address the explorer in an arched corridor. Painted in 1838 and held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the canvas presents a scene of weary petition set within the quiet architecture of the Spanish monastery.
credit: National Gallery of Art .

title: Flora Tristan 1838
description: Portrait of the French socialist and feminist writer Flora Tristan (1803–1844), shown in half-length with arms crossed and dark curling hair. A lithograph published by Aubert in 1838, the print appeared in Le Charivari no. 53 on 22 February 1839.
credit: https://www.liberation.fr/france/2018/10/10/flora-tristan-une-ouvriere-victime-de-feminicide_1684545 and https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k30494211/f3.item.zoom

title: Frédéric Chopin
description: Delacroix painted this portrait of Frédéric Chopin in 1838 as part of a larger double portrait that also depicted George Sand; the canvas was cut into two separate works after the artist's death, leaving only this fragment of the composer. Chopin appears in three-quarter view, his auburn hair loosely framing an introspective face rendered against a warm brown ground. The fragment is now in the Louvre.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"d/delacroi/3/313delac"

title: Hiroshige
description: A pair of mandarin ducks is shown near flowering plants, one swimming in the water while the other descends with wings spread. The print, dated 1838, belongs to Hiroshige's kachō-e (bird-and-flower) work, in which paired oshidori served as a traditional symbol of conjugal devotion.
credit: Wikipaintings

title: Médée
description: Medea clutches her two sons to her chest in a rocky grotto, the dagger raised as she prepares to kill them in revenge against Jason. Painted between 1836 and 1838 and shown at the Salon, the canvas was bought by the State and sent to the Palais des Beaux-Arts in Lille, where it has hung since 1839.

title: Schinkel2
englishTitle: Project for Orianda Palace, Crimea — Garden Terrace
description: Schinkel's elevation of the terrace at Orianda, a country retreat for Tsarina Alexandra Feodorovna planned on a cliff above the Black Sea in the Crimea. The architect's 1838 design fused a caryatid portico with hanging gardens and museum rooms; the cost was prohibitive and the palace was never built, surviving only in lithographs.
credit: Staatliche Schlösser und Gärten, Berlin, Postkarte, selbst gescannt

title: The death of Ophelia
description: Ophelia clings to a willow branch as it splits above the brook, her white shift catching on the bark while her wreath of flowers drifts away. Delacroix's first version of the subject, drawn from Gertrude's speech in Act IV of Hamlet, was painted in 1838 and is now in the Neue Pinakothek in Munich.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/d/delacroi/3/315delad"; Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen

title: The Last Meeting between Jacopo Foscari and his Family Before Being Sent into Exile
englishTitle: The Last Meeting of Jacopo Foscari with His Family
description: The painting was commissioned in 1838 by Emperor Ferdinand I , who had arrived in Milan for his coronation as king of Lombardy and Veneto , and it was destined for the Belvedere Gallery in Vienna. On its completion in 1840 the work was valued at the extremely high price of five thousand florins by the Commissione Permanente di Pittura dell’Accademia di Brera , which thus recognized its exceptional quality.
credit: Artgate Fondazione Cariplo

title: Wilhelmine Sulzer
description: Wilhelmine Sulzer is depicted in a white off-the-shoulder dress with embroidered neckline trim and a fur stole, her auburn hair falling loosely around her shoulders against a dark ground. Stieler painted this 1838 portrait for Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie in Munich, applying his characteristic porcelain finish and discreet idealisation.

title: "Le jardin Hoschedé à Montgeron" d'A. Sisley
description: Le jardin Hoschedé à Montgeron Oeuvre d'Alfred Sisley (1839-1899) Montgeron, 1881 Huile sur toile Collection Ivan Morozov, 26 novembre 1904 Musée d'Etat des beaux-arts Pouchkine, Moscou Oeuvre de l'exposition "La collection Morozov. Icônes de l'art moderne", Fondation Louis Vuitton, Paris Conçue par Anne Baldassari, commissaire général, l’exposition déploie cet ensemble dans une muséographie originale occupant la totalité des espaces de la Fondation Louis Vuitton.

title: A View of the Mountain Pass Called the Notch of the White Mountains
description: A horseman crosses the V of Crawford Notch in the New Hampshire White Mountains, dwarfed by twisted pines and the bleached skeletons of trees torn from the slope. Cole painted the gorge in 1839, drawing on memories of the 1826 avalanche that wiped out the Willey family and their farmhands; it hangs in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: General Sir David Baird Discovering the Body of Sultan Tippoo Sahib
description: A vast late history painting commemorating the British general's discovery of Tipu Sultan's body after the storming of Seringapatam in 1799. Wilkie staged the torch-lit scene with theatrical chiaroscuro, working in the grand manner he adopted following his travels in Spain.
credit: Scottish National Gallery NG 2430

title: Ivan Krylov
description: Karl Bryullov's unfinished portrait of the Russian fabulist Ivan Andreyevich Krylov shows the heavy-set sitter in a dark coat, a small order just visible on his chest, facing the viewer with a weary directness. Begun in 1839 and left incomplete by Bryullov, the head and upper body are fully resolved; the canvas measures 102.3 by 86.2 cm and is held by the State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
credit: here / здесь

title: Jüdische Hochzeit in Marokko-1024
description: A woman dances before a crowd of seated guests in a whitewashed Moroccan interior, musicians playing at the centre of the room while onlookers press in from every side. Delacroix painted this scene of a Sephardi Jewish wedding in 1839, drawing on sketches made during his 1832 North African journey with the Comte de Mornay and translating direct observation into a Romantic study of colour and custom.

title: Panorama vom Kreml in Moskau
description: Gaertner's 1839 panorama depicts the Cathedral Square of the Moscow Kremlin, with the white-walled Cathedral of the Archangel surmounted by a golden onion dome dominating the right, and a succession of Kremlin towers receding along the battlemented wall to the left. Figures in period dress cross the broad paved square in the middle distance. The picture is typical of Gaertner's meticulous topographical work recording imperial Russian architecture during his travels of the late 1830s.
credit: Zeno.org , ID number 20004023838

title: Portrait of Edward Hicks Painting the Peaceable Kingdom
description: Thomas Hicks portrays his older cousin Edward Hicks seated in three-quarter pose, palette and brushes in hand, with a canvas showing animals and children from the Peaceable Kingdom visible on the easel beside him. Thomas Hicks painted the homage in 1839, when Edward was in his fifty-ninth year. The work commemorates the elder Hicks's lifelong devotion to his signature subject, drawn from Isaiah's prophecy of natural harmony.

title: The Fighting Temeraire tugged to her last berth to be broken up
description: The 98-gun veteran of Trafalgar is towed by a black steam tug along the Thames toward the breaker's yard, set against a smouldering sunset. Turner contrasts the pale, ghostly hulk with the squat industrial tug, mourning the passing of the age of sail.
credit: National Gallery of Art

title: The poor poet
description: A penniless poet lies in his cramped garret bed beneath a propped umbrella, one hand raised in poetic inspiration while books and papers lie scattered at his feet. Spitzweg's most celebrated Biedermeier image, painted in 1839 and now in the Bavarian State Painting Collections, distils the era's affectionate caricature of the impoverished literary eccentric.

title: (Barcelona) Stromy Sea with Blazing Wreck - William Turner - Tate Britain
description: A late Turner oil sketch in which a burning ship is nearly engulfed by towering surf and smoke. Paint is scrubbed and scraped into vortices of orange and lead grey, rendering catastrophe as pure elemental force. The work belongs to the Tate Bequest of unfinished canvases that Turner left in his studio at his death.

title: (Barcelona) The New Moon; or, ‘I’ve lost My Boat, You shan’t have Your Hoop’ - William Turner - Tate Britain
englishTitle: The New Moon; or, 'I've lost My Boat, You shan't have Your Hoop'
description: A small seaside scene from Turner's late period, where two children quarrel over a lost boat and a hoop on a wide tidal shore beneath a pale new moon. The trivial human anecdote is set against an expansive luminous sky and estuary, characteristic of Turner's mature handling of atmosphere and light. The work entered the national collection through the Turner Bequest and is held at Tate Britain.

title: Architect’s Dream
description: A figure reclines on a broad stone platform strewn with architectural drawings, gazing over a fantastical harbour where Gothic spires rise in the foreground and classical colonnades, a domed rotunda, and an Egyptian pyramid recede into the distance. Cole painted the canvas for architect Ithiel Town in 1840; it is now in the Toledo Museum of Art.

title: Der Schmetterlingsjäger
description: A naturalist in a light coat pursues two vivid blue butterflies through a lush tropical forest, net raised and mouth agape with excitement. Towering palms and broad exotic foliage dwarf the eccentric collector — a figure type Spitzweg returned to repeatedly in his Biedermeier comedies of bourgeois obsession. The work is held at Museum Wiesbaden (1840).

title: Kuniyoshi Utagawa, Pilgrims in the waterfall
description: Men bathe and swim in the pool beneath the Great Falls of Sekison at Ōyama in this woodblock print of c. 1840. Kuniyoshi exploits the vertical ōban format to dramatise the columnar fall of water, setting the bathers in scale against the sheer dark cliffs — a theatrical staging characteristic of his Utagawa-school training.

title: Schinkel3
description: An imagined interior of the reception hall in Schinkel's projected royal palace for King Otto on the Athenian Acropolis, with polychrome red-panelled walls, Corinthian columns, and a richly gilded beamed ceiling. Caryatid figures occupy the middle register, and bright light streams through the distant colonnade. Schinkel submitted his drawings in 1834 and the scheme was never built; the design was published in his Werke der höheren Baukunst (Berlin, 1840).
credit: Schinkel: Werke der höheren Baukunst für die Ausführung erfunden von Schinkel, Berlin 1840, Taf. 9; reproduction picture postcard Staatliche Schlösser und Gärten, Berlin

title: Sun Setting over a Lake
description: Form is reduced to bands of gold, rose and slate water in a late, near-abstract evocation of dusk. Pictures of this kind, left in his studio at his death, anticipate by half a century the dissolutions of Impressionism.

title: The Slave Ship
description: A slaver flings the dead and dying from its hold as a typhoon rises over a blood-orange sea, painted in response to the Zong massacre and abolitionist debate. Turner dissolves moral horror into dazzling atmosphere, the figures and chains barely surfacing through churning paint.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Waves Breaking against the Wind
description: A pure marine, the canvas is given entirely to a churning sea raked by spray. Turner reportedly had himself lashed to a mast in storms; the picture's loose, scumbled paint claims that immediacy.

title: Кронштадтский рейд Айвазовского
description: A marine painting by Russian seascape master Ivan Aivazovsky depicting the crowded anchorage at Kronstadt. Oil on canvas, 124 × 199 cm. Housed in the Central Naval Museum in Saint Petersburg.

title: Chaos. The Genesis
description: An angel of God hovers in cruciform pose above the dark turbulent waters of creation, light tearing the cloud apart behind him. Aivazovsky painted Chaos in Rome in 1841, his early twenties; it earned him a gold medal from Pope Gregory XVI and now hangs at the Mechitarist monastery of San Lazzaro degli Armeni in Venice.
credit: http://golgofa.kiev.ua/menu/cunst/bytie/909.html upload date: 12 January 2005, 15:25:34

title: Christ on the Sea of Galilee
description: In this Romantic interpretation of the Gospel storm narrative, Christ lies asleep amid the boat's huddled figures while the disciples gesture in fear and the sea churns around them. Painted in 1841, it is one of several versions Delacroix made of the subject, each exploring the contrast between divine calm and human terror.

title: Der Sonntagsspaziergang
description: A bourgeois family in their Sunday best parades down a country path under a parasol, the children straggling behind. Spitzweg captures the small comedies of Biedermeier ritual with affectionate, miniaturist precision.

title: Hatsuhana doing penance under the Tonosawa waterfall
description: From the series Lives of Wise Women and Virtuous Wives, Hatsuhana of the joruri play Hakone Reigen prays under the icy Tonosawa falls to obtain her crippled husband's revenge. Kuniyoshi treats the ascetic subject with characteristic dynamism, the cascading water rendered in steep blue parallel lines.

title: His Highness Muhemed Ali
description: Muhammad Ali, ruler of Egypt, sits in a wooden armchair wearing a fez and dark Ottoman dress, a jewelled sword resting across his lap. The Scottish painter David Wilkie met him in Egypt during travels in the Middle East and received this commission; the portrait, dated 1841, was among Wilkie's last works before he died at sea on the return voyage to Britain.

title: Karolina Lizius
description: Karolina Lizius (1820–1872) gazes outward in a dark off-shoulder velvet gown against a neutral brown ground, painted by Joseph Karl Stieler in 1841. Stieler served as court painter in Munich and contributed numerous portraits to Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie at Nymphenburg Palace. The smooth finish, restrained palette, and composed psychology are characteristic of his Biedermeier portrait formula.

title: Katerina Rosa Botsaris
description: The young daughter of a Greek War of Independence hero is shown in embroidered Greek costume, her dark hair loose beneath a tasselled cap. Stieler painted the portrait for Ludwig I of Bavaria's Schönheitengalerie, the Munich gallery of beauties in which the king collected idealised female likenesses.
credit: artvee.com

title: Portrait of Alessandro Manzoni
description: The novelist Alessandro Manzoni, author of I Promessi Sposi, sits in sober dark dress against a neutral ground, fixing the viewer with a measured gaze. Hayez treats the literary patriot of the Risorgimento with the restrained likeness and crisp drawing of the Italian Romantic portrait tradition.

title: Portrait of Louis-Alexandre Marolles
description: A bust-length likeness of Louis-Alexandre Marolles, the sitter turned slightly and set against a dark ground. Millet painted this portrait in 1841 during his early Cherbourg years, well before the rural subjects that made his name; the canvas is now in the Princeton University Art Museum.
credit: Princeton University Art Museum

title: Sir David Wilkie's residence in Kensington London
englishTitle: Sir David Wilkie's residence in Kensington London
description: A painting by English landscape and genre painter William Collins depicting the Kensington residence of fellow artist Sir David Wilkie, created in 1841 shortly after Wilkie's death. The work documents an important London townhouse associated with a prominent figure in British art history.

title: Campo Santo
description: A tall-masted barge drifts past the island cemetery of San Michele in the Venetian lagoon. Painted alongside its Royal Academy companion the Dogano, the work converts a place of burial into a study of pearled morning light.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"t/turner/2/2041turn"

title: Odalisque with Slave
englishTitle: Odalisque with Slave (Walters Art Museum, 1842; landscape by Jean-Paul Flandrin)
description: Commissioned by King Wilhelm I of Württemberg, the picture reclines an odalisque before a garden vista while a servant plays the lute. Ingres designed and largely painted it, with the landscape backdrop entrusted to his pupil Paul Flandrin.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Peace - Burial at Sea
description: Commemorates the sea burial of the painter David Wilkie off Gibraltar, the steamer's silhouette and inky black sails set against a flaring sun. Exhibited as a pendant to Turner's fiery 'War,' the picture pairs cool nocturnal calm with the warmth of mourning.
credit: http://www.tate.org.uk/art/artworks/turner-peace-burial-at-sea-n00528 2013-09-12 08:37:46

title: Portrait of Countess Julia Pavlovna Samoilova moving away from the ball with her adopted daughter Amazilia Pacini
englishTitle: Countess Yuliya Samoylova Leaving the Ball with Amazilia Pacini
description: Countess Yuliya Samoylova strides forward in a white ermine-trimmed gown before a sweeping crimson curtain, her adopted daughter Amazilia Pacini at her side. Karl Bryullov completed this life-size oil on canvas by 1842; it is held in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg (inv. Ж-5093).
credit: here / здесь

title: Samson and the lion
description: Samson stands upright over the fallen lion, his powerful torso bare and a drape gathered at his waist, gazing downward at the defeated beast in a wooded landscape. Francesco Hayez painted this monumental canvas in 1842, applying the academic Romantic manner he developed in Milan.

title: Snow Storm: Steam-Boat off a Harbour's Mouth
description: A paddle-steamer engulfed by a vortex of snow, smoke and sea, exhibited with Turner's claim that he had been lashed to the mast to observe it. Critics dismissed the canvas as 'soapsuds and whitewash', but it remains his definitive statement on the elemental sublime.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"t/turner/2/2040turn"

title: The Temple of Segesta with the Artist Sketching
description: The unfinished Doric temple at Segesta in western Sicily stands in a broad valley landscape with mountains and a distant lake behind it, while at lower right a seated figure — Cole himself — sketches the ruins, accompanied by a companion and a donkey. Cole worked up the canvas from drawings made during his European travels, and the composition blends precise archaeological observation with the warm Sicilian light of late afternoon. The painting is in the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts Boston

title: The Voyage of Life: Childhood
description: An infant rides in a richly gilded ornamental boat emerging from a rocky cavern, guided by a luminous winged angel through a lush, flower-strewn landscape. This is the first of four panels in Cole's 1842 version of The Voyage of Life, a moral allegory of the soul's earthly passage, held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: or; Picture taken at: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C., USA 3.-; National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: The Voyage of Life: Manhood
description: The traveller, now grown, clasps his hands in prayer as his rudderless boat plunges through a torrent of black rocks under storm clouds, the guardian angel watching from above. Third panel in Cole's 1842 second version of The Voyage of Life, painted in his Catskill studio after the New York set was sold off.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: The Voyage of Life: Old Age
description: The voyager, white-bearded, drifts on a glassy black sea while his angel gestures upward toward a host of celestial spirits breaking through the clouds. Fourth and final panel of the National Gallery's 1842 set, completing Cole's allegory of the Christian soul's passage from infancy to eternity.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: The Voyage of Life: Youth
description: The young traveller, now alone at the tiller, steers toward a shining cloud palace in the sky above a verdant river valley. Second panel in Cole's 1842 second version of The Voyage of Life series at the National Gallery of Art, painted after the original 1840 set passed into private hands.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Eugène Delacroix - Collision of Moorish Horsemen - Walters 376
description: Delacroix drew on his 1832 North African journey with Count de Mornay's diplomatic mission to evoke the violent equestrian games of the Moroccan court. The clashing horses and flying robes display the saturated, almost vibrating palette he developed after seeing Maghreb light at first hand.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Le Désespéré
description: A wide-eyed self-portrait, the young Courbet gripping his hair with both hands and staring directly out at the viewer with an expression of extreme agitation. Executed between 1843 and 1845, when the artist was in his mid-twenties, it announces the confrontational self-fashioning that would define his career and the Realist project. The canvas is now in a private collection.

title: Light and Colour
description: A vortex of golden light spirals around the figure of Moses inscribing Genesis, with a serpent and submerged figures at its rim. Turner conceived the picture as a pendant illustrating Goethe's theory of positive, light-giving colour.

title: Siege of Pskov by Polish king en:Stefan Batory
description: Russian defenders led by clergy carrying Orthodox icons and banners surge against armoured Polish-Lithuanian troops in this monumental depiction of Stefan Batory's 1581 siege of Pskov. The canvas, dated 1843 in the catalogue record, was left unfinished at Bryullov's death and represents one of his most ambitious historical compositions. The confrontation of faith and force — priests and banners on one side, helmeted soldiers on the other — charges the scene with dramatic tension.
credit: From http://lj.rossia.org/users/john_petrov/441790.html

title: The Sun of Venice Going to Sea
credit: Google Arts & Culture — dwEYd5yKW43wWQ Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00535&wwwflag=3&imagepos=5 )

title: Wohnzimmer des Schlossermeisters C.F.A. Hauschild in Berlin
description: The sitting room of the Berlin locksmith C.F.A. Hauschild on Stralauer Strasse 49, with blue patterned wallpaper, a large wardrobe and mirror at left, framed pictures on the walls, and a family group at various occupations across the room. Eduard Gaertner, who trained as a porcelain painter at KPM, made a speciality of Biedermeier-era interiors and Berlin views, and painted this domestic scene in 1843.

title: Богоматерь с младенцем в розах
description: The young Mary stands by a low stone wall, the Christ Child against her, roses banked behind them. Bruni painted this oil, 'Madonna with Child in Roses', in 1843; it measures roughly 64 by 40 cm and is held in the State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
credit: art-catalog.ru

title: (Barcelona) Lake Lucerne ; the Bay of Uri from above Brunnen - William Turner - Tate Britain
englishTitle: Lake Lucerne: The Bay of Uri from above Brunnen
description: A watercolour from Turner's late Swiss tours, when he returned repeatedly to Lake Lucerne in search of atmospheric subjects. From the heights above Brunnen the bay opens in pale washes of blue and pearl, mountains dissolving into the luminous haze that defined his final manner. The sheet belongs to a celebrated group of Swiss studies now held by Tate Britain.

title: A View of the Two Lakes and Mountain House
description: Morning mist lifts off the twin Catskill lakes as the white-pillared Catskill Mountain House perches on a cliff above. Cole lived in the village of Catskill from 1836 and painted this 1844 view of the famous hotel that had drawn tourists to the Hudson Valley since 1824.

title: Fishing Boats Bringing a Disabled Ship into Port Ruysdael
description: Boats tow a damaged sailing ship into the imaginary Dutch harbour of Port Ruysdael, Turner's homage to Jacob van Ruisdael. Painted late in his career, the canvas dissolves rigging and breaking sea into broad sweeps of grey, white and salt. It is one of several pictures in which Turner used invented Dutch place-names as a critical tribute.

title: Incontro di Giobbe ed Esaù
englishTitle: The Meeting of Jacob and Esau
description: The painting illustrates Jacob's return to his homeland, asking forgiveness from his brother Esau for having deceived his birthright. Biblical subjects had a lot of luck around the mid-nineteenth century, as the suffering of the Jewish people recalled the Italian political situation.

title: Rain
description: A Great Western Railway locomotive races across Maidenhead Bridge through curtains of rain, the iron viaduct dissolving into vapour and golden light. The picture is a defining statement of the modern industrial sublime, painted with palette knife and finger as much as brush.
credit: National Gallery, London

title: Takiyasha the Witch and the Skeleton Spectre
description: A nishiki-e triptych staging the sorceress Takiyasha as she summons a colossal skeleton against the warrior Mitsukuni in the ruined Soma palace. Kuniyoshi compresses three full sheets into one continuous, theatrically lit scene drawn from the gothic literature of late Edo.
credit: Takiyasha_the_Witch_and_the_Skeleton_Spectre_1.jpg Takiyasha_the_Witch_and_the_Skeleton_Spectre_2.jpg Takiyasha_the_Witch_and_the_Skeleton_Spectre_3.jpg

title: THE ABDUCTION OF THE SABINE WOMEN
description: Roman men seize struggling Sabine women in a tangle of figures, a classical history subject. Millet worked the canvas around 1844 to 1847, in the period before he settled at Barbizon and turned to peasant labour; the scene follows the Livy episode long favoured by academic painters.

title: Van Tromp
description: The Dutch admiral Maarten Tromp puts his ship about in heavy weather, a subject Turner returned to repeatedly in his last decade. The picture extends his admiration for the seventeenth-century Dutch marine tradition into a high-key, Romantic key.

title: Venice Quay
description: The Doge's Palace and the Riva degli Schiavoni shimmer through lagoon light in a late Venetian view. By his third trip to Venice in 1840 Turner was treating the city's stones as little more than coloured vapour.

title: Feminine Wave
description: A massive, circular wave curls inward on itself, its deep indigo interior flecked with white and its outer rim dissolving into swirling foam, filling the composition from edge to edge. Katsushika Hokusai's 'Feminine Wave' (c. 1845) was conceived as the companion to his 'Masculine Wave', and together they demonstrate his late-career treatment of water as pure dynamic form within the ukiyo-e tradition.

title: Norham Castle
description: Norham Castle on the River Tweed dissolves into a luminous haze of pale yellow and blue, the sun a glowing disc in the upper half of the composition and the castle keep just barely legible as a dark blue mass. A cow wading in the foreground water is all that anchors the scene to the tangible world. Painted in 1845 and held at Tate (National Gallery collection), this late oil is among the most radical of Turner's near-abstract works.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"t/turner/2/206turne" http://www.tate.org.uk/art/artworks/turner-norham-castle-sunrise-n01981

title: Portrait of Alexandra Amalie von Bayern
dateCreated: 1845, replica of a portrait painted in 1838
description: A Schönheitengalerie portrait of Princess Alexandra of Bavaria, daughter of Ludwig I, rendered in Stieler's characteristic porcelain finish. The sitter is shown with the soft idealization the Munich court demanded of its gallery of beauties.

title: Portrait of Comtesse d'Haussonville
description: A society portrait of Louise de Broglie, comtesse d'Haussonville, that Ingres laboured over for three years and that now hangs in the Frick Collection. Mirror, ribboned slippers and porcelain are arranged with linear precision, while the sitter's improbably elongated arm exemplifies the artist's controlled anatomical license.

title: Portrait of Friederike Freiin Von Gumppenberg
description: Friederike Freiin von Gumppenberg is depicted half-length against a luminous outdoor landscape of sky, hills, and water, wearing a deep crimson velvet wrap over a white dress with dark curling hair loose at her shoulders. The open background distinguishes this circa-1845 entry in Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie, now held at Nymphenburg Palace, from the darker grounds of Stieler's earlier portraits in the cycle.

title: The Balcony Room
description: An empty room, white curtains billowing at the open balcony door, a sofa half-glimpsed in a wall mirror. Menzel made the small oil for himself, capturing transient sunlight with the immediacy of a snapshot decades before plein-air Impressionism reached Berlin.

title: The Galata Tower by Moonlight
description: The Galata Tower rises over the Golden Horn under moonlight, masts and rooftops picked out in silver across the water. Aivazovsky painted this view in 1845 after visiting Constantinople with Grand Duke Konstantin Nikolaevich; the oil measures about 52 by 80 cm.
credit: Sotheby's, London, 26 November 2012, lot 5

title: Battle of Vyborg Bay
description: Russian galleys and ships of the line break through the Swedish fleet trapped in Vyborg Bay in June 1790, smoke from broadside fire rolling across the Baltic. Aivazovsky painted the engagement in 1846 as part of a Naval Ministry commission documenting Russian victories at sea.

title: Boat Ride by Kumkapi in Constantinople
description: A boat carrying several Ottoman figures, including a veiled woman and attendants, glides along a narrow waterway bordered by lush vegetation and an ornate timber-framed building with arched windows. Ivan Aivazovsky painted this 1846 canvas during his travels in the Ottoman Empire, and the intimate garden setting and richly dressed passengers reflect the Orientalist mode he pursued alongside his marine subjects.

title: Building Site with Willows
description: Menzel turns a humble Berlin construction site, fringed by drooping willows, into a study of weather and labour. The unposed subject and freshly observed light anticipate the realist vein the Prussian painter would pursue across decades of obsessive sketching from life.

title: Coffee-house by the Ortaköy Mosque in Constantinople
description: Figures in Ottoman dress gather at a waterfront coffee-house, smoking a hookah and playing music, with the Ortaköy Mosque and its minaret rising across the Bosphorus in the background. Painted by Ivan Aivazovsky in 1846, the canvas records the site during one of his Near Eastern travels, capturing the atmospheric haze and golden light typical of his marine and coastal work.

title: Noah's Ark
description: Pairs of animals — lions, horses, zebras, goats and many others — are gathered on the hillside around the great wooden ark beneath a stormy, darkening sky. Edward Hicks, the Quaker minister and sign painter from Bucks County, Pennsylvania, based this 1846 canvas on the Genesis flood narrative, rendering the scene with the flat, vivid colours characteristic of his folk-art manner.

title: Orlando Pursuing the Fata Morgana
description: Orlando lunges after the fleeing sorceress Fata Morgana, a scene drawn from Boiardo's epic 'Orlando Innamorato'. Watts began the canvas in Italy in 1846 and finished it in London by 1848; the oil, 165 by 120 cm, was given by the artist to the Leicester Museum and Art Gallery in 1888.

title: Pizarro Seizing the Inca of Peru
description: Painted when Millais was barely seventeen and exhibited at the Royal Academy, this dramatic history scene shows the conquistador wresting Atahualpa from his throne amid scattering attendants. The crowded composition and bright local colour announce the precocious draughtsmanship he would soon channel into the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.

title: Sea Battle at Navarino on October 20
description: Warships flying Russian and Ottoman flags exchange fire in Navarino Bay on 20 October 1827, masts toppling and flames rising as gunsmoke rolls across the open water. Painted in 1846, Aivazovsky's canvas records the allied action that effectively secured Greek independence, with survivors visible in small boats in the foreground.

title: The Battle of Revel
description: Aivazovsky depicts the naval engagement of May 1790 off Reval, with Russian and Swedish ships of the line exchanging fire amid billowing gunsmoke on a choppy green Baltic Sea, a town skyline faintly visible on the right horizon. Painted in 1846, the canvas is held in the Naval Museum of St Petersburg.
credit: ( Original text: Naval museum of St. Petersburg, Russia. ), Original uploader was Pietje96 at en.wikipedia , (4 January 2010 (original upload date))

title: The Russian Squadron on the Sebastopol Roads
description: Black Sea Fleet warships ride at anchor in the roadstead of Sevastopol under a glassy sunset, the masts and yards of the squadron silhouetted against a pearl-coloured sky. Painted in 1846, the year Aivazovsky was appointed senior painter to the Russian Naval Staff and supplied with a studio at the fleet's home port.

title: Undine Giving the Ring to Massaniello
description: A fantastical pairing of the water-nymph Undine, drawn from de la Motte Fouqué's novella, with the Neapolitan fisherman-rebel Masaniello. Painted at seventy-one, the canvas dissolves narrative into a swirl of aquatic colour typical of Turner's late square-format mythologies.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"t/turner/2/208turne"

title: View of Constantinople by evening light
description: Aivazovsky surveys Constantinople from an elevated hillside at sunset, the Galata Tower — still bearing its original conical roof, destroyed by storm in 1875 — rising above the Golden Horn, the city and its minarets stretching across the horizon. Figures in Ottoman dress rest in the foreground under a large tree. The oil painting dates to 1846 and is held at the Cottage Palace in Peterhof.
credit: 1, The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic via wikipaintings.org 2. art-catalog.ru

title: Петр I при Красной горке Айвазовский
description: Oil on canvas depicting Tsar Peter I at Red Hill, painted in 1846. The work measures 223 x 335 cm and is housed in the State Russian Museum in Saint Petersburg. Aivazovsky's historical narrative captures a moment from Russian imperial history in his characteristic dramatic style.

title: Accusa segreta
description: A Venetian noblewoman pauses by the bocca di leone, the lion's-mouth letterbox into which secret denunciations were dropped under the Republic. Hayez, leader of Italian Romantic painting, often coded contemporary Risorgimento politics into such historical scenes, here rendered with his porcelain-smooth flesh and rich brocades.

title: At first glance he looks fierce, but he's really a nice person
description: A glowering giant's face is, on closer look, made up entirely of squirming naked men — a sly anatomical pun on the proverb in the title. Kuniyoshi produced such jigsaw figures to slip past Tempō-era censorship that restricted depictions of named actors and courtesans.

title: Home in the Woods
description: A settler fishes at the edge of a wilderness lake while women and children tend to chores before a log cabin on the right bank, mountains rising behind. Thomas Cole painted this Hudson River School canvas in 1847; it is held at the Reynolda House Museum of American Art in Winston-Salem.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; Reynolda House Museum of American Art

title: Lola Montez
description: The Irish-born dancer who styled herself a Spanish noblewoman, painted at the height of her hold over Ludwig I of Bavaria. Her place in the Schönheitengalerie was itself a small political event, the affair contributing to the king's abdication the following year.

title: Prometheus Bound
description: The Titan Prometheus is chained to a crag of the Caucasus at dawn, an eagle wheeling above to tear at his liver, the sun rising behind distant snow-capped peaks. Exhibited at the National Academy of Design in 1847, Cole's late mythological piece adapts Aeschylus to the vertical drama of the Hudson River sublime.

provenance.collection: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco
provenance.location: M. H. de Young Memorial Museum

title: Tamar
description: Tamar, daughter-in-law of Judah, is shown as a near-full-length figure pulling open her ochre mantle to reveal her breast, a shepherd's staff in one hand and a gold collar at her throat. Hayez, the leading painter of Italian Romanticism, treats this Old Testament heroine with characteristic sensuality, combining theatrical pose and warm Mediterranean light. The painting, dated 1847, is held at Masnago Castle.
credit: deartibus.it

title: Barrikade in der Breiten Straße
description: Gaertner's 1848 painting records a barricade erected in the Breite Strasse in Berlin during the March revolution, a black-red-gold tricolour flag planted at its summit against the façade of a large urban building. Eduard Gaertner was Berlin's foremost topographical painter, and this work stands as one of the few contemporary pictorial records of the street fighting of 18–19 March 1848.

title: Battle of Çesme at Night
description: Ottoman ships burn in the bay of Cesme as the Russian fleet under Alexei Orlov destroys the Turkish line on the night of 25-26 June 1770. Painted in 1848 and now in the Aivazovsky National Gallery at Feodosia, the canvas belongs to the marine painter's cycle of naval victories commissioned during his years as official painter to the Russian Admiralty.

title: hanging scroll
description: A hanging scroll depicting the arhat Handaka Sonja, shaven-headed and wearing large earrings, summoning a small dragon from his begging bowl amid a coiling rain cloud. Executed in ink and slight colour on paper, signed and sealed, and dated c. 1848–1854, the work demonstrates the muscular brushwork Kuniyoshi refined in his celebrated warrior compositions.

title: In the Berkshires
description: A traveller with a horse pauses on a rocky path through the Massachusetts hills as a dramatic sunset breaks through storm clouds, illuminating dense foliage in the middle ground. George Inness painted the picture between 1848 and 1850, early in his career when he was working close to the Hudson River School manner. The work is held in the Colección Carmen Thyssen-Bornemisza on deposit at the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid.
credit: Colección Carmen Thyssen-Bornemisza en depósito en el Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza

title: Menzel's sister Emilie
description: Menzel's sister Emilie sleeps in a chair, her head sunk forward and her figure enveloped in loose drapery, rendered in the broadly handled, warm-toned manner of Menzel's private domestic studies of around 1848. These informal oils, kept off the public exhibitions, anticipate Impressionist handling in their sketchy touch and unsentimentalised observation of momentary repose. The work is held at the Hamburger Kunsthalle.

title: Self-portrait Karl Brjullow
description: Bryullov turns to face the viewer in a dark coat, his arm resting against a red cushioned support, the pallor of illness evident in his gaunt features. He painted this self-portrait in Rome in 1848 during convalescence, and it now hangs in the State Tretyakov Gallery.

title: Self-Portrait with Pipe
description: An early self-portrait from Courbet's Romantic-tinged youth, the painter shown smoking a long pipe with hooded eyes and a tilted head. Strong dark-on-dark modelling and a deliberately bohemian air announce the self-mythologising persona he would build through the 1850s.
credit: Musée Fabre

title: The brig Mercury encounter after defeating two Turkish ships of the Russian squadron
description: The brig Mercury rejoins the Russian squadron after its 1829 escape from two Turkish line ships near the Bosphorus, sails crowding the horizon. Aivazovsky painted this commemoration in 1848, an oil of about 123.5 by 190 cm now in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg.
credit: bankaustria-kunstforum.at

title: The Cornell Farm
description: Cattle, horses and other livestock are paraded in the foreground of a broad pastoral landscape, with white fences, bare-branched trees and farm buildings stretching towards rolling hills behind them. Edward Hicks painted this farmstead view in 1848 in the same folk-art manner he brought to his Peaceable Kingdom series — carefully observed animals set within an ordered, sunlit countryside.
credit: Via worldart.sjsu.edu

title: Carl Spitzweg - Im Dachstübchen
description: Carl Spitzweg's oil painting shows an elderly man in cap and spectacles leaning from his garret window to water the flowers crowding his window box, birdcages hanging from the eaves above and church towers rising over the rooftops; far below, a child tends potted plants at another window. Painted around 1848-49, it is characteristic of Spitzweg's affectionate Biedermeier observations of modest life in old German towns. The painting is in a private collection.

title: Kagesue
englishTitle: Kagesue, Takatsuna and Shigetada Crossing the Uji River
description: Across a three-sheet triptych, armoured samurai on horseback and on foot surge through the rapids of the Uji River in their celebrated race to lead the charge during the Genpei War. Kuniyoshi fills each panel with churning waves and straining figures, exemplifying the warrior-print genre (musha-e) he revived in the late Edo period. The work dates to 1849 and is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
credit: Ukiyo-e.org [1] (Museum of Fine Arts Boston)

title: Portrait of Sophia Shuvalova
description: Sophia Shuvalova (1829–1912), later Countess Bobrinskaya, is shown in a white off-shoulder lace dress, holding a red flower against a lush garden background with trees and a bridge glimpsed beyond. Karl Bryullov painted the portrait in 1849, at a time when he was living abroad for his health, a few years before his death in Manziana in 1852.

title: Stormy sea at night
description: A three-masted ship rolls in heavy seas under a broken moon, its sails reefed against the swell, foam glowing pale where the waves crest. Aivazovsky painted dozens of nocturnal storm scenes throughout the 1840s, perfecting the thinly glazed translucent water that became his signature.

title: The Haunted Manor
description: A garden stream runs through a series of wooden sluice boards in the foreground, bordered by irises and dense summer vegetation, while the timber gables of a building are glimpsed through the trees at upper right. Painted in 1849 and now in the Tate collection, the work displays Hunt's meticulous early Pre-Raphaelite attention to botanical and textural detail rendered in warm evening light.

title: The Wreck Buoy
description: A scarlet buoy bobs above a foundered hull as a low rainbow arcs over a ruffled sea. One of Turner's last completed oils, the picture reworks an earlier seascape into a meditation on hazard and salvage.

title: Boar Lane
description: A wet Leeds thoroughfare at night, gas lamps casting warm amber light on glazed shopfronts and the glistening pavement below. Grimshaw built a career on these meticulously observed urban nocturnes, balancing precise architectural detail with a painterly command of artificial light and its reflections.

title: Cats Suggested as The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō
description: Kuniyoshi, a noted cat lover, replaces every post town on the Tōkaidō highway with a cat whose pose or attribute puns on the station's name. The triptych is a tour de force of Edo wordplay (mitate) and ukiyo-e woodblock printing, made when actor prints had been restricted by Tenpō reform censorship.

title: Der Maler auf einer Waldlichtung
description: A plein-air painter has stretched out on his back beneath a propped umbrella in a forest clearing, a folding stool and hat lying nearby. Painted around 1850 in oil on canvas (49.5 × 30.2 cm), the picture is a gentle self-mockery of the Romantic artist's communion with nature, entirely characteristic of Spitzweg's wry, intimate vision.
credit: Joachim Nagel: Carl Spitzweg. Belser, Stuttgart 2008, S. 11

title: Frederick the Great Playing the Flute at Sanssouci
description: Menzel reconstructs an evening concert at Sanssouci, with Frederick the Great playing flute beside C.P.E. Bach at the harpsichord and Quantz, Benda, and the Margravine Wilhelmine listening. Painted under Friedrich Wilhelm IV, it crowns the artist's long Prussian historical project.

title: Susanna at Her Bath
description: The biblical Susanna twists modestly at her bath, surprised by the elders whose presence is implied beyond the frame. Hayez handles the polished nude in the National Gallery, London, with a sculptural finish indebted to Canova and the warm tonalities of his Venetian training.
credit: the second upload from File:Francesco Hayez 054.jpg; -; National Gallery, London - online catalogue

title: Tänzerinnen in Blau
description: Four ballerinas in vivid blue tutus stand in a group, adjusting their shoulders and costumes, their faces largely averted from the viewer. Degas worked this pastel from the 1870s onward; the work, titled Tänzerinnen in Blau, hangs in the Pushkin Museum in Moscow.

title: The Bookworm
description: Spitzweg's elderly bibliophile stands high on a library ladder, spectacles on his nose, a volume open in his hands and more books wedged under both arms and between his knees, oblivious to everything but the shelf marked 'Metaphysics'. Painted around 1850, the picture is a gentle Biedermeier satire of bookish absorption and one of Spitzweg's best-loved subjects.

title: The Church at Vétheuil
description: The tower of Vétheuil's medieval church rises above the huddled roofs of the village, seen across the Seine with the whole scene loosening into broken reflections on the water. Monet lived at Vétheuil from 1878 to 1881, painting the small town and its church repeatedly from the river and the opposite bank. This oil on canvas is in the Southampton City Art Gallery.

title: The Ninth Wave
description: Shipwrecked survivors cling to a makeshift raft of timbers and rigging as the towering ninth wave — said in Russian seafaring lore to be the most destructive of a storm — rises beneath a luminous dawn sky. Aivazovsky completed the painting in 1850 in Saint Petersburg; it has remained at the Russian Museum since the Imperial collection and is regarded as the defining canvas of Russian Romantic marine painting.

title: Mariana
description: Drawn from Tennyson's poem after the Shakespearean character, Mariana stretches wearily at her embroidery beside a stained-glass window, autumn leaves drifting onto the floor. Millais paints the heraldic glass and velvet gown with founding Pre-Raphaelite precision, every fibre and pane separately observed.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — 6wGvnPEiyH8RFA Also available at http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=T07553&wwwflag=3&imagepos=41 .

title: Ophelia
description: Shakespeare's drowning Ophelia drifts among meadow flowers along the Hogsmill River in Surrey. Millais painted the riverbank botany on site over five months, then posed Elizabeth Siddal in a heated bathtub for the figure. Each bloom carries Victorian floral symbolism for grief, innocence and madness.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — -wGU6cT4JixtPA Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N01506&wwwflag=3&imagepos=2 )

title: Poplars in the Sun
description: A woman with a parasol walks through a sun-filled field beneath a row of tall poplars whose foliage catches the afternoon light in loose strokes of gold and green. Titled 'Poplars in the Sun' and held at the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, the canvas shows Monet studying the same motif that preoccupied him through the early 1890s, here combining landscape and figure under the dappled shade of the trees.

title: Portrait of Princess Albert de Broglie
description: Joséphine-Élénore-Marie-Pauline de Galard de Brassac de Béarn, Princesse Albert de Broglie, is shown seated in a luminous blue satin gown against a grey-green panelled interior, a heraldic device visible at upper right. Painted by Ingres between 1851 and 1853 near the end of his career, the portrait is now a centrepiece of the Robert Lehman Collection at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
credit: This file was derived from: Jean auguste dominique ingres princesse albert de broglie.jpg :

title: Porträt der Madame Moitessier
description: Madame Moitessier stands in a black velvet dress with bare arms adorned by heavy gold bracelets, her composure and jewellery conveying the social weight Ingres accorded his Parisian sitters. Ingres laboured over his two Moitessier portraits across more than a decade, prizing the linear contour and porcelain finish that define his late society style; this standing version of 1851 belongs to the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: An Idyll
description: An early pastoral by Gérôme in the vein of his Néo-Grec circle, reaching back to Anacreontic and Pompeian models. Slender nudes, shallow stage-like space and porcelain-cool color place the picture closer to his Greek Interior than to his later Orientalist scenes.
credit: Musée Massey athenaeum.org

title: Back View of Fuji from Dream Mtn in Kai Province
englishTitle: Back View of Fuji from the Dream Mountain in Kai Province
description: Hiroshige reverses the conventional southern view of Fuji, glimpsing the sacred peak from Kai Province on the mountain's far side. Part of his first Thirty-six Views series, the design uses graduated bokashi printing to layer mist, peak, and foreground.
credit: Ukiyo-e.org [3]; Hiroshige.org.uk [4]

title: Sokokura by Hiroshige1
englishTitle: Sokokura, from Seven Hot Springs of Hakone
description: A woodblock view of Sokokura, one of the seven hot springs of Hakone, with travelers moving along a path through a steep wooded mountain gorge beside a rushing stream. The print belongs to Hiroshige's series Hakone shichiyu zue, devoted to the spa villages prized by Edo-period travellers along the Tōkaidō, and dates to 1852.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts Boston

title: Unter den Linden
description: Berlin's grand boulevard stretches past the equestrian statue of Frederick the Great, with the Königliche Oper on the right and the dome of the Stadtschloss closing the vista. Gaertner, the city's pre-eminent vedutista, charts the Prussian capital with architect's precision under a clear summer light.

title: Awa Province : Naruto Whirlpools
englishTitle: Awa Province: Naruto Whirlpools, from the series Famous Places in the Sixty-odd Provinces
description: A vertical ōban from the Famous Places in the Sixty-odd Provinces series, looking down on the swirling Naruto whirlpools that churn between Awa and Awaji. Hiroshige flattens the sea into concentric arcs of bokashi blue, framed by a steep cliff at left.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, online database

title: Battle of sinope
description: Aivazovsky shows the Russian attack on the Ottoman fleet at the harbour of Sinope, with burning ships flying Ottoman colours on the left and Russian men-of-war delivering broadsides through dense white smoke under a turbulent daytime sky. Painted in 1853, the year of the engagement, the work commemorates Admiral Nakhimov's victory at the opening of the Crimean War and is held at the Naval School in St Petersburg.
credit: ( Original text: Naval school, St. Petersburg, Russia. ) Original uploader was Pietje96 at en.wikipedia

title: Cimabue's Celebrated Madonna is carried in Procession through the Streets of Florence
description: A long procession bears Cimabue's altarpiece of the Madonna through Florence toward Santa Maria Novella, the painter Cimabue leading with the boy Giotto. Leighton painted this over two metres tall and more than five metres wide in Rome between 1853 and 1855; Queen Victoria bought it on the opening day of the 1855 Royal Academy exhibition for 600 guineas.

title: Cornelis Springer
englishTitle: House Once Inhabited by Rembrandt on the Jodenbreestraat, Amsterdam
description: The Jodenbreestraat in Amsterdam, with the house once occupied by Rembrandt at number 4-6 reimagined in its supposed seventeenth-century guise, the Sint-Antoniesluis at right and the tower of the Zuiderkerk rising behind. Springer, a Romantic topographical painter, treated the city as a chain of historicising stage sets rather than the contemporary streetscape.

title: Hiroshige Kozuke
englishTitle: Kōzuke Province: Mount Haruna Under Snow
description: Print No. 26 from Hiroshige's series "Famous Places in the Sixty-odd Provinces," depicting Mount Haruna in Kōzuke Province blanketed in snow. A landmark work of the Tōsandō group within the series, created in August 1853 during the artist's mature period.

title: The Awakening Conscience
description: A young woman starts up from her lover's lap in a cluttered London parlour, her face caught at the instant of moral recognition. Hunt loaded the picture with Pre-Raphaelite symbolism, every object on the patterned wallpaper, the discarded glove, the cat at the table chosen to spell out the cost of a kept woman's situation.

title: The Order of Release 1746
description: A Highland wife hands a release order to a red-coated soldier while her wounded Jacobite husband, arm in a sling, leans toward her in gratitude; she carries their red-haired child and a collie dog stands between them. Effie Ruskin posed for the wife, and the sittings precipitated her separation from John Ruskin and eventual marriage to Millais. The painting, dated 1853, is celebrated as one of the most dramatic works of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.

title: The Sleeping Spinner
description: A young spinner has fallen asleep at her wheel, distaff drooping in her lap. Courbet treats the rural genre subject with monumental gravity, applying paint thickly with knife and brush so that the homely interior carries the weight of a Salon picture.
credit: Musée Fabre

title: A woman baking bread
description: A woman slides a loaf into an oven, sleeves pushed back, the dough and peel close to hand. Millet painted this domestic labour in 1854, one of the Barbizon peasant subjects that defined his mature work.

title: Christ on the Sea of Galilee
description: Christ sleeps in the stern of a fishing boat while terrified apostles wrestle the sail against a green wall of water. Delacroix returned to the Gospel subject repeatedly in the 1850s, each version intensifying the chromatic clash between the storm and the calm figure asleep in its centre.

title: Das Ständchen
description: A lone violinist perches on a rooftop wall, hat on head and back turned to the viewer, playing into the open air of a quiet town. Spitzweg's Ständchen subjects typically savour the absurdity of private Romantic impulse played out in a small-town public space. This vertical panel dates to 1854.

title: Roman Pilgrims
description: A group of pilgrims is gathered inside a richly decorated basilica interior, its walls hung with devotional images and draped textiles, the floor spread with carpets. Women and children in regional Italian costume rest and pray amid the architectural splendour of the sacred space. Painted in 1854 and held at the Yale Center for British Art, the work applies the ethnographic precision Lewis would become famous for in his Orientalist pictures to the religious folk culture of Italy.

title: The Finding of the Saviour in the Temple
The Painter's Studio
description: A monumental allegory of seven years of Courbet's artistic life, gathering critics, patrons, and anonymous figures around the painter at his easel, with a nude muse and small boy looking on. Rejected from the 1855 Exposition Universelle, it became the centrepiece of his self-organised Pavilion of Realism in Paris.

title: Watts marie fox
description: Portrait of Mary Fox (1850-1878) (later Princess Marie of Liechtenstein), adopted daughter of Henry Fox, 4th Baron Holland (1802-1859), of Holland House, Kensington, with her Spanish pointer Elia . In her history of Holland House (Liechtenstein, Princess Marie, Holland House, 2 Vols. , London, 1874, p.
credit: Barbara Bryant, GF Watts, Portraits: Fame and Beauty in Victorian Society .

title: Arab saddling his horse
description: An Arab horseman in a white burnoose tends to his chestnut horse, reaching up to adjust the animal's bridle while it stands restless beside him. A pistol and red cloth lie on the ground in the foreground. Painted in 1855, the work draws on sketches from Delacroix's 1832 journey to Morocco and is catalogued under the title 'Arab saddling his horse.'

title: Arabian nights 3 by John Frederick Lewis
englishTitle: An Armenian Lady, Cairo – The Love Missive
description: An Armenian woman reclines in a sunlit Cairo interior, beside a latticed window and richly coloured carpets, in a scene identified by its full title as 'The Love Missive'. Lewis painted the work in 1855, drawing on the decade he had spent living in Cairo; the jewel-like handling of light across costume and tilework is characteristic of his mature watercolour and oil technique.

title: Im Harem
description: A bearded man in a red fez and dark, fur-trimmed robes sits beside a hookah pipe while a woman leans against him in a dimly lit interior. Spitzweg's orientalist fantasy draws on European print culture rather than direct observation, rendering the harem through a Biedermeier lens of wry domesticity. The painting, dated after 1855, is held at Museum Georg Schäfer.

title: Rear view of the Houses at Schloßfreiheit
description: Gaertner's 1855 painting records the rear façades of the middle-class houses lining the Schloßfreiheit along the Spree, with the dome of the palace rising behind and strollers along the opposite bank. The source description notes gold and silver shops and warehouses fronting the row, overshadowed by Schinkel's Building Academy to the right. The entire street was demolished in 1896 to make way for the Wilhelmine Monument to Emperor Wilhelm I.

title: Rider Attacked by a Jaguar
description: A jaguar springs from a thicket onto the haunches of a rearing horse, its rider thrown back as the predator's claws sink into the animal's flank. Delacroix borrowed the motif from Rubens and the Stubbs lion-and-horse tradition, condensing the struggle into a tight vertical of intersecting muscle.

title: Rocks at Mouthier by Gustave Courbet
description: A close-up view of weathered limestone cliffs near the artist's native Franche-Comté, the river snaking through a narrow valley below. Courbet builds the rock face with palette-knife slabs of paint, asserting landscape as raw geological matter rather than picturesque scenery.

title: The intercepted love letter
description: Two figures lean over a window balcony on the upper storey of an old German townhouse, reading what appears to be an intercepted letter while figures in neighbouring windows look on. Spitzweg's handling of the ornate façade, animated characters, and warm light exemplifies his affectionate, narratively rich approach to Biedermeier genre painting.

title: The Potato Harvest
description: After moving from Paris to the village of Barbizon on the edge of the Fontainebleau forest in 1851, Millet devoted himself to portraying the lives of his neighbors. Some critics interpreted his paintings of working farmers as a critique of the injustices inherent in the social conditions of his time. Others have seen his work as a representation of man's harmonious union with nature.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Woman Spinning
description: A standing woman draws thread from a distaff, her spindle turning at her side. Millet returned to spinners repeatedly in these years; the oil, painted about 1855 to 1860, belongs to the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute in Williamstown.
credit: Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute

title: A Frank Encampment in the Desert of Mount Sinai
description: A British traveller's tent camp pitched in the Sinai wilderness, with St Catherine's monastery faintly visible in the distance. Lewis drew on a decade of life in Cairo to render carpets, tasselled saddles and Bedouin retainers with miniaturist exactitude. The watercolour fuses Orientalist reportage with the topographical tradition.

title: Achille De Gas in the Uniform of a Cadet
description: The artist's younger brother Achille stands in the dark uniform of a French naval cadet, a gold aiguillette at his shoulder and one hand resting on a stone ledge. Painted around 1856-57 while Degas was beginning his Italian study years, the canvas is held by the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art .

title: Male Nude
description: An academic study in oil on canvas of a reclining male nude, painted by Edgar Degas around 1856 during his years as a young art student in Paris. The canvas was reused, and traces of an earlier figure study, including toes and a bearded face, remain visible beneath the present nude. The painting is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, a gift of Philip and Catherine Korsant in 2007.

title: Milton
description: A solitary figure sits on a fallen log at the edge of a placid stream, surrounded by dense woodland under a grey, overcast sky. George Inness made this sketch-like work around 1856, approaching the more atmospheric, tonally restrained manner he would develop after his European study trips. The work is held at the Yale University Art Gallery, New Haven.
credit: Yale University Art Gallery, Yale University, New Haven, Conn.

title: Sumida River
englishTitle: Suijin Shrine and Massaki on the Sumida River, from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
description: From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, the print frames the Sumida River through the trees of the Suijin shrine grove at Masaki. Hiroshige uses the steep foreground branches and high horizon characteristic of the late series to fold the viewer into the riverside scene.
credit: Image: http://collections.lacma.org/sites/default/files/remote_images/piction/ma-18199982-O3.jpg Gallery: http://collections.lacma.org/node/190172 archive copy at the Wayback Machine

title: Tempest by Sounion
description: A storm breaks over the headland of Cape Sounion on the southern tip of Attica, the ruined columns of the Temple of Poseidon picked out above churning sea. Aivazovsky, court painter to the Russian navy, treated the Aegean coastline as a stage for Romantic seascape rather than archaeological record.

title: The Lackawanna Valley
description: A seated figure in a red jacket and hat rests on a hillside above the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad roundhouse outside Scranton, Pennsylvania, watching a locomotive trail steam through a cleared valley dotted with stumps. George Inness painted the panorama around 1856, commissioned to celebrate the new railroad while embedding industrial expansion within a pastoral Hudson River idiom. The work is now at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: The Sheepfold
description: A shepherd folds his flock into a hurdle pen under a low moon, the sheep crowding through the gap. Millet worked this nocturne between 1856 and 1860, the kind of dusk pastoral he favoured at Barbizon.

title: View of Constantinople and the Bosphorus
description: Caïques and sailing ships line the Bosphorus shore at sunset, the quay busy with figures beneath a domed mosque flanked by twin minarets, the city's skyline of masts and minarets dissolving into golden haze beyond. Aivazovsky painted the view in 1856, drawing on visits to Constantinople in the 1840s and 1850s that made the Bosphorus panorama one of his recurring subjects.

title: Yoro Waterfall in Mino Province
englishTitle: Mino Province: Yōrō Waterfall, from Famous Views of the Sixty-odd Provinces
description: The Yōrō Falls of Mino Province are shown as a single broad ribbon of bright blue water descending between steep, densely wooded cliffs under an autumnal sky. From Hiroshige's late series Famous Views of the Sixty-odd Provinces (c. 1856), the tall vertical format emphasises the sheer drop of the cataract.

title: Иван Константинович Айвазовский - Широкий пейзаж с поселенцами
description: A panoramic Ukrainian steppe landscape depicting salt farmers in transit from Crimea to interior Russia. Aivazovsky captures the Izumskaya steppe with his characteristic atmospheric rendering, illustrating the vast and harsh terrain through which the caravan moves. Oil on canvas, 1856.

title: 2560px-Gustave Courbet
englishTitle: Le Pont d'Ambrussum (The Bridge of Ambrussum)
description: A small landscape of the Roman bridge over the Vidourle in Languedoc, oil on paper later mounted on panel. Courbet builds the stonework and riverbank with the heavy palette knife and earthy tonal range that defined his realist treatment of provincial French scenery.

title: Bamboo Yards
description: An Autumn sheet from Hiroshige's One Hundred Famous Views of Edo (1857). The timber arch of Kyobashi spans the foreground beneath a full moon as pilgrims carrying banners cross the bridge, while bamboo poles stacked upright in the riverside yards rise in jagged silhouette behind it. Below, a lone boatman poles a loaded skiff across the dark water.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum

title: Egyptian Recruits Crossing the Desert
description: Painted after Gérôme's first journey up the Nile, the canvas shows conscripts being driven across the sand under guard. The high horizon, sharp shadows and ethnographic costume detail are characteristic of his fastidious Orientalist manner.

title: Eugène Delacroix - The Fanatics of Tangier - WGA06195
description: Delacroix records the ecstatic Aissaoua brotherhood spilling through the streets of Tangier, a procession he had witnessed during his 1832 Moroccan trip. The swirling crowd and sun-bleached architecture exemplify his lifelong fascination with North African religious spectacle.

title: Hiroshige Fudo Falls
description: A woodblock print from Utagawa Hiroshige's famous series One Hundred Famous Views of Edo (no. 49), depicting the sacred Fudo Falls at the Shoju-in temple in Oji. The composition captures the cascading waterfall in Hiroshige's characteristic style with bold perspectives and atmospheric depth, exemplifying the ukiyo-e tradition of landscape prints.

title: Hiroshige View from massaki
englishTitle: View from Massaki of Suijin Shrine, Uchigawa Inlet, and Sekiya
description: Print no. 36 from Utagawa Hiroshige's One Hundred Famous Views of Edo series, part 1: Spring. This woodblock print depicts a view across Suijin Shrine's sacred grove toward the Uchigawa inlet and the village of Sekiya, exemplifying Hiroshige's mastery of landscape perspective and atmospheric detail.

title: Horikiri Iris Garden
englishTitle: Horikiri Iris Garden, from the series One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
description: Tall purple irises crowd the foreground of the celebrated Horikiri garden east of Edo, dwarfing the strolling visitors beyond. The radical close-up viewpoint, from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, would be admired and copied by Van Gogh.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts Boston (William Sturgis Bigelow Collection, 11.16827) via Google Art Project / Wikimedia Commons

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - The Duel After the Masquerade - Walters 3751
description: In a wintry Parisian park at dawn, the wounded Pierrot is supported by the red-robed Duc de Guise and a black-cloaked Domino, while to the right the victorious combatants — identifiable as Harlequin and another masquerade figure — confer at a distance. The work, painted between 1857 and 1859 and based on a composition Gérôme executed for the Duc d'Aumale, stages the aftermath of a carnival duel with the precise, theatrical finish of his academic manner. Oil on canvas, 39.1 × 56.3 cm, Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.

title: Justitia
description: A weathered statue of blindfolded Lady Justice stands with broken scales while a soldier loiters in shadow behind her, a wry Biedermeier comment on the gap between law and power. The panel was sold under Nazi duress by Jewish collector Leo Bendel and only restituted to his heirs in 2019.

title: Lake Nemi
description: Lake Nemi, the ancient crater lake in the Alban Hills south of Rome, is seen under clear summer light from the wooded shore, a small town perched on the far ridge. Two women rest in the foreground while a figure swims in the calm water below. Inness painted the scene during his Italian sojourn, dated 1857, and the canvas is now in the Yale University Art Gallery.
credit: Yale University Art Gallery, Yale University, New Haven, Conn.

title: Plum Park at Kameido
englishTitle: Plum Garden at Kameido, from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
description: A celebrated plum tree in the Kameido garden east of Edo, its blossoming branch thrust across the foreground while visitors stroll behind in a red-suffused dusk. Hiroshige's print from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo was later copied in oil by Van Gogh.
credit: http://www.rijksmuseum.nl/collectie/RP-P-1956-743 ( handle )

title: Sudden Shower Over Shin-Ohashi Bridge and Atake
englishTitle: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge and Atake, from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
description: From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, figures hurry across the Shin-Ōhashi bridge as a sudden summer downpour falls in fine engraved lines over the Sumida. The compressed perspective and slanting rain made the print a touchstone for European Japonisme; Van Gogh later copied it in oil.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum

title: Suido Bridge and Surugadai
description: A giant black carp streamer hoisted for the Boys' Festival fills the foreground of this Summer sheet from Hiroshige's One Hundred Famous Views of Edo (1857), a hallmark of his daring close-up framing. Far below, travellers cross Suido Bridge over the Kanda River while smaller streamers fly above the rooftops of Surugadai, with the snow-capped cone of Mount Fuji on the horizon.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum

title: The Angelus
description: A peasant couple pause over a basket of potatoes to pray as the Angelus bell sounds from a distant church spire. Millet painted the oil between 1857 and 1859; it measures 55.5 by 66 cm and hangs in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

title: The Coffee Bearer
description: A young woman stands in a colonnaded doorway holding a tray, wearing richly layered Middle Eastern dress — embroidered jacket, striped sash and wide trousers — against a sunlit courtyard beyond. Lewis, who spent a decade in Cairo, renders the tilework floor, costume, and architectural detail with the miniaturist exactitude that distinguished his Orientalist work; the painting is held at Manchester Art Gallery.

title: The Gleaners
description: Three women stoop across a stubble field gathering fallen grain, a loaded harvest cart and stacks behind them. Millet painted 'Des glaneuses' in 1857; the canvas entered the Musée d'Orsay, Paris, where it remains.

title: Utagawa Hiroshige
englishTitle: View of the Naruto Whirlpools in Awa Province
description: A vertical triptych charts the famed Naruto whirlpools off Awa province, the churning indigo eddies set beneath a banded sky. Hiroshige stretches the ooban format to give the tide its full vertiginous scale.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Utagawa Kunisada
englishTitle: Craftsmen from Modern Life Fashionably Adapted
description: A triptych of women engaged in various craft trades — dyeing, lacquerwork, and painting — fills an interior workshop scene, each figure rendered in Kunisada's characteristic bijin-ga style. Designed in 1857, the print belongs to the series Modern Parodies of the Four Classes (Imayō mitate shinō kōshō), which reimagines the Confucian social hierarchy through contemporary Edo beauties at work.
credit: https://www.tsunagujapan.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/image.jpg ( archive )

title: 20. The Entrance Gate In Enoshima
englishTitle: The Entrance to Enoshima in Sagami Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Plate twenty of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, showing pilgrims passing through the bronze torii at Enoshima with Fuji floating across Sagami Bay. The composition is built from flat overlapping silhouettes, a hallmark of late-Edo ukiyo-e landscape design.

title: 21. Lake In Hakone
englishTitle: The Lake at Hakone, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Mount Fuji rises beyond the ring of mountains enclosing Lake Ashi at Hakone, where a pine-topped green headland and jagged ochre crags meet the pale water. The sheet is numbered twenty-one in Hiroshige's vertical-format Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, published around 1858.

title: 26. The Oi River Between Suruga and Totomi Provinces
englishTitle: The Ōi River between Suruga and Tōtōmi Provinces, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Porters ford the broad shallows of the Oi River, with Fuji's cone framed beyond. Hiroshige drew the design for the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji issued by Tsutaya Kichizo, deploying the bokashi gradient technique to suggest mist rising off the water.

title: 32. Dog Eye Pass
englishTitle: Inume Pass in Kai Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Hiroshige's view from Inume Pass in Kai Province looks down on a sea of cloud broken by Fuji's summit, plate 32 of his Thirty-six Views series. The composition compresses foreground rocks and distant peak into a single graphic plane, a hallmark of late-Edo landscape design.

title: 34. Kuroto Bay
englishTitle: Kuroto Bay in Kazusa Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Boats drift in Kuroto Bay with Fuji visible across the water, plate 34 of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. The flat blue expanses and economical drawing of sails reflect the woodblock vocabulary that would soon enthral European Japonisme.

title: 36 Views of Mount Fuji - 18. The Sagami River
englishTitle: The Sagami River, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Plate eighteen of Hiroshige's late vertical Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, published around 1858. Raftsmen pole timber rafts down the Sagami River in Sagami Province, seen through a screen of tall reeds in the foreground; beyond, birds cross the sky above low hills as the snow-capped cone of Fuji rises in the distance.

title: 36 Views of Mount Fuji - 19. The Seven-Ri Beach
englishTitle: Seven-Ri Beach in Sagami Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Plate nineteen of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting Shichirigahama, the seven-ri stretch of coast in Sagami Province. Enoshima crouches on the horizon while Fuji floats beyond, the printer using bokashi gradient to fade sea into sky.

title: 36 Views of Mount Fuji - 33. Kogane Plain
englishTitle: Kogane Plain in Shimōsa Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A grazing horse, cropped by the frame, dominates the foreground while a second stands further off in the grassy plain; Fuji rises small and pale on the horizon between scattered pines. Plate 33 of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, published around 1858, with red wildflowers dotting the green expanse.

title: 36 Views of Mount Fuji- 23. The Sea off Satta
englishTitle: The Sea off Satta in Suruga Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Plate twenty-three of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. Big stylised waves curl in the foreground off Satta Point on the Tōkaidō road, with Fuji rising serenely behind, an answer to Hokusai's earlier Great Wave composition.

title: 36 Views of Mount Fuji' - 36. The Hoda Coast
englishTitle: The Hoda Coast in Awa Province, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: The closing print of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji shows the rocky Hoda coast in Awa Province, Fuji floating across Edo Bay. Crisp keyblock outlines and indigo seas give the design the graphic clarity that defined his late style.

title: Fuji on the Left of Tokaido Road
englishTitle: Mount Fuji on the Left of the Tōkaidō Road, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Travellers move along the Tokaido highway as Mount Fuji rises to the left, a print from Hiroshige's posthumously published Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. The composition layers near figures against a flattened distance, exploiting the woodblock medium's graded skies and crisp silhouettes.

title: Fuji sanjūrokkei Tōto ikkokubashi
englishTitle: Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji: Ichikobu Bridge in the Eastern Capital
description: Sheet from Hiroshige's late series Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji, showing Edo's Ikkoku Bridge with the sacred peak rising behind the city's tiled rooftops.
