The print uses the deep cobalt bokashi gradation Hiroshige favoured for sky and water, contrasting urban bustle below with serene distance.

title: Italian Landscape
description: Sailboats drift on the still water of Lake Maggiore beneath an alpine evening sky, distant peaks fading into haze along the Italian shore. Painted in 1858 during one of Aivazovsky's tours abroad, the canvas trades his usual Black Sea storms for the softer Lombard atmosphere of the lake district.

title: Menzel Adolph Frederick the Great at Lissa Bonsoir
englishTitle: Frederick the Great at Lissa: Bonsoir, Messieurs
description: Frederick II strides into a candlelit Silesian hall after the battle of Leuthen with a casual greeting to startled Austrian officers billeted there. Menzel built his career as the great visual chronicler of the Prussian king, working from meticulous reconstructions of period uniforms and interiors.

title: The Bellelli Family
description: Degas's aunt Laura Bellelli stands in mourning black with her two daughters in their apartment, her husband Gennaro seated and turned away at right, a framed chalk portrait of her recently deceased father hanging on the wall behind her. Begun during the artist's 1858–59 stay with the family and completed in Paris, the large canvas is now the centrepiece of the early Degas rooms at the Musée d'Orsay.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — CAEtElXoJtKBnQ RMN (Musée d'Orsay) / Gérard Blot This is a featured picture on the Persian language Wikipedia ( نگاره‌های برگزیده ) and is considered one of the finest images. See its nomination here . If you think this file should be featured on Wikimedia Commons as well, feel free to nominate it . If you have an image of similar quality that can be published under a suitable copyright license , be sure to upload it, tag it, and nominate it .

title: The courier in the Rosenthal
description: A postman in a yellow coat stands in a narrow old-town street, looking up at the ornate storeys of a tall townhouse where inhabitants lean from windows and balconies. Painted around 1858 and held in the Museum für Kunst und Kulturgeschichte der Philipps-Universität Marburg, the composition is a characteristic Spitzweg vignette of small-town life observed with warm, understated humour.
credit: Joachim Nagel: Carl Spitzweg. Belser, Stuttgart 2008, S. 31

provenance.collection: Museum für Kunst und Kulturgeschichte der Philipps-Universität Marburg
provenance.location: Museum für Kunst und Kulturgeschichte der Philipps-Universität Marburg

title: The lute player
description: A turbaned musician sits against a stone wall playing a short-bodied lute, a hookah coiled at his feet. Gérôme uses the figure as a vehicle for meticulous study of costume, texture, and muted Near Eastern colour. The work is dated 1858.
credit: sothebys.com

title: The Otsuki Plain
englishTitle: The Plain of Ōtsuki in Kai Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A stream meanders through the Ōtsuki plain past clumps of autumn grasses and wildflowers, with Fuji a pale silhouette above the mist-veiled hills. The design is plate 31 of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, published around 1858.

title: The Pine Forest of Mio
englishTitle: Miho Pine Grove in Suruga Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: From Hiroshige's late Mount Fuji series, the spit of pines at Miho-no-Matsubara curls into Suruga Bay with Fuji on the far shore. The site is bound up with the noh play Hagoromo, and Hiroshige uses bokashi blues and the dense black of pine needles to set its quiet mood.

title: The Sea off the Miura Peninsula
englishTitle: The Sea off the Miura Peninsula in Sagami Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: From Hiroshige's late Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series, published shortly before his death. A foreground of dark, choppy water frames the distant cone of Fuji across the bay; the woodblock printer's bokashi gradients soften sky and sea into bands of graded blue.

title: The Teahouse with the View of Mt. Fuji
englishTitle: Teahouse with a View of Mount Fuji, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: From Hiroshige's Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji, travellers pause at a roadside teahouse while the snow-tipped volcano floats beyond. The graded blue sky and crisp foreground figures show the woodblock master's command of bokashi printing and his eye for the everyday rhythms of Edo travel.

title: The Vale of Rest
description: One nun digs a grave while a second sits beside the open earth in the fading light of a walled cemetery, a distinctive cloud hanging above the treeline. Millais began the painting outdoors at Kinnoull near Perth in September 1858, and the work marks his transition from minute Pre-Raphaelite finish toward broader, more atmospheric handling; it is now at Tate Britain.
credit: This image Gallery link

title: View At Rouelles
description: A youthful landscape of Rouelles in the Le Havre hinterland, often cited as Monet's earliest surviving oil. The careful, almost Corot-like handling of trees and stream marks the threshold before his conversion to outdoor, sketch-based painting.

title: Wild Goose Hill and the Tone River
englishTitle: Wild Goose Hill on the Tone River (Kōnodai, Tonegawa), from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: From Hiroshige's vertical Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (1858), the view looks out from the pine-studded bluffs of Konodai — Wild Goose Hill — across the broad, islanded course of the Tone River. White sails thread the channels between grassy banks, and Mount Fuji's snow-covered cone rises on the horizon above a band of red sky.

title: Богоматерь с младенцем
description: The Virgin holds the Christ Child against a darkened ground, the academic Madonna type Bruni returned to across his career. He painted this oil in 1858, in the years when he directed the Imperial Hermitage picture gallery in St Petersburg.
credit: art-catalog.ru

title: 1859 Menzel Studentenfackelzug anagoria
description: Menzel records a Berlin student torchlight procession with his characteristic reportorial eye, the crowd compacted into a flickering frieze of faces and smoking brands. He was the great chronicler of Prussian public life, equally at ease with court ceremonies and street gatherings.

title: Ave Caesar Morituri te Salutant
description: Jean-Leon Gerome's academic vision of the Roman arena shows gladiators saluting the emperor with the famous formula "Hail Caesar, those who are about to die salute you." The painting epitomizes the meticulous archaeological detail and theatrical staging of nineteenth-century French history painting.

title: Ingres Etude Bain Turc Louvre 1859
description: A preparatory drawing in the Louvre's Cabinet des dessins for Le Bain turc, the circular canvas Ingres completed at age 82. The sheet shows him reworking the languid female nudes he had drawn from life decades earlier into a single dense Orientalist tableau.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - El rey Candaules
description: In a richly appointed ancient interior, the queen of Lydia stands nude at the centre of the composition while King Candaules reclines on the bed and Gyges, having been brought to witness the scene, conceals himself in the shadows of the doorway at right. Gérôme painted the oil on canvas in 1859, drawing on Herodotus with his characteristic archaeological literalism; the work is held at the Museo de Arte de Ponce in Puerto Rico.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - The Death of Caesar - Walters 37884
description: Gérôme avoids the assassination itself, instead showing senators streaming from the curia while Caesar's body lies abandoned in the foreground. The cool, measured composition and almost photographic finish drew contemporary comparison to a daguerreotype of the ancient world.

title: The Kiss
description: A young couple embrace on a stone staircase, the woman's blue gown and the man's red tights forming the colours of the French and Italian flags. Hayez's most popular canvas became a coded emblem of the Risorgimento and the alliance behind Italian unification.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"s-e.html?/html/h/hayez/6hayez"

title: Bringing home the calf born in the fields
description: Two men carry a newborn calf on a litter toward a farmhouse, the cow following at their heels. Millet painted this oil about 1860, a study of farm routine from his Barbizon years; the canvas is in the Princeton University Art Museum.
credit: Princeton University Art Museum

title: Fox in the Snow
description: A red fox bounds through a snow-covered winter landscape, its body caught in mid-motion against granular whites and a dark sky. Gustave Courbet painted this canvas in 1860; it is now in the collection of the Dallas Museum of Art.
credit: dallasmuseumofart.org; The AMICA Library; Dallas Museum of Art, online collection

title: Horses coming out of the sea
description: A single rider in red, mounted on a grey horse, struggles to control a rearing brown horse in the surf at the edge of a North African shore, a coastal town visible on the distant headland. Painted in 1860 — three years before Delacroix's death — the canvas distils decades of the artist's Maghreb sketchbooks into a concentrated motif of animal energy and human mastery; it is now in the Phillips Collection, Washington.

title: James Abbott McNeill Whistler
description: Plate from the Thames Set, made when Whistler took rooms at the Angel Inn to study London's working riverfront. A balcony view crowded with rigging, mooring posts and a pair of seamen, etched with the dense, descriptive line he later abandoned for atmospheric suggestion.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - Diogenes - Walters 37131
description: The Cynic philosopher squats inside his earthenware tub, lighting a lamp by daylight to search Athens for an honest man. Gérôme surrounds him with the dogs that gave Cynicism its name, treating the anecdote with the archaeological literalism typical of his Greek subjects.

title: Le Printemps
description: A female personification of Spring stands with a garland of blossom, one of four season panels Cézanne signed 'Ingres'. He painted them about 1860 to 1861 for the salon alcove of the family estate, the Jas de Bouffan near Aix; the panels were later transferred to canvas and given to the Petit Palais, Paris.

title: Portrait of May Sartoris
description: May Sartoris, about fifteen, stands in a dark riding habit with a red scarf and a wide black hat, a felled tree at her side. Leighton painted the portrait around 1860; the oil measures 152.1 by 90.2 cm and is held in the Kimbell Art Museum, Fort Worth.

title: Schmetterlinge
description: Kaulbach assembled a variety of butterfly and moth species around a bare branch against a dark brown ground, recording each specimen's wing markings with finely observed detail. The composition, dated around 1860, arranges the insects in a loose arabesque rhythm across the picture surface.

title: The Black Brunswicker
description: A young Brunswick cavalry officer takes leave of his sweetheart on the eve of Waterloo, her hand braced against the door he is determined to open. Millais paired the black death's-head hussar uniform against shimmering ivory silk to heighten the parting. Charles Dickens's daughter Kate modelled for the woman.
credit: John Everett Millais

title: The Blue Grotto on Capri
description: Sunlight refracted through the submerged entrance of Capri's Grotta Azzurra fills the cavern with the cobalt glow that made it a Grand Tour pilgrimage site. The picture is in fact by Berlin landscapist Carl Friedrich Seiffert, who specialised in luminous Italian veduta.

title: The Oceanids
description: Nude sea nymphs recline and swim among storm-tossed rocks in a turbulent ocean under an overcast twilight sky, with spectral figures dissolving into cloud on the right. Gustave Doré painted this large oil canvas of the Oceanids (Naïads of the Sea) between circa 1860 and 1869, demonstrating his ambitions as a painter beyond his celebrated illustration work.

title: The Thames in Ice
description: Several tall-masted vessels sit locked in ice along the Thames bank, their dark hulls contrasting with broken white floes in the foreground, where a lone figure stands on the shore. Painted in 1860, the picture belongs to Whistler's early Thames period and demonstrates the muted, near-monochrome palette he was developing for the river.

title: Young Girl Guarding her Sheep
description: A young shepherdess stands knitting beside her flock in an open field, her back to the grazing sheep. Millet painted this oil about 1860 to 1862; it belongs to the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute in Williamstown.
credit: Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute

title: Young Spartans exercising
description: Four Spartan girls advance toward a group of nude boys in an open landscape, challenging them to exercise, while older citizens and women watch from the middle distance. Drawing on Plutarch's account of the legislator Lycurgus, who urged Spartan girls to engage in wrestling and physical contest with boys, Degas reworked the canvas across the 1860s and later. The picture is in the National Gallery, London (NG3860).
credit: National Gallery, London - online collection

title: Zeitungsleser im Hausgarten
description: A Biedermeier gentleman absorbs himself in his newspaper amid the trellised greenery of a small private garden. Spitzweg specialized in such gently humorous bourgeois vignettes, painted in rich enamel-like color, that catalogued the introspective civic culture of mid-nineteenth-century Munich.

title: Bemberg Fondation Toulouse - Self-portrait paintings by Henri Fantin-Latour
description: A brooding early self-portrait showing the artist in three-quarter profile, his gaze cast slightly downward against a deep, almost black ground. Painted in 1860 or 1861 and now at the Fondation Bemberg in Toulouse, the work reflects Fantin-Latour's close study of seventeenth-century Dutch and Flemish portraiture.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme
description: Gérôme stages the legendary trial of the courtesan Phryne, disrobed by her advocate Hypereides to sway the Athenian judges. The single sweep of light on her body and the recoiling line of bearded jurors make a deliberately theatrical machine of his archaeological reconstruction.

title: Potato Planters
description: A man and woman work a field together, he breaking the soil with a hoe while she drops seed potatoes, a basket and a donkey under a tree behind them. Millet painted this oil about 1861, pairing the two figures in the field labour central to his Barbizon work.

title: Symphony in White
englishTitle: Symphony in White, No. 1: The White Girl
description: Joanna Hiffernan stands full-length in a flowing white dress, holding a small cluster of white flowers, before a gauze curtain backdrop. Her feet rest on a bear-skin rug laid over a patterned carpet. Whistler's emphasis on subtle gradations of cream, ivory and pale flesh tones over storytelling helped lay the ground for Aestheticism's art-for-art's-sake credo.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Music in the Tuileries
description: A fashionable crowd in top hats and crinolines listens to a band in the Tuileries gardens, the canvas crowded with portraits of Manet's circle, including Baudelaire, Gautier and Fantin-Latour. The flat patches of black coats and abrupt cropping mark Manet's first decisive turn toward painting modern Parisian life.
credit: National Gallery, London

title: Ovid among the Scythians
description: The exiled Roman poet Ovid reclines on the grass of the Black Sea steppe, offered milk and bread by Scythian herdsmen while their horses graze in the background. Delacroix exhibited a smaller version at the 1859 Salon and returned to the subject in 1862, the year before his death; the painting is now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
credit: Met Museum (Timeline of Art History); Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 439631)

title: The Turkish bath
description: A circular tondo crowded with bathing women, drawn together from poses Ingres had refined across half a century of nudes. Painted in his eighties for Prince Napoléon, the work distils his lifelong fascination with sinuous contour and the Orientalist harem trope into a single hothouse composition.
credit: This file was derived from: Le Bain Turc, by Jean Auguste Dominique Ingres, from C2RMF.jpg :

title: Don Quijote illustrated by Gustav Dore III
description: A lone armoured knight on horseback makes his way through a dense forest, a stream in the foreground and a turreted castle visible through the trees in the distance. The wood-engraved plate, from Gustave Doré's celebrated 1863 illustrated edition of Cervantes' Don Quixote, exemplifies Doré's mastery of atmospheric forest light and fine parallel hatching.
credit: French edition of Don Quixote

title: Eduard Gaertner Berlin Bruederstrasse
description: The Brüderstraße on the Spreeinsel in Berlin-Mitte recedes between rows of plastered townhouses toward the tower of the Petrikirche. Gaertner painted the view in 1863, still working in the precise Berlin Biedermeier vedute mode he had practised since the 1820s.
credit: Photograph of the original painting by uploader (not that it mattered, but some Common admins have no idea about German copyright and delete it otherwise).

title: Eve of St Agnes
description: Inspired by Keats's poem, Madeline stands in a grand, candlelit interior bathed in warm amber and gold, her pale gown luminous against the richly panelled walls as moonlight falls across the floor in greenish patches. Millais painted the scene in 1863, and the work, now in the Royal Collection, exemplifies the atmospheric, freely handled manner of his later career rather than the tight early Pre-Raphaelite finish.

title: Monet w24
description: The road running past the Saint-Siméon farm above Honfleur, painted around 1863-64 during Monet's earliest Normandy campaigns. The farm's inn was the gathering place of Boudin, Jongkind and the other plein-air painters who mentored the young Monet. Wikidata records the canvas (59 × 80 cm) in the collection of the Bank of Italy.

title: Olympia
description: A reclining nude courtesan meets the viewer's gaze with cool defiance, attended by a Black maid bearing flowers from a client. Manet flattens form with stark lighting and sharp tonal contrasts, scandalising the 1865 Salon by transposing Titian's Venus into contemporary Parisian demi-monde.

title: Self-portrait by Edgar Degas
description: The young Degas, around twenty-nine, looks out from a dark ground in a black coat and high collar, his expression guarded and slightly aslant. Painted around 1863, the picture entered the collection of Calouste Gulbenkian and now hangs at the Gulbenkian Museum in Lisbon.
credit: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum in Selected work 30 from Self Portrait: Renaissance to Contemporary (Anthony Bond, Joanna Woodall, ISBN 978-1855143579 ).

title: The Christian Martyrs' Last Prayer
description: A Roman arena scene in which kneeling Christians pray as lions are released and crucified figures burn against the stadium walls. Gerome combines archaeological detail of the Circus Maximus with the polished academic finish typical of his Salon machines.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: The Goose Girl
description: A young girl, identifiable as a peasant by her kerchief and her work-roughened hands and feet, extends her leg to dip a heel into the stream. In this painting, Millet refers to a long tradition in European art of depicting the idealized female nude in a natural setting, often in the guise of a mythological figure. The artist reworks this convention from a Realist perspective, emphasizing the goose girl's working-class status, adolescent body, and vulnerable pose.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: The Princess from the Land of Porcelain
description: Painted in London during Whistler's japonisme phase, the canvas dresses Christine Spartali in a loose kimono among Asian carpets and a folding screen. Frederick Leyland later acquired it and hung it in the dining room that became the Peacock Room, now reinstalled at the Freer Gallery.
credit: This file was derived from: James McNeill Whistler - La Princesse du pays de la porcelaine - Google Art Project.jpg :

title: A Seascape
description: A nocturnal Channel scene with moonlight breaking through cloud over distant sailing vessels. Made during Monet's formative summers on the Normandy coast, the picture follows the marines of Boudin and Jongkind, with feathery brushwork capturing reflected silver on dark water.

title: Jean Frédéric Bazille - Reclining Nude - 1864
description: A female nude stretched full-length across the canvas, set against a dark ground. Oil on canvas, 70.5 by 190.5 cm, painted in 1864 and held by the Musée Fabre in Montpellier, Bazille's home city. The elongated horizontal format follows the academic odalisque tradition Bazille studied in Gleyre's Paris atelier.
credit: www.the-athenaeum.org

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - Prayer in the Desert
description: An Arnaut — a Balkan Ottoman irregular soldier in distinctive white kilt and red stockings — stands in prayer on a dark cape spread across the desert floor, his horse grazing behind him and a long caravan receding into the distance. Gérôme sets the solitary figure against a vast pale sky and open horizon, isolating devotion within the stillness of the desert. Painted in 1864 and informed by the artist's Near Eastern travels, the work is one of several prayer subjects in which Gérôme explores the intersection of landscape and ritual observance.

title: La Pointe de la Hève
description: A rocky pebble shore stretches along the base of the headland at Sainte-Adresse, with a small rowing boat near the surf and sailing vessels on the horizon. Painted in 1864 and now in the National Gallery, London (NG6565), this early Channel view shows Monet working through the open-air coastal approach he had absorbed from Boudin.

title: La Robe Rose
description: A young woman in a pink-and-white striped dress seen from behind, seated on a wall and looking out over the sunlit village of Castelnau near Montpellier. Oil on canvas, 147 by 110 cm, painted in 1864 and now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris. The sitter is Bazille's cousin Thérèse des Hours.

title: Preparation for the exam
description: A student in uniform cap sits at a desk by a window, chin resting pensively on his hand while another figure reclines on a couch in the background. Painted in 1864, the work is an early genre study by Ilya Repin that captures the mood of examination preparation with careful tonal observation and controlled interior light.

title: Romaine Lacaux
description: Romaine Lacaux sits in a grey dress with white lace collar and sleeves trimmed in blue, holding a small bunch of red flowers, before a softly rendered backdrop with floral arrangements. Among Renoir's earliest signed canvases, the 1864 portrait already shows his sensitivity to reflected light on translucent fabrics and his previous training as a porcelain decorator in the delicate nuances of the young girl's complexion. The work is in the Cleveland Museum of Art (1942.1065).
credit: https://clevelandart.org/art/1942.1065 IA

title: Self-portrait
description: A half-length self-portrait in which Watts wears a dark slouch hat and black velvet coat against a plain ground. Oil on canvas, 64.8 by 52.1 cm, painted in 1864 and held by Tate Britain. Watts painted it during his years at Little Holland House in Kensington, drawing on Old Master portraiture such as Raphael's Castiglione.
credit: Tate Britain

title: Spring Flowers
description: Peonies, hydrangeas, and lilacs spill from basket and pot against a darkened ground, painted with an almost botanical attentiveness. An early still life, it shows the young Monet weighing studio precision against the looser, light-driven handling that would soon define his work.
credit: https://clevelandart.org/art/1953.155 IA

title: Symphony in White
description: Joanna Hiffernan, Whistler's model and companion, stands at a fireplace mantelpiece in a white muslin dress, her reflection visible in the mirror behind her. She holds a Japanese fan and rests one arm along the mantel shelf, where a blue-and-white vase and pink azalea blossoms are arranged. Conceived as a study in tonal harmony, the picture was exhibited in 1865 and became a touchstone for the Aesthetic movement's pursuit of art for art's sake.
credit: Whistler Symphony in White no 2 (The Little White Girl)

title: The Battle of the Kearsarge and the Alabama
description: Two warships engage in the English Channel off Cherbourg: the burning Confederate raider Alabama, struck by Union fire, lists amid billows of smoke as the Kearsarge stands off to the right. French spectator boats occupy the foreground, including a sailing vessel whose scale underscores the distance of the action. Manet painted the scene in 1864, immediately after the battle, in a broadly brushed marine style that belongs to the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
credit: From en.wiki; The Philadelphia Museum of Art

title: The Dead Christ with Angels
description: Two angels support the slumped body of the dead Christ, his pallid torso lit against shadow. Manet borrows a traditional Lamentation type but flattens modeling and exposes brushwork in a way that scandalized the 1864 Salon, where critics also faulted the placement of the side wound on the wrong flank.

title: The Painter's Honeymoon
description: A man guides a woman's hand at a drawing as she leans against his shoulder, her golden gown set off by darker surroundings. Oil on canvas, 83.8 by 76.8 cm, painted around 1864 and acquired by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, in 1912. A genre subject unusual for Leighton, who more often worked in classical and mythological themes.

title: Портрет художника Федора Антоновича Бруни
description: Portrait photograph of Fyodor Bruni (1799–1875), a Russian painter, sculptor, and influential rector of the Imperial Academy of Arts. Taken by photographer Andrey Denyer in the 1860s, showing Bruni in his maturity during his tenure as an academician.

title: Arnaut fumant
description: An Albanian irregular sits in an ornately latticed interior, drawing on a large hookah, his costume and surroundings rendered in Gérôme's characteristic academic precision. The small oil on canvas, dated 1865, is a single-figure ethnographic study of the kind Gérôme repeated across his Orientalist series of the 1860s.

title: Bazille and Camille
description: Monet's plein-air study of 1865 shows Frédéric Bazille standing beside Camille Doncieux — Monet's own model and future wife — in a sun-dappled forest clearing, painted in preparation for the ambitious large-format Déjeuner sur l'herbe. The brisk, broken handling of light on foliage and costume anticipates the Impressionist technique Monet would develop in the following decade. The work is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington (inv. 1970.17.41).

title: Degas
englishTitle: A Woman Seated beside a Vase of Flowers
description: Madame Valpinçon glances aside while a riotous bouquet dominates the canvas, the figure pushed to the edge in a deliberate inversion of conventional portrait hierarchy. Degas treats the flowers with thick impasto, the sitter with restrained drawing-led brushwork.

title: Destruction of Leviathan
description: God smites the sea-monster Leviathan with a sword, the beast writhing in the deep amid lightning-lit clouds. Doré's wood-engraved illustration appeared in his folio English Bible, blending Romantic sublimity with the dense cross-hatching that defined his commercial print style.
credit: w:en:Image:Destruction of Leviathan.png

title: Gustave Courbet 029
description: Painted during Courbet’s 1865 stay at Trouville, this canvas shows a young woman in profile with freshly caught seagulls slung over her shoulder, their wings spilling across the picture plane. The subject came from the fishing life of the Normandy coast, handled with the dense, kneaded paint of Courbet’s Realist maturity.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - Evening Prayer
description: Worshippers prostrate themselves on the flat roof of a Cairo mosque as the day's last light slants across the architecture. The picture belongs to Gérôme's prayer series of the 1860s, in which he applied his polished panel technique to ethnographic studies gathered on his Egyptian journeys.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - Young Greeks in the Mosque - 62.85 - Minneapolis Institute of Arts
description: Two young Greek figures kneel on the polished marble floor of an Ottoman mosque interior while a standing figure in military dress looks on — a scene of cultural conversion rather than ordinary prayer. Gérôme renders the columned arcade and intricate architectural carving with Orientalist care. Oil on panel, 1865; Minneapolis Institute of Art (inv. 62.85).

title: La Pointe de la Hève at Low Tide
description: Wagons and figures cross the wet sand below the headland of La Hève near Le Havre, Monet's home town. Shown at the Salon of 1865 — his official debut — the canvas owes much to the marine realism of Boudin and Courbet.

title: Monet w58
description: A path cutting through tall trees, painted in 1865 when Monet was working in the Forest of Fontainebleau around Chailly while preparing his Déjeuner sur l'herbe. The canvas (79 × 58 cm) is held in the Rau Collection for UNICEF at the Arp Museum Bahnhof Rolandseck in Remagen, Germany.

title: Self-portrait
description: A direct self-portrait set against a dark ground, the painter holding his palette and brushes. Oil on canvas, 108.9 by 71.1 cm, executed in 1865 to 1866 and held by the Art Institute of Chicago, which purchased it in 1962. Bazille was in his mid-twenties when he painted it.
credit: cgfa.acropolisinc.com : Home : Info : Pic

title: Still Life with a Carafe, Flowers and Fruit
description: A glass carafe, scattered fruit and a small bouquet are composed on a dark cloth in disciplined Salon order. Among Fantin-Latour's earliest mature still lifes, it shows the precise tonal modelling that drew Whistler's circle to his work.

title: Still Life with Bread and Eggs
description: A baguette, eggs, red onions, a pewter tankard, a knife and a wine glass arranged on a cloth-draped table. Oil on canvas, painted in 1865 and held by the Cincinnati Art Museum, one of Cézanne's earliest dated still lifes. X-ray scanning in 2022 revealed an earlier portrait beneath the surface.

title: Studio in the Rue de Furstemberg
description: A corner of a sparsely furnished studio with two armchairs and a doorway opening onto a bedroom and a grey winter sky. Oil on canvas, painted in 1865 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. The room is the studio at 6 Place de Furstenberg that Bazille shared with Monet, in the building that now houses the Musée national Eugène Delacroix.

title: The Artist in His Studio
description: An oil sketch for an unrealised group portrait, showing Whistler at the right holding a palette, with two female models — one seated in white, one standing in a pale gold robe — in a grey studio interior. The thinly brushed, almost monochrome handling demonstrates the tonal economy Whistler was formulating in the mid-1860s. The work, dated circa 1865–66, is held by the Art Institute of Chicago.

title: The Ragpicker
description: A life-size Spanish-inspired portrait of a Paris chiffonnier propped on his stick, set against a neutral grey ground. Manet borrows the format of Velázquez's philosopher portraits to dignify a marginal modern Parisian.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; The Norton Simon Museum

title: The Sower
description: A peasant striding across a furrowed field, his arm flung out in the act of casting seed. Pastel and Conté crayon on beige paper, about 47 by 37.5 cm, made around 1865 and held by the Clark Art Institute in Williamstown. Millet returned to the sower motif across his career in oil, pastel and print.
credit: The Clark Art Institute, Williamstown

title: Calling Home the Cows
description: A herder driving cattle homeward at the close of day, the animals strung out along a low horizon. Pastel and Conté crayon on wove paper, about 55.9 by 41.3 cm, made around 1866 and held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington, in the Corcoran Collection. It comes from the William A. Clark holdings of Millet pastels.

title: Cleopatra and Caesar
description: Cleopatra steps from the unrolled carpet to confront Caesar at his writing table, the ancient anecdote staged with the polished historicism Gérôme made his trademark. Smooth porcelain finish, archaeologically researched props, and a controlled tonal palette anchor the picture in academic theatre.
credit: http://www.mezzo-mondo.com/arts/mm/orientalist/european/gerome/index_b.html Archived 2017-06-19 at the Wayback Machine

title: Dans la forêt de Fontainebleau
description: Massive oak trunks rise through a sun-dappled interior of the Forest of Fontainebleau, the ground covered in grass and low undergrowth. Renoir painted this woodland study in 1866, early in his career, working in an earthy tonal range indebted to the Barbizon painters who had long used the forest south of Paris as an open-air studio.
credit: Cooper 1959, p. 166. ; fineartamerica.com

title: Flowers and Fruit
description: A glass vase of mixed flowers — hydrangeas, peonies, ranunculus, and white blossoms — stands beside a plate of strawberries, a whole orange, and segments of tangerine, with a small white lidded pot, all arranged on a dark cloth. This 1866 still life, held at the Toledo Museum of Art, shows Fantin-Latour's characteristic precision of observation and his quiet refinement of the Dutch still-life tradition.

title: Garden at Sainte-Adresse
description: On a sunny terrace at Sainte-Adresse, two elegantly dressed figures stroll among vivid flower beds while two others sit in the foreground; two flags — one French tricolour — fly above a sea busy with sailing vessels and steamships. Painted in 1866–67 and now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, this is one of Monet's most composed and boldly coloured early canvases, its high viewpoint and flat decorative fields reflecting an awareness of Japanese prints.
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art

title: Gustave Doré - The Holy Bible - Plate I
description: The frontispiece to Doré's 1866 illustrated Bible: humans and a tigress alike struggle to save their young as the floodwaters rise. Engraved in dense black-and-white from Doré's design, the plate established the visual template for the Deluge in popular imagination for generations.

title: Inada Kyuzo Shinsuke
description: A sheet from Yoshitoshi's series Eimei nijūhasshūku (Twenty-eight Famous Murders with Verse), produced with Yoshiiku in 1866–67. The print exemplifies the late ukiyo-e taste for muzan-e — bloody, theatrical scenes drawn from kabuki and historical legend.

title: Jo
description: A portrait of Joanna Hiffernan, model and lover of Whistler, gazing into a hand mirror as she draws her copper-red hair through her fingers. Courbet painted at least four versions, the dense impasto and earth-toned palette characteristic of his Realist studio practice.

title: L'Homme au bonnet de coton
description: A seated man in a white cotton cap, his face built up in thick ridges of paint. Oil on canvas, painted in 1866 and held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. The sitter is the artist's uncle Dominique Aubert, whom Cézanne painted in a series of portraits laid in heavily with the palette knife, a phase he later called couillarde.

title: Mädchen am Klavier
description: A young woman seated at an upright piano with a second woman sewing on a sofa behind her, in a domestic interior. Oil on canvas, about 57 by 92 cm, held by the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg under accession ГЭ-9166. The work carries the subtitle Overture to Tannhäuser, after the Wagner prelude.

title: Odalisque reading
description: A nude woman sits in profile seen from behind, reading an open book against a deep crimson drapery, her dark hair falling loose around her shoulders. Francesco Hayez painted this Odalisque reading between 1866 and 1867; it is held at Villa Carlotta on Lake Como.

title: Petite Italienne chanteuse des rues
description: A young Italian girl in a headscarf shown at half length as a street singer. Oil on canvas, 131 by 98 cm, painted in 1866 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. Bazille worked the figure against a plain ground, concentrating the colour in the costume and complexion.
credit: базиль.рф www.museefabre.fr

title: Spring Bouquet
description: A generous bouquet of spring garden flowers — peonies, lilac, iris, and wild blossoms — overflows a blue-and-white porcelain vase set on a stone ledge. Painted in 1866, the canvas belongs to an early period before Renoir's palette had fully lightened, the muted grey-green ground and dense paint surface recalling his pre-Impressionist formation. The work is held at the Fogg Museum, Harvard Art Museums.
credit: Harvard Art Museums

title: Still Life with Fish
description: A still life of fish laid out on a kitchen table. Oil on canvas, painted in 1866 and held by the Detroit Institute of Arts. Bazille took up still life repeatedly in the mid-1860s, treating fish, game and a heron in turn.
credit: The AMICA Library; Detroit Institute of Arts

title: The Artist's Father
description: The painter's father, the banker Louis-Auguste Cézanne, seated frontally in a large armchair and reading the newspaper L'Événement. Oil on canvas, 198.5 by 119.3 cm, painted in 1866 and held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington. It is the second of three portraits Cézanne made of his father.

title: The Collector of Prints
description: A bearded man in a dark coat and hat sits absorbed before a wall hung with botanical and decorative prints, a portfolio of images resting open on his knees. Degas renders the collector's interior with close-toned observation, placing the human subject within an environment defined by images rather than narrative action. Painted in 1866, the canvas is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: The Little Gardener
description: A boy in white breeches, a pink shirt and a boater stands in a planted garden under a bright sky. Oil on canvas, about 128 by 169 cm, painted in 1866 to 1867 and held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston. Bazille left the foreground unfinished, the bare canvas still visible.

title: The Sleepers
description: Two nude women lie entwined in dishevelled bedding, jewellery and a broken pearl strand scattered on the sheet. Commissioned by the Turkish diplomat Khalil-Bey, the canvas treats lesbian love with a frank realism that scandalised the Second Empire.
credit: Gustave Courbet, 1866

title: The Vision of The Valley of The Dry Bones
description: An engraving from Dore's illustrated Bible, depicting Ezekiel's vision in which scattered bones reanimate as a vast army. The artist exploits dense crosshatching and dramatic chiaroscuro to give the desolate plain a haunted, otherworldly atmosphere.

title: Valparaiso Harbor
description: A large stone pier or mole occupies the foreground, with small figures walking along it; a single warship rides on a flat, cool-blue bay beyond, beneath a softly graded sky. Whistler painted the scene in Valparaiso in 1866, having travelled to Chile during the Spanish bombardment of the port. The atmospheric handling anticipates his Thames Nocturnes; the work is held by the Smithsonian American Art Museum.

title: Woman with a Parrot
description: A reclining nude exhibited at the Salon of 1866, where Courbet's frank naturalism, tousled hair and unidealised flesh, scandalised critics expecting an academic Venus. The bird perched on her outstretched hand provides the slim mythological pretext. Now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (accession number 29.100.57)

title: Women Going to the Woods
description: Figures on the main street of Marlotte, a village at the edge of the Fontainebleau forest, the women setting out to gather firewood. Oil on canvas, about 65 by 92 cm, painted in 1866. Sisley showed it at the Paris Salon that year, the first time the jury accepted his work.

title: (Venice) La distruzione del tempio di Gerusalemme -Francesco Hayez - gallerie Accademia Venice
englishTitle: The Destruction of the Temple of Jerusalem
description: Hayez stages the Roman sack of Herod's Temple as operatic Romantic history painting: massive white walls from which prisoners are cast down, soldiers bearing Roman standards, and billowing smoke above the scene. The vast canvas of 1867, now in the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice, was conceived as a meditation on tyranny that resonated with Italian audiences living under Austrian rule.

title: Adolphe Monet in the Garden of Le Coteau at Sainte-Adresse
description: The painter's father sits in a straw hat among flowering plants in the family's seaside garden at Sainte-Adresse. Painted during the same productive Norman summer as the Regatta, the picture combines a tender domestic portrait with Monet's emerging interest in dappled outdoor light.
credit: ArtDaily.com http://www.afanews.com/home/item/1753-currier-museum-exhibits-rare-monet-painting#.WrxFqy7wbIU

title: Diana
description: A nude woman holding a bow, a dead deer and an animal skin at her feet, cast as the huntress Diana. Oil on canvas, 197 by 132 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington. The model is thought to be Renoir's companion Lise Tréhot; the canvas was rejected by the 1867 Salon.

title: Édouard Manet by Henri Fantin-Latour
description: Fantin-Latour's 1867 portrait presents Édouard Manet three-quarter length in a dark coat and top hat, gloves and cane in hand, against an austere neutral ground. The characterisation — assured, dandified, self-possessed — accords with the Manet Fantin-Latour would place at the centre of his 1870 group canvas Un atelier aux Batignolles. The portrait is held at the Art Institute of Chicago.
credit: Art Institute of Chicago

title: Garden of the Princess
description: From a high window of the Louvre, Monet looked across the Pont des Arts to the dome of the Institut and the formal parterre of the Garden of the Princess. One of three Paris views painted from the same elevated vantage in 1867, it shows top-hatted strollers and carriages reduced to crisp coloured marks.

title: Glaçons à Bougival
description: Ice floes drift on a steel-grey Seine near Bougival, with a snow-covered bank in the foreground where small figures and moored boats shelter against the cold. Painted in 1867 and now in the Louvre collection (RF 1961 62), the work is rendered in restrained grey and white tones that evoke the stillness of the winter freeze.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Idylls of the King 3
description: A wood-engraved illustration to Tennyson's Arthurian cycle, showing Edyrn travelling to Arthur's court with his lady and dwarf, the party approaching a great castle perched on a rocky crag beneath a dramatic clouded sky. Doré builds the scene with the theatrical chiaroscuro and monumental architecture that characterise his illustrations for the 1868 Moxon edition of the Idylls of the King.
credit: Enid , by Lord Alfred Tennyson . London: Edward Moxon & Co., 1868.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - On the Desert - Walters 3734
description: Commissioned by Baltimore collector William T. Walters, the small panel pictures a Nubian handler walking two slim sighthounds through a windswept desert. The trim silhouettes suggest Pharaoh hounds, a subject Gérôme studied during his Egyptian travels of the 1860s.

title: Jeanne-Marguerite Lecadre in the Garden Sainte-Adresse
description: Jeanne-Marguerite Lecadre, a relative, stands among flowering beds in the family garden at Sainte-Adresse near Le Havre. The picture's bright local colour and crisp shadows show Monet absorbing the lessons of Manet and Japanese prints.

title: Landscape of Aigues-Mortes
description: The medieval ramparts of Aigues-Mortes seen across flat marshland under a wide sky. Oil on canvas, 46 by 55 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. Bazille made several views of the walled Camargue town during a summer in the region.

title: Le Meurtre
description: A violent scene in which two figures pin a third to the ground beside a body of water under a heavy sky. Oil on canvas, 64 by 81 cm, painted around 1870 and held by the Walker Art Gallery, Liverpool, under inventory WAG 6242. It belongs to the dark, dramatic subjects of Cézanne's early years.

title: Little Red Riding Hood
description: From Doré's celebrated illustrations to Perrault's Contes, the wood engraving stages the child's fateful meeting with the wolf among forest shadows. Doré pioneered cinematic tonal staging in printed fairy tales, and these designs shaped the visual imagination of the genre across Europe.
credit: National Library of Poland

title: Miss May Prinsep by George Frederic Watts
description: Portrait of Miss May Prinsep by the English painter George Frederic Watts. Date painted: 1867-1869. Oil on canvas.
credit: Art UK [1]

title: Monet w81
englishTitle: The Road to the Saint-Siméon Farm in Winter
description: A snow-covered stretch of the road leading up to the Saint-Siméon farm above Honfleur, painted in 1867. It belongs to the group of winter effects Monet made on this road, returning to the site of his earliest plein-air apprenticeship. Private collection (49 × 65 cm).

title: Nature morte au héron
description: A dead heron and other birds laid on a table, a study in greys and browns. Oil on canvas, 98 by 78 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. Bazille painted it in a Paris studio alongside Sisley, who treated the same heron in his own canvas.

title: Pierre-Auguste Renoir - Frédéric Bazille
description: Renoir portrays his fellow Impressionist Frédéric Bazille at work before an easel, brush poised over a still life of a heron. The picture is a touching record of the early Batignolles circle, painted shortly before Bazille's death in the Franco-Prussian War.
credit: Renoir, peintre du bonheur : 1841-1919 , de Gilles Néret, Köln, Taschen, 2001, p. 14. ISBN 9783822857410

title: Portrait of Pierre-Auguste Renoir
description: A portrait of the painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir seated with his knees drawn up, in a dark jacket and blue cravat. Oil on canvas, 62 by 51 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée d'Orsay, Paris. Bazille and Renoir shared a studio that year and exchanged portraits.

title: Promenade sur la falaise de Sainte-Adresse
englishTitle: Promenade on the Cliff at Sainte-Adresse
description: A solitary figure stands on a grassy clifftop above the Normandy coast near Sainte-Adresse, a church visible to the left and a grey-green Channel stretching to the horizon. Painted in 1867, the canvas belongs to the Matsuoka Museum of Art, Tokyo, and reflects Monet's sustained engagement with the coastal landscape around his family's summer retreat at Le Havre.

title: Quai du Louvre
description: An early Parisian cityscape, painted from a balcony of the Louvre overlooking the Seine. Bustling figures, carriages, and the dome of the Pantheon are rendered with the high vantage and bright daylight that anticipate Monet's mature Impressionist manner.
credit: Mauritshuis

title: Regatta at Sainte-Adresse
description: Sailboats and onlookers crowd the beach at Sainte-Adresse, the Norman resort where Monet spent the summer with relatives. The crisp horizontals and bright local colour are still indebted to Boudin and Jongkind, but already announce the open-air manner that Impressionism would soon codify.
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art

title: Réunion de famille
description: Ten of the painter's relatives gathered on a shaded terrace at the family estate of Méric near Montpellier, most of them looking out at the viewer. Oil on canvas, 152 by 230 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée d'Orsay, Paris, under inventory RF 2749. Bazille reworked the canvas before showing it at the Salon of 1868.
credit: photo Shonagon 2022-07-15

title: Self-portrait
description: Hunt meets the viewer's gaze in this large 1867 self-portrait, wearing an elaborate Eastern silk robe over red undergarments and a decorative embroidered sash, with a painter's palette in hand and brushes on the table before him. A founding member of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, he presents himself here with the intensity and meticulously observed surface detail that characterised his later career.
credit: HumanitiesWeb

title: Street in Sainte-Adresse
description: An early view of the seaside resort north of Le Havre, where Monet stayed with his aunt during a formative summer. Architecture is still drawn with relatively firm contour, but the bright Norman light and high-keyed palette already point toward Impressionist practice.
credit: The Clark Art Institute

title: The Horse Market
description: A single chestnut Arabian horse is led at a spirited trot through a narrow North African street by a handler in white, while three robed figures watch from the left and a veiled woman looks down from an upper window. Gérôme's characteristic ethnographic precision is on full display in the ornate carved woodwork of the mashrabiyya balcony and the sun-bleached plasterwork. The picture, dated 1867, belongs to the Haggin Museum in Stockton, California.
credit: hagginmuseum.org

title: The kill of deer
description: A vast hunting picture, over five metres wide, in which hounds bring down a stag in deep snow under the eye of a mounted huntsman. Courbet draws on his Franche-Comté upbringing and the Flemish hunt tradition, scaling a popular subject up to the format of history painting in keeping with his Realist programme.
credit: http://www.rmn.fr/gustavecourbet/02parcours/img/22b.jpg (broken link)

title: Афганец
description: A standing portrait of an Afghan man in regional dress. Oil painting from Vereshchagin's Turkestan series, made in 1867 to 1868 after the artist joined General Kaufman's expedition to Central Asia. Vereshchagin combined ethnographic portraits of this kind with the battle scenes drawn from the same campaign.

title: Artists Sketching in the White Mountains
description: Three painters at work on an open hillside in the White Mountains, each at an easel sheltered by a large parasol umbrella, the mountain ridges and a stormy sky filling the distance behind them. The foreground figure works intently while two others are visible further along the slope. Painted in 1868, the work is held at the Portland Museum of Art.
credit: antiquesandfineart.com; Portland Museum of Art

title: Étude pour une vendange
description: Figures gathering grapes in a Mediterranean vineyard, the left panel of a study Bazille made toward a grape-harvest composition. Oil on canvas, 38 by 46 cm, held at the Musée Fabre in Montpellier, the city near which the Bazille family kept their estate at Méric.
credit: www.tumblr.com www.museefabre.fr

title: Fisherman with a Net
description: A nude male fisherman casting a circular throw-net at the water's edge, his back to the viewer. Bazille painted the canvas in 1868; it later entered the Rau Foundation for the Third World in Zurich, and stands among his experiments with the open-air male figure.
credit: www.desordre.net; artlover.me

title: Flowers
description: A dense bouquet rising from a vase set on a console table, catalogued as Vase de fleurs sur une console. Oil on canvas, 130 by 97 cm, painted between 1867 and 1868 and now in the Musée de Grenoble.

title: From Mleta to Gudauri
description: A caravan of travellers and pack animals working along the precipitous mountain road that climbs from Mleta to Gudauri in the Caucasus, snow-capped peaks behind. Aivazovsky painted the oil in 1868, applying the atmospheric handling of mist and distance he is better known for in his sea pieces.

title: In the Summer
description: A dark-eyed young woman sits outdoors in a loose white blouse and striped skirt, her long dark hair pinned back, gazing calmly at the viewer against a lush green background. Painted in 1868 and now at the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin, the work casts Renoir's model Lise Tréhot as a summer bohémienne and retains a solidity of form that still recalls Courbet's influence.

title: Interior
description: A lamp-lit domestic interior from Monet's youth, with figures gathered after a meal. Indoor subjects are unusual in his work; here the warm artificial light and dark-keyed palette betray a debt to the realism of Manet and Bazille more than to his later high-colour outdoor practice.

title: La Pie
description: A single magpie perches on a wooden fence gate at the left of a snowbound Norman landscape, its dark form casting a faint blue shadow on the drift below. Monet explored the chromatic subtlety of coloured shadow across white snow in this large canvas of 1868–69, which was rejected by the 1869 Salon. The work is now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

title: La Porte d'Amont
description: An early seascape by Claude Monet showing the Porte d'Amont, one of the natural chalk arches in the cliffs at Etretat on the Normandy coast, painted about 1868-69. The evening sky glows through the opening of the arch while broken touches of sunset light flicker across the water below, an early statement of the coastal motifs Monet would return to at Etretat throughout the 1880s. The painting is in the Harvard Art Museums (Fogg Museum), Cambridge, Massachusetts.

title: La Siesta, Memory of Spain
description: A large group of men, women, and children huddles in the shadowed recess of an archway or doorway in a Spanish town, their varied costumes and postures evoking poverty and rest. Painted circa 1868 and now in the National Museum of Western Art, Tokyo, the work draws on Doré's Spanish travels and applies the strong chiaroscuro of his illustrative work to an ambitious oil composition.

title: Marriage of Sisley
description: A double portrait of Renoir's friend the painter Alfred Sisley standing beside his companion, both in fashionable contemporary dress, the woman's arm through his. Painted in 1868 and now in the Wallraf-Richartz-Museum, Cologne, where it is catalogued as Das Ehepaar Sisley.

title: Monet w109
description: Heavy seas breaking against the pier at Le Havre, with the harbour lighthouse beyond, painted in 1868. At 147 × 226 cm it is one of the very large marine compositions of Monet's Salon-ambitious early years. Private collection.

title: Portrait de M. Alphonse Tissié en cuirassier
description: A standing portrait of Alphonse Tissié in the uniform of a cuirassier, his plumed helmet and breastplate set off against a plain ground. Oil on canvas by Bazille, held at the Musée Fabre in Montpellier.
credit: PaintingAll

title: Portrait of an anonymous as a Troubadour
description: A bust-length portrait of a young man costumed as a medieval troubadour, his collar and cap evoking the Romantic revival of the type. The sitter is identified as the poet Paul Verlaine; Bazille painted the canvas in 1868, and it is now in the Dallas Museum of Art.
credit: The AMICA Library; Dallas Museum of Art

title: The Academy of Architecture
description: Eduard Gaertner records Schinkel's Bauakademie on the Spreeinsel in 1868, some three decades after the building's completion, its distinctive red terracotta façade filling the right half of the composition while a horse-drawn carriage and pedestrians animate the street below. A Gothic church tower rises beyond the building on the left. The Bauakademie was damaged in 1945 and subsequently demolished in 1962.
credit: Zeno.org , ID number 20004023463

title: The Birthday
description: Edith, the artist's wife, is shown in three-quarter view wearing a dark dress with white fur collar trim, a richly patterned shawl, and a red bead necklace, holding an ornate beaded purse and a red rose. Dated 1868, the portrait's exacting detail of ornament and fabric — some acquired during Hunt's eastern travels — exemplifies his characteristic Pre-Raphaelite finish in an intimate register.

title: The Luncheon
description: An ambitious early figure painting by Monet showing a woman in black, a younger woman and a small child at a white-clothed luncheon table, and a servant standing in the background of a dark interior. The everyday domestic subject anticipates the themes that would define Impressionism; the canvas was submitted to and rejected by the Salon of 1870. Dated 1868, it is held at the Städel Museum in Frankfurt.

title: The Sea at Le Havre
description: A dark sailboat rides rough, foam-flecked seas beneath a cloud-heavy sky, with the sandy shore and a harbour structure just visible at the left. Monet painted this Channel seascape at Le Havre in 1868, capturing the energetic movement of surf and sky in broad, vigorous strokes; the work is in the Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburgh.
credit: Wikipedia Loves Art at the Carnegie Museum of Art This photo of item # 53.22 at the Carnegie Museum of Art was contributed under the team name " dewey_decimals " as part of the Wikipedia Loves Art project in February 2009. Carnegie Museum of Art The original photograph on Flickr was taken by Moira Burke — please add a comment to the original Flickr page whenever a use has been made on Wikipedia or another project. Project galleries on Flickr: this institution , this team

title: The Triumph Of Christianity Over Paganism.Gustave Doré
englishTitle: The Triumph of Christianity over Paganism
description: A vast allegorical canvas in which a cross-bearing Christ, ringed by sword-wielding angels, sweeps above the toppling deities of antiquity. Dore stages the contest as a vertiginous airborne procession, exploiting the canvas's monumental scale to push the pagan host into chaotic free-fall below.

title: Thomas Carlyle Oil Painting 1868
description: A bust portrait of the historian and essayist Thomas Carlyle, white-bearded and turned in three-quarter view. Painted by Watts in 1868 and given by the artist to the National Portrait Gallery, London, in 1895 (NPG 1002); Carlyle himself disliked the likeness.

title: View of the Village
description: A young woman in a striped dress seated on a stone ledge above the village of Castelnau-le-Lez, the Hérault landscape spread behind her. Oil on canvas, painted in 1868 at the Bazille family property near Montpellier and now in the Musée Fabre.

title: View of Tiflis from Seid-Abaz
description: Tiflis, modern Tbilisi, spreads along the Kura river below the bluff of Seid-Abaz, its houses stepping up the slopes toward the surrounding Caucasian ridges. Aivazovsky toured the Caucasus in 1868 and produced a series of Georgian and Armenian townscapes, of which this is one.
credit: www.belygorod.ru

title: После неудачи
description: A painting by Russian realist artist Vasily Vereshchagin (1842–1904), known for his historical and genre scenes. The work continues Vereshchagin's tradition of narrative realism in nineteenth-century Russian art.

title: 1280px-Gérôme-Black Bashi-Bazouk-c. 1869
description: A study of an Ottoman irregular soldier, painted after Gérôme's travels through Egypt and the Levant. The figure's embroidered silks and weaponry are rendered with the polished, almost photographic finish that defined French academic Orientalism, set against a neutral studio ground that isolates costume and pose.

title: At the Races in the Countryside
description: An open carriage at a country racecourse, with a woman holding an infant under a parasol and a man in a top hat seated behind, while two horses are cropped abruptly at the right edge. Degas places the viewer alongside the Valpinçon family as racehorses and riders move across the wide green field behind them. The painting, dated 1869, is held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Boote
description: A study of moored rowing boats, the kind of riverside motif Monet repeatedly mined along the Seine. Water is rendered in horizontal slabs of broken colour, the hulls anchoring an otherwise nearly abstract surface.

title: Dervishes in Festive Attire
description: Three men stand closely together in richly patterned Central Asian robes and distinctive tall felt hats, their backs turned to the viewer. The careful ethnographic detail of their layered, multicoloured garments reflects Vereshchagin's travels in Central Asia during 1869–1870. Now in the Tretyakov Gallery, the painting exemplifies his documentary approach to the peoples and customs of Russian-administered territories.

title: Icarus and Daedalus
description: Daedalus fastening the wax-and-feather wings onto his son Icarus before flight, a subject from Ovid's Metamorphoses. Leighton painted the oil around 1869; it measures roughly 138 by 106 cm and belongs to the Faringdon Collection at Buscot Park, Oxfordshire.
credit: Art Renewal Center

title: In the Alatau Mountains
englishTitle: In the Alatau Mountains (deer in meadow)
description: A view across the Alatau range of the Tien Shan, painted during Vereshchagin's Central Asian travels. The canvas belongs to the Turkestan group of works the artist produced from sketches made on his journeys of 1869 to 1870 through what is now eastern Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.

title: Inside the Tent of a Rich Kirghiz
description: The interior of a wealthy Kyrgyz yurt, its felt walls hung with patterned textiles and the floor spread with carpets. One of Vereshchagin's ethnographic studies from his Central Asian travels of 1869 to 1870, later worked up as part of the Turkestan series.

title: La Grenouillère
description: Bathers and rowboats cluster around the floating café on the Seine at Bougival, the spot where Renoir and Monet spent the summer of 1869 painting side by side. Broken touches of opaque colour on the water mark one of the foundational moments of Impressionism.

title: Long Branch
description: Two fashionable women in bustled dresses pause on a cliff at the Jersey Shore resort, parasols snapping in the Atlantic wind. Homer's bright, almost Impressionist palette captures the new postwar leisure culture with magazine-illustrator clarity.
credit: The AMICA Library; Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, online database

title: Monet w0145
description: A snow-covered country road caught in the last warm light of a winter sunset, painted in 1869. The picture passed through the celebrated Max Silberberg collection and is now in the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rouen (43 × 65 cm).

title: Monet w148
englishTitle: Road at Louveciennes, Melting Snow, Sunset
description: The road at Louveciennes under melting snow, lit by a low winter sunset, painted in 1869. It dates from the winter Monet spent working in the villages west of Paris alongside Pissarro, testing how much colour a white landscape could hold. Private collection (40 × 54 cm).

title: On the Beach
description: A small group of bathers in dark dress stands at the water's edge beneath a brooding overcast sky, the breaking surf occupying the centre of the canvas in powerful horizontal bands of dark wave and white foam. Homer subordinates the figures to the elemental force of sea and sky, a composition characteristic of his early Atlantic coast paintings. Circa 1869, held at the Arkell Museum.
credit: PaintingDb, Object 8540

title: Portrait of Edmond Maître
description: Bazille's friend Edmond Maître seen in full profile, seated and reading a book in his lap, the ground darkening toward the upper left. Oil on canvas painted in 1869, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Selbstporträt im Alter von 78 Jahren
description: A late self-portrait at age seventy-eight, the Milanese master appraising himself with calm, unflattering directness. The restrained palette and tightly painted head reflect the academic rigour Hayez upheld at the Brera even as Romanticism gave way to verismo.

title: Still Life with Flowers and Fruit
description: An early still life arranging garden blooms alongside ripe pears and grapes on a draped surface. Painted before Monet committed fully to plein-air landscape, the canvas shows him testing dense impasto and saturated colour against the conventions of Salon still-life painting.

title: Still Life With Watermelon
description: An early student work made during Chase's Indianapolis years, the cut watermelon is laid out with the dark ground and dramatic highlights of the Munich-school tradition he would soon study at first hand. The picture predates his shift toward looser, brighter American Impressionism.

title: Summer Scene
description: Young men in swimming costume resting and wrestling along the wooded bank of the Lez near Montpellier. Bazille drew the figures in his Paris studio before placing them in the open-air setting; the oil was shown at the Salon of 1870 and is now in the Harvard Art Museums (Fogg).

title: The Bridge at Bougival
description: Painted during Monet's lean Bougival period alongside Renoir, the composition hinges on the stone-parapeted road bridge carrying figures across the Seine. The handling is still relatively tight, but already shows the rapid notation of reflections that would soon define Impressionism.

title: The Sailboat
description: Two fishing boats heel through heavy chop, their tan sails straining against a pale sky while the foreground dissolves into churned green water laid on with the palette knife. The canvas dates from around 1869, when Courbet was painting the Channel coast at Étretat and produced some of the most physical seascapes of the nineteenth century. It is in the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute, Williamstown, Massachusetts.

title: The Seine at Bougival
description: Painted from the riverbank at the village that drew Monet, Renoir and Pissarro alike, the scene catches a row of moored boats and the mirror of the Seine. Quick, comma-shaped strokes record passing reflections rather than fixed contours.

title: The Toilet
description: A seated nude attended by two servants, one kneeling to dry her foot, the other holding cloth, in a curtained interior. Oil on canvas, 130 by 128 cm, painted between December 1869 and March 1870 and now in the Musée Fabre, Montpellier.
credit: Official gallery link

title: The Wave
description: One of a series of stormy seascapes Courbet painted at Étretat in 1869, the breaking wave thickly built up with the palette knife. He treated water as solid matter, layering grey-green pigment against a leaden sky to register the weight rather than the glitter of the Channel.
credit: Städel Museum

title: The Wave
description: A large breaking wave surges beneath a brooding overcast sky, the foaming crest laid on with Courbet's characteristic palette-knife impasto. Painted between 1869 and 1870 on the Normandy coast, the canvas treats seascape as an encounter with raw matter rather than picturesque incident. The work is held at the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin.

title: В горах Алатау
englishTitle: In the Alatau Mountains (horsemen on slope)

title: Главная улица в Самарканде с высоты цитадели ранним утром
englishTitle: Main Street in Samarkand, from the Height of the Citadel in the Early Morning
description: A landscape painting by Russian artist Vasily Vereshchagin depicting the main thoroughfare of Samarkand viewed from the citadel in the golden light of early morning. Executed between 1869 and 1870, the work is part of Vereshchagin's Turkestan series, capturing the architectural character and atmospheric conditions of this historic Silk Road city.

title: Дети племени солонов
description: A painting by Russian artist Vasily Vereshchagin from his Turkestan series, depicting children from the Solon people. The work is part of Vereshchagin's ethnographic and orientalist documentation of Central Asian communities, currently housed in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

title: Киргизские кибитки на реке Чу
englishTitle: Kyrgyz Yurts on the Chu River
description: Kyrgyz felt tents (kibitki) pitched along the Chu river, which marks the border between present-day Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. Vereshchagin recorded the encampment on his Central Asian travels of 1869 to 1870, the source material for his Turkestan series.

title: Китайская палатка
description: A Chinese tent standing in a Central Asian landscape, recorded as Kitayskaya palatka. The study comes from Vereshchagin's Turkestan travels of 1869 to 1870 across the Russian Empire's newly conquered frontier in Central Asia.

title: Кочевая дорога в горах Алатау
englishTitle: Nomadic Road in the Alatau Mountains
description: A painting by Russian artist Vasily Vereshchagin (1842–1904) depicting a nomadic caravan traversing the Alatau mountain range. Vereshchagin was renowned for his historical and orientalist works, often capturing scenes of Central Asian landscapes and cultures during the 19th century.

title: Перекочевка киргизов 2
description: A small party of Kyrgyz nomads crosses the grassy steppe, their camels loaded with carpets and household goods, the lead animal carrying a tall carpet-draped litter, while a rider on horseback brings up the rear and birds wheel overhead. Vereshchagin painted the scene in 1869-1870 for his Turkestan series; it is held in the Tretyakov Gallery.

title: Проход Барскаун
description: A mountain landscape from Vasily Vereshchagin's Turkestan series, depicting the dramatic Barskaun Pass. This work exemplifies the Russian painter's fascination with Central Asian geography and his precise, detailed approach to depicting remote landscape formations.

title: Развалины китайской кумирни. Ак-Кент
englishTitle: Ruins of a Chinese Shrine. Ak-Kent
description: Painted by Russian artist Vasily Vereshchagin during his Central Asian expeditions, this work depicts the remains of a Chinese Buddhist temple at Ak-Kent in Kazakhstan. Created between 1869 and 1870 as part of his Turkestan series, the painting documents the architectural and cultural traces left by ancient Buddhist settlements along the Silk Road.

title: Развалины Чугучака
description: A landscape painting from Vasily Vereshchagin's Turkestan series depicting the ruins of the ancient city of Chuguchak (Tacheng) in Xinjiang. The composition captures the desolate architectural remains with figures and lions amid the desert landscape. Oil on canvas, now in the Russian Museum.

title: Садовая калитка в Чугучаке
description: A work by Vasily Vereshchagin depicting a garden gate in Chuguchak (Tacheng), a historical trading city in Central Asia. Vereshchagin's oriental scenes and architectural studies from the region are notable for their ethnographic detail and precise rendering of local customs and geography.

title: Barge Haulers on the Volga
description: Eleven harnessed labourers heave a barge upstream across a vast, sun-bleached Volga sandbar, their faces individuated portraits of exhaustion and stoicism. Repin's early masterpiece announced the social conscience of the Peredvizhniki, marrying academic figure construction to a panoramic Russian landscape.
credit: lj.rossia.org (missing, not archived)

title: Biondina
description: A close head-and-shoulders study of a fair-haired young Italian girl, her white blouse laced with a dark bodice, titled with the Italian for the blonde one. The oil belongs to the Hamburger Kunsthalle and is dated by the museum to 1879.

title: Camille sitting on the beach at Trouville
description: Camille Doncieux on the beach at Trouville during the family's stay in the summer of 1870, painted in the open air with sand reportedly still embedded in the paint. The handling is rapid and sketch-like, capturing wind, light and the moment of leisure.

title: Chill October
description: An autumnal Perthshire backwater under leaden skies, painted from a sandbank on the Tay near Murthly. Millais himself called this his first true landscape, and its damp, unromantic mood anticipates the meditative late landscapes that occupied his final decades.

title: Eagle Head
description: Three young women emerge from the surf onto the Cape Ann shore, their wet bathing dresses clinging in a way that scandalized contemporary critics. Homer treats the scene as a study of weight, wind and waterlogged fabric rather than narrative incident.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 20011474)

title: en
englishTitle: Entrance to the Port of Trouville
description: Boats crowd the harbour mouth of the Norman resort of Trouville, where Monet honeymooned with Camille in the summer of 1870. The pictures from that holiday — sand still embedded in some of the canvases — were the last he made before fleeing the war to London.

title: Hôtel des roches noires. Trouville
description: Holiday-makers promenade before the grand facade of the Hôtel des Roches Noires at Trouville, flags snapping in the sea breeze above. Painted in the summer of 1870, shortly before the outbreak of the Franco-Prussian War, the canvas is a rapid plein-air study; traces of actual sand have been found embedded in the paint surface. It is held at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - Riders Crossing The Desert
description: A substantial group of mounted and on-foot travellers crosses a sun-bleached desert plain, rust-coloured hills rising in the distance and a larger caravan trailing behind them in a haze of dust. Gérôme, painting after his 1868 Sinai expedition, deploys an oil-on-panel surface of great smoothness to convey the dazzling midday light. The 1870 work — 41 × 56 cm — exemplifies his frieze-like arrangement of colourful figures against an expansive desert landscape.

title: L'atelier de Bazille
description: The painter's studio at 9 rue de la Condamine in the Batignolles quarter of Paris, hung with canvases and peopled by his circle, Bazille himself shown at the easel. Painted in 1870; Manet contributed the figure of Bazille, and the work has been in the Musée d'Orsay since 1986.

title: Monomakh's hunting
description: Grand Prince Vladimir Monomakh of Kievan Rus rests on the grass after a boar hunt, his retinue and dogs gathered around the kill. Painted in 1870 while Vasnetsov was still a student at the Imperial Academy, the picture anticipates his later turn toward medieval Russian history and bylina subjects.

title: Still Life with Hummingbird
description: A hummingbird hovers at the apex of a dense floral arrangement in an ornate vase, the roses, carnations and grasses rendered against a warm ochre ground. The tightly observed bird and academic handling of the blooms reflect Chase's Munich-trained still-life manner in his earliest years. Painted in 1870, the work is held in the collection identified in museum records as Q1117704.

title: Surikov-Horseman2
description: An alternate version of the Bronze Horseman composition, with Falconet's equestrian Peter the Great rearing on the Senate Square pedestal beside the Neva. Surikov produced the study in 1870 during his Academy years in St Petersburg, before the Moscow history paintings that would make his reputation.
credit: AllArt [1]

title: The Beach at Trouville
description: Monet depicts the busy wooden boardwalk at Trouville, where fashionably dressed visitors promenade with parasols against the backdrop of the town's grand seafront hotels and flags. The sea gleams in the distance under a cloudy sky, and the composition captures the resort's sociable, sunlit atmosphere through loose, confident brushwork. Painted in 1870, the work is now in the Wadsworth Atheneum Museum of Art.

title: The boardwalk on the beach at Trouville
description: A breezy Norman seaside view from Monet's 1870 Trouville stay with Camille, days before the Franco-Prussian War sent him into London exile. Sand grains are reportedly embedded in the paint, evidence of true plein-air execution.

title: The Orchestra at the Opera
description: Degas looks into the orchestra pit of the Paris Opera, where the bassoonist Desire Dihau, a friend of the painter, dominates the foreground among portrait heads of fellow musicians, while the stage above is reduced to a frieze of cropped dancers' legs and glowing tutus. Painted around 1870, the oil on canvas now hangs in the Musee d'Orsay. Its abrupt cropping and off-axis viewpoint anticipate the compositional devices of the ballet pictures Degas pursued over the following two decades.

title: The Shadow of Death
description: A Pre-Raphaelite vision of Christ as a young carpenter stretching after labor, his outflung arms casting a cruciform shadow across the workshop wall. Hunt painted the scene in Jerusalem to ground every tool, shaving and textile in archaeological accuracy.

title: Young Woman with Peonies
description: A Black woman holding out a bouquet of pink-and-white peonies beside a basket of tulips, roses and lilac, posed as a flower seller. Oil on canvas, 60 by 75 cm, painted in 1870 and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington; a related version is at the Musée Fabre.

title: 1871 Vereshchagin Apotheose des Krieges anagoria
description: A pyramid of human skulls rises on a scorched plain before a ruined city, crows wheeling overhead. Vereshchagin, a veteran of the Russian campaigns in Turkestan, dedicated the canvas "to all conquerors, past, present and to come"; it is the closing image of his Turkestan series.

title: A rich Kyrgyz hunter with a falcon
description: A wealthy Kyrgyz hunter on horseback with a hooded falcon on his gloved fist, dressed in a heavy embroidered robe. Vereshchagin painted the subject in 1871 from observations made on his Central Asian travels for the Turkestan series.

title: After Vespers
description: Catalogue Entry: A member of the Royal Academy by 1864 and elected its president in 1878, Frederic, Lord Leighton reached the apex of the British art world at a young age. Knighted in 1878, ennobled in 1886, and elevated to a life peerage as Baron of Stretton (ironically, the day before he died), he rose through the ranks of society in a manner that was unprecedented for a modern British artist. Leighton’s great success coincided with the Aesthetic movement of the 1870s and 1880s, in which a cult of beauty reigned in literature, the fine arts, and especially the decorative arts.
credit: Princeton University Art Museum

title: Houses by the Bank of the River
description: Painted during Monet's Dutch sojourn after the Franco-Prussian War, the canvas shows a row of green-shuttered houses reflected in the Zaan. Long horizontal brushstrokes mirror the calm of the Holland waterways that fascinated him.
credit: Städel Museum

title: In the Alpine High Valley
description: A solitary figure stands at the base of a dramatic alpine gorge, dwarfed by sheer cliff faces that rise on either side into a storm-lit sky. The steep, narrow composition concentrates the sense of scale and isolation that marks Spitzweg's later landscapes. Painted circa 1871 and now in the Museum Kunstpalast, Düsseldorf.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - The Slave Market
description: An outdoor slave market in the Ottoman world: several female captives in various states of undress wait against a whitewashed wall while a figure in white attends from an alcove above. Gérôme distributes figures across the scene with the detached ethnographic precision that marks his market pictures, rendering sunlit plaster, worn carpet, and shadow with equal care. The work, dated 1871, is one of several slave-market compositions by the artist and is held in the Cincinnati Art Museum.

title: La Classe de danse
