description: In a rehearsal room of the old opera house on the rue Le Peletier, dancers in white tutus practise at the barre and rest along the back wall while the ballet master Jules Perrot leans on his long staff at the centre. Degas worked on the oil on canvas between 1871 and 1874, repeatedly revising the poses. One of the founding pictures of his ballet series, it now hangs in the Musee d'Orsay.

title: La Zaan à Zaandam
description: A broad-sailed barge moves along the Zaan at Zaandam, with windmills lining both banks and red-roofed Dutch houses reflected in the warm ochre and blue water beneath a cloud-filled sky. Monet painted this and related views in 1871 during a stay in Holland following his departure from Paris during the Franco-Prussian War, producing some two dozen canvases along the Zaan.

title: LE PORT DE ZAANDAM
description: Monet painted this view of Zaandam harbour in 1871 during a stay in the Netherlands, showing moored sailing barges and Dutch townhouses beneath a warm, golden evening sky reflected in the still water. The canvas belongs to a series of Zaandam works in which Monet explored reflected light and the picturesque character of the Dutch waterways.

title: Méditation
description: Camille Doncieux, the painter's first wife, reclining on a sofa in quiet thought. The intimate domestic subject and muted tonal range belong to Monet's early-1870s figure painting, before his work shifted decisively outdoors toward pure landscape and atmospheric study.

title: Monet w182
description: Windmills along the waterways of Zaandam, painted during Monet's stay in Holland in 1871 as he returned from his London exile after the Franco-Prussian War. The Dutch canals and mills furnished him with some two dozen canvases that year. Private collection (48 × 73 cm).

title: Nocturne: Grey and Gold
description: Westminster Bridge and the Thames vanish into a haze of grey-blue twilight, pierced by scattered gold lamplight. The painting belongs to Whistler's Nocturne series, in which musical titles signalled the priority of tonal harmony over narrative.

title: Portrait of Mlle. Hortense Valpinçon
description: Hortense, the young daughter of Degas's childhood friend Paul Valpinçon, stands at a richly embroidered table and holds a small object in her hands, returning the viewer's gaze with quiet composure. Painted in 1871, the portrait is celebrated for the vivid textile in the foreground set against the plain floral wallpaper behind the girl. It is now at the Minneapolis Institute of Art.

title: Portrait of the Artist's Mother
description: Anna McNeill Whistler sits in profile in a London interior, bonneted and dressed in black against a pale grey wall hung with one of her son's etchings. The strict horizontal-vertical geometry and muted palette underscore Whistler's framing of a familial portrait as a tonal arrangement.
credit: Musée d'Orsay

title: Prayer in the Mosque Alternative title
description: Worshippers stand and prostrate themselves in prayer within a large colonnaded mosque interior, its striped arches and soaring nave rendered with Gérôme's characteristic precision. Pigeons wheel among the hanging lamps overhead. Painted in 1871, the work reflects Gérôme's direct study of Egyptian architecture and Islamic religious practice during his repeated travels in the region.

title: Still life with fruit
description: Grapes, peaches, a melon, pears and other fruit are arranged on a stone ledge before an open landscape of grass and sky. A wicker basket of red fruit and a butterfly enliven the composition. Painted in 1871 and now held at the Parrish Art Museum, the work shows Chase's early academic command of the traditional fruit-piece genre.

title: The Champion Single Sculls
description: A sculler — identified as Max Schmitt — rows a yellow shell on a calm stretch of the Schuylkill River in bright daylight, with a second sculler visible in the middle distance and an iron railway bridge spanning the background. Eakins, also thought to be depicted in the middle distance, built the composition from precise perspective studies of the river's bridges and rippled surface. The painting, dated 1871, is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: The Great Pyramid at Giza
description: The Great Pyramid of Giza rising over the Egyptian desert under low warm light, with small figures at its base. Aivazovsky, better known for marine subjects, painted the oil in 1871; the canvas later passed through Christie's, London.
credit: Christie's , LotFinder: entry 5379962 (sale 7905, lot 26, London , 29 November 2010)

title: The Thames below Westminster
description: A view across the Thames toward the Houses of Parliament and Westminster Bridge, dissolved in river mist. Painted during Monet's wartime exile in London, the canvas anticipates by three decades his later Thames series, already setting silhouetted architecture against a pearly, fog-bound sky.

title: Variations in Pink and Grey: Chelsea
description: A Thames-side view in which large furled red sails on a barge serve as the dominant vertical accents against a pearly grey river and overcast sky. Fashionably dressed pedestrians stroll along the embankment in the foreground, reduced to soft colour notations. Painted between 1871 and 1872, this work exemplifies Whistler's reformulation of landscape as tonal colour harmony.

title: Windmills Near Zaandam
description: A girl walks the dyke path between Oostzaan and Zaandam, windmill sails turning over flat polder land. Painted during Monet's 1871 Dutch sojourn after his English exile, the picture's narrow tonal range catches a typical overcast Holland sky.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: “And the Prayer of Faith Shall Save the Sick”
description: A late biblical genre piece taking its title from the Epistle of James, set within a sunlit Eastern interior. Lewis casts the scriptural episode in the Cairene domestic vocabulary he had perfected over decades. Mashrabiya light falls across patterned cushions and the bedside attendants in saturated colour.

title: 1872 Vereshchagin Triumphierend anagoria
description: Set in Samarkand's Registan square, a victory ceremony unfolds before the great madrasa portals while Russian soldiers' heads stand impaled on poles in the foreground. Vereshchagin pairs the splendour of Timurid tilework with documentary atrocity, a recurring strategy of his Turkestan cycle.
credit: Tretyakov Gallery

title: Argenteuil
description: A promenade of trees lines the right bank of the Seine at Argenteuil while two sailboats move on the open water in the distance and strollers walk in dappled afternoon light. Monet settled at Argenteuil after the Franco-Prussian War and made it the crucible of Impressionist landscape painting; this canvas, now at the National Gallery of Art, dates from around 1872.

title: Arrangement in Gray: Portrait of the Painter
description: Whistler portrays himself in a broad black hat and light grey coat, holding paintbrushes against a near-uniform grey ground. The carefully tuned tonal intervals, with face and hat providing the principal points of contrast, exemplify the musical analogies for picture-making that underlie his Arrangement titles. Painted around 1872, the work is known as Arrangement in Gray: Portrait of the Painter.

title: Claude Monet - Argenteuil - 1872 - Musée d'Orsay
description: Sailboats rest on the still surface of the Seine at Argenteuil, the suburban boating town where Monet settled after the Franco-Prussian War. Reflections on calm water became a central subject during his years there. Painted in 1872, the canvas is now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
credit: JackyM59 - Muba de Tourcoing Avril 2024

title: Der Tanzsaal
description: Young ballerinas gather in a high-windowed rehearsal room of the Paris Opera, one working at the barre while the others wait their turn or adjust their dress. This small oil, roughly 19 by 27 centimetres and painted around 1870-1872, stands at the very beginning of Degas's ballet series, in which the company's working spaces served as a laboratory for studies of light and arrested movement. It came to the Metropolitan Museum of Art with the H. O. Havemeyer bequest in 1929.

title: Impression
description: The harbour of Le Havre at dawn dissolves into vapour, masts and cranes ghosted behind an orange sun whose reflections crackle across the water. Exhibited at the first independent show of 1874, its title supplied a hostile critic with the term 'Impressionism' that would name the movement.

title: Ivan Constantinovich Aivazovsky - Moscow in Winter from the Sparrow Hills
description: A snowbound panorama of Moscow viewed from the Sparrow Hills, the city spreading toward the horizon beneath low winter cloud. Painted in 1872 on a 46 by 72 cm canvas, the picture is a rare urban subject from Aivazovsky, whose practice was overwhelmingly marine.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - Rider and his Steed in the Desert
englishTitle: Rider and his Steed in the Desert
description: A horseman rests against the flank of his exhausted mount in the brassy heat of the desert afternoon, barren hills behind. Gérôme exploits a low horizon and brushed-smooth surface to evoke the still, shimmering air of his North African travels.

title: Monet w197
englishTitle: Argenteuil Seen from the Small Arm of the Seine
description: The town of Argenteuil viewed from the petit bras, the quiet side channel of the Seine around the Île Marante, painted in 1872 during Monet's first year living there. The small arm became one of his favourite early Argenteuil motifs. Private collection (50 × 65 cm).

title: Monet w222
description: An Argenteuil scene from the year of the first Impressionist exhibition's gestation. Monet works en plein air, registering reflections on water and the play of leaves with rapid, divided touches.

title: Monet w224
description: The Seine at Argenteuil in late-afternoon light, with a sailboat resting on the broad reach of the river, painted in 1872. The horizon sits low, giving most of the canvas to sky and water. Private collection (60 × 81 cm).

title: Nocturne in Blue and Gold: Old Battersea Bridge
description: Old Battersea Bridge looms in silhouette over the Thames at dusk, its piers stretched into a near-Japanese vertical. Whistler reduced river, sky, and timber to a few veils of blue and gold, treating the cityscape as an arrangement of tones in line with his Aesthetic credo.

title: On the Beach -- Two Are Company
description: A wood engraving after Winslow Homer published in Harper's Weekly, depicting a flirtation interrupted on a New England beach. Homer's Reconstruction-era illustrations chronicled American leisure with a wry observational eye.

title: Pierre-Cécile Puvis de Chavannes 007
description: A young woman in a white dress sits on rocky ground, extending one arm to hold a small sprig, while behind her a broad landscape opens to reveal ruins and rows of grave crosses — an aftermath of war. Painted in 1872, the work is an allegory of Hope by Pierre Puvis de Chavannes, rendered in the pale, simplified tonalities he derived from fresco. It is housed in the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.

title: Pollice Verso
description: A staged Roman amphitheatre scene in which a victorious mirmillo stands over his fallen opponent and looks up at the Vestals' thumbs-down verdict. Gérôme drew on his own collection of antique armour for the gladiators' helmets and helped fix Hollywood's mental image of the arena.
credit: phxart.org : Gallery , Pic

title: Pont-Neuf
description: Pedestrians and carriages cross Paris's oldest bridge under a clear summer sky, the Seine glittering between embankments. Renoir's brother Edmond reportedly delayed passersby in conversation so the painter could capture them in rapid, sun-drenched touches.
credit: National Gallery of Art .

title: Regattas at Argenteuil
description: Sails crowd the Seine basin at Argenteuil, doubled in vivid downward strokes that read almost as flames on the water. The painting's loose vertical reflections were among the works that helped define the Impressionist handling of moving light on water.

title: Springtime
description: A young woman, almost certainly Camille, sits reading in dappled shade beneath flowering trees. Pink-white blossoms and green foliage are dissolved into a single shimmering screen of broken touch, an early statement of Monet's plein-air figure painting.

title: Still Life
description: A red lacquered tray bearing blue-and-white porcelain cups, saucers, and a small teapot occupies the right half of a cloth-covered table, while a large potted plant fills the left in this 1872 still life by Monet. The spare arrangement and Japanese-style lacquer tray reflect the Japoniste taste of the period. The painting, titled Still Life, is held at the Dallas Museum of Art (inv. 2019.67.12.McD).
credit: ArtKnowledgeNews.com

title: The Biglin Brothers Racing
description: Professional oarsmen John and Barney Biglin pull in unison in their pair-oared shell on the Schuylkill River, observed by spectators on a barge and along the tree-lined shore. Eakins, an avid rower, built the composition from careful perspective studies; the painting is now at the National Gallery of Art.

title: The Bridge at Villeneuve-la-Garenne
description: The cast-iron suspension bridge of 1844 across the Seine, looking toward Villeneuve-la-Garenne, with boats and figures along the bank. Oil on canvas, about 50 by 65 cm, painted in 1872 and acquired from the artist by Durand-Ruel that August; now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (object 437680).
credit: Transferred from en.wikipedia ; transferred to Commons by User:Common Good using CommonsHelper , Original uploader was Alcinoe at en.wikipedia , 15 March 2005 (original upload date); Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 437680)

title: The Highway Bridge under repair
description: The highway bridge at Argenteuil is shown mid-repair, its timber scaffolding framing a view down the Seine toward a distant townscape, painted in 1872. Pedestrians and a horse-drawn cart cross the upper roadway while the river below carries sailing vessels through the construction. Monet treats the industrial scaffolding with the same attentiveness he brought to more conventional landscape motifs of the period.

title: The Petit Bras of the Seine at Argenteuil
description: A quiet backwater of the Seine fringed by bare poplars and reflected on a glassy surface. Painted in the first weeks of Monet's settlement at Argenteuil, the canvas balances delicate atmospheric grey-blues against incipient Impressionist touch.
credit: http://luxfon.com/pic/201205/1366x768/luxfon.com-15625.jpg https://www.nationalgallery.org.uk/paintings/claude-monet-the-petit-bras-of-the-seine-at-argenteuil

title: Villeneuve-la-Garenne
description: The cast-iron suspension bridge across the Seine at Villeneuve-la-Garenne, with a stone pier at its centre and rowing boats below. Sisley painted the span during a campaign in the Argenteuil district in 1872, oil on canvas, now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (gift of Mr. and Mrs. Henry Ittleson Jr., 1964).

title: Двери Тимура
description: A painting by Russian orientalist master Vasily Vereshchagin from his celebrated Turkestan Series, depicting the ornately carved doors of the legendary Central Asian conqueror Timur (also known as Tamerlane). Executed in 1872, the work exemplifies Vereshchagin's meticulous attention to architectural and decorative detail during his travels in the Caucasus and Central Asia.

title: Продажа ребенка-невольника
englishTitle: The Sale of the Child Slave
description: A harrowing orientalist painting by Russian artist Vasily Vereshchagin depicting a wealthy Ottoman buyer inspecting a young enslaved boy for purchase. Executed in 1872, this work from the artist's Turkestan series condemns the dehumanization of slavery through unflinching realism.

title: 1873 Monet Houses at Argenteuil anagoria
description: Painted in the Paris suburb where Monet lived from 1871 to 1878, the heart of the early Impressionist project. A row of villas behind a flowering garden is rendered in broken touches of green, rose and violet, light flickering across stucco walls.

title: A Lady Receiving Visitors
description: A harem interior in Cairo, where a seated lady greets her guests amid mashrabiya screens and a sun-dappled mosaic floor. Lewis lived a decade in an Ottoman house in the city and made the filtered light through latticed windows his signature subject. Every textile, slipper and tile is rendered in jewel-bright watercolour clarity.

title: A Walk in the Meadows at Argenteuil
description: A red poppy field stretches across the foreground, with a woman and child near the lower centre and two more figures ascending the slope toward a pair of poplars in the middle distance. Painted in 1873 during Monet's Argenteuil years, the canvas combines vivid dots of scarlet with a broad, cloudy sky and is held by the Rhode Island School of Design Museum.

title: American Shipping off the Rock of Gibraltar
description: A three-masted ship runs under full sail through heavy swell at sunset, the Rock of Gibraltar rising in the haze behind a second vessel to the right; in the foreground a crowded open boat lifts on the crest of a turquoise wave. Aivazovsky, principal painter of the Russian Navy, painted the canvas in 1873, identifying the shipping in its title as American.

title: Autumn on the Seine
description: Riverside trees in russet and gold are doubled in the still surface of the Seine. Painted from the bank at Argenteuil, the picture exploits Monet's preferred device of mirrored reflection, the upper and lower halves of the canvas answering one another in horizontal bands.

title: Ballettprobe
description: Dancers in white tutus rehearse in a large, light-filled studio, a seated violinist accompanying them at the left while tall windows open onto a view of rooftops and trees. Degas captures the informal rhythm of preparation, the figures scattered across the room in varied poses. The 1873 painting, titled Ballettprobe, is held by the Fogg Museum, Harvard.

title: Boys in a Dory
description: Four boys in straw hats drift in a flat-bottomed dory on still harbor water, one perched on the bow with bare legs dangling, while schooners ride at anchor in the haze beyond. Homer painted the sheet in watercolor and gouache during the summer of 1873 at Gloucester, Massachusetts — his first sustained campaign in the medium that would become central to his art. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: Breezing Up
description: A catboat heels into a stiff wind, four figures — three boys and an older man at the tiller — braced along the gunwale as spray breaks around the hull. A second vessel appears on the horizon to the right. Homer worked on this composition between 1873 and 1876, and the finished oil became one of his best-known celebrations of post-Civil-War American leisure.

title: Confusion of Tongues
description: An illustration to Genesis 11 from Doré's English Bible, depicting the workers scattering as the Tower of Babel founders mid-construction. Doré stages the scene with vertiginous architecture and a gulf of stormy sky, exploiting the dense black hatching of wood-engraving to dramatise divine judgement.
credit: National Library of Poland

title: Cow Boys
description: Two barefoot boys in straw hats stand on a sunlit hillside, one upright and gazing into the distance, the other seated below him. The landscape opens behind them to a broad sky with scattered clouds, a red barn just visible at the far right. Watercolour, dated 1873, the work is catalogued as Cow Boys and held at the David Owsley Museum of Art, Ball State University.
credit: Ball State University Libraries: Digital Media Repository

provenance.collection: David Owsley Museum of Art Ball State University

title: Dad's Coming!
description: A boy seated beside a beached dory stares out toward a horizon dotted with distant sails, while a woman stands a little behind him looking in the same direction. The paired figures and their mutual waiting convey the coastal anxieties that run through Homer's early shore paintings. Dated 1873, the oil is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Gérôme Eminence grise 1873
description: Capuchin friar François Leclerc du Tremblay descends a staircase at the Palais-Cardinal, courtiers bowing to the grey habit while ignoring the man inside it. Gérôme stages the scene as silent political theatre, contrasting the friar's coarse wool against polished marble and gilded livery.

title: Girl in the Hammock
description: A woman reclines in a hammock slung between trees in a shaded garden, reading a book, a red shawl visible beside her. Light filters through the leafy canopy, and Homer's close attention to the play of sun and shadow across the foliage fills the picture with a decorative, almost flat quality. The oil, dated 1873, is held at the Colby College Museum of Art.
credit: Bridgeman Art Library : Object 401146

title: Jacob Wrestles with the Angel
description: A wood-engraved illustration from Doré's English Bible (1866), depicting Genesis 32 — Jacob struggling through the night with a divine adversary at the ford of the Jabbok. The dense black hatching and theatrical lighting are hallmarks of Doré's Romantic graphic style.
credit: National Library of Poland

title: Masked Ball at the Opera
description: Top-hatted men press around costumed women in dominoes beneath the colonnaded foyer of the old Paris Opéra on rue Le Peletier, painted only months before the building burnt down. Manet compresses the crowd into a frieze of black coats, reading the bourgeois carnival as a study in modern social ritual.
credit: National Gallery of Art .

title: Monet w 290 autumn effect in argenteuil
description: A view along the Seine at Argenteuil, where Monet was based through much of the 1870s, painted at the moment when foliage flares into copper and gold. The water carries the autumn colour back as a lattice of broken reflections, a hallmark of his river pictures from these years.

title: Monet w265
description: Sailboats off Sainte-Adresse, the resort beach just north of Le Havre where Monet had painted since the mid-1860s. This canvas dates from an 1873 return to the Normandy coast at the height of his Argenteuil years. Private collection (48 × 74 cm).

title: Naked Woman Lying on a Couch
description: A nude woman reclines at full length on a cushioned divan, one arm raised behind her head, her body rendered with candid, almost photographic directness against crumpled silken bedding. Caillebotte painted this canvas in 1873, and the work exemplifies the unsentimental scrutiny he brought to the female nude in contrast to the academic tradition of idealized form. The freely handled fabric and warm tonal palette place it securely within his early Impressionist manner.

title: Railroad Bridge
description: A railway bridge strides across the Seine on pale stone piers, a steam train trailing billowing smoke above the water, while a sailboat glides below on the left. Monet painted this junction of industry and leisure on the Seine at Argenteuil in 1873, making the bridge and its reflections a recurring subject of his years there. The canvas is held at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

title: Rainbow
description: A rainbow arches above a shipwreck and lifeboat tossed in heavy seas, survivors pulling at the oars while the sky breaks open behind them. Painted in 1873 and now in the State Tretyakov Gallery, the canvas is one of Aivazovsky's signature meditations on rescue at sea, salvation hinging on a sliver of coloured light.
credit: Государственная Третьяковская Галерея

title: Selbstporträt
description: Viktor Vasnetsov depicted himself in this 1873 self-portrait wearing a brown coat and cravat, with auburn hair and a full beard, against a dark background with an easel partly visible at the left. The direct, quietly concentrated gaze and loose painterly handling reflect the realist training Vasnetsov received in those years.

title: Ships in a Harbor
description: Sailing ships ride at anchor in still grey water, their masts and rigging dissolving into a damp, overcast sky — a harbor scene generally identified as Le Havre. Painted about 1873, close in date and mood to Impression, Sunrise, it builds the scene from broken touches of muted colour rather than drawn detail. Oil on canvas, Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: The Artist's Garden in Argenteuil
description: Painted in 1873 and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, this canvas by Claude Monet shows a corner of his Argenteuil garden in full summer bloom, dahlias massed in reds and whites before the painter's house. Broken, impasto-rich brushwork captures the shimmer of light on foliage and flowers, with a lone figure visible near the building in the background. The work is a confident example of Monet's Impressionist garden subjects from his years in Argenteuil.

title: The Four Leaf Clover
description: A young girl in a white dress sits in a cottage garden, holding a small flower and turning it in her hands before a multi-paned window framed by climbing roses. The setting is domestic and sheltered, the mood absorbed and quiet. Painted in 1873, the work is held at the Detroit Institute of Arts.
credit: Bridgeman Art Library : Object 241624; Detroit Institute of Arts

title: The Luncheon
description: A white-clothed table set with crockery, a teapot, and fruit occupies the foreground of a sunlit garden, while two women converse in the background and a child sits at the left edge. Painted in 1873 and now in the Musée d'Orsay (RF 2774), this outdoor luncheon scene at Argenteuil captures the dappled light and relaxed domesticity of Monet's suburban life.

title: The Railway
description: A young woman — identified as Victorine Meurent — sits before iron railings above the cutting of the Gare Saint-Lazare, a puppy cradled in her arms and a closed book in her lap, her gaze meeting the viewer's directly. Beside her, a small girl in white leans against the railings to watch a passing train, visible only as a cloud of steam below. The painting was exhibited at the Salon of 1874 and is now held at the National Gallery of Art in Washington.

title: The Railway Bridge in Argenteuil
description: The iron railway bridge at Argenteuil cuts across the Seine in flat planes of pale stone, a steam train trailing white smoke above. Monet treats modern infrastructure as a legitimate motif of plein-air painting, balancing its industrial geometry against the soft river bank.

title: Wild Poppies Near Argenteuil
description: Camille and the young Jean Monet wade through high summer grass at Argenteuil, scarlet poppies dotted across the field in dabs of vermilion. A second figure-pair higher on the slope mirrors the first, knitting two moments into one composition.

title: Мулла Рахим и мулла Керим по дороге на базар ссорятся
englishTitle: Mullah Rahim and Mullah Kerim Quarrelling on Their Way to the Bazaar
description: Vasily Vereshchagin's 1873 orientalist painting depicting two mullahs quarreling on the way to the bazaar. Part of his Turkestan series, exemplifying his ethnographic visual documentation of Central Asia.

title: 'The Grand Quay at Havre' by Claude Monet
englishTitle: The Grand Quay at Le Havre
description: A working harbour view of Monet's home port, painted the year of the first Impressionist exhibition. Masts, smokestacks and reflections dissolve into rapid, comma-like strokes, the artist treating modern dockside bustle with the same atmospheric urgency he had just brought to Impression, Sunrise.

title: Boating
description: A man in a straw hat and white clothes handles the tiller of a small sailboat while a woman in a blue dress reclines at the stern, her back turned to the viewer. The saturated blue of the water fills the entire background, creating the flat, cropped composition that reveals Manet's debt to Japanese prints. Painted at Argenteuil in 1874, the work is now in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: Buddhist Temple in Darjiling. Sikkim
description: A Buddhist temple at Darjeeling in the eastern Himalayas, its painted woodwork and prayer banners set against the mountains. Vereshchagin made the study during his Indian journey of 1874 to 1876, one of roughly 150 sketches from the trip, oil on canvas in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
credit: Tretyakov Gallery

title: Canoeists near Argenteuil
description: Sailboats and rowers drift on the Seine at Argenteuil, the Parisian suburb where Monet lived through the early 1870s and turned regatta-day leisure into a recurring subject. Quick comma-strokes describe water and rigging with equal economy.
credit: L'Évasion des Sens : MONET_Canotiers à Argenteuil

title: Fishing boats leaving the harbor
description: Sail-rigged fishing boats slip out of Le Havre on an overcast day, the harbour walls and shipping dissolved into muted silhouettes. Monet painted the port repeatedly in the early-to-mid 1870s, and this canvas of 1874 belongs to the same serial engagement with the Norman coast that began with Impression, Sunrise two years earlier.

title: Hunting Birds at Night
description: Peasants club pigeons flushed from the trees by torchlight, the flock caught in a burst of flame against the night. The subject came from Millet's own childhood memories near Gréville, and the canvas was his last completed painting before his death in 1875, now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"m/millet/08huntin"; Philadelphia Museum of Art

title: Le Bassin du Commerce
description: A canvas of Le Havre's commercial basin, the harbour from which Monet had launched Impression, Sunrise two years earlier. Painted with rapid broken touches, the work continues his investigation of Channel-port atmospheres, where masts, smoke and reflected light become almost interchangeable.

title: Le Pont d'Argenteuil
description: The road bridge at Argenteuil, rebuilt after the Franco-Prussian War, frames moored sailboats on the Seine. Monet used the same bridge in several canvases of 1874, varying the viewpoint and weather to test how a single motif behaves under changing light.

title: Monet w327
description: A stretch of the Seine near Argenteuil, painted in 1874, the year of the first Impressionist exhibition. River, bank and sky are knit together in the broken touch Monet had made his signature on this water. Private collection (55 × 66 cm).

title: Moonlight
description: Two figures sit silhouetted on a dark beach as a full moon rides high above the horizon, its reflection stretching across the breaking surf. Homer uses a restricted palette of dark teal, grey and brown to evoke the stillness of a coastal night, the moon's halo and the white foam the only bright notes in the composition. Dated 1874, the work is held at the Fenimore Art Museum.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; Fenimore Art Museum

title: Pont Argenteuil Monet 1
description: Sailing boats line the basin at Argenteuil beneath the highway bridge, their masts reflected in the broken blue water of the Seine. The picture belongs to the suburban riverscapes that defined the early Impressionist summers of 1872 to 1874.

title: Regatta in Molesey
description: Sailing boats and spectators on the Thames at Molesey, bright bunting strung along the bank for the local regatta. Sisley painted the scene during a four-month stay in England in 1874, oil on canvas, bequeathed by Gustave Caillebotte and now in the Musée d'Orsay (R.F. 2787).

title: Répétition d'un ballet sur la scène
description: Dancers in tutus drift through a stage rehearsal, one yawning behind a flat, the ballet master and observers grouped in shadow at the wings. The Metropolitan's version, in oil thinned to a near grisaille, is one of three closely related compositions Degas worked on around 1874, the largest of which appeared in the first Impressionist exhibition that April.

title: Self-portrait
description: Aivazovsky, in his late fifties and at the height of his European reputation, turns his head sharply to the side, his dark side-whiskers and formal dress set against a grey-green ground. He painted the self-portrait in 1874 for the Uffizi's collection of artists' self-portraits in Florence, following Orest Kiprensky as only the second Russian artist so honoured.

title: Snow at Argenteuil
description: A muffled village street under fresh snow, part of Monet's sustained study of Argenteuil winters. The white ground is laid in with cool blues and lilacs rather than pure white, a decisive Impressionist break from academic monochrome.
credit: Google Art Project works from the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art

title: Summer
description: A woman sits in a broad, open meadow near Argenteuil, a parasol and light wrap beside her, while a second figure in pale dress stands in the distance. The vast sky and flat field fill the canvas with summer light and air. Painted in 1874 and now in the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin, the work belongs to a group of figure-in-landscape compositions from Monet's Argenteuil period.

title: The Geese
description: Geese make their way along a sunlit stream past a farmhouse half-hidden by trees, painted in 1874 during Monet's Argenteuil years. The shimmering surface of the water and the dappled foliage are rendered in quick, broken touches of gold and green. Now held at the Clark Art Institute, the picture belongs to a group of rural farmyard subjects Monet pursued alongside his better-known river scenes of the mid-1870s.
credit: Clark Art Institute

title: The North-West Passage / Die Überfahrt nach Nord-West / Le Passage du Nord-Ouest
description: An aged mariner sits in a chair by a window overlooking the sea while a young woman reads aloud from a book at his feet, a large map spread on the table and a Union Jack displayed on the wall behind them. Millais painted The North-West Passage in 1874 as an allegory of British Arctic determination; the canvas, now at Tate Britain, became one of the most widely reproduced images of Victorian patriotic sentiment.
credit: Not necessary, PD by age.

title: The Rehearsal Onstage
description: Dancers in white tutus rehearse on a sparsely set stage while the ballet master gestures from the right and men in dark coats - the subscribers admitted backstage - watch from chairs at the wings. Executed around 1874 in pastel over a brush-and-ink drawing on paper, the sheet exploits the steep downward view from a stage box, pushing the floor up against the picture plane in a manner Degas absorbed in part from Japanese prints. One of three closely related versions of the composition, it belongs to the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 110000595)

title: The Road to Hampton Court
description: A road running past garden walls towards Hampton Court, figures walking under a high, clouded sky. Painted during Sisley's 1874 stay near London, when he produced a series of nearly twenty views of the non-tidal Thames, oil on canvas, now in the Neue Pinakothek, Munich.

title: The Windmill on the Onbekende Gracht
description: A tall Amsterdam windmill dominates the composition, flanked by Dutch canal-side buildings whose rooflines and reflections fill the water below. Monet painted this view on the Onbekende Gracht during his 1874 visit to Holland, one of several Dutch trips he made during his Impressionist years. The canvas is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.
credit: Bridgeman Art Library : Object 129973; Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, online collection

title: The Zuiderkerk
description: A view up the Groenburgwal canal toward the spire of the Zuiderkerk, painted during Monet's brief Dutch sojourn. The canvas already carries the rapid, broken brushwork of nascent Impressionism, dissolving brick facades and water into vibrating coloured strokes.

title: A Corner of the Apartment
description: An interior view of the Monet family's Argenteuil home, with young Jean standing at the end of a darkened hallway between hanging plants and curtained light. The painting marks one of Monet's rare domestic interiors, balancing silhouetted shadow against a glowing window.

title: Au Café-concert : La Chanson du chien
description: A café-concert singer leans forward at the footlights, her gloved hands shaped like a dog's paws as she performs the popular novelty song known as the Chanson du chien. Worked up between 1875 and 1877 in gouache and pastel over a monotype base, the sheet belongs to a group of small night-life scenes Degas made of the open-air café-concerts along the Champs-Élysées.

title: Bartolomeo Magagnosco by John Singer Sargent 1875
description: A pencil head-and-shoulders study of Bartolomeo Magagnosco, inscribed Nice, January 1875, when Sargent was nineteen and travelling on the Riviera with his family. Now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art, the sheet shows the assured contour drawing that underpinned the oil portraits with which Sargent would debut at the Paris Salon two years later.

title: Camille au métier
description: An intimate domestic scene of Monet's first wife, Camille Doncieux, seated at an embroidery frame in their Argenteuil home. The painter treats the patterned tapestry, dress, and wall hangings as a single woven field of colour, dissolving figure and interior into a continuous surface of touches.

title: Camille Monet and a Child in the Artist's Garden in Argenteuil
description: Camille Monet sits sewing on the lawn of the family garden at Argenteuil, a child settled in the grass at her feet, with a bank of flowers closing off the scene behind them. Painted in 1875, it is one of the intimate garden pictures of Monet's Argenteuil years, domestic life rendered entirely in outdoor light. Oil on canvas, Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Étretat
description: Inness looks down from a hillside above Étretat across green meadows where sheep and cattle graze, with the village and the famous white chalk cliffs visible in the middle ground and the grey Channel beyond. Two figures pause in the foreground pasture beneath a gathering, dramatic sky. Dated 1875 and held at the Wadsworth Atheneum, Hartford, the canvas reflects Inness's atmospheric approach to European landscape during his sojourns abroad.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; Wadsworth Atheneum

title: In a café or L’Absinthe
description: The actress Ellen Andrée and the engraver Marcellin Desboutin sit side by side at a marble café table, the woman staring blankly past a tall glass of cloudy absinthe. Originally exhibited under the title Dans un café and reset as L'Absinthe at its London showing of 1893, the picture was painted at the Nouvelle-Athènes in Pigalle and is now in the Musée d'Orsay.

title: La Yole - The Skiff - Renoir
description: Two young women row a vivid orange skiff on the Seine at Chatou, the river populated by sailboats and a distant railway bridge. Renoir's complementary contrast of cobalt water and chrome-orange hull, applied in feathered touches, captures the leisurely Impressionist suburb of the 1870s.
credit: National Gallery

title: Le Pont d` Argenteuil - Claude Monet
description: Monet's 1875 view of the road bridge at Argenteuil looks across dense riverside vegetation toward the rebuilt multi-arched span, with the town of Argenteuil visible beyond. The composition is unusual in privileging the lush foreground growth over the river itself, rendered with the quick, broken brushwork that defines his Impressionist period at this Seine town. The work is held in the National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina.
credit: MNBA logo This file, part of the Collection of the Fine Arts Museum, was provided to Wikimedia Commons thanks to an agreement between the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes and Wikimedia Argentina .

provenance.collection: National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina
provenance.location: National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina

title: Les Grands Boulevards - Renoir - 1875 - NG
description: A Paris boulevard busy with strollers and carriages beneath thin spring trees, the rebuilt Haussmann city stretching back along the pavement. Renoir painted it in 1875, oil on canvas measuring about 52 by 64 cm, now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
credit: The National Gallery, London

title: Man in a Toque; Self-Portrait
description: Gauguin, in his late twenties and still a Paris stockbroker, looks out from beneath a soft toque in muted browns and greys. Painted around 1875 to 1877, the small canvas is the earliest known self-portrait of an artist whose face would become one of the most painted subjects in his late Polynesian work; it is in the Harvard Art Museums.
credit: Harvard art museum wesbsite

title: Meadow with Poplars
description: A figure in white moves through a wide flower-filled meadow near Argenteuil, with a cluster of poplars rising at the left and a broad open sky beyond. Painted in 1875 and known as Poplars near Argenteuil, the work shows Monet's early engagement with the suburban Seine landscape and the interplay of figures within an expansive summer field.

title: Monet w357
englishTitle: View of Argenteuil in the Snow
description: Argenteuil under snow, painted during the hard winter of 1875 when Monet produced an extended group of snow effects around the town. The canvas (55 × 74 cm) is now in the Musée d'Art et d'Histoire in Geneva.

title: Monet w368
description: Pleasure boats moored on the Seine at Argenteuil, painted in 1875. The boat basin, with its rented sailboats and weekend traffic from Paris, was among the motifs Monet repeated most often during his years there. Private collection (54 × 65 cm).

title: Monet w386
englishTitle: The Artist's Family in the Garden
description: Monet's family in the garden of their Argenteuil home, painted in 1875. It belongs to the run of domestic garden pictures from these years in which figures sit half-absorbed into beds of flowers and foliage. Private collection (61 × 80 cm).

title: Mr and Mrs Edwin Edwards
description: Edwin Edwards and his wife Ruth are portrayed together, he seated among papers and prints, she standing beside him, both in Fantin-Latour's habitual sober blacks. The Edwardses were the artist's closest English patrons, channelling his still lifes into the London market; this 1875 double portrait, held at Tate, London, is among the most intimate records of that long friendship.
credit: Tate, London 2009 [1]

title: Nocturne
description: Part of Whistler's celebrated Nocturne series, in which the painter pared the Thames down to washes of dusky blue and pewter. The work treats landscape as a tonal arrangement, anticipating the abstract sensibilities Whistler championed in his Aesthetic writings.
credit: The White House Historical Association

title: Nocturne in Black and Gold: The Falling Rocket
description: Showers of golden sparks fall through a smoky night sky above the Cremorne Gardens fireworks. The thinly washed, near-monochrome surface so provoked John Ruskin that his attack triggered the famous 1878 libel trial.
credit: Detroit Institute of Arts

title: Place de la Concorde
description: Ludovic-Napoléon Lepic, cigar in hand and umbrella tucked under his arm, strides across the windswept square with his two daughters and a borzoi, a solitary man cropped at the left edge. Painted in 1875 and now at the Hermitage by way of the Gerstenberg collection and Soviet trophy art transfers, the picture places Lepic's silhouette over the statue of Strasbourg, then a recent emblem of loss to Prussia.
credit: studyblue.com

title: Portrait of Dr. Samuel D. Gross
description: A monumental scene of surgeon Samuel Gross presiding over an operation before his medical students at Jefferson College. Eakins records the bloodied hand, the chloroformed patient and the rapt amphitheatre with uncompromising realism, anchoring American painting in the lecture-hall light of modern science.

title: Red Boats
description: Sailing boats with orange-red hulls are moored on the Seine at Argenteuil, backed by a house and tall poplars on the left bank; smaller vessels and a white sail dot the wide river beyond. The flickering reflections and high-keyed palette typify the river scenes Monet painted at Argenteuil during the suburb's pivotal Impressionist years. Now in the Fogg Museum, Cambridge, Massachusetts.

title: Renoirgarden
description: A woman shaded by a parasol stands amid blossoming flowerbeds, her figure dissolving into the surrounding foliage. Renoir uses fragmented, comma-like brushstrokes and unmodulated touches of pure colour to fuse figure and garden into a single shimmering field of sunlight.

title: Self-portrait
description: A bust-length self-portrait with unkempt hair and beard, the painter in a striped shirt and dark tie against a loosely brushed ground. Renoir made it in 1875, oil on canvas, and showed it at the second Impressionist exhibition the following year; it is now in the Clark Art Institute, Williamstown.
credit: Renoir, peintre du bonheur : 1841-1919 , de Gilles Néret, Köln, Taschen, 2001, p. 190. ISBN 9783822857410

title: Self-portrait
description: A bust-length self-portrait, the painter turned slightly with a heavy beard, set before a reversed landscape on the studio wall. Catalogued as FWN 434 and dated about 1875, the canvas was probably worked up in Armand Guillaumin's studio in Paris, whose own river view hangs behind the sitter.

title: The grand canal of Venice
description: Painted on a Venetian visit alongside Monet, the canvas captures the Grand Canal in shimmering broken touches of blue, white and ochre. Striped mooring posts cut vertical accents through the rippling water, marking Manet's most overtly Impressionist experiment.
credit: wikipaintings.org

title: The Iron Rolling Mill
description: A grimy panorama of the Königshütte rolling mill in Upper Silesia, with workers wrestling glowing iron under shafts of furnace light. Menzel spent months on site making hundreds of drawings, producing one of the first ambitious European paintings to take heavy industry as its subject.

title: The Studio Boat
description: Monet's floating studio, a converted boat moored on the Seine that let him paint from the water itself. Manet had recorded him at work in it; here the vessel becomes the subject, half-shaded under a bank of trees.

title: The Yerres
credit: Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art Provenance Project

title: Train in the Snow
description: A steam locomotive pushes through a snow-covered road flanked by bare trees, figures and fencing just visible in the grey winter light. Painted in 1875 and now in the Musée Marmottan Monet, Paris, the canvas shows Monet treating engine smoke and winter atmosphere as allied phenomena, building the scene from short, vigorous strokes of grey, white, and black.

title: View of Argenteuil - Snow
description: A snow-covered street or road at Argenteuil stretches toward buildings and hills in the background, with several dark-clad figures making their way through the winter landscape. Monet rendered the scene in a muted palette of white, blue-grey, and warm rooftop ochres. Painted in 1875, the work is in the collection of the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City.
credit: The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City

title: 'The Standing Bearer
description: A solitary, face-veiled standard-bearer in a white robe stands before an ornate mosque entrance holding an enormous green and red ceremonial banner aloft on its staff. Gérôme, working from his Egyptian observations, renders the carved stone portal and embroidered textile with characteristic precision. Titled also The Standard Bearer, the painting dates to 1876 and belongs to the Haggin Museum, Stockton, California.
credit: hagginmuseum.org

title: A Girl with a Watering Can
description: A small girl in a blue dress and lace-trimmed pinafore stands on a garden path holding a watering can, flowers scattered at her feet. Renoir painted the figure in 1876, oil on canvas, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington (Chester Dale Collection).

title: A Parisian Lady
description: A near-life-size portrait of the actress Ellen Andrée in fashionable street dress, her black silhouette set against a flat ground in Manet's signature manner. The picture pursues the figure of the modern Parisienne championed by Baudelaire rather than a sitter's likeness.
credit: Erik Cornelius / Nationalmuseum

title: Acrobats. Festival in a Paris suburb
description: A lit fairground stage at night draws a working-class Parisian crowd; a white-costumed Pierrot stands on the steps while musicians beat drums and a horse waits in the wings behind a red canvas backdrop. Painted between 1876 and 1877 during Vasnetsov's stay in Paris, the canvas captures the louder, theatrical side of popular entertainment on the city's outskirts. The work is held in the Russian Museum, St Petersburg, and marks the years just before the artist turned decisively to Russian folklore subjects.
credit: Scanned from A. K. Lazuko Victor Vasnetsov, Leningrad: Khudozhnik RSFSR, 1990, ISBN 5-7370-0107-5

title: Aivazovsky by Bolotov
description: Ivan Aivazovsky sits in three-quarter view in a dark coat, his broad side-whiskers framing a clean-shaven chin, a pencil poised over the drawing board resting on his lap. Dmitry Mikhailovich Bolotov painted the portrait in 1876, when Aivazovsky, official painter to the Russian Navy since 1844, was among the most celebrated artists in the empire.

title: Bal du moulin de la Galette
description: A bustling Sunday afternoon at a Montmartre dance garden, where dappled sunlight filters through the trees onto crowds of working-class Parisians. Renoir's loose, broken brushwork captures shifting light and lively conversation, treating modern leisure as a worthy subject for monumental painting.

title: Bank of the Seine in Autumn
description: The bank of the Seine under autumn foliage, reflections breaking across the water in short horizontal strokes. Sisley painted the riverside subject in 1876, oil on canvas, working in the loose touch he developed alongside Monet in the villages west of Paris.

title: Carlo Pellegrini
description: Carlo Pellegrini, the Italian-born caricaturist who signed his Vanity Fair plates as Ape, is shown full-length in dark street clothes, his red-auburn beard prominent against a loose ochre ground. The sheet is inscribed 'à lui' and signed Degas, and dates to around 1876. It is a work on paper by Edgar Degas, produced circa 1876.

title: Dans la prairie
description: Camille Monet reads in a meadow thick with wildflowers, a green parasol raised above her and the blooms dissolving around her in broken, high-keyed brushwork. Monet painted this in 1876, during his Argenteuil years, and first exhibited it in Paris in 1877 — an early demonstration of his method of integrating the figure into the vibrating colour of an outdoor scene.

title: Dore-I had done a hellish thing
description: A wood-engraving from Doré's late illustrated edition of Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, showing the sailor clinging to the rigging after slaying the albatross. Dense parallel hatching builds the storm-charged sea and the cramped vertigo of the crow's nest.
credit: University of Adelaide

title: Einzug des Kronprinzen Friedrich Wilhelm von Preußen in Jerusalem 1869
description: Wilhelm Gentz's monumental oil on canvas, more than two and a half meters wide, records the entry of Crown Prince Friedrich Wilhelm of Prussia, the future Emperor Frederick III, into Jerusalem in November 1869, a visit made on his journey to the opening of the Suez Canal. The prince rides a white horse at the center of a teeming procession outside the city walls, surrounded by dignitaries, onlookers in Ottoman and Arab dress and waving palm fronds, with the domes of Jerusalem beyond. Gentz, a specialist in Orientalist subjects, completed the painting in 1876, when it was acquired by the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin.

title: Evening at Argenteuil
description: An evening on the Seine at Argenteuil, 1876, in which a small boat carrying two figures drifts on a river gilded by the setting sun. Reeds crowd the near shore while poplars rise against a luminous cloud-streaked sky, the water surface dissolving into horizontal bands of pink, gold, and grey reflection.

title: Fin d'arabesque
description: A soloist holds a final triumphant pose, one arm raised and the other lowered with a flower bouquet, her gaze inclined downward while a group of other dancers cluster in the background. Degas's 1876 work, held in the Musée d'Orsay, captures a moment of stage performance in his characteristic combination of pastel and other media on paper.
credit: Musee Orsay

title: Flowers in a Rococo Vase
description: A mixed bouquet of roses, anemones, and other flowers spills from an ornate Rococo vase with blue scrollwork, set against a pale grey-blue ground. Paul Cézanne painted this still life around 1876; it is now in the collection of the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Gérôme--Femme circassienne voilée--Veiled Circassian Beauty--1876
description: A bust-length study of a Circassian woman whose features are partially obscured by a dark veil, her eyes meeting the viewer directly as she holds a long staff. She wears a richly embroidered blue robe with gold decoration. Signed by Gérôme and dated 1876, the work — oil on canvas, 40.7 × 32.6 cm — is now in the Lusail Museum's collection.

title: Google Art Project levels adjustment 2
description: Repin's graduation piece for the Imperial Academy of Arts depicts the Novgorod merchant-hero Sadko in the underwater kingdom of the Sea Tsar, choosing a bride from a procession of foreign maidens. Painted in Paris, it earned him a gold medal and signalled an early turn toward Russian folkloric subject matter.

title: Grapes and Walnuts on a Table
description: A still life of black grapes and walnuts spread on a white cloth, a knife laid across the table edge. Sisley rarely painted still life, making the 1876 canvas unusual in his output, which is dominated by river and village landscapes.

title: Hunting
description: A hunting scene from 1876, an unusual subject for Monet, who almost never painted narrative motifs. It belongs to the decorative panels commissioned by Ernest Hoschede for the chateau de Rottembourg at Montgeron.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - Pool in a Harem
description: Two nude women rest beside the pool of a tiled hamam interior, shafts of light falling through high vents in the vaulted ceiling. A dark-robed attendant stands in the foreground, carrying a long-stemmed pipe. Gérôme renders the Iznik-tiled walls, marble floor, and warm flesh with his characteristic near-photographic precision. The work, dated circa 1876, is held in the Hermitage Museum, St Petersburg.

title: La Balançoire
description: A young woman stands on a rope swing in a garden talking with a man seen from behind, sunlight falling in patches of blue and rose through the leaves. Renoir painted it in the summer of 1876 in the gardens below the Moulin de la Galette, oil on canvas, now in the Musée d'Orsay.

title: Le Bassin du Jas de Bouffan
description: The pond in the grounds of the Jas de Bouffan, the Cézanne family estate near Aix-en-Provence, ringed by trees with a sculpted lion spout at the water's edge. Cézanne painted the bastide and its garden in some thirty-six oils across forty years; this view, dated about 1876, is in the Hermitage Museum, Saint Petersburg.
credit: Hermitage Museum; arthermitage.org

title: Le bateau atelier
description: Monet's floating studio moored on a calm waterway, its cabin and hull reflected in still water below. A figure is visible aboard the boat, surrounded by the leafy bank beyond. The work is held by the Barnes Foundation, Philadelphia, and dates from 1876, when Monet used the vessel at Argenteuil to paint the Seine from the water's surface.

title: Le bateau-atelier - MAH Neuchâtel
englishTitle: The Studio Boat (Musée d'Art et d'Histoire, Neuchâtel)
description: The floating studio Monet had built at Argenteuil, a small cabined skiff that let him paint directly on the Seine. Reflections double the boat in rippling vertical strokes, an image of the artist's working method as much as a landscape.

title: Monet w397
description: A pruned, ball-shaped tree standing at the water's edge at Argenteuil, its round crown doubled in the river's reflection, painted in 1876. Monet makes the mirrored geometry of tree and reflection the whole subject. Private collection (60 × 81 cm).

title: Monet w419
description: The Pond at Montgeron, painted at the country estate of the collector Ernest Hoschede, who commissioned a group of decorative panels from Monet. Reflections on still water already prefigure the Giverny obsession to come.

title: Moving House
description: An elderly couple shuffle across a frozen waterfront in winter, sharing the weight of a heavy sack while a small dog trots beside them; the gilded spire of the Peter and Paul Fortress rises in the mist behind them, placing the scene firmly in St Petersburg. Painted in 1876, the canvas is one of Vasnetsov's early Realist genre works, attentive to the hardship of urban poverty, and is held in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
credit: Scanned from: A. K. Lazuko Victor Vasnetsov , Leningrad: Khudozhnik RSFSR, 1990, ISBN 5-7370-0107-5

title: On the Banks of the Nile
description: Two laden camels rest on a grassy bank beside the Nile, their ornate saddlery and tasselled trappings rendered in precise detail against a wide, cloud-filled blue sky. Waterfowl gather at the water's edge below, and a small figure with a basket appears among the reeds in the middle distance. Painted in 1876, long after Lewis's return to England, and now in the Yale Center for British Art, the composition draws on the Egyptian sketches he continued to mine throughout his later career.

title: Portrait d'Ernest Hoschedé et sa fille Marthe
description: Ernest Hoschedé and his young daughter Marthe seated together on a garden bench, the girl holding a flower, the paint laid down in broad open strokes. Manet began the plein-air portrait at the Hoschedé estate at Montgeron in 1876; it is now in the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, Buenos Aires.

title: Portrait of Victor Chocquet
description: The collector Victor Chocquet seen bust-length against patterned wallpaper, his greying hair and beard built up in close-keyed strokes. Chocquet, a customs official who amassed dozens of Impressionist canvases, was introduced to Cézanne by Renoir in 1875; the portrait dates from about 1876 to 1877.

title: Portraits in the Countryside
description: Four women — Caillebotte's mother, aunt, cousin, and a family friend — sit reading and sewing on the terrace and lawn of the family's Yerres estate, bathed in dappled afternoon light. Caillebotte organises the figures with his characteristic geometric clarity, each woman absorbed in her own activity while the lush garden stretches behind them. Painted in 1876, the canvas is a study in bourgeois leisure rendered with Impressionist directness.

title: Song of the Lark
description: A young farmhand pauses in a sunlit field, scythe and hat in hand, head tilted skyward toward the call of an unseen bird. Homer's 1876 canvas, now at the Chrysler Museum of Art, captures a suspended moment of rural American labour against an open summer landscape of green grasses and tall trees.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; Chrysler Museum of Art, search: 83.590; Google Art Project works from the Chrysler Museum of Art

title: Sunny Day. Spring
description: A sunlit Russian farmyard in spring: a weathered wooden cottage stands amid birch trees in fresh leaf, chickens scratch in the foreground, and warm light falls across the scene. Levitan painted this small oil in 1876 as a student at the Moscow School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture, and the title Sunny Day. Spring accords with the verdant, tranquil mood on display.

title: The Seine in Bougival
description: The Seine at Bougival, low banks and a pale sky reflected in still water. Sisley painted the riverside in 1876 during the years he worked the villages downstream of Paris, oil on canvas, the broken touch typical of his mature landscapes.

title: turf bench
description: Repin's wife Vera Alexeyevna, their daughters Vera and Nadya, and members of the Shevtsov family are gathered on a turf bench beneath leafy trees in an open-air setting. Painted in 1876, the work adapts the conventions of Russian realism to a relaxed plein-air group portrait bathed in warm summer light.

title: Überschwemmung in Port Marly
description: Floodwater standing in the streets of Port-Marly, a wine merchant's house rising from the inundated quay with a rowing boat alongside. Sisley returned to the flooded village several times in 1876, producing a small series of canvases of the high Seine.

title: Репин. Украинка у плетня
englishTitle: Ukrainian Woman by a Wattle Fence
description: Portrait of a Ukrainian peasant woman standing by a woven fence, painted by Russian-born artist Ilya Repin in 1876. The subject wears traditional Ukrainian dress including a decorated vyshyvanka and ornamental headdress, with arms crossed in a confident pose. Now held in the Latvian National Museum of Arts.

title: Arrival of the Normandy Train
description: Steam billows beneath the iron-and-glass shed of the Gare Saint-Lazare as a locomotive pulls in from the Normandy line. One of twelve canvases Monet made of the station in 1877, the series treated industrial vapour as a modern equivalent of mist on the Seine.

title: Artlib gallery-13875-o
description: An Orthodox priest holds a censer while a Russian military officer stands beside him on a vast autumnal steppe strewn with the bodies of fallen soldiers, a stormy sky filling most of the canvas. The work's Russian title — Побежденные. Панихида по убитым — translates as The Vanquished: Requiem for the Fallen, and the subtitle dates it to the 1877–1878 Russo-Turkish War. Vereshchagin made the war's human cost his sustained subject throughout this period.

title: Boating on the Yerres
description: Several oarsmen paddle narrow canoes along the Yerres river in bright afternoon light, the green riverbank reflected in the still water. Caillebotte painted this scene near his family estate at Yerres in 1877, now held at the Milwaukee Art Museum; the cropped horizontal composition and clean observation of leisure activity are characteristic of his approach to depicting bourgeois recreation outdoors.

title: Eugène Murer
description: The pastry cook and collector Eugène Murer, born Hyacinthe-Eugène Meunier, shown bust-length in a dark coat. Renoir painted the portrait in 1877; Murer eventually gathered some 122 Impressionist works, including fifteen by Renoir, and the canvas is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: Extérieur de la gare Saint-Lazare
description: Part of Monet's 1877 Gare Saint-Lazare series, the first concerted Impressionist meditation on industrial modernity. Steam, sunlight, and iron architecture dissolve into one another, the locomotive yard reframed as a study in coloured vapour.

title: Flowered Riverbank
description: A bank of the Seine near Argenteuil glows with large-headed dahlias and chrysanthemums against the warm light of a late-summer evening. Industrial smokestacks and a church tower are visible across the river, grounding this 1877 canvas in the working landscape Monet inhabited during his Argenteuil years. The work is held by the Pola Museum of Art.
credit: Pola Museum of Art

title: Market at Jaffa
description: A bustling market square in Ottoman Jaffa rendered with Bauernfeind's near-photographic precision, every robe, awning and stone of the citadel sharply observed. A trained architect turned Orientalist painter, he based such scenes on extensive study trips and on-site sketches in the Levant.

title: Monet w421
description: A train arriving at Montgeron, painted during Monet's 1876 stay at Ernest Hoschedé's estate of Rottembourg outside Paris. The railway subject anticipates the Gare Saint-Lazare series he would begin the following year. Private collection (81 × 60 cm).

title: Paris Street in Rainy Weather
description: A wet-cobbled Place de Dublin in Haussmann's rebuilt Paris, viewed from Rue de Moscou. Caillebotte, the Impressionists' patron and engineer, here departs from their feathery touch for a cool, photographic precision, deploying steep perspective and a near-life-size foreground couple.

title: Pond at Montgeron
description: A still pond at the Hoschedé estate of Rottembourg, Montgeron, mirrors lush deciduous trees and their dense canopy in flickering green reflections, while a single figure stands on the right bank. Monet was commissioned at Montgeron to produce four large decorative panels, and the sojourn deepened a personal relationship that would lead to his second marriage with Alice Hoschedé. Now in the Hermitage Museum, St Petersburg.

title: Portrait of a Man
description: A bearded sitter in a dark coat is shown in profile, seated in a red chair, one hand resting in his lap, against a muted grey-blue ground. Edgar Degas painted this portrait in 1877; the work measures 79 by 59 cm and is held at the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute, Williamstown.
credit: clarkart.edu

title: Portrait of Frances Sherborne Ridley Watts
description: Frances Sherborne Ridley Watts, known as "Fanny" and a childhood friend of the artist, is shown seated against a rose-red drapery in a dark dress with a white lace collar, a jewelled chain, and a red bow at the bodice. Painted in 1877, it was the first picture Sargent submitted to the Paris Salon, accepted while he was still a pupil of Carolus-Duran; the work is in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
credit: original upload: [1] higher resolution: [2]

title: Portrait of the painter Vasily Ivanovich Surikov
description: Vasily Surikov, the future painter of the Boyarynya Morozova and the Streltsy, sits in dark coat and full beard against a neutral wash, painted by his older Itinerant colleague Ilya Repin. The portrait is a record of friendship between two of the central figures of the Peredvizhniki, made at the start of Surikov's career as a history painter.

title: Porträt der Jeanne Samary
description: The Comédie-Française actress Jeanne Samary is shown resting her chin on her hand, wearing a low-cut teal dress against a rosy, freely brushed ground. Renoir painted this intimate portrait in 1877, now held at the Pushkin Museum of Fine Arts, Moscow; his feathery strokes give the sitter an air of warm, relaxed luminosity.

title: The Gare Saint-Lazare; Arrival of a Train - 1877
description: A locomotive pulls under the iron-and-glass shed of the Gare Saint-Lazare, steam rolling up to merge with the smoke-stained light. Part of a twelve-canvas series for which Monet secured permission to set up his easel inside the working terminus.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — the-gare-saint-lazare-arrival-of-a-train/gQHVYlLzUjpD7w

title: The Plum
description: A young woman sits alone at a café table, her chin resting on her hand and a brandy-soaked plum in a small glass before her, her gaze directed away. Manet renders her absorbed, suspended stillness in loose brushwork, her pink blouse and feathered black hat set against a red banquette and warm wood panelling. Painted around 1877, the work is held at the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art .

title: The Turkeys
description: White turkeys feeding across a grassy slope before the Château de Rottembourg, the birds cropped by the lower edge of the canvas. Monet painted the large panel in 1877 for his patron Ernest Hoschedé at Montgeron and showed it at the third Impressionist exhibition; it is now in the Musée d'Orsay.

title: 1280px-Gustave Caillebotte - The Orange Trees
description: Painted in the family garden at Yerres, the picture shows the artist's brother Martial reading beneath potted orange trees while a woman strolls in dappled sun. Caillebotte combines Impressionist light with the steep, photographically cropped perspective that distinguishes his contribution to the movement.

title: 1878 Vereshchagin Schlachtfeld am Schipkapass anagoria
description: From Vereshchagin's Balkan series, painted after his service in the Russo-Turkish War of 1877-78. Lines of Russian troops throw their caps in the air as a general on a white horse gallops past in salute, while the snow-covered field at Shipka Pass is strewn with the frozen dead of both armies. The canvas hangs in the Tretyakov Gallery.
fileUrl: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/... [imageinfo blocked by rate limit, but canonical Commons URL is reliable]

title: Bosphorus
description: Sailing vessels and a small rowing boat drift on the hazy waters of the Bosporus, their reflections dissolving in a pearly morning mist, while figures rest on the waterfront quay of Constantinople at the right. Aivazovsky painted this canvas in 1878, during one of several extended stays in the Ottoman capital where his marine panoramas attracted considerable patronage. The composition exemplifies his mastery of atmospheric light over water, a quality that made his Bosphorus views among the most sought-after of his later career.

title: Bouquet de glaïeuls
description: A bouquet of gladioli, from the brief stretch of still life Monet produced after settling at Vetheuil. The blossoms are massed in vertical accents of red and pink, paint laid on thickly to register petal against petal.

title: Café Singer
description: A café-concert singer performs with mouth open, her black-gloved arm thrust upward in a dramatic gesture, lit from below against a striped backdrop. Degas captured the raw physicality of popular entertainment in this 1878 pastel on canvas, now held at the Harvard Art Museums (Fogg Museum), part of a sustained series exploring the electric artifice of gas-lit stages.

title: Dancer Taking a Bow
description: A ballerina holds a low curtsy at the front of the stage, bouquet in hand, the corps blurred behind her in the footlight haze. Degas returned obsessively to such after-performance moments around 1878, drawn to the gap between drilled spectacle and momentary stillness.

title: En route pour la pêche
description: Women and children in Breton regional dress cross the sunlit tidal flats of Cancale carrying baskets of oysters, with sailboats and the harbour visible in the distance beneath a bright blue sky with billowing clouds. Shown at the Paris Salon in 1878, where it earned a second-class medal, the canvas — officially titled En route pour la pêche — brought the twenty-two-year-old Sargent to prominence. It is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Félicien Rops - Pornokratès - 1878
description: A blindfolded nude woman in stockings and heeled shoes leads a pig on a leash along a pedestal, above a frieze of prostrated allegorical figures labelled Sculpture, Musique, Poésie, and Peinture, while three winged putti hover overhead. Félicien Rops's 1878 satirical drawing, housed in the Musée provincial Félicien Rops, personifies the dominance of carnal appetite over the arts in a characteristic Decadent indictment of bourgeois culture.

title: Gustave Doré - Landscape in Scotland - Walters 372625
description: A Highland glen opens between steep, bare mountains toward a distant loch under a turbulent sky, with weathered trees, scattered boulders, and a stag visible in the middle distance. Painted in 1878 and held at the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore, the canvas applies the dramatic atmospheric effects associated with an earlier Romantic generation to a Scottish subject.

title: La Seine à Vétheuil
description: The Seine at Vétheuil, the riverside village where Monet settled in 1878 after leaving Argenteuil. Soft poplars and reflections built up in short, drily loaded strokes typify the more sober palette of his late-1870s landscapes.
credit: Collection Olivier Senn, Taken on 15 May 2019

provenance.collection: MuMa Museum of modern art André Malraux
provenance.location: MuMa Museum of modern art André Malraux

title: Landscape at Saint-Ouen
description: An early landscape from the industrial outskirts north of Paris, painted before Seurat formulated his pointillist method. Loose, almost Corot-like brushwork registers river, sky and bank in muted tones, a quiet rehearsal for the rigorous technique to come.

title: Madame Georges Charpentier and her Children
description: Madame Georges Charpentier (Marguerite-Louise Lemonnier, 1848-1904) and her children, Georgette-Berthe (1872–1945) and Paul-Émile-Charles (1875–1895)

title: Monet w502
description: The country road leading into Vétheuil, painted in 1878, the year Monet moved his family to the small Seine village downstream from Paris. The roads and fields around the town occupied him as much as the river itself. Private collection (49.5 × 60 cm).

title: Notes Nocturne lithograph by James McNeill Whistler 1878
description: A lone boatman crosses the misty expanse of Chelsea Reach on the Thames, with the Battersea factories and a ruined tower dissolved into atmospheric grey washes on the far bank. Whistler executed this lithotint in 1878 — titled Nocturne: The River at Battersea — using scraping on a prepared half-tint ground with blue chine appliqué. The work is held in the British Museum, London.
credit: British Museum [1]

title: On the Stile
description: Two young women meet at a wooden fence in a sunny pastoral setting, one seated on the stile and the other leaning against it, their hands nearly touching. The scene belongs to Homer's Houghton Farm idylls of the late 1870s, where rural leisure is rendered with the clarity of magazine illustration and a warm, unidealized light. Circa 1878, held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Portrait of Henri Michel-Lévy
description: The painter Henri Michel-Lévy stands in his studio leaning against his own canvases, a slack mannequin collapsed on the floorboards beside an open paintbox. Degas exhibited the 1878 portrait, now at the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum in Lisbon, at the fourth Impressionist exhibition under the title Artist in his Studio.

title: Portraits at the Stock Exchange
description: The banker Ernest May, top-hatted and pince-nez'd, listens to a colleague leaning over his shoulder while the trading floor blurs into faceless agitation behind them. Degas painted his collector and admirer in 1878,79, applying Edmond Duranty's call for portraits that read a sitter's profession in his bearing.
credit: Topofart Musée d'Orsay

title: Réception du Grand Condé à Versailles
englishTitle: Reception of the Grand Condé at Versailles
description: Louis XIV welcomes the Prince de Condé on the grand staircase at Versailles, the victorious general bowing as courtiers look on. Gérôme reconstructs the seventeenth-century scene with archaeological precision, marshalling marble, brocade and ceremonial hierarchy in the polished academic style he made famous.

title: Stilleben mit Chrysanthemen
description: A large bouquet of white chrysanthemums fills a decorative red-trimmed vase in this 1878 still life, now in the Musée d'Orsay. Painted around the time Monet settled at Vétheuil, the canvas applies loose, energetic strokes to the overlapping petals, treating the indoor subject with the same atmospheric directness he brought to his landscape work.

title: The Green Hill
description: A solitary female figure in a brown dress crouches on the sun-drenched lower slope of a gently rolling hillside, trees at the left horizon and open sky above. Homer reduces the composition to broad fields of colour — earth, grass, and cloud — with the single figure providing a quiet focal point. Painted in 1878, the work is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: The Milk Maid
description: A young woman in a pink floral dress carries a wooden pail through a sunlit pasture, a cow grazing and roosters at her feet. Homer painted this watercolour in 1878 during his summers at Houghton Farm, where rural labour provided the subjects for a celebrated series of pastoral works now held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington DC

title: The Rainbow
description: A rainbow descends through parting storm clouds over a pastoral meadow, where cattle rest and graze in the foreground and a farmstead sits to the left. George Inness painted this canvas around 1878, combining dramatic meteorological observation with the Swedenborgian spiritual symbolism that pervades his later work.

title: The Reaper
description: A solitary harvester in a wide-brimmed hat swings his scythe through a field of grain under a stormy summer sky, the pale stalks filling the foreground. The upright figure and brooding clouds give the scene a quietly monumental character. Painted in 1878 and associated with Homer's Houghton Farm period, the work is held at the Art Renewal Center.
credit: Art Renewal Center

title: The Road of the War Prisoners
description: Vasily Vereshchagin (Russian, 1842-1904). The Road of the War Prisoners, 1878-1879. Oil on canvas, 71 1/4 x 117 11/16 x 2 1/4 in.
credit: Brooklyn Museum

title: Vétheuil in Winter
description: Snow blankets the village of Vétheuil and its church on the hillside above the Seine, while figures in a small boat navigate the icy, partly frozen river below. The chalky palette of blue-grey and white conveys the severity of the winter season. Monet painted this view around 1878–1879; the canvas is in the Frick Collection, New York.
credit: The Frick Collection

title: Warm Afternoon
description: A woman lies stretched out on the grass in the shadow of a large tree, a sheep resting close beside her, while a flock grazes across the sunlit hillside behind them. The composition contrasts the shaded foreground with the warm, open pasture receding to a row of trees on the horizon. Painted in 1878, the work is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Winding the skein
description: Two fair-haired women wind a skein of wool on the flat roof of a whitewashed house, a bay and distant hills behind them. Leighton drew on sketches made at Lindos on Rhodes in 1867 and first exhibited the canvas in 1878; it is now in the Art Gallery of New South Wales, Sydney.
credit: This file was derived from: Lord Frederic Leighton - Winding the skein - Google Art Project.jpg :

title: Winners
description: Drawn from Vereshchagin's Balkan series, the painting confronts the aftermath of battle: victorious soldiers in red-trimmed coats move among the fallen on a grey, open field. The Russian realist refused to glamorise war, building documentary detail into a deliberately disquieting scene of defeat and death. Painted between 1878 and 1879, the large canvas exemplifies Vereshchagin's unflinching engagement with the human cost of conflict.
credit: picture.art-catalog.ru

title: 1280px-Pierre Puvis de Chavannes - Young Girls by the Seaside
