description: Three pensive nymphs are arranged in a frieze along a pale shore, an Arcadian reverie rather than a specific place. Puvis de Chavannes paints in the chalky, fresco-like matte tonality that made him a touchstone for Symbolists and for the young Picasso and Seurat.

title: At the Café
description: Café patrons gather around a table in a Parisian brasserie, observed with the cool detachment Manet brought to modern social life. A man in a top hat and a woman drinking from a glass are among the loosely rendered figures, their faces emerging from sketchy, broadly brushed handling. The high horizon and cropped edges signal Manet's increasingly Impressionist-inflected approach, painted around 1879.

title: At the Père Lathuille Restaurant
description: On the terrace of a fashionable suburban restaurant, the proprietor's son leans intimately toward a lady lunching alone. Painted en plein air during Manet's late embrace of Impressionist technique, the canvas glows with dappled sunlight and feathery, summery greens.

title: Banks of the Seine at Lavacourt
description: The Seine winds past the village of Lavacourt across from Vétheuil, where Monet lived from 1878. The riverbank views he painted there mark the brightening palette and broken brushwork of his fully mature Impressionism, made under the strain of his wife Camille's final illness.
credit: Photo I took at the Frick Art Museum

title: Camille Monet sur son lit de mort
description: Monet painted his first wife within hours of her death from uterine cancer at age thirty-two, the brushwork dissolving her features into a veil of violet, grey and white. He later confessed unease at finding himself analysing her colour rather than mourning her.

title: Campo de trigo
description: A field of standing wheat under a broad sky, the grain laid in with quick yellow and green strokes and no incident to interrupt the view. Renoir painted the landscape in 1879, probably near Wargemont on the Bérard family estate in Normandy; it belongs to the Carmen Thyssen-Bornemisza Collection in Madrid.
credit: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Carmen Thyssen-Bornemisza Collection

title: Degas
description: Two dancers in white tutus pause at the barre, both bent forward — one tending to her ankle, the other leaning along the rail. The ca. 1879 pastel and gouache on paper, measuring approximately 46 by 67 cm, belongs to the Shelburne Museum, Vermont, and exemplifies Degas's sustained attention to the unstaged moments between exercises.

title: Garden under Snow
description: A snow-covered Paris garden seen from the window, the bare branches and low wall reduced to muted whites, blues and umbers. Gauguin painted the small canvas in 1879, still a stockbroker and Sunday painter under Camille Pissarro's tutelage; it now hangs in the Budapest Museum of Fine Arts.

title: Girl and Laurel
description: A young woman in a white apron and close-fitting bonnet stands before a wall of flowering mountain laurel in full bloom, a basket in her hand and her gaze directed outward. The vertical composition and dense floral backdrop place the figure firmly within Homer's mid-career sequence of solitary rural women absorbed in the seasonal landscape. Dated 1879.
credit: Bridgeman Art Library : Object 241628

title: Grand Duchess Sofia at the Novodevichy Convent
description: Repin depicts the deposed regent Sofia Alekseyevna confined at Novodevichy Convent in 1698, her glare turned outward as a hanged Streltsy is glimpsed through the barred window. The picture compresses defeat, fury, and political claustrophobia into a single suffocating cell.

title: In the Conservatory
description: A fashionable Parisian couple — Monsieur and Madame Guillemet — pause among hothouse foliage, their hands almost meeting on a garden bench. Manet exhibited the canvas at the 1879 Salon, where its crisp drawing and modern subject bridged his Realist roots and Impressionist company.
credit: Curves adjusted from File:In the Conservatory.jpg . Originally: Google Arts & Culture: Home - pic 7 th level of zoom out of 8. Scaled down.

title: James Abbott McNeill Whistler
description: A small etching from Whistler's Venice set, produced after the artist arrived in the city following his bankruptcy. Sparing, calligraphic line on laid paper sketches a moored vessel against open water, the unworked paper standing in for sky and reflection.
credit: ArtDaily.com

title: La route de Vétheuil
description: A snow-effect view of the road leading into Vétheuil, the Seine-side village where Monet lived from 1878. The picture belongs to his series of winter landscapes painted en plein air, the broken brushwork registering the muted blues and lilacs of low northern light on settled snow.
credit: Christie's https://www.christies.com/lotfinder/Lot/claude-monet-1840-1926-la-route-de-vetheuil-6073948-details.aspx

provenance.collection: Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg, Florida, USA
provenance.location: Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg, Florida, USA

title: La Seine à Lavacourt
description: A broad, sunlit view of the Seine at Lavacourt, the village directly opposite Vétheuil where Monet lived from 1878 following his wife Camille's death. Painted in 1879, the canvas balances Impressionist broken brushwork with a spacious, horizontal calm, the sparkling river surface and cumulus sky rendered in vivid blues and greens.

title: Louise Jane Jopling
description: Louise Jopling, painter and society figure, stands three-quarter length in a dark dress richly decorated with floral embroidery and red trim at collar and cuffs, her dark hair close-cropped. By 1879 Millais had moved beyond his Pre-Raphaelite beginnings into a fluent portrait manner, and the work is now in the National Portrait Gallery, London.

title: Marie Buloz Pailleron
description: Marie Buloz Pailleron stands outdoors in a black lace-trimmed dress, her red hair and pale complexion contrasting against a lush green garden background. Sargent painted the full-length portrait in 1879 at the family estate, adopting a plein-air setting unusual for a society commission. The canvas is in the collection of the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Miss La La at the Cirque Fernando
description: The mixed-race acrobat Anna Olga Albertina Brown, billed as Miss La La, hangs by her teeth from a rope below the Cirque Fernando's painted dome. Degas attended several performances in January 1879 and produced sketches and an oil study before this canvas, his only circus subject, went on view at the Fourth Impressionist Exhibition.

title: Monet w526
description: A view of Vétheuil and the Seine valley around it, painted in 1879 during Monet's difficult first years in the village. The canvas (60 × 73 cm) is in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

title: Plum Trees in Blossom
description: Plum trees in full white blossom fill the foreground, with the rooftops and church of a village and a green hillside rising clearly behind — a composition that combines spring abundance with the settled Norman landscape. Painted in 1879, during Monet's years at Vétheuil, the canvas is held by the Hungarian National Gallery, Budapest.

title: Poppy Field near Vétheuil
description: Several figures move through a dense field of red poppies, with the town of Vétheuil and its church tower visible across the river in the middle distance. Monet painted this scene near Vétheuil in 1879, combining the poppy motif with human figures as he had done earlier at Argenteuil. The canvas is in the Foundation E.G. Bührle Collection.
credit: Stiftung Sammlung E.G. Bührle; ArtDaily.com

title: Sokolniki. Autumn
description: A woman in black walks a damp avenue through Moscow's Sokolniki park as wet yellow leaves and bare birches close in on either side. Levitan was nineteen and living in Saltykovka, having been expelled from Moscow in an anti-Jewish edict, when Pavel Tretyakov bought the canvas, the first Levitan to enter the Tretyakov collection.
credit: Tretyakov Gallery

title: Still Life with Pheasants and Plovers
description: Two pheasants and several smaller game birds are arranged on a white cloth, painted in 1879 and now in the Minneapolis Institute of Art. The still life dates from a period of personal hardship for Monet following his wife Camille's death that year. The muted, earthy handling is markedly more sober than his contemporary plein-air landscapes.

title: Susanna and the Elders
description: Laurits Tuxen's 1879 canvas takes up the biblical subject in a polished academic idiom. The nude Susanna crouches beside a serving woman while a single elder, glimpsed at the upper left, reaches for the drapery — the intrusion caught at the moment of discovery. The work is in a private collection.
credit: Self-photographed Villy Fink Isaksen

title: The Doorway
description: An ornate Renaissance doorway opens directly onto the water of a Venetian canal, its carved frame and latticed windows etched in dense detail that thins to almost nothing at the edges of the plate; a figure pauses on the shadowed steps within. The etching and drypoint belongs to the First Venice Set, the twelve plates the Fine Art Society commissioned from Whistler in 1879 after his bankruptcy. The doorway is that of Palazzo Gussoni on the Rio de la Fava; this impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: The Gold Scab - Eruption in Frilthy Lucre
englishTitle: The Gold Scab: Eruption in Filthy Lucre (The Creditor)
description: Whistler's savage caricature of his former patron Frederick Leyland, painted in 1879 after the Peacock Room dispute and Whistler's bankruptcy, in which Leyland was a creditor. Leyland appears as a scaly, peacock-feathered demon seated on Whistler's White House while playing the piano — a jab at his amateur musicianship — with sacks of money at his feet. The painting is now in the de Young Museum, San Francisco.

title: The Millinery Shop
description: A woman in a green dress leans over a counter to inspect a wide-brimmed hat perched on its stand, while other trimmed hats crowd the foreground on their stands. Degas reworked the canvas between 1879 and 1886, leaving the figure's status — customer or shopworker — deliberately ambiguous. The painting entered the Art Institute of Chicago in 1933.

title: The Road to Vétheuil
description: A pale road curves along an open hillside toward the village of Vétheuil, visible in the middle distance beneath a high ridge, painted in 1879. The brushwork is dry and broken, warm ochres and mauves marking the early leafless trees on the left and the village beyond. Now in The Phillips Collection, Washington, the picture was made shortly after Monet settled at Vétheuil during a period of personal and financial difficulty.

title: Van gogh f1040 jh100
description: A wide industrial landscape spreads across the sheet: factory buildings, tall chimneys trailing smoke, and a lone standing figure in the foreground fill a broad, flat terrain. Made on 4 July 1879, the drawing dates to Van Gogh's time in the Borinage mining region of Belgium and reflects his early, self-taught approach to depicting the working-class environment around him.

title: Vase of Flowers
description: An early still life painted while Seurat was still absorbing Barbizon and Impressionist precedents. The dense impasto and earthy palette show him before the systematic divisionism of dots that would define his mature work later in the decade.
credit: Fogg Museum

title: Vétheuil
description: The village of Vétheuil rises in tiers from the Seine to its tall Gothic church tower, which stands prominent against a pink-and-blue summer sky. The water below dissolves the buildings into shimmering reflections of golden and blue-grey. Monet painted numerous variants of this view during his years at Vétheuil; this 1879 canvas is held at the National Gallery of Victoria, Melbourne.

title: Woman in Street Clothes
description: A woman in a long coat and dark hat is shown from a three-quarter rear angle, her face visible in profile against an open ground. Degas made this 1879 pastel study of a modern Parisienne in street dress, using spare contour lines and restrained colour to evoke the character of anonymous urban life rather than the formality of a commissioned portrait.

title: Woman with a Pearl Necklace in a Loge
description: A young woman in a pale pink evening dress occupies a theatre loge, a pearl necklace at her throat and a fan in her gloved hands. The warm interior of the opera house stretches behind her, with other boxes and their occupants visible in the distance. Painted in 1879, the work is held by the Philadelphia Museum of Art and belongs to Cassatt's series depicting fashionable Parisian leisure.

title: Преферанс
description: A genre painting depicting a gathering of Russian men engaged in a card game of preferans (preference). Viktor Vasnetsov captures an intimate moment of 19th-century Russian domestic life, with figures absorbed in their game in an interior setting. The work exemplifies the artist's attention to social interaction and period detail.

title: 100 Aspects of the Moon - 67
description: A courtier in flowing light blue robes draws a yumi bow at a sika deer beneath a full moon and autumn cherry tree, fallen maple leaves scattered across the ground. From Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, this print illustrates the incident in which Minamoto no Tsunemoto killed a deer in the imperial palace grounds in the autumn of 932.
credit: British Museum [1]

title: A Box at the Theater
description: Two women in a theatre box, one in black lace resting her arm on the red velvet rail, the younger in white holding pink roses. Renoir reworked an earlier portrait into this image of spectators in 1880, oil on canvas, now in the Clark Art Institute, Williamstown.

title: After Igor Svyatoslavich 's fighting with the Cumans
description: The slain warriors of Prince Igor Svyatoslavich lie scattered across the southern steppe among wildflowers and broken armour, while an eagle descends and a pale moon rises at the horizon. Vasnetsov drew the subject from the medieval Tale of Igor's Campaign and signed the canvas in 1882, building each figure from ethnographic studies into a meditation on the cost of defeat.

title: Autumn Landscape
description: A hunter and his dog move along a path through bare late-autumn woodland, the pale sky pressing low over the tangle of brown branches. Levitan painted this Autumn Landscape in 1880, early in his career, already loading the season with the quiet atmospheric weight that would define his later work.

title: Balcony
description: Two men look down from the balcony of the artist's apartment at 31 Boulevard Haussmann — one in a top hat leaning on the railing, the other in a bowler hat standing at ease. The plunging view of a tree-lined Parisian boulevard and the modern bourgeois subject are characteristic of Caillebotte's engagement with Haussmann's reshaped city. The canvas, dated 1880, is now in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.

title: Bouquet of Mallows
description: Pink and lilac mallows fill a dark vase set on a pale surface, recorded in the rapid, comma-like brushwork Monet developed during his Vétheuil years around 1880. The loose, broken surface anticipates the enveloping all-over touch of his later garden paintings.

title: By the Water or Near the Lake
description: Two figures sit close to the bank of a river or lake, framed by overhanging foliage and dappled sunlight; a man in a straw hat faces left while a woman in lighter dress leans toward the water at right. Renoir painted this open-air scene around 1880, dissolving the surrounding vegetation into iridescent strokes of green, yellow, and violet in keeping with his Impressionist practice of that period.
credit: plain photo

title: Clear Sailing
description: Two figures stand on a rocky bank in the right foreground, watching several sailboats glide across calm, reflective water under a light sky. Homer summarises the scene with characteristic economy of wash, leaving the white paper to carry the sails' brightness. The watercolour, dated 1880, is held at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
credit: Philadelphia Museum of Art, online collection

title: Five O'Clock Tea
description: Two women take afternoon tea, the visitor at right lifting her cup to her face while the hostess at left sits composed before a gleaming silver tea service. Cassatt painted the work in 1880, treating a bourgeois social ritual with an Impressionist looseness of touch and close attention to the decorative still-life passages in the foreground. The canvas is in the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Flying Carpet
description: Ivan Tsarevich, the hero of Russian folklore, stands upright on a large ornate flying carpet high above a misty river landscape at dusk, a gilded cage bearing the Firebird at his side and a crescent moon on the horizon. Painted in 1880, the work is one of Vasnetsov's earliest explorations of the fairy-tale subjects that would come to define his mature career. The source describes it as a depiction of Ivan Tsarevich, the archetypal princely hero of Russian folk tradition.
credit: belygorod.ru

title: Francis Brooks Chadwick
description: A loose bust-length oil sketch of the painter Francis Brooks Chadwick on a small panel measuring 13.75 by 10 inches. Sargent painted his friend in 1880, inscribing the location and date directly on the canvas. The work is held in a private collection.

title: Jerusalem Artichoke Flowers
description: A large bouquet of yellow Jerusalem artichoke flowers fills a ceramic vase set on a round table, the blooms worked in feathery, broken touches of yellow and green against a flickering pink-grey ground. Monet signed and dated the canvas 1880; it is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington (inv. 1963.10.181).
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Kittens
description: A reclining woman in pale drapery plays with a litter of kittens, her arm stretched along a couch. Leighton's canvas measures roughly 119 by 79 cm and treats a domestic subject far removed from the classical and mythological scenes for which he was known.

title: L'homme au balcon
description: A top-hatted figure stands on a wrought-iron balcony overlooking one of Haussmann's new Paris boulevards, his back to the viewer as he surveys the street below. Caillebotte painted the canvas in 1880, repeatedly using the high vantage point of the Parisian balcony to explore the detached gaze of the modern urban observer. The bold compositional cut, with the figure isolated against the receding avenue, is characteristic of his Impressionist manner.
credit: Christie's

title: Le déjeuner des canotiers
description: Renoir's friends gather on the terrace of the Maison Fournaise at Chatou, lingering over wine and fruit after a row on the Seine. The composition weaves portraiture, still life, and shimmering river light into one celebrated image of modern leisure.

title: Lille PdBA monet la debacle
englishTitle: Debacle at Vétheuil, View of Lavacourt
description: Painted after the spectacular Seine ice break-up of January 1880, the canvas shows broken floes drifting past the bare poplars at Vétheuil. The subject — provoked by a thaw following one of the century's harshest winters — gave Monet a chance to study fragmented reflections and pearl-grey winter light.

title: Madame Ramón Subercaseaux
description: Amalia Subercaseaux, wife of the Chilean diplomat Ramón Subercaseaux, is shown seated at a piano in a light interior, wearing a black-and-white dress with red floral accents. The composition belongs to Sargent's early Parisian period and was shown at the 1881 Salon, demonstrating his bravura handling of costume and interior atmosphere.

title: Mary Cassatt Self-Portrait
description: Cassatt depicts herself in a large hat and dark dress, her gaze directed downward as she works at a canvas just visible at the right edge. The loosely worked gouache and watercolour over graphite, made around 1880, is a rapid, intimate record of the artist at work rather than a formal posed likeness. The self-portrait belongs to the National Portrait Gallery in Washington.

title: Monet w601
englishTitle: The Small Arm of the Seine at Vétheuil
description: The quiet side channel of the Seine at Vétheuil, painted in 1880 as Monet worked obsessively along the river's bends around the village. Private collection (68.5 × 90 cm).

title: Pierre-Cécile Puvis de Chavannes 003
englishTitle: Portrait of Pierre Puvis de Chavannes
description: A sleeping youth reclines beneath a pine tree at night, while three luminous allegorical female figures drift through the moonlit air above him, one reaching down with flowers or a garland. The muted, fresco-like tonalities and symbolic register are characteristic of Pierre Puvis de Chavannes, the leading French Symbolist painter of the nineteenth century. The work is known as Le Rêve (The Dream).

title: Poppy Field
description: A field of red poppies set against summer greens, the kind of motif Monet revisited near Vetheuil and Giverny. Dabs of vermilion are scattered with calligraphic ease across a haze of grass, demonstrating his interest in saturated complementary colour.

title: Portrait of Mademoiselle Irène Cahen d'Anvers
description: Irène Cahen d'Anvers, daughter of a prominent Parisian banking family, is shown in three-quarter profile with long copper hair falling loosely to her waist and a blue ribbon at the back of her head. Renoir set her against a dark background of foliage and painted her in a pale blue-white dress, achieving the quiet reverie that characterises his best child portraits. The work dates to 1880 and was held in the Sammlung E.G. Bührle.
credit: Sammlung E.G. Bührle

title: Religious Procession in Kursk Province
description: A vast religious procession winds across a sunburnt steppe, sweeping clergy, peasants, gendarmes, and crippled pilgrims into a single dust-clouded cross-section of imperial Russian society. Repin's panoramic canvas is a touchstone of Peredvizhniki social realism.
credit: Tretyakov Gallery

title: Reply of the Zaporozhian Cossacks
englishTitle: The Reply of the Zaporozhian Cossacks to Sultan of Turkey (Sketch)
description: A preparatory oil sketch for Repin's celebrated history painting, showing Cossacks erupting in raucous laughter as they dictate an obscene reply to the Ottoman sultan. The looser handling here preserves the immediacy and unbridled humour that the finished canvas would carry forward.

title: Selbstporträt vor olivfarbener Tapete
description: A bearded self-portrait set against a dull olive-green wallpaper whose pattern Cézanne echoes in the modelling of the head. Painted in Paris around 1880 to 1881, oil on canvas, now in the National Gallery, London. The dome of the skull is built from short oblique patches of white, red and ochre, the ear and crown outlined in blue.

title: Self-portrait
description: Leighton shown bearded in the red robe and President's chain of the Royal Academy, a fragment of the Parthenon frieze behind him. Oil on canvas painted in 1880 by invitation for the Uffizi collection of artists' self-portraits in Florence, where it remains.

title: Small Lake with Boat
description: An early oil sketch on cardboard from Munch's teenage years, depicting a still pond with a moored rowboat. The plein-air naturalism, painted before his Symbolist breakthrough, shows him absorbing Norwegian landscape conventions in compact, atmospheric form.
credit: ART & ARTISTS blog pic

title: Study of a Nude
description: An academic life study from Gauguin's early years, predating the Tahitian primitivism for which he is now remembered. The figure is modelled with conventional tonal shading, evidence of the studio training he would soon discard for synthetism.

title: The Embroiderer
description: Gauguin's wife Mette Sophie sits at a small table bent over her sewing, the dense brushwork drawn from Camille Pissarro's example. The 116 by 81 cm canvas, painted in 1880 while Gauguin was still a successful stockbroker, hangs at the Foundation E. G. Bührle in Zurich and is catalogued as Wildenstein 65.
credit: Foundation E.G. Bührle Collection Zurich

title: The Seine at Lavacourt
description: A panoramic view of the Seine at Lavacourt, opposite his Vétheuil home, submitted to the 1880 Salon as a calculated bid for official recognition. The handling is unusually controlled, the river a broad mirror of pearly cloud.
credit: Dallas Museum of Arts

title: The Wailing Wall
description: A lone figure in a green coat and tall hat stands in prayer before the vast Herodian ashlar courses of the Western Wall in Jerusalem, prayer book in hand. Painted in 1880 and now held by the Israel Museum, the composition is characteristic of Gérôme's Orientalist precision: a single human presence dwarfed by the ancient stonework, rendered with his polished academic finish.

title: Two Boys Watching Schooners
description: Two boys sit side by side on low rocks at the water's edge, watching a fleet of schooners at anchor across a calm bay under an overcast sky. The watercolour pares the scene to stone, water, sail, and muted sky, characteristic of Homer's coastal subjects. Painted in 1880, the work is held at the Art Institute of Chicago.
credit: Art Institute of Chicago : online database: entry 16803

title: Venetian Onion Seller
description: A young Venetian girl holds a long string of white onions, her dark shawl framing a white dress, while a view of the lagoon and a campanile opens through a window behind her. The canvas belongs to Sargent's early Venetian campaigns of 1880–82, when he sought out working-class subjects in the city's quieter quarters. Now in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.
credit: Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid

title: Vétheuil
description: A field of red poppies and summer grasses occupies the foreground, with tall poplars and cypresses framing the distant village of Vétheuil on the hillside. The Seine is glimpsed at the far right edge. Monet painted this sunlit meadow view in 1880, during his years living at Vétheuil; the canvas is in the Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow.

title: View of Vétheuil
description: A path bordered by red poppies and wildflowers leads through a summer meadow, with tall poplars rising to the right and the church and rooftops of Vétheuil visible in the middle distance. Monet painted this open-air view in 1880 during his years living at Vétheuil; the canvas is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: A forgotten soldier
description: A monumental anti-war canvas by the Russian battle painter Vereshchagin, showing a fallen soldier abandoned on the battlefield as carrion birds gather. The work is part of the artist's unflinching cycle exposing the human cost of imperial conflict.
credit: kunstkopie; Bridgeman Art Library : Object 266195; artpoisk.info; vereschagin.com.ua

provenance.collection: V. V. Vereshchagin Mykolaiv Art Museum
provenance.location: V. V. Vereshchagin Mykolaiv Art Museum

title: After the attack. Plevna
description: Vereshchagin painted the carnage of the Russo-Turkish siege of Plevna from first-hand experience as a war correspondent attached to the Russian army. The unsentimental documentary realism he made his trademark exposes the human cost behind official communiqués of imperial conquest.
credit: slavs.org.ua

title: Alenushka
description: A barefoot peasant girl sits hunched on a stone at the edge of a dark forest pond, her chin resting on her knees and her auburn hair loose around her. Vasnetsov drew on the fairy tale of Sister Alyonushka and Brother Ivanushka, using a local girl as model to convey the suffering of a solitary, grief-stricken orphan. Painted at Abramtsevo in 1881, the canvas is held in the Tretyakov Gallery and is widely regarded as one of the defining images of Russian Romantic painting.
credit: Tretyakov Gallery

title: Alice Hoschedé au jardin
description: Alice Hoschedé sits among flowering plants and foliage in a garden, her light-coloured dress treated as one luminous accent within the surrounding greenery. Dahlias and other blooms are visible against a balustrade in the background. Monet painted this intimate garden figure at Vétheuil in 1881, during the period when Alice was living with his household.
credit: www.sothebys.com

title: Bei Fécamp
description: A view near Fécamp on the Normandy coast, painted in 1881, looking out over a broad expanse of sea from the top of the chalk cliffs. The palette is warmer than the Channel's typical grey, the water suffused with golden-yellow light beneath a hazy sky. Short, energetic brushstrokes articulate the cliff edge in the foreground and the open water beyond.

title: Boat Lying at Low Tide
description: A large sailing vessel lists on the tidal flats, its dark hull and tall masts rising against a blue sky of billowing clouds, while figures move across the foreground sand and a harbour town stretches behind. The work of 1881 reflects Monet's sustained interest in the Norman coast and its working maritime traffic.

title: Bouquet of Sunflowers
description: A dense bouquet of sunflowers arranged in a glazed vase, painted in Vétheuil years before Van Gogh took up the same motif in Arles. Monet builds the heavy heads from short, comma-like strokes of chrome yellow and ochre, contrasting their warmth against a cool blue-grey ground.

title: Champ de coquelicots
description: A sunlit meadow of red poppies, painted in 1881 and now in Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, Rotterdam. A single tall tree punctuates the flat plain, and a broad sky of pale grey-white occupies much of the canvas above a low horizon. The open, airy composition and loose broken touch are characteristic of Monet's rural landscapes of the early 1880s.

title: Dr. Pozzi at Home
description: The celebrated Parisian gynecologist Samuel Pozzi stands full length in a flame-red dressing gown, fingers tugging at his collar and sash. Sargent's bravura essay in monochrome scarlet was painted in the sitter's own apartment and announced the young American's arrival in Parisian society.
credit: https://hammer.ucla.edu/collections/armand-hammer-collection/ image

title: Frederic Leighton
description: Frederic Leighton seated in his Academician's gown, left elbow hooked over the chair back, hands loosely clasped. Watts painted this oil from sittings in 1881, the year Leighton sat for the work now in the National Portrait Gallery, London (NPG 1049). It is one of three portraits Watts made of his friend across their long acquaintance.

title: Gérôme - Cave Canem
description: A near-nude crouching male figure huddles in a doorway beneath a stone tablet inscribed CAVE CANEM, a chain lying on the ground beside him. Gérôme sets the scene in a sun-drenched Roman streetscape with tightly rendered architectural detail. Completed in 1881, the work is held in the musée Jean-Léon Gérôme in Vesoul.

title: Heroes
description: The three bogatyrs Dobrynya Nikitich, Ilya Muromets and Alyosha Popovich sit mounted at the edge of the steppe, scanning the horizon for enemies. Vasnetsov worked on the nearly 3 by 4 metre canvas for almost twenty years, finishing it in 1898 in the rebuilt barn-studio Savva Mamontov had given him at Abramtsevo; Pavel Tretyakov bought it for his gallery as soon as it was done.

title: John Newman
description: Cardinal Newman, the theologian who led the Oxford Movement and later converted to Roman Catholicism, is shown in old age dressed in full cardinal robes — scarlet mozzetta, red zucchetto and a gold pectoral chain. Millais applies the assured, broadly brushed technique of his late portraiture to capture the aged cardinal's composed authority. Painted in 1881, the year after Newman received the cardinalate from Leo XIII, the portrait is held at the National Portrait Gallery, London.

title: La Seine à Vétheuil
description: A bend of the Seine at Vétheuil, the village where Monet lived through the bleakest years of his middle career. The river, opposite bank and sky are resolved into three horizontal bands of broken colour, a structural simplicity that points toward his coming serial work.
credit: Minnesota Marine Art Museum

title: Le havre muma monet fecamp
description: A coastal view of Fécamp on the Normandy chalk cliffs, painted during a productive Channel-side campaign in the early 1880s. Monet works the cliff face and sea in parallel ribbons of pigment, registering the cool grey-green light of the Pays de Caux.

provenance.collection: MuMa Museum of modern art André Malraux
provenance.location: MuMa Museum of modern art André Malraux

title: Leighton Moses views the Promised Land
description: Moses views the Promised Land, by Lord Frederic Leighton , wood-engraving from Illustrations for “Dalziels' Bible Gallery” , engraved by the Dalziel Brothers and published 1881

title: Lydia at the Tapestry Loom
description: Lydia Cassatt, the artist's elder sister and frequent model, leans forward absorbed in her work at a tapestry loom, painted in soft indoor light. The picture belongs to Cassatt's series of women engaged in domestic occupations, executed around 1881 with the loose, colour-saturated brushwork she developed in the circle of Degas.

title: Monet w649
description: The sea below the chalk cliffs at Fécamp in calm weather, painted during Monet's spring 1881 campaign on the Normandy coast — his first sustained cliff series. Private collection (60 × 81 cm).

title: Monet w653
description: The chalk cliff at Grainval, just south-west of Fécamp on the Normandy coast, painted in 1881 during Monet's spring campaign there. Private collection (61 × 80 cm).

title: Monet w658
description: The shingle beach at Fécamp beneath the cliffs, painted in 1881 on Monet's spring campaign along the Normandy coast. Private collection (46 × 80 cm).

title: Monet w662
description: A pure study of open sea and sky, painted in 1881 during Monet's campaign on the Normandy coast around Fécamp. With no shore or figure to anchor it, the canvas is carried entirely by the movement of water and weather. Private collection (50 × 73 cm).

title: Monet w664
description: The cliffs at Les Petites-Dalles, a small bathing village up the coast from Fécamp where Monet's brother Léon kept a holiday house, painted in 1881. It belongs to the first of the Normandy cliff campaigns that occupied Monet through the early 1880s. Private collection (60 × 74 cm).

title: Monet w668
description: A view of the Seine at Vétheuil under a setting sun, painted in 1881 during Monet's final months living in the village. Commons categorizes it among his sunset paintings of the Seine at Vétheuil. The work remains in a private collection.

title: Monet w679
description: Painted in 1881 on the Île de Saint-Martin-la-Garenne, an island in the Seine near Vétheuil where Monet often worked. Formerly in the Paul G. Allen collection, it now belongs to the Hasso Plattner Collection shown at the Museum Barberini in Potsdam.

title: Monet w683
description: One of the 1881 canvases of the sunflower-lined steps in Monet's garden at Vétheuil, painted just before he left the village for Poissy. This version hangs in the Norton Simon Museum in Pasadena; a larger variant of the same composition is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Monet w684
description: Another of the 1881 views of Monet's garden at Vétheuil, looking up the central path past tall sunflowers toward the house. It belongs to the same series as the versions in the National Gallery of Art and the Norton Simon Museum, but this canvas has remained in private hands.

title: Monet w691
description: A 1881 view of the gate into Monet's garden at Vétheuil, one of the garden subjects he painted in his last year living there. The painting is in a private collection.

title: Monet w694
description: A tall, narrow still life of gladioli in a vase, painted in 1881 — a rare flower-piece format for Monet at roughly 99 by 41 centimeters. The painting is held by the Pola Museum of Art in Hakone, Japan.

title: Morning of Execution of Streltsy
description: Condemned streltsy in white death shirts hold lit candles in carts before the Kremlin wall, watched by their wailing families and by Peter the Great mounted at the right, as the gallows wait at Lobnoye Mesto. Surikov set his 1881 canvas on Red Square in the autumn of 1698, after the second streltsy revolt; Tretyakov bought it from the ninth Peredvizhniki exhibition almost as soon as it opened.
credit: lj.rossia.org (Currently unavailable)

title: Mr. Carlyle delivering the address on his installation as Lord Rector of Edinburgh University
englishTitle: Thomas Carlyle Delivering His Address as Lord Rector of Edinburgh University
description: A wood-engraved illustration documenting Thomas Carlyle's rectorial address at Edinburgh, reproduced for a mass readership in the Illustrated London News. Such press engravings were the period's chief vehicle for circulating images of public events before photographic reproduction took over.

title: Nocturne in Rosa und Grau
description: A full-length portrait of a woman in an elaborate pink and grey gown and feathered hat, set against a muted grey-brown ground. Whistler's musical titles — here Nocturne in Rosa und Grau — subordinate the sitter to an overall harmony of tones, consistent with his Aestheticist programme. The work, dated 1881, is held by the Frick Collection, New York.
credit: http://collections.frick.org/Obj1025$18936 2

title: On the Terrasse
description: On a Chatou terrace above the Seine, a young woman in a plain red hat stands beside a younger girl whose blue hat is trimmed with flowers, a basket of yarn resting between them against a backdrop of broken foliage and river. Renoir painted the picture in 1881, and it is one of his most celebrated figure compositions of that year.

title: Temps calme
description: A view along the Normandy coast from the clifftops near Pourville, painted in 1881 and now in the Staechelin collection at Kunstmuseum Basel. The reddish-brown cliffs fall away to the left while the Channel stretches to the horizon under a pale, overcast sky. The quiet stillness implied by the French title 'Temps calme' (calm weather) is captured in the subdued, close-valued palette of greens, blues and greys.
credit: Artbook: Rudolf Staechelin’sche Familienstiftung Basel (Hrsg.): Nafea, die Sammlung Rudolf Staechelin, Basel .

title: The Burning of the Turkish Flagship by Kanáris
description: Aivazovsky depicts the Greek fireship attack led by Konstantinos Kanaris against an Ottoman flagship, its hull erupting in a column of fire and sparks while observers row clear in the foreground and steep cliffs rise in the background. The night sky and churning water reflect the blaze in the painter's characteristic dramatic marine style. Painted in 1881, the canvas is in the National Gallery of Athens.
credit: National Gallery (Athens)

title: The Hut in Trouville
description: A tarred fisherman's hut stands above the bared sands of the Normandy coast, painted on a windy summer return to Trouville. Quick, scrubbed strokes record the silvered tideline and the lift of grasses on the dune, hallmarks of Monet's plein-air practice.
credit: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza: Website , Info , Pic

title: The Piazza San Marco
description: Renoir's view of Venice's central square dissolves the basilica's Byzantine facade into shimmering touches of pink, gold, and blue. Painted during his Italian journey, the canvas treats architecture as an Impressionist screen of light, with figures and pigeons scattered across the sunlit pavement.

title: The poor fisherman
description: A gaunt fisher stands in his moored skiff while a woman gathers flowers and an infant sleeps on the bank, the scene reduced to chalky, almost frescoed planes of pale color. The austere composition and melancholic mood made the picture a touchstone for Symbolist painters and the young Picasso.

title: The Sea in Fécamp
description: Painted from the base of the chalk cliffs at Fécamp, the canvas sets a wall of rock against open green sea, with surf bursting against the rocks where the two meet. There is no horizon incident and no figure — just water, stone, and weather, worked in the agitated, comma-like strokes of Monet's 1881 campaign on the Normandy coast. The painting is signed and dated at lower right.

title: The Umbrellas
description: A crowd under a canopy of umbrellas, a bare-headed milliner's assistant with her hatbox at the left edge. Renoir worked the canvas in two campaigns, the feathery right-hand figures about 1881 and the firmer left-hand pair around 1885, switching from cobalt to French ultramarine between them. Oil on canvas, National Gallery, London.
credit: National Gallery, London

title: Un Bar aux Folies-Bergère by Édouard Manet
description: Manet's final major work, painted in 1881–1882, depicts a barmaid at the famous Folies-Bergère cabaret in Paris. The composition masterfully captures the ambiguity of modern urban life through the barmaid's reflected image and the bustling entertainment venue behind her. This oil painting is housed in the Courtauld Gallery in London and remains a pivotal work of Impressionism.

title: Viktor Vasnetsov. Battle between the Scythians and the Slavs
description: Mounted warriors locked in combat, lances raised and horses entangled across the steppe. Vasnetsov painted this Battle of the Slavs and Scythians in 1881, oil on canvas, now in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg. The subject draws on the Primary Chronicle and the artist's interest in early Russian legend.

title: Wheatfield
description: A summer wheatfield treated as an almost abstract field of warm strokes under a high sky. The subject anticipates the haystacks Monet would begin painting in series a decade later, where the same agrarian motif became a vehicle for studying changing light.
credit: The AMICA Library; thiele-und-thiele-consult

title: Перед атакой. Под Плевной
description: A dramatic military history painting by Vasily Vereshchagin depicting Russian soldiers preparing for battle during the Siege of Plevna (1877), a pivotal engagement of the Russo-Turkish War. The work is part of Vereshchagin's celebrated Balkan series documenting contemporary warfare with unflinching realism. Oil on canvas, held in the Tretyakov Gallery collection.

title: Abelard and his Pupil Heloise
description: The philosopher Abelard instructs his young pupil Heloise in an open medieval colonnade, both figures absorbed in the illuminated book resting on her lap. Edmund Blair Leighton painted this chivalric-romantic subject in 1882, rendering the costumes and stone architecture with the fastidious detail that characterised his Academy submissions.

title: Arnaut Blowing Smoke at the Nose of His Dog
description: An Arnaut warrior — Albanian soldiers who served in the Ottoman Egyptian army — reclines on cushions in a richly tiled interior and exhales pipe smoke toward the muzzle of a greyhound lying at his feet. The sourceDescription identifies the figure as fighting under Muhamed Ali, founder of modern Egypt. Gérôme, working in 1882 and employing his characteristic smooth enamel finish, treats the idle soldier with the zoological exactitude typical of his Orientalist studies.
credit: mechanical reproduction of 2D image

title: Before the Race
description: Several jockeys on thoroughbreds mill in loose formation across open ground, their mounts shown in varying gaits. Degas painted the small panel between 1882 and 1884, a period in which he drew on recently published stop-action photographs to sharpen his understanding of the horse in motion. The work is held by the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Charlotte Dubourg par Fantin-Latour
description: Charlotte Dubourg, Fantin-Latour's sister-in-law, sits in a pale blue dress on a red upholstered chair, holding a small fan or card, her gaze directed at the viewer. The portrait was painted in 1882 and is held at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris, where it exemplifies the quiet psychological intensity that characterises Fantin-Latour's figure work.

title: Cliff Walk at Pourville
description: Two women stand on a cliff top above the English Channel at Pourville, one holding a red parasol, with sailing boats visible on the sea below. Painted during Monet's working stay on the Normandy coast in 1882, the canvas uses the figures as a compositional anchor against the broad open sky. It is now in the Art Institute of Chicago.

title: Cliffs at Pourville
description: Two women sit at the edge of a grassy clifftop at Pourville, looking out over the Channel where numerous sailing vessels are scattered across a pale, mist-softened sea. Monet painted this view during his 1882 stay along the Norman coast between Dieppe and Varengeville, capturing the broad expanse of water under a clouded sky with the cliff and turf in rapid strokes of green and ochre. The canvas is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Cliffs near Dieppe
description: A chalk cliff dominates the right of the canvas, its fissured face falling to a broad, pebbly foreshore under an overcast sky, while a calm strip of sea stretches to the horizon on the left. Monet worked along the Norman coast in 1882, applying short, dragged strokes to capture the textured stone and pale atmospheric light; the painting is in the Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburgh.

title: Cliffs near Pourville
description: A massive cliff face of warm ochre and rose-tinted rock fills most of the canvas, a strip of sandy beach and turquoise sea opening at its foot under a clear blue sky. Monet paints the cliff's surface in dense, broken strokes that animate the stone with light and colour. Painted in 1882, the work is held at the Rijksmuseum Twenthe, Enschede.
credit: Rijksmuseum Twenthe https://www.rijksmuseumtwenthe.nl/content/355 Previously: Cloude Monet, Falaises près de Pourville (1882) , adagio808 from Enschede, The Netherlands, 2009-06-25 15:23

title: Église de Varengeville
description: The small church of Varengeville perches dramatically atop sheer chalk cliffs above the sea, painted in clear morning light. Monet returned to this cliff-top motif repeatedly during his 1882 stay on the Normandy coast, treating the chapel's silhouette as a study in shifting maritime light at different hours. The work is dated 1882.
credit: twitter [1]

title: El Jaleo
description: A near life-size scene of a flamenco dancer mid-stride before a row of seated musicians, lit by raking footlights that cast huge shadows on the back wall. Sargent worked the picture up from sketches made in Spain, marrying Velázquez's tonal economy to a thoroughly modern sense of theatrical staging.

title: Eugen von Blaas Bildnis Arthur Graf Berchtold 1882
description: Arthur Graf Berchtold (1843–1929), hereditary member of the Hungarian Upper House and deputy to the Hungarian Reichstag, is portrayed in a half-length format wearing a dark fur-trimmed ceremonial coat with elaborately jewelled clasps. The dark ground and three-quarter gaze lend the portrait the gravity expected of official commissions. De Blaas signed and dated the canvas 1882.

title: Fisherman's Cottage on the Cliffs at Varengeville
description: A small stone cottage, built as a customs watchman's hut, nestles into flowering scrub at the edge of the cliffs at Varengeville, the sea below dotted with sailboats. Monet painted the motif repeatedly during his 1882 campaign on the Normandy coast, drawn to the steep drop between foreground and water. This version is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Fishermen on the Seine at Poissy
description: Several figures sit and stand in small rowing boats on a calm stretch of the Seine at Poissy, their reflections diffused in the warm green water below. Monet settled briefly at Poissy in 1881–82 before moving to Giverny, and this canvas — now in the Belvedere, Vienna — is among the river scenes he produced there.

title: Flowers in a Crystal Vase
description: A late still life painted in Manet's final months, when illness confined him to small flower pieces brought by visitors. Carnations and clematis are set in a faceted crystal vase, the brushwork economical yet luminous against a darkened ground.

title: Foggy Morning at Pourville
description: Mist swallows the Norman cliffs above Pourville, where Monet spent the summer of 1882 pursuing the dissolving effects of marine atmosphere. Pale lavenders and silvered greens are knit together in short, parallel strokes, leaving the horizon as little more than a suggestion.

title: Girl Carrying a Basket
description: A young woman trudges along a windswept English coast with her basket, painted during Homer's stay at the fishing village of Cullercoats. The Northumbrian sojourn shifted his palette toward greyed blues and ochres and gave his figures the weathered seriousness that marks his late marines.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington DC

title: Jean-Léon Gerôme
description: A solitary pasha in red and gold robes sits beside the body of his dead tiger, laid out on a blue carpet and strewn with flowers, two tall green candles burning at its head in the columned courtyard of a Moorish palace. The single figure's quiet grief and the ceremonial candlelight lend the scene the weight of an elegy. Gérôme's 1882 oil, held in the Joslyn Art Museum, Omaha, exemplifies his miniaturist precision in the rendering of tilework, carved stone, and animal anatomy.

title: joseph-durand-ruel-1882.jpg!PinterestLarge
description: Joseph Durand-Ruel, eldest son of Renoir's dealer Paul Durand-Ruel, shown as a young man against a leafy ground. Oil on canvas painted in 1882, the year Renoir also portrayed Joseph's younger brothers Charles and Georges. Joseph (1862 to 1928) went on to run the family gallery.

title: June
description: A sunlit summer landscape opens across a broad meadow, a shallow stream catching the light in the foreground and tall trees casting deep shadow across the grass. Inness signed and dated the canvas 1882, and it entered the collection of the Brooklyn Museum. The freely handled atmosphere and Barbizon-inflected tonality are characteristic of his mature American manner.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum

title: Knight at the Crossroads
description: A bogatyr in heavy armour sits on a white horse before a standing stone inscribed in Cyrillic on a darkening steppe, ravens circling above scattered bones and skulls at the stone's base. The inscription warns that the way ahead leads to death, a warning drawn from Russian epic tradition. Vasnetsov completed this composition in 1882; the painting is now in the State Russian Museum.

title: La maison du pêcheur
description: A modest fisherman's cottage perched above the Norman coast, painted during Monet's productive campaigns at Pourville and Varengeville. Broken brushwork dissolves cliff, sea, and sky into a single weathered atmosphere, the cottage anchoring the composition against the windblown grass.

title: Lady with the Rose
description: Charlotte Louise Burckhardt stands full-length in a black dress against a neutral grey ground, holding a single white rose. Sargent painted this portrait in 1882, drawing on the tonal restraint of Velázquez — as urged by his teacher Carolus-Duran — to achieve a commanding silhouette and psychological directness; the work was shown at the Salon of 1882 and is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: Low Tide at Pourville
description: Exposed sand flats stretch beneath the chalk cliffs of the Normandy fishing village, painted on one of Monet's productive 1882 campaigns along the coast. Quick, broken brushwork captures the shifting light and damp air, and X-rays reveal an earlier composition lying beneath the beach.
credit: https://clevelandart.org/art/1947.196 IA

title: Monet w 763 the path
description: A sunken lane cut between steep banks of chalk and scrub vegetation, opening at its far end to a glimpse of sea and sky. Painted in 1882 along the Norman coast, the composition channels the viewer into a corridor of dappled sunlight rendered in closely worked greens and warm ochres — one of Monet's many studies of the region's distinctive hollow paths.

title: Monet w706
description: An evening view of the harbor at Dieppe, painted in 1882 when Monet first arrived on the Normandy coast for his Pourville campaign. The painting belongs to the Dixon Gallery and Gardens in Memphis, Tennessee.

title: Monet w717
description: A coastal landscape painted at Pourville, the fishing village just west of Dieppe where Monet spent much of 1882. The painting is in a private collection.

title: Monet w724
englishTitle: The Effect of Fog near Dieppe
description: A seascape painted near Dieppe in 1882, studying how fog dissolves the Normandy coastline — an early instance of the atmospheric 'effects' that would define his later series. The painting is in a private collection.

title: Monet w736
description: The small customs officer's cottage perched above the sea at Varengeville, painted in morning light in 1882. Monet was drawn back to this lone cabin repeatedly, making it the subject of a full series in the 1890s. This canvas is in a private collection.

title: Monet w752
englishTitle: Edge of the Cliff at Pourville
description: A clifftop view at Pourville on the Normandy coast, painted during Monet's 1882 stay. The painting is now part of the Hasso Plattner Collection shown at the Museum Barberini in Potsdam.

title: Monet w753
englishTitle: Path in the Wheat at Pourville
description: A path cutting through ripening wheat on the clifftops above Pourville, painted in 1882. The painting belongs to the Denver Art Museum.

title: Monet w757
englishTitle: Edges of the Cliff at Pourville
description: One of Monet's 1882 clifftop views at Pourville (French title 'Bords de la falaise à Pourville'), looking along the chalk cliffs of the Normandy coast. The painting is now in the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart.

title: Monet w759
description: A view of the chalk cliffs at Dieppe painted in 1882 during Monet's Normandy coast campaign. The painting (French title 'La Falaise à Dieppe') is held by the Kunsthaus Zürich.

title: Monet w764
description: A 1882 view of Pourville-sur-Mer, the small resort village on the Normandy coast where Monet worked through much of that year. The painting is in a private collection.

title: Monet w767
englishTitle: The Rocks at Pourville, Low Tide
description: Wave-worn rocks exposed at low tide on the beach at Pourville, painted in 1882. The painting belongs to the Memorial Art Gallery in Rochester, New York.

title: Monet w772
description: An open seascape painted near Étretat on the Normandy coast in 1882, a few years before Monet's sustained campaigns around the famous cliffs there. The painting is in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

title: Monet w776
description: The beach at Pourville at low tide beneath the Normandy cliffs, painted in 1882 (French title 'Marée basse à Pourville'). The painting is in a private collection.

title: Monet w778a
description: A small 1882 canvas of the chalk cliffs at Pourville on the Normandy coast, from the year Monet painted the area intensively. The painting is in a private collection.

title: Monet w787
englishTitle: Seashore and Cliffs of Pourville in the Morning
description: The beach and cliffs at Pourville in morning light, painted in 1882. The painting (French title 'Bord de mer et falaises de Pourville le matin') is held by the Tokyo Fuji Art Museum.

title: Monet w807
description: The sweep of beach below the cliffs at Pourville, painted in 1882. It is the only Monet in a Polish public collection, held by the National Museum in Poznań; the canvas was stolen from the museum in 2000 and recovered a decade later.

title: Monet w922
description: A small, frieze-like still life of daffodils (French title 'Jonquilles'), only about 16 by 40 centimeters, dated between 1882 and 1885. The painting is in a private collection.

title: Portrait of Dora Wheeler
description: Dora Wheeler, a designer trained alongside Chase in Munich, sits in a blue gown amid the embroidered hangings of her mother Candace's Associated Artists studio. The portrait won a medal at the 1883 Paris Salon and helped establish Chase's reputation for atmospheric, aesthetic-movement interiors.

title: Portrait of Père Paul
description: A bearded man in a white chef's jacket and tall toque looks outward in this unusual portrait by Monet, painted during his Normandy campaign of 1882. The loose, confident brushwork captures the sitter's weathered features and strong profile against a plain ground. Known as Père Paul, the subject was a local cook; the work is now in the Belvedere, Vienna.

title: Porträt des Charles und Georges Durand-Ruel
description: Charles and Georges Durand-Ruel, sons of Renoir's dealer, shown outdoors in three-piece suits against dense green foliage. Oil on canvas painted in 1882; Paul Durand-Ruel, who commissioned the double portrait, was reportedly displeased to find his sons painted out of doors. Charles holds a medallion, Georges a cigarette.

title: Road at La Cavée
description: A sunken Norman lane cuts down toward the sea at Pourville, where Monet spent productive months in 1882. Banks of grass and gorse frame a small triangle of bright Channel water, a composition organised by the steep diagonal of the path.

title: Sarkizova Ann
description: Anna Nikitichna Burnazyan-Sarkisova, the painter's second wife, gazes out from a semi-transparent veil that softens the dark ground behind her. Aivazovsky married Anna in 1882, nearly forty years his junior; the portrait hangs in the Aivazovsky Art Gallery in Feodosia, a rare exercise in formal portraiture from a painter best known for storms at sea.

title: Studio Interior
description: William Merritt Chase (American, 1849-1916). Studio Interior, ca. 1882.
credit: Brooklyn Museum

title: The Church at Varengeville
description: The little Saint-Valéry church perches on its eroding clifftop at Varengeville-sur-Mer, painted from the gully below with the Channel framed beyond. Monet returned to the motif from several angles during his 1882 Pourville stay, treating the building as a fixed point against shifting weather.
credit: Art UK : entry claude-monet-1840-1926

title: The Church of Varengeville
description: The medieval clifftop church of Saint-Valery at Varengeville, silhouetted against the Channel sky. Monet returned to this motif repeatedly in 1882, treating it as a study in tonal envelope, here flushed with the warm rose and orange of evening.

title: The Daughters of Edward Darley Boit
description: Four sisters stand in the dim foyer of the Boit family's Paris apartment, the youngest seated on the rug, the eldest pair half-swallowed by shadow beside a pair of monumental Japanese vases. Sargent borrowed the deep recessive space and palette directly from Velazquez's Las Meninas, which he had copied in Madrid in 1879; the picture entered the MFA Boston in 1919.
credit: http://www.mfa.org/collections/object/the-daughters-of-edward-darley-boit-31782 This is a retouched picture , which means that it has been digitally altered from its original version. Modifications: As much of the unfree frame was removed as possible, lossless JPG crop . The original can be viewed here: John Singer Sargent 001.jpg : . Modifications made by Keraunoscopia .

title: The Gorge at Varengeville by Claude Monet
description: Monet depicts a rocky Normandy clifftop at Varengeville with a small stone cottage nestled among the scrubby vegetation, the open Channel stretching to the horizon beyond. Painted in 1882, the canvas translates the sunlit cliff vegetation into vibrating broken touches of green, lilac, and ochre, and is now on loan to the California Palace of the Legion of Honor in San Francisco.

title: Waiting
description: On a bench at the Paris Opera, a young dancer in a tutu bends to clasp her ankle beside a woman in black street clothes with a furled umbrella, presumably her mother or chaperone, who stares at the floor. Degas drew the pastel around 1882, setting the silent pair against steeply raked floorboards seen from above. Since 1983 the sheet has been owned jointly by the Norton Simon Art Foundation in Pasadena and the J. Paul Getty Museum.

title: White Lilacs in a Glass Vase
description: A bouquet of white lilacs leans from a clear glass vase against a darkened ground, the flowers worked in loaded, gestural strokes. The picture belongs to the small floral still lifes Manet painted at the very end of his life, when illness had reduced his ambitions to flowers brought by visitors.

title: 'The Saddle Bazaar
description: A white Arab horse fitted with an ornate embroidered saddle stands in a Cairo courtyard while a buyer in colourful Eastern dress haggles with an elderly merchant at a saddler's stall. Gérôme renders the horse and its richly decorated tack with meticulous academic precision, set against the shaded stone arcades he observed on his Egyptian travels. The work, dated 1883, is held at the Haggin Museum, Stockton, California.
credit: hagginmuseum.org

title: Agitated Sea at Etretat
description: Heavy surf crashes against the Normandy chalk cliff at Etretat, the famous arch of the Porte d'Aval framing a turbulent grey sea while fishing boats and figures occupy the rocky foreground. Painted in 1883 and held at the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon (B 647), it is among the coastal studies Monet made during his concentrated campaigns on the Normandy coast in the early 1880s.
credit: Consulter cette image photographiée par Gilles Alonso spécialiste de la photo en gigapixel en très haute définition (+1 milliard de pixels)

provenance.collection: Museum of Fine Arts of Lyon
provenance.location: Museum of Fine Arts of Lyon

title: At the beer garden
description: Two men occupy the foreground of this small, densely observed beer-garden scene, surrounded by a press of figures whose hats, glasses, and animated faces Menzel records with characteristic exactitude. Painted in 1883, the canvas exemplifies the sharp, sketchbook-trained eye Menzel trained on the social spectacle of modern German urban life.

title: Bemberg Fondation Toulouse - Bateaux sur la plage à Etretat - Claude Monet - 1883 65x81 Inv.2077
englishTitle: Boats on the Beach at Étretat
description: Monet paints fishing boats hauled up beneath the chalk cliffs of Étretat, a Norman coast he returned to repeatedly in the 1880s. The pale beach and overcast sea are built from short, broken strokes that record shifting weather rather than narrative incident. The canvas now resides at the Bemberg Foundation in Toulouse.

title: Chase mrs meigs piano organ 1883
description: Mrs. Meigs is seen from behind at her organ in a simply furnished, light-filled interior, her white dress luminous against the pale walls. Chase painted several such domestic interiors in the early 1880s, applying the assured tonal handling he had developed through study of Old Masters and through his time in Munich.

title: Children on the Seashore
description: Painted on the rocky beaches of Guernsey, where Renoir summered in 1883, the canvas shows small bathers playing among warm ochre boulders. The Channel light prompts a brighter, drier palette and the firmer drawing of his transitional period.

title: Christian IX of Denmark with his family
dateCreated: between 1883 and 1886 ( Prince Valdemar of Denmark (Christian's son) married Princess Marie of Orléans on 20 October 1885. If she is not here, the painting should have been made before that date.)
description: Tuxen assembles Christian IX — the so-called father-in-law of Europe — with his children and royal grandchildren in the garden hall of Fredensborg Palace. Painted between 1883 and 1886, the large group portrait records the Danish dynastic ties that linked the courts of Britain, Russia, and Greece and is now at Christiansborg Palace.

title: Crab Fishing
description: Four figures — a fisherman in a yellow oilskin at the bow and three women amidships — ride a small open dory through choppy grey seas, a crab pot visible in the bow. Homer captures the weight of rough weather with loose washes of grey and white, the figures rendered with confident economy. The watercolour, dated 1883, is held at the Worcester Art Museum.
credit: Bridgeman Art Library : Object 247063; The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; Worcester Art Museum

title: Dance at Bougival
description: A young couple turns together at an outdoor dance hall near Paris, the woman's red-flowered hat vivid against the dappled crowd. Renoir worked from sittings with Suzanne Valadon and Paul Lhote to anchor Impressionist light within a tightly composed figural scene, painted in 1883 and now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Danse à la campagne
description: A couple dancing at an open-air ball, the woman in a red bonnet with a fan, a table of glasses behind them. Oil on canvas of 1883, Musée d'Orsay, Paris, paired with the contemporary Dance in the City. The models were Aline Charigot, later Renoir's wife, and his friend Paul Lhôte.

title: Fujiwara no Yasumasa Playing the Flute by Moonlight
description: A late triptych by Yoshitoshi shows the Heian courtier Fujiwara no Yasumasa playing his flute on a moonlit moor while the bandit Hakamadare, disarmed by the music, looks on. Long stretches of muted ground and the cool autumnal palette demonstrate Yoshitoshi's reformed late style for the Meiji woodblock market.
credit: Image: http://collections.lacma.org/sites/default/files/remote_images/piction/ma-31808204-O3.jpg Gallery: http://collections.lacma.org/node/191379 archive copy at the Wayback Machine

provenance.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

title: Georges Seurat
englishTitle: Seated Nude (study for Bathers at Asnières, 1883)
description: A seated nude figure seen in profile, rendered in Seurat's characteristic conté crayon technique, with tonal gradations built from the grainy texture of the paper rather than painted strokes. Made circa 1883 as a preparatory study for Bathers at Asnières, the work is held at the Scottish National Gallery and predates the systematised pointillist method Seurat would develop later that decade.
credit: Scottish National Gallery

title: Gérôme
description: A male lion sits upright on a rocky desert outcrop, gazing toward a vast setting sun that floods the horizon with warm colour. Gérôme reduces the composition to two confronting presences — king of the beasts and king of the sky — stripped of any human element. Painted in 1883, the work is in the collection of the Milwaukee Art Museum.

title: Gustave Doré - La Vallée de larmes
description: A vast multitude of suffering humanity fills a rocky valley, prostrate or reaching toward a luminous, haloed figure at the left who radiates divine light. Painted in 1883 and now held at the Petit Palais, Paris, the canvas — over six metres wide — extends Doré's biblical illustration practice into monumental oil, retaining the steep tonal contrasts of his engraved work.

provenance.collection: Musée des Beaux-Arts de la ville de Paris

title: Gustave Doré-Mont Sainte-Odile avec mur païen
description: A panoramic view in the Vosges of the wooded heights of Mont Sainte-Odile, ringed by the prehistoric drystone enclosure known as the Pagan Wall. Better remembered for his book illustrations, Doré here works at large scale in oil, treating his native Alsace with a dark Romantic grandeur.

provenance.collection: Strasbourg Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art
provenance.location: Strasbourg Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art

title: Houses in Provence: The Riaux Valley near L'Estaque
description: Pale ochre houses clustered on a plateau above the Riaux valley, the rocky hillside built up in cool blues and greens beneath a high sky. Oil on canvas painted around 1883 near L'Estaque on the Mediterranean coast, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. Cézanne worked the terrain in faceted planes of colour rather than line.

title: Khnopff
description: A figure in black sits in a richly furnished interior, face buried in her hand, absorbed in music heard from the piano visible at the left edge of the composition. Fernand Khnopff painted this interior scene in 1883, capturing inwardness and emotional withdrawal with his characteristic muted palette and near-photographic stillness — hallmarks of his founding role in Belgian Symbolism.

title: Les Terrassiers
description: Labourers at work levelling earth, a subject from the industrial fringes of Paris that Seurat tackled in his early career. The broad balayé brushwork and sober palette precede the ordered dots of his pointillist maturity.

title: Madame X
description: Virginie Gautreau stands in profile in a black satin gown, her lavender-powdered skin set against a brown ground in a near-monochrome scheme. Sargent's salon submission caused such scandal in Paris over its eroticised pose and originally fallen strap that the painter eventually decamped to London.

title: Man Digging in the Orchard
description: A figure bends over to dig at the foot of a bare-branched tree in an orchard, low farm buildings visible across the flat background. Made in The Hague in July 1883 and catalogued by De La Faille, the work is one of several known impressions; an example is held at the British Museum (inventory 1929,1109.4).
credit: Masterworks: Van Gogh, by Janice Anderson. 2008. Pulteney Press, Bath.

title: Monet w835
description: Wooded islets in the Seine at Port-Villez, across the river from Vernon, painted in 1883 — the year Monet settled in nearby Giverny. The painting is in a private collection.

title: Monet w844
description: A 1883 view across the Seine toward Vernon, with the medieval Collégiale Notre-Dame rising over the riverside houses. Painted shortly after Monet moved to Giverny, a few kilometers upstream; the canvas is in a private collection.

title: Portrait d'Edmond Aman-Jean par Georges Seurat
description: Seurat's friend, the painter Edmond Aman-Jean, is seen in profile against a darkened ground, modelled entirely in delicate hatchings of conté crayon on textured paper. The drawing was the first work Seurat exhibited at the Salon, in 1883, and it established the velvety tonal manner of his black-and-white sheets.

title: Sailor Boy
description: Robert Nunès in a sailor suit standing before a loosely brushed beach, his father the mayor of Yport on the Normandy coast. Oil on canvas painted in 1883, when Renoir was commissioned to portray the Nunès children, now in the Barnes Foundation, Philadelphia (BF325).

title: The Inspection
description: A solitary figure in white robes stands in an ornately appointed interior, examining a small object — a pen or similar instrument — amid an array of brass vessels, inlaid boxes, and richly embroidered hangings. Painted in 1883, the small panel exemplifies Ludwig Deutsch's meticulous Orientalist technique, in which every textile and metalwork surface is rendered with near-photographic precision.

title: The Manneporte
description: The vast natural arch of the Manneporte rises from the surf at Étretat, one of three rock formations Monet painted obsessively during his Normandy campaigns of the early 1880s. The view from below dramatises the cliff's mass against breaking sea.
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art

title: Tsukioka Yoshitoshi
englishTitle: Minamoto no Ushiwakamaru Battling Kumasaka Chōhan, from the series Yoshitoshi's Courageous Warriors
description: From the series Yoshitoshi's Courageous Warriors (Yoshitoshi Musha Burui), this 1883 print depicts Minamoto no Ushiwakamaru locked in close combat with the armoured bandit Kumasaka Chōhan. Tsukioka Yoshitoshi renders the clash with intense patterning of armour and robes, charging the composition with the kinetic energy that distinguished his late warrior-print designs.
objectKey: collection-of-beauty/NDL-DC_1302763-Tsukioka_Yoshitoshi-芳年武者无類_源牛若丸・熊坂長範-明治16-crd.jpg
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 1302763

title: 1280px-Jean-Léon Gérôme - Slave Market in Rome - WGA8652
description: A slave auction in ancient Rome, set in a vaulted brick hall: an auctioneer in a yellow toga presents a nude woman on a raised platform while bidders' arms reach up from the crowd below, and other captives wait behind him. Painted in 1884, the work applies the same archaeological precision and enamelled finish Gérôme brought to his Orientalist subjects, here turned on classical antiquity.

title: A Roman Slave Market
description: A nude female captive stands on an auction platform, her back to the viewer, while a red-robed auctioneer addresses an assembled crowd of Roman buyers and onlookers. Gérôme renders the scene with the meticulous archaeological detail characteristic of his academic practice, distributing attention between the auctioneer's rhetoric and the varied responses of the bidders. The work, circa 1884, is one of six slave-market subjects Gérôme painted across ancient Roman and contemporary Ottoman settings, and is held in the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.

title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte
description: Seurat's manifesto of Neo-Impressionism, built over two years from countless oil sketches and conté studies. Bourgeois Parisians promenade along the Seine in frieze-like stillness, their forms assembled from tiny dots of contrasting pigment — the optical method he called divisionism.

title: After the bath
description: A nude woman seen from behind and in partial profile raises one arm above her head, drawing a large dark towel across her shoulders as she dries herself. Degas crops the composition tightly around the torso, dissolving the background into warm ochre and blue pastel strokes. The work dates to 1884–1886 and belongs to the sustained series of intimate bather studies Degas produced in that decade.

title: Bridge at Dolceacqua
description: The medieval bridge of Dolceacqua crosses the river Nervia in a single high arch, with the village and the ruined Doria castle stacked on the hillside behind. Monet painted it in 1884 during his campaign on the Italian Riviera, describing the bridge in a letter as 'a jewel of lightness.' The canvas is now at the Clark Art Institute in Williamstown, Massachusetts.

title: Bridge. Savvinskaya Sloboda
description: A plank bridge crosses a dark stream amid lush summer trees and green undergrowth at Savvinskaya Sloboda near Zvenigorod, with wooden village buildings visible behind. Isaac Levitan painted this small canvas in 1884 while near Zvenigorod, as confirmed by the title on the work.

title: Constantinople la mosquée de Top-Kahné-Ivan Aivazovski mg 8270
description: Aivazovsky envelops a great two-minareted mosque on the Tophane waterfront of Constantinople in luminous morning mist, the domed structure rising into a blue-violet haze while a small boat carries passengers across the calm water below. Painted in 1884, the canvas is held at the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Brest.
credit: Cette œuvre fait partie de la collection du Musée des Beaux-Arts de Brest .

title: Cymon and Iphigenia
description: Iphigenia asleep on the ground at evening, the herdsman Cymon halted at the right as he comes upon her. The subject is from a tale in Boccaccio's Decameron; Leighton exhibited the oil at the Royal Academy in 1884. The painting is now in the Art Gallery of New South Wales, Sydney, which acquired it in 1976.

title: Dragonfly. Painter's daughter portrait
description: Repin's daughter Vera perches astride a wooden fence rail against a pale summer sky, arms spread and legs dangling in the pose that earned the portrait its nickname. She wears a patterned dress and a broad-brimmed hat; the high horizon and open outdoor light reflect Repin's engagement with plein-air practice in the intimate Russian family-portrait tradition. The work dates to 1884.

title: G. Caillebotte - Homme portant une blouse
credit: Peinture réalisée à Etretat

title: G. Caillebotte - Villas à Trouville
description: Pastel seaside villas line the Normandy coast at Trouville, a fashionable resort favoured by Parisians on holiday. Caillebotte's looser handling and brighter palette here reflect his shift from urban scenes toward the open-air subjects of his later career.

title: Hollowed Cliff near Étretat
description: Fishing boats drawn up on the shingle beach at Étretat, with the famous arch and needle of the Porte d'Aval rising to the left and a rough sea breaking beyond. Monet painted the Étretat beach repeatedly in the 1880s, and this 1884 canvas — now in the Wallraf–Richartz Museum, Cologne — records the working character of the shore rather than the geological spectacle alone. The paint is applied with brisk, directional strokes that convey both the texture of the pebbled beach and the surge of the waves.

title: Japanese Anemones
description: Fantin-Latour built much of his reputation on still lifes painted in his Paris apartment for the English market. Here he sets autumn-flowering anemones in a glass vessel against a flat brown ground, modelling the petals with the cool, even illumination he preferred to the Impressionists' broken light.
credit: Aberdeen City Council (Archives, Gallery and Museums Collection)

provenance.collection: Aberdeen Archives, Gallery and Museums collections

title: Kniende Frau
description: A seated nude faces the viewer, wrapping herself in a white cloth against a floral-patterned background, her loose reddish hair falling around her shoulders. Degas rendered the figure in pastel with the soft, chalky hatching characteristic of his bathing series, dating the sheet 1884.

title: La Corniche near Monaco
description: A coastal path winds through dense Mediterranean scrub and flowering plants below a steep rocky headland, with the sea glinting to the left. Monet made this and related Riviera views during his 1884 trip to the coast between Bordighera and Monaco, pushing his palette into the hot, saturated hues of the southern sun. The canvas is held at the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

title: Love and Life
description: A winged male figure of Love guiding the slight nude figure of Life up a steep rocky path, violets springing where they tread. Watts called the picture a painted parable and first showed it at the Grosvenor Gallery in 1885. He gave a version to the United States; the work seen here is the one in the Tate (N01641).

title: Monet w663
description: A seascape painted at Fécamp on the Normandy coast, showing waves breaking under a heavy grey sky. Catalogued as Wildenstein 663 and also known as Rough Sea (Mer agitée), it is dated 1881, when Monet worked repeatedly along the Fécamp cliffs. The painting is in the National Gallery of Canada, Ottawa.

title: Monet w867
englishTitle: Bordighera, the House of the Gardener
description: Painted at Bordighera on the Italian Riviera during Monet's nearly three-month painting campaign of early 1884. It shows a gardener's house (maison du jardinier) set among the lush coastal vegetation that fascinated him there. Wildenstein 867; held in a private collection.

title: Monet w868
description: A study of olive trees painted at Bordighera during Monet's 1884 stay on the Italian Riviera, where the silvery foliage of the olive groves became a recurring subject. Wildenstein 868; held in a private collection.

title: Monet w871
englishTitle: Study of Olive Trees at Bordighera
