description: One of several studies of olive groves Monet painted at Bordighera on the Italian Riviera in 1884, capturing the flickering light through the silvery leaves. Wildenstein 871; held in a private collection.

title: Monet w875
description: Painted during Monet's 1884 campaign at Bordighera, whose palm gardens he described as almost impossibly exotic to paint. The upright canvas (92 x 73 cm) is catalogued as Wildenstein 875 and remains in a private collection.

title: Monet w885
englishTitle: The Valley of the Nervia with Dolceacqua
description: A view up the Nervia valley toward the medieval village of Dolceacqua in the Ligurian Alps, painted on an excursion inland from Bordighera in 1884. Wildenstein 885; held in a private collection.

title: Monet w891a
description: A rare self-portrait, showing the painter seated in his studio, dated to around 1884. Catalogued as Wildenstein 891a, it belongs to the Musée Marmottan Monet in Paris, home of the largest Monet collection.

title: Monet w891b
description: A view over the bay of Monaco with boats on the water, painted during Monet's 1884 trip along the Riviera coast. Wildenstein 891b; held in a private collection.

title: Monet w892
description: A panoramic view over the bay of Monte Carlo from Roquebrune, on the heights between Monaco and Menton, painted during Monet's 1884 Riviera campaign. Wildenstein 892; the painting is in the Portland Museum of Art, Maine.

title: Moreno Garden, Bordighera
description: Painted during a winter visit to Bordighera in 1884, the canvas captures the exotic garden of Francesco Moreno, with tall palms and lush subtropical planting crowding a path that leads toward the town's buildings and bell-tower. Monet was captivated by the Mediterranean light and the unfamiliar palette it demanded — warmer and more saturated than anything on the Normandy coast. The brushwork is energetic throughout, registering each variety of foliage in distinct strokes of green, blue, and gold.
credit: Websites of museums

title: Seated Nude: Study for 'Une Baignade'
description: Seurat's large-scale oil painting of 1884 shows a group of working-class men and boys resting and bathing on the grassy bank of the Seine at Asnières, with sailboats, a railway bridge, and factory chimneys visible across the water. Although Seurat had not yet fully developed his pointillist dot technique, the canvas displays the methodical colour application and monumental stillness that characterise his mature style. The work has been held in the National Gallery, London (NG3908) since 1924.
credit: National Gallery, London

title: Small Country Farm at Bordighera
description: On a winter trip to the Italian Riviera, Monet found at Bordighera a tangle of olives, palms and ochre walls under bright Mediterranean light. He complained of the difficulty of catching the dazzle in pigment, and worked rapidly across some forty canvases during the three-month campaign.

title: Strada Romana in Bordighera
description: A sun-drenched view of the old Roman road on the Italian Riviera, painted during Monet's three-month stay on the Mediterranean in early 1884. Hot pinks, lemons and mineral blues record what he described in letters as the difficulty of capturing the south's blinding light.
credit: Own work MuseumBarberini Taken on 19 April 2022

title: The Great Bathers
description: A frieze of monumental nudes disports along a wooded bank, their crisp contours and pearly flesh marking Renoir's so-called Ingresque turn away from pure Impressionism. The picture occupied him for several years and now hangs at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

title: The Life Line
description: A coastguardsman pulls a fainting woman across the surf on a breeches buoy, the rope line cutting taut against churning spray. Homer studied actual life-saving drills on the New Jersey coast, and the obscured rescuer's face concentrates attention on the woman's limp red scarf.

title: The Valley of the Nervia
description: The wide valley of the Nervia opens beneath massive snow-capped peaks, a scatter of buildings nestled among low trees at the valley floor, painted during Monet's January 1884 journey along the Italian Riviera. The palette of pale mauves, greys and warm ochres reflects his sustained fascination with Mediterranean light and its effect on landscape form. The canvas is held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: The Young Orphan
description: A young woman in mourning black reclines on a red velvet settee, her auburn hair and pale face set against richly coloured red walls. Chase's confident, economical brushwork conveys both the weight of grief and the sensuous warmth of the interior. Painted in 1884, the canvas is held at the National Academy of Design, New York.

title: They did not expect him
description: A Siberian exile reappears in his family's drawing room, the household frozen mid-reaction in a moment of recognition. Now in the Tretyakov Gallery, the painting is a touchstone of Russian Realism, organising psychology along sharp diagonal sightlines that link the returnee to mother, wife, and uncomprehending children.
credit: www.allpaintings.org

title: View of Bordighera
description: The hilltop town of Bordighera is glimpsed through a screen of dense Mediterranean pines and shrubs, its warm-toned buildings cascading toward the deep blue sea. Monet painted this view during his 1884 Italian Riviera campaign, when the unfamiliar vegetation and intense southern light pushed his colour toward new extremes. Now in the Hammer Museum, Los Angeles.

title: Villas at Bordighera
description: A terracotta-coloured villa with arched loggia fills the left foreground, flanked by tall palms and lush flowering shrubs, with the sun-baked town of Bordighera rising on the hillside beyond. Monet spent several months on the Italian Riviera in early 1884, producing numerous canvases devoted to its luxuriant vegetation and brilliant light. This work is in the collection of Museum Barberini, Potsdam.
credit: Twitter [1]

title: ' Frosty Morning
description: A broad autumn or late-season meadow stretches beneath bare trees, with sheep grazing in the middle distance and a shepherd figure visible under an overcast sky. George Inness signed this canvas in 1885 and associated it with the New Jersey landscape around Montclair, where he spent his later years developing the atmospheric, tonal manner of his mature work.

title: Adachi Moor
description: A pregnant woman hangs bound and upside down from the rafters of a darkened house while a gaunt old woman crouches below, sharpening a knife — Yoshitoshi's treatment of the legend of the cannibal hag of Adachigahara. Published in September 1885, the vertical-format colour woodblock diptych, known as The Lonely House on Adachi Moor, is held by the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.
credit: Photograph of an original print dated 1885 owned by me

provenance.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

title: Aleksander III receiving rural district elders in the yard of Petrovsky Palace in Moscow
englishTitle: Alexander III Receiving Rural District Elders at the Petrovsky Palace
description: A wide-format Russian historical scene of Tsar Alexander III addressing village elders gathered in the Petrovsky Palace courtyard during his coronation. Repin orchestrates the crowd with his characteristic eye for individuated peasant types and ceremonial pomp.

title: Ariko weeps on her boat
englishTitle: Ariko Weeps as Her Boat Drifts in the Moonlight
description: Print 38 from Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's "100 Aspects of the Moon" (Tsuki Hyakusen), a celebrated series of ukiyo-e woodblock prints. The composition depicts Ariko, a character from classical Japanese narrative, weeping in a boat illuminated by moonlight—a poignant moment capturing the intersection of human emotion and natural beauty.

title: Arsène Vigeant
description: Arsène Vigeant sits before a table, one hand resting on a closed book and his gaze directed at the viewer, while a sword stands in the background shadow to his left. Sargent painted the portrait in 1885, linking the fencing master's twin identities as swordsman and bibliographer of the sword. The work is now in the collection of the Metz museum.

title: Birch grove
description: Sunlight filters between the white trunks of a young birch wood, the grass below flecked with light, shadow and scattered wildflowers. Levitan worked on the small picture for four summers, beginning it at Babkino near Moscow in 1885 and finishing it at Plyos on the Volga in 1889; it is now in the Tretyakov Gallery.
credit: http://smallbay.ru/levitan.html http://www.artlib.ru/index.php?id=11&idp=0&fp=2&uid=692&iid=6547&idg=0&user_serie=0 http://www.artrussia.ru/russian/artists/picture.php?pic_id=179&foa=f&rarity=1 http://www.staratel.com/pictures/ruspaint/big/351-1.htm

title: Carnation
description: Two girls in white dresses light glowing Japanese paper lanterns amid tall white lilies and rose blooms in a garden at dusk. Sargent worked on the canvas over two consecutive summers in Broadway, painting only in the brief twilight each evening to capture the transient quality of the fading light. Exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1887 and now in Tate Britain, the picture is widely seen as the work that restored Sargent's reputation in England after the controversy over Madame X.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — lAGrEoFGzGZEEQ Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N01615&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: Claude Monet Painting by the Edge of a Wood
description: Sargent depicts his friend Monet at work outdoors at Giverny, easel propped beside a thicket as a young woman reads nearby. The picture is a personal homage from one painter to another, executed with the very plein-air looseness it documents.

title: Claude Monet. Die Weide. Frühling an der Epte
description: A willow standing on the bank of the Epte near Giverny, caught in the pale, cool light of a spring morning. The pastel palette and feathery brushwork are typical of Monet's mid-1880s riverside studies, in which he began to anchor compositions around a single tree as a recurring motif.
credit: Das Willow (aka Frühjahr auf der Epte) von Claude Monet (1840-1926, France) | Kunstreproduktionen Claude Monet | wahooart.com

title: Coming into Giverny in the Snow
description: A snow-blanketed view of the village Monet had recently made his home, painted with muted pinks and blues that register the cold light of a winter afternoon. Such effets de neige let him test how a single subject changes under shifting weather and atmosphere.

title: Étretat: The Beach and the Falaise d'Amont
description: Beached fishing caïques dominate the foreground as the chalk Falaise d'Amont curves out into a green sea. Monet returned to Étretat repeatedly in the 1880s, drawn by the sculpted cliffs Courbet had also painted a generation earlier.

title: Girl with a hoop
description: Marie Goujon, aged nine, in a blue dress and sash holding a hoop against a screen of foliage. Oil on canvas painted in 1885 and commissioned by her father, the physician Étienne Goujon, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, from the Chester Dale Collection.

title: House at Falaise in the Fog
description: A house at Falaise dissolves into a dense enveloping fog, the building's roofline and walls barely legible against the surrounding violet-grey atmosphere. Monet painted the Normandy interior as well as its coast, and this 1885 canvas shows his interest in conditions that reduce form to colour and tone. Swirling, overlapping brushstrokes in muted blues, pinks, and lavenders render the fog as an almost tactile presence.

title: Inaba Mountain Moon
description: A lone warrior clings to a near-vertical rock face beneath a crescent moon and windswept grasses, his body braced against the cliff as he ascends. This is plate seven of Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon series (1885), depicting the young Toyotomi Hideyoshi in his famous assault on the castle of Inaba Mountain.
credit: National Diet Library [1]

title: Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan on November 16th
description: The tsar cradles the dying son he has just struck down with his iron-tipped staff, blood smearing the Persian carpet. Held by the Tretyakov Gallery, the picture shocked contemporaries and was briefly banned by Alexander III for its raw psychological violence.

title: James Abbott McNeill Whistler
description: Chase portrays Whistler full-length against a warm golden ground, the subject dressed head to toe in black and holding a slender cane — a dandyish self-presentation in keeping with Whistler's own aesthetic persona. Painted in 1885 and now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the canvas records Chase's admiration for his fellow artist while asserting his own formidable painterly confidence.

title: La grande piscine de Brousse
description: Gérôme depicts the great communal bath at Bursa in Ottoman Anatolia, its vaulted stone arches admitting shafts of light above a crowded pool of nude bathers attended by robed servants. Painted by 1885, the canvas exemplifies the academic precision and ethnographic ambition of his Eastern subjects, rendering human figures and architectural atmosphere with the hard-edged finish characteristic of his Orientalist work.
credit: Gérôme, La grande piscine de brousse , leo.jeje , 2011-04-12 11:30

title: Le givre à Giverny
description: Two figures walk through a frost-covered landscape near Giverny in this 1885 canvas, now in Museum Barberini, Potsdam. Frost-laden branches fill the upper half of the composition, and Monet renders the chill morning light in pale violet, rose, and white, the delicate tones characteristic of his winter subjects painted after he settled at Giverny in 1883.

title: Les Soleils
description: A dense bed of sunflowers fills the canvas, painted in the artist's own garden at Petit Gennevilliers on the banks of the Seine. The loose handling and saturated yellows reflect a late shift toward Impressionist plein-air practice, after he had largely turned from urban subjects to horticulture.

title: Madame Cézanne
description: This file was provided to Wikimedia Commons by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum as part of a cooperation project . The Solomon R.
credit: Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation

title: Monet w1010
description: A view of the Falaise d'Amont, one of the chalk cliffs framing the beach at Étretat on the Normandy coast, painted during Monet's 1885 campaign there. Wildenstein 1010; held in a private collection.

title: Monet w1018
englishTitle: The Cliffs of the Porte d'Aval
description: A view of the Porte d'Aval, the great natural chalk arch at Étretat on the Normandy coast, painted during Monet's 1885 stay. Wildenstein 1018; held in a private collection.

title: Monet w1032
englishTitle: Sailboats off the Aiguille Rock at Étretat
description: Sailboats run before the wind beneath the Aiguille — the slender needle rock that rises off the cliffs of Étretat on the Normandy coast. Claude Monet returned to Étretat repeatedly through the 1880s, treating its arches, rocks, and weather in a sustained series catalogued by Daniel Wildenstein as W.1032 and its neighbours.
credit: Claude Monet

title: Monet w1048
englishTitle: The Cliff and the Porte d'Amont, Rough Sea
description: Heavy seas break against the cliff face beneath the Porte d'Amont, the northern of Étretat's three natural arches. Monet treated the Étretat coast in a long sequence of canvases through the mid-1880s, captured in Wildenstein's catalogue raisonné as W.1048 among neighbouring entries.
credit: Claude Monet

title: Monet w928
description: A small frieze-like flower study of daffodils (Jonquilles), only 16 x 40 cm, painted in 1885. Wildenstein 928; held in a private collection.

title: Robert Louis Stevenson and His Wife
description: Robert Louis Stevenson strides across a dark red interior, his figure caught mid-step while his wife Fanny is glimpsed seated at the far right beneath a pale shawl. Painted by Sargent in 1885, the unconventional composition places the two figures in oblique relationship, the writer commanding the room while his wife recedes into the shadowed corner.
credit: John Singer Sargent Gallery

title: Self-portrait
description: Lepsius portrays herself three-quarter length holding palette and brushes, her gaze angled slightly downward against a warm golden ground. Dated 1885 and now in the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin, the picture displays the confident naturalism she developed through her training in Berlin and Paris.
credit: Selected work 33 from Self Portrait: Renaissance to Contemporary (Anthony Bond, Joanna Woodall, ISBN 978-1855143579 ).

title: Self-Portrait
description: Gauguin shows himself half-length at a table with palette and brushes, the slope of an attic beam behind him, painted in the loosely broken brushwork he was developing in 1885. Painted the year he committed fully to painting, the picture is held at the Kimbell Art Museum and is one of several self-portraits from his early Post-Impressionist period.
credit: Kimbell Art Museum

title: Shark fishing
description: A shirtless man and a young child sit in a small wooden boat while two sharks circle alongside in open blue water, the larger shark occupying the full foreground. Homer painted the scene during his visits to the Bahamas in the mid-1880s, and the work anticipates the themes of human vulnerability before the sea that he would develop in The Gulf Stream. Dated 1885.
credit: fineartamerica.com

title: Swimming
description: Six male figures occupy a stone masonry pier and the water around it in the afternoon sun, while a dog leans from the edge and a swimmer — identified in scholarship as Eakins himself — moves toward it in the lower right. Completed in 1885 and painted partly from photographic studies of Eakins's students, the canvas has been in the collection of the Amon Carter Museum of American Art in Fort Worth since the twentieth century.
credit: whitmanarchive.org; Scanned from Bolger, Doreen; Cash, Sarah; et al. Thomas Eakins and the Swimming Picture. Amon Carter Museum; ISBN 0-88360-085-4

title: The Artist's Son
description: The artist's son Paul shown from the waist up in a blue jacket and a small black bowler hat, glancing sideways. Oil on canvas worked between 1885 and 1890, the face shaded in visible strokes of slate blue, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. Paul was Cézanne's most frequent sitter.

title: The Bather
description: An adolescent boy mid-stride in a pale watery landscape, hands on his hips, his body slightly out of proportion. Oil on canvas of about 1885 based on a studio photograph of a posed model, now in the Museum of Modern Art, New York, from the Lillie P. Bliss Collection.

title: The Cliff of Aval
description: The famous Falaise d'Aval at Étretat, with its natural arch piercing the chalk cliff. Monet, who painted this Norman site repeatedly, here works with broken touches of cream, lilac and pale green to render limestone under shifting Channel light.

title: The Cliffs at Etretat
description: A view of the chalk cliffs and natural arches at Étretat on the Normandy coast, a motif Monet returned to repeatedly in the mid-1880s. He works the chalk face in pinks and creams against the green-blue Channel, alert to how the light shifts across the porous stone.

title: The Cliffs at Étretat
description: Monet painted the famous arched chalk cliff at Étretat with the slender Aiguille needle beyond, seen from the water's edge where a fleet of small sailing boats crosses the luminous surf. Broken brushwork in pink, blue, and cream dissolves the forms in atmospheric haze. Painted in 1885–86, the canvas is held by the Pushkin Museum of Fine Arts, Moscow.

title: The Fog Warning / Halibut Fishing
description: A halibut fisherman in a dory pauses at the crest of a swell to gauge the schooner against a wall of advancing fog. The diagonal of the boat and the steep horizon convert a routine moment into a measured study of solitude at sea.

title: The Minotaur
description: The Minotaur leaning on a parapet and gazing out to sea, a small bird crushed in his fist. Watts painted the oil in 1885 as a protest against the child prostitution exposed that summer by W. T. Stead in the Pall Mall Gazette. It entered the Tate in 1897 (N01634).
credit: Google Arts & Culture — vQE8NbrgEE9saQ Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N01634&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: The river
description: A male nude seated by water, the figure modelled in warm flesh tones against a loosely brushed bank. Dated 1885, the period when Renoir tightened his contours under the influence of Ingres and Raphael. The study is attributed to Renoir and reproduced from a monograph on the painter.
credit: Renoir, book.

title: View of Fort Samson
description: A coastal view from Grandcamp on the Normandy shore, part of the seaside campaigns Seurat undertook each summer to test his divisionist method against changing light. Tiny calibrated dots dissolve fortification, sea and sky into a luminous, near-abstract grid.

title: W 967 Monet - L'Entrée de Giverny en hiver 1885
description: A bare lane leads into the village of Giverny under winter light, with leafless trees and pale fields rendered in muted blues and ochres. Painted shortly after Monet settled in Giverny, the canvas catalogued as Wildenstein 967 belongs to a small group of winter views recording his new surroundings.

title: Woman Combing her Hair
description: A nude woman seen from behind raises both arms to brush her auburn hair, a white cloth gathered beside her. Degas worked the composition in pastel on cardboard around 1885, the warm orange ground and tightly cropped viewpoint concentrating attention on the body's movement. The work belongs to his sustained series of women at their toilette.

title: Woman Having Her Hair Combed
description: A nude woman sits on a yellow armchair, her head tilted back as a maid standing behind her draws a comb through her loose reddish-brown hair. Degas treated this gesture of intimate grooming in pastel and oil through the mid-1880s, an extension of his series of women at their toilette. The work dates to around 1885.

title: 2560px-Bonaparte ante la Esfinge
description: Napoleon, mounted on a dark horse, halts before the half-buried Great Sphinx during the 1798 Egyptian campaign, his army drawn up on the desert plain behind him. Gérôme, the leading Orientalist of the Paris Salon, painted the encounter in 1886 — the picture is also known by the subtitle 'Œdipe' — casting it as one civilisational riddle posed to another. The canvas now hangs at Hearst Castle.

title: 960px-Van Gogh - Le Moulin de la Galette4
description: The windmill of the Moulin de la Galette stands on its mound beneath a windswept blue sky, a stooping figure working in the foreground. Van Gogh painted the Montmartre landmark — also depicted by Renoir and Toulouse-Lautrec — several times in 1886, soon after moving in with his brother Theo in Paris; this version is in the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin.

title: At the Entrance to the Temple Mount
description: Bauernfeind, the leading German Orientalist of his generation, records a crowded Jerusalem street where pilgrims and traders converge at the gates of Haram al-Sharif. His near-photographic precision rests on sketches gathered during repeated journeys to Palestine.

title: Breton Girl
description: A young woman in the white coif and dark dress of Pont-Aven posed during Gauguin's first Brittany sojourn. The simplified silhouette and reserved palette anticipate the cloisonnist flattening he would push further in following summers among the Breton peasantry.

title: Captive Andromache
description: A long procession of women in flowing drapery filing toward a well, the widowed Andromache in black at the centre near a family group. Oil on canvas of about 1886 to 1888, the subject taken from a passage in Homer's Iliad. Manchester City Council bought the picture from Leighton for £4,000 in 1889; it hangs in Manchester Art Gallery.
credit: The original uploader was Ravenous at English Wikipedia .

title: Carnival Evening
description: Two carnival figures in white costume stand at the forest edge beneath a full moon, bare winter trees silhouetted against a blue-grey sky. A small kiosk stands at the lower left, and soft clouds drift above the treeline. Painted in 1886 and now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art, this early canvas already displays the flattened silhouettes and dreamlike stillness central to Rousseau's vision.

title: Dawn Moon of the Shinto Rites
description: A towering festival float, richly decorated with red and green ornaments, miniature figurines, and a tall banner, is shown against a clear blue sky. This is plate thirty-three of Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon series (1886), titled "Dawn Moon of the Shinto Rites," and depicts the elaborate dashi floats associated with Shinto festival processions.

title: Flame Nettle in a Flowerpot
description: A potted coleus painted in Paris during Van Gogh's transition from the dark Dutch palette toward brighter, more broken color. The everyday flowerpot becomes an exercise in observing complementary reds and greens at close range.
credit: Van Gogh Museum

title: Four Breton Women
description: Four Breton peasant women in white coifs and dark dresses are gathered in an outdoor setting, their figures clustered against a background of foliage. Painted at Pont-Aven in 1886 during Gauguin's first Breton summer, the canvas records his early engagement with the rituals and costume of rural Brittany. The work belongs to the Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen, on long-term deposit at the Neue Pinakothek in Munich.

title: Gravemarker Moon
description: The aged poetess Ono no Komachi sits before a wooden gravemarker beneath a crescent moon, a woven basket on her back and a staff in her hands, her gaze lifted skyward. Plate twenty-five of Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon (1886), the image evokes the courtly love legend in which Komachi's later life became a meditation on the arrogance she had shown her suitors in youth.

title: Hope
description: تابلوی امید اثر « جرج فردریک واتس » متعلق به ۱۸۸۶ است، در این تابلو امید در قالب زنی مجسم شده که چنگی با تنها یک رشتهٔ سالم در دست دارد. او سرش را نزدیک به آلت موسیقی گرفته است، تا بتواند نوای ضعیف موسیقی برخاسته از تک‌تار سالم را بشنود.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — CgGv3RqPFUZk4A Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N01640&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: Le Moulin de la Galette
englishTitle: Le Moulin de la Galette (hilltop view with elevated platform)
description: Painted during the Paris years, this view of the Montmartre windmill blends the muted palette of his earlier Dutch work with the lighter tonalities he was absorbing from the Impressionists. The motif, a popular dance hall draw for Parisian painters, is treated soberly rather than festively.

title: le tub
description: A nude crouches in a shallow zinc tub sponging her neck, beside a marble-topped washstand whose pitcher and brushes are seen from a sharply tilted angle. Degas drew the pastel on heavy wove paper in 1886 and showed it at the Eighth Impressionist Exhibition that May; the sheet entered the Musee d'Orsay as one of his most accomplished bather compositions.

title: Monet w1061
description: A broad view of Vernon on the Seine, the small town a short distance downstream from Monet's home at Giverny. Catalogued in Wildenstein as W.1061, the canvas belongs to the painter's quieter landscapes of the Seine valley made alongside his more famous Giverny garden series.
credit: Claude Monet

title: Portrait de Poly
description: Hippolyte 'Poly' Guillaume, a Belle-Île fisherman, is shown in a closely cropped bust portrait wearing a dark hat and a blue-green coat, his weathered face rendered with the same energetic brushwork Monet applied to the Brittany coastal landscapes of 1886. The portrait entered the Musée Marmottan Monet through the artist's family (inventory 5023).

title: Pyramides at Port-Coton
description: The jagged sea stacks off Belle-Île-en-Mer, painted during Monet's bracing autumn campaign on the Breton coast. Granite is built up in dense, crusted strokes against a churning Atlantic, a darker and rougher palette than his Norman seascapes.
credit: Alain Truong [1]

title: Regnvær
description: Rain over Étretat: the Norman cliffs and arched rock recede behind a grey curtain of weather, the Channel rendered in broken slate strokes. Monet often returned to Étretat through the 1880s, attracted by its dramatic chalk geology under shifting marine light.

provenance.collection: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design
provenance.location: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

title: Self-portrait with pipe
description: An early self-portrait with the artist's clay pipe, painted shortly after his arrival in Paris while his palette was still close to that of his Dutch years. Sober earth tones model the bearded face against a neutral ground, before the chromatic experiments of the following year.

title: Still Life with Profile of Laval
description: A bearded young man in profile crops the right edge of the canvas, staring at a ceramic pot the painter had thrown himself and a cluster of pears on a white cloth. Gauguin painted his friend and pupil Charles Laval in late 1886 after returning from Pont-Aven; the cut-off face nods to Degas's framing while the parallel strokes in the fruit pay tribute to Cezanne. Indianapolis Museum of Art.

title: Study of a Figure Outdoors: Woman with a Parasol
description: Suzanne Hoschedé strides up a grassy slope, parasol angled against the wind that flattens her white dress. The picture revisits the 1875 Argenteuil composition of Camille, now reworked as a near-anonymous figure study with the face deliberately blurred.

title: The Blute-Fin Mill
description: A lively view of the Moulin de Blute-Fin on the butte of Montmartre, showing a crowd of fashionably dressed figures gathered at the base of the mill, painted in 1886 during Van Gogh's Paris years. The palette is notably colourful — reds, greens, and blues animate the figures — showing the rapid lightening of his manner after his arrival in the city. The work is held at Museum de Fundatie, Zwolle.

title: The Breton shepherdess
description: A young shepherdess sits barefoot on the grass with her flock in a sloping Pont-Aven pasture, the village rooftops in the middle distance. Gauguin signed and dated the canvas P Gauguin 86 at lower left, among the first works of his initial Brittany summer; it entered the Laing Art Gallery in Newcastle as a gift from the National Art Collections Fund in 1945.
credit: Sotheby's (not for sale, only as a reference)

title: The Sahleb Vendor
description: A street vendor of sahleb, the hot orchid-root drink popular in Ottoman Cairo, pours a cup before a tiled wall. Deutsch worked from sketches and props gathered on visits to Egypt, finishing each picture in his Paris studio with jewel-like precision.

title: The Wrath of the Seas
description: A small rowboat crowded with figures struggles through heavy swells beneath a vast, storm-torn sky; a towering wave rises on the left while broken light pierces the clouds above. Aivazovsky, who made the sea's power and human vulnerability his central subject, painted this canvas in 1886. The composition places human presence as a minor element against the overwhelming scale of the storm.
credit: picture "wrath of the seas"

title: Tulip Fields at Sassenheim
description: Bands of red, yellow, white and purple tulips stripe the flat polder near Sassenheim, with a low farmhouse and bare trees anchoring the pale horizon. Monet visited Holland in the spring of 1886 and produced a group of tulip-field canvases in which the cultivated riot of colour offered a ready experiment in pure chroma. Now in the Clark Art Institute, Williamstown.

title: Tulip fields in Holland
description: Sweeping bands of red and violet tulips fill the foreground, with a windmill and farm buildings rising against a brisk cloudy sky. Monet visited the Dutch bulb fields in 1886 to paint these intensely saturated expanses of colour. The canvas, dated 1886, is held at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

title: Woman in a Tub
description: A nude woman stands in a shallow metal tub, bending forward as she sponges the bath, her body modelled in chalky strokes against a blue-grey ground. Degas exhibited the 1886 pastel with the rest of his bather suite at the Eighth and final Impressionist Exhibition that year, drawing critics' attacks on the bluntness of the poses.

title: Woman with a Parasol - Madame Monet and Her Son
description: Camille turns under a green parasol while young Jean stands among grasses on a windy bluff, painted from below so the figures rise into a billowing sky. The picture, now in Washington's National Gallery, is Monet's bid to handle the figure outdoors with full plein-air conviction.

title: Yoshitoshi tsuki
description: The warrior-monk Benkei stands at the prow of a storm-tossed vessel in Daimotsu Bay, calming the vengeful spirits of fallen Taira warriors with chanted prayers. From One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, Yoshitoshi pitches the scene against rolling waves and a clouded moon to dramatize the Heike legend.
credit: Polychrome woodblock print; mica on paper

title: 1280px-Van Gogh - Das Restaurant Rispal in Asniéres
description: A view of a suburban café-restaurant on the banks of the Seine, painted during Van Gogh's Paris years when he frequented the riverside towns with Bernard and Signac. The lightened palette and short, divisionist-inflected strokes register his rapid absorption of Impressionist and Neo-Impressionist colour theory.

title: 1280px-Zelfportret met grijze vilthoed - s0016V1962 - Van Gogh Museum
description: Painted during Van Gogh's Paris years, this self-portrait shows the artist absorbing Impressionist and Pointillist colour theory. Short, hatched strokes of complementary blue and orange radiate from his head, turning the felt hat into a halo of pure pigment. Now in the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.

title: 2560px-Vincent van Gogh - Grapes
description: A still life of grapes, lemons, pears, and apples banked across the table, painted in Paris under the influence of Adolphe Monticelli's heavy paint and the Impressionists' fruit studies. Now at the Art Institute of Chicago, it shows Van Gogh testing a brighter, complementary-colour palette.

title: 500px-Gipsen vrouwentorso - s0199V1962 - Van Gogh Museum
englishTitle: Plaster Cast of a Woman's Torso
description: A plaster cast of a female torso seen from behind, set against a pale blue ground. Van Gogh painted a group of such plaster-cast studies in Paris, using the neutral academic subject to work through problems of modelling and colour. This 1887 example is in the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam (inv. s0199V1962).

title: Along the Seine
description: A riverside scene along the Seine on the outskirts of Paris, painted during the artist's Asnières period with Bernard and Signac. The handling shows the impact of Neo-Impressionist contact, with broken touches of pure colour modeling the embankment, water, and screen of trees.

title: Boyarina Morozova
description: Boyarina Feodosia Morozova is conveyed through a snowy Moscow street on a wooden sledge, her emaciated hand raised in the two-fingered Old Believer sign of the cross as a dense crowd of beggars, clergy, nuns, and curious onlookers presses close. Surikov spent years preparing this monumental canvas, exhibiting it at the Peredvizhniki Travelling Exhibition of 1887. The vast composition — just under three metres high and nearly six metres wide — was acquired for the Tretyakov Gallery, where it remains one of the defining works of Russian historical painting.

title: Christmas Eve
description: A stone manor house glows with candlelit windows against a warm amber winter dusk, its bare trees and snow-covered grounds populated by crows foraging in the foreground. Painted in 1887, the work shows Millais's late landscape manner — meticulous in detail yet suffused with atmospheric colour — and is characteristic of the Scottish winter subjects he returned to in his final decades.
credit: Christie's , LotFinder: entry 5631469 (sale 5969, lot 23, London, King Street, 13 December 2012)

title: Corner in Voyer-d'Argenson Park at Asnières by Vincent van Gogh
englishTitle: Corner in Voyer-d'Argenson Park at Asnières
description: A spring corner of an Asnières park from Van Gogh's Paris years, when he absorbed Impressionism and Neo-Impressionism in the company of Bernard and Signac. Short divided strokes of green, blue, and rose lighten his palette decisively before he carried it south to Arles. The work, dated Spring 1887, is held at the Yale University Art Gallery.

title: En Norvégienne. La barque à Giverny
description: Three of Alice Hoschedé's daughters drift on the Epte in a Norwegian skiff, their pale dresses caught between dark river plants and sun-laced water. The high viewpoint and crop, learnt from Japanese prints, push the figures toward decorative pattern.

title: Fix Bayonets! Hooray! Hooray!
description: Painted between 1887 and 1895 and held at the Museum of Patriotic War 1812, Moscow, this canvas by Vasily Vereshchagin depicts Russian infantry charging through a snow-covered forest, bayonets fixed and a standard raised against bare and frost-laden pines. A mounted officer urges the advance at left while soldiers press forward through drifts and fallen timber, smoke drifting through the trees. The work belongs to Vereshchagin's series on Napoleon's 1812 Russian campaign, rendered with the unvarnished realism characteristic of his battle subjects.

title: Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse
description: Conquest, War, Famine and Death ride through a turbulent sky above a landscape strewn with the fallen, the Lamb of God faintly visible in the upper register. Vasnetsov completed the oil in 1887, drawing on the Book of Revelation to produce one of the most vivid Russian Symbolist treatments of the Apocalypse theme.

title: Fruit Picking
description: An early Martinique canvas from Gauguin's 1887 stay near Saint-Pierre, showing local women gathering fruit beneath dense tropical foliage. Painted before his Tahitian voyages, the work already shows his shift away from Impressionist brushwork toward flatter, decorative arrangements of figure and landscape.

title: Garden in Montmarte with lovers
description: An open garden on the slopes of Montmartre, with couples strolling along winding paths between young trees in bloom. Painted in 1887 during Van Gogh's Paris years, the canvas reflects his growing interest in the broken, complementary colour touches of his Neo-Impressionist contemporaries. The work is held at the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.

title: Girl with peaches
description: Vera Mamontova sits at a sunlit dining table in a pink blouse, peaches and autumn leaves scattered on the white cloth before her. Serov painted the work over several weeks at Abramtsevo in 1887, the canvas now in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

title: Glazunov by Repin
description: A three-quarter-length portrait of the young composer Alexander Glazunov, who meets the viewer with a level, brooding gaze, one hand tucked into his dark coat against a deep red ground. Repin works with the loose, painterly attack of his portrait practice in the late 1880s, when he documented much of the Russian musical and literary intelligentsia.

title: Google Art Project
description: Two young women in white summer dresses and straw hats sit in a small rowing boat, their figures reflected in the shimmering water beneath. Painted in 1887 and held by the National Museum of Western Art, Tokyo, the canvas presents its subjects from an elevated vantage point that flattens the scene into broad planes of colour, a compositional strategy Monet shared with contemporaries drawn to Japanese prints.

title: Grass and Butterflies
description: A close-range, near-aerial view of a garden corner in which flowering plants — their pink and white blooms rendered in rapid directional strokes — fill almost the entire picture surface, with butterflies visible among the foliage. Van Gogh painted the work in Paris between May and July 1887, and it is held by the Van Gogh Museum.
credit: Christie's , LotFinder: entry 6169506 (sale 15977, lot 40A, New York, 11 November 2018, page no more available)

title: Huts under the Trees
description: Thatched cottages glimpsed through tree trunks, painted during Gauguin's stay in Martinique in 1887. The tropical light and broad colour areas mark his decisive turn away from Impressionist division of tone toward the synthetist style of Pont-Aven.

title: In the Woods at Giverny: Blanche Hoschedé at Her Easel with Suzanne Hoschedé Reading
englishTitle: In the Woods at Giverny: Blanche Hoschedé at Her Easel
description: Two of Alice Hoschedé's daughters work and read in the dappled woods near Giverny, where Monet had moved in 1883. Blanche, herself a painter, would later marry Monet's son Jean and become his nurse and companion in his final years.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme 015 Carpets
description: A large carpet — white ground with a blue-green medallion and red border — is displayed vertically in a Cairo courtyard while a group of buyers examines it from below and two men observe from an upper gallery. Gérôme's oil on canvas of about 1887, now at the Minneapolis Institute of Arts, deploys his tight academic finish to capture the textile's intricate geometry and the architectural ornament of the Mamluk-era setting.
credit: Minneapolis Institute of Arts via artsconnected.org

title: Jean-Pierre Hoschedé and Michel Monet on the Bank of the Epte
description: Two young figures stand on the bank of the Epte beside tall bare-trunked trees, their reflections caught in the still water below. The muted, hazy palette — pale pinks, blues, and ochres — places the scene in late autumn or winter. Painted between about 1887 and 1890, the work is held at the National Gallery of Canada, Ottawa.
credit: National Gallery of Canada

title: La barque
description: A white rowing skiff occupies the upper right of the canvas, its hull framed by dark water streaked with sinuous aquatic grasses visible beneath the surface. Painted in 1887, La barque belongs to the group of intimate river and pond studies Monet made at Giverny; the work is now in the Musée Marmottan Monet, Paris.
credit: Claude Monet

title: Le Moulin de la Galette
englishTitle: Le Moulin de la Galette (slope view from below)
description: A view of the Moulin de la Galette, the Montmartre windmill turned popular dance garden depicted by Renoir and Toulouse-Lautrec. Van Gogh treats the wooden mill and surrounding fence soberly, its silhouette isolated against an overcast Paris sky.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic

title: Les Poseuses
description: Three views of the same studio model — facing, in profile and from behind — set against the painter's own Grande Jatte. Seurat used the picture as a programmatic demonstration of pointillism applied to the academic motif of the nude.
credit: The Artchive

title: Menter by Repin
description: A portrait of the Bavarian virtuoso pianist Sophie Menter, then teaching at the Saint Petersburg Conservatory, captured with the loose painterly bravura Repin reserved for his musical and literary friends. The Russian Realist treated such cultural sitters as documents of the late imperial intelligentsia.

title: Montmartre: mills and vegetable gardens
description: A view across the allotment gardens and windmills of upper Montmartre, then still a semi-rural quarter on the northern edge of Paris. Wooden fences, vegetable plots, and the silhouettes of the mills are arranged in receding bands beneath a wide, pale sky.

title: Moonrise
description: A large golden moon rises just above a line of dark trees, its warm light reflected in a marshy stream in the foreground, where a small solitary figure stands at the water's edge. The sky is deep and dark, tinged with orange near the horizon rather than the cooler hues of twilight. Painted in 1887 and held at the Yale University Art Gallery, the canvas belongs to Inness's late tonalist phase, when landscape became a vehicle for contemplative, near-mystical mood.
credit: Yale University Art Gallery, Yale University, New Haven, Conn.

title: Nude in a Landscape
description: A small late-1880s nude from Renoir's so-called "manière aigre", when he tightened his contours under the influence of Ingres and Italian Renaissance drawing. The pearly figure is set against a lightly brushed landscape, oil on canvas, now on long-term loan from the Pearlman Foundation to the Princeton University Art Museum.
credit: Henry and Rose Pearlman Collection

title: On the outskirts of Paris
description: A lone figure walks along a bright suburban road flanked by young trees, with rows of houses and a crop field stretching to the horizon. Painted in Paris in the spring of 1887, the canvas shows Van Gogh absorbing the lighter palette and broken touch of the Impressionists he was encountering in the city.

title: Pierre Auguste Renoir - Paysage à La Roche-Guyon
description: A wooded landscape at La Roche-Guyon, a village on a bend of the Seine in the Val-d'Oise. Oil on canvas painted in 1887, two years after Renoir had spent a summer there working alongside Cézanne. The picture is now in the Pérez Simón collection.
credit: UntitledMag [1]

title: Portrait of Etienne-Lucien Martin
description: A three-quarter bust of a man in a blue-grey work jacket and matching cap, rendered with the short, hatched strokes Van Gogh absorbed from Seurat and Signac during his Paris years. The sitter, identified as Étienne-Lucien Martin, gazes slightly to the side against a cool blue-green ground. The portrait dates from 1887 and is held at the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam (inv. s0125V1962).
credit: Van Gogh Museum

title: Portrait of Marguerite Khnopff
description: Khnopff portrays his sister Marguerite, a recurring presence in his work, with the cool, hieratic detachment that defines his Symbolist portraiture. The pale palette and flattened space distil her into an emblem of withdrawn, idealised femininity rather than likeness alone.
credit: Self-photographed , Georges Jansoone ( JoJan ), 20 August 2008

title: Seine-shore at the Pont de Clichy
description: A grassy riverbank slopes down to the Seine near the Pont de Clichy, with a wooden bridge visible at right and a pale grey sky overhead. The brushwork shows the stippled, broken touch Van Gogh absorbed from the Neo-Impressionists during his Paris stay of 1886–88. The palette of greens, yellows, and cool greys reflects the suburban landscape on the edge of the city. The canvas, dated summer 1887, is held at Tate Modern, London.

title: Self-Portrait
description: A Paris-period self-portrait of 1887 in which Van Gogh applies Neo-Impressionist methods to his own features, building flesh tones and the reddish beard from small, separate dabs of colour against a mottled green-blue ground. The handling reflects the lessons absorbed from Seurat and Signac during his time in the city. The work is held at the Art Institute of Chicago.

title: Sunset over the Sea
description: Crashing surf dominates the foreground under a stormy amber sky, the setting sun glowing orange through heavy cloud on the horizon. Inness painted this energetic marine in 1887 and the canvas is now in the collection of the Brooklyn Museum. The warm, suffused light and loosely worked surface show his characteristic merging of atmospheric luminism with expressive handling.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum ; Photo: Brooklyn Museum, 34.488_SL1.jpg

title: The Antiques Seller by Rudolf Weisse
description: An Orientalist genre interior (1887, oil on panel) by Rudolf Weisse, depicting three figures — two seated or standing buyers in colourful robes and a merchant in a doorway — examining a large brass tray in a richly appointed bazaar setting. Carpets hang on the walls behind, while a rifle, brass lamps, and decorative vessels fill the foreground. The work is characteristic of the meticulous cabinet-picture precision applied to Near Eastern market subjects in late nineteenth-century European painting.

title: The Bath: Woman Scrubbing her Back
description: A nude woman leans forward over a shallow tub, one arm reaching up her back in the act of scrubbing, her face hidden and her weight supported by the rim. The pastel of around 1887, now at the Honolulu Museum of Art, belongs to the bather series Degas pursued through the late 1880s, presenting the toilette as an unselfconscious physical act with no acknowledged observer.
credit: Honolulu Museum of Art

title: The moon through a crumbling window
description: Yoshitoshi depicts the Zen patriarch Bodhidharma wrapped in a red robe, seated on rocks beneath a full moon amid autumn foliage, his fierce gaze fixed outward. Published in 1887 as part of the series One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, the woodblock print exemplifies Yoshitoshi's expressive naturalistic shading and is one of the defining works of late-nineteenth-century Japanese printmaking.
credit: en.wikipedia; [1]

title: The Wailing Wall by Bauernfeind
description: Worshippers in prayer shawls stand and kneel before the monumental ashlar courses of the Western Wall, Jerusalem, the wall's towering face dominating the composition. Gustav Bauernfeind painted this Orientalist scene in 1887, capturing the site with the meticulous attention to stonework and devotional atmosphere for which he was known.

title: 'Plage de Juan-les-Pins' by Claude Monet
description: From Monet's Antibes campaign on the Côte d'Azur, the canvas dissolves pines, sea and Alps into a high-keyed Mediterranean palette of pinks, mauves and turquoise. The artist complained the southern light was too bright to paint, yet returned with dozens of these luminous beach studies.
credit: Dickinson Gallery, London and New York

title: « Menshikov in Berezovo» by Wassilij Iwanowitsch Surikov
description: The disgraced Prince Alexander Menshikov sits hunched in a low wooden izba with his three children in Siberian exile, the ceiling pressing down on his bulk. Surikov finished the canvas in 1883, not 1888, and Pavel Tretyakov bought it from the eleventh Peredvizhniki exhibition for the gallery in Moscow, where the brooding interior still hangs.
credit: Vasily Surikov

title: 1280px-Vincent van Gogh - The Postman
description: One of several portraits Van Gogh painted of Joseph Roulin, the postal employee he befriended in Arles. Roulin appears bust-length in his blue, gilt-buttoned uniform and "POSTES" cap, his long forked beard set off against a green ground patterned with swirling blossoms. Oil on canvas, painted in 1888; now in the Barnes Foundation, Philadelphia.

title: 2560px-The Langlois Bridge at Arles - My Dream
englishTitle: The Langlois Bridge at Arles - My Dream
description: The Langlois drawbridge spans the canal south of Arles, a lone woman with a parasol crossing as a small boat sits by the bank below and a pair of dark cypresses rise behind. Van Gogh painted the bridge repeatedly in spring 1888, drawn to its echo of the Dutch canals of his youth. This oil on canvas, catalogued F570, is now in the Wallraf-Richartz Museum, Cologne.

title: 2560px-Vincent van Gogh - Vissersboten op het strand van Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer
englishTitle: Fishing Boats on the Beach at Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer
description: Beached fishing smacks on the Mediterranean sand at Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, their masts and rigging picked out in clean primary colour. Made on a five-day excursion from Arles in June 1888, the picture marks Van Gogh's first encounter with the sea in the South of France.

title: Antibes
description: A view across the Mediterranean toward the snow-capped Alps, made during Monet's four-month campaign on the Côte d'Azur in early 1888. The pink and turquoise palette he developed here pushed his colour further than ever, anticipating the serial canvases of the 1890s.
credit: UntitledMag [1]

title: Antibes Seen from La Salis
description: A tall tree leans across the foreground while the old town of Antibes gleams white across the bay, dissolving into a haze of pink and blue Mediterranean light. Monet painted several views from the gardens of La Salis during his stay on the Riviera in early 1888, of which this is one. The painting belongs to the Toledo Museum of Art.

title: Die Brücke von Trinquetaille
description: The iron lifting bridge at Trinquetaille on the Rhône at Arles, painted with a tilted, plunging perspective down its broad stone steps. Cool blues and grays mark a deliberate departure from the high-keyed yellow palette of the artist's earlier Arles canvases.

title: Field with flowers near Arles
description: A field near Arles with a dense foreground of blue and purple irises, beyond which a broad yellow expanse of grass and crops stretches toward a line of trees and the rooftops of the town. Van Gogh painted this view in 1888, one of several canvases he made in and around Arles celebrating the intense colour of Provence in spring. The work is held at the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.

title: Field with Poppies
description: A green field near Arles scattered with red poppies, farm buildings with orange rooftiles visible across the middle distance. Van Gogh rendered grasses and blossoms in energetic, varied strokes of saturated red and green against a pale sky. Painted in 1888 and now in the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam, it belongs to his prolific series of Provençal landscapes made during his time in the south of France.
credit: Van Gogh Museum

title: Girl in the Sunlight
description: Maria Simonovich, Serov's cousin, sits leaning against a large tree at Domotkanovo, dappled summer light falling across her white blouse and dark skirt. Painted in 1888 and acquired by the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow, the portrait is paired with Girl with Peaches as the second of the two early canvases that established Serov's reputation as a colourist.

title: Grainstacks
description: Two grainstacks rise from a frost-covered field outside Giverny, their conical forms bathed in a pale rose and golden light that suffuses the entire composition. Painted between 1888 and 1889 and held at the Hill-Stead Museum, the work belongs to the Grainstacks group with which Monet pursued the serial study of a single motif across changing light conditions.

title: Green and Silver: Beaulieu
description: A small landscape from Whistler's late period, showing a broad green meadow with a lone figure in the middle distance and a low skyline of trees and rooftops beyond. Titled Green and Silver: Beaulieu, 1888, the work was painted during a French sojourn and is now in the Freer Gallery of Art, Washington. The title signals Whistler's characteristic insistence on colour harmony as the true subject of a picture.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme - Tiger on the Watch
description: A tiger sits alertly on a sandy desert ridge, turning its head toward a distant column of figures — soldiers or a caravan — winding across the plain below. Gérôme renders the animal with meticulous anatomical care, setting its warm stripes against the pale expanse of dunes and a clear desert sky. Completed in 1888, the work is now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.

title: Le Garçon au gilet rouge
description: Oil painting by Paul Cézanne created between 1888 and 1890. The work depicts a young boy wearing a distinctive red waistcoat in three-quarter view. This iconic portrait exemplifies Cézanne's mastery of form and color, combining careful anatomical structure with his characteristic approach to pictorial composition.

title: Les Alyscamps
description: Les Alyscamps depicts the ancient Roman burial ground at Arles: a canal path edged by tall flame-orange and green trees recedes toward a domed tower, with three dark-cloaked figures walking in the middle distance. Gauguin painted this during his stay with Van Gogh in autumn 1888, flattening the composition into saturated bands of colour. The canvas is held in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

title: Les Alyscamps
description: The Roman necropolis at Arles, lined with poplars turning autumn yellow, is rendered with thick impasto and a steeply receding perspective. The work belongs to a small series painted alongside Gauguin during their fraught Arles collaboration.

title: Les Meules à Giverny
description: Two grainstacks stand in the fields around Giverny under a warm sunset sky, their bulky forms dissolving into ambient orange and golden light. Painted between 1888 and 1889 and now in the Museum of Modern Art, Saitama, this work prefigures the rigorous serial investigation of the same motif Monet would undertake in his celebrated 1890–91 series.

title: Monet w1200
description: One of Monet's paintings of the meadows around his home at Giverny, recording the light of early morning across the fields in 1888. Wildenstein 1200; held in a private collection.

title: Mother of Pearl and Silver: The Andalusian
description: A standing female figure rendered in the pale, harmonised tones the title evokes, in keeping with Whistler's musical naming and his pursuit of arrangement over narrative. The subject becomes a vehicle for tonal close-keying rather than character study.

title: Open Air Breakfast
description: Chase's family takes breakfast in a leafy Brooklyn yard, the white tablecloth and hammock catching dappled sun. Loose brushwork and a bright outdoor palette align the scene with American Impressionism's domestic, garden-side mode.

title: Seascape near Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer
description: A seascape made during the artist's brief stay at the Mediterranean fishing village of Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, with small fishing boats riding choppy water under a wind-driven sky. Short, stabbing strokes register the swell, while patches of pure colour mark sails and reflected light.

title: Self-Portrait with Portrait of Émile Bernard
description: Gauguin paints himself in the role of Hugo's outlaw Jean Valjean, gaunt-cheeked against a wallpaper of pink flowers, with a small portrait of Émile Bernard pinned behind him. Sent to Vincent van Gogh in Arles in autumn 1888 as part of the exchange of self-portraits among the Pont-Aven group, the canvas now belongs to the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam.

title: Starry Night Over the Rhône
description: Gaslamps along the Arles quay double in the dark water of the Rhône while the Great Bear hangs overhead. A small couple strolls in the foreground, anchoring Van Gogh's nocturne to the human scale of the river town.

title: Still Life: Vase with Twelve Sunflowers
description: Twelve sunflowers in a cream earthenware vase, set against a pale blue-grey ground and resting on a yellow surface, painted at Arles in August 1888. Van Gogh made this canvas as decoration for the bedroom he was preparing for Gauguin's visit, and the work is among the most celebrated of the series. The vase bears his signature 'Vincent' in yellow paint.

title: Stilleben mit Früchtekorb
description: A kitchen table crowded with a fruit basket, pots and a folded cloth, the tabletop tipped sharply toward the viewer. Oil on canvas worked between 1888 and 1890, now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris. Cézanne tilts the planes and crops the cloth at the lower edge to make geometric form, not accurate space, the subject.

title: Sunset at Montmajour
description: Painted on the rocky outcrop near Arles, the work surveys the plain of La Crau through a foreground of scrub oak and limestone, the abbey ruins behind. Long doubted as authentic, it was reattributed in 2013 on the basis of letters, pigments, and the painter's own catalogue.
credit: twitter.com; nrc.nl , image

title: The Fort of Antibes
description: The old fortifications of Antibes seen across the bay, from Monet's 1888 Riviera campaign. The southern light pushed his palette toward saturated pinks, turquoises and ochres, the Mediterranean treated as a high-keyed counterpart to his northern coasts.
credit: www.mfa.org

title: The harvest
description: A panoramic view of the harvest on the plain of La Crau outside Arles, with stacked sheaves, a blue cart, and distant farm buildings under a Provençal sky. Van Gogh structures the composition with receding parallel bands of yellow stubble, layering complementary blues and oranges to register the heat of high summer.

title: The Hermit
description: An aged ascetic pads along the shore of a still northern lake, drawing the eye into Nesterov's signature blend of Orthodox spirituality and quiet Russian landscape. Painted at the outset of his religious phase, the work was acquired by Pavel Tretyakov and now hangs in his Moscow gallery.

title: The Night Cafe
description: Marie Ginoux sits at a marble café table in Arles with a green absinthe glass and a soda siphon, while a billiard table and a row of slumped drinkers fill the back of the room. Painted in early November 1888 during Gauguin's two months sharing the Yellow House with Van Gogh, the canvas was acquired by the Pushkin Museum in Moscow from the Shchukin collection.

title: The Painter on His Way to Work
description: A self-portrait of the painter trudging to a motif under the Provençal sun, easel and canvases on his back. The picture, formerly in the Kaiser-Friedrich-Museum in Magdeburg, was lost during the Second World War and survives only in reproduction.
credit: Vincent van Gogh: In der Provence , R.Piper & Co, Verlag, München 1977, ISBN 3492110703

title: The Seine at La Grande Jatte
description: Painted in 1888 at the same stretch of the Seine that had inspired his monumental Grande Jatte, this canvas shows the river's surface dissolved into patiently calibrated dots of complementary colour, with sailboats and a leaning tree composing the scene. Now in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, it demonstrates the optical mixing at the heart of Seurat's divisionist method applied to an intimate, familiar location.

provenance.collection: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

title: The Sower
credit: .mw-parser-output .ubx-floatdefault[dir="ltr"],.mw-parser-output .ubx-floatopposite[dir="rtl"],.mw-parser-output .ubx-floatleft{float:left}.mw-parser-output .ubx-floatdefault[dir="rtl"],.mw-parser-output .ubx-floatopposite[dir="ltr"],.mw-parser-output .ubx-floatright{float:right}.mw-parser-output .ubx-floatnone{float:none} This user has uploaded 202 quality images to Wikimedia Commons . Self-portrait - Vincent van Gogh

title: The Surgeon Evgueni Vasilievich Pavlov in the Operating Theater
description: A documentary group composition showing the surgeon Evgeny Pavlov operating in a St Petersburg theatre, witnessed by gowned colleagues. Repin treats the modern clinic as a secular history piece, marshalling sharp tonal contrasts and a tightly bracketed perspective around the patient.

title: The Swineherd
description: A swineherd stands in the foreground of a hilly Breton landscape above a village, a pair of pale yellow pigs grazing nearby and a horse at left. Painted at Pont-Aven in 1888, the canvas shows Gauguin moving from broken Impressionist touch toward broad, simplified zones of colour. The work is held in the Norton Simon collection.

title: Van Gogh -Die Brücke von Langlois in Arles mit Wäscherinnen
englishTitle: The Langlois Bridge at Arles with Women Washing
description: Washerwomen kneel along the canal bank as a horse-cart crosses the wooden drawbridge at Arles. Van Gogh returned to the Pont de Langlois several times in 1888, drawn to its clean geometry and Provençal light reminiscent of Japanese prints.

title: Vincent van Gogh
englishTitle: Cafe Terrace at Night (Place du Forum), Arles
description: A nocturnal view of a yellow-awninged café on the Place du Forum in Arles, with cobblestones receding under a sky of large stars. Van Gogh painted it without using black, building the night entirely from saturated yellows, blues and greens — an early experiment in his ambition to render the south at night in pure colour.

title: Vision After the Sermon
description: Breton women in white coiffes lean forward in prayer, their vision of Jacob wrestling the angel materialising across a vermilion field divided by an apple tree. Painted at Pont-Aven in 1888 and now in the National Galleries of Scotland, the canvas is the breakthrough work in which Gauguin abandoned naturalistic colour for symbolic, cloisonné planes outlined in dark blue.
credit: https://www.thetimes.com/magazines/culture-magazine/article/wild-thing-life-paul-gauguin-sue-prideaux-tk55c57wl; http://www.nationalgalleries.org

title: Walking on Water
description: Christ, suffused in a luminous golden halo, walks above a dark and turbulent sea while huddled figures crouch on rocks in the foreground. Aivazovsky painted this biblical scene in 1888, weaving his career-long mastery of storm-lit marine subjects into a devotional composition he returned to several times across his career.

title: Портрет С. П. Кувшинниковой. 1888
description: Portrait of Sofia Petrovna Kuvshinnikova painted by Russian Realist master Isaac Levitan. Oil on canvas, executed in 1888. Kuvshinnikova was a contemporary of the artist and notable figure in Russian cultural circles.

title: 1280px-Cypresses
description: A study of tall cypress trees by Vincent van Gogh, painted in 1889 during his time in southern France. The work exemplifies his distinctive swirling brushwork and vibrant palette in capturing the vertical forms and landscape. Part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art collection.

title: 1280px-De schovenbindster
description: Painted at the asylum in Saint-Rémy after a Millet print, part of Van Gogh's series translating the older peasant painter into his own thick, rhythmic brushwork. The stooping woman and golden sheaves are reworked in the saturated yellows and ultramarines of his final Provençal year, now in the Van Gogh Museum.

title: 2560px-Van Gogh The Olive Trees
englishTitle: Olive Trees with the Alpilles in the Background
description: Gnarled olives churn in the foreground while the limestone Alpilles rise behind under a clouded sky, painted from the grounds of Saint-Paul asylum. Now at MoMA, it belongs to the group of about fifteen olive-grove canvases Van Gogh devoted to the trees during his Saint-Rémy year.

title: An Out-of-Doors Study
description: The painter Paul Helleu sketches outdoors beside his wife Alice, the canoe and grass rendered in broken Impressionist touch. Sargent painted the work at Fladbury during a summer of plein-air experiment under Monet's influence. The flushed greens and unfinished edges show him at his most explicitly Impressionist.

title: Cypresses with two female figures
description: Two small figures stand beneath the flame-like silhouette of cypresses, trees the artist described as obsessing him for their dark sculptural force. The composition belongs to the Saint-Rémy cypress group, in which the species becomes a vehicle for swirling, vertical brushwork.

title: Enclosed Field with Rising Sun
description: A walled wheatfield is shown at sunrise, the sun cresting low above distant hills while curling brushstrokes animate the grain. Painted from the window of his room at the asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, it is one of a sustained series in which the same enclosed field is observed across seasons and times of day.

title: Eugen von Blaas - The Spider and the Fly - 1889
description: A smiling young woman leans against a column as a working man — carrying a large bundle of straw and a wicker basket on his back — bends close to whisper something to her. Copper vessels lie at her feet on the cobblestones. De Blaas constructs a knowing courtship scene from working-class Venetian street life, rendered with his characteristic academic precision. The canvas is signed and dated 1889.

title: Evening Hour
description: A lone farm labourer stands at the edge of a ploughed field at dusk, the golden sky deepening behind him; a plough and scattered tools lie at his feet. Painted at Saint-Rémy in November 1889 as a free copy after Millet's Evening Hour, Van Gogh replaces Millet's tonal restraint with dense swirling strokes of amber and grey-green. The picture is now in the Menard Art Museum, Japan.

title: Evening landscape at moonrise - Van Gogh
description: A reaped wheat field with stacked sheaves lies under a swollen orange moon rising from behind the hills of the Alpilles. Van Gogh painted the canvas, also known as Landscape with Wheat Sheaves and Rising Moon, in the summer of 1889, working from the walled field he could see from his room at the asylum of Saint-Paul-de-Mausole in Saint-Rémy. It is held by the Kröller-Müller Museum in Otterlo.

title: Faded Laurels
description: An elderly, laurel-crowned nobleman sits apart on stone steps while a lively medieval court celebration unfolds behind him, his isolation conveying the melancholy of faded dignity. Edmund Blair Leighton, working in his characteristically precise late-Victorian academic style, frames the chivalric subject with antiquarian attention to costume and architecture, 1889.
credit: Bukowskis – Arts & Business, Important Spring Sale 649, 14 June 2023, lot 809

title: Garçon au gilet rouge
description: The Italian model Michelangelo di Rosa in a red waistcoat, one of several studies Cézanne made of the boy around 1889 to 1890. This watercolour version, in the Barnes Foundation, Philadelphia, leaves the paper bare in places between washes. Cézanne used the repeated pose to test the figure against surrounding space.

title: Ivan Zarevitch on the grey Wolf
description: Prince Ivan rides the grey wolf through a moonlit forest, the captured tsarevna Yelena cradled in his arms among gnarled oaks and a flowering apple tree. Painted in 1889 from the Russian folktale of Ivan Tsarevich and the Grey Wolf, the canvas hangs in the Tretyakov Gallery and helped Vasnetsov define the bylina-painting genre at the heart of Russian national Romanticism.
credit: http://www.staratel.com/pictures/ruspaint/113.htm http://www.artlib.ru/index.php?id=11&idp=0&fp=2&uid=1671&iid=16272&idg=0&user_serie=0 http://lj.rossia.org/users/john_petrov/282710.html?mode=reply

title: Landscape from Saint-Rémy
description: A view of the wheat fields and olive groves surrounding the asylum at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, with the Alpilles ridges rising in the distance. Curling, parallel brushstrokes animate the soil, foliage, and sky alike, dissolving the topography into a continuous vibrating surface.

title: Les deux perles
description: A pale-skinned nude woman reclines on a large shell-like rock at the shoreline while a dark-skinned standing male nude leans over her against an open seascape with a distant sailboat. Fernand Le Quesne's 1889 academic painting, exhibited in the orbit of the Paris Salon, pairs the two nude figures in a sun-lit coastal setting, the title casting their contrasting forms as twin pearls.

title: Lion tentant de saisir un papillon
description: A lion lies recumbent in a rocky, cave-like interior, its jaws open wide toward a tiny butterfly hovering before it. Gérôme renders the animal with the precise anatomical finish of his academic training, turning the predator's power into a moment of comic disproportion; the canvas is held at the Carnegie Museum of Art.

title: Peach Trees in Blossom
description: Peach trees in full blossom on the plain of La Crau near Arles, their white and pale-pink flowers set against the wide Provençal plain with farmhouses and mountains in the distance, painted in April 1889. The composition is characteristic of Van Gogh's Arles period, with a mosaic of short brushstrokes building the flowering branches and the earth below. The work is held at the Courtauld Gallery, London.
credit: The Courtauld Institute of Art

title: Pietà
description: Oil painting created by Vincent van Gogh in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence in 1889 as part of his series copying Old Master works. The composition depicts the Pietà scene and reflects Van Gogh's deep engagement with Renaissance tradition. Originally housed in the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam (catalog s0168V1962).

title: Portrait of general and statesman Mikhail Ivanovich Dragomirov
description: A bust-length state portrait of the Russian general and military theorist, hero of the crossing of the Danube in 1877. Repin works in his vigorous realist manner, building the weathered face and braided uniform from loaded, broken strokes.

title: Self-portrait
description: A three-quarter self-portrait painted at the Saint-Rémy asylum in 1889, the face and jacket modelled in cool blue-greens against a swirling turquoise ground. The artist holds himself composed and direct-eyed, the restless spiral brushwork of the background offsetting the stillness of the figure. The work is held at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

title: Self-Portrait with Halo
description: Gauguin stares out from a flat red and yellow ground, a green snake coiling in one hand, three ripe apples floating beside his head and a thin golden halo above. Painted on a cupboard door at the Le Pouldu inn in 1889 and now at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the picture casts the artist as a sardonic Eden serpent and Christian saint at once.

title: Shurygin Levitan 1889
description: A bust-length portrait of the landscape painter Isaac Levitan, shown with dark curly hair and a beard, wearing a blue painter's blouse with a white ruffled collar. Painted by Alexander Shurygin in 1889, the work dates to the years when Levitan was consolidating his reputation in Moscow.

title: Still Life with Head-Shaped Vase and Japanese Woodcut
description: This 1889 still life pairs two ceramic vessels — a pale mask-faced pot and a smaller head-shaped jug, both filled with cut flowers — on a pink surface before a yellow wall hung with a Japanese woodcut of a white-faced figure. Gauguin combined his interest in ceramic self-portraiture with the ukiyo-e prints circulating among the Paris avant-garde. The canvas is titled Still Life with Head-Shaped Vase and Japanese Woodcut.

title: The bedroom
description: A view of the artist's own bedroom in the Yellow House at Arles, repeated in a slightly later replica painted at Saint-Rémy. Tilted floor, paired chairs, and framed prints are arranged in flat planes of colour intended, in his words, to suggest absolute rest.

title: The Reaper
description: A solitary peasant cutting grain in a sun-blanched field, a subject the artist linked in letters to Millet and to thoughts of mortality. The wheat is built from sweeping yellow strokes that engulf the figure, the reaper's body almost dissolving into the matter he harvests.
credit: Christie's , LotFinder: entry 6089477 (sale 14239, lot 6, London, 27 June 2017)

title: The Starry Night
description: A cypress flames upward through a sky of churning spirals above a sleeping Provençal village. Painted from memory at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy, the canvas welds observation, symbol and rhythmic impasto.

title: Two farmers digging over
description: Two stooped laborers turning the earth, a subject the artist returned to throughout his career as homage to Millet. The Saint-Rémy treatment swaps the dark Dutch tonalities of his earlier peasant scenes for a brighter, more rhythmic handling of soil and sky.

title: Van Gogh
description: Vincent van Gogh's oil painting depicting an olive grove in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, created during his stay at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum. The work exemplifies his distinctive post-impressionist style with bold brushstrokes and vibrant color treatment of the Provençal landscape.

title: Van Gogh - Die Schäferin
description: A peasant woman sits resting in a golden field, holding a long shepherd's crook, her blue shawl and white bonnet standing out against a turbulent sky. Painted in November 1889 at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy, the work is Van Gogh's free interpretation of Millet's celebrated shepherdess, transposing the original into his own vivid blues, ochres, and greens. It is now in the Tel Aviv Museum of Art.

title: Van Gogh - Grünes Weizenfeld
description: A Provençal field rendered in surging diagonal brushstrokes, the unripe wheat treated as a tapestry of green and blue rhythms. Painted at Saint-Rémy, the canvas demonstrates the artist's habit of converting agricultural labor's quiet subjects into studies of pictorial energy.

title: Van Gogh - Grünes Weizenfeld1
description: A lush green wheat field fills the foreground, its dense, swirling stems rendered in short curved strokes of blue-green and yellow-green, while a turbulent sky of pale blue and white clouds sweeps overhead. Van Gogh painted this close-cropped view of a wheat field in 1889, most likely during his residence at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence. It is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Vision of Youth Bartholomew
description: The young Bartholomew, future St Sergius of Radonezh, encounters a black-clad monk beneath a slender oak in a hushed Russian landscape. Nesterov's debut religious canvas joins thin, lyrical brushwork with a pale northern palette, founding the devout pastoral mode he would pursue across his career.

title: Wheat Field with Cypresses
englishTitle: Wheat Field with Cypresses (Metropolitan Museum, June 1889)
description: A wheat field at Saint-Rémy with twisting cypresses on the right and the Alpilles range behind, the sky churning with rolled, scroll-like clouds. The composition belongs to a small group of variants the artist regarded as among his strongest summer landscapes.

title: Wheat Field with Reaper and Sun
description: A solitary reaper bends amid blazing yellow stalks beneath a swollen sun. Painted from Van Gogh's window at the Saint-Paul asylum in Saint-Remy, the scene was for him an emblem of human labour and mortality bound to nature's cycles.
credit: Van Gogh Worldwide

title: Wheatfield with a reaper
description: A walled wheat field at Saint-Rémy with a single reaper at work in the high sun, the grain rendered as a near-uniform sheet of yellow. The artist described the figure as an image of humanity being mown down like the wheat, an idea that recurs across the late Provençal landscapes.

title: Zaandam2
description: Dutch windmills line a low horizon while flat water carries their reflections under a wide sky. The etching belongs to Whistler's later European tours, where his economical needlework and selective wiping of the plate convert a mundane port into a tonal study close in spirit to his Nocturnes.
credit: Library off Congress [1]

title: Волна
description: Enormous grey-green waves tower over a stricken sailing ship in the centre of the canvas, its masts and red flag still visible as it is engulfed by the storm, while a lifeboat crowded with survivors struggles in the churning foreground. Aivazovsky painted this large and turbulent seascape in 1889, signing it in the lower right in his characteristic manner. The scale of the waves against the tiny vessel is a hallmark of the Russian marine painter's Romantic drama.

title: Левитан После дождя
description: Study for a painting by Russian Romantic landscape artist Isaac Levitan. The work depicts the village of Plyos on the Volga River following a rainfall, exemplifying the artist's signature atmospheric naturalism and subtle treatment of light and moisture in the landscape.

title: 2560px-Vincent van Gogh - House at Auvers
