description: A field of green wheat and tall flowering grasses fills the foreground, with a white house half-hidden behind a low wall and dark trees on the rise beyond. Van Gogh painted it in 1890 at Auvers-sur-Oise, where he spent his last weeks under the care of Dr Paul Gachet. The canvas now belongs to The Phillips Collection, Washington.

title: 2560px-Vincent van Gogh - The siesta
description: Two harvesters nap in the shade of a haystack at noon, freely copied from a Millet print Van Gogh kept in his Saint-Rémy studio. He translated Millet's grey original into a pairing of complementary blue shadows and golden yellow stubble.

title: 2560px-Vincent van Gogh - Vineyards at Auvers
description: Rows of vines descend the slope toward the white walls and orange-tiled roofs of Auvers-sur-Oise, with wooded hills closing the horizon and red blossoms edging the foreground. Painted in June 1890, weeks before Van Gogh's death, the canvas is now in the Saint Louis Art Museum.

title: A Quiet Monastery
description: A small monastery rises above a bend in a forested river at evening, its golden domes reflecting in the still water as a plank footbridge leads toward the far shore. Isaac Levitan painted this canvas in 1890, and it is now held at the Tretyakov Gallery; the composition draws on sketches made near the Volga and exemplifies his lyrical approach to the Russian landscape.
credit: Государственная Третьяковская галерея

title: A Street Scene
description: A bustling Damascus thoroughfare rendered with the German Orientalist's exacting eye for tilework, lattice and crowd. Bauernfeind, trained as an architect, treated the city's facades almost archaeologically, balancing photographic detail with the strong overhead light of the Levant.

title: Adam and Eve or Paradise Lost
description: A nude woman with auburn hair stands with her back to the viewer near a central tree, while a large coiling serpent lies at the base and a pair of figures (Adam and Eve) walk away to the right. Painted around 1890, the canvas is titled Adam and Eve or Paradise Lost and is held at the Yale University Art Gallery.
credit: Yale University Art Gallery

title: At Eternity's Gate - Vincent Van Gogh
description: An old man sits on a plain chair, fists pressed to his eyes in a posture of complete despair. Van Gogh painted the canvas at Saint-Rémy in early May 1890, returning in oil to a lithograph he had made in The Hague in 1882 of the same model, the almshouse pensioner Adrianus Jacobus Zuyderland. It is in the Kröller-Müller Museum, Otterlo.

title: Baigneurs
description: A group of male nudes along a riverbank, some standing and some reclining, set into an open landscape. Oil on canvas of about 1890, part of the bather series Cézanne pursued from the 1870s onward, now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris. The figures are built to structure the space rather than to display the flesh.

title: Bank of the Oise at Auvers
Cesar Cui
description: Repin's portrait of the composer and music critic César Cui, a member of The Mighty Handful, shows the sitter seated in a cane-backed chair, wearing a grey military coat with a red lining. The direct gaze, spectacles, and loose painterly brushwork are characteristic of Repin's intimate portraits of Russian cultural figures, painted in 1890.

title: Flowering meadow with trees and dandelions - Vincent Van Gogh
description: Gnarled pine trunks rise from a meadow thick with long grass and dandelions, some in yellow bloom and some gone to seed, in the garden of the Saint-Paul asylum at Saint-Rémy. Van Gogh painted it in the spring of 1890, during his final weeks there, cropping the view to the ground plane so the flowering grass fills the canvas. Kröller-Müller Museum, Otterlo.

title: Gerome venus
description: Venus emerges from the sea trailing the morning star, her body lit with the pale, enamel finish Gérôme cultivated late in life. The composition revisits the Anadyomene tradition while flirting with the polychrome sculpture project that preoccupied his final decades.

title: Girl in a Japanese Costume
description: A young woman is shown bust-length wearing a pale blue kimono decorated with red and gold botanical motifs and an orange obi sash, her dark hair loosely arranged. Chase's fluid brushwork focuses attention on the sitter's composed gaze and the decorative surface of the Japanese garment. Painted around 1890, the work is held at the Brooklyn Museum and reflects the Aesthetic-movement taste for Japonisme in American studios of the period.

title: Girl in White
description: A young woman in a white dress and broad yellow hat stands before a green wheatfield scattered with orange-red poppies, her hands empty at her sides. Painted at Auvers-sur-Oise in 1890 in the last weeks of Van Gogh's life, the figure is built up in ribbed parallel touches of green, gold, and white; the work is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art .

title: Glen Birnam
description: A lone figure walks away along a snow-dusted road lined with bare birch trees in the Perthshire glen near Birnam, the distant hills visible through the winter canopy. Painted in 1890, the work is characteristic of Millais's late Highland landscapes, rendered with the freer, broader brushwork of his maturity rather than the botanical precision of his Pre-Raphaelite youth.

title: Graystaks I
description: A single grainstack rises against a warm, luminous sky in a field near Giverny — one of the celebrated series of some twenty-five canvases Monet made between 1890 and 1891, tracking the same motif through different times of day and seasons. The work exemplifies his serial method at its most concentrated and is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Guanyin riding the dragon
description: The Buddhist bodhisattva of compassion rides a coiling dragon through cloudbanks, the figure modelled with the volumetric solidity of European academic painting. A Munich-trained pioneer of yōga (Western-style oil painting), Harada provoked debate by giving a Japanese religious subject the visual language of Counter-Reformation altarpieces.

provenance.collection: The National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo
provenance.location: The National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo

title: Houses at Auvers / Houses in Auvers
description: A cluster of village rooftops in Auvers-sur-Oise, painted during the artist's final months in the small town north of Paris. Thatched and tiled roofs press together in interlocking diagonals, the brushwork rhythmic and ribbon-like across walls, foliage, and a streaked summer sky.

title: Im warmen Land
description: A woman in dark dress and white head-covering reclines in a chair on a sunlit terrace, propped on pillows against a garden setting of oleander and green hills. Yaroshenko painted the work in 1890, titling it Im warmen Land (In a Warm Land). The composition conveys convalescent quietude, characteristic of the artist's empathetic approach to his subjects.

title: Irises
description: A bouquet of cut irises arranged in a white vase, their violet-blue petals built from short, kinetic strokes against a pale cream ground. Van Gogh painted this still life in 1890, and the work is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (accession number 58.187).
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (accession number 58.187)

title: Irises
description: A still life of irises in a vase against a saturated yellow ground, executed at Saint-Rémy. Stems curve upward in calligraphic lines while the petals are massed in cool violets and blues, an overt complementary pairing that the artist used repeatedly during his late flower studies.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme
description: The Cypriot sculptor embraces his ivory creation as she turns from cold stone to warm flesh from the hips upward. Gérôme also modelled the subject in polychrome sculpture in these years; the painting plays on his own dual practice as painter and sculptor.

title: Landscape with a Carriage and a Train
description: A wide landscape with a horse-drawn carriage on a country road and a steam train cutting across the middle distance, painted at Auvers in June 1890. Green fields, farm buildings, and a row of poplars fill the composition, while the train's smoke signals the encroachment of modern transport on the rural plain. The work is held at the Pushkin Museum of Fine Arts, Moscow.
credit: The Museum of Modern Western Art (NWM)

title: Les Vessenots à Auvers
description: A view of the hamlet of Vessenots near Auvers-sur-Oise, with thatched and tiled cottages set among meadows bright with yellow wildflowers, painted in May 1890. The surface is densely worked in greens and yellows, the buildings serving as compact accents within the expansive landscape. The work is held at the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.

title: Maternité
description: A mother, her shoulders draped in a rosy wrap, gazes down at the infant she holds against her in close, quiet intimacy. Cassatt returned repeatedly to the maternité theme after 1880, treating the secular subject with a formal tenderness recalling Renaissance Madonnas while maintaining a bright, contemporary palette.

title: Monet w1245
description: A spring landscape of the meadows at Giverny painted in 1890, part of Monet's sustained study of the fields around his home under changing seasons. Wildenstein 1245; held in a private collection.

title: Portrait of Mrs. Thomas Lincoln Manson Jr
description: The sitter is shown three-quarter length, seated on a settee against a dark ground, her arms resting easily to either side. Sargent captures her dark gown and confident bearing with the fluid, assured brushwork of his American portrait practice. The work is dated 1890.

title: Prisoners Exercising
description: Convicts circling a stone yard under guard, copied at Saint-Rémy after a print by Gustave Doré of Newgate Prison. The artist's choice of source from his asylum bed gives the trudging round of figures a transparent autobiographical charge.

title: Road with Cypress and Star
description: A country road at twilight with two figures, a horse-drawn cart, a flame-like cypress, and a crescent moon and evening star above. The composition compresses earth and sky into spiraling, rhythmic strokes; it was among the last canvases finished at Saint-Rémy before the move north.

title: Roses
description: A dense bouquet of white roses fills a terracotta vase against a pale green ground, painted at the asylum of Saint-Rémy in 1890, weeks before Van Gogh left for Auvers. The swirling impasto and rhythmic brushstrokes animate what might otherwise be a quiet still-life, turning it into a study in vitality. Now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art

title: Solitude
description: A single draped woman seated on a rock above still water in a deep mountain hollow. Oil on canvas painted around 1890; Leighton described the setting as a place worn so deep that absolute silence holds. The picture is now in the Maryhill Museum of Art, Washington State.

title: Spring in Giverny
description: Tall trees in early spring foliage stand above a flower-dotted meadow at Giverny, their pink-tinged branches and fresh greenery rendered in Monet's characteristic broken touches. Painted in 1890, the work captures the seasonal awakening of the Giverny grounds that Monet had cultivated since settling there in 1883.

title: Sunlight on the Coast
description: Surf crashes against dark rocky ledges under a storm-lit sky, with a distant vessel barely visible on the horizon. No human figure appears; Homer reduces the scene to an elemental confrontation of wave, rock, and atmosphere. Painted in 1890, the work belongs to his Prouts Neck marine series and is held at the Toledo Museum of Art.

title: The Bath of Psyche
description: Psyche stands nude beside a reflecting pool, drawing aside a length of drapery as she prepares to bathe, framed by two fluted columns. Leighton exhibited the oil at the Royal Academy in 1890; it was bought under the Chantrey Bequest and passed to the Tate. The narrow vertical format echoes a marble caryatid, the figure's weight set on one leg in contrapposto.

title: The Church at Auvers
description: The medieval parish church of Auvers seen from the apse, its stonework leaning under a deep cobalt sky split by branching lanes. The masonry and lead roofs are worked in thick, undulating strokes that twist the Gothic structure into a single restless form.

title: The Gate Of The Great Umayyad Mosque
description: Viewed through the massive carved doorway of the Great Umayyad Mosque, the sunlit courtyard beyond is occupied by a handful of figures while others rest in the doorway's shade, shoes arranged on the cobbled threshold. Bauernfeind's architectural training is evident in the meticulous rendering of polychrome marble inlay, inscribed frieze, and ornamental stonework that frame the scene, painted in Damascus around 1890.

title: Wheat Fields after the Rain
description: Furrowed wheat fields on the plain of Auvers, the soil glistening after a storm, painted in the final weeks of Van Gogh's life. The high horizon, ribbon-like brushwork, and rain-washed greens belong to the productive Auvers months that ended in July 1890.
credit: Photo I took of Vincent Van Goghs' Wheat Fields after the Rain (The Plain of Auvers) from 1890. Carnegie Museum of Art

title: Wheatfield under thunderclouds
description: A double-square panorama of a wheat field at Auvers under a vast, lowering blue-grey sky that fills most of the canvas, painted during the artist's final weeks in July 1890. The horizon is placed low, allowing the gathering storm clouds to dominate while the green-yellow grain stretches across the entire width below. The work's wide format matches a small group of panoramic canvases Van Gogh made in the Auvers fields that summer.

title: Wheatfield with crows
description: A double-square panorama of a wheat field crossed by three diverging paths, with a flock of black crows lifting against a turbulent blue sky. Painted in the Auvers fields shortly before the artist's death, the work compresses storm, harvest, and flight into a single agitated surface.

title: Крещение Руси
description: Viktor Vasnetsov's grand historical oil painting depicting the moment of the Christianization of Kievan Rus in 988 CE. The massive composition (214 × 187 cm) features multitudes gathered at a river for baptism, rendered in Vasnetsov's signature late-19th-century Romantic-realist style. A seminal work in Russian art celebrating the pivotal religious and cultural transformation.

title: A huntsman and dogs
description: A hunter rests on a felled tree stump on an autumnal hillside, a rifle in hand and a deer carcass with antlers slung across his back, while two hounds flank him against a sky of rolling clouds. Homer sets the scene in a landscape of red-orange foliage and dead timber that speaks to the rougher economy of the wilderness. Painted in 1891, the oil is one of Homer's major late figural works in the realist mode.

title: Duse by Repin
description: A charcoal portrait of the Italian tragedienne Eleonora Duse, capturing the famously expressive actress in a moment of inward concentration. Repin exploits the chalky drag of charcoal on canvas to model her face while leaving the gown in summary, atmospheric strokes.

title: Edge of the Forest
description: Tall dark tree trunks rise through a shadowed forest interior, with a small lone figure visible among them and glimpses of white buildings through the haze beyond. Painted in 1891 and held at the Yale University Art Gallery, the canvas is characteristic of Inness's late tonalist landscapes, in which light and atmosphere dissolve solid forms into muted, unified fields of colour.
credit: Yale University Art Gallery, Yale University, New Haven, Conn.

title: Leo Tolstoy02
description: Tolstoy sits writing at a cluttered desk in the vaulted room at Yasnaya Polyana, dressed in the plain peasant blouse he adopted in his later years. Ilya Repin, the leading Peredvizhniki realist, captured this scene of the writer at work in 1891, the composition inscribed with the location and date in the lower left.

title: Life Study
description: A standing nude rendered with academic precision during Sargent's travels in North Africa, the body modeled in warm earth tones against a neutral ground. The study reflects his sustained interest in the figure outside commissioned portraiture.

title: Madame Cézanne with Green Hat
description: Hortense Fiquet, the painter's wife, sits in three-quarter view wearing a broad green hat, her hands folded in her lap. Oil on canvas of about 1891 to 1892, catalogued BF141 in the Barnes Foundation in Philadelphia. Cézanne built the face and bodice from planes of dull violet, ochre and grey-green laid side by side.

title: Mink Pond
description: A brightly coloured sunfish and a frog face one another across a lily pad in the dark, reflective water of an Adirondack pond, a white water-lily bloom opening to the left. Homer dissolves the boundary between underwater and surface worlds, the whole scene rendered with the precise yet luminous touch he brought to his later nature watercolours. Signed and dated Mink Pond 1891.
credit: Bridgeman Art Library : Object 125082

title: Night at Gurzof
description: A moonlit coastal scene at Gurzuf on the Crimean shore, with a glowing disc of moon laid across the water and dark vessels near the foreground rocks. Aivazovsky painted the marine view in 1891; the canvas later passed through Heritage Auctions in Dallas. The Armenian-Russian painter produced thousands of seascapes from his studio at Feodosia on the Black Sea.
credit: Heritage Auctions, Dallas, November 2008, lot 65005

title: Passage of the Jews through the Red Sea
description: The Israelites crowd the far shore as Moses, white-robed, raises his arm toward the sea closing over Pharaoh's army at the left, horses and spearmen vanishing beneath a great green wave while light breaks through the storm cloud above. Aivazovsky painted the biblical subject in 1891, bringing to it the marine effects of a half-century of seascape painting on the Black Sea coast.
credit: wikipaintings

title: Perseus and Andromeda
description: Andromeda is chained naked to the rocks while the dragon spreads dark wings over her and Perseus dives in from above on the winged horse Pegasus. Leighton painted the oil in 1891; it entered the Walker Art Gallery in Liverpool. The arched composition wraps the monster's body around the upper edge like a canopy.

title: Poplars on the Epte
description: From the Poplars series, painted from a flat-bottomed boat moored in the river Epte near Giverny. The slender trunks form a rhythmic vertical lattice, doubled by reflection, that anticipates the decorative serial logic of the later Rouen Cathedrals.

title: Portrait of Amelia van Buren
description: Amelia Van Buren, a former Eakins pupil at the Pennsylvania Academy, sits sideways in a carved armchair with one hand against her cheek, her gaze fixed past the viewer. Painted around 1891 and now at the Phillips Collection in Washington, the portrait is one of the unflinching psychological studies of Eakins's mature American Realism.

title: Spring Blossoms
description: Flowering trees in full white and pink blossom spread across a green meadow beneath a luminous pale-blue sky, with a house glimpsed in the middle distance and a solitary figure standing among the trees. Painted around 1891 by George Inness near Montclair, New Jersey, the canvas exemplifies his late tonalist approach of softened forms and unified atmospheric light.

title: Sunset on the Passaic
description: The Passaic river spreads under a luminous orange and yellow sky at sunset, with boats on the water and a hazy industrial riverbank in the distance. George Inness painted this oil in 1891, and the canvas is now at the Honolulu Museum of Art; the glowing atmosphere and dissolved forms reflect his late Tonalist manner.

title: Tahitian Women on the Beach
description: Two Tahitian women sit on a sandy beach, one in profile wearing a red patterned pareu, the other facing the viewer in a pink dress and working with something in her hands. The deep blue-green sea and a narrow strip of dark sky form a compressed background behind them. Gauguin painted the canvas in 1891 during his first Tahitian sojourn; it is in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

title: Taking a Snow Town
description: Cossack riders charge a snow fortress while villagers in sheepskin coats throw snowballs and brandish brooms, the assault staged as part of the last day of Maslenitsa. Surikov painted the Shrovetide game from memory of his Siberian childhood, exhibiting the canvas at the 1891 Peredvizhniki show before it entered the Russian Museum.
credit: Vasily Surikov

title: The Circus
description: Seurat's last, unfinished canvas captures a circus performance with a bareback rider, ringmaster and tiered audience. The arabesque rhythms and yellow-blue contrasts apply Charles Henry's theories of expressive line and colour, pushing pointillism toward decorative stylisation.

title: The Return of Persephone
description: Hermes lifts Persephone up from the underworld toward her mother Demeter, who reaches down through a gap of light at the cave mouth. Leighton painted the oil in 1891 and it hangs in Leeds Art Gallery. The figures form a single rising diagonal from the dark earth into the bright opening above.
credit: cgfa.sunsite.dk Bridgeman Art Library : Object 100045

title: Tiger in a Tropical Storm
description: A tiger crouches through whipping grasses as rain slashes a tropical thicket lit by lightning. Rousseau's first jungle picture, it stitched together motifs from botanical gardens and prints into the imagined wilderness that would occupy him for the rest of his life.

title: Warden of the Mosque
description: An elderly bearded warden sits at the arched entrance of the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus, his blue robes and red boots set against the elaborately carved and inlaid stonework of the doorway, with shoes scattered on the cobbled threshold and the sunlit courtyard visible beyond. Bauernfeind painted this intimate figure study in 1891, combining precise architectural detail with quiet observation of daily religious life in the Syrian capital.
credit: https://www.reddit.com/r/Art/comments/v8ae8j/warden_of_the_mosque_damascus_gustav_bauernfeind/ Christies

title: Watching the Breakers
description: Two women in dark Victorian dresses stand on a rocky shore as heavy surf breaks behind them; one carries a wicker basket, and the vivid orange-patterned hem of her companion's skirt catches against the grey rocks. Homer sets the human figures as a counterweight to the churning Atlantic, animating the Prouts Neck seascape with narrative weight. Painted in 1891, the work is held at the Gilcrease Museum, Tulsa.
credit: PaintingDb, Object 8550; Gilcrease Museum

title: Woman with a Flower
description: Vahine no te tiare shows a young Tahitian woman in a blue high-collared mission dress, holding a small pale tiare flower in her hands. Gauguin painted this, his first Polynesian portrait, in 1891, setting the sitter against a flat yellow ground animated by painted green foliage. The canvas is held in the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek, Copenhagen.

title: A Sunny Day at Shinnecock Bay
description: A woman in a grey dress and red hat stands beside a beached white rowboat on a sandy Shinnecock shore, while a small child in pink plays nearby and a dog investigates the water's edge. Chase painted this circa 1892 at his Long Island summer school, capturing the bright, breezy atmosphere of the bay with loose, confident brushwork characteristic of his plein-air practice.

title: Banks of the Loing in Moret
description: The banks of the river Loing at Moret-sur-Loing, with low buildings and a stand of trees mirrored in the slow water. Sisley settled in the Moret district from 1880 and painted the Loing repeatedly until his death in 1899. The sky occupies the upper half of the canvas, worked in pale blue and grey above the green riverbank.

title: Blow Blow Thou Winter Wind
description: Titled from a song in Shakespeare's As You Like It, the painting shows a young woman huddled on a snowbound hillside in a bleak winter landscape, with a dog and a distant walking figure behind her. Painted in 1892 and held at the Auckland Art Gallery, the work exemplifies Millais's broader, more mood-driven late style, far removed from the close observation of his early Pre-Raphaelite years.

provenance.collection: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki
provenance.location: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki

title: Brig “Mercury” Attacked by Two Turkish Ships
description: The 18-gun Russian brig Mercury fires from between two towering Ottoman ships of the line off the Bosphorus in May 1829, smoke and wind shredding the sails. Aivazovsky returned to the legendary encounter repeatedly, this 1892 canvas painting the small brig as a luminous wedge between dark hulls.

title: Cassia-tree moon
description: A bearded figure in green robes stands against a vast golden moon, one hand raised pointing upward while his axe rests at his side and a fan hangs from his arm. From Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon series, this design illustrates the Daoist legend of Wu Gang, condemned to chop eternally at the cassia tree on the moon.

title: Curiosity
description: Two young women climb a wooden ladder propped against a stone wall, both craning to see what lies on the other side. The painting's title and the evident delight on their faces make the subject plain: the curiosity is directed outward, not shared between them. The high academic finish and genre charm are hallmarks of de Blaas's Venetian figure painting, dated 1892.

title: Eugen von Blaas Der rote Fächer 1892
description: A young woman leans on a windowsill, her gaze meeting the viewer directly while she holds a vivid red fan loosely at her side. The single warm accent of the fan against her white dress and dark interior backdrop typifies de Blaas's skill at turning a simple prop into a focal point. The panel is signed and dated 1892.
credit: Hampel Auctions

title: Home at Montclair
credit: bestpaintingsforsale.com; Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute, Williamstown, Massachusetts

title: Inness George Early Morning Tarpon Springs
description: Tall Florida pines rise above a settlement of low buildings and a marshy foreground in the early morning light. George Inness painted this 1892 canvas during his winters at Tarpon Springs, applying the atmospheric diffusion and tonal subtlety characteristic of his late work.

title: Jeunes filles au piano
description: Two girls in white and pink dresses lean over an upright piano, one seated and playing while the other follows the score. Renoir painted this version in 1892 as the first of his works acquired by the French state, placed in the Musée du Luxembourg and now in the Musée d'Orsay. He made several oil and drawn repetitions of the composition for dealers and collectors.

title: Lady Agnew of Lochnaw
description: Lady Agnew sits in a carved and upholstered armchair, wearing a white muslin gown with a lavender sash, her dark eyes meeting the viewer directly and one arm resting loosely over the chair's side. Sargent painted the portrait in 1892 and it was exhibited at the Royal Academy the following year to considerable acclaim; the canvas is now the centrepiece of the Scottish National Gallery in Edinburgh. The relaxed pose and luminous handling of the white dress exemplify the command of character and painterly bravura for which Sargent's society portraits are celebrated.
credit: MFA Boston via the Boston Globe

title: Nasturces
description: A close, plunging view of nasturtium leaves and blossoms painted in Caillebotte's Petit Gennevilliers garden. The unusual cropping and high vantage echo the steep perspectives he favoured in his urban scenes, applied here to a horticultural subject he cultivated himself.

title: Paul Cézanne
description: Two Provençal labourers face off across a wine bottle in Cézanne's most distilled treatment of the card-players theme. The Courtauld version reduces the cast to its essential pair, the figures built from the planar, faceted strokes that prefigured Cubism.
credit: Courtauld Institute of Art

title: Paul Gauguin
englishTitle: Nafea Faa Ipoipo (When Will You Marry?)
description: Paul Gauguin's monumental oil painting depicting a Tahitian scene with philosophical themes of human existence. Completed during the artist's first stay in Tahiti, this 101 x 77 cm canvas is considered one of his most important works, combining Post-Impressionist style with Symbolist ideology.

title: Te aa no areois
englishTitle: Te aa no areois (The Seed of the Areoi)
description: A young Tahitian woman sits nude on a patterned cloth, holding a sprouting mango seed against a field of flowering shrubs. Gauguin painted Te aa no areois, the Seed of the Areoi, in 1892 during his first Tahitian stay, casting his model Teha'amana as the mythic ancestress of the Areoi religious society; the canvas is now in MoMA.

title: The Canal du Loing at Moret
description: The Canal du Loing at Moret recedes between rows of bare poplars whose trunks are doubled in the still water. Oil on canvas of 1892, given to the Musée du Luxembourg by friends of the painter led by Claude Monet after his death and now in the Musée d'Orsay (INV 20723). Sisley kept to the canal's straight perspective lines through many canvases of the early 1890s.

title: The evening bells ringing
description: A whitewashed monastery sits on the far bank of a slow river at sunset, twin boats pulling toward the landing as bells ring across the water. Levitan combined memories of the Savvino-Storozhevsky monastery near Zvenigorod with the Krivoezersky monastery near Yuryevets, the canvas now in the Tretyakov Gallery.
credit: staratel.com; lj.rossia.org; ?

title: The Garden of the Hesperides
description: Three nymphs recline beneath an apple tree, the serpent Ladon coiled around its trunk to guard the golden fruit that was Hera's gift. Leighton painted the tondo about 1892; it is held by the Lady Lever Art Gallery in Port Sunlight. The circular format sets the sleeping figures within the curve of the tree's foliage.
credit: Bridgeman Art Library : Object 5326

title: The moon on Musashi Plain
description: A pale full moon rises over the windswept grasses of Musashino, where a fox glances back through the autumn pampas. The plate from One Hundred Aspects of the Moon distills a literary motif into spare silhouette and graded sky.

title: The Siesta
description: The Siesta shows several Tahitian women resting on a wooden veranda floor, two of them stretched out lengthways while others sit nearby. Painted between 1892 and 1894 during Gauguin's first stay in Tahiti, the canvas uses flat zones of colour and a high viewpoint to dissolve conventional depth. It is held in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: The Spirit of the Dead Keeps Watch
description: A nude Tahitian woman, Gauguin's companion Teha'amana, lies face down on a bed against a deep violet background, while the tupapau — the spirit of the dead — sits as a dark hooded figure behind her in the upper left. Painted in 1892 and now in the Albright-Knox Art Gallery (Buffalo AKG Art Museum), the title refers to Polynesian spirits believed to haunt the night.
credit: proprofs.com

title: The Vladimirka
description: The empty Vladimirka road, the convict route to Siberia, runs through flat steppe toward a low horizon, a single pilgrim halted at the wayside cross. Levitan painted the unpopulated landscape in 1892 after walking part of the road himself; he gave the canvas to Pavel Tretyakov and it remains in the Tretyakov Gallery.
credit: Isaac Levitan

title: Левитан У омута
description: A serene landscape painting by Russian master Isaac Levitan, created in 1892. The work depicts a tranquil pool or small body of water nestled in a wooded setting, exemplifying Levitan's mastery of mood and natural light in landscape composition. Housed in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

title: Annah the Javanese
description: Annah, the thirteen-year-old Javanese model Gauguin took in on his return to Paris, sits naked in a blue armchair with a small monkey at her feet. Painted in the Rue Vercingétorix studio in 1893 or 1894, the canvas carries the Tahitian inscription Aita tamari vahine Judith te parari and now hangs in the Stavros Niarchos collection.

title: George Meredith
description: George Meredith , by George Frederic Watts (died 1904), given to the National Portrait Gallery, London in 1909. See source website for additional information. This set of images was gathered by User:Dcoetzee from the National Portrait Gallery, London website using a special tool.

title: Gérôme - Painting Breathes Life into Sculpture v1
description: An ancient Greek artisan paints a terracotta Tanagra figurine, the Latin title declaring that 'painting breathes life into sculpture'. The picture is Gérôme's manifesto for polychromy, arguing that the white marbles museums revered were originally as colored as this little figure.

title: Ginger Pot with Pomegranate and Pears
description: A glazed ginger jar bound with cord stands among pears and a split pomegranate on a rumpled white cloth. Oil on canvas of 1893, held by The Phillips Collection in Washington. Cézanne tipped the tabletop forward so the fruit reads against the dark ground rather than receding into it.

title: Isaac Levitan
description: Isaac Levitan sits in a dark suit, one arm draped along the back of a wicker-patterned chair, his bearded face turned in three-quarter view with a calm, reserved gaze against a dark interior. Valentin Serov painted his friend and fellow painter in 1893; the portrait is in the Tretyakov Gallery.

title: Kirche von Moret
description: The church of Notre-Dame at Moret-sur-Loing seen close up, its Gothic buttresses and stonework filling the upper canvas above a row of low houses. Sisley painted a series of views of the church between 1893 and 1894, varying the light across its west front. He worked the masonry in short strokes of cream, ochre and grey-blue.

title: Self Portrait
description: A young Léon Bakst presents himself in three-quarter view against a neutral ground, the brushwork loose and the modelling kept to essentials. Painted in 1893, well before his Ballets Russes designs reshaped European stage costume, the self-portrait dates from Bakst's early years training in Saint Petersburg.

title: The Bathing Posts
description: Two slender bathing markers rise from the surf off the Brittany coast, flanking a pale horizon where small sailboats pass under a broken, cloud-streaked sky. Whistler reduces the scene to horizontal bands of blue-grey and green, exercising the tonal restraint characteristic of his late Aestheticist practice. Painted in 1893 and now in the Hunterian Museum and Art Gallery, Glasgow, this small oil on wood measures only 16.6 by 24.3 centimetres.
credit: Hunterian Museum and Art Gallery, Glasgow

title: The Child’s Bath
description: Seen from a steep, raised viewpoint, a woman in a boldly striped dress bathes a small child in a plain basin, their bodies pressed together in tender absorption. Cassatt borrows the high vantage and patterned surfaces from Japanese woodblock prints, which she had studied closely in the Paris exhibition of 1890.

title: The Elopement
description: A young man in a rowboat reaches up toward a woman standing beside an iron garden gate on a brick wall, the two figures caught in a moment of clandestine exchange beside a still waterway. Edmund Blair Leighton painted the scene in 1893 with his customary period accuracy of dress and setting.

title: The scream of nature
description: A skeletal figure clutches its head beneath a blood-red sky on a fjord-side bridge, mouth agape in soundless anguish. Munch combined oil, tempera and pastel on cardboard to externalise an attack of existential dread, anchoring the visual vocabulary of European Expressionism.
credit: National Museum of Art, Architecture and Design

title: The Sin
description: A nude woman emerges from deep shadow with a large serpent coiled around her body in Franz von Stuck's iconic painting The Sin (1893). The frontal composition, strong chiaroscuro, and femme-fatale imagery are hallmarks of von Stuck's Symbolist manner and were sufficiently celebrated that he produced several versions of the subject.

title: Uriel da Costa’s imaginary portrait
description: A bust-length imaginary portrait depicts Uriel da Costa, the seventeenth-century rationalist philosopher, in a white collar and dark doublet, his gaze directed at the viewer. Léon Bakst painted the work in 1893, early in his career and well before his association with the Ballets Russes.

title: A Moonlit Night on the Bosphorus
description: A full moon breaks through thin cloud above the Bosphorus, laying a path of light across the strait between anchored sailing ships. On the near shore a domed mosque flanked by slender minarets overlooks a quay where small figures gather by the water's edge. Aivazovsky painted this nocturne in 1894; it is held in the Tretyakov Gallery.
credit: Государственная Третьяковская Галерея

title: Bathers
description: A group of nude bathers is arranged beneath arching trees that frame the composition like a vault, their bodies echoing the leaning trunks. One of three large Baigneuses Cézanne worked on between 1894 and 1905; this canvas is in the National Gallery, London. He sacrificed individual likeness to fit the figures to the triangular structure of the trees.

title: Beardsley-peacockskirt
description: Beardsley's ink and graphite drawing, made in 1894 as an illustration for Oscar Wilde's Salomé, shows Salome in a vast sweeping skirt patterned with peacock feather-eyes, facing a slender attendant in white. The extreme contrast of black silhouette against white ground and the integration of decorative Art Nouveau ornament with Japanese-influenced line exemplify Beardsley's graphic style. The original drawing is held in the Harvard Art Museums.

title: Day of the God
description: Mahana no atua, painted in Paris between Gauguin's two Tahitian sojourns, presents an idol of the moon goddess Hina flanked by ritual bathers. The lower foreground dissolves into pools of pure, mirror-bright color, an experiment in flat decorative abstraction that would influence Nabi and Fauve painters.

title: Despair
description: This is a painting featuring a figure standing on a bridge, gazing down, seemingly lost in thought. The background consists of a dramatic, swirling sky with striking red, yellow, and blue colors. The figure is dressed in dark clothing, and their posture and the expression on their face convey a sense of melancholy or introspection.

title: G. Caillebotte - Le jardin du Petit Gennevilliers en hiver
description: A snow-blanketed view of the painter's own riverside garden across the Seine from Argenteuil, where Caillebotte spent his final years tending plants and painting boats. The muted whites and bare branches show the late, looser brushwork he developed after retreating from Paris's Impressionist circle.

title: Jeune fille se peignant
description: An intimate domestic scene of a young woman combing her hair, a recurring subject in Renoir's later years. The soft, feathery handling of flesh and fabric reflects his shift away from strict Impressionist plein-air practice toward a warmer, more classicizing manner influenced by Renaissance art.

title: Monet w1370
description: A view of the Seine at Port-Villez, near Giverny, painted in 1894 (La Seine à Port-Villez). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1370, it belongs to the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rouen.

title: My Next-Door Neighbour
description: A young woman in 18th-century dress pauses on the steps of a Georgian doorway while a man above her leans in to speak, the encounter framed by classical columns. Edmund Blair Leighton painted this period genre scene in 1894, capturing a moment of polite social exchange with his characteristic precision of costume and architectural detail.
credit: Bonhams : lot number 190 (sales 14218, London , 14 November 2006); https://www.topofart.com/artists/Edmund_Blair_Leighton/art_reproduction/6157/My_Next-Door_Neighbour.php

title: Over Eternal Quiet
description: A small wooden chapel and graveyard sit on a windswept bluff above a vast inland lake, dark storm-clouds piled over the horizon. Levitan painted Above the Eternal Tranquility at Lake Udomlya in 1894, calling it the work in which he had put most of himself; it entered the Tretyakov Gallery the same year.

title: Portrait of a Neapolitan woman
description: A young Neapolitan woman sits turned away from the viewer, her elbow resting on a table and her chin supported on one hand, gazing downward in reverie. Repin renders her white lace-trimmed blouse and dark hair with direct, energetic brushwork characteristic of his Realist practice. The canvas, signed and dated Naples 1894, records a study made during the artist's travels in southern Italy.

title: Sacred Spring: Sweet Dreams
description: Two Tahitian women sit cross-legged in the foreground beside a sacred pool — one in a dreaming reverie with her head resting on her hand, the other holding a small red flower. Behind them, additional figures move near the water's edge in a lush tropical landscape. Inscribed 'Nave nave moe' (Sacred Spring, Sweet Dreams), the canvas was painted in 1894 and entered the Hermitage Museum with the Shchukin collection.
credit: Hermitage Torrent ( .torrent with info-hash )

title: The Adirondack Guide
description: A solitary woodsman paddles his canoe across a still mountain lake, the watercolor reserving the white of the paper for highlights on water and shirt. The picture distills Homer's late respect for the working backwoodsman into a quietly monumental profile.
credit: The AMICA Library

title: A Friendly Call
description: Two women sit in conversation in Chase's summer studio at Shinnecock, Long Island — a visitor in crisp white, parasol still in hand, faces her hostess across a long cushion-strewn divan, with framed prints and a tall gilt mirror filling the wall behind them. A leading American Impressionist and influential teacher, Chase painted the interior in 1895; the canvas hangs in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Catholicos Khrimyan Airik near Echmiadzin
description: Catholicos Mkrtich Khrimian, patriarch of the Armenian Apostolic Church, walks the dusty road near the cathedral of Echmiadzin with Mount Ararat rising beyond. Aivazovsky, himself Armenian, painted the elderly Khrimian Hayrik in 1895 shortly after his election to the Catholicosate.

title: Chinese Warship Ting Yuang Visiting Japan
description: The German-built ironclad Tingyuan, then the largest warship in the Far East, lies at anchor in a Japanese port flying her flags. Kōitsu records the ship's Meiji-era courtesy visit in a colour woodblock print that combines ukiyo-e tradition with the new Western subject matter of steam and steel.

title: Daydreaming by the shore
description: A young woman stands at the water's edge, her gaze turned towards the horizon while she rests on a long shepherd's staff. Two wicker baskets of market goods — one holding live poultry — sit at her feet, suggesting a brief pause on an errand. De Blaas renders her yellow dress and embroidered bodice with the precise textile attention characteristic of his genre work, here set against a wide, silver-toned lagoon sky. Signed and dated 1895.

title: Flaming June
description: A young woman sleeps curled in a translucent orange-saffron gown, one arm thrown over her head, a sprig of oleander above her. Leighton painted the oil in 1895; after decades of neglect it was bought for the Museo de Arte de Ponce in Puerto Rico in the 1960s. The folded pose fills a square format, the fabric worked in deep orange against a marble parapet and sea.
credit: Art Renewal Center

title: Frederick Law Olmsted
description: Sargent painted the landscape architect of Central Park during work on the Biltmore Estate grounds, posing him among the rhododendrons he had laid out. Loose, plein-air handling of the foliage gives way to a tighter likeness of the sitter, knitting Realist portraiture to Impressionist surface.

title: Gérôme - Summer Afternoon on a Lake
description: A shaded lakeside glade in late summer light, with anglers at the water's edge and a small boat visible on the still surface beyond. Gérôme renders the wooded atmosphere with careful tonal control, producing a quiet landscape far removed from his orientalist subjects. The painting dates to circa 1895.

title: Golden autumn. Slobodka
description: A birch grove turns yellow above a slow blue river in the Russian countryside, a sliver of field and far village closing the view. Levitan painted this smaller variant of Golden Autumn at Slobodka in 1895; the larger canvas of the same year belongs to the Tretyakov Gallery.

title: Golden Autumn. Золотая осень
description: A sunlit forest interior with large broadleaf trees bearing golden-yellow autumn foliage, their trunks casting deep shadows across a carpet of fallen leaves. Isaac Levitan's 1895 canvas, signed at the lower right and exhibited at the Munich Secession in 1896, captures the mood of a Russian autumn woodland in a 58 × 68 cm oil on canvas.
credit: Russian Art Masterpieces

title: Hay Stacks
description: Two haystacks stand in a stubble field at Moret under a wide sky, casting long shadows across the cut ground. Sisley painted the pair in 1895, working the thatch in broken strokes of gold and russet. The horizon sits low, giving most of the canvas to the changing light overhead.

title: Hilterfingen
description: A pencil sketch records the village of Hilterfingen, with a church tower rising above houses and trees, inscribed and dated 19 July 1895. Paul Klee made the drawing at age fifteen, and it is now held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The assured observation of the townscape suggests Klee's early facility with landscape draughtsmanship before his later stylistic experiments.
credit: Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation

title: Ivan Aivazovsky
description: A large sailing vessel lies at anchor in a coastal bay partially obscured by haze, while a group of figures with draught animals rest on the shore in the foreground and a small rowing boat crosses the calm water to the right. Ivan Aivazovsky painted this 1895 marine, one of many coastal scenes set against mountainous terrain that characterise his work from his studio at Feodosia.

title: Leda and the Swan
description: Gérôme treats the classical myth in his characteristic polished academic manner, placing the pale nude figure of Leda in a sunlit green landscape where a swan glides toward her on the water, accompanied by a flock of putti. Trained as both painter and sculptor, he returned repeatedly to mythological subjects that displayed his mastery of smooth, near-tactile flesh, as in this 1895 canvas.

title: Maison Maria with a View of Château Noir
description: A small ochre farmhouse, the Maison Maria, sits among pines on the road to the Château Noir near Aix-en-Provence. Oil on canvas of about 1895, in the Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth. Cézanne worked the ground and foliage in parallel diagonal strokes of green, blue and orange.

title: March
description: Sunlit snow lies thick around a yellow porch and stable, a single saddled horse waiting in the yard while bare aspens cast long blue shadows. Levitan painted March in 1895 at the Gorka estate, the canvas now in the Tretyakov Gallery and credited with bringing plein-air winter painting into Russian landscape.
credit: State Tretiakov Gallery. Государственная Третьяковская Галерея

title: Northeaster
description: A lone outcrop of the Maine coast pummeled by a winter storm, rendered with the muscular realism Homer developed at Prout's Neck. The painting strips the marine subject to surf, rock, and spray, a meditation on raw natural force.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 20011487)

title: Study of a Girl in Japanese Dress
description: Chase, the leading American Impressionist teacher, captures a young model in a borrowed kimono with rapid, fluid brushwork. Such japoniste studio subjects were fashionable in Gilded Age New York and reveal his admiration for Whistler and Sargent.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum ; Photo: Brooklyn Museum, 51.60_SL1.jpg

title: Surikov Pokoreniye Sibiri Yermakom
description: Cossack atamans under Yermak Timofeyevich fire muskets from low boats at Khan Kuchum's mounted Tatar host on the Irtysh River in 1582. Surikov worked on Yermak's Conquest of Siberia for four years, exhibiting the canvas in 1895; Nicholas II bought it for the Russian Museum the same year.

title: The Artist and His Model
description: An elderly sculptor — likely Gérôme himself — leans intently over a white marble seated figure, comparing it with a live nude model posed beside it on a low platform. The studio is filled with props and sculptural studies, articulating Gérôme's lifelong interest in the relationship between sculpture and the living body. Painted in 1895, the work is in the Haggin Museum, Stockton, California.
credit: hagginmuseum.org https://hagginmuseum.org/collections/gerome-jean-leon/the-artist-and-his-model/

title: Vampire
description: A red-haired woman bends over a man, her lips at his neck while her hair cascades like flowing blood. Originally titled Love and Pain, the picture was rechristened by Munch's Symbolist circle and became a key motif of his Frieze of Life.

title: Water lilies
description: Water lily pads — green and reddish — drift across a dark, still pond, their white flowers opening above the surface while aquatic vegetation fills the shallower water throughout. Levitan painted Water Lilies in 1895, approaching the subject with the same close attention to natural light and reflected colour that characterises his finest mood landscapes; the canvas is held by the Astrakhan State Picture Gallery.

title: Wedding of Nicholas II and Grand Princess Alexandra Fyodorovna
description: An imperial ceremonial scene staged inside a Russian Orthodox chapel, with Tsar Nicholas II and Alexandra Fyodorovna at the centre of a glittering crowd of courtiers, clergy and grand dukes. Tuxen, official painter to several European royal houses, marshals the assembly into a measured, document-like composition.
credit: Hermitage Museum

title: Young Italian Woman at a Table
description: A young woman in a striped blouse leans on a fabric-covered table, her head resting in her hand. Oil on canvas of about 1895 to 1900, accession 99.PA.40 in the J. Paul Getty Museum in Los Angeles. Cézanne built her bulk from broad blocks of colour while the space behind her shifts and tilts.
credit: J. Paul Getty Museum

title: 1280px-Jean Léon Gerome 1896 La Vérité sortant du puits
englishTitle: Truth Coming Out of the Well
description: An allegory of Truth, nude and enraged, climbing from the well into which liars have cast her — painted at the height of the Dreyfus Affair and widely read as Gérôme's bitter comment on public deceit. The polished academic surface gives the mythic figure unsettling photographic immediacy.

title: A Pensive Moment
description: A young woman in Venetian costume sits sideways on a low brick parapet, her gaze directed across the lagoon toward a distant cityscape, her hands resting loosely in her lap. A straw hat hangs at her back, a basket of fruit sits below on the ground, and a discarded sandal lies nearby. De Blaas uses the open waterside setting to give the figure an air of reverie. The canvas is dated 1896 and held by the Art Renewal Center.
credit: Art Renewal Center

title: Autumn
description: From the four-panel decorative series The Seasons, an allegorical figure reclines among grape vines, ripening clusters, and warm autumnal foliage, holding a shallow cup. The richly saturated ochre and burgundy palette and the sinuous interplay of figure and plant life are characteristic of Mucha's 1896 Seasons cycle.
credit: Art Renewal Center Museum , image 4426

title: Lac d'Annecy
description: Painted during a summer stay at Talloires, the canvas reduces the Savoyard lake and the Château de Duingt to interlocking planes of blue, green and ochre. Cézanne's structural brushwork and tilted perspective treat water and stone as equivalent geometric facets, prefiguring Cubist analysis of form.

title: Night Bivouac of Great Army
description: Soldiers of Napoleon's Grande Armée huddle around guttering fires in a frozen Russian field during the catastrophic 1812 retreat. Vereshchagin, a battle painter known for unsparing realism, treats the scene with documentary cold rather than heroic rhetoric.
credit: http://www.picture.art-catalog.ru/picture.php?id_picture=11061 , http://www.abcgallery.com/V/vereshchagin/vereshchagin32.html

title: Nikolay II of Russia by I.Repin
description: A formal portrait of Tsar Nicholas II, the last emperor of Russia, painted shortly after his coronation. Repin balances state-portrait dignity with the loose, vigorous brushwork that distinguished him among the Peredvizhniki realists.

title: Self-portrait »près du Golgotha«
description: In this 1896 self-portrait titled près du Golgotha, Gauguin depicts himself bust-length in a white garment against a near-black ground, his expression grave and inward-looking. The canvas was painted in Tahiti during a period of severe illness and financial hardship, and the title's reference to Golgotha aligns the artist with the suffering Christ. It is held in the Museu de Arte de São Paulo.

title: Selfportrait
description: Gauguin portrays himself in strict profile against a deep reddish-brown ground, the face lit with warm, ruddy tones while the brushwork is reduced to its essentials. An inscription on the canvas reads 'à l'ami Daniel', identifying the work as a gift to Georges-Daniel de Monfreid, who supported the artist during his Tahitian years. The self-portrait is dated 1896.

title: Spring
description: Part of Mucha's first Seasons cycle, the allegorical figure stands playing an ornate Art Nouveau harp amid flowering cherry blossoms, her auburn hair flowing freely. The pale, delicate palette and sinuous arabesque line are hallmarks of his early decorative work.
credit: Art Renewal Center Museum , image 4424

title: Summer
description: From the Seasons quartet, a languid woman wearing a poppy-blossom crown sits among summer vegetation near water, her bare feet resting at the water's edge. Mucha's warm, sun-bleached palette and the serpentine outlines of the figure and foliage give the composition its characteristic fin-de-siècle languor.
credit: Art Renewal Center Museum , image 4425

title: The Artist's Family
description: Renoir's wife Aline stands with their eldest son Pierre, the young Jean held by a maid, and a neighbour's daughter gathered in front of a wall. Oil on canvas of 1896, catalogued BF819 in the Barnes Foundation in Philadelphia. The painter set the figures close to the picture plane against a flatly brushed ground.

title: Winter
description: Closing the 1896 Seasons set, a woman wrapped in a flowing teal-green cloak cradles small birds against her chest among snow-laden branches. The warm amber background contrasted with the cold white snowfall and her verdant wrap demonstrates Mucha's command of decorative colour in this lithographic series.
credit: Art Renewal Center Museum , image 4423

title: 35390682010 46099096b2 o w1449
description: A landscape catalogued as Wildenstein 1449 in Monet's oeuvre. The artist's standard practice in such canvases is to dissolve form into broken touches of complementary colour, recording transient light with a saturated, high-keyed palette.

title: George Frederic Watts
description: This set of images was gathered by User:Dcoetzee from the National Portrait Gallery, London website using a special tool. All images in this batch have been evaluated manually for evidence that the artist probably died before 1939, or that the work is anonymous or pseudonymous and was probably published before 1923. 1897 work, painter died 1927.

title: Gérôme - L'entrée du Christ à Jérusalem - cadre
englishTitle: Entry of the Christ at Jerusalem
description: Christ rides a donkey toward the walls of Jerusalem under a cloudy sky, while a large crowd gathers to receive him, some holding palm fronds. Gérôme's panoramic composition, painted in 1897, sets the Gospel narrative in a topographically plausible Levantine landscape drawn from his Holy Land travels. The painting is housed in the Musée Jean-Léon Gérôme in Vesoul, France.

title: Henri Meunier04
description: A poster, L'Heure du Silence, by the Belgian Art Nouveau designer Henri Meunier, lithographed in the flat planes and sinuous contour the Brussels school adopted from Japanese prints. Meunier worked extensively in advertising, treating commercial commissions with the same graphic refinement as his fine-art prints.

provenance.collection: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki
provenance.location: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki

title: L'Ermitage par Paul Berthon 2
description: A poster lithograph for the Symbolist literary review L'Ermitage, showing a woman with flowing auburn hair bent over a spray of lilies, rendered in warm golden and amber tones. Paul Berthon, a pupil of Eugène Grasset, designed the piece in 1897, applying an Art Nouveau linearity that gives his work a distinctive decorative flatness.
credit: Dover Publications Sample (no long-term link)

title: Lakeside
description: A woman in a striped kimono sits by a calm lake, a round paper fan held loosely in her hands, with wooded hills visible across the water. Painted in 1897, Lakeside is among Kuroda Seiki's best-known canvases; trained in Paris under Raphaël Collin, he brought plein-air colour and a high-key palette to Meiji Japan. The work is held at the Tokyo National Museum.

title: Morning on the Seine
description: One of the Mornings on the Seine series that Claude Monet painted at dawn from a moored studio boat where the river winds past Giverny. Trees and sky dissolve into their own reflections on the still water, the whole canvas given over to a single veiled harmony of early morning light. Painted in 1897, the picture is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Mucha seasons 1897 spring
description: Spring from Mucha's 1897 Four Seasons series, personified as a young woman with loosely gathered hair amid blossoming branches and flowers. The tall decorative panel format, sinuous contour, and richly patterned border typify the Art Nouveau idiom Mucha helped define in Paris during the 1890s.

title: Napoleon near Borodino
description: Part of an extensive cycle the painter devoted to the 1812 French invasion of Russia, the canvas shows the emperor on the battlefield reduced to an ordinary, weary commander. The series was researched on site and built around demystifying the Napoleonic legend.

title: Nevermore
description: Nevermore shows a nude Tahitian woman lying along a bed, her gaze turned towards the viewer, while a large dark teal bird occupies the upper centre of the canvas and two figures converse in the background. Painted in 1897 and titled after Edgar Allan Poe's raven, the work conveys an atmosphere of unease through its flattened pattern and cool colour. It is in the Courtauld Gallery, London.
credit: Courtauld Institute - Nevermore

title: Ship "Twelve Apostles"
description: The warship Twelve Apostles ploughs through a heavy swell under billowing sail, her dark hull and tiered gun decks rendered with Aivazovsky's characteristic luminous seascape technique. Painted in 1897, the canvas depicts the celebrated Black Sea Fleet ship of the line that figured prominently in mid-nineteenth-century Russian naval history. Aivazovsky returned throughout his career to subjects drawn from the Imperial fleet, and this work belongs to the large body of maritime paintings produced at his studio in Feodosia.

title: Spring. High water
description: Slender birches and mixed trees stand half-submerged in the floodwaters of a Russian spring, their pale trunks reflected in the still surface, while a wooden boat rests on the muddy bank in the foreground. Levitan painted Spring. High Water in 1897, capturing the annual inundation of low-lying woodland that became one of the touchstones of the Russian mood landscape.

title: The Sleeping Gypsy
description: A lion stands over a sleeping figure in a striped robe on a moonlit desert plain, a mandolin and earthenware jar lying nearby. Rousseau painted this dream-image in 1897; now in the Museum of Modern Art, it exemplifies the self-taught artist's flattened forms and eerie calm.
credit: Oakenchips

title: Tsar Ivan The Terrible
description: Ivan IV stands on a stairway in elaborate gold-embroidered robes trimmed with white fur, a long staff in hand, his dark eyes fixed in watchful intensity. Vasnetsov painted this full-length imaginary portrait in 1897, drawing on chronicle sources and reconstructions of late Muscovite court regalia to give the figure archaeological specificity. The canvas is held in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
credit: Scanned from A. K. Lazuko Victor Vasnetsov, Leningrad: Khudozhnik RSFSR, 1990, ISBN 5-7370-0107-5; Tretyakov Gallery

title: Where do we come from? Who are we? Where are we going?
description: A sleeping infant, a youth picking fruit, and an old woman crouched beside a blue idol stretch across nearly four metres of Tahitian forest. Gauguin painted the canvas in late 1897 as an intended summation before a suicide attempt, and it now anchors the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts Boston

title: Alexandre Benois
description: Alexandre Benois reclines in a leather armchair reading papers, set against a warm interior with a framed portrait visible on the wall behind him. Léon Bakst painted this portrait of his friend and Mir iskusstva co-founder in 1898, the year the journal was launched in St Petersburg, where the two artists shaped a programme of Russian art nouveau and stage design.

title: Among the waves
description: Foaming swells crest under a torn, luminous sky in a wholly unpeopled marine. Aivazovsky painted Among the Waves in 1898 at the age of eighty-one, judging it the finest canvas of his late career; it remains in the gallery he founded at Feodosia in Crimea.

title: Aphonse Mucha - Rose 1898
description: A young woman in a cream gown is shown surrounded by and crowned with roses, her hair dressed with blossoms, within the vertical panel format characteristic of Mucha's decorative series. Part of the Flowers series of 1898, the design exemplifies the Art Nouveau idiom Mucha refined in Paris — sinuous line, stylised flora, and the fusion of figure and ornament.

title: Dance
description: Part of The Arts panel series, an entranced female personification swirls through flowing rose-pink drapery within a large circular medallion, flower petals drifting around her. Mucha treats movement itself as ornament, threading sinuous line through the figure in continuous arabesques characteristic of his 1898 decorative panels.
credit: Art Renewal Center Museum , image 4417

title: First Touch of Autumn
description: A sandy track winds through open coastal scrubland under a pale, clear sky, the dried grasses and low shrubs carrying the first warm tones of autumn. The wide, flat horizon suggests the Long Island shore near Chase's Shinnecock Hills summer school. Painted around 1898, the work belongs to Chase's sustained engagement with the American Impressionist plein-air landscape.

title: Gamayun the prophetic bird
description: The Slavic prophetic bird Gamayun perches on a bare branch above a blood-red dawn, woman-headed and crowned with dark plumage. Vasnetsov painted the panel in 1898 and exhibited it the following year; the imagery prompted Alexander Blok's 1899 sonnet of the same name.

title: Nach dem Bade
description: A nude woman seen from behind kneels and reaches up to dry her neck with a white cloth, set against a colourful backdrop of textiles and furnishings. Degas worked the composition in pastel, building layered hatchings characteristic of his late bathing series; the work is dated 1898.

title: Painting
description: Alphonse Mucha's 1898 lithograph Painting, from his four-panel allegorical suite The Arts, presents a young woman in three-quarter view holding a red carnation and a paintbrush against a softly tinted circular ground. Her auburn hair is adorned with a jewelled headpiece, and a ring of decorative medallions frames the composition within the arabesque border typical of Mucha's Paris-period Art Nouveau style. The work was published by F. Champenois, Paris.
credit: Mucha Foundation

title: Portrait of the composer Nikolai Andreyevich Rimsky-Korsakov
description: Rimsky-Korsakov sits half-turned at his desk in a dark frock coat, hand resting on a manuscript page. Serov painted the composer in 1898 for the Tretyakov Gallery during the years Rimsky-Korsakov was teaching at the St Petersburg Conservatory and orchestrating the operas of Mussorgsky.

title: Pyramid of Skulls
description: Four human skulls are stacked in a low pyramid on a bare tabletop against a dark ground. Oil on canvas painted between about 1898 and 1900, the only Cézanne to push the skulls so close to the viewer. He owned several skulls and returned to them in oil and watercolour in his final decade at Aix.

title: Selbstporträt mit Barett
description: The painter shown half-length in a soft beret and dark coat, turned slightly from the viewer with a guarded expression. Oil on canvas of about 1898 to 1900, in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. It is among the last of the roughly two dozen self-portraits Cézanne made across his career.

title: Series The Flowers
description: From the four-panel Flowers series, a virginal figure rises among towering white lilies in a symmetrical decorative niche. Mucha equates the woman with the bloom, fusing botanical study and Art Nouveau allegory.
credit: Mucha Foundation

title: The Hookah Lighter
description: Nude women at leisure in a marble hammam interior, a hookah and brass vessels arranged in the foreground. Gérôme's polished academic technique renders the tiled architecture, carpets, and gleaming metalwork with characteristic precision. The painting dates to circa 1898.
credit: Scanned from Smoke: a global history of smoking (2004) ISBN 1-86189-200-4

title: The Milliners
description: Three women crowd together around a hat being trimmed and adjusted, their figures loosely rendered against a warm, brushy background. Degas returned repeatedly to the millinery subject through the 1890s, and the 1898 canvas shows the late thickening of paint into broad, almost tapestry-like surfaces. It entered the Saint Louis Art Museum in 2007.

title: The Old Adam and Eve
description: Adam and Eve stand as unclothed figures on either side of a large serpent coiled around a tree, the scene rendered in dense black-and-white line. Edmund Joseph Sullivan made this illustration in 1898 for a published edition of Thomas Carlyle's Sartor Resartus, employing a bold graphic manner indebted to late-Victorian wood-engraving traditions.

title: Two Venetian Women
description: Two women are depicted in close half-length format: one in white lace with fair colouring and pearl jewellery, the other in a black gold-dotted veil with a coral necklace. Together they hold a single white rose. The intimate double-portrait format and refined costume place this work in de Blaas's more elevated register, distinct from his working-courtyard genre scenes. The canvas is dated 1898.

title: After the Hurricane
description: A black sailor lies cast up beside his shattered sloop on a Bahamian beach, the sea behind still heavy from the storm. Homer's late watercolor technique uses transparent washes and reserved white paper to convey both tropical glare and human vulnerability.

title: Cezanne Ambroise Vollard
description: The dealer Ambroise Vollard sits forward with hands clasped, his bald head catching the light against a brown studio wall. Cézanne painted the portrait in 1899; it is held by the Petit Palais in Paris. Vollard recalled posing more than a hundred times, after which the painter declared only the shirtfront finished.

title: Charing Cross Bridge
description: Monet painted Charing Cross Bridge during winter stays in London, working on multiple canvases simultaneously as the light shifted. In this 1899 version, bridge, water, and sky dissolve into a haze of pale blue and diffuse yellow, characteristic of his atmospheric London series now held in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza.
credit: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza: Website , Info , Pic

title: Charing Cross Bridge
englishTitle: Charing Cross Bridge, Reflections on the Thames
description: One of nearly forty variants Monet made of Charing Cross Bridge, focused here on the trembling reflections beneath the iron span. The series, painted between 1899 and 1904, was the artist's sustained study of London fog as a coloured atmospheric medium rather than a mere obscurant.

title: Children. Sasha and Yura Serov
description: Serov's two sons, Sasha and Yura, lean against a wooden railing with a wide coastal view behind them, their white shirts and dark trousers rendered in loose, assured brushwork. The painting dates to 1899 and is held in the Russian Museum, St Petersburg. It captures the children in the brisk, diffuse light typical of Serov's plein-air portraits of the period.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme
englishTitle: The Story of Anacreon 1: Cupid at the Door in a Rainstorm
description: On a dark, rain-wet night, a small winged Cupid stands at the heavy wooden door of a stone house, a line of firelight glowing beneath the threshold, while the bearded poet Anacreon leans out of an upper window to see who has knocked. Gérôme renders the exterior courtyard with archaeological care — rough-cut stone, climbing laurel, and the contrast of warm interior light against the nocturnal chill. The work, circa 1899 (oil on canvas, 60 × 81.5 cm), is the first in Gérôme's series illustrating the ode attributed to Anacreon.

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme
englishTitle: The Story of Anacreon 2: Young Love's Shivering Limbs the Embers Warm
description: The companion to the rainstorm scene: Anacreon has taken the shivering Cupid in and warms him by the hearth, just before the boy will draw his bow and pierce the host's heart. Gérôme stages the moral fable with the archaeological props and porcelain finish of his late manner.
license: Public domain or CC BY licensed

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme
englishTitle: The Story of Anacreon 3: Cupid Runs out the Door
description: Part of a late illustrative cycle Gérôme devoted to the Greek lyric poet Anacreon, the scene shows the mischievous Cupid escaping after warming himself at the poet's hearth. Drawn in Gérôme's tight academic line, it preserves the anecdotal charm of the original Anacreontic ode.
commonsUrl: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jean-Léon Gérôme, The Story of Anacreon 3--Cupid Runs out the Door, c1899.jpg

title: Jean-Léon Gérôme
englishTitle: The Story of Anacreon 4: The Poet Dreams of Cupid by the Fire
description: An oil painting from Gérôme's Anacreon series, showing the aged poet seated by a fire, head resting in his hand, as a luminous Cupid figure hovers in the smoke and light to his left. The classically furnished interior, rendered with Gérôme's characteristic precision, situates the literary reverie within an archaeologically detailed ancient setting. Oil on canvas, 60 × 81.5 cm, c. 1899.

title: Lake. Russia
description: A broad inland lake spreads beneath a high blue sky scattered with cumulus clouds, reeds and a low village visible along the far shore. Levitan began the large canvas in 1899 and was still working on it at the time of his death in 1900; it is regarded as the culminating statement of his lyrical landscape practice.

title: San Lazzaro degli Armeni
description: Aivazovsky depicts Lord Byron's celebrated visit to the Armenian Mekhitarist monastery on the island of San Lazzaro in the Venetian lagoon, showing Byron on the quayside gesturing toward a gondola while a group of robed monks stands behind him and the panorama of Venice stretches across the distant horizon. The scene is rendered with the luminous open-water treatment typical of Aivazovsky's late work; the painting dates to 1899.
credit: gallery.am/database gallery.am

title: Suvorov Crossing the Alps in 1799
description: Russian troops slide down a near-vertical snowfield above the Saint Gotthard pass, the white-haired general Suvorov on horseback at the cliff edge encouraging them on. Surikov completed the canvas in 1899 for the centenary of the Italian campaign; it hangs in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg.

title: Tahitian Woman with Evil Spirit
description: A semi-nude Tahitian woman faces the viewer, a necklace across her chest, while a pale ghostly face with closed eyes hovers in the upper left behind her. The work is a print or monotype by Gauguin, dateable to around 1899–1900, and depicts his recurring theme of the spirit of the dead watching over the living.

title: The Gulf Stream
description: A Black sailor lies on the deck of a dismasted sloop adrift on rough seas, encircled by sharks while a waterspout darkens the horizon. Homer's late marine paintings turn man-against-nature subjects into terse moral allegories, the figure's resigned posture sharpened by the painter's economical handling of pigment and salt-bleached light.

title: the-water-lily-pond
description: A view across the Japanese footbridge spanning the lily pond at Monet's Giverny garden, the green arch dissolving into shimmering reflections. The painting belongs to the celebrated bridge series in which Monet examined a single subject under shifting conditions of light.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — the-water-lily-pond/nQExbyttj8z58A

title: the-water-lily-pond
description: The arched footbridge of Monet's Giverny garden hangs above a pond crowded with floating blossoms, framed by curtains of willow and iris. Painted in tightly woven greens and rose-tinted whites, the canvas turns a private water garden into an enclosed world of reflection.
credit: the-athenaeum.org [1]

title: Two Tahitian Women
description: Two bare-breasted Tahitian women stand close in the picture plane, one holding a tray of red fruit. Gauguin painted the canvas in 1899, and it is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: Ukrainian Dancers
description: Three dancers in embroidered Ukrainian folk costume — white blouses, coloured skirts, and flowered headdresses — turn and lean together in a close formation caught mid-step. Degas worked the pastel around 1899, the loose, vigorous strokes and pastel palette typical of his late works on paper. The sheet is held by the National Gallery, London.

title: Waterloo Bridge. Effect of Fog
description: The bridge's arches dissolve into Thames fog while the smoke-stained palette of the south bank glows behind. Monet worked on the Waterloo and Charing Cross views from a balcony at the Savoy Hotel, juggling many canvases as the light shifted.

title: Women on the Seashore
description: Three Tahitian women stand and sit against a luminous orange-red ground, one holding a bundle and another nursing a child, while a dog and a distant figure occupy the background. Gauguin painted the canvas in 1899 during his late Tahitian period, organising the figures as a frieze of broad, saturated silhouettes. The work is titled Women on the Seashore.

title: Wrestlers
description: Two male wrestlers grapple on the floor of an athletic gymnasium, their intertwined bodies studied with the anatomical rigour Eakins brought to all his sporting subjects. Secondary figures — a rower in the background and clothed observers at right — extend the spatial depth. The canvas, dated 1899 and now at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, reflects Eakins's sustained investigation of the male figure through both observation and photographic study.
credit: Image: Museum Associates/LACMA

provenance.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
provenance.location: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

description: Paul Cézanne, French, 1839–1906 Pine Tree in Front of the Caves above Château Noir, ca. 1900 Watercolor and graphite on cream wove paper 46. 5 x 35.
credit: Princeton University Art Museum

title: At the Dome of the Rock and the Fountain of Qayt Bay
description: Pilgrims and worshippers gather between the Mamluk-era Sabil of Qaytbay and the gleaming Dome of the Rock on the Haram al-Sharif. Bauernfeind, who eventually settled in Jerusalem, painted the site repeatedly, prizing the geometry of its mosaic and stone over picturesque incident.

title: Blauwe irissen
description: Ohara Koson's woodblock print presents three large dark-blue irises with slender green leaves rising against a pale ground, the blooms rendered with bold flat colour and fine detail. The print was made in Tokyo between 1900 and 1930 and is held at the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam (RP-P-1999-419), donated by J. Perrée of Eindhoven.

title: Cabbage market
description: Bartlett's 1900 watercolour depicts a crowded provincial market square filled with vendors, buyers, and loaded carts, with heaped cabbages and other green vegetables dominating the foreground. The busy scene predates his celebrated shin-hanga print work by more than a decade and was sold at Bonhams Bond Street, London.
credit: Bonhams Bond Street, London

title: Dancers
description: Two ballet dancers rest or adjust their costumes, their figures rendered in warm rust and blue-green pastel with Degas's characteristically loose, layered hatching. Worked around 1900 as the artist's eyesight declined, the pastel is notable for its intensified, close-keyed colour and the compressed, cropped framing typical of his late dancer series.
credit: [1] the-athenaeum.org [2]

title: Dancers at the Barre
description: Two dancers in blue tutus stretch along a barre, one reaching forward and one turned away, against a warm orange ground that fills the composition. Degas worked the canvas around 1900, the broadly handled contours and saturated colour characteristic of his late style. The painting hangs in the Phillips Collection, Washington.

title: Monet w1558
description: From the London series Monet painted from his rooms at the Savoy Hotel between 1899 and 1901, showing Waterloo Bridge under an overcast sky with the smoking chimneys of the south bank beyond. Wildenstein 1558; held in a private collection.

title: Mother and daughter
description: An older Tahitian woman in dark blue clothing sits beside a younger woman in a red dress, the two figures close together against a green and ochre landscape. The canvas, titled Mother and Daughter, dates from around 1900 and is attributed to Gauguin's late Tahitian period.

title: Nitta Yoshisada
description: A mounted samurai in full armour endures a barrage of arrows as he shelters beside a large tree, his white horse beneath him in a stormy landscape. The print depicts Nitta Yoshisada, the fourteenth-century warrior commander celebrated in medieval chronicles, and was published in 1900 by Tsuchiya Kōitsu. The dense arrow shower and theatrical composition are characteristic of the musha-e (warrior-picture) tradition.
credit: Ukiyo-e.org
