title: Painter David drawing Marie-Antoinette led to her execution
description: Jacques-Louis David sketches Marie Antoinette in the tumbril as she is led to the guillotine, the queen seated upright with her hands bound behind her. Painted in 1900 by the Belgian artist Joseph-Emmanuel van den Büssche, the canvas dramatises the famous October 1793 sketch David made from a window on the rue Saint-Honoré.

title: Peter II and Princess Elizabeth Petrovna Riding to Hound
description: Peter II and Princess Elizabeth Petrovna ride out to hound — the young emperor on a grey horse, Elizabeth alongside him — borzoi streaming across the foreground beneath a cloudy sky. Serov painted the work in tempera on cardboard in 1900; it is held in the Russian Museum, St. Petersburg.

title: Portrait of Princess Zinaida Yusupova
description: Princess Zinaida Yusupova sits on a flower-patterned sofa in a white dress with a dark velvet bodice, a large white borzoi beside her in an interior hung with paintings. Valentin Serov worked on the portrait between 1900 and 1902; it now belongs to the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg (abbreviated GRM).

title: The Artist’s Garden in Giverny
description: Rows of irises beneath espaliered fruit trees in the artist's own garden at Giverny, which he designed and tended as obsessively as he painted it. The diagonal furrows of mauve and violet flowers organise the canvas as a near-abstract chromatic grid.

title: Train Smoke
description: Tall pine trees frame a sweeping fjord landscape at dusk, while a plume of white locomotive steam billows through the foliage in the middle ground. Sailing boats dot the calm water and islands lie in the distance beneath a pink-violet sky. Painted in 1900 and now in the Munch Museum, Oslo, the work turns industrial incursion into an organic element within a richly coloured natural scene.

title: Буря над Евпаторией Айвазовский
description: A dramatic seascape by Russian marine painter Ivan Aivazovsky (1817–1900) depicting stormy weather over the port city of Yevpatoria on the Crimean coast. The work exemplifies Aivazovsky's mastery of turbulent seascapes and atmospheric effects. Housed in the Russian Museum collection.

title: Спящая царевна
description: Viktor Vasnetsov's "The Sleeping Queen" (Спящая царевна) is a monumental symbolist painting depicting the Russian fairy-tale princess in enchanted slumber. Created in the early 20th century, the work exemplifies Vasnetsov's mastery of Russian mythological and folkloric themes through luminous color and dreamlike composition. The painting is housed in the Vasnetsov memorial house in Moscow.

title: Mika Morozov
description: Four-year-old Mika Morozov sits forward on a slatted wooden chair or cot, dressed in a white shirt, his wide eyes and parted lips giving the portrait its celebrated expression of vivid, almost startled alertness. Valentin Serov painted the child of the Moscow collector Mikhail Morozov in 1901; the canvas hangs in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
credit: CD-ROM "Государственная Третьяковская галерея". Издание 2-е; Допол. Издательство: AlexSoft, 2004; [/image/_id/314# Третьяковская галерея]

title: Portrait of Ivan Bilibin
description: The illustrator Ivan Bilibin sits with long dark hair and a pointed beard, a white ruffled shirt-front and a red flower in the lapel of his dark coat, painted in broad, fluid strokes against a dark green interior. Kustodiev portrayed him in 1901, when Bilibin was producing the illustrated Russian fairy-tale books that made his name.
Paul Cézanne, French, 1839–1906 Study of a Skull, 1902–04 Watercolor and graphite on buff wove paper 22. 9 x 31 cm. (9 x 12 3/16 in.
credit: Henry and Rose Pearlman Collection

title: 1902 Monet Die Waterloo-Brücke anagoria
description: From Monet's London series, painted from his rooms at the Savoy Hotel overlooking the Thames. Waterloo Bridge dissolves into morning mist, its arches reduced to violet silhouettes while factory chimneys smoke on the far bank; the canvas, signed and dated 1902, is in the Hamburger Kunsthalle.

title: Barbarian Tales
description: Two young Tahitian women sit in a flowering grove while a crouching red-haired devil, an exaggerated likeness of the Dutch painter Meyer de Haan, lurks behind them. Painted in 1902 on Hiva Oa and now at the Museum Folkwang in Essen, the picture revisits Gauguin's old Pont-Aven companion as a demonic figure shadowing his Marquesan paradise.
credit: Museum Folkwang

title: Bottle
description: A dark bottle, a glass carafe, a stoneware jug and a scatter of lemons stand on a draped table. Watercolour and graphite on paper of about 1902 to 1906, in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid. Cézanne left much of the sheet bare, letting the white paper carry the highlights between thin washes.
credit: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid, Colección Permanente

title: Dinner
description: Bakst's 'Dinner' of 1902 shows an elegantly dressed woman in a black gown and wide-brimmed black hat seated at a white-clothed restaurant table, a bowl of oranges before her. The restrained palette and confidently simplified forms belong to his St Petersburg period, when he was closely associated with the World of Art circle in the years before his celebrated work for Diaghilev's Ballets Russes.

title: His Imperial Majesty Nicholas II
description: Tsar Nicholas II stands in the full dress uniform of the 2nd Dragoons, Royal Scots Greys, his bearskin tucked under one arm. Serov painted the portrait in 1902 for the regiment, of which the Emperor served as Colonel-in-Chief from 1894 until 1918, and it now hangs in the Royal Scots Dragoon Guards Museum in Edinburgh.
credit: Art UK : entry his-imperial-majesty-nicholas-ii-emperor-of-russia-kg-col186207 , image , (detail); alaintruong.com

title: Houses of Parliament
description: From the London series begun in 1899 from a balcony at the Savoy, the Palace of Westminster looms as a violet silhouette through Thames fog. Monet pursued the same view across hours and weathers, finishing many canvases later in the Giverny studio.
credit: Unknown Unknown (image is in the public domain; see below)

title: Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives at Sunrise
description: The walled Old City catches first light from the Mount of Olives, the Dome of the Rock luminous above the Kidron Valley. One of Bauernfeind's last major canvases, painted after he made Jerusalem his home, it trades street bustle for an almost devotional topographic stillness.

title: Kustodiyev Mate
description: Vasily Mathé (1856–1917) stands at a table spread with large prints, a magnifying glass in hand, his gaze directed at the viewer. Painted by Kustodiev in 1902, the portrait honours the printmaker during the period when Kustodiev was still close to his Repin training at the Academy.

title: L'Esprit Moderne et le Catholicisme
description: Front and back covers of Gauguin's handwritten 1902 manuscript L'Esprit Moderne et le Catholicisme, with watercolour and gouache decoration of Tahitian figures and ornamental script. Written on Hiva Oa near the end of his life, the polemical text attacked the Catholic mission's authority over the Marquesans, an argument that earned Gauguin a libel conviction shortly before his death.
credit: Scan from Brettell, Richard; with Peter Zegers (1988) "The Final Years: Tahiti and Hivaoa" in The Art of Paul Gauguin , National Gallery of Art , pp. 468−71 ISBN : 0-8212-1723-2 . Museum page

title: Le sorcier d'Hiva-Oa
description: A long-haired Marquesan in a short blue tunic and red cape stands frontally with a dog and bird at his feet, two veiled women shrinking behind a tree. Painted on Hiva Oa in 1902 and now at the Musée d'Art moderne in Liège, the figure is based on Haapuani, a local healer Gauguin had befriended in his final years.

title: Notre-Dame
description: Notre-Dame's twin towers rise as muted mauve-brown forms above the Seine, viewed from an elevated vantage point over the river and a bridge, with tiny figures on the quay below. Matisse painted this oil on paper in 1902, using structural colour blocks of blue and green to simplify the Parisian cityscape. The work is held at the Albright-Knox Art Gallery.
credit: Albright–Knox Art Gallery

title: Riders on the Beach
description: Riders on the Beach shows several horsemen seen mostly from behind moving across a pale sandy shore, tall bare trees framing the scene at left. Gauguin painted this canvas in 1902 on the island of Hiva Oa during his final years in the Marquesas, treating the figures as a decorative frieze against the muted beach and sky.

title: Riders on the Beach
description: The second version of Riders on the Beach shows a group of horsemen, including figures in white and red, moving across a vivid pink-lavender shore toward the sea, with a standing woman in the foreground. Painted in 1902 on Hiva Oa, the canvas distils the scene into a flat decorative frieze of saturated colour. It is one of two versions Gauguin painted that year.

title: Self-portrait
description: Eakins faces the viewer in a dark suit and waistcoat, his grey-streaked hair swept back and a trimmed beard and goatee framing a direct, unsparing gaze. Painted in 1902 as his diploma piece upon election to the National Academy of Design, the canvas is among the rare self-portraits the Philadelphia realist produced in his maturity.

title: Still-Life with Parrots
description: Several exotic birds with brilliantly coloured plumage lie across a white cloth beside a dark ceramic vessel and a large gourd, with a gilt-framed sculptural idol presiding over the scene from the background. The canvas, signed and dated 1902, was painted during Gauguin's final years on Hiva Oa and exemplifies his late Polynesian still-life idiom. It is now in the Pushkin Museum of Fine Arts, Moscow.

title: The Moon
description: Titled 'Clair de Lune', this panel shows a partially draped woman standing before a crescent moon, wrapped in a dark star-strewn shawl and crowned with flowers, set within an elaborate floral border. Mucha works in a nocturnal, dream-laden register, with deep olive and gold tones enriching the atmospheric night scene.

title: William M. Chase
description: Sargent's full-length portrait of William Merritt Chase shows the older painter holding palette and brushes, his pince-nez and white cravat catching the light against a near-black ground. The fluid, broadly handled paint that reduces costume and setting to shadow exemplifies Sargent's debt to Velázquez. Painted in 1902, the canvas is now held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 12471)

title: 2560px-Jean-Leon Gerome - Souvenir of Acheres
description: Two deer pause amid golden autumn bracken beneath an orange-leafed tree, with hazier woodland and tall slender trees beyond under a soft sky. Gérôme painted Souvenir of Achères in 1903, the year before his death, setting aside his Orientalist subjects for a quiet record of the French countryside. The canvas is held by the Columbus Museum of Art.

title: Ceremonial Sitting of the State Council on 7 May 1901 Marking the Centenary of its Foundation
englishTitle: Ceremonial Sitting of the State Council on 7 May 1901
description: An immense official commission recording a centenary session of the Russian State Council in the Mariinsky Palace. Repin marshals more than eighty individual portraits into a coherent ceremonial space, his late brushwork looser and more atmospheric than the tightly modelled realism of his earlier work.

title: Houses of Parliament
description: The Palace of Westminster looms through Thames fog at a moment of breaking sun. Monet painted some nineteen Parliament views from a balcony at St Thomas's Hospital between 1900 and 1904, returning to his hotel each evening to refine the series from memory and notes.

title: Lyubov Gritsenko-Bakst
description: Lyubov Gritsenko, daughter of the collector Pavel Tretyakov and Bakst's future wife, stands on an outdoor terrace wearing a white dress and a wide-brimmed hat, with a wooded lakeside landscape behind her. Léon Bakst painted this portrait in 1903; it entered the Tretyakov Gallery (inventory no. 22001) and is now recorded in the Goskatalog of the Russian Museum Fund.
credit: Бакст Лев Самойлович. Портрет Л. П. Гриценко-Бакст | Государственный каталог Музейного фонда Российской Федерации

title: Monet w1656
description: From the early water-lily series of 1903, showing clouds reflected on the surface of the lily pond at Giverny (Le bassin des nymphéas, nuages). Wildenstein 1656; held in a private collection.

title: Old guitarist chicago
description: Oil painting by Pablo Picasso from his Blue Period. An elderly blind musician clutches his guitar, rendered in muted blues and grays. The work is held at the Art Institute of Chicago.

title: Self-portrait
description: Gauguin sets his bespectacled face against a pale background, the gaze direct and the features marked by illness in his final months on Hiva Oa. Painted in 1903 and now at the Kunstmuseum Basel, this is considered the last known self-portrait of the artist.

title: The Brooch. Eva Mudocci
description: The English violinist Eva Mudocci, with whom Munch had a brief affair, gazes from a cloud of dark hair in this lithograph. Drawn directly onto stone in Berlin and printed in soft black, it is among Munch's most tender portraits, sometimes called his Mona Lisa.

title: The Houes of Parliament
description: Westminster's Gothic silhouette dissolves into the Thames mist while gulls wheel through a violet, sulphur-tinted sky. Begun on the terrace of St Thomas's Hospital during Monet's 1899-1901 London campaigns and completed in Giverny, the canvas belongs to a series tracking the same view across hours and weather.
credit: Princeton University Art Museum

title: The Smoker
description: A robed man sits on a carved wooden bench, a long-stemmed pipe at his feet, in a richly appointed interior whose walls are faced with elaborate geometric tilework. Costume, carpet, and inlaid surfaces are rendered with Deutsch's characteristic precision. Painted in 1903, the work belongs to the series of Orientalist interiors the Austrian-born artist produced in his Paris studio, drawing on studies and props gathered during his Egyptian travels.

title: Virgin
description: A gaunt naked woman is draped across the bare branches of a gnarled tree, her elongated body rendered in precise etched line; a bird perches on a branch above. Part of the Inventionen series of etchings Klee produced in 1903, the print is held in the collection of the Museum of Modern Art, New York.

title: What freedom!
description: A young gymnasium student and his companion dance in the surf of the iced-up Neva, the wave breaking around their boots while the boy throws open his coat to the wind. Painted in 1903 and now in the Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg, the canvas was Repin's ambivalent response to the new generation on the eve of the 1905 revolution.

title: Assortment of Hepaticae from Kunstformen der Natur
description: Plate 82 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904) presents an array of liverworts (Hepaticae) including both thalloid genera such as Marchantia and Lunularia and numerous foliose species from Scapania, Lepidozia, and Jungermannia. The coloured lithograph arranges gametophytes, archegonial heads, and sporophytes across the page to reveal the diverse architectural forms within the group.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 82: Hepaticae (see here , here and here )

title: Ellen Terry
dateCreated: Unknown date, but author died in 1904. It is believed that the portrait was painted around the date that the author married the subject, 1864. At that time, the subject was 17 years old.
description: Dame (Alice) Ellen Terry ('Choosing') , by George Frederic Watts (died 1904). The subject is (Alice) Ellen Terry (1847-1928). See source website for additional information.

title: Haeckel Acanthometra
description: Lithographic plate gathering Acantharian protozoa whose star-shaped strontium-sulfate skeletons radiate twenty spicules from a central point. Haeckel arranged the microscopic single-celled marine organisms in a cathedral-like symmetry, advancing his argument that morphological law unites the smallest plankton with the greatest works of design.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 21: Acanthometra (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Acanthophracta
description: Plate 41 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904) depicts Acanthophractan radiolarians whose silica lattice shells radiate spines and form intricate polyhedral and stellate tests. Haeckel arranged several species, including Dorataspis and Diploconus, to reveal the geometric variety within the group and his conviction that microscopic marine life embodied universal laws of natural ornament.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 41: Acanthophracta (see here and here )

title: Haeckel Acephala
description: Plate of headless bivalve molluscs arrayed for symmetry: Venus clams, cockles, and related shells shown in opening, valve, and hinge views. Haeckel exploits the radiating ribs and growth rings to draw the eye outward from each pair, treating malacology as ornamental design.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 55: Bivalvia (see here , here , here and here and Biodiversity Heritage Library )

title: Haeckel Actiniae
description: Sea anemones rendered with their tentacle crowns spread in jewel-toned discs, including Cereus pedunculatus and Aiptasia mutabilis. The plate compresses several species into a single bouquet, using the column striations and radial muscle bands as decorative geometry.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate/planche 49: Actiniae (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Ammonitida
description: Fossil ammonite shells from the Mesozoic, shown in lateral and ventral views to display sutured chambers and ribbed coiling. The composition makes the logarithmic spiral and ornamentation of Cardioceras and Schloenbachia legible at a glance, treating extinct cephalopods as design specimens.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 44: Ammonitida (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Amphoridea
description: Plate 95 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904) brings together Palaeozoic cystoid echinoderms — including Enoploura and Pleurocystites — alongside juvenile and larval forms of living echinoderms such as Ophiothrix, Luidia, and Arbacia. The juxtaposition of armoured fossil plates with delicate modern larvae underscores Haeckel's comparative approach to echinoderm morphology across geological time.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 95: Amphoridea (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Anthomedusae
description: Hydromedusae of the Anthomedusae order, shown from above, below and in lateral section to expose the gonads and gastrovascular canals. Trailing tentacles fall in glassy curtains around bell-shaped umbrellas, a study in translucent radial symmetry.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 46: Anthomedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Antilopina
description: Nine antelope and bovid species drawn full-body, including four-horned antelope, black wildebeest, sitatunga, pronghorn, waterbuck, sable antelope, addax, greater kudu, and bushbuck. The plate functions as a comparative survey of horn forms — spiral, lyrate, forked, and straight — set against lightly indicated ground. From Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 100.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 100: Antilopina (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Arachnida
description: Spiders and arachnids in close comparative study: orb-weavers with spiny abdomens (Gasteracantha, Micrathena), a garden spider, a lynx spider, and a tailless whipscorpion (Phrynichus reniformis), alongside four mite species of the Cepheus group. Each specimen is magnified and set against a warm ground to expose sculptural cuticle detail. From Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 66.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 66: Arachnida (see here , here and here ) Modifications for Wikipedia Black borders removed with stamp tool Background brightened with mask

title: Haeckel Ascidiae
description: Sea squirts presented as solitary forms, in section, and as colonial aggregates. Boltenia echinata is shown bristling with spicules above a longitudinal cut that reveals the U-shaped gut, while compound ascidians cluster like ripening fruit on the lower register.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 85: Ascidiacea (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Ascomycetes
description: Plate from Kunstformen der Natur showing a symmetrical arrangement of sac fungi, with cup-shaped fruiting bodies and powdery mildews magnified and framed like ornament. Haeckel's lithographs translated microscopic biology into decorative compositions that fed directly into Art Nouveau design.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 73: Ascomycetes (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Aspidonia
description: Horseshoe crabs and their extinct sea-scorpion kin, including Tachypleus gigas in adult and larval form alongside the Silurian eurypterid Eurypterus tetragonophthalmus. The plate stages a deep-time comparison between living and fossil chelicerates.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 47: Aspidonia (see here , here , here and here and Biodiversity Heritage Library )

title: Haeckel Asteridea
description: Adult and larval starfish across several species: bipinnaria, brachiolaria, and pentapalmar larvae of Asterias rubens arranged in the upper register, with a large mature Asterias at centre. The lower portion shows the cushion starfish Pteraster stellifer and the webbed Hymenaster echinulatus, each rendered from above and below. From Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 40.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 40: Asteridea (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Basimycetes
description: Stinkhorn fungi arranged on a dark ground: the latticed Clathrus ruber, the tall veiled stinkhorn (Dictyophora madonna), the starfish-armed Aseroë rubra, and Phallus impudicus with a lengthwise section of its volva. Cross-sections of egg stages appear alongside mature fruiting bodies. From Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 63.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 63: Basimycetes (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Batrachia
description: Tropical tree frogs and marsupial frogs grouped for skin-pattern variety, including Hyla meridionalis, Rhacophorus pardalis, and the egg-brooding Gastrotheca. Splayed toe pads and warted backs are emphasized to register adhesive and camouflage adaptations.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 68: Batrachia (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Blastoidea
description: Extinct Paleozoic blastoids with budlike calyces drawn from above and the side, including Pentremites pyriformis. The five-petaled ambulacral fields are featured prominently, and one specimen appears with its delicate brachioles extended, folded, and removed.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 80: Blastoidea (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Bryozoa
description: Freshwater and marine moss animals centered on Cristatella mucedo, traced through statoblast, juvenile, and mature colony stages. Haeckel draws the gelatinous mat with its lophophore crowns extended in a feathered ring around each zooid.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 23: Bryozoa (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Bryozoa 33
description: Calcified bryozoan skeletons enlarged so that individual zooecia read as tiled honeycomb. Phaeostachys, Cribrilina, and Umbonula appear as porous lacework, with detail shifting between whole colonies and single chambered cells.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 33: Bryozoa (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Calcispongiae
description: Calcareous sponges of the Leucosolenia and Guancha groups, shown as branching tubular colonies anchored by spiculate roots. Haeckel sets habitus drawings beside isolated triradiate spicules to expose the skeletal architecture beneath the soft tissue.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 5: Calcispongiae (see here , here )

title: Haeckel Campanariae
description: Hydroid colonies of the family Campanulariidae, slender stems bearing bell-shaped hydranths and reproductive gonophores. The plate threads the colonies like vines across the page, foregrounding the hydrothecae as cup-on-stalk ornaments.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 45: Campanariae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Chaetopoda
description: Marine bristle worms with their feeding crowns expanded: feather duster Sabellastarte indica, the calcareous-tubed Hydroides, and the spiraled fan of Sabella spallanzanii. Tube architecture and feathered radioles are treated as the principal motif.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 96: Chaetopoda (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Chelonia
description: Comparative tableau of turtles and tortoises from Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 89. The plate ranges from the leatherback Dermochelys coriacea and hawksbill Eretmochelys imbricata at the top, through the Argentine snake-necked turtle Hydromedusa tectifera and mata mata Chelys fimbriata in the middle, to the geometric tortoise Psammobates geometricus and Galápagos giant tortoise at the lower register, with the common snapping turtle Chelydra serpentina completing the survey. Carapace pattern and head form serve as the organising contrast across the group.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 89: Chelonia (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Chiroptera
description: Bat heads arranged in frontal and lateral views, from the long-eared Plecotus auritus and leaf-nosed Megaderma to Chrotopterus auritus and the horseshoe bat Rhinolophus ferrumequinum, from Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 67. The plate lines up specialised noseleaves and ear funnels in multiple orientations to demonstrate the morphological diversity underlying echolocating sensory anatomy across fifteen species.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 67: Chiroptera (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Ciliata
description: A survey of ciliate protozoa from Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 3, ranging from the vase-shaped tintinnid loricae of Codonella and Dictyocysta at the top to the large trumpet-shaped Stentor polymorphus and the branching colonies of Carchesium and Vorticella in the lower half. The plate moves from solitary microscopic shells to elaborate arborescent colonies, demonstrating the breadth of form within this single protozoan class.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 3: Ciliata (see here , here )

title: Haeckel Cirripedia
description: Goose barnacles in habit and dissection: Lepas anatifera intact, then with one valve cut away to reveal the feathered cirri and curled body. Conchoderma colonies are shown encrusting the whale-barnacle Coronula, a study in commensal stacking.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 57: Cirripedia (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Coniferae
description: Conifer cones and foliage from monkey puzzle, Norway spruce, Santa Lucia fir, hinoki cypress, and Japanese thujopsis. Haeckel arranges scale-by-scale dissections beside intact cones to compare the geometry of seed-bearing structures across the group.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 94: Coniferae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Copepoda
description: Planktonic copepods drawn with antennae and setae fanned out to fill the page, including the iridescent Calocalanus pavo with its peacock-tail furca. The plate celebrates ornamental setal arrays that drag through seawater for propulsion and sensing.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 56: Copepoda (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Crinoidea
description: Stalked sea lilies of the genera Endoxocrinus and Saracrinus, drawn full-length with feathery arms unfurled above jointed columns. Detail studies of stem ossicles emphasize the segmented, almost machined construction of these living fossil echinoderms.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 20: Crinoidea (see here and here )

title: Haeckel Ctenophorae
description: Comb jellies suspended in implied current, their eight ciliated bands shown as iridescent ribbons running down translucent bodies. Haeckelia rubra appears from above and side, joined by Hormiphora and the winged Callianira bialata.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 27: Ctenophorae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Cubomedusae
description: Box jellyfish in lateral view, the cuboidal bell of Chirodropus and Carybdea hung over trailing tentacle bundles. The plate isolates the rigid cubic geometry that distinguishes cubozoans from softer bell-shaped medusae.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 78: Cubomedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Cyrtoidea
description: Radiolarian shells of the Cyrtoidea group, eleven mineralized lattices arranged in three rows. Helmet, bell, and tower forms display the silica skeletons that fascinated Haeckel from his Challenger expedition reports onward.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 31: Cyrtoidea (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Cystoidea
description: Paleozoic cystoid echinoderms shown from above to display the polygonal calyx plating and pore-rhomb respiratory structures. Staurocystis, Glyptosphaerites, and Cystoblastus are arranged as a comparative key to early stalked echinoderm armor.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 90: Cystoidea (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Decapoda
description: Decapod crustaceans in dorsal view, from the spiky Daldorfia horrida and long-eyed Podophthalmus vigil to the banded coral shrimp Stenopus hispidus. The plate revels in carapace ornament, spines, and elongated chelae across crab and shrimp morphologies.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 86: Decapoda (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Desmidiea
description: A plate of desmid green algae, single-celled freshwater organisms whose cell walls split into mirror-image semicells. Haeckel arranges Staurastrum and related genera to highlight their geometric symmetry, including views of mating cells in which two halves conjugate to form a zygospore.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 24: Desmidiea (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Diatomea
description: An assembly of marine and freshwater diatoms, microscopic algae enclosed in silica frustules. Top and side views display the intricate punctate ornament of genera such as Auliscus, Cymbella and Campyloneis, drawn at a scale that turns optical microscopy into ornamental design.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 84: Diatomeae (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Diatomea 4
description: Triangular and lyre-shaped diatom valves arranged in radial symmetry, including Triceratium and Lyrella species seen in valve view. The plate emphasises the lattice of areolae perforating the silica shell, a feature only resolvable under high magnification.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 4: Diatomeae (see here and here )

title: Haeckel Discoidea
description: Radiolarians of the order Discoidea, single-celled marine plankton with star- and disc-shaped silica skeletons. Most figures derive from Haeckel's own 1887 Challenger Expedition monograph, where he described thousands of species from deep-sea sediment samples.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 11: Discoidea (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Discomedusae 18
description: Studies of small disc jellyfish, with Linantha lunulata shown from above and in side profile alongside developmental stages of Palephyra. The plate documents both the radial gastrovascular canals visible from above and the bell musculature seen during swimming.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 18: Discomedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Discomedusae 28
description: Multiple views of rhizostome jellyfish from the Toreuma group, with Toreuma bellagemma rendered from the side, oral surface, and aboral surface, alongside Toreuma thamnostoma and Cassiopeja cyclobalia. The arrangement presents each species from several angles to document mouth-arms, gonad position, and the gelatinous bell as a coordinated anatomical study. Plate 28 of Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904).
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 28: Discomedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Discomedusae 8
description: Desmonema annasethe, a jellyfish Haeckel named after his late wife Anna Sethe, who died the year before he encountered the species. The trailing oral arms and tentacles, drawn in cascading filaments, are often read as a personal memorial within the scientific atlas.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 8: Discomedusae

title: Haeckel Discomedusae 88
description: Large rhizostome medusae including Pilema and Rhopilema shown from side, aboral and oral aspects. The plate captures the eight branched mouth-arms that replace a single central mouth in this group, filtering plankton through countless secondary openings.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 88: Discomedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Discomedusae 98
description: Aurelia and related semaeostome jellyfish presented alongside the polyp stage budding off juvenile medusae by strobilation. Pairing adult and larval forms on one sheet illustrates the alternation of generations central to scyphozoan life cycles.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 98: Trachomedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Echinidea
description: Sand dollars and sea biscuits including Clypeaster rosaceus and Encope emarginata, drawn with and without spines. Aboral views expose the five-petalled ambulacral pattern of the test, a hallmark of the irregular echinoids adapted to burrowing in sediment.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 30: Echinidea (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Echinidea 60
description: Cidaroid sea urchins including Cidaris tribuloides and Prionocidaris baculosa, with mouth and periproct regions shown stripped of spines to expose tubercles and plate sutures, alongside isolated pedicellaria, tube-foot endplates, and spine cross-sections from Centrostephanus, Phyllacanthus, and Sphaerechinus. Plate 60 of Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904).
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 60: Echinidea (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Filicinae
description: Staghorn ferns of the genus Platycerium, traced through successive frond stages from young plant to mature epiphyte. The shield-like sterile basal fronds and forked fertile blades are drawn to emphasise the dimorphism characteristic of the genus.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 52: Filicinae (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Filicinae 92
description: A composition of tropical ferns including tree ferns of Cyatheaceae, the bird's-nest fern Asplenium nidus and the eusporangiate Angiopteris. Habit drawings juxtapose growth forms ranging from arborescent trunks to ribbon-leaved Monogramma.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 92: Filicinae at the Tjiburrum waterfalls near Tjibodas , Mount Gede , Java (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Flagellata
description: Choanoflagellates and related flagellate protists arranged as colonial branched assemblages, including Anthophysa, Cephalothamnium and Codonocladium. The collared cells on stalked rosettes anticipate the body plan of sponge choanocytes.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 13: Flagellata (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Florideae
description: Red algae of the Florideophyceae, with Chondrus crispus, the Irish moss of north Atlantic shores, given prominence. The plate displays the cartilaginous, repeatedly dichotomous thalli that produce carrageenan and were already commercially harvested in the nineteenth century.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 65: Florideae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Fucoideae
description: Brown seaweeds drawn at habit scale, including the giant Pacific kelp Nereocystis luetkeana, Cutleria and Cystoseira. The selection traces the morphological range from pneumatocyst-bearing kelps to bushy littoral species of the order Fucales.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 15: Fucoideae (see here and here )

title: Haeckel Gamochonia
description: Coleoid cephalopods including Chiroteuthis, Histioteuthis and the common octopus, drawn from below and above. The plate sets pelagic deep-sea squids with hooked arms beside benthic octopuses to compare arm crowns, fins and chromatophore patterning.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 54: Gamochonia (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Gorgonida
description: Gorgonian octocorals with skeletal spicules detailed beside whole polyps and branch fragments. Eunicella and Primnoella illustrate the eight-tentacled polyps and calcareous sclerites that stiffen the proteinaceous gorgonin axis of the colony.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 39: Gorgonida (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Hexacoralla
description: Solitary and colonial stony corals of the Hexacorallia, including the cold-water reef-builder Lophelia prolifera. Skeletal views from above and the side reveal the six-fold symmetry of septa within each calcified corallite.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 26: Hexacoralla (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Hexacoralla 69
description: Reef corals from the genera Turbinaria, Pavona and Hydnophora arranged as a compositional bouquet. Lobate and frond-like growth forms are contrasted with branching morphologies to display the architectural variety produced by colonial scleractinian polyps.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 69: Hexacoralla (see here , here , here and here for details)

title: Haeckel Hexactinellae
description: Glass sponges of the class Hexactinellida, including the Venus's flower basket Euplectella aspergillum and the branching Farrea occa at centre. Whole-body drawings in the lower half are paired with magnified diagrams of isolated siliceous spicules — hexasters, amphidiscs, and plumicomes — arranged across the upper portion. Plate 35 of Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904).
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 35: Hexactinellae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Lacertilia
description: A gathering of lizards including the flying dragon Draco volans, the Texas horned lizard Phrynosoma cornutum and a Trioceros chameleon. The plate compares cranial casques, dermal spines and gliding membranes as variations on a single squamate body plan.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 79: Lacertilia (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Leptomedusae
description: Hydrozoan medusae of the order Leptothecata, including Aequorea and Zygocanna, depicted in blue from above and the side. The radial canals and frilled tentacle masses of the bell are emphasised throughout the composition. Plate 36 of Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904); Aequorea species are known in life for their bioluminescence, produced by the calcium-activated photoprotein aequorin.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 36: Leptomedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Lichenes
description: A diverse assemblage of lichen species shown in growth habit on a dark ground, including branching and cup-bearing Cladonia, the large lobed Lobaria pulmonaria (Sticta pulmonaria in Haeckel's nomenclature), and several foliose Parmelia species. The plate surveys the breadth of lichen thallus architecture — fruticose, foliose, and crustose forms — across temperate and boreal habitats. Plate 83 of Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904).
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 83: Lichenes (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Melethallia
description: Coenobial green algae of the genus Pediastrum, whose flat plate-shaped colonies of polygonal cells float in fresh water. Arranged in concentric rings, the species illustrate how a fixed cell number per colony produces star-, wheel- and disc-shaped geometries.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 34: Melethallia (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Muscinae
description: A garden of mosses including Polytrichum commune, Sphagnum palustre and the dung moss Splachnum luteum with its inflated apophysis. Capsules, setae and leafy gametophytes are drawn at habit scale to compare bryophyte sporophyte architecture.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 72: Muscinae (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Mycetozoa
description: Slime moulds shown across their full life cycle, from amoeboid swarm cells emerging from spores to mature plasmodia of Badhamia and Trichia. The plate treats Mycetozoa as protists rather than fungi, reflecting Haeckel's broader reorganisation of the kingdoms of life.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 93: Mycetozoa (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Narcomedusae
description: Narcomedusan hydrozoans, deep-water jellyfish whose bell margin is scalloped into discrete lobes. Pegantha, Aeginura and Solmaris are shown from below to display the peripheral tentacles arising directly from the exumbrella, a defining feature of the order.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 16: Narcomedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Nepenthaceae
description: The tropical pitcher plant Nepenthes gymnamphora, drawn with its modified leaves forming fluid-filled traps. Carnivorous insectivory had been confirmed only decades earlier, and the plate emphasises the lid, peristome and tendril that suspend each pitcher.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 62: Nepenthaceae (see here , here and here and Biodiversity Heritage Library )

title: Haeckel Nudibranchia
description: Sea slugs of multiple aeolid and dorid lineages, including the orange-tipped Facelina auriculata and the spotted Tritonia hombergii. Cerata, rhinophores and branchial plumes are rendered in colour to record pigmentation that fades from preserved specimens.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 43: Nudibranchia (see here , here and here and Biodiversity Heritage Library )

title: Haeckel Ophiodea
description: Brittle stars arranged in radial symmetry across the plate, their slender, articulated arms fanning outward from small central discs. Haeckel emphasized the spiny ornamentation and pentaradial geometry of these echinoderms, drawing on specimens collected by the Challenger expedition.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 10: Ophiodea (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Ophiodea 70
description: Basket stars and brittle stars displayed from multiple angles, including the branching, fractal-like arms of Astrophyton at center. The composition contrasts dense knotted limbs with the more sparse, whip-like rays of smaller ophiuroids to convey echinoderm diversity.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 70: Ophiodea (see here , here and here , and Biodiversity Heritage Library )

title: Haeckel Orchidae
description: Tropical orchids rendered as a dense bouquet in plate 74 of Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904), including Odontoglossum, Oncidium, Cattleya, and Cypripedium (slipper orchid) species. The composition showcases the extraordinary diversity of floral form within the family — lipped labella, ruffled petals, hooded pouches, and long-spurred blossoms — drawn from horticultural specimens known to nineteenth-century collectors.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 74: Orchidae (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Ostraciontes
description: Boxfish and cowfish drawn from multiple angles to highlight their rigid carapace of fused scale plates. Haeckel sets the angular, polyhedral bodies against one another to underscore how these tropical reef fish trade flexibility for armored defense.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 42: Ostraciontes (see here , here and here

title: Haeckel Pennatulida
description: Sea pens and sea pansies displayed as feather-like and disc-shaped colonies, with enlargements of individual polyps along the rachis. The plate documents the colonial architecture of these soft corals, showing how a single founding polyp gives rise to a polymorphic colony.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 19: Pennatulida (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Peridinea
description: Marine dinoflagellates magnified to reveal their armored cellulose plates, flagellar grooves, and projecting horns. Species like Ceratium tripos and Ornithocercus magnificus dominate the composition, their delicate sail-like extensions translated into precise lithographic line.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 14: Peridinea (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Peromedusae
description: Crown jellies of the genus Periphylla shown from side and underside, the conical bell ringed by deep grooves and trailing tentacles. The plate captures the bioluminescent deep-sea medusae described from Challenger expedition hauls.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 38: Peromedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Phaeodaria 1
description: Microscopic radiolarians with siliceous skeletons constructed in geometric forms, including the icosahedral lattice of Circogonia and the radial spines of Haeckeliana. Haeckel renders these planktonic single-celled organisms as if they were architectural blueprints.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 1: Phaeodaria (see here , here )

title: Haeckel Phaeodaria 61
description: Detailed terminations of radiolarian spicules from the Aulographis group, each tip elaborated into candelabras, asterisks, or forks. The plate isolates these microscopic ornament details to show the structural inventiveness of phaeodarian skeletons.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 61: Phaeodaria (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Platodes
description: Plate 75 of Kunstformen der Natur (1904) surveys the diversity of parasitic flatworms, ranging from cercariae larvae with forked tails — including Cercaria dichotoma as studied by Johannes Müller — to adult monogeneans such as Diplozoon paradoxum (shown as a mated pair) and the mature proglottids and scolex of Taenia solium. Disc-shaped and elongated adult forms dominate the composition alongside the smaller larval stages, together illustrating the full span of platyhelminth body plans.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 75: Platodes (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Polycyttaria
description: Colonial radiolarians shown as gelatinous spheres studded with individual cells and symbiotic zooxanthellae. The plate documents social plankton, where dozens of single-celled organisms cohabit in a shared transparent matrix.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 51: Polycyttaria (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Prosobranchia
description: Marine snails arranged as a still-life of shells, including the long-spired Murex pecten, the cone of Conus imperialis, and the harp-ribbed Harpa ventricosa. The plate functions as a survey of gastropod ornament, from spines to glossy enamel.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 53: Prosobranchia

title: Haeckel Rotatoria
description: Microscopic rotifers shown with their ciliated coronas and transparent bodies, including the trumpet-shaped Stephanoceros and the colonial Lacinularia. The plate freezes the spinning corona that gives these freshwater animals their name.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 32: Rotatoria (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Sertulariae
description: Hydroid colonies branching like miniature ferns, with magnified hydrothecae and reproductive gonangia along each stem. The plate emphasizes how these cnidarians blur the line between plant-like growth form and animal anatomy.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 25: Sertulariae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Siphoneae
description: Plate 64 of Kunstformen der Natur (1904) presents the siphonous green algae — organisms in which the entire thallus is one continuous, multinucleate cell. Caulerpa species dominate the composition, their fronds ranging from grape-cluster (C. racemosa) to peltate discs and feathered pinnules; alongside them appear Acetabularia's parasol-like caps, the calcified cylinders of Neomeris, and the plume of Struvea, collectively demonstrating how a single cytoplasm can generate the visual complexity of an entire higher plant.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 64: Siphoneae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Siphonophorae
description: Porpema colonies shown with disc-like floats and trailing sexual polyps, set against magnified gas bladders. The plate documents how a siphonophore is not a single jelly but a coordinated colony of specialized zooids.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 17: Siphonophorae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Siphonophorae 37
description: Physophora hydrostatica colonies arranged with central swimming bells and a skirt of stinging tentacles. Haeckel pairs an overall view with anatomical details of the gas float and individual nectophore to dissect the colonial body plan.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 37: Siphonophorae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Siphonophorae 59
description: A Forskalia-like siphonophore dissected layer by layer, from intact colony to stripped polyp clusters. The sequence reveals the modular construction of a pelagic cnidarian, with each zooid specialized for swimming, feeding, or reproduction.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 59: Siphonophorae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Siphonophorae 7
description: Mature and immature Epibulia and Rhizophysa colonies shown alongside cross-sections of their gas bladders. The plate emphasizes the apical pneumatophore that allows these chains of polyps to drift just below the sea surface.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 7: Siphonophorae (see here , here )

title: Haeckel Siphonophorae 77
description: Praya and Bassia colonies displayed as chains of paired swimming bells with trailing reproductive medusae. Haeckel uses the bilateral nectophores to convey the streamlined hydrodynamics of calycophoran siphonophores.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 77: Siphonophorae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Spirobranchia
description: Brachiopod shells displayed in interior and exterior views, from Paleozoic fossil genera such as Spirifer, Cyrtina, and Rhynchonella alongside living forms including Lingula anatina and Magellania flavescens. Many specimens are opened to show the calcified spiral lophophore supports inside, while others are presented as detached animals without shells. Plate 97 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904), the plate serves as a comparative anatomy reference spanning geological time.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 97: Spirobranchia (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Spumellaria
description: Spherical and spindle-shaped radiolarian skeletons with concentric latticework and radiating spines. The plate isolates the polycystine forms whose silica architecture inspired Haeckel's broader argument that nature is intrinsically geometric.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 91: Spumellaria (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Spyroidea
description: Two-chambered radiolarian skeletons rendered as miniature cages, each with a sagittal constriction and ornamental feet. The composition catalogs the helmet-like Nassellaria forms drawn from Challenger expedition microfossil samples.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 22: Spyroidea (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Stauromedusae
description: Stalked jellyfish (Stauromedusae) rendered as goblet-shaped sessile medusae, including multiple views of Haliclystus auricula and Lucernaria species shown from the side, bottom, and in cross-section of the stalk. The goblet-and-stem body plan and the radiating tentacle clusters at the bell margin are illustrated against a plain ground. Plate 48 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904).
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 48: Stauromedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Stephoidea
description: Ring-shaped radiolarian skeletons with single, double, or triple silica hoops, presented as crowns and lattices. The plate centers on simple-ringed Nassellaria, showing how minimal skeletal motifs can scaffold a living single cell.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 71: Stephoidea (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Teleostei
description: Bizarrely formed bony fish, including seahorses, the leafy sea dragon Phycodurus eques, and the antennated frogfish Antennarius striatus. The plate emphasizes camouflage and modified fins that disguise these teleosts as drifting weed.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 87: Teleostei (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Tetracoralla
description: Solitary and colonial rugose corals shown as polished cross-sections and side views, including the horn-shaped Omphyma turbinata. The plate is essentially paleontological, displaying the four-fold septal symmetry of an extinct Paleozoic order.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 29: Tetracoralla (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Thalamophora 12
description: Miliolid foraminifera arranged as porcelain-like shells with looping chambers, including Quinqueloculina and Cornuspira. The plate magnifies these microscopic shelled protists to reveal the sequential coiling that defines the order.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 12: Thalamophora (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Thalamophora 81
description: A diverse array of benthic foraminifera tests arranged against a dark ground, including flask- and spindle-shaped Lagena species ornamented with ribs and spines, alongside coiled Bulimina and Bolivina, the disc-like Rotalia calcar, and the elongate Cristellaria. The variety of chamber arrangements and surface textures — smooth, ribbed, granulate, and squamose — illustrates the morphological range within multilocular benthic forms. Plate 81 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904).
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 81: Thalamophora (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Thalamphora
description: A comparative survey of foraminiferal diversity arranged against a dark ground, with forms ranging from the elongate stacked-chamber Nodosaria and flask-shaped Lagena to the planktonic globular Globigerina bulloides, the disc-like Nummulites, and the star-shaped Tinoporus and Calcarina. Cross-sections and top views accompany side views to reveal internal chamber sequences. Plate 2 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904).
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 2: Thalamophora (see here , here )

title: Haeckel Thoracostraca
description: A symmetrical plate of malacostracan crustaceans and their larval stages, including the embryo (gastrula) of Lucifer typus, the nauplius larva of Penaeus, a mastigopus postlarva, zoea, alima, and phyllosoma larvae, alongside adult lobster and prawn forms. Haeckel arranges the developmental stages alongside the adults to juxtapose body plans across the life cycle. Plate 76 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904).
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 76: Thoracostraca (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Thuroidea
description: Sea cucumbers (Holothuroidea) and their microscopic skeletal elements arranged against a green ground: the adult bodies of Phyllophorus urna and Sporadipus botellus occupy the centre, flanked by successive auricularia and doliolaria larval stages of Synapta digitata and by a branching tree of Synapta tissue. Surrounding them are dozens of isolated spicules — anchor-, wheel-, and button-shaped — drawn from species across the class to illustrate the structural diversity of holothurian mineralised supports. Plate 50 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904).
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 50: Thuroidea (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Tineida
description: A study of plume and leaf-mining moths in which Alucita and Pterophorus species spread their feathered wings into near-radial patterns. Magnified wing-scale details at the margins underscore the geometric microstructure beneath the apparently dusty surfaces.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 58: Tineida (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Trachomedusae
description: Bell-shaped trachymedusae are drawn from above, beside, and beneath, with the long manubrium of Geryonia trailing like a clapper. The transparent tissues let internal gonads and radial canals show through, turning anatomy into a chandelier-like ornament.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 26: Trachomedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Trochilidae
description: Twelve hummingbird species, including the Sword-billed Hummingbird and Booted Racket-tail, are arranged in a naturalistic composition against a sky-blue and leafy background, displaying iridescent gorgets, crests, and tail streamers. Haeckel's note records that the specimens were drawn from millinery skins, so the postures are decorative rather than observational, foregrounding plumage geometry over flight behaviour. The plate appears as number 99 in Kunstformen der Natur (1904).
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 99: Trochilidae (see here , here and here and Biodiversity Heritage Library )

title: Haeckel Tubulariae
description: Solitary and budding hydromedusae such as Sarsia and Coryne float across the page, several shown in the act of releasing free-swimming medusae from polyp colonies. The plate compresses an entire alternating life cycle into a single ornamental field.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 6: Tubulariae (see here , here )

title: Houses of Parliament
description: One of nineteen views of the Houses of Parliament that Monet worked on from a balcony at St Thomas' Hospital across the Thames. Westminster's Gothic silhouette is silhouetted against a sun-soaked fog, the river burning with reflected colour as atmospheric haze flattens detail into pure tonal envelope.
credit: Vintage frills [1]

title: London
description: Part of Monet's Houses of Parliament series painted from his window at St Thomas's Hospital, the canvas dissolves the Gothic Revival silhouette into mauve and orange vapour. The campaigns of 1899–1904 used the Thames fog as a coloured veil through which Monet tracked the changing hours.
credit: Musée d'Orsay

title: Montagne Sainte-Victoire
description: The limestone ridge of Mont Sainte-Victoire rises beyond a patchwork of fields and trees east of Aix-en-Provence. Oil on canvas of 1904, one of the last in the long series Cézanne painted of the mountain. He built the foreground from overlapping facets of green, ochre and blue that blur the line between plain and sky.

title: Nymphéas
description: Pads of green and lavender float across a pond surface that fills the canvas, sky and bank registering only as reflections among the lilies. With this 1903-08 series Monet refined the immersive water-garden vision that would culminate in the Orangerie cycles.
credit: flickr.com; Sotheby's London,19 June 2007, L07007, lot 7

title: Portrait of Painter Peder Severin Kröyer
description: Tuxen's 1904 full-length portrait shows his Skagen colleague Peder Severin Krøyer standing on a sandy beach in a white summer suit and hat, a walking stick in one hand and what appears to be an artist's bag slung over his arm. The North Sea stretches behind him under a clear sky. The painting is held at the Hungarian National Gallery, Budapest (inv. 191.B).
credit: Yelkrokoyade

title: Sharing the News
description: A woman pauses at a washboard to look up at her companion, who stands smiling and holds a letter she has just received. The exchange between the two figures, set against a worn brick wall, captures the small social moments de Blaas drew from Venetian working life and polished with the slick academic technique that won him wide Edwardian popularity. The canvas is dated 1904.

title: The Flirtation
description: Two young women are seated on a stone bench against a brick wall while a bare-footed young man leans toward them in easy conversation, a basket of fruit at his feet. De Blaas captures a familiar moment of Venetian working-class sociability, dressed in the colourful regional costume he favoured, rendered with the lustrous academic finish that brought him success at Edwardian salons. The painting is dated 1904.
credit: Art Renewal Center

title: The Houses of Parliament
description: The Gothic silhouette of Westminster dissolves into a haze of violet and orange across the Thames. Painted from a terrace at St Thomas's Hospital, the canvas belongs to Monet's London series, in which he tracked the same motif under shifting fog, smoke and sun.

title: Waterloo Bridge
description: Part of Monet's London Thames series, Waterloo Bridge dissolves into a pale silver-grey mist, the stone arches barely distinguishable from fog and water. Tall vertical forms — factory chimneys and industrial structures — rise indistinctly beyond the river, their outlines softened by atmosphere. Completed in 1904 and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the canvas exemplifies Monet's interest in the Thames as a subject of light rather than topography.

title: Wounded Amazon
description: A helmeted Amazon writhes in a circular composition of billowing red drapery, her nude torso bearing a wound while arrows and a fallen adversary appear at the edges of the canvas. The work, dated 1904 by the Van Gogh Museum, demonstrates von Stuck's use of classical warrior iconography to produce images of intense physical drama charged with Symbolist eroticism.
credit: Harvard Art Museums

title: Yamamoto 1904
description: A heavily cloaked figure stands with his back to the viewer, surveying a harbour or coastal industrial scene rendered in bold gouged lines and flat tonal areas. This 1904 woodcut by Kanae Yamamoto, titled "Fisherman," is considered a founding work of the sosaku-hanga movement, in which the artist independently designed, carved, and printed each sheet.

title: Aged Phoenix
description: A grotesque bird-like figure stands on thin legs, one arm raised to grasp the branch of a spindly plant, feathers hanging limply from its body. Paul Klee made this etching, titled Aged Phoenix and bearing the designation Invention 9, in 1905; it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The wiry precision of the line and the absurdist subject reflect Klee's early engagement with satirical printmaking before his later move towards colour and abstraction.
credit: Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation

title: Autoportrait
description: Delaunay presents himself in a dark jacket with a patterned cravat against an animated background of bold colour strokes, painted between 1905 and 1906. The broad, unblended colour planes and vivid chromatic contrasts show the influence of Fauvism rather than Divisionism, marking an early stage of his exploration of colour relationships before his shift toward the Orphist work of the following decade.

title: Bathing of a Horse
description: Two boys lead a dappled horse into shallow water under a high summer sky, the animal's reflection broken across the surface. Serov painted the canvas in 1905, oil on canvas, now in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg. The plein-air handling and loose, light-struck water belong to his later landscape work around the Domotkanovo estate.
credit: artmight.com

title: Boris Kustodiev self-portrait
description: Kustodiev portrays himself as a young man in a flat cap and light outdoor coat, holding a palette and brushes before an open rural landscape of golden fields and fir trees. Painted in 1905 and titled Self-Portrait (On the Hunt), the canvas is held at the State Russian Museum in Saint Petersburg.

title: Cezanne-Thyssen
description: A man in a wide-brimmed hat sits against a pale terrace balustrade, his features summarily indicated and patches of bare canvas left in reserve. Painted in 1905-06, oil on canvas, the sitter is Vallier, the gardener at Cézanne's studio at Les Lauves near Aix-en-Provence; the work has been in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid, since 1993.

title: Eugen von Blaas - Plauderei - 1905
description: Three women engaged in needlework and lace-making are gathered in a vine-shaded courtyard while a young man seated backwards on a chair addresses them with an animated gesture, a basket of fruit on the ground nearby. De Blaas lavishes attention on the women's colourful Venetian costume and the varied textures of fabric, setting the lively exchange against a sun-warmed brick wall. The canvas is signed and dated 1905.

title: Female Nude with Foliage Shadows
description: A standing female nude is rendered in loose, rapid strokes of warm pink and green against a background of dappled foliage, the figure's surface dissolved into coloured patches of reflected light. Painted in oil on cardboard in 1905 and held in the Kirchner Museum Davos, the work predates the formal founding of Die Brücke later that year in Dresden.
credit: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner

title: In the Water by Eugen von Blaas
description: A nude young woman stands ankle-deep in shallow water, seen in three-quarter profile as she gazes downward, one arm extended slightly at her side. Eugene de Blaas rendered the figure with the smooth academic finish and delicate luminosity typical of his work; the canvas, signed lower left, is dated to around 1905 and measures 80.3 by 45 cm.

title: Jean Metzinger
englishTitle: Bathers: Two Nudes in an Exotic Garden

title: Moonrise: Soldier and Maiden
description: A soldier and a young woman stand in a wooded clearing under a rising moon, the figures pressed close in the half-light. Painted in 1905 during Kirchner's Dresden student years, the canvas entered the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston as accession number 98.286.

title: Portrait of Ashbury Wright Lee
description: The elderly Philadelphian Ashbury Wright Lee is shown three-quarter length in a dark coat, the loose handling of the face typical of Eakins's late portraiture. Painted around 1905, the canvas belongs to the unsparing commissioned likenesses Eakins produced for friends and acquaintances in his final productive decade.

title: Portrait of Maria Yermolova
description: The actress Maria Yermolova stands full length in a black gown, her gaze directed upward and away from the viewer, a large framed painting of an arched interior visible on the wall behind her. Painted by Valentin Serov in 1905 to mark her anniversary at the Maly Theatre, the work is now in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
credit: From en wiki

title: Portrait of the Writer Maxim Gorky
description: Maxim Gorky leans forward in a tieless dark shirt, his thin moustache and untidy hair signalling the workman writer he cultivated as a public persona. Serov painted the portrait in 1905, the year of the first Russian revolution, in which Gorky was briefly imprisoned for revolutionary agitation.
credit: http://podol.ru/serov/ PDF (for version uploaded on 10 January 2014)

title: The Open Window
description: The view from Matisse's hotel window at Collioure looks out through pots of climbing flowers to a harbour of sailboats under pink and green water. Painted in 1905 and shown at the Salon d'Automne that autumn, the canvas was bequeathed in 1998 to the National Gallery of Art, Washington from the estate of Mrs John Hay Whitney.
credit: Retrieved from National Gallery of Art, USA , 25 December 2007.

title: The Struggle for Woman
description: Two nude male figures grapple aggressively in the left half of the canvas while a pale, red-haired female nude stands apart on the right, an impassive witness to the contest over her. Signed and dated 1905, the painting is held at the Hermitage Museum and exemplifies von Stuck's use of mythic-primeval allegory to explore erotic rivalry within the Symbolist idiom of the Munich Secession.
credit: https://masterpieceart.net/franz-von-stuck/ 2009-09-06 06:59:48

title: Water Lilies
description: An early canvas in the great water-lily cycle Monet pursued at his Giverny pond for the last three decades of his life. The horizon has already vanished; only floating pads, reflected sky and submerged depth remain, organised purely by colour.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, online database

description: Paul Cézanne, French, 1839–1906 Still Life with Carafe, Bottle, and Fruit, 1906 Watercolor and soft graphite on pale buff wove paper 48 x 62. 5 cm. (18 7/8 x 24 5/8 in.
credit: Henry and Rose Pearlman Collection

title: Dancers
description: Three female dancers are shown in vigorous motion, their high-kicking legs and ruffled skirts rendered in bold black ink with rapid, gestural strokes. The work, made by Ernst Ludwig Kirchner in 1906 and held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, captures the energy of contemporary cabaret or folk dance in a medium that appears to be ink on paper rather than a print. It dates from the same year Kirchner co-founded Die Brücke in Dresden.
credit: Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation

title: Doris with Ruff Collar
description: A woman — identified as Kirchner's model Dodo — is shown bust-length in a boldly painted portrait, the collar around her neck rendered in slashing strokes of yellow, white, and red against a blue garment and flickering background. Painted around 1906 and now in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid, the canvas is an early statement of the chromatic intensity Kirchner would develop with the Brücke group.
credit: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid, Colección Permanente

title: Le Jardinier Vallier
description: Vallier, the gardener and odd-job man at Cézanne's house near Aix, sits with hands resting in his lap, the figure built from dark greens and blues. One of six portraits of the sitter, painted in the summer and autumn of 1906, the last months of Cézanne's life. The painter worked on the Vallier series within days of his death that October.

title: Les Grandes Baigneuses
description: Nude female figures arranged in two groups beneath a vault of leaning trees, the bodies pared to broad blue and ochre planes. The largest of Cézanne's Bather canvases, oil on canvas, about 210 by 251 cm, worked on over roughly seven years and left unfinished at his death in 1906. It entered the Philadelphia Museum of Art in 1937.

title: Portrait of Jean Metzinger
description: A close-up divisionist portrait of the painter Jean Metzinger, his face built from dense rectangular patches of green, yellow, violet, and pink applied in the manner of Neo-Impressionist pointillism. The background is a mosaic of multicoloured strokes, and the sitter faces the viewer directly. Painted by Robert Delaunay in 1906, the work demonstrates the artist's engagement with Chevreul's colour theory in the years before either painter turned to Cubism.

title: Robert Delaunay
description: Oil painting by French Neo-Impressionist Robert Delaunay created in 1906. This small-scale landscape (54 × 46 cm) demonstrates Delaunay's early exploration of light and geometric form, featuring a distinctive solar disc motif characteristic of his experimental approach during this period. Housed in the Musée national d'art moderne in Paris.

title: Robert Delaunay L'homme à la tulipe
englishTitle: Man with a Tulip (Portrait of Jean Metzinger)
description: A pre-Cubist portrait of fellow painter Jean Metzinger, holding a single tulip against a vivid mosaic of pure colour. The divisionist touch and saturated complementaries reveal Delaunay's debt to Neo-Impressionism on the eve of his turn to abstraction.

title: Salome
description: Salome is depicted alone, mid-dance, against a deep black background within von Stuck's characteristic gilded architectural frame, a platter bearing the Baptist's head resting at her side. Painted in 1906, the work belongs to the fin-de-siècle Munich Symbolist tradition in which von Stuck repeatedly staged the biblical temptress with jewelled ornament and theatrical shadow.
credit: Eva Mendgen: Franz von Stuck 1863–1928. Benedikt Taschen Verlag, Köln 1994; ISBN 3-8228-8953-9

title: Salome
description: Franz von Stuck's 1906 Salome depicts the dancer nearly nude, her torso bare above a fringed skirt, turning ecstatically against a dark star-scattered ground, adorned with a jewelled headdress and collar necklace. At the lower right, the Baptist's severed head rests on a dish that emits a blue glow, while a shadowed face looms behind it — a characteristic piece of Munich Secessionist Symbolism centred on the femme fatale.

title: Sten'ka Razin
description: The Cossack chieftain Stepan Razin sits brooding at the centre of a sailed river vessel, surrounded by his crew as the boat crosses a wide expanse of water. Vasily Surikov completed the large canvas in 1906; it is held in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg.
credit: Originally uploaded on en:Image:Surikov1906.jpg on 15:56, 15 February 2005 by en:user:Ghirlandajo with a caption; Vasily Surikov . Sten'ka Razin (1906). The Russian Museum , St Petersburg

title: Two Human Beings
description: A woman in a long white dress and a man in a dark suit stand with their backs to the viewer on a vividly coloured rocky shore, both gazing out to sea. The couple are painted close together yet communicating nothing, Munch's enduring image of emotional isolation. This version, dated 1906–08, is held at the Busch-Reisinger Museum, Harvard Art Museums.
credit: Harvard Art Museums

title: Vollard avec un foulard rouge
description: The dealer Ambroise Vollard wrapped in a red headscarf, the bare head and heavy features set against a warm ground. Renoir painted Vollard, who handled much of his work after 1900, in 1906; oil on canvas, now in the Petit Palais, Paris. The close-keyed reds and softened modelling are typical of the artist's late Cagnes years.
credit: Petit Palais, Paris

title: Water Lilies
description: Lily pads float in even rhythms across green-blue water, with a pale band of sky-reflection running along the upper edge. The picture comes from the first mature group of Nymphéas exhibited by Durand-Ruel in 1909.

title: Water Lilies by Monet
description: An overhead view of the Giverny pond, dotted with discs of pink and white lilies. Cool blues and greens shift toward lavender where the surrounding foliage is mirrored in still water, with no sky visible above the bank.

title: Waterlilies
description: A horizontal screen of lily pads hovers over reflected sky on the Giverny pond. By 1906 Monet had abolished the bank entirely, treating the water as a self-contained world the eye could enter at any point.

title: Bathing Men
description: Multiple nude men stand and move near the water's edge in this large canvas painted at the Baltic coastal resort of Warnemünde between 1907 and 1908. Munch celebrated sun, sea and male vitality through vigorous, gestural brushwork and a warm, luminous palette. The work is part of his series on the ages of man and is held at the Ateneum in Helsinki as part of the Finnish National Gallery collection.

title: Futsuka Zuki by Kawai Gyokudō
originalDateString: 明治40年東京勧業博覧会出品
description: A thin crescent moon (futsuka-zuki, the two-day moon) hangs in a luminous dusk sky above a misty riverbank, where figures with horses or cattle move through swirling ground fog beside a silhouetted tree and distant mountains. The work, executed in sumi and colour on silk as a hanging scroll, won first prize at the 1907 Tokyo Industry Exhibition and is held in the National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo.

title: Gabrielle mit offener Bluse
description: A bust-length study of Gabrielle with her chemise slipped from one shoulder, the flesh rendered in warm pinks against a sketchy ground. The sitter is Gabrielle Renard, cousin of Renoir's wife Aline and the family's nanny from 1894, who modelled often in his later years. Painted about 1907, oil on canvas.

title: Giambattista Pittoni
description: This engraved bust portrait of Giambattista Pittoni was made by Bartolomeo Nazari and reproduced in Laura Coggiola Pittoni's 1907 monograph Dei Pittoni, Artisti Veneti, published in Bergamo. The original painting is held by the Museo Correr, Venice. Pittoni, the leading Rococo history painter of Venice, is shown in a large powdered wig, the inscription below identifying him as 'Johanni Bapt. Pittoni Pictori Venet.'
credit: Original source: Museo Correr, Venice Intermediate source: Laura Coggiola Pittoni (1907). Dei Pittoni, Artisti Veneti . Bergamo: Istituto Italiani d'Arti Grafiche. Immediate source: https://archive.org/stream/deipittoniartist00pitt#page/24/mode/1up

title: Nymphéas
description: From the Giverny series, the Japanese-style pond seen close-up with no shore in sight. Lily pads punctuate broad zones of mauve and green reflection, the painted surface oscillating between water-skin and pure abstraction.

title: Pond with Water Lilies
description: A vertical Giverny canvas in which the lily pond is rotated almost into pure surface pattern. Pinks and violets float over deep greens, the brushwork loose enough that the pads sometimes read as drifting clouds of pigment.

title: Portrait of Henriette Girshman
description: Henriette Girshman stands at her dressing table, glancing toward the viewer as she adjusts her fur-trimmed wrap. Behind her, a mirror reflects the interior of her boudoir. Serov painted the portrait in 1907, and it now belongs to the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

title: Still Life with a Parrot
description: A still life of flowers and glass vases rendered in vivid divisionist strokes of pink, green, yellow, and blue, with what appears to be a brightly patterned parrot amid the botanical arrangement — as the title *Nature morte au perroquet* (Still Life with a Parrot) indicates. Painted in 1907, the canvas shows Delaunay at the height of his Neo-Impressionist phase, applying pure colour in small, mosaic-like touches under the influence of Chevreul and Seurat.

title: The Chess Game
description: Two friends bend over a board in a sun-shot garden during one of Sargent's Alpine summers in the Simplon. The painter spent these holidays sketching members of his travelling party in shawls, hats and Kashmiri textiles. The watercolour-like oil handling and high-keyed greens are typical of these informal late landscapes.
credit: WikiArt.org

title: The Snake Charmer
description: A dark silhouetted figure pipes serpents from a moonlit jungle on a riverbank, commissioned by the mother of Robert Delaunay. Rousseau, a self-taught customs officer, never left France; his jungles were composed from the Jardin des Plantes, picture books and dream, layered in his deliberate, flattened naïve manner.

title: The Song
description: A woman in a white dress sits absorbed in thought on a red upholstered chair in a grand interior, leaning her head on her hand as another figure plays piano in the background. Arched ceilings, a heavy table bearing books and flower arrangements, and a distant gilded figure set an atmosphere of cultivated leisure. Chase painted the work in 1907, using his characteristic fluid handling to animate the richly appointed space.
credit: patricksaunders.blogspot.de

title: Water Lilies
