description: A nearly square oil on canvas from the group of water-lily paintings Claude Monet completed in 1907, depicting the lily pond of his garden at Giverny. The water surface fills the entire field of view: rafts of lily pads bearing pink blossoms drift across reflections of sky and trees rendered in veils of lavender, green and rose. The painting is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, accession number 19.170.

title: Water Lilies
description: An early canvas from the Water Lilies series begun in earnest after 1903, when Monet shifted from views of the Japanese bridge to the pond's surface alone. Floating pads anchor a shimmering ground in which clouds and willows are fused as reflection.

title: Waterlilies
description: Lily pads and blossoms drift across a pond suffused with warm yellow-green light and cloud reflections, the surface rendered in loose, luminous strokes. Monet painted this canvas in 1907, among the most chromatically adventurous of the Nymphéas series before his later cataract years. The work is in the Kawamura Memorial DIC Museum of Art, Japan.

provenance.collection: Kawamura Memorial DIC Museum of Art
provenance.location: Kawamura Memorial DIC Museum of Art

title: Ambroise Vollard
description: Ambroise Vollard leans over a small statuette of a kneeling nude, examining it as a connoisseur, his bald head and bulbous features softened by Renoir. The bronze is after the sculptor Aristide Maillol. Painted in 1908, oil on canvas, now in the Courtauld Gallery, London.

title: Female Nude
description: A nude figure is shown hunched over in what appears to be a tub, the body reduced to bold white forms cut against a black ground. Kirchner produced the woodcut in 1908, while the Brücke group was working in Dresden, and an impression is held in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Le Palais Ducal
description: The Doge's Palace rises from the Venetian lagoon in dissolving pinks and aquamarines, painted during Monet's two-month stay in the city. The facade is treated less as architecture than as a screen for refracted light, with broken brushwork knitting stone, water and sky into a single luminous fabric.

title: Monet w1725
description: One of the water-lily canvases of 1908, in which the pond surface fills the entire frame and the water lilies float against reflections of sky and foliage. Wildenstein 1725; held in a private collection.

title: Monet w1726
description: A water-lily canvas of 1908 from the Giverny pond series, with the flowers scattered across a mirror-like surface of reflected light. Wildenstein 1726; held in a private collection.

title: Nude against the light pierre bonnard
description: A luminous composition by French Post-Impressionist painter Pierre Bonnard depicting a female figure silhouetted against backlighting. The painting exemplifies Bonnard's characteristic use of color and light, with the nude rendered through subtle chromatic nuances and the interplay of shadow and brilliance. Housed in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium.
objectKey: collection-of-beauty/Nude against the light pierre bonnard.jpg

title: Nudes
description: Two figures face each other in close proximity, rendered in loose charcoal strokes on brown paper, their heads and bare shoulders filling the sheet. Ernst Ludwig Kirchner made this drawing around 1908, and it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The sketch economy of line and absence of setting are consistent with the rapid figure studies Kirchner produced during the Brücke years.
credit: Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation

title: Portrait of Almina Daughter of Asher Wertheimer
description: Almina Wertheimer is depicted seated in elaborate Oriental costume — an embroidered robe and feathered turban — resting a long-necked stringed instrument across her lap and gazing directly at the viewer. Painted in 1908, this is among the last of Sargent's celebrated series of Wertheimer family portraits, bequeathed to the British nation and now in Tate.

title: Terror Antiquus
description: Lightning splits a darkening sky over the Aegean as an archaic kore smiles enigmatically in the foreground, the Acropolis and the citadels of Mycenae and Tiryns flickering below. Bakst built the 250 by 270 cm canvas after a 1907 trip to Greece with Serov, aiming at an apocalyptic fable of ancient cataclysm. It won a gold medal at the 1910 Brussels Exposition Universelle and entered the State Russian Museum.
credit: State Russian Museum

title: The Farm at Les Collettes
description: The farmhouse at Les Collettes seen through a screen of olive and orange trees, the foliage broken into flickering touches of green and rose. Renoir bought the estate at Cagnes near Nice in 1907 and moved there in 1908, painting the farm repeatedly between 1908 and 1914. Oil on canvas, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: The Grand Canal
description: Looking down the Grand Canal toward Santa Maria della Salute, Monet renders Venice as drifting reflections of pink and turquoise on water. The view comes from his only visit to the city, in autumn 1908, which yielded a late series exhibited at Bernheim-Jeune in 1912.
credit: Beyeler Foundation

title: The Watercarrier
description: The Italian-Austrian painter de Blaas specialised in genteel scenes of Venetian life, here a young woman pausing with her copper water vessel. His glossy academic finish made such picturesque subjects popular with late-nineteenth-century international collectors.

title: Water Lilies
description: Pink water-lily blossoms float among green pads on a softly luminous pond rendered in pale blue, grey, and green. No bank or horizon orients the viewer; the water surface becomes the entire world of the canvas. Dated 1908, the painting was offered at Sotheby's London in June 2019.
credit: Sotheby's, London, 19 June 2019, lot 10

title: Water-Lilies
description: A canvas from the second great wave of Nymphéas pictures, painted as Monet exhibited forty-eight pond views at Durand-Ruel's Paris gallery. Pads drift across reflections of cloud and sky, the water surface flattened into a pure field of colour with no horizon to orient the viewer.

title: William Rush Carving His Allegorical Figure of the Schuylkill River
description: The Philadelphia sculptor William Rush works at his studio bench, carving an allegorical female figure of the Schuylkill River from a wooden block while the nude model stands posed nearby. Eakins returned to the 1877 composition in 1908, the only subject he is known to have reworked in his career. The canvas is in the Brooklyn Museum.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum ; Photo: Brooklyn Museum, 39.461_SL1.jpg

title: Bathers at Moritzburg
description: Yellow-orange bodies wade and sprawl beside cobalt water at the Moritzburg lakes outside Dresden, where Kirchner and the Brücke painters spent summer weeks bathing naked from 1909 onward. Begun in 1909, the canvas was repainted in 1926 in lighter, more even tones. It is now in Tate Modern, London.

title: Promenade Along the Volga
description: Townsfolk in summer hats and dresses stroll along the Volga embankment at Tutaev, with birch trees, market stalls, and onion-domed churches visible across the wide river. Painted in 1909, Promenade Along the Volga marks Kustodiev's sustained engagement with provincial merchant life as a subject, rendered in his characteristically bright, saturated palette.

title: Saint-Séverin No. 3
description: The ribbed vaults and ambulatory columns of Saint-Séverin in the Latin Quarter buckle and twist inward in Delaunay's bold reinterpretation of the Gothic interior, suffused with deep blue-green light. This oil on canvas, dated 1909–10, belongs to Delaunay's celebrated series of the Paris church that marked his move toward proto-Cubist spatial distortion. It is held by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum.
credit: Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation

title: The Eiffel Tower
description: An early treatment of the iron tower that would obsess Delaunay for decades, viewed from below and toppling against a turbulent sky. The fractured planes and sharp diagonals translate Cubist analysis into a celebration of modern engineering.

title: The Equatorial Jungle
description: Oil painting by Henri Rousseau depicting a lush jungle landscape with exotic animals and stylized vegetation. Painted in 1909, it is part of Rousseau's famous jungle series, though he never traveled to a tropical region—his inspiration came from botanical gardens in Paris and illustrations. The work exemplifies Rousseau's distinctive Naïve Art style and is housed at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.

title: Vesterhavet i storm. Efter solnedgang. Højen
description: A view of the North Sea at Højen on the northern tip of Jutland, painted near Tuxen's home at Skagen. Associated with the Skagen painters, Tuxen here forsakes the colony's clear summer light for a churning storm twilight, with thick impasto registering wind-driven spray.

title: Albert Gleizes
description: A woman sits with bowed head amid faceted planes of grey, green, and buff, her hands resting in her lap and one arm raised to the drapery behind her, a vase of phlox standing at the left. Gleizes showed the canvas in Room 41 of the 1911 Salon des Indépendants, the public debut of group Cubism, and again at the 1913 Armory Show. The oil, 81.6 by 100.2 cm, belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.

title: Ballettfigurine zu: Feuervogel
description: A costume design for the Firebird, showing the dancer in a swirling confection of orange, red, and gold with feather-like flame motifs, arms outstretched mid-movement. Léon Bakst created designs for Stravinsky and Fokine's Firebird, premiered by Diaghilev's Ballets Russes at the Paris Opéra on 25 June 1910, with sets principally by Alexander Golovin.

title: Crow and blossom by Ohara Koson
description: A solitary crow perches on a flowering branch, the bird's blue-black plumage set against pale petals. Koson's shin-hanga woodblock print refines Edo-period kachō-e bird-and-flower conventions for early-twentieth-century export collectors, prizing economical line and atmospheric ground.
credit: Woodblock print circa 1910 by Ohara Koson (1877-1945)

title: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner Spielende nackte Menschen 1910-1
description: Three naked figures move through a sun-dappled outdoor setting beneath a large tree, their bodies rendered in broad, flat planes of orange, red, and green typical of Kirchner's Brücke idiom. The canvas, dated 1910, grew out of the group's summers at the Moritzburg lakes near Dresden, where communal bathing in nature served both as lived practice and programmatic subject.

title: Kustodiyev fair
description: A provincial Russian fair crowds the foreground beneath vivid church towers, vendors and buyers in folk dress pressing among textiles and goods. Painted in 1910 in tempera on cardboard, the work is held by the A. N. Radishchev Museum of Arts in Saratov, and reflects Kustodiev's abiding fascination with market days as popular spectacle.

title: Negro boy by L.Bakst
description: Costume study of a boy attendant, drawn in pencil, watercolour and silver paint on laid paper, 29 by 15.5 centimetres. The 1910 sheet is held by the MAGMA collection and belongs to Bakst's high Ballets Russes period, when his orientalist costume designs for Schéhérazade and Cléopâtre were reshaping European stage design.

title: Portrait of Ida Rubinstein
description: The dancer Ida Rubinstein reclines nude on a strip of blue cloth, her elongated limbs suggesting the flat profile of an ancient relief. Valentin Serov painted her in 1910 following her celebrated appearances in Diaghilev's Ballets Russes seasons, where she performed in Cléopâtre (1909) and Schéhérazade (1910). A green drape coils across the lower composition, its saturated colour contrasting with the spare, sandy ground.

title: Portrait of Ivan Morozov2
description: The Moscow textile magnate Ivan Morozov sits at a table, his hands clasped before him, while a brilliantly coloured Matisse still life fills the wall behind his shoulder. Valentin Serov painted the portrait in 1910, the year before his own death; Morozov's renowned collection of French modern paintings was nationalised in 1918 and forms a core part of what is now held in Moscow's Pushkin Museum.

title: Portrait of Jean Renoir as a hunter - Jean as a Huntsman
description: Renoir's son Jean, aged fifteen, poses full-length with a borrowed gun and the family dog Bob, dressed in a jacket his father thought suited a huntsman. Painted at Les Collettes in 1910, oil on canvas, about 173 by 89 cm. The sitter later became the filmmaker Jean Renoir; the canvas is in the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.
credit: Los Angeles County Museum of Art archive copy at the Wayback Machine

title: Porträt des Paul Durand-Ruel
description: The art dealer Paul Durand-Ruel seated and contemplative, his dark coat set against a loosely brushed background. Durand-Ruel was the dealer who staked the Impressionists from the 1870s and a friend of Renoir for more than thirty years. Painted in 1910, oil on canvas.

title: Rape of Europa
description: Europa clings to the back of a reddish-brown bull as it surges through blue-purple waves, a dolphin visible in the foreground. Serov's 1910 treatment of the mythological abduction compresses the figures into a boldly simplified composition dominated by cool sea tones and warm earth. The work is now held in a private or unrecorded collection.

title: Self-portrait
description: Malevich confronts the viewer in a dark green coat against a swirling red-orange background of abstracted figures, rendered in bold, flat colour that prefigures his primitivist turn. The gouache, dated 1910–1911, marks a decisive shift from descriptive form toward the declarative palette of his early avant-garde work.

title: Water Lilies
description: Held by the Musée Marmottan Monet, which inherited the artist's studio holdings, this Nymphéas frames the pond as an unbroken field of reflected light. Pads cluster as horizontal accents across deep blues and rose, the composition organised by colour weight rather than perspective.
credit: musée Marmottan-Monet [1]

title: Валентин Александрович Серов - Одиссей и Навсикая
description: A gouache painting by Russian master Valentin Serov depicting the classical moment when Odysseus encounters the princess Nausicaa. Created in 1910 and held in the Tretyakov Gallery, this work captures a pivotal encounter from Homer's Odyssey with characteristic elegance and restraint.

title: Champs de Mars: The Red Tower
description: The Eiffel Tower rises in fractured red and ochre planes above the Champ de Mars. Delaunay's Orphic Cubism dismantles the engineered iron icon into prismatic facets, part of his sustained series treating the tower as a modern motif of Parisian light and movement.

title: Eiffel Tower
description: Painted at the height of Delaunay's Cubist phase, the tower lurches and splinters as if seen simultaneously from multiple vantage points. Surrounding buildings collapse inward, dramatising the giddy modern experience of urban scale.

title: Floorpolishers
description: Two labourers scrub a parquet floor, their bodies rendered as bold, block-like volumes in yellow and red against a loosely painted interior. Catalogued as Nakov F-196, the gouache on paper is dated 1911 and is held by the Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam.
credit: Stedelijk Museum

title: Juan Legua
description: A seated man in dark suit and stiff collar tilts back in his chair, face splintered into a small grid of facets while the body remains legible. Painted in 1911 at 55 by 46 cm, the canvas is one of Gris's earliest Cubist portraits, the sitter a Spanish journalist living in Paris who likely used Juan Legua as a pen name. It is at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: Le Dieu Bleu Nijinsky
description: Bakst's 1911 costume design for Vaslav Nijinsky in the title role of Le Dieu bleu shows a cross-legged figure with green-painted skin, an elaborate feathered headdress, and richly patterned yellow and jewelled garments. The design drew on South and Southeast Asian court dress that Bakst had studied, for the Cocteau-Hahn-Fokine ballet premiered by Diaghilev's Ballets Russes in 1912.

title: Paysage à Cassis
description: The terraced hills above Cassis stack up in flat patches of pink, ochre and pine green under a Mediterranean light. Painted in December 1911 in oil on canvas at roughly 50 by 62 cm, the landscape belongs to the brief Fauve-derived phase Picabia ran through before swinging into the Section d'Or Cubism of 1912.
credit: http://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/media/97462/Landscape-at-Cassis-oil-on-canvas-by-Francis-Picabia-18th Encyclopædia Britannica

title: Portrait of Jacques Nayral
description: The writer Jacques Nayral sits with legs crossed and an open book on his lap, his grey-suited figure set among the faceted foliage of Gleizes's garden at Courbevoie. The 161.9 by 114 cm canvas was shown at the 1911 Salon d'Automne and reproduced in Du Cubisme, the manifesto Gleizes wrote with Metzinger in 1912. Tate acquired the picture in 1979.

title: Portrait of Princess Olga Orlova
description: Princess Olga Orlova is shown seated in a large feathered hat and a voluminous dark fur wrap, her pearl necklace and pale gown visible beneath. Painted by Valentin Serov in 1911, the work is a full-length formal portrait that conveys both the sitter's aristocratic bearing and an air of detached hauteur. It is now held in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg.

title: Recoveredgleizes
description: A Cubist landscape of Meudon with a small figure threaded through faceted houses, trees, and a winding path. Gleizes exhibited Le Chemin (Paysage à Meudon) at the 1911 Salon des Indépendants, the show where the Salle 41 hang first announced Cubism as a public movement.
credit: [1] , Source, new file

title: Repose
description: A languid female figure reclines on a sofa, head turned away, wrapped in shimmering ivory satin and gauze. Sargent's niece Rose-Marie Ormond was the model for several such drapery studies in the years before the First World War. The picture is essentially a virtuoso exercise in painting white folds against deep shadow.

title: Street with church in Kandern
description: August Macke's 1911 canvas shows a narrow street in Kandern winding toward a village church tower, the facades and road resolved into bold flat patches of violet, blue, purple, red, and ochre. The work, held at the Augustiner Museum in Freiburg, reflects Macke's assimilation of Cézanne's constructive approach and the Blaue Reiter colour sensibility he was developing at this time.
credit: Städtische Museen Freiburg

title: The Woman
description: Eve stands at the centre of the composition, nude, eyes closed, as Adam reaches toward her from behind; to either side coils a great serpent amid an extravagant profusion of tropical flowers, foliage, and exotic birds. John Byam Liston Shaw's 1911 painting depicts the Garden of Eden temptation scene in a late Pre-Raphaelite idiom indebted to Burne-Jones, with saturated colour and densely patterned decoration filling every part of the canvas.

title: Window on the City No. 3
description: Faceted Parisian rooftops and the silhouette of the Eiffel Tower dissolve into a grid of prismatic colour. Painted across 1911-12 and now at the Guggenheim, Window on the City No. 3 belongs to Delaunay's Fenêtres series, the first sustained experiment in what Apollinaire would name Orphism.
credit: Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation

title: Albert Gleizes
description: Cubist footballers lunge across the canvas in a tangle of jersey stripes, limbs, and faceted ground plane. Oil on canvas, 225.4 x 183 cm, the work entered the National Gallery of Art in Washington as one of Gleizes's largest Salon-scale figure compositions of 1912-13.

title: Alfons Much Slavnost svatovitova na rujane
englishTitle: The Celebration of Svantovit in Rujana: When Gods Are at War, Salvation is in the Art
description: A 1912 painting by Alphonse Mucha depicting the celebration of Svantovit (Svetovid), an ancient Slavic deity, in the context of Rujana. This work explores themes of spiritual salvation through art during times of conflict, reflecting Mucha's deep engagement with Slavic cultural and mythological subject matter.

title: Francis Picabia
description: A near-square canvas of nearly two and a half metres on each side, resolving a mountain spring into broad interlocking facets of terracotta, brown, and dark grey. Picabia showed La Source at the 1912 Salon d'Automne in Paris; the picture later entered the Museum of Modern Art, New York.

title: Francis Picabia
description: Robed penitents and processional banners pulse through a Sevillian street in a Cubist-Orphist lattice of cones and curves. Inspired by Picabia's travels in Spain, the square canvas was shown at the 1912 Salon de la Section d'Or and travelled to the 1913 Armory Show; it now hangs at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Harvard Theatre Collection - Bakst
description: Watercolour set design for Act I of Daphnis and Chloe, with a wooded grove and rocky outcrop sketched in pale washes. Bakst made the drawing in 1912 for the Ballets Russes production choreographed by Fokine to Ravel's score; the sheet survives in the Harvard Theatre Collection at Houghton Library.
credit: MS Thr 414.4 (9), Harvard Theatre Collection , Houghton Library, Harvard University

title: L'Homme au Balcon
description: A monumental Cubist figure dominates this tall, narrow canvas, the surrounding urban and industrial landscape dissolved into stacked facets of ochre, grey, and green. Oil on canvas, 195.6 x 114.9 cm, the painting entered the Philadelphia Museum of Art via the Louise and Walter Arensberg Collection. Gleizes painted L'Homme au Balcon in 1912, the same year it was exhibited at the Salon de la Section d'Or.

title: Les Baigneuses
description: Cubist bathers stand and recline along a river bank rendered as a shallow stage of interlocking planes. Oil on canvas, 105 x 171 cm, Les Baigneuses entered the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris after being shown at the 1912 Salon de la Section d'Or, the exhibition that defined the Puteaux group.
credit: Source third upload

title: Nollendorfplatz
description: Trams curve around the Berlin square of Nollendorfplatz under a steep, tipped-up perspective, with hurrying figures pressed against the kerb. Kirchner began his Berlin street pictures shortly after the Brücke group relocated from Dresden; the canvas is now held by Stiftung Stadtmuseum Berlin.
credit: Stiftung Stadtmuseum Berlin

title: Portrait of Pablo Picasso
description: A Cubist portrait of Picasso seated with a palette, his face and jacket broken into pale blue and ochre facets. Painted in 1912 and now at the Art Institute of Chicago, Gris inscribed the canvas 'Hommage à Pablo Picasso', framing his own analytic style as both tribute and challenge to the older master.

title: Self-portrait
description: Kustodiev depicts himself in a heavy fur coat and fur hat, arms folded, against a snowy Russian townscape of onion-domed churches and market activity. The canvas is dated 1919 in the artist's own hand; it places him squarely within the Russian merchant world that had become his chief subject.

title: Slavs in their Original Homeland: Between the Turanian Whip and the Sword of the Goths
englishTitle: The Slav Epic: Slavs in Their Original Homeland
description: The opening canvas of Mucha's Slav Epic shows a huddled couple on dark rocks beneath a starry sky while a towering spectral figure looms over the scene and fires burn in the distance — representing the early sufferings of the Slavic peoples between the Turanian and Gothic threats. Mucha's tempera-and-oil technique on the vast 810 × 610 cm canvas lends the symbolist scene a pale, dreamlike pallor distinct from his Art Nouveau poster work. Painted in 1912, the work is now in the Prague City Gallery collection.

provenance.collection: museum collection of the Prague City Gallery

title: The Tiger
description: A crouching tiger built from interlocking facets of yellow, green, red, and blue, its alert gaze directed outward while its body merges with the angular planes of the surrounding landscape. Franz Marc, co-founder of Der Blaue Reiter, painted this work in 1912, treating the animal as an emblem of primal vitality and borrowing Cubist faceting to fuse predator and habitat into a single dynamic composition.

title: Windows Open Simultaneously
description: A small 1912 oil in which the Eiffel Tower dissolves into a grid of translucent green, pink and ochre prisms, identifiable only by its tapering silhouette. Acquired by the Tate and measuring 45.7 by 37.5 cm, the panel belongs to Delaunay's Simultaneous Windows cycle, the founding works of Orphism.
credit: Tate Modern, London

title: Cliff Dwellers
description: Tenement crowds spill from fire escapes, stoops, and laundry-strung windows on a sweltering summer evening on Manhattan's Lower East Side. Painted in May 1913 and now at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, the canvas belongs to Bellows's Ashcan record of immigrant New York.
credit: secondat.blogspot.de

title: Edtaonisl
description: Three metres square, the canvas threads abstract bands of yellow, blue, grey, and orange around a remembered encounter between a dancer and a cleric observed during Picabia's Atlantic crossing. The invented title interleaves the French words étoile and danse; the picture was shown at the 1913 Armory Show and is now at the Art Institute of Chicago.
credit: MoMA , see also Art Institute of Chicago

title: Jealousy
description: A bearded man stares from the foreground in sickly pallor while behind him a nude central figure and a clothed woman are visible in the background. Munch returned to the jealousy motif repeatedly across his career, treating the triangular composition as an emblem of erotic anxiety. This version, dated 1913–15, is held at the Munch Museum, Oslo.
credit: Munch Museum

title: L'Équipe de Cardiff
description: Cardiff rugby players leap for the ball beneath a Ferris wheel, an aeroplane, and a luminous advertising hoarding for Astra. Oil on canvas, 326 x 208 cm, the picture entered the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris as the largest of Delaunay's three Équipe de Cardiff variants from 1912-13.
credit: Photograph by Coldcreation

title: L'Homme en hamac
description: A reclining figure in a straw hat is assembled from interlocking Cubist planes of ochre, brown, grey, and blue, with text fragments — including a reference to Alexandre Mercereau — embedded in the composition. Oil on canvas, 130 x 155.5 cm, the painting is held at the Albright-Knox Art Gallery, Buffalo, New York. Gleizes dated and signed the canvas in 1913.

title: La Pisanella by L. Bakst 06
description: Set design for the Port of Famagusta, the Cypriot harbour from Gabriele d'Annunzio's play La Pisanelle ou la Mort parfumée. Bakst made the watercolour in 1913 for Ida Rubinstein's production at the Théâtre du Châtelet, staged by Vsevolod Meyerhold with music by Ildebrando Pizzetti.

title: Picabia starDancer
englishTitle: Star Dancer on a Transatlantic Steamer
description: Abstract geometric shapes in red, black, grey, and white are stacked and interlocked across the surface of this 1913 watercolour, whose title — lettered at the top of the sheet — identifies the subject as a star dancer on a transatlantic liner. Painted during Picabia's crossing to New York for the Armory Show, the work translates movement into flat, interlocking forms rather than any legible figure. The source confirms it is a watercolour in a private collection.

title: Portrait de l’éditeur Eugène Figuière
description: The publisher Eugène Figuière sits behind a desk stacked with books and journals, surrounded by Cubist planes that name his most important authors. Oil on canvas, 143.5 x 101.5 cm, the portrait was painted to mark Figuière's publication of Gleizes and Metzinger's manifesto Du Cubisme in 1912; it hangs at the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon.

title: Portrait of Mikhail Matyushin
description: Malevich disperses the head of the composer and painter Mikhail Matyushin into intersecting metallic planes, with a band of piano keys and a fragment of neatly parted hair standing in for the sitter's likeness. The Cubo-Futurist oil on canvas was painted in 1913, the year the two men collaborated with Aleksei Kruchenykh on the Futurist opera Victory over the Sun, for which Matyushin wrote the music and Malevich the designs. It is held by the State Tretyakov Gallery in Moscow.
credit: Tretyakov Gallery

title: Promenade
description: Strolling figures, including a man in a straw hat and a woman with a white parasol, move through a sun-dappled avenue of large green trees, their forms built from broad planes of saturated colour. August Macke, associated with the Der Blaue Reiter group, painted this promenade scene in 1913, translating everyday leisure into the luminous colour harmonies he had developed in dialogue with Robert Delaunay's Orphism.

title: Samovar
description: A Russian samovar dissected into cylindrical and conical facets of grey, ochre, and tin. Painted in 1913 and now at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, the still life sits between Malevich's Cubo-Futurist machine subjects and the radical abstraction he would unveil as Suprematism two years later.

title: Sand Hills near Grünau
description: Kirchner renders the sand hills near the Berlin suburb of Grünau in broad strokes of orange and ochre, with dark evergreen trees in the foreground and a pink-red sky above. The canvas, dated 1913, applies the chromatic intensity of Brücke Expressionism to a local landscape subject. A small tower or church is visible on the distant ridge.

title: Seiltänzerin
description: A tightrope walker poised above a fairground crowd, the scene built from interlocking translucent diamonds of colour. Painted in the artist's most prolific year, the composition shows Macke fusing his Blaue Reiter sensibility with the prismatic geometry he had absorbed from Robert Delaunay in Paris.
credit: zkm.de , Museum für Neue Kunst

title: Street
description: Two cocottes in feathered hats and fur stoles stride down a Berlin pavement, a crowd of dark-suited men pressing past on either side. Oil on canvas, 120.6 x 91 cm, the picture belongs to Kirchner's Berlin Strassenbilder cycle of 1913-15 and is held by the Museum of Modern Art in New York.
credit: Kirchner and the Berlin Street MoMA

title: The Knife Grinder or Principle of Glittering
englishTitle: The Knife Grinder, or Principle of Glittering
description: A knife grinder working at a grinding wheel is multiplied across the canvas in a sequence of overlapping Cubo-Futurist facets, his legs, hands, and the spinning disc fragmented to suggest continuous motion. Malevich gave the work the subtitle Principle of Glittering and exhibited it in 1913 alongside the Russian Cubo-Futurists. It is now in the collection of the Yale University Art Gallery.
credit: Yale University Art Gallery

title: The Prince Out Hunting Sees the Castle Where the Princess Lies Sleeping
description: The prince and his hunting party pause in a vivid twilight landscape, a winged figure visible in the upper sky as they survey the enchanted terrain before them. Léon Bakst painted this panel between 1913 and 1922 as part of a Sleeping Beauty decorative cycle commissioned for Waddesdon Manor, now in the care of the National Trust.
credit: National Trust, Waddesdon Manor

title: The Princess and the Court Fall Asleep for a Hundred Years
description: Figures from the royal court lie fallen in sleep across the courtyard and steps of an ivy-covered castle, while a crowned figure in gold still stands at the entrance as the enchantment takes hold. Léon Bakst painted this panel between 1913 and 1922 for a Sleeping Beauty cycle at Waddesdon Manor, now held by the National Trust.
credit: National Trust, Waddesdon Manor

title: The Princess Pricks Her Finger on a Spinning Wheel
description: The princess recoils at the moment the spindle pierces her finger, the old crone leaning over the wheel in a shadowed tower chamber. Bakst painted the panel between 1913 and 1922 for James de Rothschild's Sleeping Beauty cycle at Waddesdon Manor, where the National Trust still keeps the series.
credit: National Trust, Waddesdon Manor

title: The Sleeping Beauty: The Prince Discovers the Princess and Wakes Her with a Kiss
description: Within an ornate arched alcove hung with violet and gold drapery, the prince kneels before the princess, who sits up in her canopied bed as she wakes. Léon Bakst painted this panel between 1913 and 1922 as part of a Sleeping Beauty decorative cycle commissioned for Waddesdon Manor, now held by the National Trust.
credit: National Trust, Waddesdon Manor

title: Two Women with a Washbasin; The Sisters
description: Two women in a colourful interior attend to a white washbasin, one in a pink coat bending her hands toward the water while the other in green looks on. Kirchner's bold use of pink and green complements, set against a warm red-orange ground, gives the domestic scene the visual tension of his Berlin period. The canvas is dated 1913 and bears the title Two Women with a Washbasin.

title: Udnie
description: Curving metallic planes and tubular forms hurtle across a near-square canvas almost three metres on each side. Picabia painted Udnie in 1913 after watching Polish dancer Stasia Napierkowska perform on the ship carrying him to the Armory Show; the picture now hangs at the Musée National d'Art Moderne, Centre Pompidou, Paris.
credit: Photograph Coldcreation at MNAM, Centre Pompidou, Paris (Feb. 2014)

title: Weeping Nude
description: A nude woman lies face-down on a red-orange surface, her dark hair obscuring her face entirely and her limbs spread across the couch in an attitude of complete abandonment or grief. Munch renders the figure raw and unidealised, channelling emotional collapse through agitated brushwork and a heated palette of reds and oranges. The canvas, dated 1913–14, is held at the Munch Museum, Oslo.

title: Zmei Gorinich
description: The bogatyr Dobrynya Nikitich, armoured and cloaked in crimson, confronts the towering seven-headed dragon Zmey Gorynych against a blazing red and violet sky. Viktor Vasnetsov completed the canvas in 1918, drawing on the Russian bylina cycle; it is held in the House-Museum of V. M. Vasnetsov, Moscow.
credit: CD-ROM "Государственная Третьяковская галерея".Издание 2-е; Допол. Издательство: AlexSoft, 2004

title: Albert Gleizes
description: Faceted planes assemble a dynamic standing figure in this Cubist portrait of the composer Florent Schmitt. Gleizes executed the work between 1914 and 1915 at 36 by 27 centimetres; the black-and-white photographic reproduction preserves a pastel that was inscribed to Josep Maria Junoy and published in the Catalan avant-garde review Troços.
credit: The European Library

title: In Russia. Soul of the people
description: An expansive procession of Russian people - peasants, monks, soldiers and intelligentsia - moves across a northern landscape in search of spiritual truth. Nesterov treats his pre-revolutionary allegory in luminous, restrained colour, blending Symbolist mood with Orthodox iconographic gravity.
credit: lj.rossia.org

title: Kustodiev Renee Notgaft
description: Renée Ivanovna Notgaft is shown in three-quarter length, seated in a green armchair in a black dress with a white neckline, a large bouquet of pink hydrangeas filling the background behind her. Kustodiev painted the portrait in 1914, in a mood of quiet elegance that contrasts with the vivid provincial festival scenes he would concentrate on in later years.

title: Le Matin clair aux saules
description: Pale lilies float on a luminous pond crossed by the trailing reflections of weeping willows. The panel forms part of the Grandes Décorations cycle Monet painted at Giverny for the oval rooms of the Musée de l'Orangerie in Paris, where pond, sky and bank dissolve into a continuous surface.

title: Les Deux saules
description: Two weeping willows anchor the left and right edges of this panoramic composition, their dark hanging branches framing the expanse of the Giverny pond below. Lily pads drift across a surface rendered in shifting tones of blue, grey, and muted lavender. The canvas belongs to Monet's monumental Nymphéas decorations, created between 1914 and 1926 for the Musée de l'Orangerie, Paris.

title: Les Nuages
description: Reflected clouds spread luminously across the pond surface, lily pads riding the image in loose clusters with no sky or bank to orient the eye. This mural-scale panel, titled Les Nuages, is part of the Grandes Décorations that Monet created between 1914 and 1926 and donated to the French state during his lifetime for the dedicated rooms of the Musée de l'Orangerie, Paris. The work dates from his final years, painted as he struggled with cataracts.

title: Matin
description: Pale dawn light catches the lily pads on the Giverny pond, the water dissolving into broad horizontal sweeps of mauve and cream. The work belongs to the great cycle Monet developed in his late, near-blind years for the Orangerie ovals.

title: Monet w1781
englishTitle: The Water Lily Pond, Rose Arches
description: A late view of the lily pond at Giverny with the rose arches of the garden (Bassin aux nymphéas, les rosiers), painted between 1914 and 1917. Wildenstein 1781; held in a private collection.

title: Monet w1786
description: A large late water-lily canvas (130 x 150 cm) painted between 1914 and 1917, when Monet was working toward the monumental Grandes Décorations. Wildenstein 1786; held in a private collection.

title: Nymphéas avec reflets de hautes herbes
englishTitle: Water Lilies, Reflections of Tall Grass
description: From the late Nymphéas cycle, the canvas dissolves the lily pond into floating pads, drowned grasses, and reflected sky. Working at monumental scale in his Giverny studio, Monet abandoned the horizon altogether to let surface and depth fuse into a single chromatic field.

title: Omphale
description: The Lydian queen Omphale stands nearly nude, draped only in the lion skin of Hercules which she wears as a hood, holding his club and displaying the amber necklace and blue bracelet that mark her royal status. Behind her an ornate roundel of mythological figures provides a decorative backdrop in the manner of John Byam Liston Shaw's late Pre-Raphaelite idiom. Dated 1914, the vertical canvas treats the mythological role-reversal — Hercules served Omphale as penance for murder — with full-length figural command.

title: Portrait of an Army Doctor
description: Broad overlapping planes and intersecting diagonals reassemble a uniformed military doctor in this Cubist portrait. Gleizes painted the canvas between 1914 and 1915 while serving in the French army; it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York. The record title is Portrait of an Army Doctor (Portrait d'un médecin militaire).
credit: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum

title: Reflets d'arbres
description: Inverted trees and clouds shimmer in the pond, lily pads punctuating the surface as the only signal of where water meets reflection. The picture pushes Monet's late style toward near-abstraction.

title: Reflets verts
description: Lily pads and blossoms drift across a deep green-shadowed pond surface, the reflections of foliage dissolving the boundary between water and sky. This large panel, titled Reflets verts, is one of the Grandes Décorations that Monet created between 1914 and 1926 and which are permanently installed at the Musée de l'Orangerie, Paris. The compressed, all-over surface leaves no horizon, immersing the viewer in the unbroken world of the pond.

title: Reservist of the First Division
description: Cubo-Futurist fragments of a soldier's ear, moustache and cap collide with pasted printed paper, a postage stamp and a real thermometer affixed to the canvas. Malevich produced this assemblage in the autumn-winter of 1914 at 53.7 by 44.8 centimetres; it entered the Museum of Modern Art, New York, after the Berlin works left in Hugo Häring's care were acquired in 1935.

title: Water Lilies
description: The surface of the lily pond at Giverny fills the entire canvas — pale greens, lavenders and yellows with drifting pads and a few small pink blossoms, no bank or horizon to anchor the view. The mural-scale panel belongs to the Grandes Décorations, the cycle of monumental water-lily paintings that occupied Monet from about 1914 until his death in 1926. Museum of Modern Art, New York.

title: Water Lilies
description: Clouds reflected on the surface of the lily pond drift in pale pink and white across deep blue-green water scattered with lily pads, the composition running across three abutting canvases of mural scale. The triptych belongs to the Grandes Décorations, the cycle of monumental water-lily paintings Monet worked on at Giverny from about 1914 until his death in 1926.

title: Woman with animals
description: A seated figure is fragmented into bold Cubist planes of green, blue, red, and ochre alongside animal forms — at least one cat-like creature is discernible in the lower composition. Gleizes finished the nearly two-metre canvas in February 1914; it is held at the Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice. The title 'Woman with Animals' and the record dimensions (196.4 x 114.1 cm) are confirmed by the museum's own catalogue.
credit: Peggy Guggenheim Collection and here

title: yellow-irises-1917
description: A late Giverny study of yellow flag irises, painted as Monet's eyesight clouded with cataracts and his palette grew correspondingly hot and saturated. The flowers swim in loose, near-abstract bands of green and gold, anticipating the decorative scale of the Grandes Décorations.

title: Albert Gleizes
description: A returning poilu, rifle and pack flattened into Cubist scaffolding, appears in this wood engraving captioned 'Retour de Bois-le-Prêtre'. Gleizes contributed the print to issue 20 of Le Mot on 1 July 1915, the wartime Parisian weekly co-edited by Paul Iribe and Jean Cocteau, while the artist was himself serving at Toul.
credit: Le Mot, n. 20, 1 July 1915, in Gallica, Bibliothèque nationale de France

title: Albert Gleizes
englishTitle: Sketch for the Portrait of Jean Cocteau
description: A spare linear sketch of a standing figure — inscribed 'Pour J.M. Junoy, amicalement, Albert Gleizes, 1915' — serves as a preparatory study for a portrait of the poet Jean Cocteau. The work was published in Troços, the Catalan avant-garde review edited by Josep Maria Junoy, in its second series, no. 2, October 1917. Medium and dimensions are unrecorded; the work is known through its printed reproduction.
credit: Troços. Segona sèrie. Núm. 2 (oct. 1917)

title: Anisimov Alexander Ivanovich
description: Alexander Ivanovich Anisimov is shown in close-up against a luminous Russian landscape with domed church spires, rivers, and autumn foliage — a backdrop characteristic of Kustodiev's outdoor portraits. Boris Kustodiev painted the portrait in 1915; Anisimov was a leading scholar of medieval Russian icon painting.

title: Composition for "Jazz"
description: A Cubist musician holding a banjo occupies the centre of this square composition, surrounded by interlocking planes of ochre, red, yellow, grey, and black. Gleizes painted the work in 1915 on cardboard, 73 x 73 cm; it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York. The title links the composition to the jazz music that animated New York's avant-garde circles during the artist's wartime visits.
credit: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum

title: Fantômas
description: A Synthetic Cubist still life of pipe, newspaper and glass, with the words FANTOMAS and LE JOURNAL legible across the fragmented planes. Painted in 1915 and held in the Chester Dale Collection at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the title cites the popular pulp anti-hero of Souvestre and Allain's serial novels.

title: Goyō Hashiguchi
description: A nude woman sits cross-legged after bathing, bent forward to tend to her foot, a red basin placed before her. The colour woodcut print, titled Yokugo no onna (Woman after a Bath), was made by Hashiguchi Goyō in 1915 and is held in the Library of Congress. Goyō's close observation of the figure and his mastery of flat, subtly gradated colour place the work within the emerging shin-hanga tradition that sought to revive the intimacy of classical bijin-ga.
credit: Library of Congress

title: Ici
englishTitle: Ici, c'est ici Stieglitz, foi et amour (cover of 291, No. 1)
description: Alfred Stieglitz is portrayed as a bellows camera apparatus with a gearshift lever, its mechanism reaching toward the word 'IDEAL' printed at the top. Picabia's mechanomorphic portrait appeared on the cover of issue No. 1 of the New York review 291 in 1915, and is signed 'F. Picabia / 1915 / New York.'

title: Kanae Yamamoto
description: A black-and-white cow grazes near a coastal shoreline, sailboats visible on the water behind it, the scene rendered in simplified flat planes of colour. This 1915 woodblock print by Kanae Yamamoto is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston; Yamamoto was a pioneer of the creative-print movement in Japan, advocating that artists design, carve, and print their own blocks.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Monet w1976
description: The centre panel of the monumental Agapanthus triptych (Wildenstein 1975-1977), a roughly two-by-four-metre canvas painted at Giverny between about 1915 and 1926. This panel belongs to the Saint Louis Art Museum; its companions are in the Cleveland Museum of Art and the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art.

title: Nature morte à la nappe à carreaux
description: A guitar, wine bottle, grapes, and newspaper are arranged on a checked tablecloth in this oil on canvas by Juan Gris, painted in Paris in March 1915. The interlocking Cubist planes fragment and reassemble each object across the picture surface. The work entered the Metropolitan Museum of Art with the Leonard A. Lauder Cubist Collection in 2014.
credit: Christie's , LotFinder: entry 5766361 (sale 1505, lot 9) New version: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Leonard A. Lauder collection

title: Nu à la toilette
description: A nude at her dressing table dissolves into wheeling discs of pure colour, the mirror and figure interpenetrating. Delaunay painted the 140 by 142 centimetre canvas in 1915 during his Iberian exile from the war; it is held by the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris and belongs to his Orphist series exploring simultaneous contrasts.
credit: Photograph by Coldcreation

title: Self Portrait in 4th Avenue Studio
description: Chase shows himself at work in his studio, holding a loaded palette and brushes before a large blank canvas, his working jacket open over a dark waistcoat. Painted in 1915 in his Fourth Avenue studio and now in the Richmond Art Museum collection, the picture captures the theatrical self-assurance Chase brought to teaching and to his own public persona.
credit: Upload Bot (Cobalty), possibly from a Art-CD-Rom; Richmond Art Museum, online collection

title: Self-portrait as a Soldier
description: Kirchner stands in his studio in army uniform with the bloodied stump of an amputated right hand, a nude model behind him in sickly yellow tones. The 1915 oil at the Allen Memorial Art Museum, Oberlin, references his service in the 75th Field Artillery Regiment and the breakdown that brought a provisional discharge; it was later included in the Nazi Entartete Kunst exhibition of 1937.

title: Snow on Ayase river
description: A Japanese woodcut print by Shōtei Takahashi depicting a snowy river landscape. The work exemplifies early 20th-century Japanese printmaking with its serene winter scene. Now held in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.

title: Still Life before an Open Window
description: A table holding a Médoc bottle, fruit dish, glass and a copy of Le Journal stands before a window looking onto a Montmartre balustrade and the trees of Place Ravignan. Gris painted the 115-centimetre canvas in 1915 from his studio in the Bateau-Lavoir; it is held by the Philadelphia Museum of Art and counts among his Synthetic Cubist breakthroughs.

title: Suprematism
description: Coloured rectangles and bars float on a white field, freed from any object reference. Malevich exhibited his first Suprematist canvases at the Last Futurist Exhibition 0,10 in Petrograd on 19 December 1915, declaring painting's right to non-objective form; he hung the Black Square in the corner traditionally reserved for the household icon.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: Rain falls in long diagonal strokes across the wooden stage of Kiyomizu-dera in Kyoto, its temple roofs darkened against a washed grey sky. Hasui treats the famed pilgrimage site not as a monument but as an atmospheric encounter with weather.

title: The beauty
description: A stout nude with reddish-blond hair sits upright on the edge of her bed, one hand resting on the pink satin quilt and her feet on a small embroidered footstool, framed by rose-patterned blue wallpaper, lace-trimmed pillows and a chest painted with bright flowers. Kustodiev painted The Beauty in 1915 with the Moscow Art Theatre actress Faina Shevchenko as his model; the canvas is in the Tretyakov Gallery.

title: Viktor Vasnetsov by S.Malyutin
description: The painter Viktor Vasnetsov sits in three-quarter length, his long beard and contemplative expression rendered in pastel on grey cardboard. Sergey Malyutin executed the 104 by 59 centimetre portrait in 1915 in Vyatka; it is now held by the Vyatka Art Museum named for the Vasnetsov brothers, inventory number Zh-180.

title: Water Lilies
description: A large-scale water-lily canvas of 1915, painted in the studio Monet built at Giverny to accommodate his ever-bigger formats. The pond has lost its banks entirely; tangled reflections of weeping willow descend through deep blues and violets while pads float as flat islands of green.
credit: Musée Marmottan Monet, Paris

title: Water Lilies
description: One of the water-lily compositions Monet painted at his Giverny pond, dissolving the surface into floating pads, reflected sky, and submerged depths. The late series pushed Impressionism toward an immersive, near-abstract vision of light on water.
credit: Neue Pinakothek

title: Water Lilies
englishTitle: Water Lilies (Agapanthus, Cleveland Museum of Art)
description: From Monet's late Giverny series, the painting abandons horizon and shoreline for a pure expanse of water surface. Lily pads and blossoms float among broken reflections of sky and trees, the brushwork loosened toward near-abstraction in shades of blue, violet, and green. Originally the left panel of a triptych titled Agapanthus, this monumental canvas — now in the Cleveland Museum of Art — was repainted by Monet before his death, leaving only water lilies on the shimmering surface.
credit: https://clevelandart.org/art/1960.81 IA

title: 'Taj Mahal' by Charles W. Bartlett
description: A 1916 woodblock print by Charles W. Bartlett depicting the Taj Mahal viewed from across the Yamuna River, with a small boat and a seated figure in the foreground. The mausoleum and its flanking structures are rendered in pale, graded washes against a clear blue sky, their forms reflected in the still water. Made during Bartlett's Asian travels and printed in Tokyo, the work combines British watercolour sensibility with the flat, refined colour harmonies of the shin-hanga woodblock tradition.

title: 'Udaipur
description: A view across the lake at Udaipur shows figures gathered on stone steps by the water's edge, with the Lake Palace reflected beyond and blue mountains rising in the distance. Designed by Charles W. Bartlett in 1916 and published in 1917 by Watanabe Shōzaburō's Tokyo workshop, the print belongs to Bartlett's series of Indian landscapes executed in the shin-hanga idiom; a fine impression is held by the Honolulu Academy of Arts.
credit: Honolulu Academy of Arts

title: 'Udaipur' by Charles W. Bartlett
description: A solitary figure in orange robes sits cross-legged within an ornate lakeside pavilion, looking out over the still water at Udaipur; a distant temple or palace is visible on the far shore, and a large tree extends its branches overhead. Charles W. Bartlett designed the woodblock print in 1916, and it was cut and published that same year in a warm palette of golden ochres and deep blues characteristic of his shin-hanga work.
credit: Frazier Fine Art

title: Charles W. Bartlett - Color woodblock print
description: Pilgrims and worshippers gather in a courtyard of the Golden Temple complex at Amritsar, their colourful robes set against the arched stone architecture. The colour woodblock print was published in Tokyo in 1916 by Watanabe Shōzaburō and is now in the Honolulu Academy of Arts.
credit: Honolulu Academy of Arts

title: Google Art Project
description: Snow-blanketed Russian rooftops, blue-domed churches and frost-white birches frame troikas and revellers celebrating Maslenitsa beneath a luminous pink and green sky. Kustodiev painted this 1916 canvas from his wheelchair following spinal surgery, drawing on the bold, flat colour of the lubok print tradition.

title: Hawaiian Fisherman
description: A Hawaiian fisherman stands at the water's edge, holding a cast-net as he faces the open sea under a luminous sunset sky. Bartlett produced this shin-hanga woodblock print in 1916, combining the Western artist's compositional sense with the Japanese publisher's flat planes of colour and serene atmosphere.
credit: Frazier Fine Art

title: Maslenitsa
description: Townspeople and sleigh teams cross a snowy public square ringed by onion-domed churches and merchant houses during the Eastern Orthodox Maslenitsa festival. Kustodiev returned to the Shrovetide subject several times in 1916, painting these celebrations of Russian provincial life from his wheelchair while bedridden Russia was fighting the Great War.

title: Parting Spring by Kawai Gyokudo
dateCreated: 大正5年 第10回文展出品
originalDateString: 大正5年 第10回文展出品
description: The left panel of a pair of folding screens by Kawai Gyokudō, designated an Important Cultural Property of Japan. Working in the nihonga tradition, the artist evokes the melancholy of late spring through misty mountains and falling cherry blossoms.

title: Parting Spring by Kawai Gyokudo
dateCreated: 大正5年 第10回文展出品
originalDateString: 大正5年 第10回文展出品
description: The right panel of Kawai Gyokudō's Parting Spring screens, designated an Important Cultural Property of Japan, depicts steep rocky cliffs looming above churning waves, with two water-mill boats navigating the rough current. Working in the nihonga tradition, the artist renders the raw energy of the river gorge in close detail, completing the panoramic seasonal landscape begun in the left panel. The diptych is held by the National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo, and dates to 1916.

title: Portuguese Woman
description: A woman in embroidered folk dress stands amid a swirl of concentric chromatic discs, exotic plants, and stacked vessels, the figure and environment dissolving into interlocking arcs of colour. Robert Delaunay painted this large canvas in 1916, applying the Simultanism he had developed with Sonia Delaunay to a subject rooted in the couple's wartime stay in Portugal.

title: Suprematist Composition
description: Geometric rectangles and bars in green, blue, yellow, orange-red, black, and pink float against a white field in dynamic, tilted arrangement. Painted in 1916 and held at the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam, the canvas is a key example of Malevich's Suprematist project to express pure feeling through non-objective form.
credit: Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam

title: The Water-Lily Pond
description: A view of the water-lily pond at Giverny, 1916, painted as a pure surface composition without banks or bridge. Water lilies — their pads silvery-white, their blooms red and orange — float across an expanse of deep olive-green water streaked with blue and lavender reflections. The canvas is held at Museum Folkwang, Essen (Wildenstein 1883).

title: Water-Lilies
description: One of the large-scale Giverny pond pictures painted after 1916, the canvas shows lily pads adrift on a surface of shimmering gold and mauve, with willowy reflections along the right edge dissolving sky and vegetation into the water. Abandoning any fixed horizon, Monet treated surface and depth as a single chromatic field; the work is now in the National Gallery, London.

title: Glass and Checkerboard
description: A drinking glass and a checkerboard are resolved into interlocking geometric planes of green, terracotta, and cream in this Synthetic Cubist panel by Juan Gris, painted around 1917. The composition exemplifies Gris's method of beginning with abstract shapes and arriving at recognisable objects, rather than the reverse. The work is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Julie de Graag December 1917
description: A woodcut print by Dutch artist Julie de Graag depicting a sleeping cat. Part of a series of December-themed works, this 1917 print exemplifies the artist's characteristic technique and intimate subject matter from her prolific career in printmaking.

title: Monet w1897
description: A large late canvas of the lily pond at Giverny (100 x 200 cm), painted between 1917 and 1919 in the loose, immersive manner of the Grandes Décorations years. Wildenstein 1897; held in a private collection.

title: Monet w1900
description: A two-metre-wide late canvas of the Giverny lily pond painted between 1917 and 1920. Catalogued as Wildenstein 1900, it entered the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art in Seoul as part of the Lee Kun-hee collection donation.

title: Philosophers
description: A double portrait of theologians Pavel Florensky and Sergei Bulgakov walking in conversation through a quiet wooded landscape. Nesterov's pared composition and contemplative palette frame the encounter as an icon of Russian religious philosophy on the eve of revolution.
credit: The Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow, Russia, [3]

title: Scheherazade
description: A stage design for the Ballets Russes production of Scheherazade, set to Rimsky-Korsakov's symphonic suite, with billowing curtains and oriental cushions in saturated greens and oranges. Bakst's 1910 décor for Diaghilev established the scenographic vocabulary of jewel-toned exoticism that defined the company's early Paris seasons.

title: A Merchant's Wife's Teatime
description: A merchant's wife sits before a samovar, holding a tea cup, with a cut watermelon, cakes, fruit, and grapes on the table before her; her cat perches at her side. Painted in 1918 and one of Kustodiev's most reproduced canvases, the picture is an elegy for pre-revolutionary provincial bourgeois life composed while a spinal tumour had confined the artist to a wheelchair.

title: Monet w1884
description: One of the monumental late water-lily canvases (about 130 x 200 cm) Monet painted in his water garden at Giverny around 1917-1919, catalogued as Wildenstein 1884 under the French title Le Bassin aux nympheas. Wikidata records it in the Hasso Plattner Collection at the Museum Barberini, Potsdam.

title: Seated Nude
description: A seated female nude faces the viewer with hands folded in her lap, the elongated neck and almond-shaped eyes characteristic of Modigliani's late figures set against a cool blue-grey ground. Painted around 1918, the canvas is held by the Honolulu Museum of Art under accession 2895.1.
credit: Honolulu Museum of Art

title: 'Silk Merchants
description: Turbaned figures rest and trade beneath spreading trees along a lakeside promenade in an Indian setting. Charles W. Bartlett's 1919 woodblock print, held at the Honolulu Museum of Art, belongs to his shin-hanga series in which Asian travel subjects are rendered through the Japanese colour-woodblock medium. The composition balances the blue water and dappled shade with the white-clad figures grouped across a broad stone terrace.
credit: Honolulu Museum of Art

title: John Singer Sargent
description: A personification of the defeated Synagogue, blindfolded and clutching a broken staff, painted for Sargent's Triumph of Religion mural cycle in the Boston Public Library. The medieval iconographic pairing with a triumphant Church drew sustained protest from Boston's Jewish community. The cycle was left unfinished, partly in the wake of that controversy.

title: Kustodiev Winter-shrovetide-festivities 1919
description: Sledges glide through a snowbound Russian provincial town during the carnival week before Lent, with onion-domed churches and crowds of fairgoers under a pink winter sky. Painted in 1919 at the height of the Civil War, Kustodiev's nostalgic merrymaking belongs to a cycle of Maslenitsa scenes that imagined the lost merchant culture as folk pageantry.

title: Le bassin aux nymphéas
description: From the late Giverny series, the canvas crops the lily pond into a near-abstract field of floating pads and reflected sky. By 1919 Monet's failing eyesight pushed him toward broader, more saturated touches that would culminate in the wraparound Grandes Décorations of the Orangerie.
credit: Private collection institution QS:P195,somevalue,P3831,Q768717; Christie's , LotFinder: entry 5100003 (sale 7599, lot 16, london, 24 June 2008)

title: Prayers at Sunset
description: Worshippers gather beneath the arches of a domed pavilion rising directly from the lake at Udaipur, its pale stone and gilded dome reflected in the deep blue water below. Bartlett's 1919 woodblock print, now in the Honolulu Academy of Arts, belongs to his Indian series and employs the flat areas of colour and atmospheric light characteristic of the shin-hanga movement.
credit: Honolulu Academy of Arts

title: Réveil Matin
description: A mechanical schematic rendered in ink, its interlocking gears, cog-wheels, and abstract structural elements arranged across the sheet with the title 'RÉVEIL MATIN' inscribed below. Made in 1919 and held by Tate, London, the drawing belongs to Picabia's machinist Dada period, when technical diagrams served to satirise human behaviour as mere mechanism.
credit: Tate, London

title: Still Life with Fruit Dish and Mandolin
description: A mandolin, fruit dish, and folded newspaper arranged on a patterned tablecloth in flat, interlocking planes of muted blue, ochre, and white. Painted in 1919, the canvas belongs to Gris's Synthetic Cubist maturity, when he composed by deduction from geometric scaffolds before adding the objects rather than fragmenting them in.
credit: The original uploader was Cactus.man at English Wikipedia . Transferred from en.wikipedia to Commons by Melesse using CommonsHelper .

title: Tabi Miyage Dai 1 - Shu
englishTitle: Souvenirs of Travel I: Mutsu Tsuta Onsen
description: A wooden onsen inn sits in darkness under a driving rain, its windows glowing amber against the surrounding mountains and deep blue-black sky. This print is from Hasui's first Souvenirs of Travel series (1919), depicting the Tsuta hot spring in the Mutsu region, published with Watanabe Shozaburo as part of the shin-hanga landscape revival. The nocturnal palette of dark indigo and warm light exemplifies Hasui's atmospheric range.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum ; Photo: Brooklyn Museum, 68.35.5_IMLS_PS3.jpg

title: Tabi miyage dai isshū
description: A small boat with a lone figure drifts on the still waters of Tsuta Marsh in Mutsu Province, framed by overhanging green pines and overlooked by a rounded forested mountain catching the last light of day. Hasui's cool blues and greens render the lake surface with characteristic atmospheric depth. The print is part of the Souvenirs of Travel I series, published in 1919 (Taishō 8), and is held in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Tabi miyage dai isshū
description: A mountain temple outside Sendai is glimpsed through a screen of trees, the architecture half-absorbed into the hillside. Hasui's compact composition and softly graded skies belong to the shin-hanga revival, which reworked classical ukiyo-e idioms with modern atmospheric effects.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts Boston

title: Tōkyō jūnidai
englishTitle: Early Summer Rain at Sannō Shrine (Twelve Scenes of Tōkyō)
description: A lone figure shelters under a yellow umbrella and walks a dog past the vermilion gate of Hie (Sannō) Shrine in early summer rain, the surrounding trees rendered in soft greens against a muted grey sky. From the series Twelve Scenes of Tōkyō, this 1919 woodblock print is one of Kawase Hasui's earliest shin-hanga works, combining quiet atmosphere with the graphic economy of traditional printmaking.

title: Water Lilies p
description: Claude Monet (French, 1840–1926) Water Lilies, 1919 Oil on canvas; 39 3/4 x 78 3/4 in. (101 x 200 cm) The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, The Walter H. and Leonore Annenberg Collection, Gift of Walter H.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art

title: Albert Gleizes
englishTitle: Woman with Black Glove (Femme au gant noir)
description: A seated figure is reduced to bold interlocking planes of orange, red, yellow, and black, the black glove of the title prominent against the warm ground. Painted in 1920 and measuring 126 by 100 centimetres, the canvas belongs to a private collection and is reproduced in the 1998 Gleizes catalogue raisonné. The work belongs to the post-war phase in which Gleizes reformulated Cubism into the rhythmic system later set out in his treatise La Peinture et ses lois.
credit: Michel Massenet, Albert Gleizes (1881-1953) , Somogy éditions d'art, Fondation Albert Gleizes, Adagp, Paris, 1998, ISBN 2-85056-241-2 Invalid ISBN

title: Albert Gleizes
description: A Cubist composition of a mother and child built from interlocking curving planes, surviving only through a black-and-white photographic reproduction. The painting was shown at the Exposition Internationale d'Art Moderne in Geneva in the winter of 1920-21 as catalogue number 185; its dimensions and present location remain unknown.
credit: Exposition Internationale d'Art Moderne, Geneva, 26 December 1920 - 25 January 1921

title: Charles W Bartlett's watercolor and ink 'Hana Maui Coast'
description: Dark lava rocks along the Hana coast of Maui meet crashing surf, with tropical vegetation clinging to the headland at left and an open expanse of deep blue ocean beyond. Bartlett rendered the scene in watercolour and ink in 1920, part of the Hawaiian landscape work he produced after settling in Honolulu following his earlier Asian travels.
credit: Frazier Fine Art

title: Evening Snow at Terajima Village
description: A snow-covered village street at night, with electric poles cutting through a deep blue sky and warm light glowing from the windows of low-roofed houses on either side of a canal. A solitary figure with an umbrella makes their way along the path in the distance. Kawase Hasui produced this shin-hanga woodblock print in 1920, depicting Terajima Village on the outskirts of Tokyo.

title: Group portrait of the Mir Iskusstva artists
description: An assembly of the World of Art group, with Bakst, Benois, Roerich, Somov, Dobuzhinsky, and other members gathered around a table. Painted in 1920 as a study for an unrealised composition, the canvas portrays the Saint Petersburg circle that had shaped Russian fine printing and Diaghilev's early ballet productions before the Revolution dispersed it.
credit: Art-Catalog.ru

title: Kustodiev Trinity day
description: Villagers in bright Sunday clothes gather under birches for the Orthodox feast of the Trinity, with onion-domed churches behind them. Painted in 1920, the canvas belongs to Kustodiev's cycle of provincial holiday scenes composed from memory during his confinement to a wheelchair, an idealised reconstruction of pre-revolutionary peasant ritual.

title: Odalisque
description: A reclining model in a red garment rests on a striped sofa, her dark hair falling across her face, in the loose, sensuous manner of Matisse's Nice-period figuration. Painted in 1920–21 and held at the Stedelijk Museum, this odalisque belongs to the series of decorative studio interiors in which Matisse returned to warm colour and relaxed figuration after the austerity of the war years.
credit: Stedelijk Museum

title: Reflections of Clouds on the Water-Lily Pond
description: A late, large-scale Giverny panel related to the Grandes Décorations Monet was preparing for the Orangerie. Clouds are present only as inverted reflections, the painting collapsing sky, water and lily into one immersive plane.
credit: Digital image, The Museum of Modern Art, New York

title: Remaining Snow at Inokashira
description: A shin-hanga woodblock print of the wooded park at Inokashira in Tokyo, with patches of late snow lingering beside dark water. Hasui treats the season with the muted palette and atmospheric stillness that defined his landscape practice.

title: Tabi miyage dai isshū
description: A solitary worker bends over mats of drying red peppers on the shore, flanked by tall thatched stacks and bare wooden drying frames, with breaking sea-waves and a blue autumn sky beyond. The woodblock print is from the first volume of Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel series (Tabi miyage dai isshū), published in 1920, and captures a working coastal landscape in the Koshiji region.

title: Tabi miyage dai isshū
englishTitle: Loading Stone on a Boat, Awa Province
description: A sailboat rests at a rocky outcrop along the Bōshū (Awa Province) coast at dusk, its masts and banner reflected in calm water as a single figure stands on deck. The pale pink sky and still sea give the composition a contemplative stillness characteristic of Hasui's shin-hanga prints. The sheet belongs to Souvenirs of Travel I (1920), the series that established his collaboration with publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō.

title: Tabi miyage dai isshū
description: A long wooden bridge spans the Asano River at Kanazawa, its dark piers mirrored in the shallow water below, while a grove of silhouetted pines rises against a muted evening sky. White egrets rest on the sandy bank beneath the bridge. The horizontal print belongs to Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel I (1920), rendered in the cool blue-green palette he favoured for twilight river scenes.

title: Tabi miyage dai isshū
description: At night, the rooflines and lanterns of the Nagare pleasure quarter in Kanazawa are reflected in the dark water of a canal, a crescent moon rising above the pine trees beyond the compound wall. Hasui's deep blues and the still mirror of the water give the licensed district an atmosphere of hushed elegance. The print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel I series (1920).

title: Tabi miyage dai isshū
englishTitle: The Mishima River in Mutsu Province
description: A large orange moon hangs over a cluster of rustic wooden buildings on the Mishima River in Mutsu Province, its glow reflected in the water below as small figures go about evening tasks. The nocturnal scene — warm light against the deep blue of the night sky — exemplifies Hasui's mastery of atmospheric colour in the shin-hanga idiom. Published in 1919 (Taishō 8), the print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel I series.

title: Tabi miyage dai isshū
englishTitle: Autumn at the Arayu Spa, Shiobara
description: A lone figure walks down the main street of the hot-spring village of Arayu in Shiobara, flanked by the dark wooden façades of inns and bathhouses, as a single autumn tree glows orange-gold at the far end of the lane and blue mountains rise behind it. The sharp contrast between the dark eaves and the luminous sky gives the composition its characteristic shin-hanga drama. The print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel I series, published in 1920 (Taishō 9).

title: Tabi miyage dai isshū
description: Pine-fringed Kude Beach in Wakasa Province curves along the Sea of Japan, the foreground trees framing a low strip of water and sky. Hasui's clean geometry and reduced palette draw on Hiroshige's coastal landscapes while pushing toward modern simplification.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts Boston

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: A snowy winter coastal scene at Nishimikawa-zaka on Sado Island, with a curving bay of deep blue water sheltered by snow-laden slopes and foreground pines. Small figures are visible on the path near the shore. A woodblock print from Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II, published 1920, exemplifying the shin-hanga interest in seasonal atmosphere.

title: Tabi miyage dai sanshū
description: A coastal view of Hinomisaki on the Izumo peninsula, where pine-clad cliffs meet the Sea of Japan. Hasui's woodblock translates wind, wave and weather into a few decisive colour blocks, a characteristic of his Souvenirs of Travel III landscapes.

title: The Bolshevik
description: A giant Bolshevik in winter coat strides over the snow-covered rooftops of a Russian city, carrying an enormous red banner while crowds fill the streets below. Painted in 1920 and held at the Tretyakov Gallery, the canvas draws on the monumental scale rhetoric of icon and lubok traditions, treating a contemporary revolutionary figure with the visual language of folk heroic art.
credit: Tretyakov Gallery

title: Tōkyō jūnidai
englishTitle: Shinagawa Anchorage, from Twelve Scenes of Tōkyō
description: A view of fishing boats anchored in the bay off Shinagawa, sails reflected on a tranquil sea. Part of Twelve Scenes of Tokyo, the design relies on flat planes of graded blue and economical silhouettes characteristic of shin-hanga.

title: Tōkyō jūnidai
englishTitle: Winter Moon, Toyama Plain (Twelve Scenes of Tōkyō)
description: A winter moon floats above a grove of silhouetted pine trees on the Toyama Plain, their reflections catching in the still water below. Deep bands of blue and blue-green fill the composition, with the luminous disc set against a gradated night sky. From Kawase Hasui's 1920 woodblock series Twelve Scenes of Tōkyō, the print exemplifies the atmospheric restraint characteristic of the shin-hanga movement.

title: Water-Lily pond
description: Water lilies float on the green-blue surface of the Giverny pond, the bank dissolved in a tapestry of brushstrokes that releases the picture from any horizon. Painted during Monet's late, near-abstract Nymphéas campaign and now installed in Tadao Ando's Chichu Art Museum on Naoshima, the canvas is housed in pure natural light.
credit: Chichu Handbook

title: Waterlilies Pond
description: A monumental canvas, two meters high and more than four meters wide, from the water-landscape decorations Claude Monet painted at Giverny between 1920 and 1926, in the orbit of the Grandes Decorations he ultimately gave to the French state. Known as Le Bassin aux nympheas, reflets verts (Waterlily Pond, Green Reflections), it stretches the pond's surface into a continuous field of deep green reflection scattered with lily pads. The painting belongs to the Foundation E. G. Buhrle Collection and is shown at the Kunsthaus Zurich.

title: WLA moma Monet Reflections of Clouds on the Water-Lily Pond
englishTitle: Reflections of Clouds on the Water-Lily Pond
description: Monet's three-panel Water-Lily triptych at the Museum of Modern Art spans roughly forty feet of canvas, carrying the Giverny pond surface in an unbroken panoramic band. Painted around 1920, the panels dissolve water, lily pads, and cloud reflections into shifting fields of blue-green and golden-amber, without horizon or sky to anchor the view. The work is held at the Museum of Modern Art, New York.

title: Woman in Blue Combing Her Hair
description: A woman in a blue floral kimono draws her fingers through her long, loosened black hair, her gaze downcast in quiet concentration. Published in 1920 as a colour woodblock print of the Taishō era, the work revives the bijin tradition in the refined shin-hanga style associated with Hashiguchi Goyō; it is now at the Walters Art Museum.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: 960px-Tokyo junidai
description: A cherry tree in full bloom spreads over a dark wooden building on Atagoyama, petals drifting down toward children playing on the paved ground below. The woodblock print, from Hasui's series Twelve Scenes of Tokyo (1921), shows the shin-hanga movement's pairing of traditional craftsmanship with atmospheric naturalism.

title: Albert Gleizes
description: Two Cubist figures — a woman and a child — are assembled from bold interlocking planes of red, orange, blue, yellow, and black. Published in 1921, the composition belongs to Gleizes's early-twenties efforts to integrate the figure into the rhythmic translation-rotation system he codified in La Peinture et ses lois. The work is reproduced in the 1998 Gleizes catalogue raisonné.
credit: Michel Massenet, Albert Gleizes (1881-1953) , Somogy éditions d'art, Fondation Albert Gleizes, Adagp, Paris, 1998, ISBN 2-85056-241-2 Invalid ISBN

title: Asahi Bridge in Ojiya
description: A woodblock print from the Souvenirs of Travel II series depicts the Asahi Bridge spanning the river at Ojiya. Hasui's shin-hanga style fuses Western perspective with traditional Japanese block-printing, building atmosphere through layered bokashi gradations.

title: Kawase Ebisu-11
description: A snow-covered harbour at night, with buildings and their reflections spread across still water as flakes fall thickly from a dark sky. The print depicts the Port of Ebisu on Sado Island, published in December 1921 as part of Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II series, and exemplifies the shin-hanga tradition's fusion of Edo woodblock technique with a modern sensitivity to atmospheric light and season.

title: KustodiyevSemenov Kapitsa
description: Pyotr Kapitsa and Nikolai Semyonov are shown in a close half-length portrait, one holding a pipe beside a gleaming samovar-like vessel. Painted by Kustodiev in 1921, the double portrait captures two physicists at the outset of careers that would both be recognised with Nobel Prizes.

title: Old Woman and Young Woman
description: Two angular figures are seated at a table, a bowl of food between them, rendered in stark black and white in a bold woodcut print. Ernst Ludwig Kirchner made this work in 1921, and it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The angular distortion of the faces and the high-contrast graphic language link it to Kirchner's continued development of Expressionist printmaking during his Swiss years.
credit: Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation

title: Part of the Byōdō-in Temple at Uji
description: A partial view of the Phoenix Hall at Byodo-in in Uji, rendered as a shin-hanga woodblock print. Hasui isolates a fragment of the eleventh-century temple's tiled roofline, using flat colour fields and quiet tonal washes characteristic of the Souvenirs of Travel II series.

title: Sailboats
description: A single junk-rigged sailboat moves across calm, luminous water, its sails and hull mirrored in glassy reflections below. This 1921 woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida belongs to his celebrated sailboat set, in which the same composition was printed in different colorways to capture varying times of day and atmospheric conditions.
credit: book scan: "Printed to perfection. Twentieth-century Japanese Prints from the Robert O. Muller Collection". Amsterdam: Hotei, 2004, p.46.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: Two boats push through choppy seas close to the base of steep, densely forested cliffs at Urahama in Echigo Province, waves breaking white around them as diagonal rain marks the stormy sky.
