The close viewpoint and the turbulent water convey the physical effort of coastal labour in rough weather. The print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel II series (1921) and is held in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
englishTitle: Kōshō Temple in Himi, Etchū Province
description: At dusk, a solitary figure walks along a narrow lane beside the high stone walls and overhanging rooflines of Kōshō Temple in Himi, Etchū Province, a large tree silhouetted against the pale evening sky above. The close, vertical composition directs attention down the darkening passage to the fading light beyond the compound wall. The print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel II series, published in 1921 (Taishō 10).

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: Tall pines with rust-red trunks line the foreground of this view of the Ōi River at Arashiyama, their green canopy framing a covered pleasure boat moving across the water against a warm golden sky. The composition looks through the vertical trunks to a middle distance of rocky shore and distant hills, a device Hasui used throughout the Souvenirs of Travel II series (1921).

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
englishTitle: Beach Shed at Himi in Etchū Province
description: A rough beach hut at Himi sits low against the Etchu shoreline, its dark timbers contrasted with pale sand and water. Hasui's interest is in working coastal architecture rather than scenic landmarks, a recurring trait of the second Souvenirs cycle.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: Two deer stand before the vermilion facade of the Kasuga Shrine in Nara, their presence evoking the sacred deer that have roamed the precinct for centuries as divine messengers. Stone lanterns are ranged along the building's front, and a large tree rises behind the roofline into a partly cloudy sky. The print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel II series (1921), from Hasui's Shin-hanga series.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: Nigatsu-do, the hall on the eastern slope of Todai-ji where the Omizutori water-drawing rite is held each spring, is shown perched above its veranda balustrade. Hasui's diagonal viewpoint compresses the wooden gallery into a strong horizontal band.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: Morning along Osaka's Dotonbori canal finds the famed entertainment district at its quietest, the theater district's lanterns unlit and its banks emptied of crowds. The composition trades nightlife spectacle for a city caught off-stage.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: A waterfront street in Aikawa on Sado Island at dusk, with rough wooden boat sheds lining a rocky shore and an adult and child picking their way along a fence. The sourceDescription notes this is a dusk scene from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II series, published 1921. Hasui renders the coarse timber structures and pebbled beach with the atmospheric economy characteristic of his shin-hanga work.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: Two figures — an adult and a child — pause on a path that descends toward the bay at Kamo-mura on Sado Island, with scattered buildings to either side and a mountainous ridge rising beyond the water. The wide middle ground of blue water and cloud-reflected sky does most of the visual work. A woodblock print from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II series, published 1921.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: Mano Bay opens across the full width of the composition, a long low coastline of green hills and what appear to be stone piers stretching along the horizon. Above it, a sky full of billowing pink and white clouds dominates the upper two-thirds of the print, their warm tones reflected in the water below. A woodblock print from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II series, published 1921.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: Night rain falls heavily on the port of Teradomari, lantern light scattering across wet ground. Hasui was a master of nocturnes, and the sheet uses successive overprintings to build a saturated, almost lacquered darkness.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
englishTitle: Dawn Snow at the Port of Ogi on Sado Island
description: Dawn snow lies thick over the harbor at Ogi on Sado, with moored boats reduced to silhouettes against pale water. The print pairs a graded pink horizon with cold blue shadows, a daybreak chord Hasui returned to throughout his career.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: Snow blankets the pine spit of Amanohashidate, the narrow sandbar in Tango Bay long counted among the Three Views of Japan. Hasui strips its familiar profile back to a quiet white horizontal between sea and sky.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
englishTitle: Snow on a Clear Day at Miyajima
description: A snow-covered corridor and gallery of the Itsukushima Shrine at Miyajima extends over the sea, its vermilion pillars contrasting with the white snow on every horizontal surface and the blue-grey water below. Snow falls steadily against a clouded sky. A woodblock print from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II (1921), published as part of his extended series of atmospheric Japanese landscapes.

title: A Young Lady’s Adventure
description: A wide-eyed young woman with streaming hair strides in profile through a murky tangle of plant forms, bird-like creatures, and floating signs, a red arrow zigzagging near her feet. Klee made the work in 1922, during his early years teaching at the Bauhaus in Weimar; it is held by Tate Modern.
credit: Tate Modern

title: At Volga
description: A woman in a white dress and a reclining man rest on a grassy bluff beside silver birch trees, gazing out over a broad, luminous river stretching to the horizon. Painted in 1922, the canvas belongs to Kustodiev's late series of provincial pastorals — warm, sunlit evocations of Russian riverside life rendered in his characteristic decorative palette.

title: Atlas and the Hesperides
description: A circular ceiling painting for the rotunda of the Boston Museum of Fine Arts, showing the Titan stooping under the celestial sphere while the nymphs of the western garden recline at his feet. Sargent took on the rotunda decoration as a late, demanding mural commission. The composition reads from any vantage on the floor below.

title: Francis Picabia
description: Concentric black and white rings form a target across the sheet, with a reclining female nude figure laid diagonally over them, part coloured in watercolour wash. The title 'OPTOPHONE' is inscribed at the lower left. Made around 1922 in ink, watercolour, and pencil on board (72.1 × 60 cm), the work belongs to Picabia's Dada period.

title: La Tour Eiffel et Jardin du Champ de Mars
description: Delaunay shows the Eiffel Tower from a vertiginous overhead perspective, its ironwork base spread across a mosaic of green parkland and yellow pathways below. Painted in 1922 and now in the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden, the canvas belongs to the series *La Tour Eiffel et Jardin du Champ de Mars*, in which Delaunay moved beyond his earlier Cubist fragmentation toward flatter, more geometric forms and vivid contrasting colour. The aerial viewpoint transforms the monument into an abstract plan embedded in the lush grounds of the Champ de Mars.
credit: Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden Collection

title: Leon Bakst - Peasant woman Costume design for the Vaudeville Old Moscow
description: A peasant woman seen from behind, wearing a white blouse with green and red banding, a boldly patterned skirt with floral embroidery in red, yellow, and blue stripes, and a flower-decorated kokoshnik. Léon Bakst designed this costume in 1922 for the vaudeville Old Moscow, drawing on Russian folk dress to evoke the repertoire of his early career.

title: Night Shadows - Oct 1922 Shadowland
description: An anonymous pedestrian crosses an empty street under a sharply raking street lamp, watched from a high, vertiginous viewpoint. The etching, published in Shadowland magazine, sets out the lonely urban geometry Hopper would later expand into his great oil paintings.
credit: Shadowland (Sep. 1922 - Feb. 1923) on the Internet Archive

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: The cliffside Kannon Hall at Abuto perches on snow-covered rocks as a blizzard sweeps across the composition, with a small glimpse of the Inland Sea visible at lower left. The bold vertical framing and diagonal lines of falling snow are characteristic of Hasui's shin-hanga handling of winter subjects. The print was published in 1922 as part of the Selected Views of Japan series.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
englishTitle: Goryō in Amakusa, from Selected Views of Japan
description: A coastal view of Goryō on the Amakusa islands of Kyushu, from Hasui's Selected Views of Japan. The shin-hanga design pairs distant headlands with quiet anchorage, demonstrating the careful balance of woodblock colour and reserve that defined Hasui's travel sheets.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: Terraced green fields stretch across the foreground, with a path winding toward the sea where a sailing vessel is just visible, and Mount Onsengadake rises in blue-grey tones across the water. The print belongs to Hasui's Selected Views of Japan series, published in 1922, and is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. The work exemplifies his integration of agricultural landscape with distant topographical landmark.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
englishTitle: Hakozaki in Chikuzen Province, from Selected Views of Japan
description: A monumental stone lantern tower dominates the foreground, with a woman in kimono and a child pausing beside it as sailing boats drift on the calm sea beyond. Published in 1922 as part of Selected Views of Japan, the print depicts the famous stone tōrō at Hakozaki in former Chikuzen Province, near present-day Fukuoka. Hasui's flat colour planes and open horizon give the scene a calm, meditative quality.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: Dark volcanic rock walls enclose a deep pool of vivid turquoise water, with blazing orange autumn foliage crowning the cliffs above. The print belongs to Hasui's Selected Views of Japan series, published in 1922, and depicts the Kayagafuchi pool within Chōmonkyō Gorge in Yamaguchi Prefecture. The intense contrast of warm foliage, dark stone, and jewel-coloured water is among the most striking compositions in the series.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
englishTitle: Tochinoki Hot Springs in Higo Province
description: A night rain scene at Tochinoki Hot Springs in former Higo Province, with glowing windows piercing the dark while rain streaks fall against mountain silhouettes. From Kawase Hasui's Selected Views of Japan (Nihon fūkei senshū), held in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, the print exemplifies the shin-hanga movement's capacity for atmospheric nocturnal landscape.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts Boston

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
englishTitle: Kabeshima in Hizen Province, from the series Selected Views of Japan
description: A coastal hillside at Kabeshima in Hizen Province, with thatched farmhouses, tall conifers, and flowering shrubs overlooking a calm sea with a distant island on the horizon. Part of Kawase Hasui's Selected Views of Japan (Nihon fūkei senshū), published in 1922 and held in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, the print exemplifies his ability to find intimate pastoral beauty in regional scenery.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: The fishing village of Kyodomari in former Hizen Province, set into a sheltered cove of the Kyushu coast. Hasui uses softly registered color blocks and a low horizon line, in keeping with the contemplative pace of the Selected Views of Japan series.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: A full moon hangs over a multi-arch stone bridge on the Kōtsuki River in Kagoshima, with bare trees, street lanterns, and moonlit water in a quiet nocturnal scene. From the Selected Views of Japan series (Nihon fūkei senshū), created by Kawase Hasui in 1922, the print exemplifies the shin-hanga tradition of atmospheric night landscape.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: Sakurajima rises in warm reddish-orange tones above the calm bay opposite Kagoshima, with numerous sailing vessels dotting the water in the foreground. Published in 1922 as part of Kawase Hasui's Selected Views of Japan (Nihon fūkei senshū), the print captures the iconic volcanic landmark using the bold colour and refined perspective of the shin-hanga movement.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: A nocturnal canal scene at Kasuga-machi in Kumamoto, with white-walled storehouses and their reflections in dark water under a deep blue sky. Published in 1922 as part of Kawase Hasui's Selected Views of Japan (Nihon fūkei senshū), the print exemplifies his shin-hanga mastery of atmospheric night scenes with luminous architectural forms.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
englishTitle: Sōfuku-ji in Nagasaki (from Selected Views of Japan)
description: Sofuku-ji, an Obaku Zen temple in Nagasaki founded by Chinese merchants in the seventeenth century, recognizable by its red Ming-style gate. Hasui frames the precinct within Selected Views of Japan, marking Nagasaki's distinctive Sino-Japanese heritage.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
englishTitle: Slope of Senkō-ji Temple in Onomichi
description: The steep slope leading up to Senko-ji Temple in the port town of Onomichi, with rooftops descending toward the Inland Sea. From Selected Views of Japan, the print captures Onomichi's celebrated layered terrain.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
englishTitle: Shimabara Tsukumojima, from Selected Views of Japan
description: Tsukumojima, the cluster of small islets near Shimabara in Nagasaki Prefecture, seen beneath billowing cumulonimbus clouds tinted rose and violet. From Selected Views of Japan (1922), Hasui places a rowboat with two figures in the calm foreground water, their reflections merging with those of the pine-covered islets and sky. A torii gate on the nearest island anchors the composition in the shin-hanga tradition of atmospheric landscape.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: The Golden Pavilion of Kinkaku-ji in Kyoto under fresh snow, its gilded upper stories set against bare branches and a frozen pond. From Selected Views of Japan, this winter scene is among Hasui's most familiar treatments of a celebrated subject.

title: Senecio
description: A stylised head composed of geometric planes of yellow, orange, and pink, with two symmetrical round red eyes set within a circular form against a warm, textured ground. Painted in oil on gauze in 1922 during Klee's years at the Bauhaus in Weimar, the work reduces a human face to its essential geometry while preserving an uncanny expressiveness. It is held at the Kunstmuseum Basel.
credit: Kunstmuseum Basel

title: Sleeping Beauty by L. Bakst 04
description: Bakst's 1921 design for Scene 4 (The Awakening) of Tchaikovsky's Sleeping Beauty shows crimson curtains framing a canopied bed, with a dark winged form presiding over the sleeping figure. Executed in pencil and watercolour (48 × 66.8 cm) and held in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Collection in Lugano, the sheet was made for Diaghilev's 1921 London production at the Alhambra Theatre — the last major Ballets Russes collaboration before Bakst's death in 1924.

title: Starry Night
description: Painted from the terrace of Munch's Ekely estate outside Oslo, this nocturne reduces landscape to broad zones of indigo, snow-white and shadow. A revisitation of his 1893 motif, it trades earlier symbolism for a quieter, late-career meditation on solitude under the winter sky.
credit: Photo Van Gogh Museum

title: Franz von Stuck
description: A late self-portrait on board, signed and dated 1923, presents the Munich Secession founder in dark dress against a neutral ground. The clipped scale and sober finish reflect von Stuck's habit of treating his own image as part of his public persona as artist-prince.
credit: Christie's

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: A large Japanese sailing vessel with billowing white sails occupies the centre of the composition, its hull reflected in the calm blue water, with rocky headlands rising behind. The print belongs to Hasui's Selected Views of Japan series, published in 1923, and depicts the coastal waters off Iwafune in the former Bingo Province. Hasui's characteristic clear sky and precise colour planes give the scene an air of quiet confidence.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
englishTitle: Cherry Trees at Kakize, Bungo Province
description: White cherry trees in full bloom fill the centre of the composition before a backdrop of steep green cliffs, with thatched farm buildings nestled along a stone wall and a lone figure standing beneath the blossom. Issued within the Selected Views of Japan series in 1923, the print captures the brief spring flowering at Kakize in former Bungo Province, combining precise woodblock colour with a strong sense of mountain enclosure.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: A stone arch bridge spans a clear stream in Kanahama, Hizen Province, with two figures visible on the parapet and scattered boulders in the water below. Issued in 1923 as part of Kawase Hasui's Selected Views of Japan (Nihon fūkei senshū) and held in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, the composition demonstrates the shin-hanga interest in regional architectural and natural detail.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: The stone embankment and moat of Kumamoto Castle are reflected in calm water, with a small bridge visible in the middle distance beneath a soft dawn sky. From Kawase Hasui's Selected Views of Japan (Nihon fūkei senshū), published in 1923, the print pairs the castle's distinctive stonework with a tranquil waterside view in characteristic shin-hanga landscape style.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: Lake Ezu in Kumamoto under summer rain, with lush green reed beds in the foreground, a solitary figure in a small boat, and tree-covered islets receding toward distant rain-veiled mountains. From Kawase Hasui's Selected Views of Japan (Nihon fūkei senshū), published in 1923, the print captures the atmospheric breadth of the lake using the layered colour gradations of shin-hanga printmaking.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: Nonomiya Shrine in Kyoto's Sagano district at night in winter, with tall tree trunks framing a snow-covered shrine building and stone wall under a deep blue starlit sky. From Kawase Hasui's Selected Views of Japan (Nihon fūkei senshū), published in 1923 and held in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, the print renders the ancient shrine in a contemplative nocturnal atmosphere.

title: After the Battle of Grunwald
description: From the twenty-canvas Slav Epic that Mucha worked on for nearly two decades, this scene shows the aftermath of the 1410 Polish-Lithuanian victory over the Teutonic Knights. The Art Nouveau poster designer here deploys monumental tempera-and-oil composition to advance a pan-Slavic political mythology.

title: De Gion brug te Hondo in Amakusa Amakusa Hondo Gionbashi
englishTitle: Gion Bridge at Hondo in Amakusa (Amakusa Hondō Gionbashi), from Selected Views of Japan
description: A woman carrying vegetables pauses on the riverbank beneath the arching wooden piers of the Gion bridge at Hondo in Amakusa, as ducks rest in the shallow water beside her. Kawase Hasui designed this woodblock print in 1924 for Watanabe Shōzaburō's publisher, as part of the series Selected Views of Japan. The composition uses cool blues and the textured structure of the bridge to frame the quiet, low-tide scene.
credit: http://hdl.handle.net/10934/RM0001.collect.47567 Rijksmuseum

title: Kustodiev Voloshin
description: Portrait of the Symbolist poet and critic Maximilian Voloshin, painted in 1924. By that date Kustodiev had been confined to a wheelchair for eight years after spinal surgery, working almost entirely from photographs and sittings arranged at his Petrograd apartment.

title: Matsue
description: A crescent moon hangs in the twilight sky above a quiet canal at Matsue in Izumo Province, a lone boatman poling through still water that mirrors the warm glow of lamplight from the low buildings lining the bank. The woodblock print of 1924, titled 'Matsue (Crescent Moon), Izumo,' belongs to Hasui's 'Souvenirs of Travel, Third Series,' published by Watanabe Shōzaburō as part of the shin-hanga revival.
credit: Flickr The Sandiego Museum of Art collection

title: Rachel Strong by L.Bakst
description: Léon Bakst's 1924 portrait shows Rachel Strong — described in sources as the future Countess Henri de Buazhelen — standing outdoors in a dark dress with a white wrap, a cane in hand and a dog at her side. The golden-ochre landscape behind her reflects the warm palette of Bakst's late society portraiture.

title: Shironeko by Takahashi Hiroaki
description: A white cat with orange patches and a decorative red collar rests compactly against a dark green ground, gazing directly at the viewer. Published in 1924, this shin-hanga woodblock print by Takahashi Shōtei is held in the National Diet Library and exemplifies the movement's close observation of animals within a traditional Japanese printing format.
credit: National Diet Library

title: Tabi miyage dai sanshū
englishTitle: Asahi Peak Seen from Mt. Hakuba
description: Asahi Peak fills the composition as seen from Mount Hakuba, its steep rocky faces streaked with snow and flanked by dark green forest slopes under a vivid blue sky. A single bank of cloud breaks around the upper ridge. A woodblock print from Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III (1924), the print's bold close-up perspective and saturated colour are characteristic of Hasui's mountain subjects within the shin-hanga tradition.

title: Tabi miyage dai sanshū
description: The narrow lanes of the Arifuku hot-spring quarter in Iwami Province glow with the warm amber light of inn windows at night, red-tiled rooftops clustered beneath a dark hillside of pines. A few figures move along the alley. A woodblock print from Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III (1924), the composition conveys the intimate warmth of a provincial onsen town through its contrast of lit interiors against the dark forest above.

title: Enbu by Hayami Gyoshu
description: Moths of varying colours — white, cream, spotted, and pale blue-green — spiral upward through tongues of flame against a deep dark ground. Hayami Gyoshū painted this work in 1925, fusing nihonga pigments with a decorative, rhythmic energy that reflects the Taishō-era modernism of his circle; the work is held in the Yamatane Museum, Tokyo.
credit: Yamatane Museum, Tokyo

title: Het Zojo heiligdom in Shiba Shiba Zojoji
englishTitle: The Zōjō-ji Temple at Shiba (Shiba Zōjōji), from Twenty Views of Tokyo
description: The Zōjō-ji temple at Shiba, captured by Kawase Hasui for Twenty Views of Tokyo. Hasui became the most prolific landscape designer of the Shin-hanga revival, working closely with the publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō from the early 1920s.
credit: Rijksmuseum

title: Irissen
description: Deep blue irises rise against a softly graded pale background in this colour woodblock print by Ohara Koson. Published by Watanabe Shōzaburō between 1925 and 1936, the print belongs to Koson's celebrated series of Shin-hanga flower subjects and is now in the collection of the Rijksmuseum.

title: Kawase Zôjôji
description: View of the Tokugawa mortuary temple Zōjō-ji at Shiba, from the Twenty Views of Tokyo series. A solitary figure shelters under a paper umbrella as snow falls against the vermilion gate, a hallmark of Kawase's quiet, weather-soaked urban landscapes.
credit: Collection Walter Schmidt

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
englishTitle: Dawn at Mihogaseki in Izumo Province
description: A harbour scene at dawn in Mihogaseki, Izumo Province, with a stone jetty, a lantern post, moored sailboats, and a green headland reflected in still water. From the Selected Views of Japan series (Nihon fūkei senshū), published in 1925, the print is characteristic of Kawase Hasui's shin-hanga attention to specific times of day and coastal atmosphere.

title: Russian Venus
description: A full-length nude woman stands in a wooden bathhouse, smiling as she combs her long auburn hair, a birch besom held in her other hand, with steam and bath implements around her. Painted c. 1925–26, Russian Venus was Kustodiev's last major work, completed from his wheelchair; it now hangs in the Nizhny Novgorod State Art Museum.
credit: lj.rossia.org anzenbergergallery.com

title: Siberische Blauwe Nachtegaal bij een pioenroos onder een besneeuwde schoof
englishTitle: Siberian Blue Robin with Peony Beneath a Snow-Laden Sheaf
description: A small green Siberian blue robin perches on a snow-dusted reed shelter above a single pink peony, the composition set against a deep black ground. Ohara Koson worked closely with the Watanabe house to produce a long sequence of bird-and-flower designs for export.

title: Tabi miyage dai sanshū
englishTitle: Futomi in Awa Province (from Souvenirs of Travel III)
description: A torii gate stands on a rocky shore at Futomi in Awa Province, flanked by a pair of stone lanterns and backed by crashing waves and distant green islands. A small figure shelters beneath the gate, and a wooden boat rests to one side. A woodblock print from Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III (1925), the composition centres on the coastal shrine's gateway as a framing device for sea and sky.

title: The Grand Canyon
description: The South Rim falls away into vast layered cliffs flushed with desert light, a Japanese sensibility brought to the American Southwest. The print belongs to Yoshida's United States series, made after his sketching tour abroad, and uses successive overprintings to suggest the canyon's atmospheric haze.

title: The Wetterhorn
description: A woodblock print from Hiroshi Yoshida's Europe Series, depicting the Swiss mountain peak of the Wetterhorn. Created in 1925, this shin hanga work exemplifies Yoshida's distinctive blend of traditional Japanese woodblock technique with Western landscape subjects.

title: Twee kaketoes op tak met pruimenbloesem
englishTitle: Two Cockatoos on a Plum Branch
description: Two white cockatoos perch among the early flowers of a plum branch. Ohara Koson produced the design for Watanabe Shōzaburō's Shin-hanga programme, which translated the kachō-e tradition into a refined modern colour-print idiom.

title: 2560px-NDL-DC 2586549-12 Kawase Hasui T15 crd
description: Jagged rock pinnacles, caught red by the low sun, rise from a teal sea off Ryūga Island on the Oga Peninsula in Akita, grassy slopes climbing behind them beneath a bank of grey cloud. The woodblock print comes from Hasui's series Souvenirs of Travel III, published in 1926; this impression is held in the National Diet Library Digital Collections.

title: 960px-Robert Delaunay
description: The Eiffel Tower surges upward as if seen from its base, its lattice splayed against interlocking planes of saturated colour. Delaunay returned to the monument repeatedly across his career, fragmenting it through the Orphism he developed with Sonia Delaunay; this 1926 oil on canvas is in the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris.

title: Apotheosis of the Slavs
description: The closing canvas of the Slav Epic, in which Mucha gathers the history of the Slavic peoples into an allegorical apotheosis culminating in a youthful figure of independence. The cycle of twenty monumental paintings was his self-declared life's work, given to the city of Prague.

provenance.collection: museum collection of the Prague City Gallery

title: Clearing Sky after Snow
description: A plate from Hasui's Twenty Views of Tokyo, depicting the Sensō-ji temple complex at Asakusa under fresh snow. A leading figure of the shin-hanga revival, Hasui rebuilt the older ukiyo-e collaboration of designer, carver, and printer to record a modernising city in soft, atmospheric colour woodblock.

title: dahlias
description: Orange, red, and yellow dahlias fill a blue-and-white ceramic vase in this vibrant floral still life, each bloom rendered in thick, swirling strokes against a warm, pale ground. Monet returned to the cut-flower bouquet throughout his career, treating the arrangement as a concentrated study in colour and impasto rather than a botanical record.

title: Dahlias
credit: Claude Monet - Dahlias , Irina , 2015-01-07 18:57

title: Eiffel Tower
description: A graphite drawing depicts the Eiffel Tower from close below, the lattice ironwork and arched base filling the composition in a steep upward-looking perspective. Robert Delaunay made this study between 1926 and 1928, and it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The monochromatic pencil work records the tower's structural geometry with an emphasis on the play of angled members that also informs his painted versions of the subject.
credit: Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation

title: Hiroshi Yoshida, Hikaru umi, 1926
description: Two sailing boats rest on the glistening water of the Inland Sea, their reflections shimmering on an almost glassy surface. From Yoshida's 1926 series Setonaikai shū (A Series of Ocean Views at Seto), the print demonstrates his mastery of tonal gradation and the subtle play of light on water.
credit: https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/jpd.02224/

title: Hodakayama
description: From Yoshida's Twelve Scenes in the Japan Alps, this view of Hotaka-dake records the artist's own mountaineering observations of the Northern Alps. Yoshida combined ukiyo-e block techniques with Western tonal modeling, often printing the same blocks in different palettes to capture changing light.

title: Junks in Inatori Bay
description: A woodblock print by Japanese artist Takahashi Shōtei depicting traditional junks moored in Inatori Bay in the Izu region. Published in 1926, this work exemplifies the beauty of Japanese maritime scenes and traditional sailing vessels. The print measures 392mm by 268mm and is held in the collection of Te Papa Tongarewa, the Museum of New Zealand.

title: Kanae Yamamoto
englishTitle: At the Foot of Mount Tokkō (Tokkō sanroku shūi)
description: A view at the foot of Mount Tokkō in oils, painted after Yamamoto's return from Europe where he absorbed Post-Impressionist palette and brushwork. Better remembered for woodblock prints, he pursued painting alongside his advocacy for the children's free-drawing and farmers' art movements in interwar Japan.

title: Kōjaku cavern at Oga Peninsula
description: A sea cave on the Oga Peninsula renders blue-green water against weathered rock, from Hasui's third Souvenirs of Travel series. The artist toured rural Japan compulsively, and these prints document a coastline that motorised tourism was just beginning to reach.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Kumoi-Zakura (Kumoi Cherry Trees)
description: Two figures stand beneath a weeping cherry tree at night, its blossoming branches silhouetted against a deep teal sky and a luminous full moon. The woodblock print, dated 1926 and held at the Toledo Museum of Art, exemplifies Yoshida's ability to capture atmospheric nocturnal effects through delicate gradations of colour.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
description: A three-storied red pagoda at Kiyomizu-dera in Yasugi, Izumo Province, stands against a dark night sky while snow falls and settles on surrounding trees and stone walls. From Kawase Hasui's Selected Views of Japan (Nihon fūkei senshū), published in 1926, the print illustrates the shin-hanga mastery of winter atmosphere and architectural silhouette.

title: Ochanomizu
description: From Hasui's Twenty Views of Tokyo, this woodblock print shows wet snow muffling the rooftops along the Kanda River at Ochanomizu. The artist was renowned for his subtle differentiation of snowfall, here rendered as soft cotton-like accumulation.

title: Sailing Boats
description: From the Inland Sea series of woodblock prints, this view shows fishing junks under afternoon light. Yoshida printed the same key block in successive variants from morning to night, a shin-hanga experiment in atmosphere achieved by altering only the inking and color blocks.

title: Sailing Boats
description: Junks ride a glassy sea under a low evening sun in this version of Yoshida's six-state Sailing Boats suite. The warm orange ground and silhouetted sails show how shin-hanga printers could transform a single composition through color alone.

title: Sailing Boats
description: Sailing junks drift in a pale, fog-bound sea, their masts dissolving into the haze. One of six time-of-day variants printed from a single key block, this state demonstrates Yoshida's command of bokashi gradations and his shin-hanga sensitivity to weather and air.

title: Sailing Boats
description: Sailing junks rest on a glassy sea suffused with warm rose and orange tones in this morning state of Yoshida's Sailing Boats suite, part of his Inland Sea series of 1926. One of six time-of-day variants printed from a single key block, the work exemplifies shin-hanga's command of atmospheric colour.

title: Sailing Boats
description: In the night state of Yoshida's Sailing Boats suite, the junks' sails appear luminous against a deep indigo sea, their reflections shimmering below while distant shore lights glow on the horizon. Printed in 1926 as part of the Inland Sea series, the sheet demonstrates shin-hanga craftsmen's ability to evoke nocturnal light through carefully graded colour blocks.

title: Self-Portrait with Palette
description: Munch portrays himself outdoors, palette in hand, against a backdrop of green foliage and a pale clouded sky. The face is rendered with characteristic directness, the brushwork expressively loose. Painted in 1926, the work is now in the Kunsthalle Mannheim.

title: Tabi miyage dai sanshū
description: A woodblock print from Hasui Kawase's Souvenirs of Travel III series (1926), depicting the torii gate of Gozanoishi Shrine standing in the waters of Lake Tazawa. The large, dark-timbered gate occupies the foreground, its reflection shimmering in the calm lake, with green hills rising beyond under a cloud-dappled summer sky. The composition exemplifies the shin-hanga movement's combination of traditional Japanese subject matter with precise, luminous colour printing.

title: The Dinner
description: Four figures are gathered around a white-clothed table beneath a hanging oil lamp whose warm glow picks out the dishes, a jug, and the faces of the diners, while a figure in a white cap is dimly visible in the background. Painted in 1868–69 and held by the Foundation E.G. Bührle Collection, the work is an early experiment in depicting artificial interior light, a subject Monet rarely revisited.

title: Tōkyō nijū kei
englishTitle: The Grounds of the Kanda Myōjin Shrine
description: The stone-paved grounds of the Kanda Myōjin Shrine are dominated by two towering dark cedars, a stone torii gate at the end of the path, and a small shrine lantern visible to one side. Billowing summer clouds rise dramatically behind the trees, filling the upper half of the composition. The print is from Kawase Hasui's series Twenty Views of Tōkyō (Tōkyō nijū kei), published in 1926.

title: Tōkyō nijū kei
englishTitle: Shin Ōhashi Bridge from Twenty Views of Tōkyō
description: The steel girders of the Shin Ohashi bridge over the Sumida River, rendered through slanting rain and a darkening sky. Hasui treats modern Tokyo infrastructure with the lyrical atmospherics of traditional landscape woodblock printing.

title: Vase of Tulips
description: Red-and-yellow and white tulips splay from a slender dark vase against a pale ground, the leaves swept in as long strokes of blue-green and the blooms built up in thick wet-in-wet colour; the canvas is signed at lower right. Monet painted flower still lifes chiefly in the early 1880s, between landscape campaigns, and this bouquet belongs to that vein of his work.
credit: Claude Monet - Vase of Tulips , Irina , 2014-05-29 23:25

title: Hachirōgata Lagoon
description: A nocturnal scene from Hachirōgata Lagoon in Akita, showing a large tree and a wooden structure beside still water under a deep blue night sky. Kawase Hasui's print, from the series Souvenirs of Travel III (published 1927), uses deep indigo tones to capture the quiet darkness of the lakeshore.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Kameidô
description: The arched drum bridge of Kameido Tenjin shrine reflects in the still pond below, surrounded by spring wisteria. Yoshida revisits a motif made famous by Hiroshige, but rebuilds it with the soft tonal gradations and calibrated overprinting of the shin-hanga revival.

title: Karasu Marsh
description: Karasu Marsh in Akita is seen across open water, pine-clad hillsides rising on the far shore beneath a sky of layered clouds. Kawase Hasui's print for the series Souvenirs of Travel III uses a restrained palette of blue and green to convey the calm of this inland landscape, published in 1927.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Kawase Tenno-ji-27
description: A solitary figure with an umbrella stands before the multi-storeyed pagoda and snow-laden roofs of the ancient Shitennō-ji temple in Osaka. Published in 1927 as part of Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III series, the print applies the shin-hanga woodblock tradition to a wintry scene, conveying the hush of falling snow through quiet tonal contrast.

title: Tōkyō jūnidai
description: A small cargo boat makes its way along the Sumida River beside the Daikon vegetable wharf, while produce is piled on the near bank under willows and workers tend to the waterfront buildings above. The print belongs to Hasui's series Twelve Scenes of Tōkyō (Tōkyō jūnidai) and exemplifies his shin-hanga approach of merging traditional workshop technique with Western-influenced perspective.

title: 2560px-NDL-DC 2586549-07 Kawase Hasui S03 crd
description: On a rain-puddled quay, a dog stands beside a water pump and looks out across the harbour, where sailing vessels and a steamer ride at anchor and the lights of the far shore streak the still water. Akashi-chō after Rain belongs to Hasui's series Twenty Views of Tokyo, published in 1928 (Shōwa 3); this impression is from the National Diet Library Digital Collections.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Dawn at Beppu
description: Moored boats rest in a Beppu harbour at dawn, their reflections held in still water beneath a crescent moon and a warm band of colour at the horizon. Tall hills press against the sky behind them. From the series Souvenirs of Travel III, the print demonstrates Hasui's mastery of bokashi gradation to render the cool, transitional light of early morning.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Espagnole et agneau de l'Apocalypse
description: A Spanish woman's face is overlaid with the lamb and other contour images in superimposed line. Made in 1928, the work belongs to Picabia's Transparencies series, begun the previous year, in which he alternated paint with resinous varnish so that motifs drawn from Renaissance frescoes, Catalan murals and popular sources could coexist without fully merging.

title: Hōrai Rock
description: A scene of the towering Hōrai Rock rising from the Kiso River, drawn from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III. The print balances the cliff's bulk against soft atmospheric washes, a hallmark of the shin-hanga revival of traditional landscape woodblock.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Kamezaki in Owari Province
description: A nocturne depicting a quiet street in Kamezaki, Owari Province, with a large tree, a stone wall, and the warm glow of a lit window glimpsed through deep blue darkness. Kawase Hasui's woodblock print, from the series Souvenirs of Travel III, was published in 1928 and demonstrates the artist's skill in evoking atmosphere through dense, layered colour fields.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Kiyomizu-dō Temple in Ueno
description: The Kiyomizu Hall in Ueno Park seen across blossoming trees, from Hasui's Twenty Views of Tōkyō. The shin-hanga design preserves the planar colour fields of the woodblock tradition while introducing softened, plein-air light.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Nishi Park
description: Tall pines frame a wide bay view at Nishi Park in Fukuoka, with small islands and sailing boats on the calm water below a pink and blue sky. Kawase Hasui's woodblock print, from the series Souvenirs of Travel III (1928), uses the vertical rhythm of the pine trunks to draw the eye across an open coastal panorama.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Rapids at the Upper Reaches of Tone River
description: Powerful cascading water fills the composition in Hiroshi Yoshida's 1928 woodblock print, with white foam churning over dark rocks as the river plunges in a broad torrent. Yoshida, who trained as a Western-style oil painter before turning to woodblock printing, achieves the water's translucent force through the layered impressions characteristic of his technique.

title: Red Cavalry Riding
description: A thin band of red horsemen gallops along the horizon against a vast pale sky, underpinned by bold horizontal stripes of red, black, green, blue, and cream — a Suprematist landscape painted between 1928 and 1932 by Kazimir Malevich. The work entered the State Russian Museum in Leningrad and stands as a rare bridge between Malevich's abstract language and recognisable Soviet iconography.

title: Starlit Night at Miyajima
description: From the shin-hanga series Souvenirs of Travel III, this nocturne shows the floating torii of Itsukushima beneath a star-pricked sky. Hasui pairs deep indigo bokashi gradations with sparse highlights to register the hush of Miyajima after dark.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Yoshida Komagatake
description: From the summit of Komagatake, a vast sea of white clouds fills the composition, with the distant cone of Mount Fuji rising above the cloud layer at the left. A small shrine or refuge marks the rocky foreground ridge in this 1928 woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida, whose lifelong mountaineering informed his alpine series.

title: Evening in Beppu
description: A solitary figure with an umbrella picks their way along a rain-slicked path beside a large bare tree, with softly lit buildings and distant mountains receding into a dark, wet night. There is no coastal view; Hasui locates the scene in Beppu's streets rather than at the shore. From the series Souvenirs of Travel III (1929), the sheet uses bokashi to convey the deep-blue chill of a rainy evening.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Hera
description: Multiple female faces are superimposed in transparent contours across a ground of leaves and flowers in shades of yellow-green and blue, with hands and foliage woven throughout the composition. The work, dated around 1929, belongs to Picabia's Transparencies series, in which layered figures drawn from diverse visual sources are merged into a single ambiguous image. It is one of the series Picabia developed after his departure from the Paris avant-garde.

title: Kagurazaka Street at Night after Rain
englishTitle: Kagurazaka Street at Night after Rain, from Twelve Scenes of Tokyo
description: A woodblock print from Hiroshi Yoshida's "Twelve Scenes of Tokyo" series (shin hanga). Completed in 1929, this composition captures a wet Kagurazaka street at night, rendered with the artist's characteristic approach to modern Japanese printmaking. Part of the Tokyo Fuji Art Museum collection.

title: Kamisuki
description: A bijin-ga showing a young woman drawing a comb through her loosened black hair, her undergarment slipping from one shoulder. Kotondo revives the intimate vanity scenes of Edo-period printmaking within the early Showa shin-hanga movement.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Shinobazu Pond in Rain
description: Rain falls across Shinobazu Pond in Ueno, the lotus leaves and far shore softened to muted greys and greens. Hasui's mastery of bokashi gradation and overprinted rain-lines made him the foremost printmaker of weather in twentieth-century Japan.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Takinogawa River
description: From the series Twenty Views of Tōkyō, this print follows the Takinogawa River as it winds through suburban greenery. Hasui captures a quieter periphery of the modernizing capital, layering subtle woodblock washes for foliage and reflected water.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: The Pond at Benten Shrine in Shiba
description: Figures in kimono cross a low wooden bridge over a pond densely covered with lotus leaves and pink blooms, the overcast sky above suggesting a grey summer day. Kawase Hasui produced this shin-hanga woodblock print in 1929, using layered bokashi gradations and a precise keyblock to capture the Benten Shrine pond in Shiba, Tokyo.

title: American Gothic
description: A stern Iowa farmer and his daughter stand before a white frame house with a Carpenter Gothic window, the pitchfork echoing the seams of his overalls. Wood used his sister Nan and his dentist as models, fashioning a dry, hard-edged image that became shorthand for rural America.

title: Moon at Magome
description: Part of Twenty Views of Tōkyō, the print shows the moon hanging over the rural fringes of Magome. Hasui builds the night scene from layered indigo blocks and a single luminous disc, demonstrating shin-hanga's debt to classical Edo landscape traditions.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Nikkō Kaidō
description: A shin-hanga woodblock print depicting a quiet stretch of the Nikkō Kaidō, the historic highway leading to the Tokugawa mausoleum. Hasui captures the avenue's towering cryptomeria with the soft atmospheric tonality and precise gradation that define his landscape work.

title: Ōmori Coast
description: A view of the Ōmori coast on Tokyo Bay, drawn from Twenty Views of Tōkyō. Hasui registers the meeting of urban edge and water in soft, overcast tones, the shin-hanga answer to Hokusai and Hiroshige's earlier capital views.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586550

title: Sumō-wrestling toads by Hōson
description: Ohara Koson's colour woodblock print shows a group of toads in various animated poses — two grappling upright, others leaping or watching — on a grassy ground with a single autumn leaf in the air. Working in the shin-hanga idiom, Koson brings naturalist observation to a comic subject with long roots in Japanese caricature, here dating to around 1930.

title: Woman Before a Mirror
description: A bijin-ga in which a woman, her patterned kimono fallen from her upper body, raises both arms to arrange her hair before a mirror visible at the print's left edge. The richly decorated fabric — pink with floral motifs and contrasting obi — pools in the lower half of the composition. Kotondo balances flat decorative pattern against the quiet intimacy of a private dressing moment in this 1930 shin-hanga print held at the Walters Art Museum.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Meguro Fudō Temple
description: A shin-hanga woodblock print by Kawase Hasui of Ryusen-ji, popularly known as the Meguro Fudo temple, in Tokyo. Seen from beside the vermilion main hall, a woman in kimono pauses at the entrance while blossoms show beyond the gate roofs and dappled light falls across the stone steps and lanterns of the precinct. The print was published in 1931; this impression is preserved in the National Diet Library, Tokyo.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Midnight Ride of Paul Revere
description: Grant Wood collapses the night of 18 April 1775 into a single moonlit vista, the white steeple of the Old North Church lit at upper centre as Revere gallops the country road through sleeping Lexington and Concord. Painted in 1931 on Masonite in the Iowa Regionalist's mature style, the canvas entered the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1950.
credit: Grant Wood

title: Shinagawa
description: Rain slants across a canal in Shinagawa's old fishing quarter at dusk: roofed boats lie moored along the bank, a figure under a blue umbrella hurries past the weathered houses, and a single lit window warms the gray-blue scene. The 1931 color woodblock print is characteristic of Hasui's shin-hanga landscapes, which revived the ukiyo-e tradition with Western atmosphere and a fascination for rain, snow, and nightfall. Shinagawa was the first post station of the old Tokaido road out of Edo.
credit: Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art https://jmapps.ne.jp/apmoa/det.html?data_id=18651

title: Snow in Mukojima
description: Thick snow falls through a darkening sky onto a boat landing at Mukojima, on the bank of Tokyo's Sumida River: moored boats lie blanketed in white, a stilt-built boathouse glows from within, and a lone ferryman crosses the still water. The 1931 color woodblock print shows Hasui's shin-hanga manner at its most atmospheric, using graded blues and untouched white paper to carry the weight of the snowfall. Snow scenes such as this became the works for which he is best remembered.

title: De rand van de Shinobazu vijver tijdens een mistige avond. Kasumu yube Shinobazu chihan
englishTitle: Edge of Shinobazu Pond on a Misty Evening (Kasumu yūbe Shinobazu chihan)
description: Lanterns burn in the haze of a foggy evening at Ueno Park, with figures passing beside the still water of Shinobazu Pond and a pagoda rising behind. Kasamatsu Shirō was a leading designer of the second Shin-hanga generation; this print was issued by Watanabe Shōzaburō in 1932.

title: Morning Mist in Taj Mahal
description: A color woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida of the Taj Mahal looming through early-morning mist, its marble silhouette dissolving in pale light above the reflecting garden. The design, Morning Mist in Taj Mahal No. 5, belongs to the India and Southeast Asia series Yoshida produced after travelling across the subcontinent in 1930-31, returning to the monument at different hours in companion prints. It was published in 1932.

title: Rudolf Ernst After Prayers
description: Two men leave prayers through a magnificent horseshoe-arched doorway framed by carved stucco and blue-green tilework: an elderly worshipper in white robes and turban leans on his cane, steadied by a companion in an embroidered violet kaftan and red fez. The oil on panel, signed 'R. Ernst,' is typical of the Vienna-born Orientalist's polished studio compositions, which assembled Moorish architectural detail — much of it derived from the Alhambra — around quiet moments of daily ritual. Ernst spent most of his career in Paris painting such scenes for the Salon market.

title: Self-Portrait
credit: polarbearstale.blogspot; Figge Art Museum, online

title: 50 Kawase Hasui S0806 crd
description: A colour woodblock print by Kawase Hasui from a print collection published by Watanabe Shōzaburō's print shop in 1935 (Shōwa 10). Hasui's shin-hanga landscapes pair traditional ukiyo-e craftsmanship with naturalistic light and atmosphere, and this sheet is preserved in the National Diet Library's digital collection.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586550

title: 58 Kawase Hasui S0807 crd
description: A colour woodblock print by Kawase Hasui, issued in 1935 (Shōwa 10) through the publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō as part of a collected print album. Like the rest of Hasui's shin-hanga output, it renders an atmospheric Japanese landscape with carved-block colour gradations; the copy digitised here belongs to the National Diet Library.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586550

title: 74 Kawase Hasui S0812 crd
description: A colour woodblock print by Kawase Hasui from an album published by the Watanabe print shop in 1935 (Shōwa 10). Hasui, a central figure of the shin-hanga revival, supplied the watercolour design while Watanabe's carvers and printers produced the blocks; the impression shown is held by the National Diet Library.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586550

title: Charles W. Bartlett - watercolor self-portrait
description: Bartlett depicts himself in watercolour, signed and dated September 1933. The English-born artist had settled in Hawaii by 1917 after extensive travels in Japan and India, where he became closely associated with the shin-hanga movement and collaborated with the Tokyo publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō. The work is held in a private collection.
credit: Miles, Richard and Jennifer Saville, A Printmaker in Paradise, The Art and Life of Charles W. Bartlett, with a catalogue raisonné of etchings and color woodblock prints , Honolulu, Hawaii, Honolulu Academy of Arts, 2001

title: Ohara koson
description: A color woodcut of 1933 by Ohara Koson, the leading designer of bird-and-animal subjects in the shin-hanga print movement. A black-and-white cat wearing a red collar and bell crouches on the wooden floor, staring intently into a glass bowl in which orange goldfish circle, a small hand net lying beside it. An impression of the print is in the Cincinnati Art Museum.

title: The Golden Pavilion
description: Yoshida Hiroshi's colour woodblock print of Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion in Kyoto, from his 1933 Kansai District series. The gilded temple rises over its reflecting pond in the layered, atmospheric colour that defined Yoshida's shin-hanga landscapes. This impression belongs to the San Diego Museum of Art.
credit: San Diego Museum of Art

title: Akashi strand Akashi no hama
description: A solitary pine bends over the moonlit waters of Akashi Bay as sailboats drift in the distance. Tsuchiya Kōitsu designed the print for the Watanabe Shin-hanga workshop, which carried the lyric landscape tradition of Hiroshige into the twentieth century.

title: De grote lantaarn van de Kannon tempel in Asakusa Asakusa Kannondo ochochin
englishTitle: The Great Lantern of the Kannon Temple at Asakusa (Asakusa Kannondō ōchōchin)
description: Pilgrims climb the steps beneath the giant red lantern that marks the entrance to the Kannon temple at Asakusa. Kasamatsu Shirō issued the design through the Watanabe publishing house at the height of the Shin-hanga revival of traditional ukiyo-e subjects.

title: Het drijvende paviljoen te Katada in de sneeuw Yuki no Katada Ukimido
englishTitle: The Floating Pavilion at Katada in the Snow (Yuki no Katada Ukimidō)
description: Ukimidō, the floating pavilion of Katada, stands in the dark waters of Lake Biwa during a night snowfall, its lantern light reflected in the still surface below, while a snow-laden pine frames the scene from the near shore. This colour woodblock print, published by Watanabe Shōzaburō in March 1934, exemplifies Tsuchiya Kōitsu's mastery of nocturnal atmosphere within the Shin-hanga tradition.

title: Rhythms
description: Interlocking discs of blue, red, green, yellow, and black-and-white rotate against a light grey ground. Painted and signed in 1934, the canvas belongs to Delaunay's late *Rythmes* series, in which cascading arcs of pure colour generate a sense of kinetic rotation without any representational content. The work was displayed at the Centre Georges Pompidou's *Rythmes sans fin* exhibition (October 2014 – January 2015).
credit: Exposition Robert Delaunay "Rythmes sans fin" - Centre national d'art et de culture Georges Pompidou - Paris [Note: This caption is incorrect. The painting by that name is actually this one also in the same gallery, same artist, same creation year. The painting depicted here is simply "Rythmes".]

title: Archers
description: Two figures raise a single large bow in a vivid, light-filled landscape of yellows and greens, a target visible in the distance, while a third figure at lower right holds a clutch of arrows. Kirchner painted this work between 1935 and 1937 during his final years near Davos, applying the flattened, bold contours characteristic of his late style.

title: Suzukawa River
description: A color woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida, dated 1935 in the margin, showing snow-capped Mount Fuji rising beyond a stand of pines and farm buildings along the Suzukawa river, the mountain and trees doubled in the still water of the foreground. Yoshida trained as a Western-style painter, and his prints join Japanese woodblock technique to a naturalist's handling of light and atmosphere, produced under his close supervision in his own studio.

title: Walpurgis Night
description: Dense, swirling blue lines scratched over a near-black ground conjure half-legible figures and watchful, owl-like eyes in this 1935 panel by Paul Klee. The work evokes the German folk legend of witches gathering on the Brocken on the eve of May Day, made the year after Klee left Düsseldorf following his dismissal by the Nazi authorities. It is held at Tate (T00669).
credit: Tate Modern

title: 'Three Sisters' by Yamakawa Shūhō
description: A four-fold screen painted in ink and color on silk by the nihonga artist Yamakawa Shuho in 1936. Three young women in kimono are grouped around a white motor car: one leans against the front fender holding a handbag, another sits inside the open rear door, and the third looks out through the back window, a quietly modern image of well-to-do life in 1930s Japan rendered in the flat, elegant manner of traditional figure painting. The screen is in the Honolulu Museum of Art.
credit: Honolulu Museum of Art

title: 溥僩丙子夏日寫生
englishTitle: Summer Study from the Bingzi Year
description: A summer sketch study created in 1936 (the year of Bingzi in the Chinese zodiac) by the modern Chinese painter Pu Xuan. This work exemplifies the artist's approach to observational painting during a productive period of artistic exploration.

title: De warme bronnen van Shuzenji Shuzenji onsen
englishTitle: The Hot Springs of Shuzenji (Shuzenji onsen)
description: Lit hotels line the Katsura River at the hot-spring town of Shuzenji on the Izu peninsula, with cherry blossom in the foreground. Kasamatsu Shirō's 1937 design pairs the meticulous block-cutting of Shin-hanga with a romanticism inherited from late nineteenth-century landscape prints.

title: huang-binhong-landscape
description: A landscape scroll painting by Huang Binhong (1865–1955), the influential Chinese-Taiwanese painter, art historian, and journalist. This work exemplifies the traditional Chinese mountain landscape tradition that Binhong championed throughout his career.

title: Kanae Yamamoto
englishTitle: Early Autumn at Lake Haruna (Haruna-ko shoshū)
description: Oil painting by Japanese artist Kanae Yamamoto, a prominent modernist painter of the early twentieth century. The work is housed in the Municipal Museum Kanae Yamamoto in Ueda, Japan.

title: Toshogu Shrine
description: A colour woodblock print of the Tōshō-gū shrine at Nikkō, designed by Yoshida Hiroshi in 1937. Towering cryptomeria trunks frame the lantern-lined approach to the shrine, rendered with the soft gradations Yoshida carried from his watercolour training into woodblock. This impression belongs to the San Diego Museum of Art.
credit: San Diego Museum of Art

title: Yomei Gate
description: A color woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida of the Yomeimon, the lavishly carved and gilded gate of the Tosho-gu shrine at Nikko, with small figures on the steps below and towering cedars closing in behind. Yoshida renders the gate's dense ornament in a subdued harmony of golds and greys, capturing the gleam of gilding in deep forest shade. The print was made in 1937.

title: Kanae Yamamoto
englishTitle: Mount Fuji from Kami-Ide (Kami-Ide no Fuji)
description: An oil painting of Mount Fuji seen from Kami-Ide, a village at the foot of the mountain, painted by Yamamoto Kanae in 1938. The snow-streaked cone rises under drifting clouds beyond a foreground of plowed fields and autumn-red trees. Yamamoto, a pioneer of the sosaku-hanga creative print movement, devoted much of his later career to oil painting; the work is held by the Kanae Yamamoto museum in Ueda, Nagano.
credit: Municipal Museum Kanae Yamamoto, Ueda

title: Old Korea-Keith-BRIDE
description: A portrait of a Korean bride in traditional hanbok wedding attire. Published in "Old Korea: the Land of Morning Calm" by Elizabeth Keith and Elspet Keith Robertson Scott (Hutchinson & Co. , 1946).

title: Rythme n°1
description: Concentric arcs and rotating disc forms in bold primary and secondary colours fill this large canvas, painted in 1938 as a mural decoration for the Salon des Tuileries. The composition exemplifies Delaunay's mature Orphist language of simultaneous colour contrast, here brought to a monumental decorative scale. The work is held by the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris.
credit: Photograph by Coldcreation

title: Sketches of Famous Places in Japan: Asakusa Kinryūzan Temple
Bamboo Grove
credit: Flickr (www.flickr.com/photos/thesandiegomuseumofartcollection)

title: Kanae Yamamoto
description: Oil painting by Japanese artist Kanae Yamamoto (1882–1946). The work depicts the landscape near Iizuna in the Kōgen region. Held in the Municipal Museum Kanae Yamamoto, Ueda.

title: Parson Weems’ Fable
description: Painting depicting Parson Weems and his famous story of George Washington and the Cherry Tree.

provenance.collection: Amon Carter Museum of American Art
provenance.location: Amon Carter Museum of American Art

title: 'January' by Grant Wood
description: January is a painting by American artist Grant Wood, created between 1940 and 1941. The work is housed in the Cleveland Museum of Art and represents Wood's characteristic style blending regionalism with modernist elements.

title: Evening at Tagonoura
description: A shin-hanga woodblock print by Kawase Hasui from 1940. Mount Fuji rises with rose-colored evening light on its snows, framed between the dark trunks and boughs of pines, while a farmer leads a loaded horse cart across the fields of Tagonoura below, a stretch of coast whose views of Fuji have been celebrated since classical poetry. An impression is held by the Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art.
credit: Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art https://jmapps.ne.jp/apmoa/det.html?data_id=18666

provenance.collection: New Britain Museum of American Art
provenance.location: New Britain Museum of American Art

title: Indefinite Divisibility
credit: Buffalo AKG Art Museum digital assets collection

title: Nighthawks
description: Edward Hopper's oil on canvas of 1942 shows a late-night diner on a deserted New York street corner, its three customers and white-jacketed counterman sealed behind curving plate glass under harsh electric light. The painting's air of urban solitude has made it the most famous image of Hopper's career and one of the most widely recognized works of American art. The Art Institute of Chicago bought it from the artist within months of its completion in 1942, and it remains there in the Friends of American Art Collection.

title: Portrait of a Man
description: A full-length standing portrait of an unidentified bewigged man in a grey coat, one hand resting on a cane and the other holding a tricorn hat, set against a plain dark ground with a glimpse of drapery at left. The work is attributed to the Venetian late-Baroque portraitist Bartolomeo Nazari and entered the Fogg Museum at Harvard under accession number 1943.116.
credit: Harvard Art Museums

title: MC Escher Three Spheres I
description: A wood-engraving by M. C. Escher depicting three spheres in spatial arrangement, created in 1945.

title: Dutch girl in landscape
description: A color woodcut by Yamamoto Kanae of a girl in Dutch folk dress standing on a sandy path before a flat river landscape of fields, trees and a distant cottage, the scene built from broad, simplified planes of green and ochre. Yamamoto, the founding figure of Japan's sosaku-hanga movement of self-carved, self-printed artist's prints, took up European subjects of this kind in connection with his years of study in Europe from 1912 to 1916. The print is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Carnival in Paris in Honour of the Russian Navy
description: A large crowd fills a Paris square at dusk, with French and Russian tricolour flags, flares, and the silhouette of a monumental statue against a fiery sunset sky. Léon Bakst painted this record of the festivities held in 1893 to celebrate the French Republic's reception of the Russian Imperial Navy, the diplomatic occasion that sealed the Franco-Russian Alliance.

title: Tabi miyage dai nishū
description: A full moon rises over a calm bay at Ogi on Sado Island, casting its reflection on the dark water while a lone figure crouches at the base of a large rock formation in the foreground. A woodblock print from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II series, the composition contrasts the luminous moon and its reflection against the dark mass of rock and densely wooded islets beyond.

title: The Disquieting Muses
description: A modernist oil painting by Giorgio de Chirico from 1950, depicting mysterious classical female figures in an enigmatic architectural setting exemplifying his metaphysical style.

title: Heirin-ji
description: A late woodblock print by Kawase Hasui, published in 1952, of Heirin-ji, a Rinzai Zen temple at Nobidome in Saitama prefecture. The temple's dark timber gate stands in deep shadow while sunlight breaks through the foliage in bright patches across the flagstone path, autumn maples burning orange in the middle distance. An impression is held by the Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art.
credit: Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art https://jmapps.ne.jp/apmoa/det.html?data_id=18693

title: Morning Sun
credit: Photo taken by self on Sunday 10/08/23 during a visit to the Museum. The photo here was the result of seven 108 megapixels photos using Samsung Galaxy Ultra S22, then stacked, aligned, blended and combined in Adobe Photoshop with minor adjustments including lens distortion, cropping, color and contrast correction.

title: Nihon fūkei senshū
englishTitle: Main Hall at Heian-jingū Shrine, Kyoto
description: Three women in kimono stand before the sweeping vermilion halls of the Daigokuden at Heian-jingū Shrine in Kyoto, with spring-green trees framing the lacquered architecture against a pale sky. From Kawase Hasui's Selected Views of Japan (Nihon fūkei senshū), the print pairs the shrine's grand Tang-inspired architecture with figures that lend human scale to the composition.

title: Snow over Zojoji Temple
description: Kawase Hasui's woodblock print of 1953 shows the great red gate of Zojo-ji temple in the Shiba district of Tokyo under heavily falling snow, kimono-clad figures sheltering beneath umbrellas at its base against a darkened sky. The print was commissioned by the Japanese cultural authorities to document the craft of polychrome woodblock printing, subsequently designated an intangible cultural property. It was published by Watanabe Shozaburo in the large oban format, carved by Sato Jurokichi and printed by Ono Gintaro.

title: MC Escher Convex and Concave
description: A lithograph by M. C. Escher exploring visual perception through interlocking geometric forms.

title: Kawase Hasui-No Series-Konjikido in Snow Hiraizumi
description: Kawase Hasui's final print design, published in 1957, the year of his death. Snow-covered stone steps climb between snow-laden cedars toward the hall sheltering the Konjikido, the famed Golden Hall of Chuson-ji temple at Hiraizumi, while a lone figure ascends under an umbrella through the falling snow. The design is traditionally honored as the artist's zeppitsu, or last work.

title: View of the Brenta
description: A late-eighteenth-century view of a canal on the Brenta waterway, with a prominent palazzo at the centre flanked by a church dome, elegantly dressed figures promenading, a horse-drawn cart, and sheep in the foreground. Attributed to Giovanni Battista Cimaroli, the canvas entered the Robert Lehman Collection at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1975 (inv. 1975.1.91).

title: The Descent from the Cross
description: The body of Christ is lowered from the cross by several figures while the Virgin, clad in blue, has collapsed at the foot of the cross among the holy women. Painted by Charles Le Brun in the late 1640s during his first years back in Paris after studying with Poussin in Rome, the canvas was acquired by the Los Angeles County Museum of Art in 2004 with funds provided by the Joseph B. Gould Foundation, and Cary Grant and Fred Maxwell by exchange (M.2004.239).
credit: Image: http://collections.lacma.org/sites/default/files/remote_images/piction/ma-31731258-O3.jpg Gallery: http://collections.lacma.org/node/210510 archive copy at the Wayback Machine

provenance.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
provenance.location: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

title: Woman Showing Her Portrait
description: A woman presents an oval portrait of herself to a small company while a gentleman peers at her through a magnifying glass. She appears twice, as both the living sitter and her painted likeness. Painted about 1790, oil on canvas, roughly 46 by 56 cm, in the Dallas Museum of Art.
credit: Dallas Museum of Art

title: "Weeping" from Le Brun
englishTitle: Weeping, from Le Brun's Conférence sur l'expression
description: An engraved head with furrowed brows, clenched eyes, and a downward-drawn mouth illustrates the passion of weeping, captioned 'WEEPING' below the image. The print reproduces Charles Le Brun's analysis of facial expression, derived from his influential lecture on the passions delivered at the French Royal Academy in 1668. This impression is held in the Wellcome Collection, where it forms part of an extensive archive relating to physiognomy and the study of human expression.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/41/4b/e4c8e2b3bc4c7e196e5b4782513a.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0012153.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-21): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/z6ry4986 CC-BY-4.0

title: (Venice) Aristotele by Francesco Hayez in gallerie Accademia Venice
description: A full-length depiction of Aristotle seated in classical robes, stylus in hand, his gaze turned upward with intensity; sculpted lions on a pediment and garden foliage fill the background. Painted by Francesco Hayez and held in the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice, the work exemplifies his ability to fuse careful academic draughtsmanship with the expressive ambitions of Italian Romanticism.

title: 1993-151-1-pma2018
description: A Monet of 1888, catalogued as Wildenstein 1191 and now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art. By this date the artist was working in extended series, breaking form into mosaics of high-keyed colour to record a single motif under shifting light.
credit: Philadelphia Museum of Art

title: 500px-Kuniyoshi Utagawa
description: A hawk poised in profile, its plumage detailed in the layered keyblock and colour blocks of an ukiyo-e print. Hawks were a favoured subject of late Edo print designers, the bird's predatory stillness suiting the medium's graphic economy.

title: A Coast Scene with Fishermen Hauling a Boat Ashore
description: Fishermen drag a boat up onto a windswept beach beneath a heavy, scudding sky. Part of the Iveagh Bequest at Kenwood, the picture sits in Turner's lifelong dialogue with seventeenth-century Dutch marine painters such as van de Velde and Cuyp. Salt spray, wet sand and weather become as much the subject as the labour.
credit: ArtDaily.com

title: Agnes Dürer
description: A rapid pen sketch of Agnes Dürer, the artist's wife, shown in profile with head bowed, wearing the voluminous sleeved dress and headdress typical of Nuremberg burgher fashion. An inscription at the lower edge reads 'mein Agnes' with Dürer's monogram. The sheet is preserved at the Albertina, Vienna.
credit: https://sammlungenonline.albertina.at/?query=search=/record/objectnumbersearch= []&showtype=record

title: Alain Chartier
englishTitle: Alain Chartier (Margaret of Scotland Kissing the Sleeping Poet)
description: Edmund Blair Leighton's 1903 painting depicts the moment Margaret of Scotland is said to have kissed the lips of the sleeping French poet Alain Chartier in tribute to his eloquence, surrounded by attendant ladies on a garden stair. The subject suits Leighton's characteristic medievalising genre, here enriched with elaborately rendered gold brocade and lace costumes within a Gothic architectural setting.
credit: Art Renewal Center

title: Albinus
description: An engraving from Tabulae sceleti et musculorum corporis humani (Tables of the Skeleton and Muscles of the Human Body, 1747), the anatomical atlas of the Leiden anatomist Bernhard Siegfried Albinus, with plates drawn and engraved by Jan Wandelaar. The second table presents a full-length male ecorche displaying the superficial layer of muscles, posed with one arm extended before a parkland backdrop where a big cat watches from behind a masonry wall; Wandelaar's pictorial settings were meant to lend the figures depth and life. This impression is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/f0/71/bc9f44456b3b72471345971c37c1.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0023549.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-23): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/nufbvr6n CC-BY-4.0

title: Allee de chataigniers - Alfred Sisley
description: An avenue of chestnut trees in the woods at La Celle-Saint-Cloud, the path running back between heavy trunks toward a clearing. Among Sisley's earliest plein-air canvases, painted in the mid-1860s alongside Bazille in the same woods. Oil on canvas, in his pre-Impressionist Barbizon-inflected manner.

title: Along the River During the Qingming Festival 清明上河圖
englishTitle: Along the River During the Qingming Festival
description: A Qing court reinterpretation of the celebrated Song handscroll documenting Qingming festivities along the Bian River. Shen Yuan, an academician under the Qianlong emperor, executes the panorama in fine ink line touched with sparing ochre washes.
credit: Stitched and then resized from the original files located at: A Special Exhibition of Paintings on "Up the River During Qingming" in the Museum Collection (exhibit). Taipei: National Palace Museum.

title: Anatomy
englishTitle: Écorché figure, back view, with rhinoceros in the background (Grignion after Albinus, 1747)
description: The companion écorché figure seen from behind, engraved by Charles Grignion after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Albinus's anatomical atlas, again with the rhinoceros Clara in the background. Pairing the flayed figure with the exotic animal made these among the most recognisable anatomical prints of the eighteenth century. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/c0/df/23f659282c9c19b8502d33eff68a.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0021856.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-23): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/e4nzst8g CC-BY-4.0

title: Anonymous - Brustbild eines jungen Mannes - 4641 - Österreichische Galerie Belvedere
description: A bust-length study of a young man, plainly dressed and turned slightly toward the viewer, kept in the Belvedere as part of the German Romantic holdings. Runge favoured this kind of clear, almost severe portrait pared back to face and gaze.

title: Battle Scene
description: Two dense formations of pike-armed infantry engage head-on in this sixteenth-century work after a design by Hans Holbein the Younger, the long shafts of the weapons forming a lattice across the picture plane. The composition descends from Holbein's Basel-period battle drawings and was likely made to serve as a model for decorative or print commissions. The work is dated to the sixteenth century.
credit: Christian Müller; Stephan Kemperdick; Maryan Ainsworth; et al , Hans Holbein the Younger: The Basel Years, 1515–1532, Munich: Prestel, 2006, ISBN 9783791335803 .

title: Bellini — Pietà Martinengo
description: The dead Christ lies in the arms of the grieving Virgin in a sunlit landscape, the two figures alone in a composition of extraordinary stillness and tenderness. Towns and a river wind through the hilly background. Known as the Pietà Martinengo, the work is attributed to Giovanni Bellini and is among the most celebrated of his devotional panels.

title: Blaas Eugen Von An Interesting Story
description: A young Venetian woman pauses over the white linen piled in her lap, laughing and gesturing mid-conversation toward someone beyond the edge of the picture — the interesting story of the title. Her red kerchief, coral necklace, and yellow skirt supply the bright local color that made de Blaas's scenes of Venetian working girls hugely popular with collectors. The oil painting is a characteristic example of the genre subjects he produced in Venice through the late nineteenth century.

title: Carp leaping up a cascade
description: A koi battles upstream against a thundering waterfall, illustrating the Chinese legend that any carp scaling the falls of the Dragon Gate is transformed into a dragon. The motif, emblematic of perseverance and male coming-of-age, was a staple of East Asian ink painting and ukiyo-e print design.

title: Cattle Watering by a Stream
description: A pastoral scene of cattle pausing at a wooded stream, painted with the feathery, scumbled foliage typical of Gainsborough's mature landscapes. The work belongs to his Suffolk-derived rural idylls, indebted to Dutch seventeenth-century models yet handled with English freshness.

title: Cawing crow by Ohara Koson
description: A black crow perches on a snow-covered branch, beak open mid-call, while snow-laden willow fronds hang around it against a pale grey ground. Koson specialised in kachō-e (bird-and-flower) prints for the early-twentieth-century shin-hanga revival, producing naturalistic studies such as this one for Western collectors.

title: Charles le Brun
description: Studies of emotive heads, including wonder, despair and joy, from the series Le Brun developed to illustrate his 1668 lecture at the Académie Royale de Peinture et de Sculpture. Published posthumously as Méthode pour apprendre à dessiner les passions, the drawings codified facial expression for two centuries of academic teaching, with the eyebrows treated as the primary diagnostic feature.
credit: Charles le Brun, The Expressions, from the Trait é des Passions

title: Chaumiére Italienne
description: This etching by Jean-Honoré Fragonard depicts a dilapidated Italian rural cottage sheltered by trees, with small figures visible nearby. The composition is characteristic of Fragonard's landscape prints made from sketches gathered during his Italian travels, and an impression is held at Ghent University Library.
credit: Ghent University Library

title: Christ Bearing His Cross
description: An engraving of the procession to Calvary thronged with mounted soldiers, jeering onlookers and dogs winding across a vast horizon. Schongauer, the leading German printmaker before Dürer, brought a refined, silvery line and unprecedented compositional ambition to copperplate engraving.
