provenance.collection: Museum of Fine Arts of Nancy
provenance.location: Museum of Fine Arts of Nancy

title: Colourfull dance
description: Three nude female figures dance against a dark ground, their bodies rendered in flat planes of blue, yellow, and red separated by bold contour lines. Kirchner's Farbentanz (Colour Dance) belongs to his late period, when he reduced the figure to simplified, interlocking colour fields. Sunflowers at the base and circular forms above frame the composition in a decorative vertical format.

title: Crucifixion - Andrea Mantegna - Louvre INV 368
englishTitle: The Crucifixion (predella of the San Zeno Altarpiece)
description: The central panel of Mantegna's San Zeno altarpiece predella, showing Christ crucified between the thieves on a rocky knoll. Mantegna deploys archaeological architectural detail and sharp foreshortening, treating the figures with the chiselled severity of Roman relief sculpture.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Danceringreen
description: A ballet dancer in a green tutu tilts and sways mid-performance, her arms lifted and her figure caught from a steep overhead angle characteristic of Degas. Pastel hatching layers powdery greens and warm orange accents, with additional dancers visible in the background, in a composition from Degas's long series devoted to the Paris Opéra.

title: Danse Macabre. II. The Temptation
description: The Temptation, the second plate of Holbein's Dance of Death, depicts the serpent in Eden as the origin of mortality. Holbein opens the cycle with the Fall before Death claims figures across society in succeeding plates.

title: Die-kreuzabnahme-rubens
englishTitle: The Descent from the Cross (after Rubens)
description: A Descent from the Cross after Rubens, transposing the master's Antwerp altarpiece composition into reproductive form. The diagonal sweep of Christ's pallid body lowered onto a white winding-sheet preserves the Baroque dramaturgy of the original.

title: Don Quijote illustrated by Gustav Dore V
description: A turbaned figure seated in an ornate stone archway reads or writes, surrounded by scattered books and papers, with the domes and minarets of an Eastern city visible beyond. Signed by Gustave Doré, this wood-engraved plate depicts an Oriental subject and does not belong to the Don Quixote cycle despite the catalogue title.
credit: Gustave Dore

title: E1924-3-16-pma2018
description: A meander of the Epte near Giverny, the small river that fed Monet's water-garden. The canvas is built from short, broken touches that knit foliage, bank and reflection into a single shimmering surface, characteristic of his late 1880s plein-air practice.
credit: Philadelphia museum of art

title: El jardín de las Delicias
description: Bosch's triptych unfolds from the Garden of Eden through a teeming central panel of nude pleasure-seekers to a hellscape of musical instruments turned instruments of torture. Painted for a Habsburg patron, its inventory of fantastical hybrids has resisted definitive iconographic decoding for five centuries.

title: Ernst-ludwig-kirchner-sertig-valley-in-autumn
description: The Sertig valley unfolds in autumn brilliance, its forested slopes ablaze in ochre and orange beneath jagged peaks rendered in Kirchner's angular Expressionist palette. A foreground railing anchors the panoramic view down to a cluster of valley buildings. The canvas belongs to the alpine body of work Kirchner produced near Davos after his wartime breakdown, where mountain geometry tempered the urban intensity of his Brücke years.

title: Expulsion of Adam and Eve
description: The Expulsion of Adam and Eve, the third plate in Holbein's Dance of Death cycle, follows the Temptation as the source of human mortality. The angel drives the pair into a thorny world while Death takes up his fiddle to lead them onward.

title: Five Egrets Descending in Snow by Shôson
description: Five egrets glide through falling snow toward a quiet shoreline, their white forms dissolving against the pale ground. Koson, the leading kachoga (bird-and-flower) printmaker of the shin-hanga era, captures the species' winter behaviour with delicately graded woodblock impressions.

title: Fourth muscle man
description: A woodcut from Andreas Vesalius's De humani corporis fabrica, the fourth in the famous sequence of muscle men that strip away the body's musculature layer by layer; here dissected muscles hang loose from the figure's arms as he stands in a landscape of hills and buildings that continues from plate to plate across the series. The blocks, cut for the book's first edition of 1543 and attributed to artists in Titian's circle, transformed anatomical illustration. This impression comes from the 1555 second edition and is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/4e/d6/302698ee4bbfbd55b5b93997e7b1.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0001647.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-03-29): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/jq3wthjj CC-BY-4.0

title: Fritillaria imperialis in Les liliacees
description: A crown imperial (Fritillaria imperialis) with its ring of pendent orange bells beneath a tuft of upright leaves, drawn life-size against a plain ground. Plate from Redouté's Les Liliacées, the eight-volume folio issued in Paris between 1802 and 1816. The image is a colour stipple engraving after Redouté's watercolour on vellum, finished by hand.
credit: Les Liliacées (1802–1816).

title: FWN 1974
description: A landscape study in pencil and watercolour, the forms of trees and rock laid in with translucent patches of blue and ochre over open paper. Catalogued as FWN 1974 in the online Cézanne catalogue raisonné among the works on paper. Cézanne built such sheets from overlapping washes, leaving the white of the paper to carry the light.

title: G. Caillebotte - Intérieur
description: An interior scene by Gustave Caillebotte depicting a woman at a window. The painting exemplifies Caillebotte's characteristic interest in domestic interiors and unusual compositional angles.

title: Gaertner6
description: A rooftop panorama of Berlin taken from the Friedrichswerdersche Kirche, showing monumental civic buildings — including a large domed rotunda and the broad forecourt of the Royal Palace — stretching to the horizon under a warm, hazy sky. Figures including an artist with a drawing board stand at the church parapet in the right foreground. The panel belongs to Eduard Gaertner's six-part panorama of Berlin executed in 1834.

title: Garden of Eden
description: A Flemish Baroque collaboration in which Jan Wildens supplied the wooded paradise landscape and Paul de Vos populated it with the assembled animals of creation. Such division of labor was standard practice in Antwerp's specialist workshops, here producing a dense menagerie set within a luminous park-like clearing.

title: Gentile and Giovanni Bellini — Saint Mark Preaching in Alexandria
description: Saint Mark addresses a crowd of turbaned Mamluks and Venetian onlookers in a sun-bleached square dominated by a domed basilica conflating San Marco with Alexandrian architecture. Begun by Gentile Bellini around 1504 and completed by his brother Giovanni after 1507, the canvas was painted for the Scuola Grande di San Marco and now hangs in the Pinacoteca di Brera.

title: Gherardo delle Notti-Supper with a Lute Player
englishTitle: Supper Party with a Lute Player
description: A large company gathers around a candlelit table — a lutenist plays at centre while the other revellers drink, laugh, and converse in the warm glow of a hidden candle. Gerrit van Honthorst, known in Italy as Gherardo delle Notti for scenes like this one, deploys Caravaggesque nocturnal lighting to animate an expansive genre subject. The work's current location is unrecorded in the catalogue sources.

title: Giovanni Bellini — Holy Allegory
description: A tiled marble terrace beside a lake gathers the Virgin enthroned, saints, and the infant Christ playing with cherubs beneath an apple tree, while pilgrims and a centaur wander a rocky shore. Long known as the Sacred Allegory, the small panel of around 1490 is one of Bellini's most enigmatic compositions and entered the Uffizi from the Habsburg collection in 1793.

title: God Speed
description: Edmund Blair Leighton's farewell scene shows a red-haired woman in cream and gold dress leaning from a castle parapet to fasten a red token to the armour of a departing knight below. The composition is typical of his medievalising Academicism, combining careful costume detail with warm, clear lighting and a narrative of chivalric devotion.
credit: Sotheby's Sale catalogue

title: Group with Parasols
description: Four figures recline on a grassy slope beneath parasols, their forms half-dissolved in dappled shade. Sargent treats the bourgeois leisure scene with rapid, broken brushwork, prizing the play of filtered light over portrait specificity.

title: Gynaeceum or ancient Greek Interior
description: A scene in the women's quarters of a Greek house, with nudes lounging amid braziers, drapery and patterned tile. The picture is one of Gérôme's Néo-Grec confections, dressing up an academic studio nude in archaeological props derived from Pompeian wall painting.

title: Henri Rousseau — The Hungry Lion Throws Itself on the Antelope
description: In a dense jungle at sunset, a lion sinks its teeth into the neck of a collapsing antelope while other creatures — an owl among the branches, a dark feline half-hidden in the foliage — look on. Rousseau exhibited the huge canvas at the 1905 Salon d'Automne with a long narrative caption, in the same room as Matisse and his circle, whose paintings prompted the label 'fauves.' It is now in the Fondation Beyeler near Basel.

title: Hieronymous Bosch Tondals Visions
description: A visionary narrative painting depicting Tondal's Vision, a medieval tale of spiritual otherworldly journey. This work is attributed to a follower of the Flemish master Hieronymus Bosch and exemplifies the Northern Renaissance fascination with intricate allegorical and fantastical imagery. The painting is housed in the Museo Lázaro Galdiano in Madrid.

title: Hiroshige
description: Several travelers hunch forward against a sudden downpour on an open road or hillside, their yellow rain-capes bent nearly horizontal as they press on through the squall. Hiroshige renders the storm with sweeping diagonal lines that emphasize the force of the weather against the small, determined figures. The woodblock print belongs to his Tōkaidō series and exemplifies his skill at capturing the hardships and drama of travel.

title: Hiroshige A shrine among trees on a moor
englishTitle: A Shrine Among Trees on a Moor
description: A wooded shrine complex stands on a low promontory or islet amid a flat coastal marsh, its grove of dark pines reflected in the surrounding water. Sailing boats move across the broad inlet beyond, and a flock of birds crosses the pale sky. Utagawa Hiroshige depicts the site with the same reverent quietude he brought to rural sacred places throughout his landscape work.

title: Holbein — Dead Christ
description: Christ's corpse lies life-size in a cramped tomb niche, emaciated, eyes and mouth still open, the wounds beginning to discolour — death observed without any visible promise of resurrection. Hans Holbein the Younger painted the panel in Basel in 1521-22, possibly as the predella of an altarpiece. Now in the Kunstmuseum Basel, it famously shook Dostoevsky, who has a character in The Idiot say a man could lose his faith looking at it.

title: Holbein d. J.; Danse Macabre
description: From the Dance of Death cycle, Holbein stages Death as an active intruder rather than an emblem, lunging into a tableau of contemporary life. The series helped fix the iconography of the danse macabre for the print era.

title: Holbein d. J.; Danse Macabre. XIV. The Abbot
description: The Abbot, plate XIV of Holbein's Dance of Death, shows a skeletal Death seizing a mitred prelate who clutches his crozier, dragging him away from an outdoor setting. The compact woodblock was designed by Hans Holbein the Younger and cut by Hans Lützelburger, combining sharp characterisation with a Reformation-era critique of ecclesiastical power. The series was first published in Lyon in 1538.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 10
description: A plate from Holbein's Dance of Death cycle, in which Death intrudes upon a figure of contemporary estate, abbot, merchant, peasant or king. The miniature woodcuts, executed with Hans Lützelburger's exacting cutting, were an early printed vehicle for Reformation-era social critique.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 11
description: A woodcut from Holbein's celebrated Dance of Death cycle, designed in Basel and cut by Hans Lützelburger. Each compact scene stages Death intruding upon a figure of medieval estate, satirising clerical and worldly vanity with razor-sharp draughtsmanship.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 12
description: Part of the Dance of Death series first issued in Lyon in 1538, where Death visits every rung of the social ladder. The miniature woodblock concentrates dense narrative into a few square inches, a hallmark of Holbein's reformist printmaking.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 13
description: Holbein's pocket-sized memento mori reduces a moral sermon to a single arrested gesture: the skeleton's grasp, the victim's surprise. Cut by Lützelburger from Holbein's drawings, the prints circulated widely in Reformation Europe.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 15
description: Another scene from the Dance of Death series, in which Death claims a representative of the medieval social order. Holbein's tightly composed woodcuts pair grim humour with precise observation of costume and gesture.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 16
description: From the Dance of Death cycle published at Lyon, this plate confronts a worldly figure with the universal leveller. Holbein's drawing translates fluently into Lützelburger's miniature woodblock technique, reading clearly at thumbnail scale.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 17
description: A plate from Holbein's Imagines Mortis, conceived in Basel in the late 1520s. Death's skeletal cameo within an ordered domestic or civic scene gave the series its lasting force as moral and social commentary.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 19
description: The Advocate, plate XIX of the Dance of Death, finds the lawyer pocketing a coin while Death stands ready at his side. Holbein's reformist satire jabs at venal professions, the woodcut's miniature scale concentrating its sting.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 20
description: A plate from Holbein's Dance of Death in which Death, wearing a leafy crown, insinuates himself between two standing men — one richly dressed — and asserts his claim. Cut by Hans Lützelburger from Holbein's designs, the series was published in Lyon in 1538 and became a landmark of Northern Renaissance printmaking.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 21
description: In this plate from the Dance of Death, a priest preaches from a pulpit to a kneeling and seated congregation while Death observes from a lectern above. Holbein inserts the skeleton into the very act of spiritual instruction, undercutting clerical authority with quiet irony characteristic of the series.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 22
description: Another plate in the Dance of Death sequence, joining its survey of estates from pope to peasant. Holbein's compositions remain models of pictorial economy, every line bearing narrative weight.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 23
description: From the Dance of Death, Holbein again pairs the living with the cavorting skeleton, their gestures locked in a brief, fatal duet. The Lyon edition of 1538 became a model for memento mori imagery for centuries.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 24
description: A scene from Holbein's Dance of Death cycle, in which Death steps into the everyday with grim levity. The series remains a high point of Northern Renaissance printmaking, sharpened by Reformation-era anticlerical wit.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 25
description: Plate from the Imagines Mortis cycle, where Holbein's Death overturns hierarchies one estate at a time. The miniature woodcut format encouraged private meditation on mortality alongside its public satire.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 26
description: Another tableau from the Dance of Death sequence, illustrating Death's universal claim. Holbein's draughtsmanship and Lützelburger's exacting cutting give the prints their crisp, almost engraving-like precision.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 27
description: An astronomer sits at a table crowded with books and an armillary sphere while Death leans over his shoulder, interrupting scholarly inquiry with the same finality it brings to every estate. The image belongs to Hans Holbein the Younger's Dance of Death series, published in Lyon in 1538, in which no profession can purchase an exemption.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 28
description: A Dance of Death plate carrying forward the cycle's procession through every rank of society. The format - small block, pithy scene, accompanying scriptural verse in the original edition - became the template for emblem books to come.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 29
description: Holbein places Death amid the routines of trade or labour, reminding the viewer that no occupation provides exemption. The Imagines Mortis remained in print across multiple Lyon editions through the sixteenth century.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 30
description: Another scene from the Dance of Death, marrying biting moral commentary to compact woodcut design. Holbein's cycle gave Reformation Europe its definitive picture of mortality stalking every estate.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 32
description: From the Dance of Death series, Holbein renders Death as both companion and antagonist, mirroring the gestures of the living. The plates retain a draughtsman's vivacity despite the resistance of the woodblock.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 33
description: A Dance of Death plate from Holbein's celebrated cycle, the figures locked in a brief contest of will and fate. Lützelburger's cutting captures every flicker of Holbein's pen-line at miniature scale.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 34
description: Part of Holbein's Imagines Mortis, the small woodcut sets a skeleton against a figure of social rank, a formula the artist varies with inexhaustible invention across the series.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 35
description: From the Dance of Death, Holbein uses the miniature woodcut as a stage for a quick, devastating morality play. The cycle pairs each image with a biblical citation underscoring its lesson.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 36
description: From Holbein's Dance of Death, this plate depicts Death intruding on a sickbed in a well-appointed chamber, where skeletons attend a figure laid low in a carved four-poster bed. No rank or wealth can delay the summons. The woodcut belongs to Hans Holbein the Younger's celebrated cycle, designed in Basel and first published at Lyon in 1538.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 37
description: A scene from the Dance of Death cycle, in which Holbein's skeleton mimics or mocks the trade of his victim. The miniature woodcut carries an outsized influence on later memento mori imagery across European print culture.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 38
description: From the Imagines Mortis series, this plate continues Holbein's procession through the social order. Designed in Basel and printed in Lyon, the cycle balances religious gravity with sharp-edged worldly humour.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 39
description: From Holbein's Dance of Death, this plate depicts a domestic interior where women tend a fire or cauldron while a skeleton approaches from the side. The scene belongs to Holbein's cycle of small woodcuts designed in Basel and first published at Lyon in 1538, in which Death intrudes on the routines of daily life regardless of station.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 4
description: A woodcut from Hans Holbein the Younger's celebrated Dance of Death cycle, designed in the 1520s and first published at Lyon in 1538. Skeletons drag the living from every social rank, the moral message compressed into miniature scenes carved with extraordinary economy of line.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 40
description: This plate from Holbein's Dance of Death cycle depicts a divine or eschatological scene: a enthroned figure presides above a celestial sphere while crowds of naked souls gather below, evoking the Last Judgement that frames the series. The woodcut was designed by Hans Holbein the Younger and cut by Hans Lützelburger in Basel; the series was first published at Lyon by the Trechsel brothers in 1538.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 41
description: From Holbein's Dance of Death, an unsparing memento mori in miniature woodcut. Death intrudes on daily life with theatrical bluntness, the densely worked black lines reflecting the early sixteenth-century northern fascination with mortality and judgement.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 42
description: A page from Holbein's Dance of Death, designed in Basel and printed at Lyon in 1538. The series subjected pope, emperor, merchant, and ploughman alike to Death's hand, channelling Reformation-era anxiety through tightly composed woodcut tableaux.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 43
description: From Holbein's Dance of Death cycle, in which a capering skeleton interrupts the routines of medieval life. The print's terse narrative and crisp black-line carving exemplify the small-format moralising woodcut perfected in early sixteenth-century Basel.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 44
description: Plate from Holbein's Dance of Death, a sequence of moral vignettes first issued at Lyon in 1538. Each scene confronts a different rank of society with mortality, the figures animated by Holbein's economical draftsmanship and the precision of Hans Lützelburger's cutting.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 45
description: An image from Holbein's Dance of Death, the German painter's most widely circulated print cycle. Death is staged as both intruder and equaliser, a theme rooted in late medieval European tradition but rendered with Renaissance compositional clarity.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 46
description: From Holbein's Dance of Death, a series of forty-one woodcuts in which Death appears as skeletal companion to every walk of life. The prints became a touchstone of Reformation-era moral imagery and shaped the iconography of mortality for centuries.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 47
description: Plate from Holbein's Dance of Death, designed around 1526 and printed in Lyon a decade later. Crammed into a tight rectangular field, the scene typifies the cycle's blend of social satire and pious warning.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 48
description: From Holbein's Dance of Death, where Death stalks every estate of society with grim impartiality. The miniature woodcut format favoured by Holbein concentrates psychological force into a few square inches of black line.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 49
description: A late plate in Holbein's Dance of Death cycle, a programme of small woodcuts whose dark humour and moral urgency defined the German Renaissance memento mori. The figures are sharply observed, the architectural settings reduced to telling props.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 5
description: Plate from Holbein's Dance of Death, the influential moralising sequence designed in Basel in the 1520s. Death descends without warning on princes and labourers alike, a theme intensified by the woodcut's confined format and emphatic shadows.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 6
description: From Holbein's Dance of Death cycle, in which the skeletal figure of mortality breaks into an everyday scene with sardonic relish. The series helped fix the visual vocabulary of the danse macabre for European print culture.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 7
description: An image from Holbein's Dance of Death, a Reformation-era meditation on mortality issued in Lyon in 1538. Death's intrusion is staged with theatrical compression, every gesture pared to its essential meaning.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 8
description: Plate from Holbein the Younger's Dance of Death, where skeletons enact a mocking equality across every social rank. The cut is sharply contoured, drawing on the Basel woodcut tradition that Holbein elevated to a new pictorial intelligence.

title: Holbein Danse Macabre 9
description: From Holbein's Dance of Death sequence, designed about 1526 and widely reprinted across Europe. Death's grip is sudden and absolute; Holbein's command of small-scale figure groups gives each plate the punch of a self-contained drama.

title: Ingres - Mme Victor Baltard & sa fille Paule
description: Ingres portrays Mme Victor Baltard standing beside a stone balustrade, her young daughter Paule at her side. The inscription at lower left reads 'offert à son ami M. Ve Baltard / Ingres Del. Rom.', confirming the drawing was made in Rome. The face is rendered with Ingres's characteristic precision, while dress and background are lightly sketched in graphite.

title: Isenheim Altarpiece - Concert of Angels
englishTitle: Concert of Angels, from the Isenheim Altarpiece
description: A photographic record of the Concert of Angels panel from Matthias Grünewald's Isenheim Altarpiece (c. 1512–16), housed at the Musée Unterlinden in Colmar. The original shows angel musicians serenading the Virgin in jewel-coloured robes, part of the great folding altarpiece made for the monastery hospital of St Anthony.

title: Isenheim Altarpiece - Saints - Left
description: This panel from the Isenheim Altarpiece depicts the Temptation of Saint Anthony: the hermit saint is overwhelmed by a writhing mass of grotesque demons and hybrid creatures in a rocky landscape, with a fiery sky above. Matthias Grünewald completed the altarpiece around 1516 for the Antonite hospital at Isenheim; the scene's raw depiction of bodily torment was designed to speak directly to patients suffering from ergotism. The work is now housed at the Musée Unterlinden in Colmar.

title: Isenheim Altarpiece - Saints - Right
description: This panel from the Isenheim Altarpiece depicts the Meeting of Saints Paul the Hermit and Anthony Abbot in the desert: the two aged figures converse in a rocky wilderness landscape, with a palm tree and a lion visible to the right. Matthias Grünewald painted the scene as part of the altarpiece created around 1512–1516 for the Antonite monastery hospital at Isenheim; it is now at the Musée Unterlinden in Colmar.

title: Isenheim Altarpiece — SECOND OPENING
description: Three scenes unfold across the altarpiece's second opening, from the Annunciation through the Nativity with its angel concert to the Resurrection, where Christ rises in a halo of incandescent yellow and red. Grünewald completed the polyptych around 1516 for the Antonite monastery at Isenheim, structuring the wings so successive feast-day openings revealed different cycles of the redemption story.

title: Jacopo Tintoretto — Creation of the Animals
description: A photographic record of Tintoretto's Creation of the Animals (c. 1551–52) for the Scuola Grande della Trinità, now in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice. God the Father sweeps across the sky propelling birds, fish, and beasts into existence in a single rushing diagonal.

title: John Constable by Ramsay Richard Reinagle
description: The young John Constable, then twenty-three, faces the viewer in dark coat and stock, his curling hair brushed forward. Reinagle painted the portrait in 1799, the year both men entered the Royal Academy Schools, and it now hangs in the National Portrait Gallery in London.

title: John Liston Byam Shaw Boer War
description: A young woman in a dark dress stands lost in thought at the edge of an overgrown stream, the summer vegetation around her painted with Pre-Raphaelite exactness. The war of the title never appears: Byam Shaw shows only its cost at home, a woman mourning a loss in a conflict thousands of miles away, the indifferent lushness of the English countryside sharpening her grief. Painted in 1901 under the title The Boer War, the oil is in the collection of Birmingham Museums.

title: Kanō Eitoku - Rakuchū rakugai zu
englishTitle: Scenes in and around the Capital (Uesugi) - left screen
description: A panoramic bird's-eye survey of Kyoto in and around the capital, with thousands of tiny figures threading temples, markets and noble compounds amid gilded clouds. Eitoku codified the rakuchū rakugai zu format for the Momoyama elite; this pair was reportedly given by Oda Nobunaga to Uesugi Kenshin.
credit: ブレイズマン 05:15, 17 April 2008 (UTC)

title: Kisokaido14 Itahana
description: Snow-laden pine trees line the road at Itahana, the fourteenth station on the Kisokaidō, as travellers make their way through a deep winter landscape. The print belongs to the celebrated Sixty-Nine Stations of the Kisokaidō series; the artist recorded in the record is Keisai Eisen. A warm pink band at the horizon brightens the otherwise white and grey composition.
credit: The Sixty-Nine Stations of the Kisokaido

title: Kuniyoshi Utagawa
englishTitle: At the Shore of the Sumida River
description: A waterside Edo scene along the Sumida, the river that defined the city's ferry traffic, festivals and pleasure boating. Kuniyoshi, an Utagawa-school designer best known for warrior prints, here turns to a quieter genre subject in the bold linework typical of late ukiyo-e.

title: Kustodiev GoluboyDomik
description: A blue-roofed provincial house fills the canvas, its balcony occupied by figures taking tea at a samovar while a child releases kites from the rooftop and neighbours gather in the sunlit garden below. Boris Kustodiev returned obsessively to small Russian towns and merchant life, painting them in saturated colour — an idealised vision of provincial domesticity drawn from memory.

title: KustodievB Provinc
description: Townsfolk in mid-nineteenth-century dress stroll through a tree-lined provincial Russian square, with onion-domed church towers rising behind a bakery shopfront. The scene belongs to Kustodiev's cycle of idealised merchant-town views, capturing the rhythms of everyday provincial life.

title: La debacle - Monet w562
description: The breakup of ice on the Seine after a hard winter near Vétheuil, with floes drifting past bare riverbanks. Monet returned to this motif repeatedly in 1880, using broken brushwork to register the shifting interplay of water, ice and reflected sky.

title: Lady Hamilton as Nature
credit: Yale Center for British Art

title: Leonardo da Vinci - Virgin and Child with St Anne
description: Saint Anne supports the Virgin on her lap as Mary reaches for the Christ child, who plays with a lamb foreshadowing the Passion. Left unfinished at the artist's death and now in the Louvre, the panel is celebrated for its pyramidal grouping, soft sfumato modelling and atmospheric mountainous landscape.
credit: original file: C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition : image page

title: Les Papillons
description: A young woman reaches after butterflies in a small boudoir scene, the figure finished with the close, enamel-smooth handling Boilly favoured. The Lille-born painter built his reputation on such intimate genre pictures in Paris from the late 1780s. Oil on canvas.

title: Levitan VesnaVItalii
description: Blossoming trees in shades of pink line a winding road through a mountain valley, snow-capped peaks rising beyond forested slopes under a blue sky. Levitan painted Spring in Italy during his foreign travels, capturing a luminous southern landscape sharply different from the melancholy Russian scenes for which he is best known.

title: Lilium superbum
description: A Turk's cap lily (Lilium superbum) with downward-facing orange flowers spotted maroon, the petals sharply reflexed and curving back toward the stem. Plate from Redouté's Les Liliacées, published in Paris by Didot Jeune between 1802 and 1816. The print is a colour stipple engraving after Redouté, finished by hand.
credit: Les Liliacees. Paris: Didot Jeune, 1802-1816. [1]

title: Los nenúfares
description: A study of water lilies drifting on the surface of the Giverny pond, where reflected sky and submerged stems dissolve any fixed horizon. Monet returned to this motif obsessively in his final decades, building dense, broken touches of pigment into a shimmering field of colour.

title: Löwenjagd
description: Mounted hunters and lions tangle in violent diagonal motion, men and beasts pulled into a single churning mass. This small oil sketch, held by the Alte Pinakothek in Munich, is a preparatory modello for one of Rubens's larger hunt scenes, with the brushwork left openly visible.

provenance.location: Alte Pinakothek, upper floor, small gallery 12

title: Lucretia
description: Veronese's Lucretia presses the dagger to her breast in the Roman matron's act of self-destruction after her violation by Tarquin. The painter dresses the heroine in Venetian silks, fusing classical exemplum with sixteenth-century courtly elegance.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"v/veronese/10/4lucretia"

title: MB-Mon-16 Monet Les-Petites-Dalles-bei-Ebbe
description: A coastal study of Les Petites-Dalles on the Normandy shore at low tide, where Monet records the chalk cliffs and exposed shingle in feathered, broken brushstrokes. The painting belongs to the artist's recurring engagement with the Channel coast, tracking shifting light and atmosphere over a familiar stretch of beach.
credit: Self-photographed MuseumBarberini Taken on 19 April 2022

title: Memories
description: A half-length young woman in a black and gold dress turns to one side, her head resting against her hand. The model was Edith Pullen, sister of Leighton's regular model Dorothy Dene; the picture dates to 1883. Leighton kept his contours smooth and his palette restrained in the manner of his classicising portraiture.

title: Monet 1401
description: A view of the fjord at Christiania (now Oslo), painted on Monet's 1895 Norwegian campaign while visiting his stepson. Snow-bound water and shoreline are rendered in cool blues and pinks, his northern palette pushed toward near-monochrome refinement.

title: Monet w 106
description: Ice floes crowd a wintry river, its banks blanketed in snow and lined with bare trees whose reddish branches echo in the still water; a small steamer is silhouetted in the distance. The muted grey palette and close observation of ice and reflection are characteristic of Monet's winter river paintings. By Claude Monet.

title: Monet w 208
description: Painted in the early 1870s as Monet established the visual language of Impressionism, the picture trades finish for immediacy, applying paint in mosaic-like touches. Works of these years preceded and prepared the 1874 group exhibition that gave the movement its name.

title: Monet w 235
description: A broad river or estuary stretches across the lower half of the canvas, reflecting the overcast sky, while a low-lying town with a church spire extends along the far bank beneath a dramatic mass of cumulus cloud. The wide horizontal format and divided composition — water below, architecture and sky above — are characteristic of Monet's landscape work along the Seine. By Claude Monet.

title: Monet w 272 Apple Trees in Bloom
description: Apple trees in full blossom, their pinkish-white canopies set against fresh spring green and dabbed in short broken strokes. The subject was a favourite of the early Impressionists, who valued orchards as outdoor studios where colour and light could be studied together.

title: Monet w 338
description: Painted during the year of the first Impressionist exhibition, this work shows Monet's mature open-air method fully formed. Pigment is laid down in distinct touches that resolve into atmosphere only at viewing distance, refusing the smooth surface prized by the Salon.

title: Monet w 42
description: A full-length portrait of a man in a dark frock coat and pale trousers, hands tucked behind his back, set against a deep reddish-brown ground. The signed canvas — 'Claude Monet 64' — dates to 1864 and shows the controlled tonal handling of Monet's earliest training before his turn to open-air landscape.

title: Monet w1001
description: A country road near Giverny, the Norman village where Monet had settled in 1883, painted in 1885 (65 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1001; the work remains in a private collection.

title: Monet w1003
description: A view of the Seine valley at Port-Villez, the hamlet on the river bank opposite Giverny, painted in 1885 (65 x 92 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1003 and held in a private collection.

title: Monet w1016
description: The chalk cliff of the Falaise d'Aval at Etretat on the Normandy coast, silhouetted against a setting sun, painted during Monet's 1885 campaign there (81 x 100 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1016, it now hangs in the Pola Museum of Art in Hakone, Japan.

title: Monet w1035
description: The Manneporte, the largest of the three natural rock arches at Etretat, painted at high tide during Monet's 1885 stay on the Normandy coast (65 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1035; private collection.

title: Monet w1042
englishTitle: The Rock Needle and the Porte d'Aval Seen from the West
description: The Aiguille (rock needle) and the Porte d'Aval arch at Etretat seen from the west, painted in 1886 in an unusual vertical format (81 x 65 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1042, it belongs to the Kreeger Museum in Washington, D.C.

title: Monet w1050
englishTitle: The Rock Needle Seen through the Porte d'Aval
description: The needle rock at Etretat framed through the arch of the Porte d'Aval, painted in 1886 (73 x 92 cm). One of several canvases Monet devoted to this view; catalogued as Wildenstein 1050 and held in a private collection.

title: Monet w1054
description: A snow-covered landscape at Falaise, a hamlet near Giverny, painted in the hard winter of 1885-86 (66 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1054; private collection.

title: Monet w1056
description: A winter scene at Limetz, a village on the Epte just upstream from Giverny, painted during the snowy winter of 1885-86 (65 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1056 (Effet de neige a Limetz); Wikidata records it in the Hasso Plattner Collection at the Museum Barberini, Potsdam.

title: Monet w1065
description: Fruit trees in spring blossom near Giverny, painted in 1886 (65 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1065 and held in a private collection.

title: Monet w1075
description: A plein-air figure study from 1886 (102.5 x 75 cm) related to Monet's two large Woman with a Parasol canvases of that year, for which his stepdaughter Suzanne Hoschede posed on a riverbank near Giverny. Catalogued as Wildenstein 1075; private collection.

title: Monet W108
description: A portrait of the artist's infant son Jean Monet asleep, painted in 1868 (42 x 50 cm) during the family's straitened years on the Normandy coast. Catalogued as Wildenstein 108, it belongs to the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek in Copenhagen.

title: Monet w1089
description: Wave-battered rocks on the wild Atlantic coast of Belle-Ile-en-Mer, Brittany, painted during Monet's ten-week campaign there in autumn 1886 (65 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1089; private collection.

title: Monet w1120
description: A squall of rain sweeping the coast of Belle-Ile-en-Mer, painted in an unusual square format (60 x 60 cm) during Monet's stormy autumn 1886 stay in Brittany. Catalogued as Wildenstein 1120; Wikidata places it in the Musee des Beaux-Arts de Morlaix.

title: Monet w1121
description: Rain over the rocky coast of Belle-Ile-en-Mer in Brittany, painted in autumn 1886 (60 x 73 cm), a companion to the square-format version of the same subject. Catalogued as Wildenstein 1121; private collection.

title: Monet w1138
description: A field of irises near Monet's house at Giverny, painted in 1887 in a strongly horizontal format (45 x 100 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1138; a close variant, Field of Yellow Irises (W1137), is in the Musee Marmottan Monet. Private collection.

title: Monet w1155
description: Poplar trees in the meadows near Giverny, painted in 1887 (73 x 92 cm), several years before Monet's famous 1891 Poplars series on the Epte. Catalogued as Wildenstein 1155; Wikidata records it in the Hasso Plattner Collection at the Museum Barberini, Potsdam.

title: Monet w1179
description: A view across the Mediterranean from Antibes toward the snow-capped Alps, painted during Monet's early-1888 campaign on the Cote d'Azur (59 x 84 cm). Also known as The Mediterranean at Antibes; catalogued as Wildenstein 1179 and held in a private collection.

title: Monet w1296
englishTitle: Poplars on the Banks of the Epte at Dusk
description: One of Monet's 1891 Poplars series, showing the trees lining the River Epte near Giverny at dusk (100 x 65 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1296 (Peupliers au bord de l'Epte, crepuscule); Wikipedia places it in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Monet w1336
description: Ice floes drifting on the Seine near Bennecourt during the freeze of winter 1893 (65 x 100 cm), part of a small group of ice-breakup canvases that includes the Metropolitan Museum's Ice Floes (W1335). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1336; private collection.

title: Monet w1524
description: From the Charing Cross Bridge series painted on visits to London between 1899 and 1904. Monet worked from a balcony at the Savoy, watching trains cross the Thames as fog and smoke turned bridge and water into shimmering bars of mauve and gold.

title: Monet w1563
description: Waterloo Bridge over the Thames under an overcast sky, from Monet's London series painted from his window at the Savoy Hotel between 1899 and 1901 (65 x 100 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1563; private collection.

title: Monet w1636
description: A morning view of the village of Vetheuil across the Seine, painted in 1901 when Monet returned to motifs from his 1878-1881 residence there (89 x 92 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1636 (Vetheuil, effet du matin); private collection.

title: Monet w1668
englishTitle: The Bridge over the Water-Lily Pond
description: The Japanese footbridge arching over the water-lily pond in Monet's garden at Giverny, painted in 1905 (90 x 100 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1668; private collection.

title: Monet w1675
description: One of the Nymphéas canvases Monet painted in his water-lily pond at Giverny in 1905, catalogued as W.1675 in the Wildenstein catalogue raisonné. The square-format composition (89 x 92 cm) fills the frame with floating lily pads and reflections, dispensing with any horizon line. It is held in a private collection in the United States.

title: Monet w1695
description: A Nymphéas canvas from 1907, part of Monet's long series painted in the water garden at Giverny and catalogued as W.1695 in the Wildenstein catalogue raisonné. The painting belongs to the Mohamed Mahmoud Khalil Museum in Cairo.

title: Monet w199
description: A spring landscape painted at Argenteuil in 1872, shortly after Monet settled in the town on the Seine that became the heartland of early Impressionism. The painting (W.199) is in the Portland Museum of Art in Maine.

title: Monet w288 the sheltered path
description: A tree-lined country path painted in 1873, during Monet's productive years at Argenteuil. The painting (W.288) belongs to the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

title: Monet w579 springtime in vetheuil
description: A view of Vétheuil in spring, painted in 1880 while Monet was living in the small village on the Seine downstream from Paris. The painting (W.579) is in the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen in Rotterdam.

title: Monet w611
description: A landscape of willow trees painted in 1880 during Monet's years at Vétheuil. The painting (W.611) is in the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C.

title: Monet w646 jetty at fecamp in rough weather
englishTitle: Jetty at Fécamp in Bad Weather
description: A storm-tossed view of the jetty and lighthouse at Fécamp, painted during Monet's campaign on the Normandy coast in spring 1881. Waves break against the pier under heavy weather. The painting (W.646) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w648
englishTitle: The Sea Seen from the Cliffs of Fécamp
description: A view over the Channel from the clifftops at Fécamp, painted during Monet's 1881 stay on the Normandy coast. The painting (W.648) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w651 morning by the sea
description: A morning view of the cliffs of the Normandy coast near Fécamp, painted in 1881. The painting (W.651) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w678 lane in ile st martin
englishTitle: Lane in the Poppy Fields, Île Saint-Martin
description: A path through poppy fields on the Île Saint-Martin-la-Garenne, a river island in the Seine near Vétheuil, painted in 1880. The painting (W.678) belongs to the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

title: Monet w700 near vetheuil
description: A landscape painted in the countryside around Vétheuil in 1881, near the end of Monet's three years living in the village on the Seine. The painting (W.700) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w712 low tide at pourville
description: The beach and cliffs at Pourville near Dieppe at low tide, painted during Monet's 1882 campaign on the Normandy coast. The painting (W.712) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w812 vase of chrysantemums
description: A still life of chrysanthemums in a vase, painted in 1882 — one of the flower pieces Monet produced between his coastal landscape campaigns. The painting (W.812) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w816
englishTitle: Étretat, the Cliff of Aval at Sunset
description: The Porte d'Aval, the famous arched chalk cliff at Étretat, seen at sunset. Monet painted it during his stay at Étretat in early 1883. The painting (W.816) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w849
description: A tall still life of poppies in a porcelain vase, painted in 1883, the year Monet moved to Giverny. The painting (W.849) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w904
description: The chalk cliffs at Les Petites-Dalles on the Normandy coast in Seine-Maritime, painted in 1884. The painting (W.904) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w948
description: A still life of a potted white azalea, painted in 1885 at Giverny. The painting (W.948) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w961
description: A snow-covered winter landscape at Giverny, painted in 1885, two years after Monet settled in the village. The painting (W.961) is in the Pola Museum of Art in Hakone, Japan.

title: Monet w962
englishTitle: The Seine at Port-Villez, Snow Effect
description: A winter view of the Seine at Port-Villez, across the river from Giverny, painted under snow in 1885. The painting (W.962) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w982
englishTitle: Trees by the River, Springtime in Giverny
description: Riverside trees in spring at Giverny, painted in 1885. The painting (W.982) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w986
description: A spring landscape at Giverny in morning light, painted in 1885; Monet painted a companion afternoon version (W.987) of the same motif. The painting (W.986) is in a private collection.

title: Monet w996
description: A flowering meadow at Giverny, painted in 1885 during Monet's early years in the village. The painting (W.996) is in a private collection.

title: Myriad Miles of the Yangtze River
description: An eleven-metre handscroll on silk that travels the Yangtze from its mountain source to the sea, opening section by section in the hand of the viewer. Long attributed to the Southern Song master Xia Gui, it strings together mist, gorges, fishing villages and city walls in characteristic axe-cut brushwork.

title: Old Woman with a Basket of Coal
description: Three figures huddle in near-total darkness around a small pan of glowing coals: an old woman leans in from above while two children — one younger, one older — gaze intently at the light and warmth below. The chiaroscuro modelling of the upturned faces against the deep shadow is characteristic of the Northern nocturnal genre tradition. The painting, dated to the seventeenth century, is held at the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.

title: P.1948.SC .276-scaled-aspect-ratio-16-9-3-scaled
description: A landscape from Monet's mature Impressionist period, catalogued as Wildenstein 1192. The painter's broken touch and high-keyed palette translate atmosphere and shifting light into the building blocks of the picture.
credit: Courtauld Institute

title: Painting of Susanna and the Elders by Rubens
description: Susanna, surprised at her bath, twists away as two elders lean in over the garden wall — the apocryphal story from the Book of Daniel that let painters join a nude to a moral subject. Rubens painted this version in about 1606-07, during his years in Italy, and its compressed drama reflects his study of Italian models. Oil on canvas, Galleria Borghese, Rome.

title: Paolo Veronese 008
description: A reproduction documenting a painting by the Venetian master Paolo Veronese, photographed without its frame for archival study. Veronese's output spans grand religious cycles, mythologies, and ceiling allegories executed across sixteenth-century Venice.
credit: This image has an extracted file : Paolo Veronese 008 - selfportrait.jpg .

title: Paul Gustave Dore Andromeda
description: Gustave Dore's vision of Andromeda, the Ethiopian princess chained to a sea cliff awaiting Perseus's rescue. The composition exploits Dore's signature contrast of luminous flesh against turbulent rock and sky, a Romantic theatricality refined through years of book illustration. This file represents a digitally restored version of the image.
credit: www.artpassions.net

title: Pêches
description: Five peaches, two of them halved to expose the stone, lie on a bed of dark green leaves against a warm orange-brown ground. The feathery brushwork and close-keyed orange and pink tones are characteristic of Monet's small still lifes, and the picture is catalogued as Wildenstein 952.

title: Pinacoteca Querini Stampalia - Angelo Maria Querini - Bartolomeo Nazari
englishTitle: Portrait of Cardinal Angelo Maria Querini
description: Cardinal Angelo Maria Querini is shown seated in a gilded chair, dressed in black clerical robes with a cardinal's red garment beneath, one hand resting on an open book placed on a richly covered desk. Shelves of books behind him and the pendant cross at his collar identify him as a high-ranking ecclesiastic and bibliophile. The portrait by Bartolomeo Nazari is held at the Pinacoteca Querini Stampalia in Venice.

title: Portrait of a bearded man
description: An elderly man with a bald crown and a long white beard turns toward the viewer, dressed in a plain dark coat and holding a white handkerchief in his right hand, set against a warm brown ground. The portrait is attributed to Domenikos Theotokopoulos, called El Greco, whose sober Toledan likenesses stand apart in register from his visionary religious compositions.

title: Portrait of a Man
description: A young man in a black doublet turns toward the viewer with one hand resting on a parapet, his face emerging from a darkened ground. Andrea del Sarto painted the sitter around 1517, and the picture was long thought to be a self-portrait; Vasari wrote that had Andrea's spirit matched his judgement he would have been without equal among Florentine painters.
credit: mechanical reproduction of 2D image

title: Portrait of a Monk
description: A young, bearded man in a dark brown habit is shown bust-length, his face lit directly against an earthy brown ground, meeting the viewer's gaze with quiet intensity. Rubens made such character studies as preparatory heads for his larger altarpieces, and this example is held in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (inv. 48.599).

title: Prayer in the Garden
description: A nocturnal Agony in the Garden, with Christ kneeling in radiant spotlight while the disciples slumber and torch-bearing soldiers approach through the olive grove. The picture exemplifies Tintoretto's preference for elongated figures, plunging diagonals and theatrical chiaroscuro.

title: Queensland Art Gallery - Joy of Museums - Figure with Snow Falling by Takahashi Hiroaki
description: A woodblock print by Japanese artist Takahashi Shōtei, held in the Queensland Art Gallery collection. The delicate composition captures a solitary figure amid falling snow, exemplifying the artist's refined treatment of winter landscapes and human presence in nature.

title: Red and Pink Poppies
description: Two opium poppies — one deep crimson, one pink — and a closed bud rise on long stems from a slim glass vase, their silvery scalloped leaves brushed loosely against a pale ground. The canvas is signed at upper left and painted in an unusually tall, narrow upright format. Monet's flower still lifes belong chiefly to the early 1880s, when work indoors filled the gaps between landscape campaigns.
credit: Claude Monet - Red and Pink Poppies , Irina , 25 December 2013, 02:31

title: Redoute flowers01
description: A spray of cultivated flowers drawn life-size against an empty ground, each bloom and leaf described with botanical precision. A plate after Redouté, the botanist-painter attached to the Jardin des Plantes and to the Empress Joséphine's garden at Malmaison. Colour stipple engraving finished by hand, in the technique used throughout his folios.
credit: from en:Image:Redoute flowers01.JPG

title: Remigius van Leemput - Whitehall Mural
description: Remigius van Leemput's 1667 oil copy of Holbein's lost dynastic mural for the Whitehall Privy Chamber shows Henry VIII standing in the foreground left and Jane Seymour in the foreground right, with Henry VII and Elizabeth of York disposed behind them flanking a central inscribed plinth. Painted for Charles II, the canvas is now in the Royal Collection (RCIN 405750) and is the primary record of Holbein's original composition.

title: Resurrection
englishTitle: The Resurrection, from the Isenheim Altarpiece
description: Christ rises from the tomb in a halo of gold and crimson light, his shroud trailing as the helmeted Roman guards collapse blinded beneath him. The Resurrection forms the right wing of the Isenheim Altarpiece's second opening, painted by Grünewald between roughly 1512 and 1516 and one of the most extreme depictions of divine radiance in Northern Renaissance art.

title: Ribbons and Laces for Very Pretty Faces
description: Three women in 18th-century dress gathered at a doorway examine goods offered by a male pedlar bearing a basket, the scene animated by the exchange of ribbons or lace. Edmund Blair Leighton painted the work in 1902 under the full title Ribbons and Laces for Very Pretty Faces, rendering costume and setting with his characteristic attention to period detail.

title: Rocks at Belle-lle
description: Jagged dark rocks at Port-Domois on Belle-Île rise dramatically against a warm sunset sky of pink and gold, the sea below rendered in deep blue-violet. Monet made an extended campaign on the storm-battered Breton coast in autumn 1886, producing a sequence of canvases focused on the island's rugged granite formations under shifting Atlantic light.

title: Rogier van der Weyden - Triptych- The Crucifixion
description: Christ on the Cross occupies the central panel, flanked by mourning figures including the Virgin Mary and Saint John; the wings show Saint Mary Magdalene (left) and Saint Veronica with her veil (right), all set against an open Flemish landscape of hills and towns beneath a blue sky. Mourning angels in deep blue hover at the top of each panel. Now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna, the triptych exemplifies van der Weyden's command of precise drapery, restrained gesture, and narrative clarity in fifteenth-century Netherlandish devotional painting.

title: Sans-culotte
description: A standing sans-culotte in the striped trousers, short carmagnole jacket and red cap of the Revolutionary Parisian, a pike at his side. Boilly recorded such figures and the street life of Paris through the 1790s. Oil on canvas, in the small finished format characteristic of the artist.

title: Scops Owl
description: A scops owl swoops in flight through a spray of cherry blossoms against a pale full moon, in the kachō-e bird-and-flower tradition. Ohara Koson's woodblock print, held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, combines soft tonal printing with the quiet naturalism characteristic of his Shin-hanga work aimed at early-twentieth-century export markets.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts Boston

title: Shaw John Byam Liston Now is Pilgrim Fair Autumn-s Charge
description: "Now Is the Pilgrim Year Fair Autumn's Charge" // "The title of the work is an enigma. It appears to be a poetic quotation, but is from none of Shaw's preferred writers, including Christina and Dante Gabriel Rossetti, Tennyson, and Shakespeare. "

title: Shepherd Tending His Flock
description: A shepherd stands wrapped in a cloak as his flock spreads across a flat plain under a wide, luminous sky. Painted in the early 1860s, oil on canvas, now in the Brooklyn Museum. Millet drew his rural subjects from life around Barbizon, where he settled in 1849.

title: Show booths. Kustodiev
description: A colourful theatre booth dominates a winter fair, crowds in bright coats gathered around it beneath frost-white trees hung with pennants. Boris Kustodiev's painting of the Shrovetide balagany captures the festive character of provincial Russian folk celebration, a subject the artist returned to repeatedly around 1916–1920.

title: Snowscape
description: A winter landscape of snow-laden peaks and bare trees rising above a misty valley, the foreground pushed to one corner in the asymmetric manner that earned Ma Yuan the nickname 'one-corner Ma'. Attributed to the Southern Song court painter and held in the National Palace Museum, Taipei. Hanging scroll, ink and colour on silk.
objectKey: collection-of-beauty/雪景图轴.传宋.马远.画.纸本设色.台北故宫博物院藏.jpg

title: Spring. Kustodiev
description: A spring thaw in a Russian provincial town, with flooded pathways, figures including children crossing planks over the melt-water, and birch trees coming into leaf before colourful houses and a distant church. Boris Kustodiev captures the festive mood of the Russian season in a bright, high-keyed palette typical of his townscape paintings.

title: St Mary Magdalen
description: A solitary image of the penitent Magdalen withdrawn in a rocky wilderness with her book and ointment jar. Tintoretto isolates the saint against a brooding twilight landscape, animating the meditation with flickering, sketch-like brushwork.

title: Stitching the Standard
description: Edmund Blair Leighton's 1911 canvas shows a young woman seated on a castle battlement, sewing a yellow-and-black heraldic standard against an open landscape. The medieval-revival subject is characteristic of Leighton's Academicist work, combining careful attention to period costume and stone setting with a quietly focused feminine figure.
credit: https://www.sothebys.com/en/auctions/ecatalogue/2011/victorian-edwardian-art/lot.51.html 1 &; Art Renewal Center

title: Summer
description: A sweeping Flemish landscape animated by peasants, cattle, and a laden cart making their way along a dusty road beneath a dramatic sky of breaking clouds and shafts of light. Rubens's Summer, dating to the 1620s and now at Buckingham Palace, situates the season's agricultural abundance within the long Flemish tradition of landscape painting, filling the foreground with the textures of rural life and the middle distance with a vast rolling prospect.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/r/rubens/5landsca/04landsc"

title: Suzanne et les vieillards
description: Susanna recoils in her bath as two white-bearded elders crowd in from the shadows, one gripping her arm as the other pulls back the drapery. Giambattista Pittoni painted the Old Testament subject in the 1720s in his Venetian Rococo manner, treating the apocryphal Book of Daniel episode with the pale flesh tones and sweeping silks typical of the city's settecento.

title: Tab V
description: An engraving from Tabulae VII uteri mulieris gravidae (Seven Tables of the Pregnant Uterus, 1748-51), the obstetric atlas of the Leiden anatomist Bernhard Siegfried Albinus. The fifth table shows a full-term fetus curled with its limbs drawn up, the umbilical cord running to the opened placenta, whose branching vessels are spread for display; an engraved Latin key fills the lower part of the plate. This impression is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
credit: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/9e/54/5e3a318daa3aaa966e022d01508a.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L0034071.html Wellcome Collection gallery (2018-04-03): https://wellcomecollection.org/works/pnbunkzq CC-BY-4.0

title: Tamakatzura Tamatori attacked by the octopus
description: A woodblock print by Utagawa Kuniyoshi depicting Tamatori, sword raised, confronting a large octopus as she recovers the Dragon King's pearl from his underwater realm. The composition shows a sailing vessel in an upper vignette and the dramatic underwater struggle below, with waves and the octopus's coiling tentacles filling the lower sheet. The subject, drawn from the legend of Prince Fujiwara no Fusasaki's mother, was a recurring theme in Kuniyoshi's ukiyo-e narrative prints.

title: Tamatori being pursued bya dragon
description: A second telling of the Tamatori legend, with the diver fleeing the underwater palace as a dragon and its attendants give chase. Kuniyoshi exploits the woodblock medium's capacity for sweeping diagonals and undulating tendrils of marine life.
credit: Visipix . Archived from the original on 2016-01-09 . Retrieved on 2005-09-08 .

title: The Accolade
description: A medieval-revival fantasy of a queen knighting a young warrior with the flat of a sword, set in a sun-streaked palace hall. The picture is by Edmund Blair Leighton, a late Victorian academic painter whose chivalric scenes drew on Pre-Raphaelite costume study and theatre design.
credit: nevsepic.com.ua ( direct link )

title: The Baptism of Christ
description: A Mannerist treatment of the Baptism in which crowds press toward the Jordan beneath a luminous descent of the Holy Spirit. Tintoretto orchestrates space through deep diagonals and silvery, restless light, characteristic of his late Venetian altarpieces.

title: The Barber Institute of Fine Arts - Joseph Mallord William Turner - The Sun Rising through Vapour
description: Turner's marine pairs working fishermen and beached fish with a low sun burning through coastal mist. Held by the Barber Institute, the picture exemplifies his early atmospheric naturalism, in which form is dissolved by light and humidity rather than drawn line.

title: The Beautiful Servant
description: In this oval-format Rococo canvas, a young woman reclines on a canopied bed and turns to glance at a youthful male figure who reaches over her, the whole scene bathed in golden-yellow drapery. Fragonard's fluid, loaded brushwork animates the silks, linens, and curtains with characteristic speed and lightness. The painting is held by the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm.
credit: Nationalmuseum

title: The Butcher's Shop
description: Two aproned butchers work among hanging carcasses and joints of meat, one trimming a cut while the other hangs a side — a small canvas of the early 1580s, the more compact of Carracci's two butcher-shop pictures (the larger is at Christ Church, Oxford), now in the Kimbell Art Museum, Fort Worth. Carracci's interest in low-life genre, drawn from northern prints and direct observation, gives the scene an unusually frank realism for its date.

title: The Dedication
description: A Crusader knight in chainmail lays his sword upon an altar as a woman in a green gown and white veil kneels beside him in prayer within a stone chapel. The work was known only through a 1908 black-and-white photogravure for over seventy-five years before the original canvas was rediscovered; it was sold at Christie's, London, in December 2013.
credit: Christie's , LotFinder: entry 5755480 (sale 1177, lot 49, London, King Street, 12 December 2013)

title: The End of the Song
description: ] Although The End of the Song illustrates no specific incident in history or literature, it recalls two well-known literary subjects, Tristram and Iseult and Paolo and Francesca . [. ]» (Christie's)
credit: Art Renewal Center

title: The Hostage
description: A young woman in a rust-red gown leans against the stone parapet of a coastal castle, gazing out over the sea, while three attendant figures — a seated woman with a book and a standing companion — remain behind her on the sun-lit rampart. The work, signed and dated 1912, depicts a subject that sources link to the legend of Tristram and Isolde, and the painting was subsequently sold at auction by Sotheby's.
credit: http://www.artsfairies.com/leighton/leighton_biography.htm [ dead link ]

title: The King and the Beggar-maid
description: King Cophetua kneels before the barefoot beggar maid, who stands beneath a gilded baldachin clutching her shawl, as he offers his crown. Edmund Blair Leighton painted the subject in 1898, drawing on the Tennyson ballad, with richly modelled brocade and warm Orientalising architecture characteristic of his academic narrative style.
credit: Edmund Blair Leighton

title: The Lion and the Mouse
description: A lion struggles and roars within a heavy rope net stretched across a stormy landscape, its powerful body pressing against the cords while birds circle in the darkening sky overhead. This large canvas, now at the Château de Canisy, is attributed to the collaboration of Frans Snyders and Peter Paul Rubens and illustrates the Aesopian fable of the lion caught in the hunter's net.
credit: château de Canisy [1]

title: The Magdalen with the Smoking Flame
description: The penitent saint sits in shadow, her cheek resting on her raised hand as she gazes at a smoking oil lamp whose wick trails a thin curl of smoke. A skull lies in her lap, and books are arranged on the table beside the lamp. One of several Magdalen meditations La Tour painted, this version — now at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art — reduces the vanitas iconography to flame, flesh and darkness.

provenance.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
provenance.location: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

title: The Moscow Cathedrals and river Moskva
description: A view across the thawing Moskva toward the bulbous domes of the Kremlin cathedrals. Vereshchagin, better known as a war painter, here records the Russian capital with the same documentary precision he brought to his battlefield reportage.

title: The New-born
description: A tightly cropped nocturne in which a woman shields a candle as another presents a swaddled child, often read as a Nativity in contemporary dress. The smooth, sculptural surfaces and concealed flame are hallmarks of La Tour's late Lorraine candlelit manner.

title: The Nubian Palace Guard
description: A palace guard stands sentinel before a carved geometric screen, dressed in a voluminous yellow cloak and blue garment, carrying a long spear and a round shield surmounted by a coiled serpent and falcon finial. Deutsch returned repeatedly to this figure type, polishing each gilded boss and inlaid tile to an almost photographic enamel finish that made his Orientalist set-pieces sought after across European salons.

title: The sleeping hermit
description: An aged hermit in a white habit dozes on a bench set against a rocky cliff face, his breviary fallen to the ground beside him, while a wide seascape opens out behind. Spitzweg used these solitary monastic figures as gentle emblems of retreat from the modern world, rendered here with the sunny, detail-laden touch characteristic of his Romantic panel paintings.

title: The Spy
description: A solitary informant figure rendered with the documentary literalism for which the Russian battle painter was known. Vereshchagin's military scenes typically reject heroic convention in favor of the bleak human detail of campaign life.
credit: Sotheby's: http://www.sothebys.com/en/auctions/ecatalogue/2012/important-russian-art-l12111/lot.9.lotnum.html

title: The Stolen Kiss
description: A young woman in a silvery silk gown turns to receive a clandestine kiss in a doorway, the card party visible through the room beyond. Long attributed to Fragonard and now generally given to his sister-in-law and pupil Marguerite Gérard, the late-1780s panel passed through the Stanisław August collection to the Hermitage, where it still hangs.
credit: Hermitage Torrent

title: The story of Nastagio degli Onesti
description: The third panel of Botticelli's Story of Nastagio degli Onesti depicts the crucial banquet scene: an armoured horseman on a white horse bursts in among shocked guests at an outdoor table as hounds pursue a fleeing nude woman, the ghostly vision appearing before the assembled company. The courtly pageantry of the feast, richly dressed figures, and open pine-grove setting reflect the refined humanist taste of the Florentine commission.

title: The Zaporozhye Cossacks Replying to the Sultan
description: A boisterous huddle of Ukrainian Cossacks dictates a profanity-laced letter to the Ottoman sultan, their laughter rolling across the tabletop. Repin worked on the picture for over a decade, building each character from ethnographic studies into a celebration of stubborn Slavic insolence and freedom.

title: The-moreno-garden-at-bordighera
description: Palms, agaves and dense subtropical foliage press forward in the foreground, with a tower and white buildings glimpsed through the canopy beyond. Monet painted this canvas during his 1884 stay at Bordighera on the Italian Riviera, recording the exotic garden of the Moreno estate with the richly varied greens and blues that mark his response to southern Mediterranean light. The work is held by the Norton Museum of Art.

title: Three Friends of Winter 歲寒三友
description: An ink album leaf bringing together the three classical scholarly emblems of resilience — pine, bamboo, and flowering plum — in spare, calligraphic brushwork that interweaves the three plants into a single composition. Zhao Mengjian, a Song-dynasty literatus, renders the trio with economy and precision, surrounded by collector seals accumulated over centuries. The leaf is in the collection of the National Palace Museum, Taipei.
credit: Upload of August 2011: Qin, Xiaoyi [editor] (1995). Songdai shuhua ceye mingpin tezhan - Famous Album Leaves of the Sung Dynasty . Taipei: Guoli gugong bowuyuan pianzhuan weiyuanhui. p. 222. Cited in: Ebrey, Patricia Buckley et al . Bamboo, Plum, and Other Plants . A Visual Sourcebook of Chinese Civilization (online reference work). Upload of April 2018: Not given. Upload of May 2024: Cropped from image downloaded at 墨林拔萃 冊 宋趙孟堅歲寒三友圖 . 故宮典藏資料檢索. Taipei: National Palace Museum.

title: Tokaido28 Mitsuke
englishTitle: Mitsuke Station: View of the Tenryū River
description: Mitsuke, the twenty-eighth station of the Tokaido road, depicting travelers crossing the Tenryu River by ferry. Hiroshige's woodblock design uses graded blue bokashi and a low horizon to evoke morning mist over the water.
credit: The Fifty-three Stations of the Tokaido

title: Transparence
description: Overlapping semi-abstract figures are interwoven in warm ochres, reds, and dark browns, their contours dissolving into one another across the surface in a dense, gestural composition. The work belongs to Picabia's Transparences series, in which he layered figural forms to produce images readable at multiple depths, a direction he pursued from the late 1920s.

title: Tsar nikolai
description: A portrait of Tsar Nicholas II in full imperial dress — red military uniform with blue ribbon and numerous orders — set against the golden-domed churches and towers of the Moscow Kremlin. The work is unsigned and held without museum attribution in the catalogue, but the physiognomy and iconographic setting identify the sitter as the last Russian emperor, reigned 1894–1917.

title: Utagawa Kunisada
description: A triptych nishiki-e print from Utagawa Kunisada showing elegantly dressed women holding umbrellas as they walk through snow at Ueno, their vivid kimono and lacquered umbrellas set against a white ground. The design belongs to the ukiyo-e bosetsu (evening snow) theme, here treated with the bold colour and decorative pattern characteristic of Kunisada's mature work, published in the series Nishiki-e.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 1301809

title: Vase of Flowers with a Coffee Cup
description: A loose spring bouquet — striped and red tulips, yellow wallflowers, clusters of small daisy-like blooms and a sprig of lilac — fills a round glass vase, with a white porcelain coffee cup, saucer and silver spoon set before it on the polished tabletop. The canvas is signed and dated at lower right. Fantin-Latour built much of his reputation on quiet flower pieces of exactly this kind, which found an especially eager market among English collectors.
credit: Henri Fantin-Latour - Vase of Flowers with a Coffee Cup , Irina , 2014-04-05 21:59

title: Venus At Her Birth Attired By The Three Graces
description: Venus stands upright on swans amid waves while two female figures above her hold billowing drapery, and a winged putto hovers to one side. The work belongs to West's late mythological output and is recorded through a Sotheby's auction catalogue; no firm date or medium is established in available sources.

title: Vesalius Fabrica p163
description: A woodcut from Andreas Vesalius's De humani corporis fabrica of 1543, showing the complete human skeleton standing upright in a landscape, leaning on a staff — the Latin caption identifies it as the anterior view of the assembled bones. Part of the foundational Renaissance atlas of anatomy, the plate combines scientific precision with a theatrically posed figure set against an open countryside background.

title: Vesalius Fabrica p184
description: A muscle-man plate from Vesalius's De humani corporis fabrica, depicting progressive layers of dissection with the cadaver theatrically standing in a Paduan-style landscape. The series broke with medieval anatomical convention by presenting direct observation as the basis of medical knowledge.

title: Wildenstein 1996
description: A close-up mass of chrysanthemums fills the entire canvas, their rounded heads in purple, yellow, red, and white packed so tightly that no background is visible. Monet produced a series of chrysanthemum studies in the 1890s at Giverny, treating the flower garden as a sustained subject in the same way he approached his series paintings. The paint is applied in short, looping strokes that follow each petal, building a dense decorative surface.

title: Wildenstein 1996
description: From Monet's Giverny years, this work reflects his sustained meditation on water, reflection, and shifting light around the property he had transformed into a living motif. The palette favours violet-blues and greens applied in dense, woven strokes that flatten depth into surface.
credit: Clipped from https://wpi.art/2019/01/16/monet/

title: Wildenstein 1996
description: Purple irises grow at the edge of the Giverny lily pond, their tall stems and open blossoms rising above a carpet of floating lily pads that extends into the background. The palette of violet, blue-green, and grey places this among Monet's late garden subjects, painted when the pond and its plantings had become his principal motif. Broad, gestural strokes merge the irises and their reflections into a single unified surface of colour.
credit: Clipped from https://wpi.art/2019/01/16/monet/

title: Wind God and Thunder God Screens by Tawaraya Sotatsu hi-res
description: Sotatsu's pair of two-fold screens places Fujin clutching his wind sack and Raijin riding a ring of drums against expanses of unworked gold leaf. The bold negative space and tarashikomi ink pooling became a touchstone for the Rinpa school and a National Treasure of Japan.

title: Yoshitoshi The Ghost
description: A translucent female figure with long dishevelled hair drifts among climbing gourd vines bearing white flowers and fruit, the full moon glowing behind her against a blue ground. The cartouche links this image to the "Yugao" chapter of The Tale of Genji, and the print is part of Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon series.

title: Голова Христа в терновом венце
englishTitle: Head of Christ Crowned with Thorns
description: The head of Christ crowned with thorns is presented within a circular format, the face bowed and eyes downcast in meditative sorrow, long hair and beard rendered with fine linear precision. The monochrome tonal modelling places the work in the Russian academic graphic tradition; it is catalogued in "Русская графика от А до Я" (Moscow, 2002). Fyodor Bruni was a leading figure at the Imperial Academy of Arts in St Petersburg, where he held the chair of historical painting.
credit: Русская графика от А до Я. М.:СЛОВО, 2002. С. 43

title: Мавзолей Шах-и-Зинда в Самарканде
description: Photograph of the Shah-i-Zinda mausoleum ensemble in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, one of Central Asia's most significant architectural complexes. The site comprises a series of connected mausoleums built from the 11th to 15th centuries along a narrow street on the outskirts of the ancient Silk Road city. This image captures the ornate tilework and facades characteristic of Timurid-era Islamic architecture.

title: 名绘集珍册 9 宋 李迪 春潮带雨
englishTitle: Spring Tide with Rain (Li Di, Song dynasty)
description: A Southern Song album leaf depicting a spring tide laden with rain, attributed to the court painter Li Di. Soft ink wash and atmospheric distance reflect the lyrical small-format landscape tradition cultivated at the Hangzhou academy.
